This equipment is for heroes of the Dominion. Have you earned it?
Only heroes of the Covenant may purchase my goods, warrior.
Only those who've fought well for the Covenant can purchase from me.
When you've fought for the Pact, you earn the right to my wares!
I extend greetings, warrior, and invite you to examine my wares.
I don't really feel safe here, but I don't know where else to go.
We're still too close to the Doomcrag, if you ask me. We should keep moving. We're just asking to be attacked out here.
Witches… everywhere, witches…
How? How could we have failed so?
So cold… Everything is so cold.
Thank you—I owe you my life!
What did you say about me?
I've heard so much about this great city of Mournhold. Strange how legends and tales differ from the reality of things.
Yesterday an Ordinator reminded me of the homily of the boiled kagouti. Is this why we are requiring registration of visitors? To keep ourselves from being boiled slowly?
Someday, I hope to become a proud member of House Indoril and the Ordinators. Then, maybe I can be one of Mother Almalexia's Hands!
Betrayal!
Let's see what these stones reveal.
They didn't deserve this. Any of it.
Strike quickly like a snake. Time is of the essence.
Approach, mortal.
Did you really meet the Bramblebreach Elders? Impressive!
I heard you fought that mad mage at the Wilderking's throne.
My brother was in Longhaven when the mist set in. Thank the Divines you were there to get to the bottom of it.
You're the one who uncovered the plot on the Queen's life.
You're the hero who saved Seaside Sanctuary from the Maormer invasion!
You're the hero who single-handedly stopped the Daedric invasion at Moonhenge!
It's a shame about the losses at Moonhenge, but I hear it would've been much worse if you hadn't been there.
You were at Hectahame! Is it true that Indaenir rose from the dead?
Jonah … good ….
Imperials coming from that door to the south!
Imperial troops coming from the ruins to the West. Quickly!
They've opened a portal by the eastern waterfall!
I'll share <<1>>'s gift. Make you respect my power!
Kneel before me!
Ahhh!
You enjoy killing, don't you?
When blood flows in the streets, the ale flows in the tavern. It makes me feel guilty, but what do I do? Turn people away?\n\nI don't think so.
This city's cursed, I tell you. Cursed!\n\nThe only safe place is inside this tavern. It's the ale, you know. Fortified for our protection.
Somebody! Somebody needs to go see! I need to know if my house is still there before I try to stumble on home!
No, no, no more. Not another drop. Clearly, I'm already drunk.\n\nOn the other hand, since I'm already too drunk to walk, I might as well stand here and have another drink!
Now, hold on. I have this idea. What if under all those helmets, all those soldiers in the Shornhelm Guard are really the same person? What then?
Just enjoying some time alone. I'd rather keep it that way, thank you.
I was thinking of preparing something special tonight. Something to make the taste buds tingle. But I don't seem to have any kwama livers in the pantry.
This is my spot. For my cart. No one else can put their cart here. It's a law or something!\n\nLet me show you what I have for sale today.
Look at it. The Thizzrini Arena. It's so… majestic.
My money… All of my money, it's all gone!
Thank you! I can leave this nightmare!
I'm ruined. I can't go home now, can I? I've nothing left.
Oh, you must be a combatant. I like the look of you.
You are here to fight? Then, fight. This one must see your worth to know whether you are a fine wager or not. Practical matters, this one has seen.
Nothing… I have nothing left. Not even the strength to leave this place.
Why must it be 'to the death'? I am confident, but… not that confident. Perhaps 'to the maim'?
Ignore all the paupers. Things here? They're just fine.
What a mess. This is just awful.
You just wait until the mayor finds out!
I'm telling the mayor about this! Then you'll be sorry! You'll be so sorry!
Is that smoke? Why, I do believe that is smoke!
Well. I don't know what to do, so I'm just going to sit here until I figure something out.
I don't see how anyone could stay in Southpoint. It's … well, it's crazy.
Blessed be the name of the god of mercy, Stendarr.
I continually pray to the Eight for the sanity of the townsfolk. Keep them in your heart, please, for their minds are not their own.
How many lives have you taken?
You don't deserve to live.
Interesting, it's all so … interesting.
One tale says Y'ffre turned Falinesti into a mountain when it was threatened by the Knahaten Flu.\n\nWhether its inhabitants remained in the mountain is a true mystery.
Falinesti will return. And when it does, we Faithful will be here to greet it.
Falinesti will return. Fools insist the city never existed, that it was a grand Wood Elf hoax. These ruins are proof enough for me.
Falinesti … where could it have gone?
The Wood Elf rulers once maintained their throne in the highest branches of Falinesti. I suspect <<1>> knows more than he's sharing.
I doubt Falinesti's people cohabited with trolls. From where did they come?
What if Falinesti was burned? The thought is appalling. Such a grave fate for a graht-oak.
Come, my children. Let's … play!
We don't get many visitors in the Halls of Torment, but there's always room for a few more … permanent residents.
Show me respect for what I've done!
<<1>> is mine!
What a nightmare that was! I guess I can thank my good fortune the creatures that took Northpoint weren't exactly big drinkers.  \n\nAnything I can get you?
Keep that bear away from me!
What once was and will be, trapped in flesh. Set it free!
Hello! …Oh, goodbye.
Hello! I'm not supposed to talk to people. It's embarassing.
I'm certain these targets were facing outward before. I don't understand … why would anyone turn them around?
Smarten up, Captain Fuzzypaws!
Jeanne wanted me to pack the house up so we could go elsewhere, but … I lost the key.\n\nThat must be really stupid, mustn't it? I'm sure I had it just a minute ago.
I'm working on it. Whatever it is, I'm working on it!
The fury of Almalexia guides us!
I told you it would work! Let's find the others!
Nerien'eth, I demand that you stop this! Please ….
<A shrill yell. This text should not be shown.>
One of you must fall. Let it be your opponent.
You'll leave <<1>> in my stomach!
Only Apocrypha knows the number of times the pact viridian will be breached. And how far-reaching the consequences.
Stop, thief!
Let's go.
Imposter!
Where …?
The fabulous town of Pa'alat is ready for you! Your coin will go far in the gambling halls of Pa'alat!
Hear and know! Krin Ren-dro was a traitor to the crown! The town of Pa'alat patrolled by Dominion soldiers!
Looking to lighten your coin purse? Come to Hadran's Caravan! Games, races, and fights of all kinds!
Come one, come all to Hadran's Caravan! Now under kindler, gentler management!
Get away from there!
You've done enough, Nerien'eth! Stay your blade!
I won't be defeated! I've come too far!
I'm not at all sure we can turn this around.
Whoever said all knights are brave? I confess this howdy-do makes me rather nervous.
End my misery. Kill me.
Drove out the infidels, eh? Good.
Why so busy? Join us in celebration!
Do you want to get me killed? Go away!
What mounts I have left are sure to be fine steeds, indeed! Trust my experience on this.\n\nConflict may make horses testy, but their will to survive hardens them.
So, you've come to try some of my potions and ingredients.
Enchanted steel is objectively superior to mundane steel. Truth!
Is that all you've got, little Elf?
Say your farewells, old man!
We need to ensure we can fight off the Imperials, and any other sort of attack that might visit us.
What do you think he has planned this time?
It is critical that we reach Alik'r promptly.
We've fought all over Tamriel, but never frost trolls. How can those things be so vicious?
I've no idea how long things were cooking in those ruins, but it's boiled over into quite a mess. Quite a mess, indeed.
Taking stock of our supplies is a touch depressing. We've got less of a presence than our stores would suggest.\n\nIt feels wasteful. But, if reinforcements arrive, I suppose we're prepared.
If you've got a thirst, I've got something for you.
Come, come and eat! If your belly is empty, fill it!
In all the Dominion, you will find no finer foods than mine.
The finest of drinks from anywhere in Tamriel!

I have, in my many years, traveled throughout Tamriel and … tasted nearly everything that could be brewed into a potion.\n\nYou may benefit from this experience: I know more of alchemy than most alive today.
Come out! Come out and talk to us!
It doesn't matter how skilled you are or what magnitude of soul you invest into an object.\n\nIn time, the magic will still fade. Enchantment is a study of disappointment.
I get a lot of strange looks for my choice in armor. It requires some talent to imbue ebony with Daedric essence, you know.\n\nI consider it a point of pride. A mark of my trade, if you will.
Orcs are the strongest, that's a simple fact. And when it comes to smithing the finest weapons, it's not enough to make the metal ring or sing. The metal must scream.
The working of steel is a walker's gift.\n\nAfter all, only steel is sharper than one's own claws, yes?

You look like someone who needs a bag. Perhaps a sack, purse, or parcel? A sabretache, knapsack, or satchel? Medicine bag, messenger bag, bindle, or haversack?\n\nOr just a backpack? You decide. I'll be here.
Some call this junk. This one?\n\nThis one also call this junk, resell it at deep discount.
I wouldn't say staves or other enchanted items are mandatory for any spellcaster.\n\nThey certainly help, though!
Thank you for tracking down that shipment, friend. If another opportunity opens up, I know I can count on you.
The raw destructive power imbued in a staff of quality is enough to make a difference on any battlefield.\n\nImagine: An entire army hurling bolts and blankets of fire, frost, or lightning. Majestic.
If you lack the claws, a sword will do. Yes?
Original access to this site came through the fissures in the main chamber, not the tunnels we currently use.
This crack in the wall was once a mine, if you can fathom that.
Why are you still here? You like what you see, mmm? Want to spend time with your old granny Alyxe, eh?
A weapon depends upon the material from which it is made. The sharpener's skill is just as important.
Scholars so often become a fixture within the sites that they hope to study.
Ah, a colleague of mine. I would say peer but to call any corpse a peer is unsettling.
Nobody makes bows like the Bosmer!\n\nNo, really. Nobody does. Everyone else cuts down trees, it's insane.
Robes, surcoats, and jacks! Battle-ready clothing for all physiques and figures!
I weave dreams and memories into my textiles. Outside of Artaeum, you will find none other capable of my tailoring.
Bone, hide, and scale. No other material compares to these in the marriage of durability and mobility.
This one knows your needs. You need lightweight, rugged armor to suit your active lifestyle.\n\nThis one knows and can provide.
Stone, steel, or bone. These will all stop a blade and save your life.\n\nWood too, I guess.
I deal with many merchants from many guilds. I even trade in wood.\n\nI just don't handle it myself.
No safer vault in all of the Dominion. Do you see the trolls? We have trolls guarding our vaults.\n\nNowhere else has the troll security guarantee. Nowhere.
This one can guarantee not even Baan Dar will steal anything you leave with us.\n\nUnless you are Baan Dar in disguise. This one supposes, then, anything you leave with us is yours.
Nothing steals from us. Nothing and nobody.

We don't do loans. We're not that kind of bank. Think of us as a vault. Long-term storage. \n\nEven if you were to say, die, and return to life thousands of years later, you could retrieve anything of yours we have.
It must be around here somewhere.
I can assure with every confidence our vaults will never be breached.\n\nAnd I should know, as a reformed robber of banks.
I wear my armor proudly, for it is a symbol of the Legion with which I once served.\n\nNot the one that exists today. Help the Dominion retake Cyrodiil. Help us make the Empire right.
Siege engines. It takes a calculating, peerless mind to construct them.\n\nFortuitously, I am so armed.
The majority of the work to be done as a tactician is logistical in nature. You know - managing supply trains, ensuring our forces have food, arrows, that sort of thing.
This one has just the thing to get one into Cyrodiil, to best fight for the Dominion.
A champion of the Dominion needs the very best equipment one can get.\n\nI provide only that: The very best.
Looking for a place to stay?
This one knows your type. Adventurers. Always in need of more places to stow their things.
Hungry? No reason to wait. Pull up a chair and I'll have something for you in no time.

I learned when I was young that High Elves brew things from berries and grains.\n\nI had such an argument with mother after that. There is essentially no reason to be brewing anything from beetle stomachs.

Did you know Wood Elves have a way with animals? Nobody else handles animals the same way we do, since we're the only people who observe the Green Pact.\n\nSo, really, I'm the best stablemaster you'll ever see!
As Boethiah ate and digested Trinimac into Malacath, so too do I digest warriors into … better warriors.\n\nIt's a metaphor. I'm no cannibal. I just beat whelps like you into shape.

Thanks in part to the strong network of trade that passes through Elden Root, we have an outstanding supply line here.\n\nThis makes Samati's job very much easier than it otherwise could have been, yes?
Did you know? Lamaia has many resources for fellow mages to exploit.\n\nLamaia is resourceful, of course. She has earned this post here, at Elden Root. This one assures you of this.
Aetherius is a deep, dark, and endless sea. Endless, too, are the secrets of magic and its myriad forms and expressions.\n\nConsider me a tutor, provided you merit my tutelage.
Are Khajiit really welcome in your Dominion?
Elden Root doesn't need your construction!
This one is tired of waiting!
I'm nearly free, after all these years!
One who complains about the quality of our wells has never drunk water from a hoofprint.
Kuzashi is thinking … perhaps we include some of these trees when our embassy is built. A show of solidarity, yes?
How much longer must we wait?
I cannot spare this much time, truly.
What was your name again? Target practice?
What are you doing? Get out of here, you're going to bring the guards down on us!
Hah! Finally caught you! You think you can just walk into someone else's camp and take whatever you want?
Keep your voice down. Loud speech attracts unwanted attention.
Spare some coin? Or some skooma?
What, are you going to hit me too? You're just like the rest of them, aren't you?\n\nEveryone that comes through here—they all hit me.
Can't you just leave us alone? Haven't you types already done enough?
Do a poor Elf a favor? Kill as many of the bastards who've brought their filth in here as you can.\n\nThey've beat us down, taken our things, and gotten some of us strung out on skooma. It's awful.
I am creating for myself a holy place. A site where, in time, the Divines might restore my sight.\n\nIt's my sight site. Don't laugh. Everyone does.
Thats what you think! Get'em boys!
That'll show you.
Champion! Congratulations on your victory!
Champion, you are always welcome at Thizzrini!
Finally … something to eat.

This. All that's left of my research. I had it all when I came down here, but most of it's been burned. No matter, no matter.\n\nI'll be on top again. I'll set back into my position, and everything will be set right.

Of course, nobody down here recognizes me. It's been so long since they've been to Summerset, I expect they wouldn't.\n\nWhen Phynaster finally comes to take me home, they'll see. They'll all see. And none of them will come with me.
It is so hard to keep one's fur clean in these conditions, but … this one has no place else to go.
<<1>> worries much about his <<2>>. She sleeps so much these days.\n\nIs she sick, this one wonders? Or is it the sleep of sorrow? For we have nothing left but that.
Stay back! These … glowing flowers, they belong to this one!
I'm looking for my rug. I sent it to my son some time ago, and then … I came to be here.\n\nI can't leave. But my rug can come to me.
Finally, some meat! I don't even care where it came from anymore.
Keep it up, you slime!
You're enormous! How can you hope to keep up?
We'll see how funny you think you are when you're flying off this tree!
Please, my children are starving ….
That's what you get for denying my babies.
Even the duke has acknowledged this is the best course of action!
Can you believe how awful this music is?
Keep the noise down!
Die!
Hey, friend. Hey.
Help a walker out. This one had … has needs, this one does.\n\nThis one needs to hire a caravan, yes? You buy this mammoth cheese?
Morndas is the worst. All my obligations and duties just standing there, screaming for attention.
You seem a bit too serious.
Get some rest, have something to eat. Maybe have a chat with the commanders over there. \n\nIt's what this place is for, right?
The beauty of vistas like this reminds me that Y'ffre has a song for us everywhere.
They abbey is reduced to rubble! What will we do now?

Y'ffre the Singer is the most important god we worship. We know many people—especially other elves—place Auri-El higher, for Auri-El's province is that of time, in itself uninterruptible and majestic.\n\nBut Y'ffre is the Now, the living moment.
Y'ffre, the Singer, the Storyteller, who resides in the Now ….
You don't follow the Green Pact, do you?
You should stop and read more. It's good for you. Someone told me that once, at least.
Something about these Bosmer-made tables is … off-putting to me.
I think Countess Tamrith is doing a damn good job myself.
Baron Dorell's going to have all this mess cleaned up in no time. You'll see.
That's all they've got? Pathetic.
That's it! Have some lightning!

Do please leave me my space. I am researching the vagaries of culture in Valenwood, to best avoid committing any social blunders as we work in the region.\n\nEvidently before we arrived, the Bosmer would … nonviolently raid fellow villages. Bizarre.
No! No! It is not just terrible, it is awful! This simply will not do!
<Crowd cheers.>
<Person gasps.>
Why does she look like me?
Such lovely plants.

I read in a book that the Wood Elves call themselves tree-sap people. This is also true of Argonians!\n\nThe Hist are our trees, and their sap our sap. For the Wood Elves it's the Graht trees. Isn't that interesting?

This one is being pressured by his family to seek a mate from our political alliances. <<1>>'s quandary is the Wood Elves. They seem so lazy, and you cannot trust their cooking.\n\nBut the High Elves are so … tall. They are very tall, truly.

I have been studying this structure since I first arrived here in <<1>>, and I must say, it is simply fascinating! Stones of these size moved into this interior portion of the tree—how was it done?\n\nCould the ancient Bosmer have done this?
Ah, yes … very interesting.

I've been watching the scholar over there poke at and sniff and rub the shrine since he arrived.\n\nIt's fun, in a weird way. I've heard songs and stories of these things all my life, so I'm just relaxing and watching him try.
Sabibi wonders if this tree truly grew this way naturally.\n\nIf the Wood Elves do not harm wood, could they coax it to grow in this fashion?
The decision you must face is black and white. The fate of one … Man … rests in your hands. Mercy or torment—make no mistake.

I struck off west to try to ensure new—or better—trade partners for the Great House Hlaalu. That's actually going fairly well.\n\nBut I never imagined I'd end up traveling this far. Who knows? Maybe I'll end up in Summerset some day.
You know, in Ald'ruhn the Redorans live in a massive crab shell. It's not nearly this tall, though.

Have you been to the Elden Root Fighters Guild hall? It's quite large. Possibly the largest in the Dominion.\n\nOf course, the size of your hall doesn't make you a better combatant. That takes work, right?
Have you been to the Elden Root Mages Guild? We ensure our members are prepared for the Daedric and undead threats we're currently facing.\n\nIt's nice there. A lot of open space to practice.

This is wonderful. I am here drafting sketches for more involved pieces of artwork depicting Valenwood. I'm under contract with a group organizing scenic trips for the nobility of Summerset.\n\nSo, naturally, I am expecting substantial profit.
Oh, hello. Isn't this scenic?
Be sure to stay near, and don't leave the road. The wilds can be a dangerous place.
Here, you can get a view of majestic Elden Root in all its splendor.

Hello. I'm a Spinner, as in a spinner of tales and stories, yarns and … tales. Being a Spinner is a pretty important thing. I'm sure you'd agree, unless you wouldn't, in which case you don't.\n\nBut we speak myth for Y'ffre.

Strange wanderer, wandering wayfarer, roaming vagabond of adventure, hail. I invite you, sit a spell and join me.\n\nPerhaps I shall spin a tale for you, perhaps not. It all depends upon your temperament, doesn't it? To listen or to not.
The jungle port has suffered pests before, and will again.\n\nIt takes a clever mind to repel vermin—they do not see it coming.
We never used to get this many visitors to Elden Root. But now, we've got Khajiit and Altmer living here.\n\nIt's a bit of an adjustment, I suppose.
Such is the fate of all foes of the Empire.
The Elden Tree is so different from any of our towers in Summerset. It's beautiful, in its way.\n\nI wonder how long it must have taken to grow?
How dare you tresspass here?
Weakling!
Nothing but bad deals today. Waste of this one's time.
This one sees some things he likes, but … times are hard, yes?
Only the best food in all of Cormount!\n\nThat's what I serve, I mean. I don't want to be overly vague, I'm sorry. I'm a cook by trade and I serve excellent cuisine.
It was something I saw this morning. On the scroll, perhaps?
Keep your robes on. I'll get to it as soon as I can.
Fancy a drink? Or maybe two, or ten?\n\nIt's such a good day for a nice drink, don't you think? A fine time for a fine time.
Hello, and a fine day to you! Are you interested in any of the goods I have to offer?\n\nI assure you, despite our location our stock is ample.
Hello! Is there anything you might need for your travels? I am always happy to do business with adventurers like yourself.
I know, I know … I'll keep looking.
The forest certainly is beautiful, isn't it?
All this talk of the Pact and the Covenant and the Imperials, it's all very interesting, isn't it?
You, go! Bakkhara can only hold this back for so long.
The joke's on Endarwe. I'm bound to that sword now. Though he does still have my body—a little off-putting, actually.
Here to help the Dominion, that is me. Helping to keep everything tidy and in its place.\n\nSometimes this means I have to hunt wild things or thieves, and that is fine too.
Eager to move on. \n\nI can't really say anything aside from that—tired of the Black Sap and tired of working with all these steel-clad hardheads.
All these little papers the Dominion write up seem so interesting! I just want to know what's on them.\n\nIt's driving me crazy.

With all of the problems in Bangkorai, we decided to try and weather the storm, so to speak.\n\nThere's good fishing here, and good shelter, for now. If we have to move on, that's fine, but things are okay out here.
I never liked fish. This was all my brother's idea, and it works, I suppose.\n\nBut really, it's torture. I can't stand fish at all. I'd rather run off and join the witchmen at this point.

So… here we are. Another day in paradise.

All the fish I could ever want, all the water I could ever hope to see. None of the fighting I could ever fight.

Paradise.
Quickly, follow <<1>>.
Lyris Titanborn is a mighty and noble warrior. Trust in her.
No sign of them yet, eh? Too bad. They were nice enough fellows.
I'm glad I can walk around the upper city safely again. I always found it more peaceful than the hustle and bustle of the lower city.
Have you seen what the Countess wears? It's positively scandalous! I guess that's what they're wearing at the High King's court, but it seems a bit ostentatious for a place like Shornhelm.
Montclair's thugs wrecked my home, my shop … how in Oblivion am I ever going to recover from this?
Trouble to the west and north? Not our concern. As long as Shornhelm's secure, nothing else matters.
Are we really safe now? I'm not so sure. I don't think this business with Montclair is finished. Not by a long shot.
Mark my words—vampires are behind all this Montclair nonsense. I know they are.
Fascinating.
In the name of Molag Bal, come forth and destroy his enemies!
No, no. To the tor's central tower.
Baron Montclair's audacity is a personal affront to Arkay.
Nice work, heard you help Baron Dorell. Now we have to figure out what to do with these stragglers.
Stop them! They must not reach the crystal!
Not sure how I thought that ritual would play out. Thanks for the hand, traveler.
Hircine, why do you forsake me?
Whose there?
Frost troll! A frost troll!
I don't understand why Baron Montclair would betray Rivenspire.
The Montclairs betrayed Rivenspire and Shornhelm. Never saw that coming.
Baron Dorell is so … reckless. He needs to be more cautious, like the Countess.
Baron Dorell is an excellent leader. They should just crown him king and be done with it.
I hid most of my horses from the Wood Orcs. No mean feat! You know how horses get when they're frightened.\n\nBut I have a way with animals. It's a gift.
<<1>>'s soldiers were no match for the inner vault. Step carefully.
You'd best be moving along.
Do you mind? This is my house, such as it is.
We've disturbed this ancient place and awoken its guardians!
Adusa has claws enough for all of you.
That is the best you can do? Adusa laughs at you.
Daedra, spawn of Padomay's black blood! Answer the cry of your servant! Come forth and walk upon the face of Nirn!
Arlie's room. Dear, sweet Arlie. If anything's happened to her, I don't know what I'll do.
What did you just do? It's getting hot over here!
The air is starting to fill with dust!
Nothing.
It's back to where it was when we came in!
Damn! We were almost there. Keep trying!
That trap door led down to an undercroft beneath the manor, but Arlie's mother sealed it up long ago.
Aldmeri Dominion!
Blood for the Pact!
For Daggerfall!

Lord Sotha would urge clemency toward his fellow scholars of Aetherius, given the destruction of their guildhall.\n\nAnd so, they shelter in our temple. Seekers of the Triune Way will simply have to cope with their neighbors.
Yeah!
<evil laughter 1>
Always be careful with knives while cooking. One slip and you can lose an eye.
I try to ignore what goes on downstairs. I've seen things that would make Ysgramor blush.
Welcome to the Outside Inn! We're the only inn outside of Elden Root itself, hence the name.
These Bretons are fine folk, but they eat like tiny bunny rabbits. Not to worry, though. My food will make them grow large and strong—like Nords!
Bring forth the blood offering.
Lord of Domination and Brutality, we sacrifice this innocent in your name!
We submit to your will and call forth the chains of Coldharbour!
When Coldharbour calls, Nirn obeys!
Through the spilled blood of an innocent, we call forth your anchor to join our worlds!
No hope for our people. No hope.
We'll stop him, I'm sure of it. Keep away from those thorns and you'll be fine.
Why thorns? Why not casks of ale? That's how I'd decorate my inner sanctum.
Strike swiftly and without mercy. Angof will offer none to us.
Better to suffer in silence.
Arkay bless this soul and sanctify this broken vessel.
I'm a fish … fisher … catcher … person.
What do you think you're doing?
That isn't yours! Now hand it over!
Into the drink with you.
Welcome to Bha's Bargains. Take a look at my goods or die!\n\nI jest. I didn't mean the "or die" part. Not really.
Wherever you find people, you find someone who wants to buy and sell. Supply and demand, and all that.
I truck in magical goods. If that interests you, wonderful! Let's do business.\n\nIf not, then make room for anyone who is.
I'm still not sure how I ended up in this place, but this city seems safe enough. For now.
I hate this place! Coldharbour. What did I do to deserve this fate?
I can't believe I volunteered to come to this place. What was I thinking?
I feel safe enough in the Hollow City, but I don't think we should linger here too long.
I'm happy to see that the Councilor has finally agreed to Giron's plan. I just hope it's not too little, too late.
That advisor from Mournhold … he doesn't act like any advisor I ever met before.
Between Ralden and Giron, we'll be past this crisis in no time.
The House Councilor is missing? Oh, what dreadful news!
What did Varon tell you? It's a lie! It must be! Giron would never betray us like the advisor claims.
If the councilor has been hurt, we'll make Giron and the Maulborn pay!
Giron? Working for the Maulborn? The very thought of it chills me to my bones.
The Maulborn claimed they wanted to help. The liars! There's a special place waiting in Oblivion just for them and their kind.
Have you located the House Councilor yet? With every passing moment, the chances of finding him alive become less and less likely.
Port Hunding's a place for honest merchants, you know.\n\nAnd honest merchants trust me to keep their goods under lock and key. You know, so they don't get stolen.

Running out of room in your pack? Never fear—the solution to your problems is here! I commit to providing the finest of bags to store your goods! In.\n\nBags in which to store your goods. That is what I sell.
Did you see the forest spirit?
Be careful with that!
What in Oblivion is that?
You interested in buying a mount? Because I'm selling them. Assuming werewolves or something worse doesn't show up and make a meal out of them first, of course.
Can you feel it? With the Wood Orcs gone, it's like the forest is breathing a huge sigh of relief.
This one has the bag for you! Nurisipa has just the thing to carry your items—in style and comfort!
There's something I definitely like about living among Argonians. It may be … how much they appreciate a finely-made bag or satchel.\n\nOr basket. Baskets are fine, too.
I don't like the cold much. So, I keep a bunch of blankets in one of my own bags—after all, I've got bags to spare, right?
I made myself scarce while the Red Rooks were here. Now that things have been sorted out, I can get back to the business of buying and selling my beautiful mounts.
Not on my watch!
I adore my horses, but I can be persuaded to part with one. For the right price.
We've been looking for a new deckhand. It's going to be you.
I'll chop your head clean off!
This won't take long.
Ha ha ha! Ow! I quit.
Well, you're tougher than you look.
Rise! Rise and slay these fools!
Whatever happens, the Mages Guild will continue its mission, in Arenthia and elsewhere. It is simply our way.
Need a horse? Or just a place to hide yours for a while?
The Scaled Court claims this place. Do not resist. You will become thralls, just like the Sword-Disciples.
Death by a hundred cuts.
The sword shouts!
The sky falls!
The Ansei forges a singing sword.
The wave crashes.
The sword sings.
The mountain charges.
The stars fall.
The sun rises. The blade shines. First-blood goes to the Ansei.
The blade breaks.
Wood Elves aren't made of wood. Sea Elves aren't made of water. M'aiq still wonders about High Elves.
No ships depart for the Summerset Isles. M'aiq wonders if the High Elves made them up.
M'aiq once climbed the Elden Tree. Then he learned of the stairs inside. Good thing, for his claws began to hurt.
Why should M'aiq stay off the grass? He always steps lightly.
M'aiq hates weddings. There are never enough sweetrolls.
The Mane is chosen by scent. Had M'aiq known, he would have bathed.
M'aiq wonders, who wants to live on a bleak rock? Why not a pleasant rock?
M'aiq heard an old-timer speak of lost mittens. Keep looking, says M'aiq. Mittens will turn up somewhere.
M'aiq learned too late that ash pits are home to Dark Elf ancestors. He … erm … hopes they don't mind the rain.
M'aiq had a horrible dream last night. Mudcrabs, flying through the air. Horrible!
The people of Windhelm are strange. Wherever M'aiq went, they spoke of licking corn.
It is so cold here, yet M'aiq sees Nords in sandals. Madness!
M'aiq heard much of Headman Bhosek, but saw very little. For the best, M'aiq thinks.
M'aiq cares little for politics. Truly, he thinks everyone is his ally.
M'aiq was told to stay away from Oldgate. This confused him. M'aiq remembers when it was called "Gate."
Can vampires have families? How? Perhaps M'aiq does not wish to know.
Step on sand and burn your feet. Bury feet in sand and grit gets under the claws. Poor choices for M'aiq.
M'aiq speaks the truth, except for when he doesn't. With you, always the truth.
M'aiq could not find the Tower of Lies. Molag Bal plays a joke, yes?
Khajiit tell M'aiq he is unlike most Khajiit. M'aiq tells Khajiit he is most like M'aiq. Then, we eat moon-sugar.
M'aiq asked an Argonian if she could breathe underwater. She asked if he could see in the dark. M'aiq had no good answer.
M'aiq paid a merchant to ship his things to Stormhaven. Half went to Stormhold, the rest to Haven. Stupid merchant.
The milksop returns victorious! The milksop is a dangerous milksop, I see!
Damn! Almost had it!
I heard you and those mages ran headfirst into something evil in Elden Hollow. Good to see you live to delve again!
Close the noose, boys!
I've got you now!
I heard those Daedra you faced at the City of Ash were led by Mehrunes Dagon himself! You must be a beast in battle, my friend!
People are still talking about that battle on Tempest Island. Did you really kill a hundred Maormer with your bare hands? Alone?
Hrm. Heard you ran into a changeling in Selene's Web! And survived! You might just be worth a damn.
And the Undaunted returns! And from the Vaults of Madness themselves! Hope it was worth it—defeating the Mad Architect couldn't have been an easy feat.
So the spider-slayer returns! Heard you cleared those cobwebs with prejudice!
All finished mucking about in the sewers, are we? Heard it was noble delinquents stirring things up. I take it you taught them a lesson.
Some of our Undaunted brethren say you delved into the Crypt of Hearts—and reported the sounds of supernatural battle. I guess the fools were too cowardly to follow you! Ha!
I guess you fancy yourself the new ruler of Volenfell, now that you've conquered it. Too bad all your subjects are dead!
Ho, ho, the captain's dead! Captain Blackheart's dead! And here comes the one who done the deed ….
Well, if it isn't the king of Fungal Grotto! Tell me, is your head heavier now that you're the king?
I heard you fell into a scuffle at Darkshade, new blood! Did you teach those Kwama a lesson? Tell me, how hard is it to squash a bug?
You're back, new blood! Heard you wrestled with lamias in that old Imperial fort! How'd you like it?
Heard you fought a fierce battle in Direfrost Keep, new blood! Our brethren said they heard fierce storms raging before you emerged! Must've been an epic battle!
What is this? Are you Champion of the Crucible now, new blood? I heard you put on quite the display!
Now is not the time!
I told you to keep your head down!
Don't make me leave you behind!
It was your idea to ask for directions!
Keep back! Watch our enemies fall before me!
You said you'd handle any trouble!
You said you were the best!
The main road! I said we should take the main road!
This is your fault. You let this happen!
No, not that way! Swing to the left! The left!
You should have left us to our duel!
The winds take your ashes!
The storm shall end you!
I'll freeze the flesh off your bones!
It is past time we ended this!
I'll bind your soul!
I can smell your fear!
Think you're clever? Ha!
I'll make you dance, before your end!
Tava's frost! Die, already!
Was that supposed to scare me? How quaint.
Overextending yourself is a poor strategy!
I can smell the tempest of your suffering!
Clivia Tharn sends her regards!
No flesh, no pain.
I, er, uh—"this one" has much talent in the workings of enchantment. Apparently.
The Celestial Mage summons me to deny your presence. Begone from this realm!
Meddlesome fools! This ends now!
The more the merrier, I say!
Look at this pile of debris! Sahalu will die of old age before it is cleared. Poor Sahalu.
Burn in our rekindled fury!
The flame hungers!
The slumbering beast awakens!
The Shehai of a first rank Ansei sank Yokuda. This Warrior's Shehai is beyond first rank.
Do you louts think you're going to save my wife? She doesn't deserve to be saved.
Over here!
I don't pay you to think, <<1>>.
This island reeks of corruption.
I cannot control my creations!
Mind your step.
My magic is splintering!
We told the Orc that the next interloper would lose his head. The Firstmages make good on their promises.
When we are finished, peace will be upon you.

There's a lot of fire up there. I don't like fire I don't control. Fire I don't control is terrifying.\n\nLook, just buy something so that I can leave. There's adventuring to be had, fires to be setting. On things other than me.
This one is tired of dragging goods and wares to taverns and monster-infested caves. This one pines for a simple vendor stall.\n\nKhajiit sacrifices a lot to be an Undaunted.
You looking for something to buy? Undaunted should be leaping into ancient tombs. Not lugging this stuff around.
If you've got coin, I've got things to sell. Also crippling gambling debts. The two may be related.\n\nNo, really. I've lost so much money to gambling.
Your survival instincts must be immense! Even the gladiators of the Blessed Crucible would pale in comparison to you!
M'aiq wonders, how can there be kings for other kings?
I'll crush you!
No! Not like this!
Taking aim!
Raaawwwr!
Bracing for attack!
Kill them—they are not to reach Nerien'eth. Alanwe is not to be harmed!
I will see to it the Golden Flame erases you.
Fall!
None escapes the reach of my spells!
Burn!
Here—allow my friends to show you a good time!
Eat their flesh!
This will end you.
Pray to the Eight. You'll receive no mercy from me.
I could kill you myself, but I have hungry souls to feed.
My wife has been dealt with. It's your turn.
Your deaths won't empower the Blade, but I'll be happy to add your souls to my collection.
You'll make a fine meal for my children.
You would do well to run.
How do you think this will end, mortal? Give up!
Protect me, you fools! The mortals are not to reach the Blade!
Burn.
The Blade is not for your hands.
What need have you of the Ebony Blade?
Ignore these dull-clawed miners and traders—nothing but thieves and swindlers, the lot of them. The best deals happen here, with Shurami!
Mauloch's third jaw-bone! How do those spindly legs hold you up? Let's put some meat on that skinny frame!
If you plan on thumping some Iron Orcs, that's dangerous business. Need a little liquid courage? I have a few select brews you might want to try.
There's nothing but brambles and poison berries out there in the crags, friend. If you need quality provisions, I'm the Breton to talk to.
Our Mistress has wounded this place forever.
Too many haunt this place. I miss solitude.
Send more fodder!
Must I do everything myself?
You had to come farther. You could have escaped with your lives. Mortals.
My web will hold your bodies for later.
Iron Orcs? Pshaw! More like … like … paper Orcs! Gonna write some bad words on them, fold them up, and post them back to their ugly Orc mothers! Har!
Kill me, please!
It's not my fault! I'm sorry!
Get me out of here!
You had to come farther. You could have escaped with your lives. Mortals.
You had to come farther. You could have escaped with your lives. Mortals.
Damned miners keep dragging that red stone down here. Nothing but worthless rock, if you ask me.

Been days since we've seen an ore wagon. Bah. A mine's just a hole in the ground if you can't trade what you chip out of it. \n\nBeen hauling red brittle just to make ends meet. That's how desperate it's gotten. Damned Iron Orcs ….
Just need … a moment. I'll be fine. Just let me rest for a bit?
Would it kill the workers to just use the ramps? This winch is about as reliable as a three-legged mule with the red brittle shakes.
I like it up here. A brisk wind blows off the slopes, and you can't beat the view.
Allow me to show you a vision of the inevitable.
I am giving your friends a taste of Nirn's future.
With the mine closed, we only have to work when we want to. That gives me much more time to work on my epic story!\n\nI'm going to be a famous storyteller, just like Veesk-Olan and Fjokki the Bard.
Let those other fools mine red brittle. Azzaril prefers iron and orichalc ore. Gold is much better than the shakes, yes?
Though all Mundus totters on the brink of Oblivion, we must not lose faith.\n\nNo matter what the Daedra do, we soldiers of the light must be ready to stop them.
Make way for the Paragon's return!

The Rat detects a familiar scent. Yes. This is the smell of a friend. \n\nHe's grateful that you're his friend and not to all these others. They may need help, but do they deserve it? The Rat thinks not.

I think this axe is too heavy. Does it look too big to you? I should have gotten a spear. A really long spear. Don't want to get too close when you stick an enemy, right? I heard the blood spurts all over the place.

My accompaniment had to sail back to Auridon. Alas, he lost all the fingers on his playing hand in a tragic accident. \n\nBut do not concern yourself. It was a favor to everyone near and far. His music was terrible, even before the accident.
Keep your head down out there. Those Xivkyn are grabbing people and dragging them off to the arena.
I became an acolyte at the Temple of the Divines when I was seven years old. I've been there my entire life.\n\nI can't believe everything is lost.
In my wake, the seas will boil, and the roots of the earth will rise to tear civilization apart.
This architecture is really something, isn't it? Those old Nords really knew what they were doing. Hard to believe it was made by hands as big and clumsy as mine.
This table is off limits. Taken. Reserved.\n\nThat means keep walking, pudding pie.
Best lighten that purse before someone puts a hole in it. Let's make a deal!
I hate waiting around! I didn't march half-way across Cyrodiil to fight practice mannequins!\n\nIf we don't get to kill something soon, I might have to go pick a fight with the Blood Feathers!

Hello. I'm the healer for the Diamond's Daughters. And it's thirsty work! Keeping these sods alive is like trying to grow dragonthorn in saltwater.\n\nBut lucky for them, I have plenty to drink and I'm equal to the challenge.
Our heroic warriors have been defeated. Too bad. But what can you expect from a bunch of ignorant mortals?
Plan to compete in the Arena? Well, mind the traps. A spike in the arse will kill you just as dead as a sword in the belly.
No utensils required! We don't stand on ceremony here. Dig in!

Kazbur suggests you leave immediately. All you will find here is horrible, horrible death. Of course, no one ever listens to Kazbur.\n\nSince you cannot take your gold with you, this one suggests you buy something expensive.
Shaveskins laugh at this one's belly. Lucky for them, Sugar-Dance has plenty of self-confidence and a very calm demeanor.

You look … interesting. I've certainly seen worse. Not much worse, mind you, but I'm sure you'll perform better than that blind Argonian who demanded to compete by himself.\n\nWhat a mess. Scales everywhere. Took weeks to clean him all up.

Dahnkin is a very good listener and has heard many things about the Arena. More than just fighters roam the Arena—much more. \n\nThis one does not know how they get all the strange creatures inside, but this one promises to find out.
When so many warriors gather, egos become as fragile as egg shells. Walk softly and try not to step on too many as you go.
When you and your group are ready to enter the Arena, let me know.\n\nOnce you enter, however, there's no turning back.
Sit.
Slay them!
May your blood burn!
You will die with your people!
Ahhh, just who I wanted to see. We must speak. Will you take the pledge of the Undaunted?
We'll deal with you ourselves.
Death has not yet claimed you. That is good. Take the pledge, and we will see how the day ends.
So, you've fled here too? I'm sure it's a sad story, but I can't stand any more bad news right now.
Who needs the Temple of the Divines? We can just conduct services in here from now on!
Yes, I'm dirty. What of it?
Stick around. Kerennia always has tasks for strong warriors.
It's good to see you, comrade. Your Guild needs you.
The Imperial Prison is a source of great trouble. A grievous twilight calling itself Dusk is said to rule the Prison with an iron claw.
Many greetings, my friend. Glorious view, don't you think?
Nice work today! Get out there, have a drink, and toast the evening stars! Tomorrow brings a new chance to stain the ground with blood.
Good to see you. We can always use more guildmates down here.
Between the Imperial Prison and the Dark Anchor, this is the deadliest district in the City.
Another mortal! How quaint.
You have done well today, Undaunted. You have let death pass you by for another turning of the sun. Return tomorrow … and we shall see if you can do it again.
You think you'll survive this? Amusing!
Why go to Cyrodiil when we can bring Cyrodiil to you? Have a look!
Blood and fire!
It's done! Now hold that position and split your group to clear the other side!
No! They've taken that site!
You think this weapon's a needle? What if I put it in your eyes?
You don't plan to compete in this challenge, do you?\n\nI say this with the best intentions—leave now. I hate to see the weak get stomped upon. And that's my good deed for the day.
Welcome to the Arena!\n\nDon't let the Battlemaster get to you. He invites people to come play, then mocks them for trying. He takes a certain pleasure in being annoying, I think.
Those who let overconfidence cloud their perceptions will fall in this arena.\n\nKeep your mind clear if you decide to compete.
A clear mind is the key to victory.
We came a long way to compete. Our tribe may not approve, but it was time for my brother and I to leave home and create our own adventure.
My sister talks of adventures and destiny. It's hard not to get caught up in her excitement.\n\nI guess that's why I followed her on this crazy journey.
Who needs to fight? We won! We drank up all the ale!\n\nHa! Let's see you top that, scum!

Look at all of these puny excuses for warriors! Do you know how Orcs prepare for a battle? We eat! We drink! And in Gunran's case, we throw up all over the fancy floor!\n\nThat's how an Orc gets ready for a fight!
You're going to fight in the Arena? With that crew? Ha!\n\nIf I had any more ale, I'd drink to your memory.
What a strange place this Arena is. I'm sure it wasn't here when I visited the area a year ago.
Not certain if we're going to compete. My partner is more interested in discovering the secret of this place.\n\nMe? Oh, I just want to light someone on fire.

My group left me! Every one of the horkers! Just packed up and took off without even a proper good-bye.\n\nI have half a mind to compete on my own. They'll feel really bad when my body is returned to Skyrim in separate containers!
Everyone's got a story to tell and I'm here to listen.
Feh. These gray Orcs smell like a mammoth's armpit, but this red metal will fetch a fine price, yes?
I hear that they punish deserters in my cohort by drowning them in a well. I guess that's all right. It's pretty difficult to drown an Argonian.
Fighting for Isrudde's a real joy, let me tell you. Queen Ayrenn's nice on the eyes, sure, but she pays about as well as a one-legged farmer. Now I earn more in a week than I did in a year.
This lot has ventured far enough. Slay them!
What's the holdup? Don't you want your reward?
If you're not wearing Orc-crafted armor, you might as well be naked.
I have a passion for working with leather. The smell, the texture … everything. So you see, each piece is a labor of love.
Orcs. What a fascinating people! If they were of one mind, I dare say they'd be unstoppable!\n\nBut I digress. What can I do for you?
I'll be shocked if this city is still standing ten years from now. Destruction follows Orcs the way vultures circle a corpse.
Fix this. Now.
Thanks to the skill and dedication of the forge-wives, Orsinium's army will wield the best weapons in all of Tamriel.
Blood and fire.
Cities need wood and lots of it. Khaguur and I can hardly keep up!
The concept of banking may be foreign to the Orc strongholds, but you shouldn't worry. I learned my craft in the vaults of Shornhelm.
Tear the mortals to pieces!
The flame of the Fire Maw burns like a second sun!
Come! We'll deal with you ourselves!
Arise. We have visitors.
This rain will cleanse you.
You won't elude the Golden Flame forever.
This indignity ends here.
Mind your surroundings!
Be still while I end you.
The Golden Flame will find you, wherever you go.
Welcome to the Greedy Gut, the finest inn and tavern in all of Orsinium!\n\nWhat can I do for you?
Genuine boar-leather bags here, all the way from Valenwood! You can't beat Wood Elf craftsmanship. Have a look!
How am I supposed to run a stable in these conditions? Clan Shatul hasn't even sent their promised mounts yet!
This one has never seen a city come together so quickly. Perhaps we should hire the Orcs to build a city for the Khajiit, yes?
Chief Ushruka sends her regards. Do you need help with your steed?
My chief! What can I do for you?
Orcs worshiping Trinimac? How absurd!\n\nI'm sorry, did you need something?
Chief Laurig sends his favor to the chief-maker of Clan Shatul.\n\nWhat can I do for you?
I keep waiting for a handsome clan chief to take me away from this place.
Here they come again! Steel yourselves, troops!
They say clothes make the man, but they are wrong. It's the man who makes the clothes that make the man.
The king demanded that if the Fighters Guild wanted to operate in Orsinium, they had to have an Orc representative. Guess who got selected for the job.
Most Orcs don't like the idea of Redguards and Bretons in Orsinium, and I can't say I blame them.
Too many of my people fear magic. I try to teach them that magic is nothing more than a tool, no different than a hammer or an ax.\n\nWhile, I suppose it's a little different ….
How disappointing! The Orcs refused to let us build a proper Mages Guild, so we're forced to settle for these … less than ideal … accommodations.
I don't sell anything I won't drink myself. I have high standards, you know.
Hello there.
Hope you've got a strong stomach. Orc cooking can be brutal for folks used to lighter fare.
A city won't build itself—especially not on an empty stomach!\n\nBest meat and vegetables inside the city walls! Get them right here!
You missed. Now you die.
Kill them.
Converge!
Another day, another delivery.
Thank you for this shipment.
Much appreciated, sera.
Their death matters not. My forces will still overwhelm you!
You nearly missed the delivery. I'll try to send it out today, but no promises.
If you discover items of interest, this one will buy from you. My prices are fair, all things considered. There are few customers down here, and fewer merchants.
Hmm? Oh, yes, there is fine. We'll get to it eventually.
This one must talk to you.
You've been warned. Your path is locked.
Wonderful. The more we have, the more we can defend ourselves.
The Golden Flame will consume you—forget you.
There was nothing for you here.
Can I help you?
May I help you?
How can I help you?
What can I do for you?
Can I help you?
How can I help you?

When my father was young, he jumped off this bridge on a dare. Just before he died, he dared me to do the same. I have to do it … I … just .…\n\nAll right, all right. I'm going to do it. You'll see. Soon.
You ever done any cliff-jumping? This is the best spot in all of Wrothgar.
The barrow never bothered us until <<1>> made it a problem. I always knew he was a fraud.\n\nAnd less strapping than I imagined.

We salvaged a few things from the ship. Two bottles of grog, a cask of old spiced wine, four sacks of black bread flour, a half-barrel of heather-tea, and two bedrolls. \n\nAt least it wasn't a total loss!
I'm worried about anyone still out on the ice. Those Riekrs are vicious!
Fish and ale. That's what our clan is known for. The draugr? That's just a distraction.
If the fish don't bite, we don't eat.\n\nStill, I'd rather fish without having to worry about dead Nords, so thank you very much.
I'm the chief's daughter. The old chief, not the new chief.\n\nAnd I'm not bitter. The new chief has been very gracious to me and my family.
If you're here at the king's behest, then my supplies are available at cost.
I'll defend Orsinium to my dying breath.
Word is spreading about the quarry. People are starting to return to help.
Chief Ramash is a fool. Too stubborn for his own good.
Can I help you?
Hurry. I don't have all day!
All right, let's go.
Just one more month till furlough ….
That's one way to stop all that damn screeching!
Alchemy has always fascinated me! Or maybe it's just the fire ….
Eat, drink, and be merry. Just not to excess. That'll make you sick, you know?
I haven't seen my husband in days. He went to help a friend, Plautisanus Favonius, on the other side of the district. He hasn't returned.
I heard noises from the quarry … and then everything got real quiet.
I heard it was Dwarf mischief down in the quarry. Those machines aren't natural!
I do feel sorry for the chief. Everyone is scared and looking to him for help.
Ak'saz was only here a few days when the things went all to Oblivion. It seemed wrong to leave.
Wonderful news! The quarry is open and business is brisk!
This is what happens when you meddle!
Please. Just let me go!
Let's thin that flesh of yours!
Thank you for your aid, warrior. With Daedra everywhere, we'll surely need your help again.
You didn't drink any of this medicine, did you? These bottles feel a little light.
The savages. If the fights were fair, I could hold my own, but the Daedra taunt me endlessly when I'm not in the ring. They don't let me sleep. \n\nHow can I recover under such circumstances?
Though your tidings were not what I hoped, I thank you all-the-same. At least now, I know his fate.
You killed the monster!
The monster has been vanquished!
No bad news, please. This one has reached her limit.

Just let them come! Covenant Soldiers, Pact Soldiers, Legion Zero, Daedra, it matters not. Shaghila will chop them down, one by one!\n\nWhat's on the other side of that door is another matter. On that side, we need support.
Thank you for coming to the city's aid, soldier. I won't lie—I don't think we've ever faced a threat like this, at least not here.\n\nAt least we're alive though, and that means there's some hope.
I can tell from your face that Maximinus is dead. Then we truly are the only ones who survived.\n\nThank you for looking for him, friend.

I've been sitting here for days now, and I have to say, you Covenant types really know how to put on a good show. \n\nYour officers seem to think it's a comedy, but I'll go ahead and spoil the ending for you … it's actually a tragedy.
I'm free!
That foul Daedra will keep me no longer!
I'll never wear silk again!
Flee! Flee, everyone!
"The sewers are safe," he said. I will never trust a scholar again!
To the surface! Surely it's safe now!
Truly Evgir Unslaad is upon us!
There's no shame in fleeing. To fight another day!
It seems today is not the day I lick the Tree.
Swim the foul waters to safety, dryskins!
Did someone slay the Lady or is this a deceit?
May Tu'whacca lead me from these horrors.
Let me out of here!
Save some Daedra for me!
I laughed when my friend fell in the trap, and then she got me.
Must get out!
If my legs will carry me, I must flee this place!
What horrors await me?
This one is free?
Oh, to see the light of the moons once again!
I'm glad you've returned. \n\nYou'll be disappointed to hear this, but it seems the Daedra are again preparing the summoning ritual in the temple.
Unless you are a trained gladiator, I would not suggest entering the arena.
Intruders! The Flesh Sculptor is not to be disturbed!
You won't hold me forever.

I'll fight them. I'll fight every last one of them. I dare them to come here. \n\nI've never been in a fight before, but I've always known that if it came down to it, I can beat anyone, even a Daedra.
I did not think it would be this cold. The moisture on my scales has turned to frost, and that just makes me even colder.
May the hand of Auri-El protect you, soldier.
Keep looking for more papers. The captain says the last ones you found were very helpful.
Kill you! I'll kill you!
Reinforcements are in great need here. Speak with General Nedras for orders.\n\nGood hunting, warrior!

Greetings again. General Nedras was very pleased to hear about those documents you recovered from the Dremora. Knowing their patrol patterns will save many lives. \n\nIf you find any more, you know where to bring them.
Many thanks for your good work. We might win this thing yet.

Watch your step!
Succumb to darkness!
Let shadow flay the meat from your bones!
This is the end!
Open wide!
A brave one! You die first!
You die first!
Impossible!
Mind where you stand!
Breathe! Breathe and suffer!
Who's there?
What was that?

Mortals from the surface? Slay them!
New rats for my experiments. Let's see what colors your flesh turns!
You return. We'll see who triumphs this time!

Arise, minions!

Halt!
Come here, pretty one!

That s'wit! I can't believe she expected me to come back and work for her.

We should have allied with the Worm Cult ages ago.
Put my blade right through his belly. Served him right!
Did they take any of the Imperial Army to the Arena?

It was comical. She popped her head out, and I put an arrow in her eye.
So the fool drew a dagger at ten paces! Last mistake he ever made.
Knitting a wound is hard, but it's better than animating dead flesh.
He was an embarrassment. I sent him to the Arena.
That Xivkyn just keeps looking at me. I feel like a mouse under the gaze of a housecat.
The city belongs to the Cult of the Black Worm, above and below.
Mournhold's sewers are far more sanitary.
Kill them all, I say. Let the necromancers have the bodies.
The fools think we don't know about their sewer base. They'll learn soon enough.
Preserve the corpse, but not too much. A little rot goes a long way.
Raising a dog from the dead? Is she a savage?
I sliced him in half. He stood there and blinked twice before he fell.
The city reeks like a rotten wamasu.
Fear kills, much to my amusement.
I'll have them soiling themselves before you rub the sleep from your eyes.

Food is not my concern. I expect you to provide it.
If I see her again, I'll freeze her solid.

This city should burn. Burn it all, I say!

I am not so crude as to need a blade.
Mortal flesh is so easy to manipulate.
The little ones from the forest make the most amusing servants.
This mortal land is too colorful for my taste.
Were you spawned from the waste in the sewers?
Keep watch. The mortals seek to break the chain.
Paint the ground with the blood of mortals!
The Planemeld must continue!
Complain again, and you'll be a pile of ashes.
How can we command the Daedroth when they are ignorant of our orders?
Elven wine tastes best in the blood of an Elf.
If there is more work, then we need more thralls.
Fool. You'll find yourself in the sewers for that.
I wonder if we have secured the Nobles District yet.
Look behind that building. There may be more.
I do not know which is more foul, the sewers or the altar to the Aedra.
The great chains must hold.
I am but a tool for the kyn.
May the flesh peel from any mortal who dares come near.
I will unleash a storm upon the next worm that tries to get through.
The Dremora could learn from their betters.
The sewer portals are almost complete.

If it were up to me we would destroy every structure in this city.
Come, mortals! The Devourer needs fresh meat!
These thralls would be more useful digging ditches.
Our Dark Lord demands a sacrifice!
We should throw the Worm Cultists into the arena.

These insects hardly merit our attention.
Have fun with the mortals. Send them to the Market when they are spent.
These mortals are naught but disposable playthings.

Embrace my flame!

Break this mortal, but leave it alive for the Arena!
Break this mortal, but leave it alive for the Arena!

General Aklash is a strong leader. I am honored to serve under her command.
Shoo! Go away! The monsters will spot us and then we'll die. Well, I'll die anyway, and that's all I care about.
Don't burden me with any tales of woe. I have misery enough for any ten of you.
These soldiers are fools! They'll die like all the others! You will too!

That General Pollius is a fool. Better to leave and fight another day. That is what I say.

Wait! Watch your step, sera! That anchor's shaken the whole damned city apart!
I can't control it!

Boo!

Check the bodies. None of them are to leave alive.
For the Empire!

Now the Planemeld can begin!
Silence the mortals!
You cannot stop Lord Bal's will!
Be gone!
Run, mortal!
Enough!

Another stupid move!
Do not think about running. There is a bounty on your head.
Good. Carry on.
You will not escape!
Hold a moment! I--uhm ... I had something to say. Oh right, you've got a bounty! Pay up.
What is this for? Oh right! Bounty.
Why are you running? Oh, right!
It seems you owe a bounty. Once you pay, you will be on your way. Simple as that!
Wonderful! On your way, then!
Oh my! You will not get away!
I will give you some free advice--find a new line of work. Now, pay your bounty.
Smart move. Now be about your business.
Bah, I just polished my weapon!
You are cornered. Pay your bounty forthwith!
Go. Commit no further transgressions!
You provoke me? Foul grub!
It proves true time and again--criminals occupy the lowest rung on the social ladder.
What a surprise! You paid!
Just as I expected! Not a bit of honor!
I believe you have a debt to pay, and not just to society. I require your bounty, friend.
Thank you for your timely payment.
What happens next is your fault, villain!
Did you forget to pay? I forget things, too. What were we discussing? Oh, yes, your bounty.
I forget. Why were we talking?
Refuse to surrender, did you?
I sound angry? Of course I am angry! You would be angry too if you had to deal with idiot criminals!
A bit extra would have been appreciated.
If you make me chase you, I will hurt you!
Your evil endeavors end here, wrongdoer! Pay your bounty or suffer my wrath!
The light of reason prevails!
Escape? Not on my watch, knave!
Did you fail to notice me, outlaw? I get that a lot.
Another bounty paid in full.
Why make this harder on yourself?
Anyone who tells you crime does not pay does it wrong. It always pays ... me.
Yes ... well this ought to settle things.
We could have made a deal ... too bad.
I know, I know. You did not mean to do it. Irrelevant--the bounty must be paid.
All right. Have a nice day, then!
Why must it always end this way?
Good day, criminal! I'm excited to be able to accept your bounty and clear your name!
A pleasure doing business with you!
Very well, I can treat you like a criminal!
Another tramp dirtying up my streets. Typical. Just pay the bounty and be on your way.
Painless, yes? Now get out of my sight.
That was your last mistake, vermin!
I erect the spine of 'pay your bounty so I can get back to my patrol.'
Pleasure doing business with you.
Attack the Guard? Great idea!
You're not going to pay your bounty, are you?
Well, that went better than I expected.
I knew you would be trouble!
Sithis can't forgive your crimes, but you are in luck. The law accepts gold.
Praise the egg! The bounty is paid.
I expected more of you, villain!
The law is a river--fight it and you will drown. So pay me your bounty ... or take a deep breath.
Wise decision.
This will cost you, vermin.
How does this go again? Um, yes ... 'Stop, criminal, and pay the bounty for your crimes.'
Wait, you paid? Oh thank you!
Was I not intimidating?
Back home we'd take a finger for each crime. Sadly, we deal in gold here. Lucky you.
Do it again and I'm taking some teeth.
I'll make a drum of your hide!
You! I'm talking to you, criminal! You owe a bounty, so hand it over!
Now, was that so hard?
This is entirely your fault!
The waters of justice flow downhill. Pay your fine or ... what were we talking about? Right, the bounty.
You paid your bounty? That's wonderful news!
Didn't I warn you not to do that?

All right, I guess we're done here.
You just cracked the egg, scum!

Ah, friend! All is forgiven!
I'll make this as painless as possible.

Compensation for your debt has been received!
You can't outrun the wamasu!
You give me gold, I make this go away. Just don't ask what the money's for.
Your gold flows like a fresh spring.
You should have paid the gold!
My records indicate you owe a bounty for a past crime. And my records are never wrong.
A paid bounty bores me to tears.
I knew this would happen!
You have to pay a bounty because you're a bad person.
All right. You can go now.
Now I get to hit you!
You don't want to pick a fight with me. Pay your bounty or else.
Damn. I was hoping you'd run.
And I thought I wouldn't hit anything today!
My scales moisten in your presence. I desire much from you, but I must settle for your bounty.
I erect the spine of bashful farewell.
The wind of justice must blow.
Uhm ... excuse me. I'm going to have to ask you to pay off your bounty .... Or else?
Thanks .... Seriously. Thank you.
Oh, why me?
No one except you and me needs to know about this. Got it?
Plink, plink. Such a musical sound.
Should have paid the gold!
So, criminal, what appendage would you like me to remove? Or will you ruin my fun and pay your fine?
The bounty has been paid. Hurrah.
Ah, and now the fun begins!
Your illicit activities are remarkably noteworthy. I'm almost embarrassed to ask for your bounty.
Consider your bounty paid in full.
But I didn't want to hurt you!

Criminal. Pay your bounty.
That's right.

Might I trouble you to yield, please?

Everything appears to be in order.
Now, this is too much excitement.
Excuse me. I ... I hate to be a bother, but I'm supposed to ask you to pay your bounty.
I did it! I collected a bounty!

How sad. Your name has been cleared.

May the gods help you, my friend.
Stendarr's justice must be done.

I'm so glad that's done with.

Such malfeasance cannot be ignored!

I'm going to make this hurt!

Hurrah! The bounty is paid in full!
Escape? What audacity!

Quick and painless, right? Off ya go.

Your compliance is appreciated.
I will end you!

Sufficient.

Find the exit and get out.

Fun fact: You're the third mistake I let walk free today.
I fear I must ruin your day.
I will perform my duties, citizen.
It must feel good to have your record cleared. Let me show you my stock.
I am not involved.

Zeht's tears, help me!
You will be punished for this!

That is not a thing you should be doing.

Destroy the vampire!
A werewolf! Kill it!
Did someone borrow it?
Your hands are not welcome in my pockets!
Worthless gadabouts. Don't make me throw you on your arse.
No more warnings. Get out!
Dogs! I was so looking forward to beating you senseless.
Stand still, criminal.
There are consequences for breaking the law.
Now that you completed your unpleasant business with the guard, how can I help you?
You and I should just keep our distance.
Enough with the attacking.
Help and help, please.
Someone apprehend that villain.
Bid the guards come and stop that criminal.
A curse upon the murderer's head.
I have nothing to say to you right now.
I wish to remain steadfast, but I cannot.
Please, just keep your distance.
Don't make me alert the guards.
Your tale ends here, thief.
Go back to Oblivion, vampire.
Guards, a werewolf.
I just had these pockets sewn!
Excuse me!
You're trespassing.
No more warnings. Get out!
Very well. Neither of us was ever here.
Hold, criminal!

I don't usually deal with criminals like you, but it has been a lean year.
This is not my concern.
This violence must end!
Help me!
Flames of Satakal! You will pay for that!
What's this?
By Onsi's bright blade! A murder!
Alas, I cannot. Make peace with the law first.
Back, you dog!
For Morwha's sake, let me be!
You are acting very suspicious.
By Ruptga! A thief!
Tu'whacca curse you, vampire!
Stay back, werewolf!
I could have sworn I grabbed it before I left.
Why was your hand in my pocket?

I understand your confusion. Now go.
Fresh off the line, eh? Check in with General Nesh-Tan. She can give you the rundown on our situation.\n\nLet me spoil the surprise—it's bad.
I'm actually a caravan guard from Nibenay. I was just here to deliver goods when the invasion began. The rest of the caravan went and got killed.\n\nSo for now, I'm just staying here.
Make yourself comfortable. It's not much, but at least your face isn't being scratched out by a daedrat.
They resemble me, yes? It is in the eyes I think …. So lovely.
I don't buy stolen goods.\n\nOh, just kidding you. Of course I do!
Ah, my favorite customer! Let's see what you've got.
No haggling on the goods. We pay a flat rate.
I can move all this in a week, if I need to.
I assume you have something to sell?
I don't deal in relics or anything that smells of the blood-curse.
Look what the desert winds blew in! Welcome, friend!
My, you've been busy! Let us do business, my friend.
No one brings me anything good anymore. Perhaps you'll change all that?
I grow weary of moving the same old goods. Have you brought me something new?
Great, another customer! What have you brought me?
I can't wait to see what you have. I'm a-tingle with anticipation!
I try to keep my dealings with common criminals to a minimum.
I do hope you have some quality merchandise. My last client was a disappointment.
After we conclude our business, you must have a drink!
In honor of the Konunleikar, I'm offering a number of specials today.
Aren't you a tall glass of mead! I hope you came to see me.
I admit it. I'm attracted to the darker side of life. It's why I got into this business.
Trying to move your ill-gotten gains? Fine, show me.
No time for chatter. Show me the goods.
Been dipping our hands into strange cookie jars, have we? Show me what you have.
I can move anything, but I specialize in the finer things.
Don't tell me where the goods came from. This one doesn't need to know!
You weren't followed, were you? Good … good, good.
I'm in the orphaned goods business. I find new homes for lost items.
If they wanted to keep those things, they wouldn't have let them get stolen.
Don't like my prices? Good luck trying to sell that stuff elsewhere.
I'll move hot goods for you, but my rates are final.
Ooh. Making trouble, are we? Wonderful.
Don't worry. This will be our little secret.
Don't say I never gave you anything. Actually, don't say I gave you anything. To anybody.
I never saw you. You never saw me. You get me?
I'm not fond of the way these Enforcers do business, but I'm not required to look up to these clods.
Let's see what you've got. We'll do our best to get it back to its rightful owners.
You Enforcers are great. I'm thinking about leaving the Guard and joining up!
What can I help you with today, good Enforcer?
Some Enforcers treat me like a glorified clerk, but my job is important, too.
I hope you have that contraband in order. It makes my job so much easier.
Ah, Enforcer! Always happy to help!
I'll personally make sure these things are returned to their owners.
Confiscated goods. They're what I live for.
Any chance you recovered something interesting on your latest adventure?
Well, look at you! I hope you're here to see me, Enforcer.
I may work for the Guard, but I find myself attracted to the Enforcer attitude. It's so … cavalier.
Let's get this over with, Enforcer. Some of us have actual work to do.
No time for chit-chat. What can I do for you?
Some of us have to follow rules and regulations. The drink helps.
If you buy me a drink after my shift, I'll let you in on a few secrets about Guard patrols.
Got contraband? Show me what you have and we'll talk reward.
Present any confiscated goods and I'll see about your reward.
Hmm. Enforcers. Always looking for easy coin.
There are better ways to keep order than paying Enforcers for contraband.
Please, don't crowd me. One item at a time, so I can note it in the record.
Have no fear, I carefully appraise each item of contraband and derive a fair reward.
I pay top coin for contraband. I wouldn't dream of shorting you and pocketing the difference.
Money for stolen items, eh? Not a bad racket.\n\nContraband, I mean. Money for contraband.
If you have contraband, I have coin!
You bring me the contraband, and I'll provide the gold. Easy as that!
Impressive. So, you killed criminals to confiscate this stuff? Scary.
You have contraband for me? Because I can't give you reward if you don't have contraband.
Enforcers are so brave. I could never face down criminals every day like you do.
Oh yes, this one will give everything back to its rightful owner. Everything.
Returning stolen items is a great service. Thank you for your efforts.
If there were more honest Enforcers like you, crime would no longer be a problem.
Ah, friend! May I call you friend? You must be here about the opportunity.
Ah, you've returned! I knew you would. I had a feeling about you. Are you ready to take advantage of that opportunity now?
Just leave me. I appreciate you killing the bastards, but I couldn't escape even if I wanted to. I'm done for.
Ah, friend! May I call you friend? You've seen how the Enforcers live. Now let me tell you about a real opportunity.
Ah, you've returned! I knew you would. I had a feeling about you. You know that the opportunities are so much better on this side of the law, don't you?
So you decided to see what life was like on the other side of the law? That's no life, trust me. The Enforcers pay better and there's much less chance you'll get arrested.
Good luck out there, Enforcer. Give those outlaws a good drubbing for me.
Do not distract me. An Enforcer must always be vigilant.
Stop, criminal scum! Nobody breaks the law on my watch. Pay the fine, or I'll cut you open.
Submit to the Three, the spirits and thy lords, or you will pay with your blood.
I'll be watching you.
You dare oppose Imperial might?
Cherish my mercy, citizen. It is a rare thing.
Go. Now.
You cannot escape the righteous!
Cause no more trouble. We're watching you … scum.
You cannot end my pain.
You there! Interested in hearing about something new?
We've lost everything, everything but our lives. And in a place like this, even those have little value.

I just can't stop wondering—when did it all start to fall apart?\n\nI've served on the Elder Council for years. I've seen Emperors come and go, but I took it for granted that the Imperial City would be safe, that the citizens would be safe ….

I represent the Daggers. Maybe you've heard of us? My brothers are gadgeteers and I'm here to secure a contact with the Enforcers.\n\nWe've got a trap that didn't work too well against harpies, but how many outlaws do you know that can fly?
Outlaws will dine upon my justice this day, but they won't get any dessert!
So, stopped any interesting criminals lately? Got exciting stories to tell?
Did I tell you how I took down seven outlaws with a single arrow? It's all a matter of timing and angles. And waiting for just the right amount of breeze.
My, you put the rest of these so-called Enforcers to shame! Your bearing, that scrumptious grin playing across your lips … it makes me want to do something illegal just so you'll notice me.
I can't believe they let me join the Enforcers. I'm so excited! I can't wait to catch my first criminal.
No criminal has ever escaped my wrath. I'm just that good.

It is the duty of the chronicler to ensure our system of justice maintains its high ethical standards. That's why we watch and report on what we see. \n\nMost Enforcers bring honor to their profession, but there are a few rotten eggs in the nest.
I'm on the trail of a necromancer with certain … proclivities. Been traveling Tamriel looking for "fresh corpses."\n\nDisgusting.
The Commander told me it wasn't his idea to make me an Enforcer. I think he's just being modest, though.

Is there a reward for providing information about potential criminals?\n\nTake my neighbors, for instance. I'm certain they're up to all sorts of illegal activity, in that ramshackle eye-sore they call a home.

Most of these other Enforcers are small time. Me, I must have taken down hundreds of criminals.\n\nJust last year, I stopped an armed robbery with nothing but a broken lockpick and some torchbug guts.
Is there a reason you're standing close and breathing on me? Some Enforcers may like that kind of thing, but I'm not one of them.

Are they holding you here, too? They think I know something about a fence. I told them I'd seen the ghostfence, once. Now they won't let me out of their sight!\n\nThese Enforcers are heartless—the lot of them!
What did the law ever get me? A few scraps from the tables of the nobility?\n\nThe way I see it, they want us to skim off the top. Otherwise, they'd pay us more.
I provide special equipment for the Enforcers. Gear that isn't completely tested—or even safe, for that matter.\n\nBut when it works, it's a wonder to see!
The Dark Den sent us to keep Enforcer spirits high. Sort of a thank you from the Lord and Lady of the Den.\n\nIt's the least we can do for those keeping us safe from all those ruffians and hooligans.
They call me the Green Hood. I didn't ask for this. But sometimes the world needs a champion who can step up and do the right thing.\n\nI'm not saying I'm that hero, but I do my best.
Thane Mera isn't happy, but how are we supposed to remain sober when there's a Konunleikar going on?\n\nBesides, I do some of my best enforcing when I'm ineb— intox— when I'm drunk!

Are you an Enforcer? I've been trying to lodge a complaint for hours now, but nobody will listen!\n\nI want to put a bounty on my worthless son-in-law. That sluggard refuses to get a job. If that isn't a crime, I don't know what is!
Sometimes I can hardly believe the amount of time I wasted, stealing scraps and picking fights in the street. I'm lucky to have lived this long, really.

It's hard to earn a living when the Commander won't let me have a real weapon. Can't be too careful, he says. Not since the "mammoth trunk incident," he says.\n\nWho knew the sword was so sharp? You make one mistake and it follows you forever!
Finish me, scum. End this … this farce. If you don't, those skulking Imperial scouts will.

Its humiliating! I came here to make amends and turn myself in. But these Enforcers won't even listen to me. Told me my bounty was too insignificant!\n\nWho do I have to murder to surrender around here?
The Rat is thinking. Can't you see this? You're looking right at him! \n\nHe doesn't want to talk right now. Come back later.
By the Steadfast, there is no higher calling than aiding those who seek justice!
Dead, alive … who cares? Only thing that matters is the sweet sound of gold clinking in my pocket.
What is wrong with you people? No-Ears George killed my father in cold blood, for naught but a pony and a saddle. I wish someone would listen to me!
