Don't let me keep you, hero. We both have things to do, yes? For instance, your friend Guybert sees a fetching laundry maid in desperate need of wooing!
If you have a steady sword arm, I have an endless supply of business propositions! Care to hear the details?
That's enough for today, I think. Go! Fritter away your earnings and make merry! But come back tomorrow, eh? The sands and jungles of Elsweyr never stay quiet for long.
Die, little rats!
Let's stir the pot a bit, hmm?
Frosts of Oblivion, come forth!
This should cool you off ….
Kjarg, be a good little boy and smash them to bits.
I'll have your bones for a stew!
I stomp them to pieces!
Send them to an icy grave, Gohlla.
Hiti! Burn them all!
Looking for new playthings, Bani? They'll be dead soon enough.
Show them the storm's fury, Maefyn!
Icereach sisters, give me strength!
The wild is mine to control, Dragon!
Taste the blight!
Ah! Keep these blighted ticks away from me!
Hey! They're killing her spiders! The plants I mean!
I've skinned many a Dragon. A cat will not be trouble.
This one has no fear of your sword, old bat. She is too swift!
Hmm. Bruised, but triumphant, yes? Good.
Those Dragons will not kill themselves. Go. Now.
The people of Elsweyr cry out, "why do these Dragons plague us so?" The answer is simple—because we have not killed them yet.\n\nYou stand ready to hunt these creatures, yes?
Chizbari has no more work for you today, walker. Come back tomorrow—then we talk.
Have you more pieces for the frame? Bebbia is eager to see them in place.
What took you? Feels like I been sitting here forever.
Well, go on. We both got things to be doing.
If you're tired of Dragons breathing down your neck, I've got something for you to do with a slimmer chance of death.
Going to take some time to chase down another lead. Go hunt some Dragons or something.
Nord bastards. The Reach belongs to us!
Mark me. When I find that Nord, I'm going to cave her head in.
I saw her turn a man into a pig. So mind your manners.
One day I'll earn a briarheart. One day.
To arms!
Invaders! Cut their hearts out!
It's a fight, eh? Come on, then!
More intruders? Kill them just like the others!
Death to Azurah's litter.
Khajiit did not dance before the Lorkhaj showed him the steps.
Khajiit craves the taste of misery.
Fill their veins with bile and True Cats go astray.
This one was so empty before the Darkness filled her up inside.
No need to huddle in the Darkness any longer.
She bites her tail, bites her tail in time
Poach the blind, the sickly, and the lame. They belong with us.
That didn't work. Try again.
You won't leave this fortress alive!
We can't let them escape!
You don't stand a chance!
You call this competition?
Ruddy Fangs! Attack!
You're no match for us!
Your life ends here!
For the Iron Orcs! For victory!
This way, five-claw.
Took this poison from a Baandari fresh out of Murkmire. Very effective, but spoils the blood.
Fo Krah Diin!
Feel my freezing might!
The only positive to come from the tapestry's shredding is the opportunity to study the intricate construction of ancient Khajiiti textiles. I've never seen cloth woven in this matter.
Where's the damn grog? You better not have drunk it all!
Salted pork, salted pork, always salted pork! Can we get some greens around here?
Scrawny jekosiits …. Eat a steak for Mara's sake.
Guard duty. Hmph. What a waste of time.
Cats and their sugar. Where can a man find a decent kabob around here?
Dragons … feh. I dare one of those lizards to come tangle with us.
Ugh. I don't even want to know what the cook put in that stew.
More moldy bread? That does it. I'm on the next ship to Summerset.
Rats aren't so bad. Sure, they carry diseases, but who here doesn't?
Keep a sharp eye, mate. Too many newcomers prowling about.
Who's got the water skin? It's too damned hot down here ….
Never seen a Dragon before. Way I hear it, they could swallow a whale in one gulp!
Ugh. One more hour till my shift's over. One more hour ….
Heard there's a hurricane bearing down on us. Make sure everything's tied down, eh?
Fifteen gold says this one can strike a frog's eye at fifty paces. Any takers?
Bastard wants to eyeball me? This one's got two arrows to fix that problem.
Slaves, mudcrabs, lazy hackwings …. I need a real challenge!
Anybody up for a game of dice? I'm falling asleep here ….
Good day to you. If you're here for the honeyed rolls, I'm afraid I sold the last of them. They're turning out to be my most popular item here in Senchal.
One need only walk about this city to find artistic inspiration. The ruins, the castle, the bustling marketplace. Almira finds beauty even in ruin.
I hired you to lead me to a specific site, not the middle of nowhere!
This one did what he promised, now pay what you owe!
Take the coin, you lying Khajiit. I hope it brings you nothing but despair.
Keep your coin, you nasty elf. It likely reeks worse than you.
Hm. Wrong again ….
Come sit for a while. There is always room for another traveler in this one's audience.

Welcome! Please come and rest. This one is always happy to have a new listener.\n\nThis one has traveled the breadth of Elsweyr and has many stories to tell. Would you like to hear a tale of Khunzar-ri?
Come, Tulip! Roll over! I'll even give you a nudge if it's helpful.
This creature is either as willful as she is intelligent or as lazy as she is stupid. Either way, I can't get her to obey a single command.
Of course this one feels badly for those who lost their homes to Dragons, but we don't hand out food and drink for free. We also need to eat and drink, and supplies cost coins!
Mogdal and I have faced countless battles together. Sometimes I think we know each other better than we know ourselves.\n\nI'd ask her to marry me, but she's already committed to her blade.
Sure, the Dragonguard needs warriors. But what is a warrior without a good meal to strengthen their bones?
You never should have sold me that bell, Za'ji!
We're suppose to live here? I thought the Dragonguard were a dignified order. Not ones for sleeping next to cave rats.
These Dragons took everything from me. My home, my family, my life. And so I'm going to repay the favor by killing every last one.
My furnishings are for those with a hero's spirit. The more notoriety you gain, the more I'll have available for purchase.
I'm here for one reason, and one reason only. To study Dragons.\n\nI'll certainly do my best to help you kill the beasts, of course. But don't expect me to neglect my research to do so.
Gold or skooma! We don't care which!
Please! This one is worth nothing to you. Less than nothing!
Do you cats ever shut up? You're spoiling my drink!
This armor may be well crafted, but does it have to be so flashy? I'm trying to kill Dragons, not impress them with my sense of style.
Lost one. We can spare you these deprivations.
How? Please tell me!
No! This was a chance for a better life!

This one once had a life filled with forging horseshoes and bargaining with farmers. Now she can create weapons for the Dragonguard, the greatest adventurers Tamriel has ever known!\n\nQuite the improvement, wouldn't you say?
Puny morsels! Why delay the inevitable?
Come closer and let me end your insolence.
I will burn you till naught but ash remains!
I have waited centuries for this day!
The dead heed my call!
Her eyes gleam like sugarcane in the morning, as dewdrops drip ….\n\nKra! You made Imeretto lose his place! You are strangling this one's muse, walker! Off with you!
Stinking, sweaty animals! Kill them! Kill them!
Blood for the Coven!
The storm's strength is ours!
At least something in this one's life is looking up.
The storm's rage is endless!
Korabi hears people complain about Dragons burning their homes. After … after eating that cheese, Korabi's guts can empathize.
Sometimes a soldier's life leads to Dragons. So it goes, and so I go!
A Dragon! Here? I must report back. Now.
What do you want? Whatever it is, I don't care
This one is always open for business!
Get in here and kill these shaveskins!
The rule of Dragons will save us all.
The old order will burn, and we shall usher in the new.
This one thinks the skooma is cursed. We never should have defiled this place.
This one only drinks from the shrine fonts. You should too.
If blood must be shed, then this one shall wield the knife.
Why must we wait? Our moment of glory is at hand!
If I wanted to brew skooma, I'd have become a barman.
If the Tigershark wants to test his recipe, he can drink it himself.
How about we beat up a few of the crazies?
I could take one of those tusking Pahmar-raht, easy.
This one already tried flushing the waste out to sea. The tide's too strong.
Whenever the shaveskins get too full of themselves, this one conjures a great tailwind to deflate them a bit.
Most of these Khajiit would make better rugs than crew.
I wish those smoke addled wastrels would keep it down for once.
I think the lizards are plotting something. Sleep light.
Thought smuggling skooma was supposed to be safer than slaving.
What do you say we strip down and take a dip?
Think this stuff is sweeter than mead?
You'll not smoke that stuff around this one, if you know what's good for you.
Filthy shaveskins. Water all around and still they do not bathe.
It stinks of fish, skooma, and spew. This one would rather be out to sea.
Keep slacking off and you'll get tossed to those wild sugar-tooths.
I want to catch some jellies for dinner. I rarely have them outside Black Marsh.
Stay out of the stock, unless you want to wind up like those other sap lickers.
I never expected to end up in some backwater like Senchal, but here I am. Just in time for Dragons to burn me to cinders, no less!\n\nWe Mattuses all have impeccable timing.
This one shall prove himself! Look upon my works, New Moon!
The New Moon shall rise in glory! Listen! Listen to me!
My strength is yours to command, Ra'khajin!
Ra'khajin speaks the New Moon's truth, and this one obeys.
Hazazhur tries to keep in good spirits, for his sweet Tebabi. She does not fare well, you see, and we have lost so much.
<Hysteric giggling and gibberish muttering.>
<Raving slurred gibberish.>
<Grunting, angry yelled gibberish, exertions as if smashing something.>
<Paranoid muttering, whispering to self.>
<Painful, miserable moaning.>
<Howling like a wolf, chuffing and raving gibberish.>
<Nauseated murmuring and retching.>
Rah! Grr!
Wah! Ahh! Ahh!
Show me your guts! Show 'em to me!
You won't take me!
Knew you were coming! Knew you were all coming for me!
Ahroo! Ah! Rrah!
Hsst! Kaoc!
Grrrah!
I am here to aid you, Ahkahtuz!
This one does not see the vexing shadows along the path now. His hackles can finally lay flat again.
Finally, a decent fight!
The mask is charged, five-claw! Call Nahfahlaar!
The Dragon! Force him down or wait for his return!
That doesn't look good. Grapple-bow out of the way!
Defeating those enemies lit the lanterns by the shrine. Seems like we're on the right path.
Look out!
You deal with the Dragon, I'll take care of the aegis!
No handouts today. Get lost!
You shall not escape!
Where are you, little hunter?
Ah, good. You look like a tough one. I have plenty in stock for an adventurer such as yourself!
All of Elsweyr is abuzz, speaking about your exploits. As a result, I have quite a few furniture offerings for you.
You may not have a house, but I still have furniture to peruse. Perhaps you can help spruce up the sanctum.
We're all lost here. Lost in the dark!
I will deal with you with claw and tail!
Nothing important.
Every journey begins with a single step, but you still have a long way to go. Longer than most, yes?
Time for the harvest!
There must be something that connects these graves to the medallions.
I'm not sure what happened exactly, but Karthwatch was destroyed.
This should keep you busy.
Watch your step!
Enough appetizers. Time for the main course!
I knew these things would come in handy.
A fight? If you insist.
Ha! You have no idea what you're up against.
Dead, eh? Just toss their bones in with the others.
Looking to play a game of chance? If so, avoid the Iron Priest. His games are rigged. Pretty sure he's from Karthwatch, too.
For Karthwatch!
Don't leave me down here. Please.
You're on the right path. Please, hurry.
You're nearly here. I can feel it.
Yes. Just one more leap of faith.
Rise, ancient dead. Rise!
Let's make this quick.
Yes! Your death for a life. My life!
This is where we part company.
Why do you persist?
Your fieldwork went well, I take it? Tell me every detail!
You should speak with the scholar authoring the study. They're much more likely to cite you in their work once you've established a rapport!

There really used to be more people willing to take an unspecified amount of personal risk in the name of academic discovery. Maybe I should study what happened to them?\n\nYou're still here, at least. Can I interest you in a new study?
I'll need some time to organize your findings before submitting them. We are the Coterie of Organized Scholars, after all. \n\nDo come back tomorrow so we can continue our efforts!
Did I overbid that last auction? Ah, well.
Gah!
Block that attack!
Strike back!
Shake it off!
Almost had you!
Interrupt that strike!
Follow up with a heavy attack!
Slaughter them!
That storm … I've never seen anything like it.
Nord scum? Kill them!
Keep an eye out for the bear-woman. Big as an ox, she is!
Time to die!
They'll never take this island away from us. Never.
Icereach for the Reachmen!
A nice warm goat shank. That's what I need.
Trespassers! After them!
Let the Nords come, I say. More blood for the Coven.
Cut them off! Don't let them escape!
Ugh. This ash … my boots are full of it!
Meddling bastards! Put a knife in them!
Oh, you got one of those new grapple bows? Lucky bastard.
On your feet, Draugrkin! Get them!
Bones, bones … it's like a damned kennel in here.
You think you can steal from us?
The one who hired us? I hear even Kjalnar's scared of him!
Intruders! Bury them like the others!
If you die down here, I'll raise you as a thrall!
Look lively, now! Intruders!
Ugh, this place is too damned hot.
Look! More corpses!
Way I hear it, they buried something else down here. Something big.
You should not have strayed from the path, children.
Our true power is limitless! You cannot stop destiny!
Have you brought good news? I tire of Silgrett's judging stares.
Be quick and be victorious. The Swords of Solitude's reputation demands it.

Shor deliver me someone with some spirit! Even a month ago it wouldn't have been this hard to find a few strong Nords to kill what needs killing. Now?\n\nWell, if you have some fight in you, our militia needs it.
There's nothing more for today. Enjoy a moment's peace. It won't last long.
This island is hardly worth our time.
Why fight us when you could join us?
You can't kill what's already dead!
You look especially delicious.
Why wait, little fish? Come, face the shark.
You are trapped. All that remains is the fighting.
You only delay the inevitable.
Dead already? Weak.
Gragh na … pathetic.
Rest easy. I will put your corpses to good use.
We're all lost here. Lost in the dark!
Get out! Get out!
Sanity is an illusion! Be free of it!
Here's a gift! Now pass it on!
Come out, spirits! Come out!
I got potion testing duty tomorrow. Still haven't recovered from the last time!
Was the red one for healing or fire resistance? Wait, this is juice.
Intruders? Intruders!
Got some new test subjects here!
You've wandered down the wrong path, little sheep.
Hah! You are rightly awed! Marvel at my creation!
Surrender now and I'll spare you my most excruciating experiments!
Once again, my unassailable intellect prevails!
I'll be honest, I don't understand a word Vaduroth says.
Let us hope that our control runes for Vaduroth stay in place.
These souls are weak!
Now I can try my new spells!
Sing the void. Pull it out. Arrive.
Well come on then! Feel the power that you could have held!
I'm ready for a meal. Let us begin.
Empty. Flawed. Barely meat. No use for her.
Now you see the power you could have held!
Your blood will fuel my growing power!
Die, fool!

One day, despite what my sister says about any place that's not Solitude, I want to see the Mysterious Mermaid of Anvil statue. Apparently, it was there before the city was even built. Strange, right?

You'd think that someone with my experience in combat and diplomacy would not consistently be talked over when advising others. \n\nEven when I manage to get a word in, I'm ignored. Next thing I know, Rakrek of all people is getting credit for my idea!

A part of me wonders if I chose the right vocation. I enjoy crafting with leather, but it's such a change after years of sailing. On the sea, you know your crew has your back. On land, things feel much more complicated.
Whatever you might have heard, my name's Gell. Hard G. Just had a courier from who-knows-where mispronounce it again. Troll's blood, it's not that hard!

My singing instructor once told me this: You are enough. You don't need to bind yourself to another in Mara's — or anyone else's — eyes to be a complete person.\n\nMaybe she was right. Maybe one day I'll believe it, too.

By all the gods anywhere, what did I do to deserve such a preening, shame-ridden, blame-throwing … gah! Can you believe the man I serve day in and day out just accused me of stealing his pastry? Right after he ate it?\n\nCame here to calm down.
I'm worried about my sister. She's obsessed with a piece of wood. Claims it killed over a hundred Daedra.
We didn't build Solitude on the great arch originally. No, we started near it, letting it shelter us from the winds.
Orkey's an interesting fellow, really, when you get to know him. We shouldn't hold a grudge about that mortality situation.
Orkey's trickery, I hate working days. I just got assigned to Dragon Bridge, and it's always all day shifts when I get there.
Don't know if you've been out to Dragon Bridge yet, but I'm off duty from there. Glorious terrain. Fresh air. Miss it already!
If you're here for the hunting, avoid places marked by three sticks tied with a green ribbon. Those are sacred spots. Only those blessed by the bear may hunt there.
I may have been discredited in the Solitude Mages Guild, but they know nothing about the Khajiit. Housecats are Khajiit! I can prove it!
Just in time! You! You're just in time to hear about my success with my new mountain flower mead! Tried it. Lots of it. So good.\n\nBut maybe I should go home and sleep it off. Too good.
I hate asking, but spare some coin? I was exiled after I chose to liberate some Argonians many, many years ago. I'd make the same choice, but right now? My circumstances are less than ideal.

I can't tell anyone here, but I'm burning up inside. Thaezara is like lightning—exciting, invigorating. Viatrix was like porridge—comforting, but plain.\n\nWhat have I gotten myself into? Oh, forget I said anything.

A student told me that one of the very first Bards College instructors shows up every night as a ghost, singing about his lost love.\n\nNonsense! I'd think he'd be haunting whoever killed him, not pining over some ridiculous lost love.
Have you read the latest mystery story by Yvonna Graymoth? If not, you should! You'll never guess who the killer is! I didn't.

I suspected that I wouldn't find much about Peryite here in Solitude, but I can't leave any location unverified.\n\nSo far? No books, no cultists, no bardic lore. Nothing. I must be missing something.

Ever had mead? I hadn't until I came here.\n\nDon't tell anyone this, but I hate Solitude. Absolutely detest it. But the mead! The mead gets me through it. Don't know what they do to it, but it's liquid magic.
Did you know that the clouds are vapors from the passing of Dwemer air beasts? Someone at the Lonely Troll just told me that! I never knew.
I'd stay back from me, were I you. I tried to make a fungus-based healing unguent using a recipe I found in the Bards College.\n\nI'm seeing smells right now. Makes getting around hard.

My sole duty here in Solitude is to learn the Nord's customs and deliver them back to my elders. Knowing that, would you prevent me from entering the Halls of the Dead? The priest of Arkay there did just that!\n\nI shake my head in disbelief.
You've seen how the Nords mark themselves? I'm here to study that phenomenon. I intend to learn how they showcase their strength and vigor.\n\nIt can be breathtaking, I assure you.

Solitude is a wonderful location to study my passion project: the Sea of Ghosts.\n\nOh, to speak to Yngol and learn more about his death on that sea! And to have discourse with Ysgramor to discover how he tamed those ghosts!
It does the Nords a great disservice to ignore their stone art. So much lore exists in those artfully carved rocks! I already have enough information to write several books!

Why is this one in Solitude? Rathzin asks himself the same question. Dragons in Rimmen and Senchal made this one venture far.\n\nYet, Dragon mounds exist here in Skyrim. Can one ever truly flee Dragons?

I've been here for days now. Someone or something keeps visiting my farm and killing livestock, so I thought the king might send some hunters out to help me track them down.\n\nSo far, no audience allowed. What keeps our king so busy he can't see me?

Can you believe it? My brother, who was accepted by the Bards College last year, is missing! What kind of place is this college if students vanish? Not a good one, I can tell you.\n\nThey're not even going to help me track him down. Hmph.
Can you believe it? Some know-nothing priestess tried to tell me that talking to plants does nothing for them. How wrong can a person be?

The moment I arrived in Solitude, several cats found me. \n\nIs this to be my fate in every single port city I visit? This is the fourth time it's happened! I like the creatures, but this is ridiculous.

You're real, right? I'm not seeing things?\n\nOh, pardon, never mind. Strange and unsettling dreams plague me of late. The ones that leave you drained of all energy in the morning and questioning reality. I'll be fine soon, I'm sure.

Have you ever followed an insect for awhile? Just to see where it goes and what it does? I do that at least once a day.\n\nThese creatures are fascinating! Especially bees. Bees are magical creatures.
I'm happy to be in the land of glorious mead! Even beggars benefit from it here in Solitude. It warms me during the coldest nights.\n\nBut the scowls of these stranger-hating Nords warm me even more!
Ilazun is disappointed in these Solitude Nords. No empathy for one seeking his lost sister.\n\nBaandari this one might be, but Ilazun deserves basic respect even while among these strangers!

All I hear about in Solitude is the Divines. The Divines this, the Divines that. Some even claim the Divines bless their silly superstitions, but I think they'd throttle those spreading them instead.\n\nI stay in the refuge as much as I can.
Whenever I see you, I know that Skyrim is in good hands.
You may feel a burning sensation.
Death was the expected result.
<<battle shout>>
Watch your step!
The ritual grows more perfect every day.
Aren't the new bloodfiends adorable?
I serve the Icereach Coven.
All shall bow before our coven!
May the matron guide you.
I need something to kill.
Has Sister Balra perfected the ritual yet?
Stay alert. The plan has reached a crucial stage.
Isn't the new ritual exhilarating?
Neither the matron nor Sister Balra tolerate failure.
I thirst.
The next prey is mine.
Find your own shadow. This spot is mine.
My fangs for a decent meal!
That witch gave me a look.
Too many ceremonies for my taste.
Tell me the word has been sent.
I smell fresh blood!
My thirst must be sated!
I crave blood!
Activate the constructs!
Kyne's Aegis needs your help! Sea Giants and vampires are everywhere!
There you are, young blood. I have need of you.
I like you, young blood, but you're becoming a bother. I'll holler when we've spotted anymore harrowstorms on the horizon.
Stuhn's grief, young blood, I've told you all I needed, haven't I? If I was in my prime, I'd be halfway to Mor Khazgur by now.
The skies seem clearer to me, though my eyes aren't what they used to be. Report.
One of these days Vund will blow himself up, and us with him.
Vund's methods are foreign, but there's no questioning their effectiveness.
I can't wait to see that bridge turned to rubble.
The bridge is just the start.
The smugglers were resourceful, at least.
The smugglers had to die, they'd outlived their usefulness.
These fools have no idea what's coming.
I feel our power grow.
Vund can dissolve stone, he is capable of anything.
The Reach shall be victorious!
Once the bridge falls, we will make our move.
The Reach will weaken this land.
Breathe deep.
Hmm. No jars in this cart. Let's try another one.
You'll find this invigorating.
Your essence belongs to me!
Mara's mercy! Watch out!
Muffins! Come back!
Who's a good little mammoth? You are!
Fresh hot skeever kabobs! Get your delicious skeever kabobs here!
You mock me? The great Arkasis? I'll show you! I'll show everyone!
I'll have to lick what's left of you out of my fur.
Rrrah! Die prey!
Grah! Die! Die! Die! Die! Die!
This mixture creates blistering heat with no weakening of the stone. Don't let this splash on you! It will contaminate my findings.
No, no. Too much heat dissipation. I must try a higher concentration.
Expunge that flame formula! I've seen enough!
This will freeze it harder than an Atmoran mountain, but it will flow like an avalanche!
I'm barely shivering! It should be colder! But not cold enough to freeze the formula. Hmm.
Begin the thaw! I have more than I need.
Come fools! Throw yourselves upon the sacrificial pyre!
Your struggle is impressive, but you will not starve our ritual.
Another pike falls, but you will soon join it.
So what if the winds die? This storm has served its purpose.
Come! Obey the pact, creature of the Void! Defend our harvest!
I almost feel bad killing someone so puny. Almost.
You came all this way just to die.
You call yourself a warrior?
When we're finished with you, the vampires are next.
Hroag jarn rot! Your meat stinks of fear!
Have you been through here before? Might explain the tracks I've found.
There's plenty of room, if you're looking for a place to rest.
There's not a thing in Skyrim that can scare me.
I have more than bloodknights to deal with you.
Arise my newest creation! Have your first taste of the living!
Stop gawking and assist me you worthless assistants!
Ready to buy furnishings? If not, let me know when you are!
You have that gleam in your eye. Looking to add furnishings to your home?
Lucky you! You're free to dive into battle. Me? I have to sell things to people. Make it worth my time?
Before you do anything else, such as join a Battlegrounds match, you need more gear. Am I right?
It's so nice to be out in the wild with the ones you love.
Thank you. I don't know what I would do if I lost my mother or husband.
Despite what some superstitious Solitude Nord might have told you, I assure you that my goods are worthy of a jarl's attention.
I know I shouldn't be amused, but these Solitude superstitions! Adding salt to bathing water to prevent death by horker? Glad these people put up with my giggling long enough to buy my goods.
Protect your favorite weapons by storing them with us!\n\nBut please, no fish. I can't stomach the smell.
Keep your belongings safe and sound while you explore Haafingar. And if you find any new fish recipes, please do share them with me!
You need more hiding spots for your belongings, don't you? All my bags and packs have secret places to thwart nimble fingers.
Got somewhere to be? Maybe fast? I can help. Better than any other stablemaster you may have dealt with, I'm sure.
Looking for a weapon or shield? If you expect to be cracking horker heads any time soon, there's a spot where, if you hit just right … well, it's messy, but effective.
Ooh! Here to see my shiny rings? One day I hope to make one that changes songs into a magic shield. Can you imagine being a bard with such a ring?
I'm supposed to be far away from here, yet I'm not. Instead, I sell things so that I might one day leave this place. Please consider buying something?
While you're browsing my goods, think about this: adding an eighth dog to my pack of seven.\n\nWondrous idea, isn't it?
Perhaps you'd like to buy something from me while I'm here? I plan to leave … soon.
Interested in exotic wares? I have all manner of goods for sale!\n\nJust, please, keep any horses at a distance. They make it hard for me to breathe.
Have you found the delight that is Solitude brown sauce? It reminds me of licorice worms!\n\nWhile I don't sell that, I do have other wares that might appeal to you!
I saw my ancestor's remains in my dreams, but I only know roughly where they are.
People bring me horker tusks to carve into animals during my off hours, yet I've not seen a horker. Been busy here, selling gear, food, and more.
I've found this part of Tamriel to be filled with people suspicious of outsiders, even merchants like me. I'm sure you've experienced the same.
If you don't see me here selling my guild's goods, I'm usually off climbing trees somewhere. Maybe in another year or so, I'll wander off to a new area for some fresh challenges.
I hope to one day join the ranks of the Bards College, though my pieces still aren't as polished as I'd like.\n\nIn the meantime, my guild has many wonderful things you should own.
Solitude not the place for you right now? We can get you to Dominion, Covenant, and Pact territories.
Sometimes, the wind sounds like screaming at night. Or, at least I think it's the wind. \n\nIt makes my sales out here on the road interesting.
On your way to Solitude, traveler? Then let me show you my wares!
The only reason to cut flowers is to use them in potions or food. Otherwise, please let them grow!
I hear the basement of the Blue Palace has a new ghost! A couple months ago, one of the kitchen staff fell down, hit her head, and died.\n\nOh, but you probably want to buy some armor, don't you?
Some fellow dropped off a book detailing smithing techniques that were used by Dwarves in that one ruin. I'd say it, but the tongue. It tangles.
A Dark Elf brewer told me of a dark ale that causes no hangovers. It's called Percipient Admonitions. Odd name. But if you ever learn how to make it, let me know.
The feel of the wood's grain under my hands … it speaks to me. See if any of my wares speak to you, too.
I offer many excellent items, but they require proper accessories. You can't go wrong with accents of metal.
Those new to Solitude might find people here unwelcoming. My advice: listen and watch. And stop by if you start feeling isolated. You won't be the first to do so.
The temple priests talk about the less fortunate. I've worked hard all my life, but I barely have two coins to clink together.\n\nCare to help an honest vendor out and look at my wares?
I heard a tale about a man and his ghost adventuring companion. Now I kind of want one for my inn! Might keep us company, you know?
I'm working with horker skin to see if I can turn it into a good leather option for lighter armor. It's difficult to say the least. But I'm getting closer!
You ever hear about someone cursed to have draugr follow them? Because I think that's happening to me.\n\nOh. You're probably thinking I should pull myself together and sell clothing. So sorry.
Here to buy? Sell? I'm here to sell! Buy!\n\nOh, that sounded better in my head. No wonder the Bards College didn't take me.
Ever hear of a Solitude soldier getting a sliver of wood stuck in their nail while fighting? No, and you never will as long as they use my weapons.
Let's explore the depths of your fear!
I see a glint in your eyes that tells me you have something for me! Please tell me it's the annoying "No Thieves Allowed" sign from the Lonely Troll! I put a bounty on it yesterday.
Watch the cats. They're always looking for more fish to eat. If you have some, they'll know. Just like I know I can help you with some fishy goods.
I may be new to selling items, but I'm a veteran at the art of, shall we say, re-appropriating goods. The ones I sell are worth buying.
You! Know anyone who can handle my hair properly? Solitude is not a friendly place for outsiders, or well-coiffed hair.\n\nOh, and here's me saying that your goods are safe with me.
This one was pleased to find the refuge, and now this one is even more pleased to be selling her guild's goods from it. Much better than in Solitude proper.
Elsweyr has always sparked my imagination. Can you imagine living among all those Khajiit? Or traveling with the Baandari?
These souls have been bound so long they're like putty in my hands.
Just kill the draugr. They're too hard to control.
I know they're our namesake, but I hate draugr.
I get the feeling these draugr aren't so much trying to kill us as drag us off somewhere.
Why is it we don't let zombies carry the loot again?
I hope the next tomb we rob has more treasure.
Dragons will reign once more.
For the Dragon Cult.
There's power in this place.
Have you lit the flames?
Skyrim will be ours.
I can feel the power of our ancestors.
I feel connected to the Dragon Cult of old.
I'd like to see a Dragon.
These draugr make me uneasy.
We should be honored to share a place with the draugr.
No one will ever find us here.
Dragons will rule the skies once again.
I don't like how the draugr sound.
I've prepared the altar.
Wake, beasts! Fresh meat!
Up, beast. Time to do war!
Come, rime! Come, frost!
Hahl noo rakh!
Kill Yandir's beasts? You pay in blood!

Just got back from a heist over in Windhelm. I really need a bard to follow me around. Someone who can tell tales of my exploits.\n\nI assure you, they're filled with excitement and adventure! Plus a little romance.
Beasts! Fight to the death!

I think that some folk are happier alone. One of the Divines priests even agrees with me. No need for pledging to someone in Mara's name.\n\nAnd don't you start in on the idea that I haven't met the right person yet. I know myself.
Come, old spirit! Yandir calls. You will answer!
Some folk are so dull. Imagine being told that dancing is not appropriate for someone who makes and sells food. Not true!
How did you get in here? Out with you both!
Wouldn't be wise for us to talk.
Don't drag me into your perfidy.
Leave me alone!
No! Your presence tears apart the very Firmament!
Wouldn't be wise for us to talk.
Move away. In fact, flee. Your kind is not welcome.
I've no time for this.
Move away. In fact, flee. Your kind is not welcome.
I can't be seen dealing with the likes of you.
How did you get … never mind! Away with you!
Stay back!
Pardon me!
I can't be seen dealing with the likes of you.
Leave this area now. You are not welcome here.
Remove yourself from my presence straight away.
Pardon me.
I have no desire to speak with you right now.
I can't be seen with you.
Keep your distance, creature, or feel my bite.
Please, I am a fragile egg. I don't want trouble.
I have no desire to speak with you right now.
I can't be seen with you.
You are not welcome here, monster!
Please, I am a fragile egg. I don't want trouble.
Come no closer, beast.
I won't traffic with wanted criminals.
Stay away from me, fiend!
Come no closer, beast.
No, leave me alone.
Leave us in peace, monster!
Go back to your cave, creature!
Stay back, beast. I mean it!
Sorry, friend!
Back! Back, you horrid beast!
Back! Back, you horrid beast!
What manner of creature are you?
Come near and I'll scream.
Beast! Vile thing! You're an affront to Y'ffre's good!
Not interested.
Beast! Vile thing! You're an affront to Y'ffre's good!
I shouldn't be seen talking to you.
It's nothing personal.
I want you gone.
What manner of beast is that?
I shouldn't be seen talking to you.
Get out of my sight, you foul creature!
Shapeshifter! Blasphemer! Curse your kind!
An affront to Y'ffre, that's what you are! Begone from here!
This must be a dream. I'm dreaming this, right?
What would I have to say to you?
A beast? Here? Oh, I've had quite enough of this!
Please, just go.
Your facade hides something monstrous! Monstrous!
What would I have to say to you?
You don't mean to harm me, do you?
Off with you, creature!
You! You're not—? You are! Stendarr protect me!
I'm not talking to you.
Not this again! Is no one what they seem?
Please, creature, just leave me alone!
You don't mean to eat me, do you?
I'm not talking to you.
Go away.
Can't you do this somewhere else?
Almalexia shield me from this creature.
That thing's so ugly it's criminal!
Almalexia shield me from this creature.
Don't hurt me! I taste terrible! I swear!
Stay back, you s'wit.
I want nothing to do with this, so leave me be.
Get away from me, fiend!
Go away! Or else!
Gah! What are you? Guards!
We've got nothing to discuss.
Gah! What are you? Guards!
It'd be bad form if I were seen talking to you.
To Red Mountain with you, creature!
How about you find something else to do?
What in Tribunal's name?
It'd be bad form if I were seen talking to you.
Stay away from this one, monster.
Your presence here is making me uncomfortable.
Don't even think about it.
Go away! Or else!
Horrid thing! May Hircine hunt you down!
I am an upstanding business person… understand!
Horrid thing! May Hircine hunt you down!
Stay away from me!
This one makes a habit of only talking to honest people.
This one says go away.
Watch out! We've got a nasty one here.
Leave now.
This one makes a habit of only talking to honest people.
This one says go away.
I do not like the look of you.
I'll keep to myself, thank you very much.
Agh! Get away from me, you … whatever you are!
Why do monsters always find their way to me?
Be off, creature! Get!
Go away! Please?
Wanted criminals aren't welcome here.
I don't know what you are, and I don't want to find out.
Oblivion take you, creature! Get away from me!
Oblivion take you, creature! Get away from me!
I only talk to honest people.
Please go away.
Shor's bones, what are you?
Stay away from me, creature!
I only talk to honest people.
Please, creature, just stay away from me!
Beasts like you have no place here. No place at all!
Don't eat me, please. I'm stringy!
Nothing to say to you.
What manner of creature are you?
You're drawing too much attention from the guards.
Clear out. I can't talk to you right now.
Nothing to say to you.
Leave this place, beast! Else you'll feel my axe!
You're drawing too much attention from the guards.
Clear out. I can't talk to you right now.
What foul creature gave birth to you?
Gore and glory, foul beast.
Not interested.
Begone, you foul creature!
There's a beast about! Call the Watch!
Gore and glory, foul beast.
You'll leave this place, or you'll taste my steel!
You'll leave this place, or you'll taste my steel!
Go away.
You spit on our laws, I spit on you. Go away!
I cannot be seen talking to you.
The guards are looking for you.
Go with Tava's blessing. Just don't bother me.
You spit on our laws, I spit on you. Go away!
I cannot be seen talking to you.
Please, stay away from me.
A beast such as you cannot be here.
I have nothing to say to you right now.
Be gone, monster! I'm warning you!
Get away from me!
Walk away. Easier for us both.
I have nothing to say to you right now.
Stay away!
Please, creature. Don't kill me!
To the deck! Grahg na! Loose your flames!
Hmm. Incorrect, it seems. Two mountain flowers …. Perhaps there's an order there?
More warriors, conjurer! Now!
Feh. Nords. Makes me sick to share blood with these weaklings.
All praise His Rolliness, the Pastryarch! Join the First Church of the Holy Sweetroll today and taste the glory of this wondrous confection for eternity!
I overheard some folk whispering about witches in the area.\n\nBah. Those witches better watch out. The Pale Lady might not take kindly to them.
The Mages Guild has an unofficial dog competition each year. We'll be at the Solitude Mages Guild next year, and I plan to bring my youngest pup Wagnur. I have high hopes for him.
You'd think that people around here would welcome me!\n\nWith all the hardship they've faced, why wouldn't they show their faith to the gods and ask for some peace?

Did you get the fresh logs? Wait, you're not Sondi. I don't want your logs!\n\nSondi will be back any minute with fresh firewood from the copse outside town. Peddle your accursed dusted products elsewhere!
Grilled horker makes me ill.
A roaring fire sounds nice right now.

It's tricky, isn't it? The lute?\n\nIt looks so simple, but I've been trying for years and I'm not making any coin from playing. The Masters at the Bards College said I wasn't ready. But, how am I supposed to get better if they don't teach me?

Have you come looking for furs? I'm sorry. Already bought. The meat, too. I'm efficient and good at my work. I don't come cheap, and I don't break deals.\n\nBit of advice if you head out to hunt yourself. Watch the mists. Something's in them.
A shame to waste such vigorous blood.

It's not so bad being a soldier. Regular meals. Not many responsibilities. But you've got to take orders. Go where you're told. Fight when you're told.\n\nDon't tell my captain, but part of me wants to wander and live off the land.
Smell this air! It's invigorating, isn't it? I spent decades behind a trading desk, lending money. Now I'm out under the open sky hunting.\n\nAnd if I come home empty-handed, it's still a good day.
What a display! All the life here snuffed out in an instant.
Who'd have thought you could make vampires with witchcraft?
I saw a few survivors. If you could call them that.
This one does not appreciate these harrowfiends hissing at him.
Make sure no one interferes with the witch pikes.
I almost pity these unsuspecting mortals.
You know Skyrim has the largest pike in all of Tamriel?\n\nI been all over. No better place than Hjaalmarch for fishing.

Watch who you sneak up on! You're lucky I didn't put my pick in your throat!\n\nDon't act surprised. There isn't much law around here and people disappear all the time. I don't mean to be one of them.

Please don't find me, I can't be free. Please come find me. Your death haunts me, your death haunts me.\n\nOh, hello! I did not see you there. It is easy to get lost doing the work down here. Digging through the stone doesn't require much thought.
What brought you here, I wonder?\n\nWe all have our reasons for coming to Dusktown. Well, many seek riches. Those who came in search of adventure are far fewer, I suspect.
I never knew such incredible dishes existed! This is what I live for.\n\nNew, exciting food in strange, faraway places. Skyrim is indeed wondrous!

I never pictured myself in a place like this, but here I am!\n\nThere's a lot of work to be done, but I'm no stranger to hard labor. I did not come down here just for a purse full of coins.  Well … not entirely.

Ah, the thrill of combat! Have you been in the battlegrounds yet? I've been training since childhood, but this … this feels right. The glory! The adrenaline!\n\nIt makes me feel alive, but without the politics of war.
There's another skeeving cub!

Welcome to Dusktown, stranger! You're new here too, right?\n\nAs for me, I'm not here to mine or uncover whatever trinkets are buried out there. I'm setting up a simple shop for the laborers to pick up goods they might need.
I'm worried about Dreva. Not like her to go wandering off.
Troll's blood, that was close!
More people going missing every day. I haven't been sleeping much.
Did you see Bargrolor in that last match? No? You missed some incredible moves!\n\nPit Daemons for life, right? They just have that … something! They're so great. I can't wait until the next match!
The Bitterblade Mining Consortium doesn't cower!
Keep an eye on each other, there's no telling what else is down here with us.

You don't look familiar. You're new around here, yeah? I'll tell you everything you need to know.\n\nBut my shh … my shhh … my turn to work is coming up soon. I just need a few more minutes to relax. That's all.

Greetings, traveler. A new face around Dusktown is always welcome.\n\nI provide spiritual guidance to those who might need it.  I am here for the laborers, but if you desire counsel, I will avail myself to you. Just ask.
You challenge Yandir? Ha! Come, then! Come and die!

I'm waiting for a shipment from the surface. I knew it would take longer to get goods down here, but all this secrecy has made it nearly impossible.\n\nTrying to explain that to the miners is a losing venture.
Yandir is too strong? Ha!
What do you think happened to Horold?
So many have gone missing. I wonder who will be next.
I keep leaving a space at the table for Falgryf every night, thinking he's going to come back.
Has anyone else gone missing? Seems like there's one every day.
A challenge? You will burn like the rest!
Drown in shame, little fish!
Is that all these puny Nords have got?
Continue the rites! Breathe life into the flames!

So many problems plague Tamriel these days, stranger. How do I choose which to address?\n\nEverywhere you turn, someone needs help—if it isn't some Daedra causing havoc, it's Dragons, or vampires, or necromancers, or … or … something!
Do you like my armor? Made it myself. My father's a tanner back in Wrothgar. I grew up with the smell of boiling hide in the house. I grew to love it … reminds me of home.\n\nOne day I'll go back.
There aren't many of us here in Dragon Bridge. This was once a busy post, but over the years, more of us have been pulled back to the city proper.

Hm. Might've heard that I'm not offering prayer anymore. Not for Mauloch at least.\n\nI followed Mauloch's way all my life. Don't know if I can anymore. The strict teachings of recent years chill me to my bones.

People wonder why we still guard this old bridge. \n\nI try to … gently remind them that the Dragon Bridge isn't just symbolic. It's a crossroads for the northern region. This area is the first line of defense for Solitude and the neighboring holds.
I can't help you with usual Mage services. This rift between the Overseer and the Chief caused quite a bit of chaos around here that I need to attend to. \n\nBegone!
Let the feast begin!
Make sure no one follows the coven. A few storms have been interfered with already.
Keep an eye out for stragglers fleeing our harrowstorms.
Dragon Bridge is a little quiet for my taste. I want someone to come pick a fight! \n\nThere aren't that many of us here, but that just means more targets for me.
Don't spill any of that new netherroot brew. Nearly passed out from the fumes.
Damn vampires act like they're in charge just because the Ashen Lord's one of them.
Lost signal. Imperfect emergency protocols enganged.

I've served at a lot of posts all over Western Skyrim. This one's definitely the smallest.\n\nA few of my friends used to be stationed here. They told me that this was once quite a busy road. Times have changed, for sure.
I'm here only for as long as it takes to find my wandering mother, but if you want some goods, I'm selling some.
Blech. So many insects here! Yet, I'll ignore them and continue to sell my goods! Even if I have nightmares tonight.
Ach! If you know anyone that needs a reliable place to sleep, send 'em my way. Might be on the floor, but safe is safe.
When my contract's up, I'm going to buy a mansion on Summerset and retire on the beach.
My hands blister any worse, I won't be able to use them.
We keep getting new hires, but I never see that many folk at work.
No one's seen Hedold in days.
Our princess will join our ranks soon.
These tunnel took forever to dig.
I'll be honest, Briarhearts make my skin crawl.
The Icereach Coven's magic is crude, but effective.
These Reachmen smell more like wet-dog than the werewolves.
I would have liked to have seen the Gray Host at the height of their rule.
Leave the Draugrkin to their own devices. They have their uses.
Have you seen a harrowstorm? Gives me chills.
I don't like the harrowed blood. It's bland.
I pledge myself to the Gray Host for the armor alone. I mean, look at me.
I prefer Blackreach to the world above. It feels like where I belong.
Finally, the Reach will rise up!
I don't like the eyes of the fiends. So empty.
The coven unites our clans with purpose.
I pity those who won't experience the glory of a harrowstorm.
All our efforts will soon be rewarded.
How many bodies did we acquire today?
Did you see who Urgala was speaking to?
It won't be long now. The Ashen Lord's plans are nearly complete.
Oof—I need a wash.
Be ready. Sometimes the storms leave a few unharmed.
I won't touch those witch pikes. I don't trust anything made by Reachmen.
Should we kill anyone who's unaffected?
We'll start with remote places like this, but soon the storms will be everywhere.
Harrowfiends only understand one thing: hunger.
They smear something on those pikes before the ritual. Makes me glad I don't need to breathe.
This plan isn't bloody enough.
We'll have our own kingdom soon.
Keep a few alive. Captain has plans for them.
Come on! I'll take all of you at once!
I say we fatten up some horkers on what's left of these Nords.
Thanks for all the loot!
We cannot become complacent. Not now.
We must stay vigilant, especially now.
This does not bode well. We need to be on guard.
Watch the shadows. We should expect trouble.
We must not leave ourselves vulnerable to attack.
Now is the time for caution, not rashness.
The sun will soon set on the kingdoms of Nords.
Mind what you grab for kindling. The spriggans loathe those Nords as we do.
Fir co non madoora. Fir na nog camare!
Feed the mountain to bursting!
I don't think we're the first to camp here. Lots of fresh tracks.
Ah! What is this witchcraft?
I fear no witch!
How'd they get the drop on us?
Allow yourself some rest. The Divines are watching over us.
You put too much stock in rumors that are old wives' tales.
We freeze you to the bone!
Thunder! Glory! Ha!
Lightning child! Fight with me!
Get back!
Fish on, lads!
We'll feed you to the sea!
Our harvest begins!
Continue the offerings!
The exchange is complete!
How? How can you survive the ritual? How can you stand against our storms?
You looking for a fight too? Come on then!
Come on, pit bait! I challenge you!
What are you staring at? Come and face me!
You, come over here. Fight … me.
You're too weak to beat me! I'll crush you!
Retainers, to me!
You there! Help! That pale abomination will kill me!
Stendarr, protect me! I do not want to die at the hands of that monster!
Thank you, stranger! I thought I was dead for sure!
Kyne bless you, stranger!
Oh, I must have drank too much. Thank you, stranger.
You killed them? Thank you, stranger!
Stop, you idiots!
Do it like I showed you, you witless husk!
New lesson — attack!
Are you a brainless idiot? Oh … yes, you are.
Watch me do it!
Change of plans … kill them!
Thank you, friend! You saved me!
Not sharing, are we? How unkind.
Spineless worm! That blood is ours!
This one hungers too.
Dryskin, we feed together.
It's rude not to share.
Am I too late?
Thank you! That was terrifying!
Thank you! I need to be more careful!
Thank you … you saved my life.
Thank you so much! I owe you my life.
Thank you, sera.
Shor's bones! Thank you, stranger!
Mmmm, this one looks delicious.
I just hope the blood's not polluted with mead.
The blood reeks of alcohol, but it will have to do.
A feast! And it's all mine!
Not drunk, I hope. I hate tainted blood.
I feel like gorging myself.
Shor's bones! What's going on here?
What in the nine holds?
Kill anything that moves!
Stand ready!
What in the nine holds is going on down here?
We can't stay down here!
Lorkhan's spit, they keep coming!
Imagine, they almost killed us!
More of you?
This one is glad that is over.
These s'wits don't stop!
These guar tried to kill us!
Are we going to disappear too?
We need to get out of here!
What kind of magic cursed this place?
Stay alert, don't trust your eyes!
By Hircine, there's more!
Well fought, my kin.
Look, another challenger!
We almost died! Now that's a good fight!
Hello, stranger! Welcome to the Whispering Axe. We got mead, mudcrabs, and mattresses. Pick your pleasure!
Nothing beats a troll-hair horse blanket during a cold winter. Thick as marsh mud and the smell keeps their blood pumping hot.
One less filthy monster in the world.
Another one! Kill it!
We got the filthy bloodsucker!
You'll die just like this one, bloodsucker!
Take that, bloodsucker!
Was this your friend? Would you like to join him?
It's dead. Nasty looking bloodsucker.
Another bloodsucker! Bring it down!
What an ugly bloodsucker.
What fortuitous timing! Kill it!
What pitiful, ugly creatures vampires are.
Another of those filthy creatures! Kill it!
Mmm, a dead vampire is a good vampire, no?
We kill this one too, yes?
Filthy creature. This one is glad we killed it.
Another one! Let us kill it!
It does not appear to be moving.
Another vampire … let us kill it.
This one has a stench to it. Let's dispose of it quickly.
Did we kill your friend, vampire?
Mangy beast! Stay down!
Ha! Another challenges us!
Praise Vivec, it is done.
Come to avenge your friend? How pathetic.
It tried to flee, how pitiful.
Two dead werewolves is better than one!
Another werewolf down!
There's another one! Kill it!
It put up such a good fight, I enjoyed making it scream.
Another brute! Let's get it!
What a dreadful beast.
Another beast challenges us!
It is done, yes? We killed it?
Let's make this one suffer, yes?
The beast breathes no more.
We should make this one suffer, no?
The beast is slain … we were successful.
This one looks weaker than the first.
It's almost like they wish to die.
This one will fall, just like the last.
You seek your death as well, traveler?
A visitor? Let's kill them.
This'll be quick.
You're in the wrong place, stranger.
Does this fool not know who we are?
Allow us to grant your death as well.
Ah, perfect. This one was not finished killing yet.
Challenge us, will you?
This one looks weaker than the last, does it not?
If you seek mercy, you will find none here.
The blood runs cold at my approach!
The storm is mine to command!
You wish to see my works? Very well! I will plunge you into deeper darkness!
Come, cattle! Time for the slaughter!
Summon the bloodknights
You had little hope before. Now, you are truly lost.
Stop that! Stop that this instant!
This should incapacitate you.
Damn you!
Father! Why did it have to come to this?
The mist from that sprayer changed. Keep going!
That didn't help.
Greater cowardice would serve you well.
My stock's depleted, but what little I have is yours to browse.
Fair warning—I don't have much to sell. But you can have a look if you like.
Harrowfiends stink of death.
The hour of our triumph draws near.
The harrowed are more troublesome than they're worth.
We need more catgut for our bows.
The experimentation chambers need a cleaning.
More bodies are needed for the ritual.
The harrowstorms are developing nicely.
Bring me more ale to warm my bones.
From here we can push deeper into Nord lands.
Do you have everything prepared?
Each harrowstorm seems angrier than the last.
Finally, the Reach will rise up!
Ours is an alliance of mutual interest, nothing more.
Not knowing the witches ultimate plan unsettles me.
We must be patient. The time draws near.
Harrowfiends are an unexpected byproduct of the storms.
The medallions will protect us.
My legs tire from this standing about.
You are your mother's daughter, I see.
Arise, guardians of the tower!
Feel the power of my harrowstorm!
Drain!
Skin of wheat. Chaff of soul. Sifted.
I'll hold him as long as I can!
Rise up and grind them to dust!
Rise, rise, rise!
You will become ashes!
The feast begins!
Gather up so I can get a tasty look at you!
Suffer!
Let me taste!
There is no escape.
Accept my embrace!
This blood is weak!
Now you're trapped!
Expose your veins, I want a taste.
Spoiler…
You've returned! I trust your venture went well? What news do you have for me?
Watch yourself out there. More than one adventurer has underestimated the dangers of the Reach.
You look like you can handle yourself. Care to explore a bit of the Reach and make some gold along the way?
I still need to consult with my friends in the Reach. I doubt I'll have anything more for you until that happens.\n\nBe safe out there.
You're back and not dead, so I assume you bring good news.
Deal with this problem and you will be rewarded. The vaults of Markarth are full and we have gold to spare. The Stonehands pay their debts.
The Stonehands serve the ard's interests in the Reach, and we only employ those who are worthy. Do you think you have what it takes? There's a fine reward in it from the Markarth vaults if you do.
We don't have any more work for you today. Come back soon.
Bleed!
Intruder.
Arg! If he keeps doing that I'm going to snap my tools off in this lock!
Are you up for a challenge? We need someone to go and deal with the storm-summoners.

I appreciate your lust for battle, but there's nothing to be done until the fools summoning these harrowstorms show themselves again. Go get drunk, find someone to warm your bed, then come back tomorrow to win another victory.

I'm confused. Did you or did you not just agree to put down the villains summoning these harrowstorms? Because it seems like you're standing here talking to me instead of going out and disrupting one of their rituals.
Saw the skies clear some time ago. You do that?
We shall battle for honor!
Just a crate of knickknacks. Nothing important. Keep looking.
Too static! Too static! Needs more randomization!
I made that potion! You think I don't have an antidote?
Beast on the loose!
Have another potion! I'm sure it'll be fine!
You call yourselves soldiers? Inadequate. Again!
The Dark Heart hungers!
Looks like he had quite the set up down here.
All these pipes lead into that chamber he's in. Look for a weak spot.
You've got to do something about those shock-things! Can't you dig them out somehow?
JB TABLE TEST 1
JB TABLE TEST 2
JB TABLE TEST 3
Don't tell the boss, but a little mead helps his potions go down.
Standing guard is the least dangerous job here.
Ho ho! That second dose was a good idea!
Time to earn my keep. I guess.
Feels good to be part of something. Besides a cult, I mean.
I didn't come here to pick mushrooms. I want to work in the laboratory!
Nobody disturbs the great Arkasis!
I'll finally get promoted to the laboratory!
You're pretty good at this!
They locked up a new batch in the basement yesterday.
I look forward to our final march on Skyrim.
Savor these calms, because the bloodshed soon begins.
Does it ever feel like the gargoyles are watching you?
We hunt them, we find them. They never see us.
I had a perfect shot, right between the eyes.
They mock us. Despise us.
How dare you breach the Lady's home?
Have you seen Tara the Nimble, the tavern dancer? She would be happy to come over for—er, book club. Yes. Book club.
My blade has a bite!
Our army shall rise!
These shall be the first to fall!
This one has never stolen a thing in his life, no matter what else you may have heard.
People say you should never mix hard liquor and beer, but—hrng, ugh—it's wine and fur that are real trouble. Ulp ….\n\nWhich way to the little Khajiit's room?
A poison blade for your guts!
I'll aim straight for the heart!
Time to even the odds!

There's perfectly good food and drink going to waste in the pantry. It could be better used to show guests some hospitality. Guests like me.\n\nNot anyone else who might be hanging around, though. All for me.

Mmm. Not so loud. Use the itty-bitty voice if you must. I've had, perhaps, three bottles too many. Now it feels like broken glass between my ears. \n\nOne day, I will create a spell to deal with this. Then the gold will roll in!
What's the point of building great houses for your gods? Do people really think the gods can't hear them if they don't pray inside a stone building?\n\nWaste of good stone, I say.

I am a practicing adherent of what most of Tamriel considers anathema. Yes, I am a follower of a Daedric Prince. Multiple Princes, to be precise. I hope that won't be a problem for you.\n\nAnd if it is, well, then pretend I haven't said anything.
Hail.
Oh, I am so disorganized! I could use an assistant to help me catalog all my books and letters.\n\nAny chance you're avail—no, no, forget I mentioned it.
I'm afraid I depleted my supply of paper and ink. And also quill tips. And sealing wax.\n\nBring some with you the next time you visit, please. A historian is nothing without the tools of her trade.
Hello there.
Greetings.
Pathetic!
Nipping rats!
Graaah!
[sniffs the air then gives a satisfied babble]
[suspicious Goblin babble indicating she heard something]
[fast, manic gibbering]
[sinister Goblin cackle to taunt her enemy]
While you wait, the fires burn all around us!
Witnesses, all! You cannot be allowed to leave!
The True-Sworn never fail their mission!
Now burn, like the rest!
<<Light coughing.>>
<<Light coughing.>>
Welcome, new slaves! Breaking you will be my pleasure.
My plans, ash!
Not even strong enough for a pickaxe!
Ah, perhaps this shall please my lord.
Good! That should slow the effects!
No! Hit them, you buffoon!
Protect me, Dread Lord!
Careful, they're delicate.
Well done.
Perfect.
Got to admit—when I saved a Reach maid from Nords years ago, never thought I'd end up smithing here.\n\nCare to see what they find useful?
A house of stone's a cold, hard place. But the right bit of woodwork, aye, that can make it into a home.\n\nWhat can I do for you?
Can you believe it? Some Timbercrow clanfolk made dolls from my goods. What evil do they plan? Probably catching souls with them … such wicked work.
Ah, yes, I believe I see someone who would vastly appreciate my skills! Yes, that's you! While my techniques are in high demand around here, I can certainly make time for you.
Pilbira saved the Twisted Briar's chief from a Spiritdancer raid years ago—killed them all by fortuitous accident. Probably why this one's hide is still attached, yes?
I promise my produce is extra clean! I washed it all five times before setting up this morning.

The Reach is a dangerous land for a traveler in the best of times, and doubly so these days. My wares might be all that stand in between you and a bad end under a werewolf's claws or a wilder's blade.
I've plenty to buy if you're looking to augment your gear. If you seek to join my martial lessons to the Reachfolk, though, I'm afraid my classes are full.
I don't know what it is about Markarth, but the worms here … fragrant and spicy! I add them to several of my brews to give them an extra kick.
Do you happen to know if Imperial Stuffed Piglet is piglet stuffed with Imperials?\n\nHeh, a little Reach humor for you, freehand. You'll want provisions if you're heading into the wilds.
I make a point of minding my manners around witches. The last thing I need is a hex on my house. Bad dreams for my guests? Soured ale? No thank you.
Not going to ask me about the writ-scratches on my signs, are you? Honestly, if not for Ard Caddach's laws, I'd be reduced to grunting my prices at customers.
Use only the purest water when quenching steel. You want your blades hard, not weak like some who think blessed oils add a god's favor to the weapon. Some clans, I swear!
True Reachfolk put their trust in wood and bone, not iron dug out of the ground. The forest provides you all the protection you'll need in these lands. Staves, bows, shields—mine are the best.
Markarth takes some getting used to. My family came through by way of Cyrodiil during the Longhouse times. Glad I'm here and not in the middle of that war.
Word of advice: Don't crowd the clan folk of the Reach. Especially the ones new to Markarth. It's an invitation to enjoying a dagger prick.
The cider here beats any I've found elsewhere, including my home town of Daggerfall! Truly exceptional. Not sure how they manage it.
I never thought I'd stay in Markarth, but I can't bring myself to leave. Like the Reachmen say, you've got to listen to the spirits.\n\nNow, I think I hear the spirits telling you to buy something!
Looking for a safe place for your sundries? Can't say as I blame you. The Reach is an unforgiving place.
I never pictured myself as a banker, but counting buck antlers and sabre cat skins is the safest profession around.\n\nNow, then. What can I do for you?
Say, did a dancing light lead you to Markarth? And did the Skyweaver clan greet you like they were expecting you?\n\nThe Reach is an odd place.

Keep an eye on the locals. The clan I traveled here with chased off another band that picked a fight on the road. Then the troublemakers showed up here a few days later.\n\nThey might not have learned their lesson yet.
I'm used to seeing Reachfolk tame all sorts of creatures for riding, but I've never seen such a strange menagerie of beasties in one place as has been collected here.
Ah, my friend! Shall I dance for you? I would play, too, but I had to sell my instruments just to make it here to wonderful Markarth!
Did you know that Markarth was originally called Nchuand-Zel? Sorry. I'm just eager to share my discoveries!\n\nBut you wish for goods, not trivia, I think.
Got a job you need doing? Gonna have to wait until I help out the Timbercrows. Might be awhile.
The will of the Hist sent me here. One day, I will discover why.\n\nFor now, I tend to my wares and my customers.
Always heard the terrible reputation Reachfolk carry was a bunch of Nord codswallop. I see some of where that came from, sure.\n\nLet's get out of here, yeah?
A wilder can hardly breathe in this great stone tomb. I'm this close to just leaving and heading back to my forest. I don't care what's out there.
You don't want to get banged on your skull, lose your memory, and end up here, right? I certainly didn't. So, wear a helm or something. Always. Maybe I have one for you.
Have you met Ard Caddach? He reminds me of a giant bear, he does. A clever one, to be sure, but a bear nonetheless.
The Reachmen seem very cold, but they dance well and often. I do miss the tones of the vossa-satl, though. No matter.\n\nWhich of my goods will bring you joy?
You're not the person who drank cider out of everyone's boots a few weeks ago, right? Sorry! Just have a thing for gossip, you know?\n\nWhat can I get you?
Looking for a quick one?\n\nBlades, of course. I might have what you need!
What are you looking for, traveler? Markarth's a long way from anywhere, but many strange and interesting goods fetch up here. My guild can help you find them.
You cold? Agh. Never mind. Everyone else seems to be fine. You're probably fine, too.\n\nSpeaking of fine, I have some goods that are. Fine, that is.
Markarth's really something, eh? As a Wood Elf, I really admire the decor!\n\nBut enough about that! Alchemy! What can I get you?
Look at this place! So much slippery stone. Yet not enough warmth.\n\nAh, but you seek a place to handle some hot items, yes?
You weren't followed, were you? Last thing I need is a band of Reachmen trying to steal from me what you stole from them!
I put all sorts of items up for sale, friend! Why don't you take—not now, sis ….\n\nSorry. Why don't you take a look?
This place is fancy for a refuge, isn't it? Beats freezing your arse off in a Skyrim sewer, I'll tell you that!

I used to have a voice like an Elven troubador, but a life of screaming and hollering knocked it right out of my throat.\n\nMoral of the story? Buy some of my goods and let the others do the screaming.
Ah! A fellow traveler! You might want to stock up before heading off. I'm hearing rumors of vampires, werewolves, and even Daedra about.
All kinds of strange items come from Dwarven ruins. Sometimes those just leaving one complain about having to leave things behind! Staggering under their weight, they are!

Greetings, stranger. How dangerous were the roads that brought you here? Would a traveler on her own stand a chance of slipping past the monsters beyond the walls?\n\nI just can't stay in Markarth any longer.
Any greenery you see around here of late comes from the efforts of me and my friend from the Mistrunner clan. Though, I don't know that she intends to stay here much longer, vampire threat or no.

These Reachfolk are curious. I wasn't originally happy with my assignment here, but to make the best of it, I'm recording the various clans and their alliances.\n\nTo be blunt, these people are a mess. I redo my charts each day.
The non-Daedric clans of the Reach possess some interesting magic. I intend to learn as much as I can while here.\n\nPreferably without causing bloodshed.

When survival is at stake, you shape your character. When you make deadly mistakes, you sit with them to learn or you ignore them and warp your character.\n\nSuch are the beliefs of the Shunned Ones, a clan consisting of the cast-offs of other clans.
It would have been nice if that Tharn told me what to expect when I got here, but then again, that family isn't one to volunteer information.
Some say the stone here is dead, but how can you not look at this place and see it lives?\n\nThe people here send life reverberating through the rocky bones of Markarth, pure and simple.
Bells, chimes, gongs—anything you strike to sound a note draws the spirits' notice. Never sound something of that sort unless you know which spirits you're likely to call.
Not nearly enough Malacath worshipers here in Markarth. I aim to change that!
It is not this one's fault that skooma caused many warriors to improperly defend their clan, despite what you might have heard.
Someday I mean to follow the Karth River all the way to the sea. I've never seen the sea, but I've a yearning to look on it. Wouldn't that be a story to tell my grandchildren?

In the wilds, all the sounds flow at random. Nothing to get stuck in your skull like the noise here in Markarth. I'm about to go nutty-off-my-arse because of the nightly drummings and all manner of Dwarf-things clanking and rattling!

Some of these Reachfolk are so thick-skulled. I understand they've gotten along just fine without writing anything down, but if an entire clan dies, so does its lore and customs!\n\nDon't they understand that writing all that down lets them live on?

My aunt came out here to help the Reachfolk with their written records—and she told me so much about the stonework that I had to come out here myself. Magnificent, isn't it? Not me, I mean. The architecture here!
Some clans here in Markarth actively worship and call upon Daedric Princes, so keep the spines of caution raised.
Struck by my beard, are you? I've watered it with the blood of my enemies, waxed it with the grease of rabid mammoths, and combed it with the bones of betrayers. What do you say to that?
I do miss the tall trees my clan once wandered under. Being under a canopy of leaves on trails worn only by deer? Bliss, my friend. Pure bliss.
I love the exhaustion that comes when you've put in a hard day's work. \n\nEven better? Waking up the next day with that bone-deep ache.
What a waste of time writing is. What purpose does it serve? Are thinblood memories so bad that they can't just tell their stories? Maybe it's all just nonsense. A cruel trick played on us.
The Crow-Eye have been through a lot. Some of them might not be kind to an outsider. Don't judge us too harshly. All we have ever known is curled fists and sharp teeth.

I was part of another clan before this. I was out in the woods hunting when some reekers came in and massacred them all.\n\nI promised myself I would never let that happen again. I'll protect every member of the Crow-Eye to my last breath.

Sorry if I was staring, outlander. I thought for a second … but no.\n\nLast winter I crossed spears with a wandering hero who happened to be passing through a Nord village my clan raided. Thought you might be an old foe, but no quarrel here.
Hoooooo! Hooo-hooooooooo!\n\nThat's the sound the owls around here make. Well, at least as best as I can imitate them, which, sad to say, isn't well.

Quite a few Reachmen in Markarth know their letters. Here, I seem to be the only one. My fellow rebels bring every scrap of paper to me in case it's important.\n\nSuch is my fate for making enemies in Markarth. Ah, well. I like it out here better.

You won't catch me near the haunted stones of Markarth. And Ard Caddach? A true despot, just as the foreigners say.\n\nI'll face what's out here on my feet instead of kneeling to a would-be king behind stone walls.
My clan, the Deathwings, reveres the cycle of life and death. \n\nDeath informs every piece of art I create.

It's one thing to gather together among these stones for protection. It's entirely another to watch as some of our customs are swallowed whole in this shared space.\n\nI fear that none of the clans will be the same after this.
The Timbercrow clan does not eat crows. That's not where they get their name from!\n\nI need to track down who's spreading gossip and falsehoods.

So far, since coming to Markarth, various clans want to talk to me. I can't count the number of moots I've barely stayed awake in.\n\nI know that my experience among many now-dead clans is useful, but these moots might just kill me.
Ah, a fellow traveler. Care for story?

You'd not think that an actual caravan would make its way to the Reach, but you'd be wrong. One day, I might even tell the tale of how I ended up in that caravan, too, but I need a lot more mead before I consider it.
What was that? Did you see a Scamp over there?\n\nNo, you didn't, did you? Things haunt my dreams after I got stuck as a captive in one of these Reach clans.
I heard that chipmunks abound in the Reach! I'm here to learn from them.\n\nAnd maybe teach them a thing or two.

You know that feeling you get when someone tells you that if you don't do something they want, you're evil in some way? But to do it would actually diminish you intolerably?\n\nThat was my every waking moment back in Morrowind.
Your brittle bones are only fit for pups to chew.
Another brilliant success for Arkasis!
Good work.
Fiery winds, sear their flesh into coals!
Creatures of flame, rend them limb from limb!
Brimstone serpents, scour the earth!
No! I must not fail!
Blast it from history!
My heart's fire forges this blade!
Strike them down!

Have you been back to the Stitches recently? Tasnasi is really turning that place around. I even saw her smile once. I think it was a smile. I guess it could have been a frown. I was lying on my back at the time, so everything was upside down.
You were there. You know what it's like. The Stitches. If I never see that place again, it will be too soon. I've barfed in better gutters than that. I do have my pride, you know.

You completed the training? That's … wonderful. I'm still not qualified for most fieldwork. Oh, I have the requisite knowledge. It's the courage that's lacking.\n\nYou can measure my bravery with a small spoon and still have room for pudding.
Ah, always good to meet another … scholar. You know, a scholar, yes? And by scholar, Biro means a comrade in the Thieves Guild. But we should never mention that name.

Svargrim. I hear you were the one who took care of that particular problem. Good riddance, I say. He was no friend to the Reachfolk and I won't shed a tear for that tyrant.\n\nI expect you won't, either.
So we just keep looking forever?
You shall taste ashes!
Do you think we will get back by dinner?
Glory to the flame!
Up there. Try concentrating on that pocket of energy.
Use the portal. Get out of there!

Stand up straight. You're in the presence of royalty.\n\nI am Prince Irnskar, heir to the throne of Windhelm and Eastern Skyrim. It's a great honor to have someone of my rank and station as a houseguest.
You there! Where are the servants? I'm in desperate need of libation and no one comes when I call.
The Gray Host has finally been vanquished. Thanks to you. You are a remarkable individual, champion. All of Skyrim owes you a debt. I won't forget that.

I pray to never lose hope as High King Svargrim did. Once, he was a strong ruler who cared for his people. Until the corruption set in.\n\nAt least you were able to stop him before Solitude fell. We owe you for that.
Champion, good to see you, my friend! You made my father's Konunleikar one to remember. Windhelm will be talking about it for years to come!
This one is a vampire, yes. Oh, do not get your tail all twisted. Adusa is not that kind of vampire. I only feed on willing subjects, and never to excess. This one has good table manners, yes?
We are both vampires, five-claw, and by the blood, we decide what that means.\n\nAdusa hopes you walk the same path as the Ravenwatch. I would hate to find out that was not the case.
Five-claw! This one is glad to see a familiar face from Rivenspire. The province would have been lost without your timely assistance.
In all her years, Adusa-daro has never faced an enemy like the Gray Host. This one never expected an ancient army of vampires and werewolves to return from the dead!
At long last, the threat of Rada al-Saran and the Gray Host is over. Thanks to you, five-claw.\n\nKnow this. The Ravenwatch owes you. And the Ravenwatch always pays its debts.
What are you looking at? Ain't you never seen an Undaunted Reachman before? I'm not a dancing bear, so close your gape, go piddle in the corner, and fetch me a beer!

Tried to sail to Yokuda once. A slaughterfish the size of a leviathan swallowed my boat. Nearly starved before I found a Sea Sload stuck in its guts. Ate like a king and had enough left to fashion a raft and sail out when the great fish … belched.
Don't know what sorry skald-kisser thought up the Undaunted initiation, but if you can survive an assault of witless dobbers howling like durzogs in heat, you can survive anything.
Milksop this, milksop that. Turuk's claws are sharp, but his head is full of soggy bread.

Who's a high and mighty Undaunted now? Welcome to the elite level, milord! Shall I wash your fancy britches for you?\n\nBah! Come back and see me when you're ready to wrestle a pit full of lurchers in nothing but bare skin as nature intended!
I'll need more souls to cage Rada again! Continue to slay the Gray Host!
I just need one more drop ….
No living thing may pass.
I don't want to become one of the crawlers.
Lady Belain says we will be restored.
I long for the touch of the Void.
Once, the Reach feared the night.
Why do I feel so empty?
We have been weak for too long.
Going somewhere? I'll wait here for you to return.
I didn't even want to come to this stone pile of a city. It's not natural for Reachfolk to live like this.
Pryner complaining, is he? Aye, he does that a lot. Doesn't mean half of it.
Use the portals to escape!
I didn't want to come to this city. But now that I'm here, I have to say I appreciate good shelter and a warm fire at night.
This is my fault. I begged my father to come to Markarth for his safety. Spirits curse me!
I met Ard Caddach a few times. I like what he's trying to do here.
First time I met Ard Caddach, I got so nervous I dropped my blade. Some impression I made, eh?
Honestly, I thought this Ard Caddach wouldn't care if we went in and studied the Dwarven ruins here. But they wouldn't even let us into the first room!
I had more interest in exploring the Reach than I had in being stuck inside an old Dwarven mausoleum. \n\nI wish I'd thought more about this before I signed up.
My wife told me to make sure to buy warmer clothing on my way here. I really wish I had listened to her.
I hadn't planned on hiring on to guard a pair of outsiders, but it's been an interesting job.
You probably want to talk to my brother, Tahzim. He's the one in charge.
Came to this place ten days ago but I can't find honest work.
You going to ask me why I'm like this? Sod off then. I like my ale.
The effort put into digging these tunnels. The Dark Heart was clearly vital to the Nighthollow clan's power.
Summers in Skyrim are just like the winters, but instead of snow piled above your head, it just comes up to your shoulders.\n\nYes, I'm exaggerating. Slightly.
Enough of your pointless defiance!
