Look at this flotsam.
I'll snap you like driftwood.
Sorry bunch of landfolk wandered up from the arena!
Let'em be, for now, but if they start anything: gut'em.
Watch yourself, drysole, and keep your weapons at your side.
Surprised to find an Altmer cozying up to Maormer? Well, the enemy of my enemy is my friend, and I'm not exactly welcome back home.
I wouldn't say I like dealing with Maormer, but the Fleet Queen has big plans for the Systres and I don't want to be left behind.
Taleria knows how to treat a guest! This one hasn't had good moon sugar since she started sailing these waters.
Hmph.
So, how did you do it? <<1>>, I mean. Knife across the throat? Or in the belly?\n\nDid you boil his blood or freeze it in his veins?
I hear they've fed one monster of a shark down in the reef. Careful, or Taleria will feed you to it.
This is neutral ground. I aim to respect that even if you weren't invited by the queen. No fighting, no problem.
Our guardian hides its red heart ….
Our beast, it called bolts from the sky ….
Now go, oh me hearties so grim ….
That last sacrifice sure liked to scream.
I can feel the tide going out.
I'm tired of waiting!
I just want to poke holes in the sea elves before we sacrifice them!
I could've made a better bridge between the cliffs.
The outsider's time in power will end.
If we cull the outsiders, there's no need for the coral.
We should be in charge!
Really? My bests can't have just one of the prisoners?
How will we trap the next sacrifices?
Drown the unworthy!
I feel like something's staring at me.
Don't drift off.
Nobles. Pah! What do they know?
There's nothing here.
I've never seen the coral feed before!
You strike me as a worthy challenger. Care for a game of Tribute?
The Gonfalon Chapter's greatest cardsharp, is it? Good! I always seek to play the best!
No one can stop the Eldertide!
Fancy a match? I always preferred dice, but this Tales of Tribute really is addictive!
Hmm. I think I've heard of you. Gonfalon Chapter, right? Let's put those rumors to the test.
Looking for a Tribute match, right? Sit down. I'll teach you a thing or two.
If you want to rise in the rankings, you've got to play the best. Lucky you. The best is sitting right here.
You wish to challenge me to a game of Tribute? I warn you—my deck has few flaws, and my luck is ample.
Your legend grows, hero of Gonfalon Bay. Sit, and let me take the true measure of your skill.
Greetings, cerum. I've got a fresh deck and nowhere to be. Let's have a match, eh?
A fellow contender, eh? You don't make it this high in the rankings by dumb luck. Let's put ourselves to the test, shall we?
It's a Tribute match you're after, right? Well sit on down. Let's get to it!
I learned to play from the best! Well … not the best, but they were pretty good. Middling, I suppose. All right, they were terrible, but who cares. Let's play.
Vivec himself couldn't craft a deck as good as this! You haven't got a chance.
We've both got places to be, I'm sure. So, shuffle those cards and get on with it.
You do not need to twist this one's tail, walker. There is always time for Tribute!
Finally, this one can match claws with a true cardsharp! Come, walker. Shuffle and deal.
My boredom sac is engorged. Do you wish to play Tribute or not?
My roots in Tribute grow deep and strong. If you chose to face me, do not expect a victory.
You a milk-drinker or a Tribute titan? I'm itching to find out!
Tribute, eh? Well, let's make this quick, because I am parched!
Hmm. I was led to believe several royals might be here today. I suppose there's been some sort of delay.
How typical of the Duforts. Rather than address a serious problem, they put appearances first and carry on as if nothing's wrong. What a farce!
Huh. You look a little out of place here. Sir Moric Girarde, at your service.
A pleasure to meet you. This one is called Nadari-dra. Rarely has she found herself in such a gathering of wealth. But then Nadari-dra's business ventures in the Systres are proving most profitable.

You don't look like one of High Isle's grandees—you must be here for the conference.\n\nI came with the Aldmeri Dominion's advance delegation. But without Queen Ayrenn, I wonder if there's any point to holding the talks at all.
Attack, my pets! Sink your fangs into these fools!
Feed on the blessings of Satakal, my scaly pets.
I'll enjoy teaching you the error of your ways!
Bah. Weaklings, all of them.
For the Magus and the Lord!
Brother, do you hear that?
With the coral, our power will be unstoppable!
The old hierarchy is dying. It's up to us to replace it with something better.
The alliances are folly. Systems designed to turn nation against nation.
The people are misled. We can do something about that.
Be ready. We don't know what lies in wait.
The Magus says our victory is at hand!
Once the land's free of titles, all will be equal.
Down with the nobility! Through the Order, all will be made equal.
I met the Ascendant Lord once. Now there's a leader with vision.
Have faith. People everywhere will thank us when our work is done.
Yes, I once fought for the Covenant. But now I know who my true enemies are.
These islands are warm, yes. But still I miss Black Marsh.
I'm starving. I would kill for some nice fat echatere jerky.
I'll summon a gale to push a few more ships into the shoals today.
I could be the next Dreadsail Fleet Queen. Wipe that smirk off your face!
They ain't Dreadsail Reef, but the Systres will make a decent hideaway.
I already miss the sway of the ocean beneath my feet.
Look at all the wrecks around. Not a single sailor in Tamriel worth a damn.
Don't kill off any shipwreck survivors. Easiest thralls you can catch when they're half-drowned.
You got a skeever problem on your ship? If I find one more in the bilge I'm mutinying.
That haul from Shipwright's Regret really paid off. Those lodestones have us running circles around the dryheels.
I have the cutest adder in the fleet. Admit it.
You're going to wind up with viper fangs in your backside if you don't watch it.
These outsiders must pay for their intrusion.
Someone must protect these lands.
Pirates, foreigners, despoilers? Enough, I say.
Y'ffre guides us. Let us cleanse this land!
The spirit of the storm will sweep away the unworthy.
Pirates befoul our oceans while Tamsfolk invade our lands. Unforgivable.
Nature provides for all of us, yet these fools defile it?
Be still. You cannot hear Y'ffre when you fill the air with words.
Do you hear that? That is the song of Y'ffre. He thanks us.
Draigh! I think I forgot to bank my cookfire.
Y'ffre's power is stirring. The earth is angry.
The Stonelore Circle? Bah! They are fools. We do not compromise.
I heard the boss struck up a deal with someone…
Once we get paid I'll finally have enough to buy that armor I've been wanting.
Soon we'll control all of Amenos.
Keep the ornaugs away from those poison traps.
I hate the smell of the sea… and it's everywhere!
I love the smell of the sea.
I said discreetly.
I miss the pirate's life.
The boss says the whole island is going to be ours soon.
I supplied warships all around Sentinel before coming to the Systres. A little combat won't rattle me.

When I was assigned to the Dufort flagship, I thought it would be a safe, prestigious position. Now we're charging straight into the sea viper's nest!\n\nWell, make your final preparations. Hopefully not too final ….
It doesn't seem like the Hadolids made homes here yet. Maybe they'll be more likely to leave.
Dress your kills quickly if you take them down by the waters. The ornaugs like to sneak them away if you leave them unattended. Or so the locals tell me.
I thought I'd gotten too used to the ship when I first landed on High Isle. Turns out the land itself likes to growl a warning to those living on it.
You look busy enough. Just keep your eyes on the skies and the land—both are dangerous to those not paying full attention to their surroundings.
Have you heard? Druid Audrine and a brave adventurer saved our grove! And they made Audrine an elder! How exciting!

Have you come to give honor to the sacred vents, stranger? These manifestations of the island's fiery heart reveal the majesty and power of the natural order.\n\nThe sight always leaves me without words.

This one must do her part. The spirit of the grove needs our help to restore the natural order and wipe out the lingering corruption.\n\nSo Adhahara supplicates as often as possible. For the good of the grove.
Watch yourself, stranger. I'm keeping my eye on you.
I love hunting in Stonelore Grove. The serenity, the abundance of wildlife. And the druids are especially welcoming. Just so long as I show respect and never take more than I can use.

What? Do you assume that only Bretons can be druids? Hardly. The Stonelore Circle takes in any and all aspirants who seek to follow the True Way. Some of us have come a great distance to be a part of this community.
Only the most promising squires of the Oaken Order are sent to study with the Stonelore Druids. It's a great honor and I plan to learn as much as possible during my time here.
You have done a great service, not only for our grove but for all of High Isle. May Y'ffre guide your steps, friend.

The druids of Stonelore Grove belong to a circle of druids who believe that every faith has a place in the Systres Archipelago.\n\nOurs may be the True Way, but we would never try to dissuade anyone from following their own convictions.
The dice love me. Well, everybody loves me. I'm extremely lovable!

I am a second cousin to Duke Mornard, on his mother's side. For that, I got this wonderful posting to the back end of nowhere. Be glad you aren't a noble, adventurer. It isn't all wine and roses—especially if you aren't high up on the family tree.
That's right, citizen. You're talking to an actual knight of House Mornard! Try not to get any of your dust on my boots, if you please.
A day of hard work makes me very happy! Nothing beats a job well done!
The challenge of this tiny island called to me, stranger. Now I keep the overseer safe while he makes the banished prisoners labor in his mine.\n\nNot exactly the type of test I was hoping for.

The waters around Amenos are treacherous, my friend. The only safe and reliable port is right here in Amenos Station. You'd have to be braver or more foolhardy than me to try to navigate to any other part of the island.

Let's pretend I never saw you. That way, whether you're a prisoner who slipped out of the stockade or a citizen wandering where you're not supposed to, I don't have to fill out any paperwork.\n\nJust get out of my sight. Now.
I came all this way to get my brother out of the prison stockade, but I was too late. He was already banished. So now I'm getting drunk before I go back to explain things to our parents.
Oh. Hi. Um, what am I doing? Oh, nothing Daedric I assure you. I'm just … decorating! Yes, that's it. Just sprucing up this little section of Amenos Station.
Dust. This damn island has an endless supply of the stuff.
Some gold for a poor beggar? Give or not. But if I starve, it'll be on your conscience.
This one builds things for the prison stockade. Chains, manacles, tables. Whatever the jailers ask for. \n\nRight now? No, this one is on a break.
Not now. Can't you see I'm losing? I need to concentrate!
Woodworking. It may not be as glamorous as being a knight or a sailor, but it pays the bills. And I rarely have to worry about someone swinging a sword at me or drowning, so there is that.
I swear, you make one crack about the shape of the ice sculptures. And here I am. Docks duty.
Is it just me or are the aspirants this year much, much more attractive than last time out?
We've got another half-dozen ships coming in, next day alone. Going to be a long week.
I say, do you think that Langley fellow is any good? I've put up quite a good deal of money to sponsor him. Hmm.
Master Lanarde has entrusted me with … well. It's quite a long list here. I'm sure I'll get it all done in time.
Hah, you here for the tourney as well? Course you are. Just … helping out the family business, you know. Are you in textiles?
Lots of knights come in here. I try to keep the place looking nice for them. My brother wanted to be a knight. Maybe that would have ended better for him.
Ho, there. If you're looking for a drink, you won't find  a better place than the Ancient Anchor. Just be mindful of your pockets in there.

You lost? Naw, you don't look lost. Can't help but wonder why you're out here talking to me, though. If you're looking to work on the docks, you'll have to talk to my employer. \n\nYou look like you could handle it.

This place has the best drink anywhere in Gonfalon Bay. Quite roomy, too, although I'm sure you've already noticed that. Say what you will about the dirty business that goes on here, but all things considered, it's a good spot to be.
Care to join me? I could use a partner.
I was just telling my friend here that Gonfalon Bay isn't a place for pessimism! How can anyone be glum in this magnificence? You understand, I know you do!
The rest of Tamriel can leave me be. I've got this soup, and that's all I care about. You see enough battle and a warm, full belly becomes all the happiness in the world.
Can't talk, have to count carrots. Five … or was that six? Draigh!
Keep moving, stranger. There's a lot of full pockets in this place and I plan to lighten them. Don't need anyone drawing attention to me.

Druids, a volcano, stuffy knights every which way you look and nobles who will sneer at you if you're bleedin' in the street … I can't figure what's so great about this place. I wouldn't be here if I had a choice.
Good fish around these parts if you've got the patience to wait for 'em. Waters are fairly temperate, so there's a lot of variety. And if you can't eat it, you can sell it.
The ladies Iameesh and Hizjoahna require much of my time.
The rest of Tamriel seems so far away from here, doesn't it? All the echoes of war … I can still hear them, but they're softer now.\n\nHmm? Oh, don't mind me. I'm just thinking aloud.
Mmm, better be careful with your possessions around these parts. These docks are known to eat coin like they eat bird droppings.
This one is looking for a druid. Perhaps you have seen them? One would think they would seem out of place here, but even still, this one's quarry eludes him.

This one had the distinct displeasure of running into a filthy peasant the other night in this very area. The poor thing groveled for my coin, even asked for my jewelry! The brashness. This one was almost impressed.

I'm here studying the local flora and fauna. The temperature of the islands is quite unique, it facilitates all sorts of strange and beautiful things. I've learned so much and I've only been here a few months!

My sister is a Knight of the Iron Knot. When she was a squire, I thought she'd die from the challenges. I suppose I understand, they only want the best of the best and have to weed out everyone else. But still, I worried for her.
A Wood Elf sailor taught me how to do this. I'm going to beat her record before she docks here again!
That temple priest doesn't approve of these statues. But what does she know, eh?
I cannot be bribed for my lady's secrets. My loyalty lies with the greatest mind in Gonfalon Bay.
Took sick just the once that last voyage. Something to celebrate, eh?
Even on a hot day, cold winds blow off the water.
I sit out here to watch the sea birds. They're fascinating!
There won't be meat enough for us common folk with all those gadabouts making port.
Statues? Pah! As if the gods favor those over a temple.
I apprenticed for a noble years ago when I first came to Gonfalon Bay. Somehow that man managed to never get his hands dirty, even working with metal and grease and fire. Astounds me to this day.
I got seven skips on that last rock! I wonder if I could get eight?
Tying knots is an art, especially when it comes to seafaring vessels. Takes a long time to get used to it. Lots of blisters, too.

The plants that grow in the Systres are more lovely than anywhere else I've ever been. I'd love to study with the druids … or the vinebeards as folk are wont to call them around here. But I don't know if they'd accept me.
I worry for the people of Gonfalon Bay. Too often are they captivated by the druids' woodland religion, charmed by its purported freedom. But Y'ffre pales before the true Divines.
Had some beef-wit ask me the other day if I was a knight. Do I look like a gods damned knight? No shame in being one, I suppose, but that life was never meant for me. I don't like taking orders.

I met a druid the other day! I always thought they were a bit strange, I mean … I heard stories. He showed me a plant that smells like a damned stable but can fix any strained muscle! Got me my arm back, it did!
Do you read much, my friend? It is such a beautiful way to broaden one's horizons. Many people could benefit from nourishing their minds with words rather than nourishing their throats with ale.
My goods are very good! Very good indeed!\n\nYou will want at least ten of each, certainly.
The relic must be around here.
So many dead things to choose from!
You prisoners better behave.
The new fish need to learn their place.
Does that island smoke all the time?
If they want to sail on the tide, they'd better strike that cargo below.
I don't trust the weather here. Looks fair, feels foul.
Terala is puzzled. Who would take a barrel?
The lazy rats. Why did they get to go to Gonfalon Bay?
Always liked High Isle. Maybe I'll stay this time.
Spare a coin or two, friend?
Worried about Mount Firesong? Eh, don't be. It just smokes sometimes. And shakes a bit, too.
Strange weather in the passage yesterday. Storm blew up out of a clear blue sky. I've never seen anything quite like it.
I have little time to chat, mainlander. We've got a rush order, and we need to finish fitting out every hull in the yard.
Anything going on over here?
What wretched things we've become.
The fools getting stuck in these shallows are easy pickings.
My vipers will tear you to pieces!
We can reshape these islands with the strength of these stones.
Thrones are for fools. This is true power.
Begone or I will destroy you!
You dare? You'll pay for that!
None have bested us!
This can't be!
You don't seem to be here by invitation, which could be beneficial to the both of us. Hear me out?
I anticipated your return. The device has become much easier to tune, thanks to your work no doubt.\n\nPlease, give it a try. You've earned the right to be the first to partake in its benefits.
Mathluz suspects he'll never leave this island. Not with those two preparing the escape plan.
Incredible! You appear infused with some … unstable magic. Its effects shifting like the tides. They don't seem to be destructive in nature.\n\nAren't you fortunate?
I hear the Far Shores' tides lapping against these cursed rocks, but I'll never reach them!
The Commodore knows best. Don't question him!
The Debonaire was such a beautiful ship. I was such a beautiful captain ….
None escape the pull of the deep.
I'm gonna show off a little!
Ha! That will teach you to mess with Ember the sorcerer!
We just beat a Dragon! A Dragon! When I asked for adventure, you really delivered, didn't you?
You find trouble wherever you go, don't you? I like it!
Let's do this!
Oh, yes! Come on, you big lizard!
Whew! That was fun!
Thanks for the heal!
Help? I don't feel so good.
You have to break away!
Hey, stay with me!
No!
You stopped them! Nice!
You don't look so good!
Your magicka is low! Be careful!
Don't slow down now!
Ha! They're in for it now!
You're kind of terrifying, you know that?
Here's the Ember special!
Come on, let's do this together!
Skywatch hasn't changed much since I was a kid, but it seems so much smaller to me now.
It would have been exciting to grow up here. I wonder if I would have turned out to be a pirate.
I love cities. They all have a kind of rhythm to them, and it's just a matter of learning the steps.
Nothing good happens in here, I can tell.
I'll try not to fall off!
Yes! Are we going to race?

I wish I had the patience to write about my adventures. I have a lot of stories! But my hand cramps after the first few lines of writing and I usually get hungry or bored and abandon the project all together.
Ooh! Got to be something good in there.
I'm getting to see all sorts of places traveling with you!
I love a good fire. Reminds me of being a kid. Being hungry wasn't so bad when you were warm.
That Lady Arabelle, she's something else! I might have to start reading those Investigator Vale books.
I don't think I'm cut out for being around nobility. Being formal makes my ears itch.
I've heard some things about Amenos. None of them were good.
Whew! That was exciting, never thought I'd get to meet the Alliance leaders. Was I casual enough?
I hate the Ascendant Order. I can't believe Count Damard was the Ascendant Magus the whole time! Ugh!
The Ascendant Magus never stood a chance. People should learn to stop messing with you.
You made sure there's at least a chance for peace and saved the alliance leaders. You should be proud of that.
Are we going to drink that weird stuff again? I'm so excited!
You're every street kid's dream, you know that? If you're offering lessons, I'm first in line!
Ooh, pretty! I love lightning. It's so ... chaotic!
My friends and I used to have those! We'd scare the pants off the merchants in Skywatch and steal bread while they were distracted.
Do I look stronger to you? What about my smell? I feel like I smell stronger!
Treasure?
Nice haul!
Well, look at you! Luck follows you, I swear.
Whoa! Shiny! You look amazing, I can see my face in your chest!
You're doing this just to spite me, aren't you? Ugh. You stink.
You're looking especially strong lately, I like it!
Here, take this. It's not much, but I wanted you to have something special. From me.
Do we have to stand around and talk? I joined up with you to go on adventures, not to chatter.
Need something?
Need me to do anything?
I grew up on the streets. To me, stealing, lying, sneaking about, and violence are all necessary aspects of survival. It doesn't have to be a moral thing.
Look, I'm only traveling with you because you go to interesting places. Doesn't mean I like being around you. Just be thankful I haven't turned you into anything while you're asleep.
Do you even have to ask? What do you want me to do, spell it out with runes? I. Don't. Like. You.
We're fine. I don't really like getting into the sentimental stuff, so let's just leave it at that.
Traveling with you is a good time. Better than sitting around reading books.
I can count on one hand the amount of people I trust. You're one of them.
I can be a lot to handle, but you've always been patient with me. I appreciate that.
I used to not trust anyone. Safer that way. But you? You changed all that.
All riiiiight, but can we do it fast?
You're not going to make me talk about my emotions, are you? Ugh, fine, but only for you!
Ember the Sorcerer, reporting for duty!
All right, I'm not dealing with you anymore.
Ha! Stupid dog, that's what you get.
Werewolves have such a distinctive stink, ugh! It's awful!
That was exciting! Not how I would have done it, but I like their style!
Another day, another good haul. This is fun!
Sometimes, even small jobs can make a big impact. I'm glad we took the time.
Ugh, they're all to busy poring over their books and swirling their robes to get anything done. That's why they use us.
Look at you, being all devious and sticky fingered!
You make that look easy!
Heh, that was too easy.
Anything good? Mages always carry something shiny on them.
Thieves trove? Nice!
I couldn't have done it better myself!
These places always remind me of where I grew up. It's comforting. I feel more at home here than anywhere.
That was satisfying just to watch!
You brought the right Khajiit for the job.
Hahaha! I love running from the law!
Well, well! Look at you, little silver-tongue. That was impressive!
Good eye, I didn't even see that runestone at first.
I probably would have done the same thing.
I used to play games like these all the time. It's a great way to pass time, and maybe make some coin.
Nothing sweeter than the smell of treasure!
More coin in your pockets is always better than a fancy trinket.
We need to be more careful when it comes to being naughty.
Fish biscuits!
What was that? We could have taken them!
I like fish as much as the next person, but I've never had the patience for it. Boooooring.
As much as I hate sitting around doing nothing, sometimes it's kind of nice to slow down for a bit. I don't mind this place for that very reason.
My friend Jhaka tried to teach me how to meditate the other day. I respect the big guy, but that stuff's just not for me. I can't sit still long enough! How does he do it?
The Ascendant Order is a strange organization. It almost seems like they're being bad guys for the sake of it! I've got no respect for people like that.
Awww, look at it! It's so sweet with it's big, stupid ears!
I don't trust that thing. I feel like it's judging me. Or it's about to get me in trouble for something.
Oh, yeah, I like that one. That's a good little friend to have at your side.
It's wearing a little hat! That's adorable. Can I teach it a spell or two?
I just wanted to eat. Now look at where I am.
This island won't be the death of me.
The lords took all the good servants. I'm sure of it. No one 'round here to help. Want my drink again. Slow now.\n\nHey! What is this place?

You … look familiar. I knew someone with the same look in their eye. Always asking questions. Curious. And annoying. I hated that person. \n\nStill, there's something about your face that I actually quite like. Hmm.
For Stendarr!
Hah! One less fiend in the world.
Dragon down! A fight fit for the storybooks!
I didn't think they'd ever stop. Nicely done, my friend!
You and me. We got this.
We're fighting a Dragon, then? Lay on!
Stendarr see you safely to your rest.
Ahh. Thanks for that!
I'm not doing so well.
Roll free!
Shake free!
Get up! We need you in the fight!
That's it! Keep your guard up!
You're wounded, be careful!
Give your magicka a chance to recover!
You're winded, take care.
Impressive!
Nobody's going to believe this story.
This could turn the tide!
Let's do this together!
I've been reading about Wayrest since I was a kid. The books don't do it justice. It's so … big! Hahaha. What should we do first? Visit the docks? Have some food? So many options.
These walls are incredible! Did you know this isn't the first city to bear the name Orsinium? Tamriel hasn't been very kind to the Orcs. I wonder if it won't be the last.
This den of Daedra gives me an uneasy feeling. Let's be careful.
Do you think there's a sweets shop around here? Let's take a look.
I'll watch your back. Who knows what's in here?
I'm with you!
Ready to ride.

Did you spend much time with your parents? My mother and father were at sea most of my life, working the trade lanes. I'm so proud of them. But. I suppose everyone says this as they get older … I wish I'd had more time with them as a kid.
Hmm. I wonder what's in that sack of supplies.
I can't believe I'm here. Look at this place.
Ahhh. This is nice. Aurelia and I used to go camping like this on High Isle. Seems like a long, long time ago.
These Ascendant Order thugs give knights a bad name. Glad you're doing something about them.
This Magus character threatens the heart of my homeland. Honor demands we stop him.
We're going to Amenos, are we? Stendarr keep us safe.
You saved the alliance leaders! Stendarr's breath, what can't you do?
The Ascendant Order have eyes everywhere. We should be careful.
Draigh, look at you. The hero of the day! And you've brought me along as part of the tale. Thank you, my friend. For everything.
Because of you, we might see an end to this bitter, stupid war. It's an honor to ride with you, and be a blade in your service.
Stendarr's Breath! It's so beautiful!
Ahh! Yech, why would you do that?
Hahaha. Lovely! Happy festing!
Careful. Ohh. I can't watch!
Our travels together have taught me so much.
Ah, that could be helpful.
Aww. Why did you do that?
Stendarr provides!
Oh, lucky! Stendarr must be watching.
Hah, Stendarr is generous today.
Nope! I know it's just an illusion, but I don't like it, I don't want it. Uh uh.
Is this a joke? Because I'm not laughing.
Your quest to improve never ends. Just like a knight.
This is for you. Stendarr's blessing goes with it.
I know you have to deal with all kinds of people. But I know in my heart Lyranth means to do you wrong.
Ahh, what is that? Why do you even have that thing?
Hold. My. Sword! Look at that dog! It's so cute!
I swore to ride with you, and so I will. What do you need?
I'm in your service.
I know that look. What are we up to?
I grew up squiring for the knights at Castle Navire. Just because my family comes from nobility, I hope you don't think I'm stuffy. \n\nI certainly don't think I'm stuffy. Am I stuffy?
It's clear honor means nothing to you. I don't believe there's more to say.
I offered you my blade, and I hold to my word. But your actions make me uncomfortable.
If I'm to continue in your service, I hope you'll seek a more honorable path.
I wouldn't have offered you my service if I didn't trust you, my friend. A knight's word is her bond.
I'm so glad we met the day of the tourney. And I very much hope you feel the same way.
You inspire me every day! Don't laugh. I mean it.
I'm so proud to ride at your side. I thank Stendarr every day that I met you.
Of course. What did you want to discuss?
It would be a pleasure to chat.
I'm at your service.
I can't fight beside someone without honor.
Back to Oblivion with you!
Think of the tales we'll tell! Hah!
Another one in the books. I hope you never get tired of exploring dank caves and ruins. Because I love them.
Giving aid to the people of High Isle makes me so proud. Thank you, my friend.
I believe in you! Guard up, and lay on!
Hahaha. Can we do this every day?
You made the honorable decision.
Lyris is so intimidating. How can you stay so calm around someone so … powerful?
You know, Queen Ayrenn seems like the kind of person I'd like to get an ale with. Hmm.
It fills my heart with pride to know the High King knows something of our deeds. Hah!
You know, I heard a rumor that the Skald-King is seeing someone. They must be quite a person to stand up to his … personality.
Look at all these artifacts. I hope we get to see all of these dungeons someday.
I cannot believe this place exists. Look at … look at all these people! Look at all this stuff! Are you part of the Undaunted? Can we go explore a dungeon? Oh, I'm so happy.
Hmm. Good craftsmanship, there. Well made.
Do you need any help taste-testing that? As a knight in your service, I'm here and willing.
It's a wise knight that looks after their own kit.
You're better than this, my friend.
Murder is a sin against the divines, my friend.
Stendarr, please. Forgive them. Their affliction is a darkness on their soul.
Nothing good comes from places like this.
I can feel the darkness here. We should leave as soon as we can.
Remember, how we treat the least among us reflects strongly on our honor.
It's so relaxing here. Quite the change of pace from my days as a squire. Ahh.
I cannot believe Aurelia lost my family's signet ring. Just goes to show you how we change over the years, I suppose. The Isobel of today would never trust anyone with something so precious.
Aurelia might come to visit from time to time. I told her to make sure to bring Marso, make it a little party. We could play some Tribute together and use candies for bets.
The Ascendant Order's plot almost worked. Terrifying.  Who would want to undo a bid to end the war?
This one sweeps away as many hours as dust ….
Hmm, fascinating! Just one more chapter. Or two.
Wish I could've been assigned to the party. This is just too quiet.
A lucky guess!
Representing your team in these competitions? It's not a snowball fight.\n\nBut it can be as fun as one.
That shaking underfoot? Ignore it. Focus on winning.\n\nThat's all that matters if you're a Storm Lord.
Very well, I concede. Well played.
I win, it seems. Better luck next time.
Hmph.
There it is.
A true Pit Daemon keeps their gear in good shape. Clean, too.\n\nI recommend multiples of any fabric elements. Sometimes things get a bit … unfriendly in matches.
Are you planning on taking a turn?
I bow to the victor. Very well played, indeed.
And just like that, we're done! If you want a rematch, you know where to find me.
Damn, damn, damn.
And now, we reap the harvest.
Don't tell me you've fallen asleep.
Yeah, yeah, good job. Ugh. I should have stuck to vosh ball.
You had me sweating for a moment. Don't let up next time.
Took that one in the tusks.
Har! Yes!
My tusks aren't getting any shorter. Speed it up!
I salute your skill, wayfarer. I still have much to learn.
You show grace in defeat. That is the sign of a worthy foe.
Unfortunate.
Thank you, Tall Papa!
Have you made your decision?
The grove suffers. Can you not feel its pain, stranger?
Welcome to our humble village, stranger. All who come in peace are welcome in Stonelore Grove.
Is it true? Is there a corruption spreading through our sacred grove? That's terrible!\n\nI wish I was further along in my studies so I could help in some way.
Sorry. I'm new to the Stonelore Circle. I'm still learning the basics of the True Way so I really don't see how I can help you.
It seems I underestimated you.
Don't blame yourself. You never really had a chance.
Oh, drat.
Aha, my skill reveals itself.
You can't delay the inevitable.
I won? I mean … I won!
I lost …. What else is new?
Oof. Right in the acorns.
Y'ffre's bones, I got you there!
Did you forget it's your turn?
You got lucky. Go on, then.
Ha! I knew I would win!
B'vek ….
Ha! That's just what I needed!
You have to take a turn at some point.
You have a sharp mind and clever fingers, walker. There is always next time, yes?
You played well. This one just played better, yes?
Ziss'vo!
Fragrant, yes?
This one may take a nap while he waits ….
I erect the spine of respect. Well played.
I rest in the hut called victory. Perhaps you will play better next time.
Kaoc!
I inflate the sac of delight.
Before Sithis takes us, please.
Good playing. Winner buys the loser a drink, right?
You did your best. Now, loser buys the winner a drink, eh?
Gods damn it!
Ha! I'll drink to that!
Buy me a drink if you're going to make me wait.
How am I to capture the majesty of the Colossus on such a small canvas …? I going to need a bigger easel.
If that guard doesn't use the bathroom soon, I'm going to have to go right here.
Rarely catch anything up here, but I love the watch the ships come in.
Sea water's not so bad with a little rum.
The dummies don't put up much fight. Or any. Will I really improve like this?
I bring a lot of gold through Gonfalon, it's only fair I enjoy some hospitality.
Of all the places for my brooch to come loose. It can't have fallen that far. I'm just not seeing it.
Patience, Mary. You know their routine. They'll show.
Pah, sailors. Leave nothing but salt and spew in their wake.
Water bearing is murder on the neck ….
Least they could do is bury me in the crypt, seeing as I take such good care of them.
Hey, no pissing in those alleys. People live here, you know?
Think that barrel of pickled herring was leaking.
Just need to stash this somewhere for a little while.
The sea takes so much from some of these poor souls.
Heard we've got visitors from all three banners. Hope things stay peaceful around here.
Going to need more fuel for this signal lamp soon.
Don't spook the mare. She's trained to kick for the head.
Another quiet patrol around the bay. Just the way I like it.
I was a c-captain, you know? Before those D-Dreadsails sank us and—and the s-sharks!
Nothing like working in the fresh air and cool sea breeze.
Take this offering of blood and blade, curse my enemies with stormy seas and rolling waves.
Ornaugs are good eating if you know how to cook them.
No good will come of stirring up trouble with the druids.
Ah, where could I be?
The spirits of nature are upset. Something is wrong in the grove. Can you not feel it?
I can't believe my half-finished painting is the last rendition of the Colossus of Gonfalon before it's ruin …! It might sell well though ….
No! No! All this quaking is ruining my stroke work! Maybe I can call it abstract?
People call me a drunk, but even that giant statue fell over the other day. Can happen to anybody!
Hehe, that must have been some really good grog. Everything's way more wobbly than usual.
I saw the colossus come down. What a sight that was!
Not sure I can keep fishing up here. Darn quaking near pitched me into the drink when it started.
Can't believe the colossus was destroyed! Bad omen, surely.
More and more soot blowing in. All I can do is sweep it away and pretend everything's fine.
Stay clear of any fallen debris, let the work crews do their jobs, and everything will get back to normal.
Gonfalon Bay used to be such a paradise. How am I supposed to keep the peace when the whole city is in upheaval?
All I'm saying is we should focus on the richer targets. Coin for the cause.
Remain vigilant. The Order expects no less of us.
You heard the Magus. This is our time!
I hear they're promoting new guardians. And bannerets, too.
The Magus isn't happy. Someone should have found something by now.
Great work! Keep it up!
It's up to you! Slay the beast!

You did it, didn't you? The air feels calm, and you look satisfied.
Thinking of taking a little vacation. Nothing too exciting, just a few days with a warm fire and a bottle of Theilul.\n\nI wonder if Varisse would miss me. I know I'd miss her.
The danger has passed, but like my Egg-Mother always said, keep your teeth sharp.\n\nStrange, working through it all, but I'm here to be of service as best I can.
There's a prickliness to the air, can you feel it? Oh, sorry. Talk of tension amongst the druidic circles has my thoughts buzzing worse than a kicked hive. \n\nHow can I help you?
The key to a good brew is its smell. Most folks don't consider how much work our noses put into drinking.\n\nTry our special blend and tell me those notes of honey don't make a difference.
I reckon we could all use a drink after what we've been through, losing the cathedral and all.\n\nMy hands are still shaking so please excuse any spills.
I've been working on something special to commemorate the end of all this.\n\nI'll set a bottle aside for you when it's ready. It's the least I can do.
I see you eyeing my work. Don't be afraid to take a closer look. Come, come.\n\nNote the grain and how it strengthens these tools.
A terrible thing, what befell the cathedral. A shame to lose something so beautiful, especially when it meant so much to so many.
Know, O wayfarer, that this humble carpenter will not forget the aid you offered in these troubled times.\n\nPeace be upon you.
If you're looking for a fair price on a new bow, I promise not to string you along.
You look as weary as I feel, dear. I don't know how this sea air does anybody any good. \n\nRest awhile, before a gust from the port knocks you over.
We've been plenty busy after what happened with the cathedral. Such a dreadful tragedy. \n\nTuck in and have a drink, now. We're all commiserating.
I was dreadfully homesick when I first came here. But nothing makes a place feel more like home than having it styled to your liking. \n\nLet me know how I can help you with yours.
Even having a wall of rock at your back is no guarantee of safety. Armor up, friend, and thank me later.
I saw the whole cathedral collapse from right here. Just goes to show you that disaster can strike at any time, from any direction. Best prepare yourself for it.
Don't mind Astinia over there. She's been through a lot. I do my best to watch her back these days. \n\nBut if you need something with which to watch yours, take a look at my stock.
My ship is yours. I just need our heading. Let's move with the wind while we have it.
Did you know it's cheaper to get to the Systres as cargo than as a passenger? Depending on what else you're shipping, the journey can be downright cozy.
So what if most of my stock is grown by prisoners on Amenos? You'd never be able to taste the difference.
Between you and me, I used to be one of the best fences this side of Leyawiin. This job? It's not so different.
Much has happened, and yet I think more will happen still. \n\nPonder on this while you browse my wares.
Stefan Mornard was my first customer when I set up this stable in Vastyr. He chose a beautiful midnight mare and named her Cinder. A finer horse couldn't have gone to a finer man.
Step lightly, will you? My stock's still skittish after what those crazy druids did to the cathedral.

My friend Haidouna wants to set me up with some old pirate that's been frequenting her inn. Can you imagine? A pirate and a banker? How ridiculous! My heart's fluttering just thinking about it.\n\nWere you going to make a deposit today?

That Stefan Mornard is quite a catch, isn't he? Not for me, of course. My daughter. She could have been a countess, if only she hadn't run off to join some wyrd coven in Bangkorai. Silly girl. \n\nAre you here to make a withdrawal?
Can you tell this squirrel that unless she's decided to thank me or apologize, I'd like her to stop bothering me? Maybe she'll listen to you.

The guards say we won't have to worry about the Firesong Druids making any more trouble in Vastyr. I suppose I'll have to think of some other reason to ask Chath-Kasi to walk me home at night.\n\nWell, how can I help you?
[The squirrel stares at you.]
I suppose that shifting environments are just something I'm used to. One grows accustomed to a changed horizon, just as one might to a newly furnished room.
Now, I don't know anything about the business of druids or whatever disagreement they're having, but my mother always said there's nothing a good meal couldn't solve. Eat up and take care.
You want to know what I think about Stefan filling his father's shoes? I think the boy still needs folks to chew his food before he can eat it.\n\nAll of this? So suddenly? I'm worried about him.
You would think we were handing out free meals with how busy the place has been. Everyone is finally breathing easy again.\n\nClear skies and calm seas, what more can you wish for?
Folks sure are keen on putting distance between them and Galen these days. Can't say I blame them. \n\nWhere are you headed?
You shake a broom at a squawking gull one time, and suddenly the whole flock is out for blood! \n\nTake a look if you'd like, but keep your head down.
The gulls all scattered when the cathedral collapsed. Here's hoping for another disaster, so I might know a moment's peace.
I used to shudder that we lived in Y'ffelon's shadow. Now, I shudder to see it so quiet.\n\nBut I suppose we shouldn't take these moments of peace for granted, should we?
You look like the type to take the fight back to whoever brings it to you. Good. We need more of that here.
I heard a Dreadsail captain helped free the folk those Firesong Druids took to Y'ffelon.\n\nSay what you will about this island, but it's never boring.
Mages from all over the guild wanted this posting, but in the end, it went to me. Because who would understand druid tribalism better than an Orc?
What the Firesong did to Count Mornard is the price we pay for magic we don't take the time to try and understand.
Do you know anything about enchanting, or will I have to hold your hand? \n\nHand holding costs extra, of course.
I had my first kiss in the shadow of the cathedral, hiding from our parents after stealing sweets from the market. Now it's gone.
I try not to kick out all the children that find themselves in my shop. Some of them are young enchanters just waiting to be inspired by a dusty tome or ancient bauble.
Most people find the leather curing process to be quite smelly, but me? I find it comforting. Reminds me of making small pouches with my father when I was a kid.
Just last Frostfall my wife and I were married in that chapel. She wore the most dazzling dress and I made my own guar leather jacket. It was quiet fetching.
Now that things have calmed down, I'm hoping my shipment of stained netch leather arrives soon. I'd like to make Stefan Mornard a gift. He's earned some praise for stepping into his father's shoes.
I once knew a warrior who did not have enough bag space for all his gear. He was quite the sight, no one respected him.
I would never run from a fight, but I wish I had a bag big enough to hide everyone during the attack. That would be a bag worthy of a bard's song.
You'll need a tightly sealed bag to keep your items safe from sea water. We even have some waterproof bags made with oiled leather if you have the coin.
With just a few minor alterations, you could really show off all those muscles. Let me know if you're interested, Wayfarer.
I already have a stack of orders for funeral attire now that word of the Count's death has spread. Seems sad to think of fashion so soon, but we all have our ways of coping.
Now that the chaos has subsided, a dear friend of mine proposed. To me. Seems my next wedding gown order will be my own.
Your home should feel like the perfect escape from all your problems. I can help make that happen.
The Count is dead? I just placed an order for commemorative busts. I wonder if I can have them altered to look like Stefan. Hmm.
I sold a bed so comfortable its owner slept through all this druidic drama. He had no clue that there were even earthquakes. Can you believe it?
While you are poking around all those shipwrecks and beach drift, be sure to keep me in mind. Everything has a price.
My wife and I got married in that cathedral. She took the kids though so I say good riddance!
Business is doing great now that all that druid business is settled. Thanks for that, by the way.
Hmm? Soul stones? Yes, yes just rummage around, you'll find them.
I froze up during the attack. A cowardly thing, I know, but that's why I'm back in here studying. I do not want to feel that way again, Wayfarer.
Always intriguing seeing an adventure like yourself practice the mystic arts. Do be careful, won't you, Wayfarer?
Calm tides to you stranger! Stay awhile and view my wares?
The Count always struck me as kind and generous. I hope that stands true and he's judged kindly in the afterlife.
I slept easy knowing that the island wouldn't split in half while I was sleeping. Do I have you to thank for this calm?
Come, come! This one has wares that are sure to catch your eye.
The children that play in the market trust Arzalaya so this one made sure to protect them when the fighting started.
It is good listening to the children play in the market without worrying about an attack. A gift to be certain.
I do miss wrapping my hands around the hilt of an axe, but a heavy coin purse will do.
You look like you handle yourself well in combat. Good. We need more strong warriors protecting Vastyr.
The ground is calm again. Now the only rumble comes from the liveliness of the market. A welcome sight indeed.
Trying to play hero? Not with our catch you're not!
Three attacks in as many days. These damned spriggans deserve to burn!
Go on, give it a good kick!
Beasts of flame, attend me!
Fire-spirit, take shape!
Fire-gryphon, answer my call!
I am the fire, fools!
The Druid King's regalia belong to me!
Face the wrath of an archdruid!
Is someone there? I could use a hand!
You dare defy the prophecy?
I grow tired of this sport!
Not today, creature!
Over here, you beast!
You, with the shimmering aura. Come over here. Let me open your eyes.
Go on, all you have to do is dig the little mind-bending friend up.
Squawk! Raise the mainsails! Squawk!
It's drawing energy from the distortion!
Spread out! The creature's releasing its power!
Take shelter in the light!
That orb! Stop it!
You think being inside a frog will stop me?
How dare you interfere with our work?
I survived a frog's belly. What can you do to me?
Fire-bird, destroy my foes!
Oh, you're so salty.
How about we sneak away?
You have such strong arms.
You must be tired from running through my mind.
You fit so well in those breeches.
I just love that scowl of yours.
Pirate life involves too much waiting.
Did you craft those earrings yourself?
What a lovely smell in here. Like if mold could sweat. Ugh.\n\nKeep searching for leads. I'll keep watch.
We need to go back and find Lady Arabelle.
We will make short work of you!
Burn the Sea Elves! Sink the ship!
You shall perish in fire!
Abandon ship while you can!
Take the ship!
Find the captain! Slay her!
You are no match for us!
Burn them! Sink them!
You will never retake this ship!
This ship is Firesong now!
That chef makes better food than she lets on.

Oh, why must I be stuck here? We'll get home someday, little squirrel friend. I hope I can find some more acorns for you to eat in the meantime. And I promise we'll visit Grahtwood for you again soon.
The market smells good today.
I should not show up for work more often.
Hmm. How long does it take someone to buy a guar, anyway?
Beds are for fools, this is the best place to sleep.
Sometimes the best treatment for someone is to hit them in the head with a large stick.
My friend, you are missed. I hope you see that I've honored my oath to bring you here.
May the ancestors hear my prayers.
They keep a nice spread on the sideboard here. Now if only they'd serve a good roast.
New dice or old dice for my next game? Perhaps if the old ones fail me again, I'll find a way to crush them finally.
Hey! My tankard's empty again. When did that happen?
Hmm. We need to remeasure this beam.
I'll never get used to these brews.
Keep your eyes open, and your mouth shut.
Things seem slow today. Doesn't anyone need a gift for their ancestors?
The candle makers in this city must be rich!
I detest this city. Everyone changes their routines at a ghost's request.
I think my mother will love this urn I'm making for her.
Someone keeps taking my spellbooks!
Coin for a poor Hlaalu?
I have no gift for poetry. I would sound ridiculous.
Ancestors, hear my words, but don't stir yourself. Know well that I serve the Buoyant Armigers, honing their swords and repairing their armor, as you would wish.
Good boots, or a heavy cloak? It gets cold up north.
I made a mistake. Please, forgive me!
A lot of Dark Elves think the Tribunal is our only choice, but that's not true.
Oh, Varle! Why did he have to die?
Haven't hooked a pygmy shark in months here. Might be time to move on.
Brewers keep their costs low. There's enough mourners here to drink a harbor dry.
Feels good to stretch my legs.
The beauty of milkcaps comes not from their spores, but instead from the parts that we add to our stores.
Generations of my ancestors are interred here
The Stormwing's a great ship. Pity it's been quarantined.
Take your time and mend it properly. Might save my life someday.
What are the dead going to do with those offerings?
Attack you coward!
I'm too comfortable around this much death. Hmmm….
This clay feels strange.
You chop wood well, and what do they do? Bring you more wood.

Have you seen a journal around here? I found it in a drawer of one of my furnishings. The writing was gibberish, but the illustrations intrigued me.\n\nAh, never mind. Let's focus on your needs instead.
All manner of fungi make for powerful alchemical properties. Curative ointments. Destructive poisons. They aren't to be trifled with, I assure you.
You strike me as someone in need of some good armor.\n\nWhat can I do you for?
Some fighters don't like this city—superstitions drive them away from the dead. Looks like you're not one of those ones. \n\nWhich is good! I don't want any of my weapons in the hands of fools.
Necrom has strict regulations against thievery. Your coins are safe here.
Welcome to Necrom. We treat your deposits like our own!\n\nEr, maybe that didn't come out right. How can I help you?

Need some smithing done? I'm your smith. Just to be up front about it, I make things according to my family's heritage.\n\nSo if you're Psijic Order like the fellow I had last week, I'll repair what you have but not craft it from scratch.
Is this your first time in Necrom? Can't imagine a better place to sit for a drink. I've worked in my fair share of taverns and I assure you, this one has them beat by miles.
Look at this wood's grain! That's fine Vvardenfell timber, there!\n\nHow can I help you?

All these Elves are too thin. I'm here to help them put some flesh on their skeletons. Happy to serve delicious food to anyone who can pay for it. \n\nSee what I have that's ready. Maybe it'll put a rumble in your stomach.
I offer tailoring on all my garments. No charge, of course. I just want you to know that they'll fit you and no one else.
Hello! Don't mind my little friend Dusty. He brings me good luck!\n\nNow, can I help you with some runes or glyphs?
Pumpkins, apples, and more to appease your appetite! All of them provided by me for you!\n\nSpecial goods for the recently deceased of Necrom, too, as is right.
I see you eyeing my wares. I promise every item here was sourced equitably. And by equitably I mean it was cleaved, plucked, or hewn by someone I don't question and relatively trust.
I tell you, there are a lot of light-fingered thieves in this neighborhood.\n\nYou buying or just looking?
Looking for something in particular or just browsing? \n\nDoesn't matter much to me, but my suppliers want to keep an eye on what's in demand.
Necrom is a city that's rich in artistic talent, but poor in material production. That's where I come in. You won't find better imported goods anywhere else.
Falani does not claim to offer the finest goods in all Tamriel. She merely offers the finest goods in Necrom!\n\nCome, have a look.
Before you ask, I don't sell urns. Usually.\n\nNow, how may I help you?
You smell that? It's a special incense mix of my own creation. I call it, things Murkholg stepped on while walking home, on account of it being made of, well, you know.
We run a clean place here. Well, mostly.\n\nWhat can I interest you in?
It's awl-fully nice to get to talk to you. Get it?
They may not look flashy, but the spells in my goods are strong, I promise you that.
Thinking of venturing outside Necrom's walls? I can fit you out for a jaunt in the wilds.\n\nWhy don't you take a look at my wares?
You're really there. Yes. Not a spirit.\n\nThen I may ask you to look at my wares.
The waters are as good as any sailor could ask for. Interested in making a voyage? There's no time to waste.
We all need a little … space. Get it? Space? \n\nYou look like you need an upgrade.
Don't ask me about a beast unless you're equipped to ride it. I refuse to hear another sob story about how some reckless adventurer got eaten by their own mount.
This one makes beautiful clothes, no? Try them on yourself. You'll see.
Greetings, stranger. You'll find no finer steel in all Morrowind. Trust me … you might need it.\n\nWhat are you looking for today?
Hold on, I thought I saw a Buoyant Armiger a few minutes ago. They're so courtly and noble! I wish I were a Dark Elf of House Redoran. Maybe I could join them then.\n\nOh. You want to see my wares?
I don't see the appeal in living gods. The wisdom of the departed is often more poignant. I thought the Dark Elves here would appreciate that more than most.

Even though I'm temporarily stranded here, it's better by far than being trapped by a Daedric Prince. Any of them. Which one only changes the flavor of captivity.\n\nAlways bargain from a position of strength. Always.
The keepers are active at all hours and the dead don't sleep. Am I the only one in need of rest here?
Nethyn here is always fishing, but never catches anything.
Greetings. Isn't it strange, the people one meets by a grave? Evidently, Lloros Telen had friends and acquaintances I never suspected.\n\nI offer my consolation, traveler.
Ships bring travelers, both dead and alive. Do whatever you can to make sure you can arrange your own travel when coming here.
I once new a guy who had his broken teeth fashioned into dice. Used to say that they spoke for him now. Man was more confident with those dice than he ever was with a full smile.
The keepers are pretty particular about the urns they use, but I think I can create some that are up to their standards.
Necrom's plazas are impressive, until you have to clean them.
I don't know what's been going on at Necrom Abbey lately, but I've seen a dozen or more pilgrims turned away from the catacombs in the last few days. People are upset.
I'm studying the rock formations of the Necropolis. Some, most likely fanciful, sources say the entire geography of this place is made from the ashes of the ancient Dunmer.
You'd never guess the sorts of goods I've seen brought through this port. Necrom's reputation doesn't do it justice. From funerary urns and magically shrouded bodies, I've seen it all.
There's a grit here in Necrom that I've found nowhere else. It's like a mix between sand and chalk powder. Gets in your boots and stockings so easily.\n\nExcellent for my next soap experiment.
I love this city, but it is surrounded by the Telvanni.
I swear, they'll let just anybody into Necrom these days.

Good day, serjo. Stranger in town? I'll be happy to show you around Necrom for a little coin, just as soon as I finish up with my current client.\n\nShe has a lot of questions about the ways we honor our ancestors.
Move along, stranger. My anger at being misled means nothing to you. Let's keep it at that, shall we?
If it's a mentor you're looking for I suggest looking elsewhere. I certainly don't have the time or patience to take on an apprentice.
If you eat here, try not to spill. The keepers aren't fond of messy eaters here.
There's something about Necrom that makes Necromancers think they can just come here and animate our ancestors.
If you'll excuse me, I was working on a new spell.
Admiring the view of our fair city? Understandable. I like to walk the battlements and do the same. The dome to our right is Necrom's wayshrine. And just past that, you can see the guild district.
You haven't been sent to check on me, have you? I swear, the Magisters here take far too much interest in the day to day goings on. I barely get any work done.
Not always good fishing here, but maybe I'll catch a mollusk.
High prices. Low Quality. Unimpressive.

If you're looking for something to drink, the bar is right over there. If you're looking for something else, keep on looking. This isn't that kind of establishment, and I'm not that kind of tavern maid.
I take great care when crafting funerary urns. Could you imagine having your ashes stored inside blemished brass? I shudder at the thought.

I am fascinated by the pumpkins in Necrom. I hear that if you eat the seeds, you'll dream about your ancestors.\n\nFrankly, I think that's so much blathering nonsense, but you thought about it for a moment, didn't you?
The city is restless and it'll take some time to calm down. \n\nMy orders are to remain vigilant, so kindly be on your way.
What? Oh, sorry, stranger. I was training. You can't always choose the enemies you meet on the battlefield. But you can choose to keep yourself in top shape!
I never cared for magic. The study of my great culture holds more appeal.
There's something strange at play in the streets of Necrom. I have a nose for that sort of thing, trust me. I'd keep my eyes open, traveler.
This city is delightful, but these are Munsora's favorite streets
These Dunmer genealogies are fascinating. Fascinating! No one pays more attention to their ancestry. So many stories are preserved here.
You shall feel my blade!
Y'ffre protect you, stranger!
I thought I was going to die!
The flames of the Firesong Circle will not be extinguished so easily.
The other circles are fools to oppose us.
They killed Archdruid Orlaith, but a new Druid King will rise after all!
Y'ffelon's volcano spits and spews with unbridled rage, the time is drawing near.
We seek to bring back the old ways. A new Druid King must be crowned!
The Firesong are the caretakers of our true legacy.
Stay vigilant! There are still those out there seeking to stop us.
The Dream of Kasorayn will come to pass.
Rule under a new Druid King will set things back to the way they should be.
The circles can only truly be united under a Druid King.
Archdruid Orlaith will be avenged!
The Ascendant Lord will be a worthy successor to the Ivy Throne.
Come, my pets. Fight!
Like all who defy me, you die!
Let my flames consume you!
We of the Eldertide Circle pride ourselves on fighting our own battles. But I am glad you came along when you did, mainlander.
Face the fury of Mount Firesong!
I and the mountain are one!
Spirit, protect your king!
The guild refuses to fund my research! They consider collecting toad saliva for potion experimentation foolhardy. And gross. \n\nGross! Can you believe it?
Ever since the cathedral collapsed, my hands have been worked raw creating potions. Look, I have splinters!
Well, this was far more excitement than I'd hoped for. I never even got to study those precious toads!
This Y'ffre-cursed cow. It won't stop following me!
All this unrest is making sellers wary. I have shopping to do!
Y'ffelon is out of the question, High Isle is uppity, Amenos … no. I suppose I'll have to stay here and see if the turmoil is over.
We been out here so long I don't even know what day it is.
Saw it all from here. The crumble and the dust. Beautiful sight. Wonder if they'll do it again.
Now all the excitement's over and I can get back to my ale.
Keep your scales wet and no one will hear you coming.
The collapse has done well for my line of work.
All of the excitement is supposedly over. Ha! Forgive me if I erect the spine of disbelief.
This minstrel is quite good.
Music is good for the city, for healing our spirit.
Wait, is that the cat?
Hmm. I guess not. But try not to attract more attention.
Practice? You should know what you're doing at my age.
My uncle keeps contacting me asking about his daughter. But he's the one who sent her away. It shouldn't be a surprise that he can't find her.
Maybe I should leave Vastyr. It doesn't feel safe here anymore.
Don't ruin this one's concentration. Chirrdibazi keeps her eyes on the biggest threats in Vastyr.
Chaos is good for this one's purse, but there's no satisfaction in it.
I've never seen the Jaded Ornaug this crowded.
Look at these fools, they seem so eager to lose their fortunes.
Murderous Sea Elf pirates. Stubborn druids. I may take on steady work again.
You want to visit Oblivion? Come closer, I'll let you see it without the rifts.
Don't save these ones for the feast, Lamikhai.
Daedrats put up more of a fight than you.
No one will take the scribes from me.
You dare mar the flagstones of Hermaeus Mora with that banner?
Been too long since I faced enemies on this side of the gate.
You challenge Flame-Herald Bahsei? I happily oblige.
This won't take long.
When there's little else to lose, a fortune doesn't seem like much of a wager.
Don't mind me. I'm just trying to stay out of Thakuzag's way.
Avoid the third table. Lloros's fingers are lighter than a breeze.
These are some dark days, aren't they? \n\nOr maybe it's just dark in here. I should go outside.
Maybe those druids are on to something, spending so much time outside.
Two strange Bretons came through here not too long ago asking about the Fauns' Thicket. I wonder what they were up to.
Walls and guards are not enough to keep us safe. We have to look out for one another!
Ahh kitten, Raz could tell you … but then he'd have to kill you. Do not worry, you wouldn't feel a thing! And he would be most respectful with your remains.
The city may be a natural fortress. But as we've learned, rock can still crumble, and when it does, it can take all beneath it.
Pacrooti welcomes you! So much of his business is carried out through couriers, it is nice to finally place names with faces!
Admirable!
A monumental reward!
You have no crates remaining. Purchase more if you wish to try again!
Bright Moons, welcome! Are you interested in valuable rewards? Pacrooti can help!
Greetings, my friend! Are you ready? There could be outstanding rewards in here, let's see!
Pacrooti sees that you are ready to play! Excellent!
Your gem collection grows quickly!
Root and stone, what could you possibly want? You're not in my league. Not yet, anyway.
Aye! You did it. You found me. Druid Braigh, just as foretold.

With the leaping ornaugs, the passing ships, and High Isle hazy in the distance, it's easy to get distracted from one's reading out here. But it's better than reading by candlelight in some dreary study!
I was so near when it happened. I didn't run. Great pieces of the cathedral fell into the water, and the waves lapped at my feet, and I could do nothing but watch.
The waters are calm again, and I can get back to my book.
Wind keeps blowing smoke in my face.
Terrible thing what happened to the count, but he'll be remembered, that's for sure.
You smell that? Mint I think. Always around the guild house this time of day.
We're not supposed to be suspicious or nervous, but those Eldertide have been staying here an awfully long time now.
The count would want me to have a drink or two in his name. Facts.
Having a pint after work is like a daily ritual of mine. Sacred.
If you're going to ask me about protection spells forget it. I haven't the time.
I haven't the time for sunsets or beach walks, I've got a stack of books and a cup of tea with my name on them.
I came to study how the Stonelore and Eldertide coexist. Never expected the Eldertide to be so offended by my presence though.
While I may not have any thrilling novels to share, I do have a few recommendations for sea fairing historical texts.
In times of mourning I often turn to old books for guidance, but the loss of the count feels immeasurable.
I've only been studying druidic culture for a short time, but it's plain to see that the Firesong Circle's actions are wrong.
As a scholar, I've studied how the Stonelore and Eldertide interact for months. And now? They want me to help mediate peace between the circles!
I had nothing to do with the cathedral.\n\nI know you didn't ask, but I just felt like I should make that clear.
I hope we've all learned that the druids of this island have much to teach us.
Those druids didn't take me. They'd never be able to catch me if they tried.
My friend mistook me for a practice dummy once. So I keep to this side of the guild hall now.
All those people in the cathedral … I just can't believe it.
I knew someone could turn this city around! Vastyr's got a bright future, I'm sure of it!
Where's Marjacques? I want to pretend to take a swing at him again.
If you're looking for skilled crafters, you'd be hard pressed to find better than those here in Vastyr. Though I admit I'm somewhat biased.
Met a druid who knows how to coax wood from the ground with their hands. What I'd give for that skill.
I try my best to keep my hands busy. Keeps my mind from wandering.
Don't want to go outside. I swear, you can still taste the dust on the air from the cathedral collapse.
You're the one who showed those Firesong what happens when they mess with Vastyr! Good on you! Ha ha!
Don't mind Aldred. He get's a little talkative whenever his mother is visiting.
I need to brush up on my druidic texts. A lot to admire about the role druids play on this island.
Let those sea elf raiders attack again. I've never been afraid to squash a bug with a heavy book.

Glad I was down here when the cathedral fell. The folk who live above might sneer at us in the refuge, but we helped them anyway … on the sly.\n\nHas to be on the sly, you see. Otherwise they'd arrest us.

All sorts of rumors are flying around here. I heard there was a nature spirit walking around in the Vine District, straight from the Green!\n\nMaybe things will calm down finally. Which means more gamblers to clean up after.
Keeping this place in shape isn't easy, let me tell you. Especially with all those gamblers about.
Dreadsails are getting bolder these days. Seems like someone should do something about it.
Hear a lot of folks talking about leaving Galen after what happened. But I'm not the type to quit when things get tough!
I do enough for this city. Why hasn't anyone asked me to join the guard yet?
Dreadsail attacks are making it hard to get shipments in on time. Or get them here at all ….
There's more to Vastyr than the main roads.
This is one of the best spots for fishing. We're close enough to the city that the waters are calm but not too far from the true abundance of the sea.
I'm lucky to be alive after the Dreadsail attack. But how am I ever going to sort out these manifests now?
Things are finally looking up! For me, and for Vastyr.
Vastyr has been so busy as of late. I won't speak ill of travelers, but the sores on my feet might.
Terrible thing losing the count. Vastyr's been guided by his wisdom for almost as long as I can remember.

I … heard the cathedral fall. I didn't know what it was at first. I couldn't see what was happening. But I'll never forget that sound. It went way deep down into my bones, it was like the ground itself was groaning.
Yes, I know, a hunter stalking a courtyard is quite the sight, but there's a particularly nasty wasps nest hidden nearby and I will find it.
Even with all the passing ships, fish aren't scared of making their way into the bay. Makes for a profitable location if you've got the right bait.
You have to admire a druid's ability to grow and nurture plants across all areas of the island. Even in the most stubborn soil they can grow a garden.
If you're looking to spar, I'm your man. It'll cost you a pint or two at the tavern though, I'm not about to get bruised for free.
I've been asked to join the Society of the Steadfast over on High Isle. But I don't know if I could ever leave Galen ….
Perhaps I should have taken the Society of the Steadfast up on their offer when I had the chance.
I think I'll stay in Galen. Tempting as it might be to head somewhere like High Isle, it's clear I'm more needed here.
Look at this beautiful mace I found! It's a wonder no one's claimed it.
Sway as we kiss? You know what that song's actually about, right?
The Firesong took people? Where? Out for a drink?
Tu'whacca guide you, stranger. Vastyr is a place that welcomes many. Oh, it bursts with life. Everywhere you look, there's something new to explore.
Tu'whacca will guide us through these troubling times, I believe this with all my heart. Though the cathedral no longer stands, we must keep hope in our hearts.
I wonder how old this tree is. I've been trying to get an idea based on the size but even for Galen, this is a big one!
Stand and listen, traveler. What does the stream offer you? What does the biting sea breeze say?
The best hunters I know make their own arrow fletching. Mine's got moth wings woven in for extra silence.
Look who it is! Glad to see you made it off Galen. Sure, I loved the scenery, but all that lava made me nervous.\n\nLucky for you, no one has accepted the job yet. It's all yours, if you want it.

Thanks for joining me. What a relief. I already hired a ship—find me where I've noted on your map.\n\nOh, you'll want some lockpicks. A merchant here can sell you some. You and I both know the value of preparation.
Your ability to achieve is directly related to the quality of your gear. Choose carefully.
Your mortal trash could be Deadlands treasure. Let's see what you've got.
The stonework on this is incredible!
The spirits have plenty to say at this place where fire and water meet.
The shrine's many shadows give the figure many faces.
If I practice with Rasiza for too long, I start seeing stars.
Was walking a bit further down the road. Saw some folk fighting a beast with three heads. Think I've had enough to drink for one evening!
The ignominy of sheltering in this place filled with ruffians! I should never have left Gonfalon Bay.\n\nHonestly, if you're not counting cards in Tales of Tribute you're not trying to win.
Those druids did something to my cards. I'm sure of it. If they can knock down a cathedral to prove some silly point or another, they can certainly twist my fortunes.\n\nNever trust strange magic!
The gaming hall threw me out just when my luck was about to turn. The nerve! I'll find a way back in, mark my words.
This place gets chilly, doesn't it? Perfect for helping me take some heat off any goods you may have recently acquired.
I dreamed you would be here, friend. My dreams, however, did not tell me what you have for me.
No, the hermit crab is not for sale. And I know it's cute and all, but I think it was once a Khajiit. I don't sell people either.\n\nNow, how can I help you?
Looking for the unusual? The uncanny? The unmatched? Look no further!\n\nOr is that farther? Bah. Just look at my wares. They're unrivaled.
It's hard to stay focused when the world around you is on fire. Sometimes literally.\n\nAnd that's why I'm here, in this refuge, instead of out being a proper banker. So, let's bank.
Even druids must make a living, friend. Come, let's trade.
Walk these lands long enough, and you see just about everything. Well, not everything. But more than you would expect.\n\nNow, how may I help you?
I left Cyrodiil for the quiet island life. But lately, Galen's been anything but quiet.\n\nAnyway, want to see my wares?

It's enjoyable to be somewhere other than Castle Mornard. I know I have my duties there, and I can't just ignore them, but to step away and rest my feet for a moment is a luxury I won't take for granted.

By the Green, my family's feud with House Dufort is exhausting. The perceived slights happened in the past. Why can't we who exist in the here and now move forward? Everyone's heads are as hard as blades, I swear it.
Ah, it's good to see you. I should thank you again for your help at Castle Tonnere. Those damn sea-wolves would have made a sail out of my skin had you not gotten there in time.

We've been through so much together, I can hardly believe we're still standing. Thank you for being by my side. Your friendship has meant the world to me.\n\nCount Mornard. It still sounds so strange. I wonder if I'll ever get used being called that.
I'm a big talking cat. So good of you to notice.
Like all Senche-rahts, I'm an excellent hunter. Once I pick up the scent, there's no stopping me.
Five-claw! Good to see you! I missed your overwhelming aura of courage and competence.\n\nAnd your scent. I've never smelled anyone else like it.
You have the look of one who has seen much. I can relate to this.
Every hunter needs time to stand down, if even for a moment. Weapons must be maintained, armor repaired, food eaten. Annoying, yes, but necessary.

Is that … ah, yes. My senses are keen as always. You are afflicted with the bloodthirst. Worry not. In this place you are safe. As long as your fangs stay hidden and you make no move to harm an innocent, my blade will remain sheathed.

Good to see you, hunter. I find it pleasant to speak with you in a setting where the unhinged jaws of a blood-starved leech are not waiting in the shadows.\n\nConversing without the clash of blades or the shrieks of the blood-cursed is refreshing.

Once again, a job turned upside-down. I choose to believe that's the life of a thief. Not specific to the two of us. At least we're alive and free.\n\nUnless the Iron Wheel finds us. We should be going, shouldn't we? Let's get going.
I want you to know something. It's about why I'm in Abah's Landing.\n\nWhen we met for the <<1>> job, I said I needed a partner. I never explained why. Not really.
Curse these fire-druids! What next?
Up and at them, Gilded Blades!
Be on your guard! The fight's not over!
Foolish druids. We have seawater in our veins!
Curse this fog! Where are they?
Here! The druids are here!
Let these druids have a taste of Maormer steel.
There's nothing for you here but a cold, dark death!
This is where we stand. Death to the Firesong!
The Firesong attack! Hurl them into the sea!
Captain Siravaen! What should we do?
The Firesong are coming! Stand and fight!
Ready yourselves, Gilded Blades. We're not done yet.
Feed these fire-druids to the eels!
Die, Sea Elf scum!
Kill the Sea Elves!
You should have sailed away, Sea Elf!
The shadows aren't our friends.
My back feels stiff.
Burn!
I'll sear your flesh.
Did you hear shouting?
All my spells seem to backfire.
Come to me, creatures!
No more of this!
Only a few more hours.
My burn scars have healed.
Enough of this!
We've waited for you.
So much ash in the air.
The explosion shook the ground.
A serpent's bite!
For lord Peryite!
<<Light coughing.>>
They mock us. Despise us.
<<Light coughing.>>
They mock us. Despise us.
Hmm, this stack looks promising.
What are you waiting for? Go on through.
Too fast!
<loud angry growl>
This has happened before!
Peryite blesses you!
Feel the weight of time!
Taste what Peryite offers you!
A shard of time!
Do you think we'd be as in demand if we weren't mercenaries and vampires?
You … not win!
Know your place!
Surely, they can't need all of us for this job?
I'm just glad they pay well for our services.
Why'd they send Blood Knight? Are they expecting trouble?
Their fear is delicious!
Blah! Cultist blood tastes terrible!
Cultists? Again? Not even a little challenging ….
I always take a souvenir. Helps me remember the job.
Dusksabers, to me!
I love being a mercenary! Every job is different!
I haven't heard who hired us, but they pay well.
That cultist tried to convert me.
I do not know who you are, but I thank you for coming to our aid. An enemy of our captors is our friend.
To defeat the master himself! We had given up hope. I will make certain your deeds are remembered.
Xuth! We did not believe anyone would know of our captivity. So far below ground, we were unseen. Yet here you are.
I dust and polish these shelves every morning. See how they gleam?
You're back! And victorious. Excellent, you may enter the vault.
A Cartoklept? Be gone foul beast! This is not a library!
Always a sulfury stink that hangs around these Daedric shrines.\n\nAt least, I hope it's sulfur.
Here you are! I felt a surge of power and … what is that?
There's no escape!
I'll defeat you with the works of the scribes.
Knowledge, give me power.
I'm stronger than you.
Think you're quick?
No one gets through me.
My records! You'll pay for that.
She was my friend!
Outside the hall, everything is mine to burn!
Watch your step.
You will burn.
You live? Let's fix that, shall we?
You're pitiful!
Between a Telvanni mage and a Daedra, I'd rather face the Daedra.
Surely the mage doesn't need all of us here.
I don't care where they send us. As long as I get paid.
I bet Lamgash is still waiting there. The fool.
Bah. There's nothing to fear in this ruin but us.
I swear … next person to cross me, I'll feed to the death hounds.
The Dreamcarvers? They're an arrogant lot. You'll see.
I'm getting a little … thirsty. Must be something warm-blooded around.
This whole place smells like trouble.
Telvanni have deep pockets. They can afford us.
This whole region is an alchemist's wonderland.
I've always liked sabre cats. They feel like kindred spirits.
Fate is immutable.
The best secrets are on the highest shelf.
Time and fate are linked.
No sense in running. Fate is inescapable.
Hermaeus Mora tends secrets like a garden.
We prowl the dark corners of Apocrypha.
Every secret is a stepping stone to power.
Our tomes will last an eternity.
Most don't have the sense to keep quiet in a library.
How many falsehoods has our Prince shaped into truth?
No mortal nor Daedra is good enough for our books.
Prince of Fate, grant me knowledge!
Mages took everything from me!
Anyone who opposes magical rule isn't worth your attention.
This mind is a wreck. There's nothing here worth salvaging.
