You chose the wrong side.
See, Vanton? Nothing can stop us.
Vanton is mine.
A challenge? Do you think I would hold back before?
You rush to defend these abominations?
You think you can stop the most powerful mage?
If you have to make this more difficult, Twelvane will comply.
Oh mortals, you don't know when to give up.
You saw all of that and still long for more? I'll have fun breaking you.
<Zilipif chirps anxiously>
This could prove more difficult than I expected.
This looks familiar. Activate my ghost sight!
By the grace of the Tribunal, you've returned.
Do not underestimate the dangers along your path. Many adventurers have ventured out and haven't returned.
It looks like you've yet to encounter a foe you couldn't handle. The Ordinators could use someone like you. You will be well-rewarded.
Unfortunately, all my pending tasks for today have been taken. Stop by later and I may have new jobs to tell you about. May the Three preserve you!
I loathe this place. Let us finish our task and go.
I care not for the servants of Peryite. They are foul allies.
What does Hermaeus Mora fear, I wonder?
We should hide nightmares among the tomes. Mementos of our visit.
Maintain your guard. Hermaeus Mora has many servants.
Seekers are truly nightmarish. We could learn from Hermaeus Mora.
For a seeker of knowledge, Hermaeus Mora hides many truths ….
There is nothing here to frighten one who serves the Lady of Nightmares.
*Curious Gibberish*
*Curious Gibberish*
My lord could always do with a few more skeevers.
Perhaps my work will finally earn me the favor of our Lady of Dreams.
Our Vaermina allies do enjoy their brooding.
Poisons and plagues are two sides of the same, virulent coin.
How many other princes has Hermaeus Mora wronged?
Skeevers are kinda cute, aren't they?
The faster we finish this business, the better.
Hermaeus Mora's followers can resist all they like. Every man and mer falls to Vaermina when they sleep.
Can we truly escape Hermaeus Mora's notice?
Our Peryite allies seem so joyous in sickness. It's unnerving.
Our enemies shall be blessed with ailments unceasing.
May Peryite's will spread like a festering plague.
Sleep always comes, in time.
I can't stand skeevers.
I'll clear a path.
How extensive a mind can be when treated as a library.
This mortal's secret is quite amusing!
Knowledge is a maze. The farther we travel, the greater the chance of getting lost.
Knowledge must be preserved at all costs.
Fate works in mysterious ways.
Secrets are gifts that must be cherished!
Knowledge is like a blade, sharp and deadly.
Our work is too important to be interfered with.
We are the Darkreave Curators! We are Apocrypha's organizers!
The ciphers dared invade our space again.
The next one to bend a page loses a hand!
Books provide insight to those who read them.
I wasn't quite sure I'd see you again. I take it your task was successful?
The Ordinators pay their debts. Do right by us, and we will do right by you.
We pay well for those who can handle themselves in a fight. Do you think you have what it takes?
We don't have any more work for you today. But that's likely to change soon.
My power comes from knowledge. This is a library. You're doomed.
Rumor has it another black book wound up in the historical shelves. I want it.
Protect the books!
Tides and darkness wait between our shelves. The rift change is nearby.
Can you even read?
Imbeciles. Idiots. Map makers and their incessant doodles. Where is the real knowledge?
The Magnastylus will hear of your pitiful death.
Your intrusion ends here.
Why does the master favor filth like the Dark Seducers?
Sheogorath brings chaos to this Asylum!
My magic yearns for Dark Seducer blood!
The Golden Saints happily serve Sheogorath.
We spread madness in Sheogorath's name!
Dark Seducers approach. Get ready.
Stay alert. Dark Seducers are near.
Sheogorath is the mastermind, we are but his tools.
Is something watching us? Can you sense the Dark Seducers?
Sheogorath is chaos, Sheogorath is truth!
Another place, another conquest for Sheogorath.
How can the Dark Seducers hope to stand against us?
What is that horrible smell?
I smell something foul. A Saint must be near.
The Saints are no match for us!
Did you hear that? It might be a Saint.
Golden Saints will perish.
Sheogorath see our chaos!
I've littered this land with the corpses of Golden Saints.
No Golden Saint dares approach me!
Find me a Golden Saint to kill.
What Daedra shall we call forth today?
I hunger for the heart of a Golden Saint.
More corpses! The death is maddening!
We'll feast on your skin.
I saved a brood spider from a rockslide. Now an impossible number of spiderlings adore me.
Telvanni mages are similar to daedrats in that if you don't act quickly you'll soon have an infestation.
Don't stand there gawking.
I think the Itinerant Staff's a myth to fool the Magnastylus.
The Infernium's tunnels made a glorious wreck of this cave.
I just like to watch the mortals panic.
You won't make it to the infernium.
Your audacity will be your demise.
The flame-worm's spawn will learn not to crawl over my feet.
You're not who we expected, but you'll die anyway.
My web of bones will crumble under the Spinner's approval.
You were foolish to come here.
I will pop one of those Hoarvors like a tick.
New bones for my collection.
Moonshadow has nothing on the beauty of combat!
I was trapped in Moonshadow and you went and replaced the Magnastylus?
I fight for the Magnastylus.
Interfering still feels strange.
I should have tested this!
Do you think that's funny? I'll teach you to laugh at progress!
Send these creatures back to the Void!
What is this place? Where am I?
Is this the best the Void has to offer?
This one cannot wait to sink her claws into these Voidlings!
Light is the most divine of all the elements.
May Herma Mora grace us with his presence!
Was that a pirate that just ran through here?
Shh! Did you hear that?
You know, I'm directly related to one of the Ten Ancestors.
Truth can be found in the words of Molag Bal.
I am Gelon. Gelon is me? I am—arrgghh!
The whispers … what are they saying? I must know!
Vorm seems excited about that one!
Quickly! Lure her into my trap!
Across the bridge. Hurry!
Such a magnificent creature!
Dumac take that fetcher Luaffyn, I should be out smuggling not on guard duty.
Wonder what all those big eggs are for.
You think the cargo'd be the problem, but really it's the rats.
Next time, Luaffyn better second my plan.
The Ebonhart Pact was a mistake.
My ancestors are cheering me on.
Those chitin creatures? Too many legs.
Pouring fermented beverages on your wounds doesn't actually count as taking care of them!
Doesn't matter where we are, everyone ends up in Necrom.
Who fed the prisoners last?
I'll show that S'wit. Like, I've got nothing better to do.
It'd be easier to keep this place clean without all the animals in it.
What's it today? Graves or a cesspit?
At least I have a shovel to go along with your nchow.
No Golden Saint escapes!
I shall take your armor as a keepsake!
To battle! For Sheogorath!
No mortal can stop us!
Fear and anger take you!
I will have your blood, foolish weakling.
I spread chaos in Sheogorath's name!
You cannot overcome the madness and fear!
No Seducer escapes!
Pray Sheogorath takes pity on you!
Seducers will fall today!
You can't stop the Golden Saints!
What? Get away. Quickly!
Mortals are so weak!
Mortals? This will be fun!
Fear my golden boot!
Quit running mortal!
Feel the pain!
Out of my way mortal!
Come, Golden Saints! Destroy them!
Dark Seducers! Wipe them out!
I will crash down on you all!
The shadows will consume you!
Eat my axe!
I will rain doom upon you!
I wonder what I can do with this.
So alone. We can't hear them. Too quiet. Please, no. Bring them back.
The oven seems fine. There is no problem for Akkhiri to fix.
Chimer. Dunmer. Velothi. Ashlander. This one is confused.
Spare a coin? Your ancestor won't use it anyway.
Huh. That's interesting.
Where was that cheese monger? He had one I've never heard of before.
These flowers remind me of home.
I don't care if they say she's an unlucky ship. I need a billet.
Oh, so now I'm a fetcher? Yes, I go get things and bring them back to whoever pays me. But that's also an insult? Ugh. Dark Elves. Why can't they just say what they mean?
The rats are well-fed in this city. Don't think too hard about that.
She's been here. I can sense it.
Centuries old and still no patience.
Hmmm … not a choice I'd have made.
The Dark Elves fletch their arrows in a strange way. But it seems to work.
I wish Vevia were here to enjoy this with me. Ah, but she died on her own terms, at least.
The magic of my childhood was a desert compared to this oasis.
It is a warrior's saddest and most solemn duty. Sometimes she must take the fallen home and see to it they are buried in the manner of their people. Shuzashi will not fail her friend Rovone.
Did you know that Necrom also has a city of the dead?\n\nI suppose all the dead around here should hint at that.
Care to put some coin on the line? I may have gambled away my ticket out of here, but I'll win it back in no time.
Looking for the boat to Stormhaven? Ha! Do I look like the dockmaster?
Shor's bones! I knew the statue was important, but I didn't think it'd be this big!
Hmm. Colorful without being gaudy and expensive looking but still tasteful. These artisans' work is exquisite.

Surprised to see a Nord priest giving reverence to dead Dark Elves? You shouldn't be. In Skyrim, priests of Orkey entomb the dead. I came to Necrom to study from others who treat their dead with respect.
I really do admire the traditions here in Necrom. I hope my own descendants treat me with as much respect as these Dunmer treat their ancestors.
Most of the Dark Elves I know do not like to speak of it, but sometimes tombs are … forgotten. A family dies out, and no one is left to remember the dead. Those are the tombs I tend.
The shape of knowledge is ever twisting. Like a stream which rewrites itself with every passing season. Don't convince yourself that there's nothing new or nothing exciting left to learn.
If I use gall from Apocrypha to make my next batch of ink, this should work.
Best to wait for him to return. I don't care for my chances out … there.
Read anything interesting lately?
The ink makes my eyes ache.
If that wagon forgots to bring provisions, I swear I'm going to start eating books.
Will I ever be able to read all these books?
Why is that Watcher here? Doesn't Hermaeus Mora trust us?
The Great Eye wishes Thawia to get that book.
They say mortals don't age here. How can that be?
More than a lifetime's worth of literature and none tells how to cure the sniffles.
Those damn tomeshells keep taking the books I want.
These shells are … too big.
No, that can't be right. But if it's wrong, would it be here?
This one wouldn't swim in those waters for all the books in this library.
Master a simple light spell and you'll never be in the dark.
Studying makes me hungry.
There's a certain beauty to Apocrypha, isn't there?
Does the position of a tome within a stack signify anything?
This is no place for a mortal.
Why, this doesn't agree with Procillus at all!
Never an index when you need one.

Are you surprised to see one of my kind in the robes of a cipher? Do not be. I was born in Vvardenfell. The Hist never spoke to me, so I sought another voice. The Great Eye chose me when my own kind turned away.
A book is a lie, stranger. A mold that fixes words into a shape and imprisons them in that form. The Woodland Man taught me this. He remembers when many things could be true at once.
We see the flow of knowledge and secrets better from elevated positions. That's why Watchers and Seekers float.

Do not mistake me for one of these mortal ciphers. They scrabble and hunt after precious tomes, hoping to gain some glimmer of insight before death takes them. A fool's errand.\n\nI can be more … deliberate.

Not everyone you find here started out as a scholar or a mage seeking forbidden knowledge. Sometimes those of us who worked the soil or built structures sought information for personal reasons. Which eventually brought us here.
You must be new to the Midden. No one around here ever bothers to ask me what I think. Or where they get the food and drink to keep them in their books.

As long as you devote your hours to reading and discovering something new, no one here cares much about your past. \n\nTimes were when I would rob folks of their gold. Now I rob books of their knowledge.
I am honored to be here. I hope you understand what a rare privilege that is.
You never really think about how heavy books are until you have to carry stacks of them around every day.
I'm here! I'm finally in the Lord of Fate's library! This is so exciting! I have to read all I can and find some way to thank him for this wonderful gift.
Ah. Forgive me, stranger. The tale of the Oathbreakers of Ouze makes for heavy reading. A terrible secret most of my people chose to forget. Yet I know it now.
I wonder how many books are in the piles around here.\n\nAh, well, best get to sorting again.
Spells and magic should have an effect on the foliage here, yes? In this one's studies, they do not.
Don't look up until you're prepared for it.
Something is stirring here. Something deep. Possibly even dark.\n\nI hope to watch it unfold.

Do you see how no one is bothering me, apart from yourself? \n\nWell, that is because I'm someone to fear. If you want to go to bed tonight knowing you'll wake in the morning, I suggest you move along. Now.

You look like you can handle yourself in a fight. I'm looking for ferocious reavers to pillage the lands of these soft-handed Telvanni. All I need is a good longship. And the coin to fit her out. And, well, a crew.
Where is she? How much longer am I supposed to wait?
If you want to know what's really going on, this place will know. Just gotta watch your pockets.
I don't think the places on this map exist.
Don't hurt my friend!
Destroy the Golden Saints!
The Golden Saints are no match for us!
This war is beginning to bore me!
The smell of Dark Seducers is making me sick!
The Dark Seducers will perish!
Wipe them out! All of them!
I've focused my ghost sight!
Use my ghost sight to strike true!
Here, mortal. Let Apocrypha smite your foe!
Wasn't that amazing?
Let the threads of fate restore your strength.
Leramil's amulet can protect us both!
Burn mortals, burn!
No one can match my power!
Is this too difficult? Why do you even bother?
<Hoarfrost stares at you expectantly.>
<Pyroclast stares at you confidently.>
This poor soul was ignorant of the dangers of the season.
Despite my reservations, this place is fascinating. The Aurbisal emanations alone could fill a dozen tomes.
Be mindful around Howler. My furry little companion's smile may be adorable, but he's never known a coin purse he couldn't pilfer.\n\nIf yours goes missing, let me know.

There's a beautiful cove not too far from here, perhaps a few days journey. I go there to unwind. Sometimes I lay in the sand and pretend I'm writing a book about my adventures. A nice dream, but I don't have the patience to be an author.

I've learned to never ask the origin of anything I buy. It took me over a decade to get rid of a spirit attached to a locket I acquired.\n\nSo, let's stick to business, eh? Preferably without spirits.
We find ourselves in interesting places sometimes, friend. Just remember to duck if you see books heading your way. They like to attack sometimes.\n\nNow, to business.

I hoped you'd return soon. I heard good tidings from my eyes and ears in Apocrypha, but few details. Perhaps you can elaborate.\n\nDid you succeed in clearing Hermaeus Mora's enemies from Bastion Nymic?

While Hermaeus Mora's enemies are tireless in their plotting, it appears that for now Bastion Nymic is safe.\n\nThere is no threat for you to deal with today, but come back soon. I have a feeling that will change.

You return? I shouldn't be surprised. The foes of Hermaeus Mora are relentless, and so we must be too. Peryite and Vaermina have once again sent their legions against Bastion Nymic.\n\nThe Golden Eye needs you again, hero.
Remember that time in Saints—. Or was that in Betnikh? Maybe Shornhelm? Anyway, we had such a grand adventure! \n\nThat was you, wasn't it?

J'baanluk is proud to serve as a soldier in the Northern Elsweyr Defense Force. This one will protect his homeland to his dying breath, but every soldier requires a break from time to time. This one finds this location … relaxing.
J'baanluk takes great care in finding a skilled armorer wherever he goes. This one cannot stand armor that pulls at his fur or pinches his tail.
Elsweyr feels your absence, five-claw. Tales of your daring exploits still fill the air around campfires. In fact, many a drink has been lifted in your name. Do be sure to visit us again.
It warms J'baanluk's heart to see another Khajiit. This one has friends and associates of all heritages, but speaking with another Khajiit … no one else sees the world quite the way we do, yes?
Have you heard the word of the Blighted Lord? Would you like to? No? \n\nI get that a lot.

Itch-inducing rashes cover most of my body. Open, oozing sores decorate my blistered feet. And don't get me started about my aches, pains, and rumbly stomach. I have been truly blessed by the Lord of Pus and Pestilence!
I was sure this was where I parked my guar.
Can't they keep the servants inside during the day?
That courier should have been here ages ago.
This place makes me homesick.
He's really not going after that guar, is he?
Not a very proper use of scrib jelly, but certainly creative.
Jorck discovered we can take as many breaks as we like, so long as it looks like you're praying at the meditation pools.
Hild may have suggested otherwise, but I really am praying.\n\nIn troubled times, in lands far from home, I'll pray to whoever might hear me.

Took a wrong turn in Deshaan once and ended up here instead of Bal Foyen.\n\nCould have been a disaster, but I kept my head and offloaded what I had on my cart. Now, they keep asking me to come back. And they pay.
Elvali won't stay still long enough to have a drink with me.\n\nI guess I'll have to get rid of this whole bottle myself.
I tracked mud all over the floor Norus was cleaning. If he finds out it was me, he'll make sure I wake up in the kagouti nests.

Someone took my journal. Not my research notes, my personal writings. I can't go asking around for it. I'd never be able to face the person who ended up reading it. \n\nMaybe I should just pack my things and change my name and leave forever.

Good to see you again, friend. I'm still recruiting for my order, but there are three things I've learned to never discuss with some people: food, politics, and the Lord of Pestilence. Luckily, you're not one of those people!
Dead. And at half my age. Half! Death can happen anytime, to anyone!
Smell something, boy?
Oh Ma'nna, if only I had been more careful.
A decent haul for one day, I have to say.
Try to move around now!
Catch this, mortal.
Outsiders? Creature, attack!
I didn't mean me.
A figment of your fear!
You don't belong here.
Get her out of my head!
You're lying to me. Get out of my head, Ansuul!
If he won't succumb, I'll just have to break him completely.
I know where you are.
Help! She's making sense.
Oh, Vanton!
Thanks for distracting me from Vanton's cries. I don't scare easily, but imagining whatever he's going through really gives me the creeps.\n\nWhat can I get for you?
We've done what we can. But, after you buy what you need, the rest is up to you. Good luck.
Woe to those who do not heed my warning!
By the gryphon's freezing winds, we will have order!
Submit to the lion's flame!
Wamasu! Send your storms!
You did it? You woke the gryphon?
Did you take the lion's fire?
You have the wamasu's power?
The creature sleeps, but this one does not.
What starts cannot be stopped.
Wrong! You failed.
You're too slow.
You did it! You beat the puzzle.
This should slow you down.
Nothing escapes me.
Someone's coming. I'm sure they're just passing through.
You've come far enough!
My master's power is shocking isn't it?
You all must burn!
Burn bright!
Wolves, attack!
Do not let up!
My family may support the Pit Daemons, but I'll sell to any who wish to buy.\n\nNow tell me … how may I help you today?
Ah, it is nice to be in a new land, learning new customs, and playing for the Fire Drakes.\n\nI promise that I sell the best goods to all who can pay.

Perhaps we are lucky to be outside Necrom right now. We had some angry Dark Elves pass by not long ago, complaining about the closing of the catacombs.\n\nThey took out their ire in a few competitions after I sold them some goods.

I find it odd how we honor our teams. For instance, my fellow Fire Drakes find it important to dance around this standard before a match.\n\nOh, I sell my goods to anyone with the ability to pay my fees.
Alas, Pirrunira is a better furnisher than fighter. A mild sprain might serve to remind her that the battleground is no place for novices.\n\nHow may this one help you?
You mortals never seem to learn.
Need something before you ride into glorious battle? I'm the merchant for you.
I don't much care for grave robbing. I won't ask where your goods are from, but you won't catch me cracking open a tomb. I've got my own ancestors to worry about.
Ho there! We see you walk the dark paths.\n\nIs there something we can do for you?
You ever deal with mercurial customers? I've had to learn to duck to avoid being hit in the head by any of my own goods. Or I use a handy tray as a shield. Useful, yes?
Behave yourself around my stall or there'll be a new body joining the crypts.
In need of a discreet place to store your coin and possessions? It's a common predicament in our circles, friend.\n\nHow can I be of assistance?
Have you lost your way, mortal? Apocrypha is as unforgiving as it is endless. Rest when you can and be wary of the reaching ink.
The Pit Daemons will be victorious, mark my words.
Surprised to find a gladiator reading a book? You shouldn't be. I've always found great wisdom in the writings of Weapon-master Grutsug. Yes, the Orc. So many insights!
Where could that blasted book be?
Of all the- of course a tomeshell had to find it.
My blade's as thirsty as a drunkard in the desert.
I'll tear the still-beating flesh from your bones, malpracticer.
Oh you poor little mages. You're going to die painfully. And slowly!
You don't belong here.
Oh look, another fool to torture!
They're all so weak without magic. It's adorable.
A few tried to run, but I severed their ankles. That stopped them.
Death to all non-mages!
For the Mages Guild!
Vanton will never amount to anything at this rate.
Vanton is such a disappointment.
You're struggling. You can't win.
Leave Vanton to us!
After we clear all the filth from this city, we'll move to the rest of Tamriel.
I can't wait till we're rid of these malpracticers.
You're not one of us.
You're taking their side?
Why did we let non-mages live as long as we did?
Just produce a spark and I'll let you live.
This is a city for the strong!
Do you really want to do this?
Just give up, Vanton.
We'll find you, Vanton.
I wondered when you'd turn up.
Ansuul sees all your failures.

Greetings, traveler. This is a strange find, isn't it?\n\nI can't help but wonder what waters this ship once sailed before it came to be wrecked here. Or was this part of Apocrypha a sea in some ancient time?
I have spent most of a mortal lifetime preparing this altar to manifest the hidden energies of Apocrypha. Look about if you like, but do not disturb any of my arrangements.
Twenty-three, twenty-four, twenty … twenty ….\n\nWhy did you interrupt me? No, don't answer that. I need to get back to counting.

Roaming out here can be dangerous, yes? Learn to anticipate what Hermorah wants to keep a secret and what is knowledge safe to take. \n\nSinjari doesn't know about you, but she wouldn't want to upset a prince in their own realm.
Not much to glean from here, but these bones still hold some valuable lessons. Importantly, do not go swimming near these rocks.
I hunt poachers and game both. Best keep an eye on what you kill around here, wanderer.
These great fungal cups have the most striking coloration. I've seen few specimens quite so spectacular!
I've seen many sights in my life, but this landscape is stunning. The mushrooms are strange, but the view is spectacular.
Well met, traveler! I'm not having much luck today, but you're welcome to cast a line and see if you can do better. Plenty of room here for the both of us, and I'd welcome the company.
Our Dark Elf friends here are unhappy right now. Or should I say they're unhappier than usual?\n\nI should probably look into why, but my work keeps me here.

I always check the drawers of any furnishings I sell. We've had less reputable folk use them as caches for things I would rather not talk about.\n\nI'll do the same for anything you choose to purchase from me.
Clumsy oaf! How dare you drop priceless works in my presence!
Though most are close-mouthed about this, you'll find parts of Necrom off limits for now.\n\nYou want to know more? The spirits will tell you if you ask nicely. Maybe.

My family keeps its secrets, yes. Including some smithing tricks none other than my family knows.\n\nDon't go asking the spirits about them, either, you. They're likely as not to lie instead of admit ignorance.

I can't decide if I like selling extra goods to angry visitors or not. On the one hand, better profit. On the other, angry visitors.\n\nI hope you're not upset due to the closing of the catacombs! If you are, consider some food to take the edge off?
I'm not one for sentimentality most days, but it's just nice not to be worried about strange doings in the catacombs.\n\nWe should both celebrate with some tasty treats.
It's just as well that I can't visit my ancestors right now. No. No, it isn't.\n\nDistract me by looking at what's for sale.
Seems like everyone's back in business around here now that the catacombs are open again.\n\nSpeaking of which, let's get you shopping.
There! See my sigil? I always liked this layer of reality. Dig here!
Spirits and mortals alike are not happy with things as they are now in Necrom. Decidedly so. I wish I knew why.\n\nOr perhaps I don't and should stick to selling soul gems.

I'm not sure I can appreciate that Necrom is fully open again. The way some of these spirits celebrate. Noisy. It's noisy. Not now. But when you leave….\n\nPlease forgive me for my lack of focus today. I want your patronage, I assure you.
Accept Lord Peryite's blessing!
She's going to try to burn us out. Run!
Ummm … do you know what's going on around Necrom? The Dark Elves seem, well, irritated. Or worse.\n\nUgh, never mind. I should just do my job, shouldn't I?

I thought I respected Buoyant Armigers a lot, but I think you showed them up recently if I'm hearing correctly. Thank you!\n\nSo, ummm, do you need some armor repairs? I still have to charge, but I'll work on your gear with a big smile. Promise!
Where do all these machines keep coming from?
How many doors and corridors are in here?
I'm trapped in here. Help me!
Enough! Any more superstitious drivel and you'll both get something to fear!
No. I've already been this way!
Gah!
Out of my way!
Leave me alone!
Quick! Get rid of the nest!
Wh—what is that thing? Destroy it!
I'm not gonna hurt you. I just want to be your friend.
You seem like you have good instincts. I believe in them.
The sweet one? Of course. Who doesn't like sweet things?
Sour treats are my favorite. I hope he likes them too.
My tomes. My food!
"Flashing through, the blade did part, blood of Dreugh …."\n\nAh. Yes? Do you require assistance?
Ah, a challenger. Were this a duel of arms, you would find me atop a mountain of broken bodies.\n\nLuckily for you, that is not the weapon I wield this day.
Somebody help me!
Get me away from these creatures!
Just kill the beasts.
Why … didn't you help me ….
Whew. I am forever grateful to you, my friend.
I've had enough. I'm out of here.
Our Vaermina allies seem to brood a lot.
Both poison and plague can humble mighty foes. You'll see.
How many other princes has Hermaeus Mora wronged?
I don't like those Seekers. All those tentacles ….
The Taskmaster has given us an important job. We cannot fail him.
They say names of power are hidden here. But where?
<Encouraging unintelligible gibberish.>
Oh-ho, adventurer! Today is your lucky day.
I just learned to speak perfect Daedric!
The mountain charges.
The sky falls!
Behold and be amazed as I—in perfectly articulated Daedric—tell this feisty little creature to dance!
The stars fall.
How are we going to get out of this place?
We shouldn't have come here.
Soon we'll find our way out, I'm sure of it.
We're doomed!
How did we end up here?
There has to be some way out of here.
<Very excited gibberish.>
Let's make this quick.
That's what I thought.
That wasn't easy. But if it were, everyone would be doing it.
I feel like we could've kept at that all day.
About time we faced an actual challenge.
Hope we're getting paid for this. It's gonna be rough!
Psh. Easy.
Never going to get used to that.
Got to hang on.
Move it!
Hey! Stay with me!
You're too tough to go out like this!
HA! Got 'em!
You're bleeding out!
Looking drained, merc. Top yourself off!
Don't slow down now!
Show them who they messed with!
Damn. I'm glad I'm on your side.
Let's see how you handle this!
Together? You got it.
After I woke up without my memories, that graht-oak was the beacon that eventually led me to civilization. In some strange way, coming here almost feels like coming home.

Someday, when I'm ready to settle down and make roots somewhere, I think it will be here. It's not exactly rife with opportunities for coin, but there's plenty of everything else. The important stuff.
Ah, Stormhold. Half the guard spend their time in the Outlaws Refuge, and all the mud huts and collapsing ruins make it feel more like a big campsite than some crowded city. I don't hate it.
Let's just do what we came here for and get out of here.
Baddies in here. Probably goodies, too. Keep an eye out.
If I nod off, nudge me when we get there.
I'm with you.

When I stay too long in one place like this, people tend to approach me. And if I slip up and make eye contact, they ask me things. Directions. If I'm selling something. How I'm doing. It's why I always try to keep on the move.
Loot there. Don't pass it up.
We hiked all the way out here for this? … I guess it's not so bad.
Resting up before I'm ready to fall over. That's new.
I'm more of a hunter than a trapper. Just make sure whatever you catch doesn't go to waste.
Ack! Stop! What the—? Grr, you know I hate those things.
Seeing that makes me feel … heavy. I can't explain why. It just does.
Look, I'm all for scavenging, but I would not eat that. And I am not cleaning up after you.
Didn't think I had much more to learn. Guess you're proving me wrong.
Better overstocked than under.
Anything good?
Always nice to get stocked up.
Well, look at that.
If that wasn't you in there, I'd break you down, melt your parts, and sell you at a markup.
Hehehehe. Think of the people we'd scare off if we could both do that.
Always finding room for improvement.
I sent you a little something. Don't make a big deal out of it.
I like efficiency. I like getting paid. But as someone who should have asked more questions on the last job I did on my own—you trust Leramil, right? Just want to make sure.
Shame to get that curate dragged into all this. He seems young and in over his head.
You're really gonna have to carry around that soul gem with the—he can hear me, can't he? … Never mind.
Scruut seems all right. Certainly more personable than some people I've worked with before.
All that stuff you hear about Apocrypha containing horrors beyond mortal comprehension …. Those horrors seemed pretty comprehensible to me.
If I wasn't with you, I would have thought that was the normal way for a meeting of Telvanni masters to go.
Forgotten Prince? Do you think Torvesard …. Nope. Never mind. I'm not curious. Curiosity just gets people killed.
Nirn is lucky we have someone like you looking out for bad things happening in realms outside of this one. Can't say for sure if we deserve it, but we're lucky all the same.
What?
What?
What?
I hate, hate fabricants, automatons, Clockwork creatures—whatever you want to call them. \n\nHate the brass. Hate the clicking. Love to see them in pieces.
I don't like mouthing off to half-cocked adventurers. So I'll just stay quiet.
I can't decide if I don't care for people, or I just don't care for you. Probably both.
I'm here out of obligation. That's it.
I think you're good at what you do, and with me, you're even better.
Steel sharpens steel. We make each other better.
I'll just say that I don't often cross paths with people I'm glad to meet. You might be the first.
Didn't ever think I'd spend so much time traveling with another person. I'm glad it's you.
Uh … sure.
Mushy stuff, huh? All right.
Not sick of me yet?
Don't know why I bothered coming.
Broke it down for parts.
Move on, already!
Well, that was a good warm-up. What's next?
Sure, these jobs are a bit out of the way, but they always feel worth doing.
Sure, these jobs are a bit out of the way, but they always feel worth doing.
You hear that? It's like whispering, or … I don't know. I've never heard anything like it. It's probably just my imagination.
Hehehe. I love this guy. There's something comforting about knowing exactly when someone's pulling your tail.
Hehehe. I love this guy. There's something comforting about knowing exactly when someone's pulling your tail.
Surprised that didn't lead to some kind of trap.
You could brew something nice with that.
Hope they're thankful.
I owe you for that.
Should keep you on your toes a while.
Nothing like that freshly-charged feeling.
That weapon of yours can't hold out much longer.
Preparation. Love to see it.
Oh, something useful for a change.
Hey, look at that! You earned it.
Great catch! See if you can hook another.
Fix your gear! You're better than that.
Your gear's looking pretty rough.
We could have sold that, you know.
Keep your head down next time.
At least take from someone who deserves it.
Suppose you think it's better in your pocket than theirs.
Might be better off trying your luck at the end of a line.
You look fine. Really.
Can't say this beats sleeping on a bridge somewhere. But it's a fine enough place.

Federo called me a pessimist once. Didn't seem like an insult. He said a pessimist would drink beer and say it tastes like piss, while an optimist would drink piss and say it tastes like beer.\n\nMe, I don't like beer. I'd just order something else.

Dimik-ei's been writing me. She's been explaining these elaborate inside jokes we used to have together.\n\nI don't remember them, but when I read about them, I feel a strange warmth in my chest. Maybe the good parts of what I lost aren't truly gone.
The Forgotten Prince? Doesn't narrow it down, in my case. I'd just as soon forget them all.
How invigorating!
If you find a dripping pellet of crushed material, hang onto it. Quite valuable.
And the tide abates. Peerless!
And now: Violence!
I am extremely flammable!
Bah, to Apocrypha with you.
Many thanks, cohort!
My vigor wanes!
Move! Now! Please!
Focus your intellect!
Inexcusable! You're needed here!
Exceptional!
Tend to that laceration!
I sense your arcanum has drained you!
You're worn out.
Majestic!
Anomalous! Exceptional! Inconceivable!
Tentaculus Eruptum!
Together!
Hmph. I spent some time here early in my research. Bad memories, cohort.
The jewel of Auridon! And home to my favorite research lab!
Ahh, smell that air. I've been here many a time. Where to?
Keep your eyes open for a good tea shop. Always happy to try a new blend.
Always nice to discover a new smell, I suppose.
How pleasant. Drive on, cohort.
(clearing his throat, annoyed)

You have most likely noticed, but all my life I have erm. Struggled. With communication, commiseration. My intellect is attuned to a frequency all its own. But you seem to appreciate this. And thus, I appreciate you.
Mmm. Treasure over there.
Ahh, very nice. Good to settle my old bones for a bit.
Onward and upward!
Hmm, we can use this.
Hmph. Seems a waste of time.
Coin! Plunder! Commerce!
Fortuitous!
Fate must be smiling.
Hah! Your search for knowledge continues.
A servant of Mora. Is it here to keep tabs on me? Speak, minion.
A Vvardvark! Magical advancement in its most adorable, cuddly form. Look at those ears!
Key, Rite, and Door. And a name. Torvesard. I love a good mystery!
Peryite worshipers are the lowest of the loathsome. Superlative work, cohort.
If I had a coin for every ambitious idiot that went insane trying to decipher a Black Book I could pay for my own research! Hah!
I'm using every iota of restraint not to beg Mora to know what is in that Vault. I'm a professional, you see.
That Torvesard has even succeeded to this extent is astonishing. What might the Fateweaver Key see along his loci, I wonder?

Shelreni's fate is precisely why I've kept my relationship with Hermaeus Mora at tentacle's length. Daedric Princes are wells of fathomless power ... right up until they are very much not. And then you die.

A … forgotten Prince! An entire Daedric Prince! Heretofore unknown by the academic community. And thanks to our current circumstances, I can't write a paper about it? Truly, my meddling in fate has cursed me!
To have been able to play a role in restoring Apocrypha to constancy …  it's more than this scholar could ever have hoped for. Peerless as always. Peerless.

To think, my colleague is now eternally listed in a codex that sits within Mora's personal library. And I, Azandar al-Cybiades played a part in the tale. Hah! Now, what say we get some celebratory tea?
You have ceased to interest me. Speak.
You wish to engage in badinage?
What can we learn today?
I'm currently seeking new research opportunities. I hear the Ordinators out of Necrom are looking for assistance clearing dungeons both in the region and in Apocrypha. Could be fruitful!
I honestly am unsure why we still collaborate.
We are cohorts, of course. But your lack of respect has me on guard.
We still have much to do, but I'd ask you be more considerate of my boundaries.
Tentatively optimistic. I believe we can accomplish much together, you and I.
I would describe our collaboration as genial. I hope you do as well.
I'd happily make you a cup of tea.
I've become very accustomed to your presence, and you hardly irritate me at all.
Yes, certainly.
A pleasant distraction. Of course.
I'm here. What's next?
My time is valuable, and you spend it unwisely.
Yech, good riddance.
The stench! Mora's thirteenth eye!
Now that it's dead … fascinating lore behind these creatures. Compelling!
Fascinating academic material. I took rigorous notes, don't worry.
Resources acquired, and our understanding of arcane imbuement enhanced. A good day's work.
The cultural research opportunities in extra-Nirn settlements like this are … well. Incalculable!
Ah, Kozanset. My family is most likely not in town, but let's not go out of our way to find them. Agreed?
But why … wells? The meteoric iron lining the heart of these installations is exceedingly rare. Of all the shapes they could have forged, why this one?
Ahh. Can you feel it? The aetherial currents swirl here with unrealized potential. Most likely drawn by the stone itself.
Ah, a new lead! The pursuit is on! Wisdom awaits!
And: quietude. Or as best as we can get here. Let's gather our plunder and scoot.
This disjunction of the Daedric realms is extremely harrowing. But! It will make for several interesting papers.
Masterfully done! Couldn't have done it better myself.
Breathtaking! Extraordinary! How esteemed!
Ah, anything interesting?
Ah, scholarship. I can smell it from here.
[amused old man cackle]
Oh, that sounds delicious. I'd be happy to taste test it for you.
Masterful work! The fundament of the Aurbis is yours to command, it would seem.
A superlative act of craftsmanship. Exceptional skill. And an eye for detail! Hah!
From aetheric potential to a fearsome implement in your hand! Hah!
As the aetheric currents uncoil, your kit has been changed. But how? And what is your new schematic plan? Hmm.
Superlative work! The understanding of taste, technique, and texture this implies ... I am most impressed.
Ahhh, yes. Breath in the herbal bouquet.
Before you resolve the economic value of this item, might I have a chance to examine it?
Please, can we be away from here as quickly as possible? I'd like to retain the current number of apertures in my skull.
Hmm. How can you know with certitude they were telling the truth?
Hmm.
Surely you have better things you could do with your time?
Ugh. Dirt fungus.
You're sure you wouldn't like some delicious tea?
Ugh. Bean stink.
Quite a blissful environment here. Not quite how I would have decorated the place, but it's … mmm. \n\nYes. Nice.

My sanctum in Skywatch was a bit of a coup. I convinced the local Mages Guild that there were dire threats to the city down in those old ruins. Hah!  A bit of a jape, but it's certainly come in handy over the years.

I took extensive notes based on our experiences with the adversary, all in service to future research. \n\nIf one of my fatelines can skew so drastically away from my own path, what does that say about the nature of choice and chance? Galvanizing!

I still cannot get over it. An ancient secret. An entire Daedric Prince culled from every mind in existence. \n\nAnd I'm here sitting on my quill. Just goes to show that sagacity and intellect are not the same thing. Confound it!
A fascinating encounter.
Interesting place. I'll take some notes. And try not to gawp.
The sword sings.
Amazing! Look how talented I am- I mean, they are!
Hermaeus Mora! I'm here! To serve you!
Hey! Mortal! Is that what you are? Doesn't matter. Come here. Quickly!
Look! It's Herma … Hermorah … Mora … it's really him this time. I'm sure!
You don't believe me? Look!
I hope this bauble is worth the trouble of hostages.
Soon as we get our cuts, I'm going to double my money in a game of Tribute.
Oh mighty Prince! All-knowing knower of knowledge! I am your humble servant!
Another one! Do my eyes deceive me or are you truly a monster? Back away, I beg you!
Please! If you're not a monster, just back away! I will defend myself!
May your blood burn!
The clanless one's plan is clever, I grant you.
I am growing impatient. Give me a real fight.
Look about. Is this not proof of our devotion to our Prince?
I intend to please both the Taskmaster and the Dark Lady.
Who dares disturb my meditations?
Allow me to give you a taste of chaos!
You are no match for a true champion of Hermaeus Mora.
Hermaeus Mora, forgive my weakness.
Come closer. I want to properly thank you for disrupting my studies.
I don't know how you go back to your everyday life after something like this. I'd say that I'm glad it's over, but I can't imagine these Daedric Princes are done with you yet.

I thought ending up in Necrom after my unfortunate experience with that one book I can't name was not, shall we say, the best.\n\nNow I'm hearing rumors about some sort of sickness that's spreading. May the rumors be false.

Well, I've survived another bad situation. Perhaps it's time to seek passage elsewhere. No, not Elsweyr. They have Dragons.\n\nSomewhere else. With a fluffy bed and extremely thick blankets to hide under. And absolutely no cheese. Or dreams. Or books.
I like to watch people. Lately, I've seen a lot of nervous, angry, and even frightened Dark Elves.\n\nSomething interesting is happening somewhere. But that's true of every moment, isn't it?
The flow of people through Necrom is no longer disturbed.\n\nI'm glad. The rhythm they have is so peaceful to watch. Especially with good mushrooms filling your belly.

Ah, you found me. Excellent. One day I hope to have a map of my route through the peninsula, but until that happens, I rely on memory and luck. \n\nMemory to walk my route and luck to bring me customers.

I heard that people who sing loudly right now are spirited away by priests.\n\nI also heard that when a guar falls asleep at your feet, you'll have five seasons of peace. Of the two, neither has happened to me. Yet.
Ah, back to the daily rites. I grew to miss hearing the processions of the dead and the stentorian prayers of the priests.\n\nI wonder if this is my cue to start poking around other places.
I'm sure any followers of Peryite are feeling all nice and comfortable right now given the news of illness here in Necrom.
Stories claim that the foundation of Necrom consists of bones. If you're interested in learning more about that, I suggest looking around for resources about GULGA MOR JIL.
Ah, it has begun. I feel it. I must stay down in this refuge, but the events unfolding around Necrom—so delightful to observe the ripples spreading outward and nudging people into different patterns.
I must soon seek out a new place to linger. I feel the story of this place has come to a pause of sorts. Perhaps we'll meet again.
What do you think of that blend? Curious about your predilections.
Good to have that up your sleeve. Just in case.
That enchantment of yours has run dry.
Looking for some sage advice? Fine. Don't eat ash yams after drinking sujamma. You'll blow a hole through your smallclothes!
Fate's chosen. Again we meet. And in so doing the Infinium becomes mine again, as it always does.\n\nYou performed well against Graccus.
Ah, fate's chosen appears before me once again. It is I, the riddle unsolvable. The door unopenable. The book unreadable. The question unanswerable. \n\nI wonder if you understand why you are here.

Ah, fate's chosen. So you are the one the waters of destiny carried here to stop this transgression?\n\nI had watched this pathetic spirit's attempt to avoid her fate with some amusement … but I knew it would eventually come to an end.
I am the answer to all questions and the question behind every answer.\n\nFate brings you once again to my gaze, mortal. And your business here is plain to see.
I will make you scream, mortal!
Destroy Vaermina's nightmares to power my ghost sight.
You cannot resist my nightmares!
Now you die!
Look away, Mortal. You saw nothing!
Looking for your next destination? Why not give Ald Isra a try? They've got the best bittersweet, let me tell you.
We've been looking for a new deckhand. It's going to be you.
Ah, looking for a way out of Ald Isra? I admit, it's not to everyone's taste. But perhaps I presume too much.\n\nRegardless, I can get you to Necrom on Bittersweet here.
I will consume every word of your story.
From this ink I draw my strength.
I cast you from my study.
To ink I return.
I guard the entrance and so it remains locked.
You are ordinary. You will not be displayed here.
I don't think Leramil sent us this way.
They're tearing me apart.
That shirt brings out your eyes. \n\nI like a customer with a good pair of eyes. Means I can trust their judgment and enjoy their company more.
Again.
Come closer. I want to properly thank you for disrupting my studies.
I serve Vaermina, my strength is hers!
Welcome … to my nightmare!
Vaermina will haunt your dreams forever!
Your nightmare … has only just begun.
Everything's ready. Come and get it!
Curse it! The tower keeps summoning more atronachs!
You … die!

Don't let the mask fool you. We performers of the House of Reveries don't miss a thing. You may think our attention focused on a juggled blade, but in truth, our eyes never leave your smiles. No performance is complete without it after all.

It's rare to have a Reveries member removed from the troupe, but it has happened. A performer trained his pet skeevers to pick the pockets of audience members. When confronted, he said he thought it'd be fine as long as they wore costumes.

You don't look at me the way most others do, friend. So often it feels that they want to claw at my mask. Dig into these eye holes to find a buried treasure. But not you.\n\nNo. You see me as I am. As Alchemy. Material born anew. Thank you for that.
I've sailed from one end of Tamriel to the other, mostly in service to the Daggerfall Covenant. I've served on many ships, but the Spearhead was the best of them.\n\nBest vessel I ever captained.
I tend to be overly cautious. Comes from having one too many blades thrust at my back over the years.
You've come up in the world, friend. I can't believe that bit of flotsam we fished out of the waters by Stros M'Kai would turn out to be a hero like you.

Bow in the presence of Scruut! Powerful servant of Hermaeus Mora, corrector of the contradictions in fate, observer for the Great Eye! I go where the ripples of destiny lead me! \n\nBut not today. I'm having a holiday.
Are you sure this domicile is safe? I think it looks unsafe. I don't want to have to reconstitute myself if I'm squished in a completely foreseeable structure collapse.

Oh, hello mortal. I thought I sensed your ripples in the fabric of fate. You should know that Apocrypha has returned to normal. Mostly. Thanks to you. I do still get a tingle near Cipher's Midden, but that's probably just me.
Spirit, protect your king!
No such thing as a wasted day so long as we go fishing.
You will burn in their place.
This was deserved.
Enough! I'll turn your world to ash!
My other versions will carry on.
You summoned me?
Did you ask for brute force?
I make my own experiments.
Look to the sky at dawn or at night.
Tear the pages from the book.
I wouldn't want this to be too simple.
Test your strength against this.
Eyes grow cold and empty.
From ink to life and back again.
It is not over yet.
Did you think we were done?
You haven't defeated all of me.
Thus ends the tale.
You cannot kill a story.
Stories change. You end the same.
Dealing with you will be simple.
Charging external chassis.
Assistance request sent.
Come here! Xeemhok pick teeth with your bones!
Taste the blight!
What is she doing?
There's more? Why is there more?
Ink isn't supposed to do that.
Fall!
Fall!
Here—allow my friends to show you a good time!
Eat their flesh!
This will end you.
So many sheaves—orderless papers—scattered all over this maze.\n\nIt's all right, you can find them. One page at a time. You will help me again, right?
There's nothing else missing … that I know of. Oh no. Now I'm worried that's not the case. \n\nPlease, come back later. I need to do an audit of every volume in here.
Good luck. Stay vigilant out there. I'd be very disappointed if you valiantly slew the enemies outside only to miss the pages I needed.
You're back! Did you find the pages?
Your deaths won't empower the Blade, but I'll be happy to add your souls to my collection.
My wife has been dealt with. It's your turn.
This will end you.
You cannot stop Lord Bal's will!
Silence the mortals!
Now the Planemeld can begin!
You will die with your people!
Now you will know despair!
Meridia, lend me your power!
There is order in ice. Rigid and pure.
The sun warms the righteous, and scorches the worm.
Your ashes will be pure, at least.
Her light will flash from the sky and smite you.
Her will, is now your will. Rejoice.
Kneel before me, I will make you pure.
Her power is limitless, as are her legions!
I can strike from anywhere, mortal!
Let shadow flay the meat from your bones!
Watch your step!
This is the end!
Kneel before the void-crown! Kneel!
Stop goat! Don't run!
No more sweetrolls for you.
Graaah!
I'll have to lick what's left of you out of my fur.
I shall find that point where you break.
You are not the one I seek.
Well this looks different. It must be the right place.
Don't hang back now. I'd like you with me when I use Tho'at's nymic.
I hold your name and bind it here!
Your blood will fuel my growing power!
You could fight more maligraphies, but the filers say this other portal leads to a Verse.
Let me taste!
There is no escape.
Gather up so I can get a tasty look at you!
Accept my embrace!
Die, little rats!
I'll banish every last trace of you from this world.
Trade? Wares and goods for valuables? Mortal and Daedra, doesn't matter. What matters is the trade. The exchange!\n\nTake a look. See? Want? Trade.
The chill of the north lies deep in the bones of the mammoth.
Venomous serpents are the heralds of a slow and painful death.
The shalk glimpses the flame and sees only prey.
From the wamasu, I claimed thunder. Feel it course through you.
The lurcher takes its time to choke the life out of its prey. As do I.
Their sacrifice was not in vain.
Gloom hangs over us all.
Weep as I do!
Share in our grief, forever.
Bear witness to the strength of Oblivion!
You were barely a test of my strength.
Face me, coward!
You won? I … misjudged you. I won't hold back next time.
What? Never met a floating, talking doll before?
Give me a sharp knife, a mirror, and a goblet with which to catch the blood of my enemies and I can work wonders!
I know you. Yes, I was a doll. Then I wasn't. Now I am a doll again. \n\nLet's not talk about it, shall we?

Greetings! This one is Mizzik Thunderboots, investigator of mysteries, solver of crimes. Clients pay well for Mizzik's services. This one's skills at deduction are without peer. It is the violent aspects of the work that make Mizzik's fur crinkle.

Investigator Vale uses such unconventional methods in her stories. Mizzik has learned the hard way that a glass of wine is not always essential to solving a mystery. In many instances, wine presents far more problems than solutions.
Since our last adventure, Mizzik has been working on building his confidence and assertiveness! \n\nHe thinks. Maybe. Time will tell. Or perhaps it will not. Who can say for certain?
I've got to stop saying I'm no good at small talk. People take it as an open invitation to start blabbing away. Like I'll hate it less if I get some practice in or something.
Ever do much with these Undaunted you see in the city sometimes? That Mighty Mordra tried to recruit me once. Nice lady, but I don't have anything to prove to anyone.

If you ever heard Darien talk about beating me at cards, you should know those weren't exactly fair games. \n\nNot that he cheated. He was just too stupid to remember the rules and I was usually too drunk to care.
Phew. It takes a lot to kill these.
You are every book, but I am your librarian!

Copies of Tho'at Replicanum keep infecting this archive with maligraphies.\n\nI can offer you the same deal as last time. Destroy the maligraphies, find Tho'at Replicanum, and I'll reward you. How does that sound?
You fought well, but you have much to learn.
You come to challenge me? I'm flattered.
You've made it this far. Keep it up.
That was invigorating! I can't wait to fight you once more. \n\nNot yet, of course. I want to give you some time to rest and improve yourself. See how you measure up to me after some time.
You fight well, I'll have to remember that little move you pulled. Caught me completely off guard.
Well, that's one Replicanum erased. Just how many are there?
I'm going back to the Index. No one is going to try to stab me there.
With our luck, the other Replicanum know you're looking for them. Be careful.
Stay alert. Torvesard says enemies move against us.
Did you hear something?
Have faith. Many wrongs will be set right.
Torvesard expects great things from us.
I thought there'd be less standing around when I joined the Recollection.
No one's laughing at us now.
Never forget. We are meant for great things.
With every memory returned, we gain more power.
We've been cheated of our heritage. That ends now!
The path to restoration is bloody indeed.
Too scared to fight me? You can always run away.
Take your time. None of us are going anywhere.
I defeated every Oathsworn. What makes you think you can win?
The pack feasts tonight!
I didn't even need to kick you into a wall.
Dulzush! Your turn.
On your feet!
There are too many secrets here.
Join us!
Isn't it wonderful that we live in a realm that contains sights like this?
Our job isn't done yet.
What incredible fighters they were.
We won. Give up!
Calling the Oathsworn the best warriors in Tamriel will be a bit of an insult after this.
A banner? And after I defeated one of your precious lodge leaders? You'll regret that.
You'll die here!
Oh, a flag. Do you think that will change the outcome?
Hit them, construct!
I can withstand the forge's fire and you think challenging me is a good choice? Ha!
The Recollection will not fall to the likes of you!
Pay for your curiosity in my trial.
You ran out of blood. The trial is mine!
Blood determines the victor!
You need time to think. Conquest takes precision.
Don't be embarrassed, few survive the trials.
Concentrate on conquering territory.
Having second thoughts? You can turn away from the trial if you're intimidated.
Armies fall apart without their leaders.
Defeat me, but have more atronachs when you do!
Torvesard has revealed the many paths before us.
I remember. I remember it all.
They're going to see we were right. They all will!
Give me one good fight. Just one.
Too late. Thank you for trying.
Hurry! I can't keep myself together.
Oh no. The ghost lights. Bring them back to me.
Goodbye, delicious frog.
Hurry! I want to get this froggy aftertaste out of my mouth.
You saw nothing! Except my ghost lights. I need those.
You won't get the treasure without me.
If you want a piece of my treasure, you better speed up.
You startled me. You gather my lights.
It seems as though my practice is over for now.
Hurry! I can't practice in this state.
So many spells, but none to gather all my ghost lights.
Well, now we know who we're going to haunt.
Hurry, you don't have much time left.
My friend says you shouldn't have done that.
That smell! A mortal is near.
We have forgotten ourselves for so long.
I will not be confined again.
Mirrormoor shall rise again!
Ready yourselves and strike true!
What a pitiful realm this is!
For Clan Shardborn! For Mirrormoor!
No one must pass. Torvesard commands it.
That was fast. Report, mercenary!
Everything is recorded and official. Now get to it. The sooner you complete the task, the sooner you get paid.
Count Calantius has authorized the Imperial Legion of West Weald to hire capable individuals to handle delicate situations throughout the region. Would you be interested perhaps?
No more work available today. I must finish these reports for Count Calantius. Return tomorrow and I am sure to offer you something intriguing.
Have you completed your task? I'm eager to get the report filed away.
I appreciate your help. My superiors are pleased with my results lately, which would be a point of pride, if it didn't mean they keep giving me more to do.
I have more problems than soldiers to handle them. Please tell me you're available to lend your strength to the Legion for a time.
Incredibly, I don't have any work at the moment. The calm before the storm, I suppose.
Ah, you're back! The West Weald Legion could use your help again, adventurer. The battle against the Daedra invading our world does not go well.
I can see you're ready for another round with Mirrormoor's forces. Unfortunately, I can't hire you on at this moment. Check back again later, hero.

Onsi be praised! It shouldn't take you long to find an incursion.\n\nYou must defeat the Mirrormoor champion leading the attack to repel its incursion. But first, you must eliminate the Shardborn valkynazes who protect it. Good hunting, hero!
Ah, you return! Do you come bearing a report of victory, adventurer?
We're whole again!
Your mortal appendages are useless. I can fix that.
No more tomeshells? Good. I can file all those books.
Maybe the problem isn't with the mortal form. All right, I'll turn you back.
Deal with the tomeshells. I have filing to do.
Lure them over here!
Over here, friend!
Get back here!
Stop ruining my garden!
What have you done?
You killed my husband!
We'll eat well tonight.
Right behind you, friend.
Hmm. That's a strange looking thing.
Someone help me!
I'd be mulch if not for you. Y'ffre bless you!
How dare you harm my children!
I will avenge my children!
Hey! What's that?
Fire brings life, but not for you.
I saw something hop in this barrel! Take a look!
The pit will claim your bones.
Well, you have fun with that!
Death comes from above!
My illusions will engulf all of West Weald!
See only what I want you to!
Witness the power of the Recollection!
None can stand against my illusions.
The Recollection will remember!
Wh—what's happening?
I can't … move away .…
My head … is clear again!
I—I don't hear the music anymore!
Thank you for setting us free! The Green bless you!
We'd still be their puppets if not for you! Y'ffre bless you.
Count Calantius has done a good enough job, for an Imperial. But he should keep his legion at home.
Ugh, studying is such a bore.
It's best not to ask too many questions.
It is less egregiously hostile here.
You gave the pesky maligraphies a sound thrashing.
Is it over? Good, good. Now I can get that book Malkhest needed.
At last, the ink creatures are gone and I can resume my work.
Have a taste of the fires that will claim you.
I must perceive the forthcoming. For the accounts.
What a fine time it is for bloodshed and violence!
You should have seen the state of this wing before we filed it.
Oh great, you haven't started yet.
Modulate yourself for a tactical advantage.
Go on. Hit them. Hit them!
This is so exciting!
I heard that you fight well for a creature without eye beams.
You dare harm my mushrooms?
Where have my friends gone? They better not have started drinking without me!
I swear I heard little claws scratching.
My scales feel like sun-baked stones.
I don't need your money. My husband is a prince, you know. I'm sure he'll be back soon.
I only fight for a worthy cause.
What's the deal with that new forest?
Where can I find a mug of rotmeth?
There's work for everyone! And more importantly, wine!
I hear they call the new forest Dawnwood.
I'll take any coins you don't want, visitor. I know how to spend them!
Dawnwood is beautiful don't you think?
I can't wait to explore an Ayleid ruin!
Every tree is part of Y'ffre's domain.
Safer to be here than my usual haunts.
The Mages Guild has too many rules.
They sure know how to prepare meat around here. Blunt as a cudgel with their words, though.
Our town grows larger every day!
I haven't had any success hunting today.
There's plenty of meat to be had in Dawnwood!
We need to be prepared, just in case.
Toss a coin to a hungry stranger!
The Divines look kindly upon a generous soul. Won't you spare just a little coin?
Real soldiers know how to take a hit.
Where did I put my leeches?
The Legion will protect us.
The gossip about angry Wood Elves can't be true.
My honor is worth more than a bag of coins.
I told my dearest not to leave! Now I'm all alone here.
Doesn't anybody want to spar?
I plan to return to Necrom and become an Oathman, like my sister.
So many lovely things for sale!
Magic makes life easier.
I appreciate that the Wood Elves welcomed me into their community.
Come closer, friend! One touch and I'll share with you the blessing of Peryite!
Ah, the clink of coins. I love the bank.
Are there no revels in this town?
My brother just joined the Legion.
Let's see. I have turnips for the salad. Need to find some carrots. And pears! That's what I forgot. Pears!
We are surrounded by reminders of the Ayleids. We built our empire on the bones of titans.
What are the ranchers up to this time?
Each little grape holds an infinite number of possibilities. I love that about them.
Curse the legion! Kick me out, called me a deserter. The fools!
I wish the count would let me design the Legion uniforms. I'm sure I could come up with something better than those gaudy crests.
Finding that thief is hopeless.
It takes many years to become a strong warrior.
This one must tend to her duties.
Is there really honor among outlaws?
This one could use new greaves. But the old ones might hold up for another season or two.
Wood Elves think they're tough, but this one can out-drink them all!
So many people in town these days!
That Medallus Valerius, such a noble soul! Always looking out for people like me.
Through Zenithar's grace, I have caught the biggest fish!
My back is sore!
Lift and carry, lift and carry ….
I'm so happy I could dance!
The Divines will protect.
I must speak with Count Calantius about the sorry state of the city's walls.
I'm not a criminal!
This city is so confusing.
Bears aren't scary. You know what's scary? Skeevers!
Ach, my shoulder!
Ah, the start of another fine day in Skingrad! I can't wait to get to work!
The longer you temper the steel, the stronger the sword will be.
Where did he go? We were in the middle of an argument.
What's with all the adventurers?
Blast it! The fencing for the new vineyards didn't arrive. We can break up some old barrels, but that's just a half-measure.
A sharpened sword cuts both ways.
I need to find a better job.
Seems like all I ever do is pack.
Feel my head! Am I hot?
I lost many friends to the fever.
The afterlife has plenty of room for all. Point to my next target and I will send them there!
You need to listen to your material.
I hope I don't get the fever.
A new constable? What happened to the old one?
The people of Ontus need to learn more about hunting.
Tava's red feathers! My deepest apologies!
A short visit, than back to the Legion.
Why do I bother? I never win.
I find ordering and cataloging the volumes favorable to being assailed by them.
Those creatures may have superior forces, but we have what they lack. Fleshy limbs and a good, violent disposition!
I hope you're not expecting me to volunteer to go in there with you. That's not my purpose here. And frankly, I can't fight.
The problems here aren't small. If you think you can solve them, be my guest.
Kindly die now.
Hmm, I should have toyed with them a little longer.
Care to dance?
Who's next?
Look at me when I'm fighting you!
Euch! This place smells disgusting. And weirdly salty.
Watch your step, this ground is unfamiliar to us.
You won't stop our search!
You're not following the path!
I want to see how this creature fights.
I've never been affected by a Mind Terror. I wonder, will it affect you?
It appears that they couldn't beat the Atronach, master.
Do you think they noticed they were dying?
You had no chance. The Echonir is mine.
Riddle them with holes.
This place feels … moist.
You're not supposed to be here.
This place sounds strange. I don't like it.
You can't stop us!
Do you even know what this is for? Stop poking it then!
You made it far, but you go no further.
We're not here to relax or rest. Stop getting distracted!
You want a challenge? I'm sure you'll get it.
You're challenging this creature? This will be very entertaining.
This is so exciting!
Here they go!
You think that was wise?
You will regret getting in my way!
There is no escape!
Kneel!
Back, vermin!
The storm approaches ….
Your wards are weak!
The vampires are dangerous. We need to be on guard.
Official business. Don't come any closer.
I have suffered your interference long enough, outsider!
Might not be a bloodsucker anymore, but I can still hunt with the best of them.
Thank you, stranger. May the Divines bless you.
The Moons have forsaken you! All that remains is shadow and death!
All of you will burn!
Proximity sensors engaged.
Responding to hostile behavior.
Damage critical. Shutting down.
I stomp them to pieces!
So bold! Yes! Test my strength! Feel it bear down upon you like the weight of a thousand seas!
A formidable effort. Alas, you are nothing without the shell of my power.
It could be worse. We could have left them alive.
Anyone else keeping notes on what the Oathsworn do? No?
Work's not over yet!
You aren't Recollection.
Jerky, jerky, and more jerky. I want fresh meat!
The egos on these Orcs. Phew.
Tear their limbs off!
You won't make it out of here.
This place is far from cozy. I hope they didn't sleep here.
These lodges are enormous.
Burn them!
Make the Recollection proud!
When all this is over, the pit wouldn't be a half bad vacation spot.
Do you think I could sharpen my blades on these rocks?
There's life left in the Oathsworn.
Come here. I want to cut you.

Don't complain to me if you want something that's not available. Mortals and their lack of patience. It's like you haven't waited an eon to set your eyes on the book you really need. \n\nSo, yes. Take a look, but don't complain.
What you're wearing now couldn't stop a branch in a windstorm. No, you need Azimurr's famous armor. Best quality in Skingrad. Stops all blows from snapping your bones. Azimurr guarantees it.
My customers always say that my wares have dual purposes. Get it? Weapons? Duel? Ha! I slay me! Get it? Slay? Anyway, have a look.
The master mages need to stop dueling the adepts. It's not fair.
Me? You trust me with your gold? Not that you shouldn't! It's just that some people think Orcs aren't good with numbers. I am though. Really good.\n\nUm, what can I help you with?
Vyla uxun, vyla vesek. Vyla uxun, vyla vesek.
Are we at war with Vashabar? I've heard conflicting stories about the Wood Elves and I'm very confused.

Skingrad's trading guilds just don't accept anyone, friend. You need to know someone who knows someone. Connections, you understand?\n\nIf you ever want an introduction, I am sure we can come to an arrangement.
Simple laborers deserve respect, too. I may not be heading off to join the Legion anytime soon, but that doesn't mean I want to be snapped at for the smallest mistake.
I have always believed that adopting the ways of other lands is not good for Redguards. But I must go where my people go if I am to safeguard our traditions.
I admit I entertained some ugly suspicions about the people of Vashabar. I am … relieved … to hear that they, too, were deceived by their king.
I feared that it was a mistake for my people to come here. But now that the Recollection has been exposed and defeated, I deem things are changing for the better.
Like a lion that prowls one's camp at night before moving on, a great danger has passed us by. Something strange, unseen by all but a few. I have a feeling you perceive it too.

I once downed an entire bottle of Skingrad muscat in one long draw. You're supposed to sip it, but I'm not much of a sipper.\n\nStuff had more kick than I expected. Bitter, too. Not what I expected from these Skingrad vineyards.
There is always work for those with sharp knives and silent steps. I have both, and Ontus has a plethora of disgruntled residents. If you practice the same trade I do, move on. This is my town.

My wife isn't sure we should have come to Ontus. I tell her everything will be all right—the work is plentiful, the streets are safe, and the Colovians are friendly. None of it's true, but it makes her feel better.
I wish my husband believed in himself more. I'm sure he could find work if he was just a little more confident. I'll pray to Zeht to make the farms here flourish. Then, there will be plenty of work.

There is room for all in service to the Prince of Trickery and Bargains! My master handsomely rewards those who obey his commandments. Abandon your foolish quests, and join with the illustrious Clavicus Vile.
The Legion let me come home to help my family after my mother died from the fever. I hear the new constable is a legionary, too.
Mud, muck, and filth of all kinds! It never ends! Travelers are disgusting.
Have you ever seen anything as magnificent as a glassfish in the current? Many people think fish are simple creatures, but that's not true. There's much we can learn by studying them.
I quit my job at the quarry. Decided my time was better spent here with my bees.
I despise Colovian wine. It's too sweet and it makes my scales itch. It's disgusting.
Winemaking is an art, especially here in the Weald. Much more important than ranching or quarrying. Ontus would be better off if we planted more vineyards.
Vyla uxun, vyla vesek. Vyla uxun, vyla vesek.

A fine home. I will have my Black Fins perform a security sweep. Nothing too intrusive. Just a check of all the ingresses and egresses. Maybe interrogate a few of the other guests and servants. Can never be too careful about the comings and goings.

Having disposed of Dres slavers in my early years, I was recently asked to consult on a manuscript of "The Green Hood and the Dres Slavers."\n\nI found it to be fanciful, unpolished, and derivative. Has all the makings of the next best-seller.

Good to see someone I trust, mercenary. After Vandacia revealed his treachery, I gave much thought to the duplicity of others close to me. It is with great effort that I face each new day fighting to fend off needless suspicion of my alliances.

I am Kor! Hunter, soldier, brother to Hildegard by love if not blood. And I happen to be part of a larger family. A dark brotherhood, you might say.\n\nBut if you mention a word about such things, I'd have to kill you. Seriously.
These times certainly are strange. I don't know what to make of that business with Nantharion, but it does my heart good to know the Wood Elves were never truly our enemies.
One thing at a time, that's what my father always told me. Today, we are safe from the nefarious plot of the Recollection. That is no small thing!
It does my heart good to see all this chaos cleared up. In fact, I can't seem to remember what the fuss was about in the first place ….

The Night Mother? Of course I know the stories about the Night Mother! But I know better than to repeat them! Don't you know she hears anyone who speaks to or about her? Now look what you did! She's probably listening right now!
It matters not where the Wood Elves' allegiance lies. I care only that my blade is sharp and sure, and my target is clear.
The people of Skingrad think they're safe simply because the Recollection has been thwarted. They forget that there are always enemies—even within the walls of their city.
My mind is usually as sharp as my blades, but something doesn't feel right. It's as though my thoughts have been blunted. Am I losing my edge?

Good to see you again, Silencer. Always pleasant to visit with a member of the family! Well, for the most part. Elam can be a bit draining to spend time with. Very judgmental. And let's not talk about Speaker Terenus. He scares me.
Hildegard's around here somewhere, looking for the privy. I hope she finds it. In her werewolf form, she's not too choosy about where she answers nature's call.
You have Hircine's Gift, if I'm not mistaken. Just like my little sister. Always nice to meet one of the pack, as it were.

Not to be one of those big brothers, but I couldn't help thinking about you and Hilde. You're both accomplished in your field. You have a lot in common. And you're both werewolves. That must be why the two of you get along so well.

Call me Hildegard. Or Hilde. I don't mind. My brother Kor calls me that. Or little one. He is larger than me, at least while I'm in this form. We're part of the Dark Brotherhood, but that's a secret. And I'm a werewolf. I guess that's a secret, too.

My friend told me to meet him here, but I seem to have forgotten when we arranged to meet. Was it supposed to be yesterday, perhaps? Or maybe he simply hasn't arrived yet. I'm not sure. I'll just wait.

Do you smell that? Wait, now it's gone. No, there it is again! A rat, maybe? Or some other vermin?\n\nOh, sorry. Don't take offense. There are so many different smells here. It takes time to get used to.
Out of my way, traveler. I may have been dismissed from the Legion but that doesn't mean I'm ill-prepared for a fight.
I have a nagging feeling I've forgotten something. Eh, it's probably the amount of wine I've had recently.

Oh, Silencer, it's good to see you! I've missed you terribly! And about that conversation we had, the time I abandoned our family? I remember everything you said. I may not have shown it at the time, but it helped. It really did.

When they invited Kor over, I hope they didn't expect a quiet evening. My sweet brother thinks a shout is the same as a whisper. Just be prepared for good mead and loud boasting.\n\nI wouldn't have it any other way.

You're a werewolf, like me. Do you remember your first transformation? Mine was painful and scary. All I had ever known was one body, and then suddenly I began to change against my will. It's good to talk to someone who can understand that.

If you don't mind me asking, you're a werewolf, aren't you? Oh, don't be concerned. I can tell. It's not hard to spot another member of the pack. I don't go out of my way, but when I encounter a fellow were-creature, I like to compare notes.
All this fuss about Nantharion! He's dead, that's it. At least with everyone so distracted, drills are canceled for now.
Sigh. Nothing ever happens around here. It's always the same story. Quash the rebellion. Stop the Daedra. Protect the count. It's mind-numbing.
Legionaries tell the best stories! Blood, battle, beasts—it's thrilling! I'm no good in combat, but I'd love to see some action one day.
Are you new here, traveler? This one can help. She finds the Colovians a bit particular, but complimenting their wine and buildings will have them purring and lapping the moon sugar out of your paws.
Last week I saw a legionary cut down an attacking Daedra. It was incredible! I heard you couldn't kill Daedra, but it fell like a tree to a logger's axe!
No, no, no. There cannot be a realm called Mirrormoor. It defies everything we know about the Daedra! Ugh, all this uncertainty is making my tail twitch.

You forget to place one little glyph on one little sword, and all of a sudden everyone's pointing fingers at you. What were they doing that was so important? Training? I was on a very good part of my book!
What brings you here, traveler? Everyone comes here for something. Coin. Glory. Work. It's the main draw of Skingrad—there are opportunities everywhere. If you know where to look.
Good show! Master Malkhest requires this fragment. So I'll just pop it over to him, shall I?
Master Malkhest instructed me to retrieve this fragment for him.

Life here is so different from Summerset. There are opportunities to be found in Skingrad, but there is also strife. The people are restless and rash. It's something the High Elves of my homeland would never stoop to.
I'm not sure what to make of the news about Nantharion. He was undoubtedly a villain, but I concede that this is a difficult time for the Wood Elves. It's akin to the upheaval here in the Empire.

Shh! Don't be suspicious. We're not doing anything illegal—at the moment, anyway—but the Legion knows my face and they're always looking for a reason to toss me in the stocks. My neck is still sore from last time.
Keep your wits about you in this city. Wood Elves aren't the only ones who are good at thieving. In fact, you may want to sew your pockets shut.
My turn to pick the nymic fragment out of an ink puddle. I'm ecstatic.
Let me just grab this fragment. Nothing to see here.
Compared to the might of Hircine, the Divines are nothing but fairy tales for children. We Reachfolk know the truth—real gods demand sacrifice. That's why we abide by the Law of the Fair Hunt.
Oh, traveler. Don't despair. Dibella cannot bless us all. Could we recognize true beauty if everyone was blessed this way? Even homely creatures like yourself have a place in Akatosh's plan.

Have you been to the temple of Julianos, traveler? It's a fascinating place! Oh, my tail twitches just thinking about it. A sacred site constructed for the worship of an intangible god of logic. How deliciously illogical!
Long live West Weald! Will our victories never cease? I suspect they'll have to at some point. Sooner or later, we're bound to run out of enemies to vanquish.
You performed marvelously. Claim your reward and travel to the next batch of vile enemies.
