First of the Earth Bones, who sang the songs the seas and birds now carry in their hearts ….
Don't touch that! That's Y'ffre's wood!
According to this author, the Khajiit actually come from the moon. Pretty strange, isn't that?
I really don't enjoy the thought of sitting on something with a face on it.
There was a time when I thought Montclair was a decent man. I guess he had me fooled.
Harsh, swift justice is the best. Baron Dorell won't let this Montclair madness continue.
Fools! Fearing death is cowardly, but rushing headlong into it is stupid!
You want more lightning? I have plenty to go around!

Do try to avoid any undue noise. I am studying the cultures of Valenwood, to best ease our work in the region.\n\nObviously, the Bosmer are primarily carnivores. This extends to their liquors, the majority of which are comprised of meat and mold. Odd.
How could anyone hope to eat this? It is worse than bile!
<Crowd cheers loudly.>
<Person gasps loudly.>
They pulled these thoughts from Sai's head? I don't understand!
Must be careful. Don't want to harm them.

I'm very interested in all of these plants that just grow like this within the Elden Tree. My interest as an alchemist is piqued, but if I cannot harvest these things ….\n\nI just collect their leaves and petals that fall. Perhaps I can use them.
This one is thinking he could cope with a High Elf's height, but they are so often concerned with order and control.\n\nIt doesn't feel right. <<1>> cannot live in such chains, you know?

I am not proposing that the Bosmer could not have done this, but it seems unlikely. It does not seem Ayleid in origin, either. And these engravings … what could they mean?\n\nIt is a mystery. To me, at least. And I am a learned scholar.
These engravings, yes … yes.
Do you think he's considered the Green Pact? Or, really, do you think he knows anything about us?\n\nCould he really have come out here to explore our culture with no idea what we're like whatsoever?

If Sabibi were to climb the inside of this tree, do you suppose the Bosmer would take issue? It is just a climb, after all. This one merely wishes to have a better look at the apex of this chamber, where the tree meets the tree.
He batters the shore like angry waves. The sand washes away, but the strongest rocks remain.

There's a correlation between distance from Morrowind and probability someone will be more open when talking to me, I've noticed. I blame the Telvanni.\n\nPeople were fairly cold in Black Marsh and Anequina. Here, people have been more friendly.
Is this the tallest tree in all of Tamriel? Probably all of Nirn, come to think of it.

Bosmer have a reputation as peerless archers. It's hard to practice as an archer with that lingering over you, because there'll always be someone heckling you about it.\n\n"Hey, you're a Bosmer, shouldn't you already be a master?" It's foolish.
I prefer to do my reading out here. Learned tourists pass by, and I can talk to them about theory and practice.\n\nI like that. I never know if I'm bothering them, though.
My commissions require me to travel across half of Tamriel. I am to see most of the Dominion's lands! It is already quite interesting.
Oh! Mind the light, please.
Come along. There's plenty more to see!

During the Blacksap rebellion, this bridge was demolished by Colovian mercenaries marching to join <<1>> at <<2>>. The magic granted us by the Green Pact has since regrown it, but you can still smell the ash.
Greetings. Uh, if you want to hear a story I guess I can tell you one.\n\nI'm just full of stories, because I'm a Spinner. We're made of fiction, haven't you heard?

I speak, and through me sings Y'ffre. My tales are echoes of echoes of songs He once sang, of threads woven by his throat into tapestries ingrained in the minds of we faithful. The calls of birds, twinkles of stars, and lap of the sea live within me.
Their lead holds the reins of the charge—they will not persist after the fall.

A lot of us here enjoy meeting new people. I know I certainly do—but with the traffic we're getting through Elden Root it's impossible to keep up.\n\nI basically sleep down here, now. It's very strange!
Victory. Was there any doubt?

As much as I miss the more colorful gardens back in Summerset, the range of greens one finds here is quite appealing.\n\nIf it is possible to do so, I would love to bring a seedling back home for cultivation.
I'll feast on your blood!
Pathetic mortal!
Junk. All of this is junk, junk, junk.
Soon, this one must return to S'ren-ja. Hopefully, he leaves with good things.

Hello! You're here for a meal, correct? I mean, I don't want to be too forward or assume too much about your presence in my kitchen.\n\nSurely it's for food, and not any sort of official business, I mean. I'm just a cook, after all!
Have you found the tome?
Have you found the one I asked you to look for?
You seem a little too serious. Why don't you have a seat and relax?\n\nCome to think of it, everyone around here has been powerful serious lately. Maybe it's in the water.
I've been getting this feeling around town lately that someone's been watching me. Isn't that strange?\n\nCormount is such a lovely town, I can't imagine why that would be the case. What a mystery!
One of my favourite things about Grahtwood is the way the stars look through the tree canopy. It really is quite lovely.\n\nBut I'm letting myself grow distracted! How may I help you?
We'll find it. It must be around here.
I'm growing hungry. I should stop by Mongoth's, I think.
I never know where I'm going in Cormount. That's all right, though.
By the Divines, I had no idea death would be so boring. Literally nothing happens. Let that be a fair warning to you, adventurer!
Hello. I think Cormount is a fine town, I do. I see some people in town do not, and that is their opinion and their business.\n\nBut it is fine to me.
I'm not actually from anywhere in Valenwood. I guess that makes me rare, as Bosmer go.\n\nFrankly, I'm sick of it. I like being able to see the sky. I miss Reaper's March.
Someday, I might know what's happening outside of <<1>>. I snatch reports occasionally, just to look at them, but I always put them back.\n\nI wish I knew how to read.

I think the one thing I miss most about living further inland is the vegetables.

I never thought I'd say this, but I really miss potatoes, carrots, and cabbage. And, uh, fruit.

Really anything but fish and oysters would be nice at this point.

I think when this whole 'war' business blows over, I'm going to pack up and move to the Alik'r desert, or Anequina, or somewhere where they don't have bays like this.\n\nI'd frankly be happy to never see water again outside of an oasis.
I think I'd rather be on an island. I'd like that. Plenty of time to think.
There are weapons in the forge beyond these cells. Arm yourself!
Courage, Vestige. Confidence is a beast that grows two heads for each that is cut off.
I thought for sure they would be back by now.
I used to love the weather around here, but now I just find it very gloomy.
I know they're blaming Montclair for all our troubles, but if you ask me, none of our nobles are worth a drop of troll spit!
Honestly, I don't even know how to start rebuilding my livelihood.
Now that the Montclair threat has been dealt with, the city of Shornhelm can get back to more important matters.
The nobles have a lot of work ahead of them if they want us all to feel safe and secure again.
If you ask me, I think there's something not quite right with that Count Ravenwatch. He gives me the frights, and I don't mind admitting that.
Surely, there is a way.
Heed me, Daedric minions, and obey!
You're going the wrong way.
Countess Tamrith has learned her lessons well. She has taken the teachings of Arkay to her heart and basks in his brilliant Light. She's just a lovely young woman.
I think Zeli is constantly praying to herself. Her muttering is driving me crazy.
Don't let them reach the top!
I'm sure I got that spell right. What in Oblivion happened?
No! The spell failed! Stay away!
Please. Let me go.
All three of its eyes are staring at me!
Shornhelm is an old city, we've withstood plagues, wars and other disasters.
There seems to be problems all over Rivenspire these days.
Countess Tamrith thinks before she acts. I appreciate that in a leader.
Those Montclair traitors won't get away with this. Baron Dorell will see to that!
Do Wood Orcs fear horses? I couldn't stop them from whinnying while we hid.\n\nThat would be ridiculous. Wood Orcs, afraid of horses? Hmph.
Take caution you don't end up like those frozen soldiers.
You saw nothing and no one. Got it?
Do you often root through stranger's belongings?
I can handle these pitiful creatures.
How courageous of you. Ill advised, but courageous.
This one expected a better class of villain.
By chaos, by the void, and by the darkness, may the doors of Oblivion be flung wide!
My dearest Arlie. Who would harm such a vision of grace?
It's as if the air itself is catching flame ….
Ugh … it's getting hard to breathe.
Still nothing. Damn.
Nope. No, it's stopped again.
Maybe you should try the one you haven't done, last?
Funny, it smells like brimstone in here.
Aldmeri grandeur!
Ebonheart honor!
For the Covenant!
It seems the mages have taken some liberties with our temple, an offense we will not readily forgive.\n\nAs the Three-In-One are my guide, so too am I their hands in this. Their… scolding hands.
Woo!
<evil laughter 2>
Creating layers of flavors and aromas to appeal to people is a fine art, and anyone can do it if they try.
Hungry, eh? I know the feeling. Mushrooms and bugs may be enough for these Dark Elves, but a Nord needs meat!
I came up with the name Outside Inn, because we're just outside of the Elden Root. Get it? Outside Inn?  I'm pretty clever that way!
Look at you! All skin and bones! You must be hungry. Come, come. Eat, eat!
Summon the blood sacrifice.
God of Schemes, we offer this victim to honor you!
Bind this world with your chains! Draw it ever closer to your realm!
Let Coldharbour remake Nirn in its own image!
Through the power of innocent blood, bring forth your anchor and let two worlds become one!
I want no trouble.
Fortune doesn't favor the Kothringi.
May the light keep you in its warm and soothing embrace.
Why is everything moving so much? It feels like I'm still out on my boat.
Get away from that!
Hey! I'm leaving that there to ripen!
Now get off my dock.
I enjoy a good bargain. Bargains are better than slaughtering useless mortals. Usually.
It wasn't my plan, to end up here in Coldharbour, but I always try make the best of a bad situation. So now I have this little trading post.
Hello, dear adventurer! Have you any need of magical goods, supplies, or equipment? For should you have such a need, I can meet it!\n\nIf you have no such need, you should probably go.
Molag Bal hates this city. It must really tweak his horns that he can't do anything about it.
I wish I could remember how I ended up here.
I can't wait to take the fight to Molag Bal.
I'm ready to take the fight to Molag Bal. Well. As ready as I'll ever be, I suppose.
Councilor Ralden has finally decided to take action. I must say, it's about time.
I was invited to a meeting with some of the townsfolk. All very hush-hush. They won't even tell me where the meeting is taking place until the last possible moment.
Narsis is in good care, what with both Ralden and Giron watching out for us.
It was the Maulborn, wasn't it? I knew they seemed too good to be true!
Why would Giron betray Narsis or his friend, Ralden? It makes no sense to me.
Maybe the townsfolk have the right idea. Maybe we do need to take matters into our own hands.
To think I supported Giron! The man is less than kwama droppings!
How could things get so out of hand? I blame the Argonians. Ever since they were given their freedom, Morrowind hasn't been the same.
I heard Varon mentioned the name Vox. I've heard that name somewhere. If only I could remember where and when. I'm sure it will come back to me—eventually.
The last time anyone tried to crack open my vault, he died. He died because I hit him.\n\nThat's security you can trust. That's the gro-Dugronk promise.
Need a bag? A haversack? Knapsack, backpack, or satchel? You will find none finer!
Have you seen the forest spirit? I think it wants us to leave.
Don't dally! We have a schedule to keep.
Defend the camp!
I got a few mounts to sell, if you're interested. And no, members of the Lion Guard or the High King's army don't get a discount. Prime stock requires solid gold.
The guardians just ripped the rest of the Wood Orcs to shreds. I swear—it's just incredible to watch them work.
Come! Indulge! Buy one of this one's beautiful bags!
The best thing any adventurer could do is pick up a larger bag.\n\nAfter all, when you're going to carelessly toss your things somewhere, the bigger that somewhere is, the better! Right?
Some day I'll hawk enough bags to finally get out off this rock.\n\nI don't even remember how I got here, but the locals seem tired of me crabbing about the cold—so I should just move on.
With the Red Rooks gone, I can bring my mounts back to the stables. I took them far away from here when I figured out what those sneaky bandits were up to.
Where do you think you're going?
Interested in purchasing a mount? My beauties are better than any you'd find in a city like Wayrest.
This will make you feel much better, I assure you.
Come at me!
Don't be timid!
Oof! I yield, friend. Good fight!
All right, you got me. Say, you're not bad!
Those who serve me never stay dead.
It's very strange, Reaper's March. Very unlike Black Marsh, yet similar in some ways.\n\nMakes me a bit homesick. But, the Mages Guild demands I travel.
I tend horses, yes. They aren't my life. I wish people would stop asking me random questions about them. It's really quite irritating.
The end of the world is unavoidable. Chaos is inevitable. The Serpent wills it so.
The calf weathers a rain of swords.
Crumble!
The lightning crashes!
<Straining grunt.>
The mountain falls.
The sword sings.
From aegis to cudgel.
The hammered blade sparks.
This battle was over before the sword ever left its sheath.
First-blood goes to the calves.
"Come no closer" said the ghost, so M'aiq did not. But she kept saying it, wherever he went.
The Elves here have so many titles, all of them fancy. M'aiq prefers a simple one.
Why the need for embassies? M'aiq thinks all are ambassadors, wherever they go.
Sea Elves? Do you see Elves, from the sea?
Wood Orcs are Orcs who live in the woods, yes? If they were made of wood, M'aiq thinks they'd stop using torches.
The Moon Priests have many strange rules and stories. But M'aiq thinks they make it up as they go along.
M'aiq wonders why no guards stand watch on the mushrooms. They are taller than towers and far more comfortable.
M'aiq learned the Brothers of Strife are either volcanoes or Elves. If one of each, their mother could have some explaining.
What if the ordinators are the Dark Elf gods, hiding among their people? M'aiq avoids them, just the same.
M'aiq regrets few things. Failing to wear boots in a swamp is one of them.
It is so cold here, yet M'aiq sees Nords in sandals. Madness!
M'aiq could never fight for prizes. He has a weak chin.
M'aiq has never seen so many Orcs in one place. Even their forges have forges.
M'aiq's father was Qia'm, from a long line of Qia'ms. But M'aiq does not believe this. His father was a known liar.
M'aiq had a horrible dream last night. Mudcrabs, flying through the air. Horrible!
M'aiq despises bats. Tiny, winged skeevers. Disgusting!
Redguards fear the undead, but why? The gnawing upon the flesh? The stench of death? Hmm. Perhaps M'aiq understands.
M'aiq once met Captain Blackheart and his raiders. M'aiq can think of a better word to describe them.
Do not drink the water that glows. M'aiq learned this the hard way.
Some like to buy the whole meal. Others want to pay for what is on their plate. M'aiq just prefers to eat.
M'aiq used to travel alone, but he has grown accustomed to joining his friends.
M'aiq fishes wherever there is water. He finds it is far less crowded.
Nocturnal's breath!
Oy! To me!
That was your last mistake!
You said we weren't carrying valuables!
You said this was a shortcut!
"Take the high road," you said! "It's safer," you said!
Stay out of the way! You'll get yourself killed!
Still like water … smooth like mud!
You said we'd be safe! This is not safe!
We escape now, yes?
Do you think this is the best time to bicker?
Next time I hire from the Fighters Guild!
What, still not dead? Strike harder!
You weren't supposed to interfere!
Flames take you, s'wit!
Char your skin! Snap your spine!
To Oblivion with you!
You think you'll get the best of me? Ha!
Hail Sithis!
There is no hope. You're already lost!
Fires of the forge, strike hot!
There won't be enough of your heart to eat!
Frozen sands await you!
That must be impressive, where you're from.
You call this a duel? Stop holding back!
Your fear is a monsoon!
False Emperor!
The war chief has plans for us.
Split-Nose hears much of what happens in town. I, uh—"he" does not care.
The Celestial Mage has summoned me to stop you—she did not say I could not feast on you.
You will regret this, mortals!
How many of us can you handle?
This one is wasted as a laborer. Sahalu is management material.
Flames of Yokuda take you!
The sapling burns!
A dying flame rekindled!
This doesn't concern you, outsider.
Not there!
Did you figure that out for yourself?
The magistrate has no honor.
I cannot stop my armory from growing.
You will regret coming this far.
You will not survive this!
Prepare yourself. The Learned One will not suffer your presence.
The renewed Ra Gada will strike you down.
You're here for adventure, aren't you? You should buy some of my wares.\n\nBecause when I run out, I get to be somewhere else. Setting fire to something.

This one told the other Undaunted she would sell the wares for a while. She just wanted them to think better of her.\n\nBut now they make her do it all the time. This one has learned a sobering lesson: never be nice to friends.
Come on. Buy something.\n\nI'd rather be stabbing beasts, and the sooner I unload these wares, the sooner that can happen.
Look, we don't get many customers around here. I'd appreciate it if you bought something so that I can fund fights with Welwa and leaping off roofs.\n\nYou know. Undaunted fare.
My friends are savages. And I think you just outdid them.
M'aiq heard there are caves full of spiders and whispers. He prefers the spiders.
You're nothing to me.
Please, no!
Ready to fire!
Summoning protection!
Make ashes of the intruders! But Alanwe is not to be harmed.
Your skins will make fine banners!
I don't even need the Blade to best you!
I'll use your bones to build a chair! A comfortable one!
Run, fools!
Why resist? Your deaths are assured.
Consume their souls!
None of you will survive this.
Your soul is forfeit!
I've consumed the souls of an army. Allow me to show them to you.
You'll never leave this place. Not alive, anyway.
Death won't be the end for you. You will serve me for as long as your body remains.
Give up. Let my web take you!
Die.
My horde is endless!
You're powerful, but my legion will match you.
Turn to ash.
My lightning will sear their flesh, brother.
Death by flame or lightning—it's our choice!
Dung-covered Iron Orcs! What did Shurami ever do to them? Shurami only uses her knives to cut prices!\n\nLet me show you my stock.
Ha! I heard that! Your stomach's growling like a hungry welwa! Sit a spell and let me fill that belly.
If these Iron Orc attacks get any more frequent, I'm going to have to start brewing tree-bark ale and gravel brandy. A woman's got to make a living, after all!
I know, I know. Who can eat fresh meals out here in the wastes? But you know what? Even boot-leather tastes good when cooked with the right spices. \n\nI think you'll like what I've got in stock.
The Spinner's work here will never be undone.
Warm bodies! The arts of the Mistress mean little to ghosts.
More entertainment!
Face me!
Your bodies will serve us. You won't be needing them anymore.
We'll eat well tonight.

You there, have you heard the one about the Orc chief and the pumpkin patch? No? \n\nDon't give me that look! I've got plenty of Orc friends. One of them even told me this joke! Where do you think I got it?
I'm sorry. I can't help myself!
I can't… regain… control!
Please—help me!
Your bodies will serve us. You won't be needing them anymore.
Your bodies will serve us. You won't be needing them anymore.
Feel free to use the equipment—just so long as you don't have any of that damn red brittle on you.

Never thought I'd be hauling red brittle out of this mine, but that twitchy High Elf down in the storehouse seems to think it's worth something. Hopefully we'll be back to mining gold and real ore in a few days. \n\nIt's not worth getting the shakes.
It's nothing. I just haven't been sleeping well. I've got to get back to work. Right after I catch my … my breath.
Fix the winch. Keep it working. Don't let the rope break.\n\nYou know the best thing about being an engineer? Me neither. I should have stuck to gambling.
I'd love to lend a hand and take out a few of those ugly Iron Orcs, but these rocks aren't going to mine themselves.
Under my guidance, the jungles will reclaim your shining cities.
I will drive Men and Mer from Nirn.

Want to hear the name of the epic story I'm writing? "Trees Rain Stone in an Empty Sea." Evocative, isn't it? \n\nYou don't look very well. Perhaps you should step away from the mine and get some fresh air.
This one is happy that so many have fled Dragonstar. Azzaril has the whole mine to himself. Harder work, but a bigger share, yes?

Our homes, our city may have fallen under the shroud of darkness, but a new dawn will always bring the light.\n\nWhatever evils the Daedra contrive, we will find a find a way to stop them. I believe this with all my heart.
See the strength of the true Orsimer!
The Rat is flattered that you keep wanting to chat with him. Those others, they never talked to the Rat … that's why he doesn't care. \n\nEven if they need help, it's not the Rat's problem.
As long as no one hits me in the face, I'll be fine. I hate it when people hit me in the face.
Hail, noble adversary! Come and break bread with me, for tomorrow we may die!
Keep moving, friend. I'm looking for my brother.

I know the Worm Cultists and these Legion Zero soldiers are bad people, but I still don't understand why taking over the Temple of the Divines was a priority for them.\n\nWhat do they intend to do with the place? I just can't imagine.
As you die, so will the countries of man and mer.
You're wearing that gear into the Arena? Well, I'd bring along a restoration staff or two if I were you.

Excuse me, capon jam. I think one of us is confused. This table is reserved for Stone-Fish warriors.\n\nI don't see any Stone-Fish colors and I don't recognize your ugly face, so I wager you're in the wrong place. Get lost.
Don't believe everything you may have heard. My goods certainly did not fall off the back of a caravan wagon.
The Captain frowns upon loose talk, but I heard the Arena uses some powerful magic. Some kind of glamours they turn on and off like lanterns. Be ready for anything in there. I know I am!
Some friendly advice. In the Arena, keep your menders safe. If you take out your opponent's healer while protecting yours, you'll be one step closer to victory.\n\nHealers are useful that way.
Oh, good attempt! Not perfect, mind you, but good all the same!
You have that killer instinct. I can see it in your eyes. Hold on to that feeling, stranger. There's no room for mercy in the Arena.
My nan always said that a starving bear will eat itself. \n\nI say it's better to eat someone else. Am I right?
Ah, more fodder for the arena! This one would wish you luck, but what would it matter?\n\nBut enough of this sadness. Let me show you my wares.
Meat without moonsugar is like chewing without teeth. Bah. Sugar-Dance would trade your left arm for some sugar-cane fritters right now!
You came with them? You're braver than I thought.
This one hopes you have traveled far and wide. Knowing your way through a blizzard will help you in the Arena—or so I have heard.
Why do the furless ones wear so much armor? Do they enjoy getting hit? All those pots and pans just slow them down. That must be why they get hit so much.
Another group of losers? Well, if you insist on getting your arses kicked, let me know and I'll send you into the Arena.
Weakling.
You wandered into the wrong ruin, friends.
Suffer!
I will not be contained!
Last time we spoke, Turuk Redclaws called you a milksop! Don't let him get away with that! Take the Undaunted pledge.
For the Serpent!
Turuk Redclaws implied you were a wet piece of bread, used to sop milk off a plate. I would not let this stand. Take the pledge.
The priests are doing all they can, but it's not enough. The city is lost, Molag Bal has won.
I hate to say this, but I think those who were killed may have been the ones who were truly blessed. \n\nThe rest of us—the gods want us to suffer.
I'm never leaving this room, never. They're going to have to bury me here. And probably pretty soon too.
Keep your head down. Last person who stood there lost his.
It's good to see another member of the Fighters Guild here to fight at our side. You are here to fight, yes?
Speak with Kerennia for the latest news. Sharapal merely watches the streets.
The air's so fresh and clean up here, it makes me want to sing!
A hard fought victory. Toast the Eight tonight, Undaunted. For tomorrow, you may beg their mercy. Hah!
The Imperial Prison's to the northeast of here. Between that and the Dark Anchor, this district's the worst place in the whole City!
Kerennia has plenty for you to do, if you're here for more than just sight-seeing.
It's raining mortals this day! Kill them!
I do not know if you have a soul. I hear much discussion of such things. If you value yours, pray this evening. Tomorrow may bring Oblivion.
So many visitors this day! So many dying mortals.
We've got all kinds of goods for sale! Only … slightly used.
Flame and guile!
Good work! Now hold that position and split your group to clear the other side!
Defend both sites—neither can fall to the Daedra!
My allies have scattered your minions to the winds!
Do yourself a favor and save on the healer's fees. Abandon your dreams of competing in the Arena. I'd hate to see that rugged face receive any additional damage.
You look familiar. Have you been to Deshaan or Eastmarch recently? No, don't tell me! I prefer the mystery of it all!
Do you have a preferred weapon? I am a master of the blade.
A superior weapon is the key to victory.
My brother is good with a bow, but I'm better.
My sister is good with a bow, but I'm better.
Let me tell you. I got very, very, very, very … very drunk.
I can't believe Gunran finished the last of the ale! He's such a selfish hog.
More fodder for the Arena? I'll try not to step on your remains when we get in there.
These ruins are ancient, but I could swear the Arena itself is practically new.
My partner cares about such things as the whys and wherefores of a particular situation.\n\nOn the other hand, I just want to deal out some meaningful destruction.

After my group departed, it took me days to find another team.\n\nBut do you know what happened? One had indigestion and had to return home. Another one's guar caught on fire. What obvious excuses! I have half a mind to pack up and go home myself.
Hello there! Braving the Craglorn wilds? How exciting!
You want to buy the spoils of war, yes? Speak to Severa—she has what you need.
I'm not cut out for army life. Too many rules, too much marching. And yelling. I hate yelling.
On the run? Pull up a stump. I could use some decent conversation.
This is unacceptable. Slay the mortals!
Daedra got your tongue? Hah! Want your reward?
My father crafted armor for Kurog himself, friend, and I'm twice the smith my father was.
All my pelts and hides come from local hunters. You won't find any musty imports here, I promise!
Back in Wayrest, we often consider Orcs to be brutish savages. But tell me, friend, could brutes and savages build such a magnificent city? I think not!
My uncle was the finest tailor in Evermore, back in the day. He'd be mortified to see me set up shop among these savages.
This is a disgrace. Rectify it.
When the city is completed, there will be a reckoning. Make no mistake. Every slight and insult will be repaid in kind.
Waters of Oblivion aid me.
Bows, staves, shields—you name it, I sell it.
Your possessions will be safe with us, I assure you.
Break them! Break the mortals!
Envelope them in flames!
Let the battle be joined!
Show our visitors how bright a new day can burn.
Burn, and be reborn.
Give in. Every life ends.
I will bring your body to the Valkyn.
Burn!
Mortals—always scampering about.
Let the fire and brimstone purify you!
We have rooms to rent for every occasion. But if you need something a little more discreet, you should talk to my daughter, Mulzah.
I expected Orcs to smell bad, but they're really not much worse than the hunters back home.
The king needs to get the clan chiefs to cooperate soon or this glorious city of his is going to crumble under its own weight.
Use this one's enchanting table as you see fit. The moons know the Orcs seem to have little interest in it.
These stables were shameful. I wouldn't have put a three-legged dog in here, let alone a horse! It's a good thing we came along.
As promised, we have refurbished the stables here in Orsinium. I hope it meets your standards, my chief.
Forgive me for this meager stock. Wrothgar does not surrender her reagents easily.
These stables looked rougher than Malacath's nethers when I got here. They're better now.
I'd make a fine hearth-wife. All the Orcs say so.
They're here! The Iron Orcs are here! Stand your ground!
You seem surprised to see an Orc in this line of work. Well, that's your problem.\n\nBut if you want the best that gold can buy, then you've come to exactly the right place.
You want to join the Fighters Guild? Then talk to Ehshaz. He's the Hall Steward.
We're the Fighters Guild. We don't take sides in political conflicts.
When the Mages Guild offered me this post in Wrothgar, how could I say no? I've always dreamed of seeing a rebuilt Orsinium. And now, here I am!
Why we bothered to offer our services to Orsinium I'll never know. Most Orcs stay away. If not for the visitors from other lands, this would be a lonely place indeed.
All this Trinimac and Malacath nonsense makes my head spin. Luckily I've got potent ales to right the ship.
Hm?
As the clan wise-woman always said, "If you don't like the offal, get out of my kitchen." Heh.
Not that many farms in Wrothgar, so most of my stock comes from hunters and gathers. But what I lack in selection, I make up in freshness!
A valiant effort. But futile.
Come—aid me.
Return!
Have no fear. I'll get your shipment where it needs going.
Your shipment makes standing here all day worthwhile.
A strong mind can outwit the strongest arm. But I see you use both in your work.
The fires of Oblivion rage on!
I can fit your goods in with the next shipment. They shan't be delayed.
Trade with Daedra is troublesome. Mostly we run from Daedra before they torture and kill us.\n\nDaedra are not good customers.
Another delivery? Er, no, there's no problem.
The dark ones have told me your fate.
Why do you bother us? Our fates may not intertwine.
Thank you. We'll need a proper supply chain, of course, but every bit counts.
I will offer your burnt skulls to the Valkyn.
Utter foolishness. You should not have come.
Anything I can do for you?
Now here's a likely one.
Customers are always welcome.
Speak of your desires.
Anything I can do for you?
Come, and do business!
Malacath's nethers! It's just such a long way down.
Jumping off cliffs is a cherished Orc tradition. Into water, I mean.\n\nI think it's one of the reasons we settled in Wrothgar. There are so many good cliffs!
You ask me, we should collapse the supports inside that barrow. Let the stone take care of those dead Nords.
It was like the ice just sprang out of nowhere! And all that water! I was raised in the Alik'r desert. The cold and the wet—that's just so unnatural to me!
Soft, little Bretons! All they do is moan and complain about the cold.\n\nHa! They should come to the Pale in springtime. And don't get me started about our winters!
I plan to head north during the thaw and trade for echatere meat with the Shatul clan.
When an Orc buries her dead, they have the good manners to stay buried!
Father, Oneg is dead. He died before I was born.\n\nYou'll have to excuse me. I need to deal with my father.
If you need steel to spill Winterborn blood, then I probably have something you want.
I feel strong today.
Dwarves or no Dwarves, Clan Tumnosh doesn't roll over for anyone.
An Orc with friends is a sign of worthiness. Ramash's pride is going to get us all killed.
At your service!
I want that buried—now!
I love being the king!
Damn these Imperials! Couldn't they have left us some decent goods when they fled? Selfish if you ask me.
That should provide the soldiers with the opening they need to reach the fortress.
Do the Winterborn have any magic that isn't just vile and disgusting?
You want food or drink, I'm the only place to get it between here and Orsinium.
When Canuldil gets back, I'm going to give him a piece of my mind. He's left me alone here for days!
Can't work since the cave-in crushed my leg. I hope everyone's okay down there.
Now that the quarry's safe, Orsinium's finally sending workers to help us dig. Hope they don't make a mess of it.
The workers in the quarry just disappeared when the fog rolled in. I don't want to think about it, but I bet they're all dead.
The Orc chief does not seem to like this one very much.
The Orcs need tools to dig out all this stone, and Ak'saz is just the one to provide them!
We're not betraying the Empire, we're saving it!
Let me go—I won't tell anyone you're down here!
May this venom boil your blood!
The Divines bless you, friend. See me again if you ever return here; we may have further need of your services.
You don't happen to know the way out of here, do you? I was a little … y'know … disoriented when I arrived.
Thanks, friend. Even a moment's rest from their jeering is welcome. I will stay and fight again, though I fear it may be my last.\n\nI need healing if I am to survive.
I just wish it could have been me instead of him. Doesn't seem right.
I'm free from that horror after all these years!
You did it! You freed us!
This one will soon be a civilian, if General Nedras has his way.

If you are braving the sewers, make sure to have your weapon at the ready. Between this Legion Zero and the Daedra, every nook and cranny is packed with danger.\n\nIf you are going, perhaps you can do this one a favor?
They destroyed it all, our home, our furniture, all our belongings, even my cart. \n\nIf we survive this, picking up the pieces and starting over again won't be easy.
Maximinus wasn't a good friend, but someone from home nonetheless. Thank you for looking for him.

Oh, you're nice and shiny, aren't you? Either you're smart enough to have avoided the sewers, or you're nimble enough to avoid stepping in the sludge and blood.\n\nI'd ask you which, but I really don't even care.
Must leave all this filth!
How do I get out of here?
Is it safe to leave?
Must seek safety!
Thank the Three, I'm alive!
Many thanks! I would have not survived in that shell much longer.
I will never complain about the smell in Mother's stables again.
The Lady can torture me no more. Thank you!
Am I truly free of my silken prison?
The shell of the false egg has cracked and I am free!
My fate is not to die today.
I shall not die today!
I will not be some petty Daedra's breeding vessel!
Watch out for the Daedroth!
Of all the creatures, it had to be spiders!
I have hope once more!
By Stendarr's everlasting mercy, I'm free!
The Lady will be angry with me!
Too long has this one been trapped!
Freedom!
I do not enjoy feeling dependent upon anyone, let alone a stranger, but I'm afraid I have dire news. The Daedra have again begun the ritual in the temple.
Of the gladiators who fought in the arena before the attack, only a handful remain.
When I get free I'll tear your mortal shell to pieces.
I'm not afraid of some stupid Daedra. I've never been in a fight, but I've read all about Coldharbour. \n\nI can beat them. I can beat them all!

When it's this cold, I try to remember the time when I was still inside my egg. It seems impossible, but it must be in our memories somewhere. \n\nMaybe right before we die, we remember … and then we return to the roots and do it all over again.
If you go into the upper city, I pray the stars light your way.
Back again? No papers this time though, I see.
Come here! I'll tear the head off your neck!
Welcome to the Imperial City, warrior! Speak to General Nedras for your orders.
The hero returns! This one's heart is glad to see you once again, my friend.\n\nIf you stumble across any more of those patrol documents, bring them to Tapak and he will put them to use.
By the Three, you've been busy haven't you? Keep up the good work.
I never thought our glorious invasion of the Imperial City would look so … wet.
How about you take a look at my wares?
You'll need equipment. Just so happens I have some I could sell you.
General Aklash keeps finding excuses to keep me from going out on patrol. Something tells me she prefers to watch me patrol back and forth in here.
My prey never escapes!
This spell will break you.
Let the darkness take you!
The dark of Coldharbour take you!
Perish in Coldharbour's flame!
Accept this gift, and perish!
If you won't run, then perish!
One death at a time!
How dare you?
The Abomination doesn't know his own strength!
May your lungs rot, your body perish!
What?
Oh, no, not again!
If only Canuldil had stayed home with me, he'd still be alive now.
Who's more mad? \n\nThe mage who runs around testing the water while the city's under siege, or the apprentice who follows her?
I'm so glad to have my book back. The question is do I add my new experiences to part two, or do I start in on part three? I'll have to think about it.
The Divines bless you, warrior!
I long for the days when rats were the worst thing down here.\n\nPerhaps I can repay your kindness, friend.
Perhaps you can talk some sense into that stubborn ass, Pollius. He certainly won't listen to me, a mere citizen. We need to take this fight to the streets!
We will retake this city. We have to.
You'll regret coming here, mortal!
Ready to die, mortals?
Back again, little rat?
You have to catch me to kill me.
One day I'll be free. I'll tear you to pieces and return you here, where you will suffer agony unending.
You don't have enough holes in you yet!
This time, I'll put an arrow through your eye!
You'll look good in flames, mortal!
More victims for the pile!
My axes long to taste your blood!
A fool and his blood are soon parted!
The Emperor is dead. Long live the Emperor!
It's always a pleasure to see new faces!
This time, I shall burn the flesh from your bones!
Visitors are too few down here. I wonder why?
Still trying to kill the unkillable?
Come to gaze upon my handiwork, mortal?
We meet again ….
Ah …. A tasty morsel approaches!
The Lady always returns. You must not disturb her again.
Rise! Rise and fulfill your new purpose!
You should have fled from this place when you could. Now your flesh will serve me.
Feed on their corpses. Yours is growing flesh.
Do not fear. Even in death, your organs will serve us.
Die, wretched creature!
I call you from the mist, children!
All subjects approach and pay respect!
Come alive, my thralls! Protect me!
Eviscerate them!
Let me get a taste of you!
Mauloch's jawbone, I'm tired of this stink. Next time I'm picking the base site.
Sorry, soldier. I'm busy. \n\nThere's a lot of dangerous creatures out there …  Daedra, undead, and gods-know-what-else. I'm sure you can find something to do.
Empower me, minions!
I've seen some of the nicest houses in the city, but right now, I don't think any of them are as cozy as this place.
The last time I picked up a broom, a splinter almost killed me!
Seek the flames!
I don't care how thirsty you get, I wouldn't drink the sewer water down here.\n\nIt'll kill you faster than a Daedra. I saw a man die that way just the other day.
I will say one thing about setting up shop in a sewer—the customers are always desperate.
Your goods are probably safe with me.
A rolling egg often winds up getting cracked. Stay a while and peruse my wares.
If this one were you, she would want to travel light in the Imperial City. Might need to run at a moment's notice!\n\nLeave your heavy things with Shamaea. She will keep them safe.
You know, if you're headed out up into the city, the odds are that you're probably going to get yourself killed.\n\nThat being the case, why not go on a little shopping spree. Buy yourself a treat.
I will take good care of all you leave with me, never fear.
Don't be a stranger now. If the Veilweavers return, we will have to be ready to do it again. Yes. I'll prepare the spell.

Hm. How very serendipitous that you've returned. I wonder … is it perhaps some form of Daedric magnetism?\n\nIt seems you are drawn here just as the Veilweavers have again begun projecting themselves.
We're a family again. I can't thank you enough. Now to find a way out of this city ….

I do hope you washed your hands thoroughly. You might also want to put on a different set of clothes. And clean your weapons …. \n\nIn fact, you should probably just burn all your possessions and start fresh. I need a healthy assistant.
Ah, thank Mauloch you've returned. My experiments are going well, but I'm afraid I've been a little overzealous.
Anxious to get back in the fight, eh? Best to let these traitors sweat for a while. Let them think long and hard about their treachery before we slaughter them.
I'm told that the traitors are back in position. It's time to strike.
Thank you for reuniting us, friend.
I don't know if it's the cold or being restrained for so long, but my legs are completely numb. Thanks to you though, I can feel the blood returning to them already.
The Elven Gardens have always been a symbol of the Summerset Isles' support for the Empire. I worry about the implications if they are destroyed.
The district is far from safe, but at least it's not on the verge of being reduced to cinders. Not right now, at least.
There you are. History is once again threatened in the Elven Gardens, my friend. \n\nThe Xivkyn have returned with a fiery vengeance.
No work yet. Come back and see Aishah later.
Aishah has been thinking, walker. It was a very profitable day the day she met you. Perhaps there are opportunities for more profits together.
You made my day by killing that thing. I mean it. If we don't leave … maybe I'll see you tomorrow.
I hate to say this after everything you did, but I fear I have bad tidings.
I think I need some time alone. Forgive me.
Thank you for all your aid. My scouts tell me that the alleys have quieted somewhat, but that will likely change soon. Don't stray too far.
Thank you for warning me about Holia. I half expect her to show up here looking for me. Dumac take her.
Still no Gryna. Well, she's out of a job. There are plenty of other peasants who'd love to work for me.
While I appreciate the supplies you delivered from General Pollius, I'd like it even better if he did something about all the horrible Daedra wandering around, eating people.
Every notch in the shield is a story. The last story has no notch.
Next one who touches my stash will draw back a stub!
I want to get into the White-Gold Tower. Imagine the loot!
Now we're the ones with the gold. We should have done this long ago.
Nobles Plaza, a filthy sewer … doesn't matter. Guard duty is guard duty.
Filthy daedrats. They're everywhere.
Don't you love what we've done to this city?
Say what you want about Dremora. At least they pay on time.
Please, do me a favor. Kill them before they wound you.
I do miss the sun. It's hard to tell when I should sleep.
Once it's over, the Daedra will leave, and the city will be ours.
A Dremora called me "Worm-slave." Is that really how they see us?
I would prefer to be posted to the Arboretum.
We're not keeping the Legion after it's done, are we? Maybe as slaves.
Shields are meant for bashing faces!
There have to be more bodies in the water.
The Xivkyn can't admit our importance in causing the Planemeld.
I don't question Legion Zero's capability. Just their loyalty.
I have been in the White-Gold Tower before. It's not that impressive.
Any word on the Magisterium? I long for its secrets.
Always take their fingers before you pluck out their eyes.
The key is to pose the bones properly, so they accept the animus.
So hungry. The flesh colossus won't mind if I take a slice. Will it?
The White-Gold Tower? Not that impressive.
Why do these fools resist? The Planemeld is inevitable!
The sooner these fools realize the Divines are finished, the better.
The kyn will burn this city for Molag Bal!
I would suffer no mortal to live!
This city will be a fine addition to Coldharbour.
I miss hunting mortals. Perhaps we killed too many of them.
This city will be raised from the dead!
Ebral learned a new technique to apply magicka to skeletons.
The city is ours. At this point, who can stand against us?
This place is unworthy. Why do we waste our time?
These mortals … endlessly scampering. Such unpredictable targets.
We will make a carpet of our victims' bodies.
Molag Bal is the greatest prince I've ever served.
Not enough burning. Fetch me a Worm Cultist.
Even the game master joins the fight sometimes.
Has Molag Bal forgotten us? I refuse to believe it.
The vermin in the slums are easy pickings.
Duty to the kyn. Duty to the Dark Lord.
Why the Dark Lord wants this pitiful city is beyond me.
I smell man-flesh. There is prey nearby.
Sacrifices must be made in the name of Molag Bal.
The White Gold Tower will be swallowed into the sky.
I have died a thousand deaths in service to Molag Bal.
There will be none left to mourn this city.
This city is ours. Now we must keep it.
Our Dark Lord wastes us, leading such weak kyn.
We must engineer a cleaner method of piercing the veil.
If you fill the building with enough fire, it suffocates the mortals.
Not all Xivkyn force the kyn to lick our boots, but I do.
Round up the mortals. The games must continue.
Mortals fail because they are weak. Taking this city was too easy.
I'd prefer to impale the mortals myself, but our orders are clear.
Something watches us. Can you sense it?
No opponent has ever truly challenged me. It's shameful.
Dig in the ground and you'll find even more of these vermin.
Magicka has great power over flesh.
Few of the bodies are useful after the kyn are done playing.
I should have gone with my cousin Lulius. He left for Cropsford before the bridges came down. A little odd, but he's better company than these ogrim.
Weep in Coldharbour's light!
You'll do well in the Arena, mortal. Feel free to weep before you die.
You'll do well in the Arena, mortal. Feel free to weep before you die.
This is my hiding place. Go away … please?
The Game Master will be pleased to meet you … and to watch you die.
The Game Master will be pleased to meet you … and to watch you die.
The Xivkyn trained a daedroth to do amusing things to banekin, and then called him "General." How droll.
If you've got orders for me, you can just forget them. I'm not moving until a general pulls me up by the pauldron and shoves me in line.
Steer clear of the Imperial Prison is my advice. It's infested with Daedra and is an even worse place than when we ran it.
It's a sad fact that this is the only place in the city that's truly safe.\n\nI had hoped we would have the sewers under Covenant control by now.
Each day is a new challenge to a warrior's prowess, and down here, it is a test of survival.
You provincials are all alike—always looking for excitement. Well, as a resident of this once-lovely city, I can tell you excitement isn't all it's cracked up to be!
Just when you think life can't get any worse, another boulder gets dropped on your head.
You want to die, you go right ahead! I'm going to hide up here until the Tharns come back and free the city! \n\nClivia promised! She promised she'd be back!
We'll make it back to General Pollius eventually. Have you seen him yet? He's holed up in the refuge not far from here.
This one is far to sleek to die in a place like this. Especially at the hands of filthy traitors.
I have no idea who's in charge of the city now, with the Tharns gone. Just as well. Never liked them anyway.
I've been up here for hours. A coward's fate I suppose.
Where others see ruin and despair, I see beauty and hope.
I wonder what Molag Bal does with all those souls. We'll find out when we retake the city!
If you see any soldiers shirking their duty, you grab them by their chin-strap and tell them to get back on the line!
What is it? Are you one of those haughty Sintavs? No, you're not, I can tell just by looking at you. Until they come back, this place is mine, so go away.
Behind this one lie the Alessian Catacombs; you will not make it far before you too flee. Even worse horrors await in the greater depths.
If my snooty old friends could see me now, they'd be horrified at what I'm wearing. But, they're dead and I'm not, so I win.
We keep sending out runners asking for new orders. None of them have ever come back. Dead, I expect.
I don't know how much longer I can stand that screaming. I'm ready to attack the Temple all by myself.
We heard there were piles of gold down here. Almost nothing so far but hordes of Daedra and strange bandits. I think we were duped.
White-Gold has fallen. Existence itself will follow.
Come! Face darkness and flame!
He says he's the emperor, but I saw him and he's horrible!
What's that you're carrying? Something for me, I hope.
Good to see you again. Anytime you find caches out in the sewers, think of me, please.
There are flames enough for all!
Writhe in my flame!
There! Attack the rifts, she calls her allies!
Death won't stop me!
Honor requires that I avenge my comrades. I will heal for a while longer, then seek vengeance.
Your will—against my flame!
Thank you again for finding this, my friend. It may not hold any arcane power, but it's full of great ideas for holiday apple dishes!
Things are quiet, too quiet. This one does not like the quiet.
You wouldn't know it by looking at me, but I once lived in the finest section of the City.
Welcome back. Others have told me Maximinus is dead. Alas that he died before paying off his debts.
Kyne's favor brought you here. No doubt about it.
I grieve for the Orc Otholug once was, but I am thankful you destroyed what he had become.
Oh, my aching tail. It may never straighten out. Thank you for freeing me!
You will die here, as the Imperial Legions did!
The two Thrones will be joined!
You invade my realm, filth, intending to do harm? You will fail. The servants of my devices protect them at all cost.
The chains break. The anchors crumble. The gears halt. But I am still Lord of Domination, and you are still nothing.
An anchor broken from its mooring? Reinforce the heart of the device and launch another anchor!
Nithings and nikyn, the lot of them.
By the command of the Empress, you must die!
Confirm that they're dead. Then kill the priest.
For Clivia Tharn!
To arms! The Daedra are coming!
The Elder Scroll was right about you! Let's move!
Nirn and Coldharbour shall be one!
Reduce the mortals to dust!
My light will feast on your flesh!
Die!
Run for your lives!
I will erase you in Lord Bal's name!
I sentence you to eternal suffering!
Your soul belongs to Lord Bal, now.
You are the criminal I have been hunting? Really? How disappointing.
Perhaps we should start a tab for you.
I knew you would run!
You are caught red-handed. Pay the bounty or else.
That works.
You shall not run!
Thought we would not catch you, eh? Well, we catch everybody! Everyone who breaks the law, I mean.
Go, and do not do ... that thing you did again.
Did I say something wrong? Oh, right!
If it were up to me, I would let your bounty slide. But it isn't up to me, is it? You will need to pay.
Do avoid repeating your offenses!
I will stop you, fugitive!
Kicked up quite a fuss haven't we? Just hand over the bounty and I'll smooth things over. Easy.
See how easy that was? On your way.
Did I stutter? Surrender, you rogue!
You cannot escape justice, you miscreant.
May your nose remain cleansed.
Poor choice, knave!
You are a criminal. You owe a bounty. Pay me and perhaps your deplorable condition will improve.
A bounty paid? Who would have thought it?
Let your death be on your own head!
On the matter of your criminal behavior, I will gladly accept your bounty.
Another bounty dealt with. What a good day!
I did not want it to come to this!
Bounty? Do I owe you a bounty? No, no, that cannot be right. It must be the other way around.
Crime? I have no idea what you mean.
This is probably all your fault!
You are making my head pound, criminal! Just pay your bounty and away with you!
Another criminal has purchased justice.
I am in no mood for your shenanigans!
Your illicit activities have a cost, lawbreaker, and that cost is judgment!
Perhaps there is hope for you.
You would run from justice? Never!
I will not read your charges. You would doze off before I finish. Pay your bounty and be on your way.
Thank you for making restitution.
You made me raise my voice, felon!
I caught you. Just pay me the bounty. I will bring it to the ... appropriate parties.
A little light. Eh, it will do.
Foolish. Very foolish.
Yesterday, a criminal tried to run. Had to take his feet. Not pleasant! Why not just pay the bounty?
There you go. A clean slate.
Oh well. This is what they pay me for.
Justice can be invigorating if you pay your bounty with a smile!
See? Was that so bad?
Now we must fight. A shame!
Another day, another witless oaf disrupting the peace .... Pay your bounty or suffer the consequences.
Do not let me see you again.
Impudent swine!
Real law enforcement is so boring. Why stop crimes when you can just stand around demanding bounties?
Great. Let's do this again some time.
Suicide by Guard? So be it!
I'm not a judge or a jury. I'm just here to collect your bounty.
I suppose we're done here. Move along.
One of us will regret this!
Your crime is like a blockage in the river of your soul. I can clear it up if you pay your bounty.
Every time a debt is paid, a torchbug sings.
You were hatched from a rotten egg!
Your crimes are known. Pay the bounty or suffer the fangs.
Good. Now, don't make ripples.
Now I'm angry!
Why did you have to break the law? Now you have to pay the bounty.
What's this? Oh, the bounty. Right!
I'll tell my superior about this!
You break the law, I break your jaw. Unless you pay the bounty of course.
No snappy come-back? Too bad.
Finally, some action!
You're a criminal. And I'm not as thunk as you drink I am. Wait ....
Bounty collected! Drinks are on me. No, not your drink ....
Now you've done it!
Have you seen an outlaw around here? I'm supposed to collect a bounty, but I can't seem to ... oh, it's you!
Crime? What crime? You're free to go.
Didn't I ask for your surrender?
You should be careful. I'm an egg on a precipice and I'm about to crack!
Paid in full. Good, good. Paid in full.
You crossed the wrong guard, felon!
Well met! I know you plan to pay your fine. I'm here to accommodate your needs.
A pleasure clearing your record.
I tried to be nice about this!
I do hope you're not a violent sort. I much prefer to deal with civilized lawbreakers.
Another bounty paid in quick fashion.
Fleeing was a grievous error!
Uh, yeah, that's right. I represent the town guard. So, uh, pay the bounty, all right?
Don't tell anyone you saw me, all right?
Can't we work something out?
Sometimes the law moves at the speed of mud flowing uphill. If you pay now, I'd be grateful.
I knew you were going to cooperate.
Why did you try to run?
You did some crime. Now you pay a bounty.
What's this for? Oh yeah.
Should have paid the bounty!
Go ahead. Don't pay your bounty. That would make my day. I'm just itching to hit something.
Criminals have no spine.
You're leaving? Over my dead body!
I am drawn by your musk, but also by my duty. Please. Do not make me scar such a pretty face.
Farewell, luscious flower.
The grass waves in the wind. I do not.
I don't mean to--I mean, I know you're busy--but you have a bounty on your head that needs paying.
Oh good. I was worried that would go roots up.
Stop! I--I mean it!
Want to see a trick? You give me gold, and I forget I ever saw you.
Pleasure doing business.
You suicidal, or just crazy?
I prefer you don't pay your bounty. Then, according to the law, the bone breaking can begin.
Your slate's clean, but I'll be watching.
Yield, or I'll scoop out your brains!
You have turned deplorable into an art form! I'm not worthy to collect a bounty from you.
I wish you well with your newfound freedom.
I thought we had an understanding!
You're not going to try something, are you? Look, just pay your bounty and be on your way.
On your way. Try not to do it again.
You won't get far!
Justice catches up with us all eventually. Do yourself a favor and pay the bounty.
Smart move. It's unwise to resist fate.
It had to end this way: you versus me.
I've come to collect something. Give me a moment. Oh, yes! The bounty! For your crimes and all.
Your slate is clean, so I guess we're done here.
This is your last warning! No, this is!
You're a lawbreaker, and I'm the law. Now pay your bounty.
Move along.
To arms!
I wonder ... if it's not too much trouble ... could I get you to pay your bounty now?
Bounty paid in full? How ... unexpected.
I must insist you surrender!
The Anti-Criminality Act, Section II, Subsection B states: Criminals must pay a bounty commensurate to their crimes.
Good. Now to file the paperwork.
Fleeing a crime is also illegal!
Are you the violent sort? You don't look violent. I really hate dealing with violent criminals.
That worked out better than usual.
Try not to hurt me too badly!
By Y'ffre's lush branches, justice is a spiritual experience! Will you pray with me and pay your fine?
The gods smile on those who pay their debts!
Yield, villain, or suffer mightily!
Look, I've heard it all before. Just pay your bounty and be on your way.
Good. Off with you. Keep your nose clean.
I'm not even on duty!
I usually deal with a higher class of criminal, but I suppose I can accept your bounty.
I applaud your good sense! The bounty is paid!
Make no mistake, you'll regret this!
Listen, I don't want to be the bad guy here. Just pay the bounty and everyone's happy.
Great. Now, we can all get some rest.
Let's get this over with!
How did you hope to get away with this? Are you from the moons?
Huh. I thought you weren't going to pay.
I gave you a chance!
Sometimes I wonder, what's the point? You're just going to go out and break the law again.
It's just a matter of time, but you'll be back.
I knew this would happen.
I believe we can clear up this situation as soon as you pay the proper bounty.
I have cleared your record and restored your good name.
Resist and this will go harder on you.
Let's play a little game. I catch you and collect your bounty. Then you. Catch. Me.
Pleasure doing business with you.
So you want to play rough, do you?
Wouldn't it be great to just start over with a clean slate? All you have to do is give up the gold.
I think that went well for both of us.
Last mistake you'll make!
You have strayed from the path of virtue, but you can still find your way back. Pay your bounty.
I will pray for your redemption.
I will pray for your soul.
I can't help but notice you're armed. Um … would you be willing to pay your bounty?
Thank the Divines! You paid!
Stop, criminal! Please stop!
You've shown us what a tremendous criminal you are--now show us what an upstanding citizen you can be!
Thank you! It was a pleasure.
You're smarter than this!
Every crime carries a cost. Lucky for you, I am a duly appointed bounty collector.
In accordance with the law, your bounty has been paid.
I will note this in your record!
You're stuck, criminal. Cornered. So pay the bounty and I'll let you move on.
Hmph.
You're not going anywhere!
Your deplorable actions have a cost, and that cost is justice!
Go and steal no more, felon!
Escape is not an option!
Please. This doesn't have to get ugly. Just pay your bounty and we can both walk away.
Gods. That was easier than I thought.
Oh gods! I don't want to die.
You made a mistake. Things happen. Let me help you clear this up. Can you pay your fine?
Don't you feel better now?
Well, if you want a fight ....
There's no need for violence. Simply pay the bounty and you're free to go. Easy, right?
Excellent. Now you be smart, all right?
This could have been so easy!
Just a minute. Your crimes are known here, and I would see your bounty collected.
All right. Carry on.
You're forcing my hand!
I don't care why you did it. Pay your bounty and you're free to go.
Try not to do it again, would you?
You shouldn't have done that!
I can tell you're full of crime. Give me some coin, Crimey. I'll let you go, I swear.
On your way, then.
I've fought better than you!
We can sweep all this down the kwama hole for the right price ....
Better not have short-changed me.
Brave! Stupid, but brave.
You don't look like you can afford to pay your bounty. No way you have enough gold.
I suppose you're free to go now.
I suppose you are a criminal after all!
No one escapes justice, you malcontent! Now pay your bounty!
Another contrite criminal makes amends!
Have at thee, villain!
There's nothing I'd like more than to gut you, but I'm supposed to ask you to pay your bounty.
Fine. But next time I won't be so nice.
You're not going anywhere!
Pay the bounty ... if scum like you even has that kind of money.
This money's filthy.
Another runner. What did I expect?
Yes, I know. I make this uniform look good. Now stop staring and pay me your bounty.
Now see. That wasn't so bad!
And now the inevitable begins!
Your bounty now, if you please.
Thank you.
You defied the law for the last time!
Let us do this by the rules. Pay your bounty and you can remain free.
Go on. I don't want to be seen with you.
You should have submitted!
Please, no explanations. I don't care why you did what you did. I just need you to pay your bounty.
Almsivi be praised.
You brought this on your own head!

Halt, you craven cur.
Crime does not pay, friend.
By the gods, that was murder.
Not until you pay your fine.
Away, dog.
Not my concern.
Try anything illegal and I summon the guard.
Thief! Someone call the guards.
A vampire in our midst!
The dog reveals its true nature!
I have a suspicion I didn't simply lose something.
Try that again and I'll cut you.
Hey, who are you?
The guard will be here any second. Last chance.
I guess I can let you go with a warning. This time.
Neither I nor the law is merciful.
I don't condone your actions, but I don't condemn, either.
Guards, a violent person!
Tall Papa, help me.
Such wickedness! I need a guard.
Rouse the alarm and call the guard.
I pray that's the last life you take.
Perhaps you could return after you pay your bounty?
Tava grant me speed.
I don't want to face your blade.
What could possibly interest you over there?
Blade's edge, stop that thief!
I believe that you're a vampire.
Get the mangy beast!
Must be a hole in my pocket.
Pickpockets should have their hands cut off!
What gives you the right to just barge in here?
The guard will be here any second. Last chance.
I can be reasonable. You're free to go.
You are trying my patience.
Not this again.
Stay your hand!
Someone! I require aid!
What have you done?
You there! What are you doing?
You murderous dog!
Settle your debts with the guards. We can talk after.
Please, don't do anything hastey ….
On my honor, I saw nothing.
Are you ill? Why do you hunch so?
I'll see you in chains, thief!
Flee or die, vampire!
Away, you slavering beast!
Did someone just touch me?
You filthy pickpocket, get away!
Stop loitering and get out!
The guard will be here any second. Last chance.
I suppose an accident isn't a crime. Now go.
You are making a fool of yourself.
More crime? Pathetic.
Control yourself!
I need help! Please!
Sound the alarm!
You will eat sand for this.
Such a waste!
Not until your law-debt is paid.
Not another step!
Please, I want no part of this.
You're doing a poor job of hiding.
That does not belong to you.
Begone, blood-drinker!
Help! It's a werewolf!
Why do I keep losing things?
Do I look like a charity for ruffians?
You've overstayed your welcome.
The guard will be here any second. Last chance.
A mistake? How original. But you may go.
If you commit a crime, I will hunt you down.
This is not my concern.
Guards, there's been violence done.
Upon my honor, I need aid.
Halt, you craven cur.
Crime does not pay, friend.
By the gods, that was murder.
Not until you pay your fine.
Away, dog.
Not my concern.
Try anything illegal and I summon the guard.
Thief! Someone call the guards.
A vampire in our midst!
The dog reveals its true nature!
I have a suspicion I didn't simply lose something.
Try that again and I'll cut you.
Leave or face the guards. Your choice.
You're not leaving? This should be fun.
Your cooperation is appreciated. You may go.
The stars observe your actions, and so does the guard.
I don't condone your actions, but I don't condemn, either.
Guards, a violent person!
Tall Papa, help me.
Such wickedness! I need a guard.
Rouse the alarm and call the guard.
I pray that's the last life you take.
Perhaps you could return after you pay your bounty?
Tava grant me speed.
I don't want to face your blade.
What could possibly interest you over there?
Blade's edge, stop that thief!
I believe that you're a vampire.
Get the mangy beast!
Must be a hole in my pocket.
Pickpockets should have their hands cut off!
Think you can just barge in like this?
You're not leaving? This should be fun.
I wouldn't even bloody my blade on you. Go away.
Enough nonsense. Move along.
Not this again.
Stay your hand!
Someone! I require aid!
What have you done?
You there! What are you doing?
You murderous dog!
Settle your debts with the guards. We can talk after.
Please, don't do anything hasty ….
On my honor, I saw nothing.
Are you ill? Why do you hunch so?
I'll see you in chains, thief!
Flee or die, vampire!
Away, you slavering beast!
Did someone just touch me?
You filthy pickpocket, get away!
To be a guest, you have to be invited.
You're not leaving? This should be fun.
Go in peace, citizen, and may prosperity find you.
Amusing, but tiresome. On your way.
More crime? Pathetic.
Control yourself!
I need help! Please!
Sound the alarm!
You will eat sand for this.
Such a waste!
Not until your law-debt is paid.
Not another step!
Please, I want no part of this.
You're doing a poor job of hiding.
That does not belong to you.
Begone, blood-drinker!
Help! It's a werewolf!
Why do I keep losing things?
Do I look like a charity for ruffians?
Leave these premises at once.
You're not leaving? This should be fun.
Next time, I won't be so understanding. Move along.
First time in the sewers? Tighten up those laces, friend. There are worse things than swamp-foot down here. Trust me.
I'm getting sick of hiding out down here, but every time I leave I get chased right back.\n\nSome days I think it might be better to just give up.
Every once in a while, a friendly face comes by. Glad to see you, friend.
Perhaps they will see the Hist tree someday—lick its sap and learn their worth. They deserve more than a sewer … my beautiful children.
Isn't it remarkable how things keep falling off the back of wagons?
Do I look like I trade in stolen goods?\n\nReally, do you think I look like a proper fence?
I don't care about your troubles. But I can make them go away.
The Guard knows better than to come down here.
Damn the war. Good for business, bad for everything else.
We need a new king in Shornhelm like a Nord needs snow. But I'm sure you're here for another reason.
I do not haggle, but I pay an honest price. On that, you have my word!
I assume you weren't followed? We don't need the Guard down here.
Ah, and just when I was about to close up, here you are.
I miss being on the other side of the counter … procuring, instead of purchasing.
Where else can you get rid of ill-gotten goods around here? Nowhere! So let's deal.
I know you've brought something good. I can just feel it!
You won't get a better price anywhere. If you disagree, perhaps you can take it up with the Guard.
The intricacies of Dark Elf transactions can be daunting. That's why I'm here.
Of course this one is drunk! But we can still make a deal, yes?
Those goods better not be stolen, hmm? This one would hate to call the Guard. Ha!
I can make sure all your troubles go away … and I know what I want in return.
Yes, I know. You want to get to know me better. Everyone does. It's a curse, really.
Looks like you've been busy. Show me what you have.
Let's keep this business-like. If you're selling, I'm buying.
What delights have you pilfered for me today?
Hot items burning your hands? Allow me to cool them off.
Discreetly, discreetly. You can never have too little attention.
Ssh! No need for all of Valenwood to know what you brought me.
I suppose some people would call it theft. I call it "economic adjustment."
Some people can be so uptight about things like "ownership" and "the law."
No haggling. Security isn't cheap.
The way I see it, I'm doing you a favor. No complaints about my prices.
Stolen goods, hmm? How exciting … how dangerous!
All this sneaking about, taking illicit things—isn't it exciting?
After this is done, we don't know each other. Understand?
If this ever gets back to—let's just say it better not get back to anyone.
The methods your organization employs are far too brutal. But none of you care, do you?\n\nWhat have you got for me today?
If we had more guards, we wouldn't need you Enforcers.\n\nI mean, how can I help you?
It's an honor to accept your confiscated goods, friend Enforcer!
I'd love to hear of your exploits—after I take care of your business, of course!
Is there something I can do for you, Enforcer?
Step right up, Enforcer. You know how this works.
Were you the one who brought in that notorious bounty? Well done!
I hope you have proper documents for this contraband.\n\nHa! Just pulling your leg, Enforcer!
Oh, proud and powerful Enforcer, how may I serve you?
Another customer. Wonderful. What have you brought me?
Have you brought me contraband, Enforcer? You know how much I love contraband!
Come back when my shift ends. I might let you handle my private stock.
Looks like you've been busy. Show me what you confiscated.
Let's keep this professional, Enforcer. We both have a job to do.
You'd drink too, if you had to put up with all these Enforcers.
Shh! Yes, I'm drunk. Don't tell anyone. I still have hours to go on my shift!
Gold for contraband. Simple as that.
The Guard pays top coin for contraband. We call it a "finder's fee."
Let me guess. You expect a reward for your contraband.
Come to collect your blood money? All right, show me what you have.
Try to keep things orderly. I assure you, everyone will get what they're owed.
All contraband is returned to the owner in whatever condition it was found.
Such pretty little things people steal. What? It's just an observation.
Wouldn't I like to bash a few criminals over the skull, like you do. Must be nice, emptying their pockets.
I don't know how we kept the peace without you Enforcers around!
You're doing good work, Enforcer. Theft and murder have no place in society!
Um, right. Gold for contraband. You don't have to tell me twice.
All those criminals you kill … it must weigh on you Enforcers.\n\nI, uh, I didn't mean anything by that. Do you have any contraband?
Gold? Oh yes, you mean for recovered goods. My pleasure.
You have contraband for me? It is this one's lucky day!
Show me your contraband, and I'll pay the reward. It's a simple system, but it works.
The guard authorizes me to dole out rewards for recovered contraband.
I knew I was going to like you the moment I saw you. Let me tell you about a golden opportunity.
Welcome back, my friend! Are you finally ready to join us and partake in a golden opportunity?
I tried. Gods know, I tried. I won a few bouts, at least. \n\nNext match, they'll be dragging my corpse out.
I like you, despite your willingness to operate on the lawful side of the law. Let me tell you about a better opportunity for someone of your obvious skills and abilities.
Welcome back, my friend! Are you finally ready to come back and resume your membership? It's a golden opportunity!
Honestly, I'm not angry. I'm disappointed. I know it can be hard to walk the narrow precipice of lawfulness, but I thought we were friends.

Seeing eager Enforcers like you jumping into the fray reminds me—it's been too long since I've flipped an outlaw onto his back and given him a good kick in the ribs.\n\nOnly when they resist, of course.
Osgug is very enthusiastic, but take care not to take his claims too seriously. He makes the Enforcers sound little different from the criminals they hunt.
It's over, lawbreaker. Pay your fine, or suffer Imperial justice.
I am the righteous arm of Almsivi. Pay the bounty or suffer the wrath of the Three.
This life is suffering.
Psst! Over here!
Any minute now, those chains up there are going to drag this whole city into Coldharbour. Might as well get used to it. Molag Bal is in charge now.
If there are survivors up there … please, do what you can to help them. I suspect they're in dire straits.

My brothers Armel and Balin aren't the sharpest tools in the shed, but their hearts are in the right place.\n\nI'm sure their gadgets will be a boon to Enforcers everywhere—if I can just get someone to talk to me.
I bring law to the lawless and justice to the unjust. After all, someone has to do it. And since I'm pretty good at it, I thought, why not me?
It must be really exciting being an Enforcer. No collecting tiny bounties. No paperwork to file.

Outlaws fear me, and well they should! After all, I single-handedly took down the Northpoint Gang with a blunted dagger and a fist-full of talcum powder.\n\nYou really don't want to hear how I smuggled those inside.

I admit it, I'm attracted to law and order. That's why I hang around places like this. It's full of such forceful individuals … strong, stoic, good-looking … just like you.\n\nIf I were a criminal, you could collect my bounty any time.
You look like a seasoned Enforcer. I'd love to shadow you one day, so you could show me the ropes.\n\nYou are an Enforcer, right? Keeping track of the latest garb is so confusing.
When I deal with a bounty, I don't tolerate any shenanigans.\n\nShenanigans have no place in law and order.

I am investigating reports of false bounties being applied to honest citizens. If true, it is appalling!\n\nListen, if you hear anything that could help my inquiries, please let me know. And don't worry. I protect my sources!
If you ask me, most mages are trouble. No one should have that kind of power.\n\nBut necromancers are the worst.
I'm one of the Commander's best Enforcers. He told me so himself. He said he no one has mangled more bounties than I have. I'm a regular bounty mangler! \n\nThat's good, right?
I want to report a crime—any crime at all! As long as I get a reward, I'll agree to whatever you want me to tell you. It's my civic duty.\n\nAnd besides, I need some gold.
You heard of the Green Hood? I make that jerk look like an amateur. I expect they'll give me an award for my services.\n\nScratch that—I expect they'll name the award after me.
You know what happened to the last person that interrupted my meditations?\n\nNeither does anyone else! Now go away and bother some other Enforcer.

I've told them a thousand times, I don't know anything! But do they listen to me? No! They just keep asking me about something I don't know.\n\nWell, I know a little. But I'm not going to give them the satisfaction.
Deep down, everyone's dirty. Some of us just look clean.
The Commander allows me to work with select Enforcers. He doesn't completely trust my inventions, I must admit.\n\nYou burn down one village and it marks you for life. Simpletons.

You look like you've picked up more than one Dark Den Remembrance Pillow in your day. I'm sure I recognize you. I never forget a face—especially one as attractive as yours.\n\nHave we shared a moment or two. If not … well, we could start now.
The tragedy of my past haunts me at every turn, but I have found a way to use it as motivation to build a better future.

So what? I had a few meads with Thane Jeggi and Rigurt. It was all in the name of duty! I was looking for a few bounties when they asked me to join them. How could I refuse?\n\nAnd that Rigurt, his tips always pay off big.

Why won't the Enforcers listen to my complaint? I don't know what a citizen has to do to get someone to take action!\n\nI come in here all the time, but no one will issue a bounty for any of my complaints. Maybe I should put a bounty on one of you!
I was suprised the Enforcers would take someone like me in. I'm grateful for the chance to get my life in order.\n\nI'm no good at most things, but this is one thing I can do.

A dull sword, blunted arrows … those aren't weapons for an Enforcer! But that's all the Commander lets me carry. Says I'm too dangerous to wield a weapon around here.\n\nYou know, all my bounties make fun of me? I'm an actual laughing stock. Pah!
There's nothing you can do. It's too late. The Imperial Legion has fallen at our hands. The city is next.

Do you know what these Enforcers told me? They suggested I go out and "commit some crimes!" Get my bounty up to a "profitable level" and they'll be happy to accept my surrender.\n\nBut I'm trying to reform. This is not helping!

The Rat does not have time to talk to strangers all day! He has very important things to do, important people to talk to.\n\nIf you wish an audience with the Rat, you will have to come back another time.
Ever since my youth, I have looked to the God of Mercy and Justice for guidance. At last, Stendarr called to me and led me to these Enforcers. Praise be.
Been with the Enforcers a long time. Before that, I was independent.\n\nI expect I've pulled down more bounties than any one of these amateurs.
If no one here will hunt No-Ears George, I might just do it myself. I'll find justice for my father, one way or the other.
Every time I restock, those thieving bastards clean out my shop! The Enforcers promised they'd take care of it, but nothing ever changes. If the thieves strike again, I'll be ruined!

In my experience, the killer always thinks they're smarter than everyone. They think they can get away with it.\n\nAsk enough questions, though, and they all slip up eventually. Their stories always have one crucial flaw … they're not true.
Imagine it. An outlaw and an Enforcer ….\n\nIt's not possible. I must try to forget him. But how?

I can tell a lot about a person by observation. Take yourself, for instance. You are in this for the thrill, the adventure. You have seen a lot of action, taken a lot of wounds. You have even … died a few times?\n\nNo, that cannot be correct.
Bounties, bah. While the Guard piddles about collecting tiny payments and filing papers, we Enforcers do the real work. Cleaning scum off the streets is its own reward.
