Enforcers exist to supplement the Guard, not to rule the people through fear and bullying tactics. When everyone is already treated like a criminal, what incentive is there to obey the law?\n\nIf the Enforcers cannot police their own, the people shall.

There's only one sure way to cure criminals of their evil ways. Harsh? Cruel? I say necessary!\n\nWhen you find rot in a piece of fruit, you cut it out. When a limb blackens with disease, you chop it off. Consider me the axe.
Werewolves, pah. Every scar is a reminder of why I hunt those Daedra-worshiping animals. Better me than some poor kid who doesn't know what he's in for.
Just between you and me, I brought in a nice haul today. Might be enough to retire on.\n\nJust … don't let any Enforcers catch wind of this.

Enforcers used to be tough as nails and ornery as a senche in heat. But this new breed? Educated, clean-cut, polite? They sicken me!\n\nIf I wasn't so ornery myself, I'd retire and leave this sorry excuse for law enforcement to these namby-pambies.
Mel Adrys is not what you'd call charming. But that doesn't matter when you're hunting vampires. He's focused and relentless. That's what matters.
It takes a deft hand to read magical clues left behind by evildoers, but I've been studying the aftermath of magical events my whole life.

I know I had a couple of bounties with me when I came in here. Caught them this morning. Now where did I leave them?\n\nI tell you, if I lost another pair of criminals, the Commander is going to take it out of my hide.

It takes a very particular set of skills to grow prize-winning pumpkins. And it takes another, different set of skills to avenge the ones who vandalized my garden.\n\nFortunately, I have both sets of skills.
Solving crimes is such fun, isn't it? Delightful. I think a murder mystery would make a most diverting party!

I once spent an entire month among the outlaws. They thought I was one of them! Even hired me to perform a job or two.\n\nThey were sorely disappointed when I eventually arrested the lot of them. Ah, good times!

I wrote a poem for Razum-dar. Do you want to hear it?\n\n"I love you my kitten, from whiskers to tail. I love you in the morning, when you break me out of jail. If you remember one thing, remember this do. My love for you is endless and always true."
You have to listen to me! It's not a prison anymore. It's a nightmare!

You wouldn't believe the bounty Eddie the Pincer had on him. Killed half a dozen people and did unspeakable things to the bodies. But he didn't even see me coming.\n\nGoodbye, Eddie. Hello, retirement!

A true Enforcer can stay on the trail for days on end. Doesn't need to eat or sleep. Refuses to bathe or stop to relieve herself so as not to fall behind.\n\nTake me for instance, I'm so ripe even skeevers won't come near me. But I caught my bounty!
As I see it, the difference between the Enforcers and the army is that the Enforcers do some good, cleaning up the streets. The army just keeps the coffin-makers in silks.

I say if a kid picks up a cheese wheel and throws it at you, that's intent to use deadly force, and I was within my rights to defend myself.\n\nMore than that, I was obligated to remove a violent criminal from the scene.
My name? What, are you writing a book? Look, pretend you never saw me and we'll get along just fine.\n\nOtherwise … well, you won't like "otherwise."

You know the best way into a bank vault? Get to know the banker! Me and Angier Stower have gotten real close, if you know what I mean. She calls me her little lender bee.\n\nBut why am I telling you my plan? Get lost, you piker.
Looks like you've put us back in the fight almost single-handed! We'll handle it from here.\n\nDon't stray too far, though. We might call on you again.
Roy was so much better at this than I'll ever be … him and that dog. But, I have to soldier on, for Roy—and the king.\n\nOh dear, I said more than I meant to. Again! I think I need to be alone now.

I am a great grage! Mage. Great Mage! I cast spells for kings and nobles across the land. So maybe a mis-cast here and there. Anyone can have a bad day. That Breton noblewoman didn't need her eyebrows, not really.\n\nWeren't you buying me a drink?
Graverobbing is a noble profession. If not for us, perfectly good valuables would languish beneath the dirt or in musty tombs for absolutely no reason.\n\nWe perform a public service, we do!
So I'm a vampire. So I drink living blood. I'm not a bad person!\n\nWell, I'm not a very bad person. Why does the Guard want to put a stake through my heart? It's prejudice, pure and simple.
If it weren't for my political leanings, I never would have been targeted.
I am a weapon. Tough as steel and twice as sharp. Remember that, and stay out of my way.

Fahdah the Eyeful hit me. Said I was a terrible thief and a worse beggar. What an honor! It's rare that she displays her prowess for free.\n\nI worked with her once. For the Khajiit crime lord, Splendid-Paws. Those were good days, my friend!
I'm sorry, but the guard confiscated all of my equipment. I can't make any poisons for you, so do not ask.

I've worked for all the best fences and crime lords. Even did a couple of jobs for the Khajiit crime lord, Splendid-Paws.\n\nPerhaps you've heard of me? I robbed the Evermore trade caravan when it was coming and going. No? That figures.

I admit it. I'm attracted to thieves and villains. That's why I like to hang around places like this. It's full of such interesting people.\n\nAre you an interesting person? I think you are. So which one are you? A thief, or a villain? I have to know!
Cyrodiil's an abbattoir, and I got tired of being cattle.

A mask, I need a mask. Oh! And a cape. Yes, yes … though I can never find capes for sale.\n\nOooh—and a code-name! Something that will make the Guard tremble and the nobles eager to hand over their valuables! Something like … the Purple Plague!

A life on the run is no life at all. Take it from me, I've been running for a long time!\n\nAnd you know the worst part? I didn't even commit the crime I'm accused of! It was the tailless Argonian … but no one believes me!
Do you know what they'll do to me if I leave this place? Please, don't tell anyone you saw me here.
Have you seen a beautiful but dangerous-looking Dark Elf around here? Goes by the name of Naryu?\n\nShe told me she was going to meet me down here, but I think she stood me up. Again.
Illegal? How ridiculous! I'm simply purchasing second-hand goods from a reputable dealer of questionable merchandise.\n\nI see nothing wrong with that. And I receive a discount!

I was at Shad Astula trying to master a particularly devious illusion spell when I swear I saw a two-headed rabbit run past. In my distraction I misspoke one of the critical words of the spell and, well, you know the rest.\n\nI was promptly expelled.

They called me a "milk-drinker" for refusing to raise a glass of mead to the Skald-King. The crowd of drunken louts rushed me, but I was able to elude them. So far.\n\nBut I'm afraid to show my face upstairs while the festivities continue.

I prefer the clientele down here to the clods I have to deal with at the Cold-Moon Inn. There's no pretense. No song and dance. Just a frank exchange of goods and services.\n\nSpeaking of which, if you want your goods serviced, just show me your gold.
Why is it if you kill ten or twenty you're a murderer, but if you kill hundreds you're a hero?

I collect items of power—Ayleid relics, Daedric tomes, ancient curios … even family heirlooms. As long as it's unique and hard to acquire, it has a place in my collection.\n\nIf you hear of anything like that, you know where to find me.

I can't do anything right! Today I tried to snatch a fat gold purse, but the mark turned out to be an Enforcer. I barely escaped with my life!\n\nIf you have any tips and wouldn't mind sharing, I'd find some way to make it worth your time.
Serves me right for dying in a sewer. Why couldn't I die on a scenic hilltop or … ooh! In a brothel!
It's true. It's all true. I am the greatest pickpocket who ever lived.\n\nOh, please, all this attention is so embarrassing.
Don't understand why some werewolves try so hard to blend in. What's the fun in that?

I won't say I enjoy killing things, but I won't say I hate it, either. It's a way to make a living, and I'm good at what I do.\n\nNow if I could only find a way to get the Guard off my back, everything would be perfect.
Heel! Heel, Sithis!
The Pact are just puppets. Almalexia? She is just the face of the conspiracy. You will never find the true masters.

Some say that if you delve into the secrets of the ancients you will go stark-raving mad. Balderdash! I've studied arcane lore and Daedric tomes for years, and I'm as sane as anyone down here.\n\nWell, other than you. You appear to be a bit … off.
Criminals really are a dense lot, aren't they?
I don't understand why everyone's so upset. Since when is it a crime to pretend to be one of the queen's tax collectors?

The trick is to always think twelve steps ahead, to keep one eye on the Guard, and to plan for every contingency. That's why I'm a mastermind.\n\nMy intellectual capacity is the desert, while yours is but a grain of sand. It's what I do.
Who knew graht-oaks were so flammable?
There's no retiring from this life. Either your friends turn on you, or the Guard catches up with you.

"The best skooma in Bruma," they used to say. But what does reputation matter now that pirates attacked Haven? This one bets five bottles of her best product that those filthy butchers slaughtered half our clientele!
I can't be the only one whose hands shake when picking locks.
A real criminal! Could I—if it's not too much to ask—could I have your autograph?
What's wrong with you? Never seen a crooked guard before? Well, don't get your armor in an uproar. You people pay me well to mind my own business and make sure this place is a safe haven.
So I got to thinking, what if everything we've been taught is wrong? What if the government is just robbing us, and this whole war is just a distraction?
I once removed a corpse from under a dinner table. At a royal banquet.\n\nNo one was the wiser.

Sometimes I use wigs and costumes, but you'd be surprised how easy it is to change your appearance just by shifting your stance or tilting your head.\n\nDid you see what I did there? I bet for a moment, you thought you were talking to somebody else!
Oh me? I'm not a criminal. I am a student of the criminal mind, however!
Would you hold this jar of spices for me, just a moment?

The indignity of it all! One little mistake and I went from respected scholar to tomb raider, wanted by the Guard. Where's the justice in that, I ask you?\n\nAh well, I do love to collect shiny trinkets from ancient tombs, though!
Hear ye. These citizens were found among the slain. Know that the Empire weeps with you ….
What's taking you so long? Enter the tomb, retrieve the relic, and return it to Tanval. Sounds easy enough to me.
Enter the tomb, retrieve the relic, and return to me.
Your mission is important. Are you done already?
<The creature mutters unintelligibly beneath its breath. It sniffs the air, then snorts.>
Let's go!
You really need to work on your flourish when you deliver the opening whack.
Load those catapults faster, soldiers! We have them right where we want them!
I'm sure Lady Sovelle will turn up. She's a brave and resourceful woman. Far braver than her husband, I'm afraid. He's a bit of a mouse, truth be told.
No!
I think I want to kill something today.
I'm beginning to get a little sick of all this blood.
I wish I had time to properly tend to these wounded soldiers.
Most of our young blood has gone to Cyrodiil. Me? I fish.
Let the action begin! Show us what you've got!
Behold! Vile monstrosities, imported for your entertainment!
The bigger they come … ah, but you know the rest!
Victory!
That had to hurt!
Orc males are only good for two things, and one of them involves war.
A big Orc city just gives everyone an excuse to come here and knock it down. Thought we'd have learned that the first twelve times.\n\nWe don't need Orsinium. Just meat, drink, and land to work.
I need a think-wife. She can think my thoughts while I do other things.\n\nHmm. I don't know what I would do if I wasn't thinking. I guess that's why I need a think-wife.
We moved out here to get away from trouble. Well, at least the old Nord bones should go back to sleep now.
Let's hope that this time it's more of a contest!
Damn Reachmen! The cowards ambushed us!
I'll be all right. I've had worse in my time. But the Orcs—we need to help them!
You look brave. Braver than me, anyway. Are you going to go help Chief Bazrag?
Damn Winterborn! Savages from the Reach, every last one of them!
I don't know what High-King Emeric sees in these savages.
This one has the luck of Two Moons. The Orc peasants? Not so much.
Smash those rifts or be overwhelmed!
I originally named this place "The Far From Home Inn." But as soon as the king became a regular, I decided to rename my humble tavern in his honor.\n\nAfter all, he is my best customer!
The special today is one of the king's favorites.\n\nI recommend ordering something else.
Orutha and I have opened our home and our laundry to any Orc women who need a safe haven. We know firsthand how difficult life can be for a stronghold Orc.
The king invited any stronghold Orcs to abandon their clans and take up residence in his new city. We gladly accepted and never looked back.

I made my fortune as a trader from Northpoint to Daggerfall. I even funded Kurog's earliest attempts to establish an Orc nation. It was only natural that I would retire here.\n\nI want to spend my last days watching Orsinium grow and prosper.
Flames take you!
Join the Vosh Rakh or die!
Kurog was a fool to trust you. Die!
Just help yourself, why don't ya?
Bah. I'll make my own way out of this den of idiots.

We're rather busy here, as I'm sure you can plainly see. We recently opened this guild hall at the invitation of the king.\n\nNow if only we could get him to provide us with more suitable facilities ….
Kill! Kill! Kill all!
Ragh!
Death to unbelievers! Death to false Orcs!
We didn't think anyone could be so gullible, but you proved us wrong!
You killed my echalettes! I'll never join you!
You said you'd protect me! In no way does this match my definition of protection!
Be quiet or I'll let you deal with these brigands yourself!
They didn't have to do this. We run a good inn.

Welcome, welcome. You've discovered the Greedy Gut, the finest inn and tavern in all of Orsinium.\n\nBut if you're looking for a really good time, I'd visit the exclusive cornerclub in the Residential District if I were you.
Where have you been, overseer? Go to the Chamber of Loyalty. Now!
Trinimac lover? How dare you call me that!
Malacath knows you're a coward, and so do I!
You dare interfere in a blood feud?
We have to find that scroll!
Would you like to take over?
Hey there! Can I speak to you for a moment?
We can't raise enough money this way.
Corintthac will not tolerate your interference!
Thanks again. We'll put this donation to good use.
Kurog, no! I will sacrifice my life so that you may live!
This city will be ours, eventually. Of that, I am certain.
I could have sworn these crates were full.
More people coming to Orsinium every day. Luckily, they all need a place to sleep!
<<1>>, get off that wall before you break your neck!
Heads up, sweetie.
Come forth, my other self!
Return! Give me your strength!
What was I thinking coming here? I never should have left Auridon.
I wish I could get you a bigger pen, little ones. For now, get cozy!
Begone, fiend!
Don't! Those are priceless! You don't know what you're destroying!
Not as serene as Elden Root or as bustling as Daggerfall, but Orsinium does have its charms.
How do you tell an Orc from a troll?\n\nIn my experience, you can't tell either much of anything!
Not so loud! You're going to get us killed!
Bal take you, backstabber.
If he doesn't get here soon, I'm going in without him.
Finally you're—oh, you're not him.
No, no … if I jump from here, I'll probably just break my legs.
Please, Yisraza, just go away!
This is the place, right? It has to be!
I should never have come to this miserable place. So cold, so cold ….
<<1>>, have you been drinking again?
I drank just the right amount!
Is there anything you need?
If I catch some fish, perhaps I can trade for food? But wait … if I catch fish, I have food! Everything is coming up Shumeesh!
Are there even fish in there?
Molag Bal cannot be stopped!
This architecture is astounding. A mix of old and new—and some of it truly inspired!
Another customer? I can barely keep up!\n\nWhat can I do for you?
Molag Bal will reward me for this. More bones! We attack tomorrow morning!
You will join the Vosh Rakh or you will die!
How much longer will I need to search?
A hit, a palpable hit!
What next? I love the anticipation!
One good thing about letting in outsiders—new customers mean more variety! I was getting sick of Orcish brew.
Come on! More fighting, less dancing!

I'm studying a bottle of ancient Nord mead we found at the barrow. Alchemist Telarnel proclaimed it perfectly safe to drink.\n\nTo be honest, I'm still working up the nerve to take a swig. It has an unpleasant, musty smell that kind of makes me gag.
Where is my assistant? I swear, he'd lose his tusks if they weren't attached!\n\nOh, is that you Gloorot?
Fight! Fight! Fight!
By Dagon! That must have hurt!
Remember: no mercy, no quarter!
All right, let's get frosty here!
Poison and venom, toxin and tentacles!
Now, meet the cleansing flame of the Igneous Cistern!
Prepare them, those gross creatures! You know the ones I mean!
Bob and weave for us! Strike, thrust, parry, and strike again!
Will they attack from in front, or behind? Spin like the flywheel!
Argonians aplenty in the Vault of Umbrage!
Now you will be tested as never before! Begin!
Demiprince! Make them fight!
That hit the mark!
Call that a death-blow?
Less dancing! More killing!
That's rather better!
This is better than Dragonstar Arena!
What are you waiting for? An invitation?
That was a worthy blow!
A fine blow, savage and merciless!
Now we'll see something memorable!
Don't let that happen again!
Demiprince! Did you see that one?
Such violent urges! Let's give them life, shall we?
Ah!
Let us see how you … ah, yes!
[Quick shout]
You struggle, despite yourself.
Shrok! Shrik! Shrikaaaah!
I shall savor your agony.
Araaaaawwwwnn ….
Ha ha ha!
Amusing sweetmeats! So soft! So full of life!
[Sheets of ice grinding together, laughing]
Faster, you miserable worms! Put your backs into it!
Ha! Did not anticipate that, did you?
The shoes of happiness wrap warmly about your feet.
You don't have to have tusks to hear the truth of Trinimac!
I thought I was done for. A whisker's-width to the left and we wouldn't be talking.
Let those who have tusks listen and hear the truth of Trinimac!
The Xivkyn are at the top, which means …. My apologies. What do you need?
<<1>> used to take bets on racing fiendroths. The army shut it down. Typical.
I had a choice—pay my bounty, or sell goods in the sewers. I should've paid my bounty.
Spend time in the Imperial City, they said. For the Dominion, they said.
The beast hungers!
You don't have the tusks to understand Malacath's fury!
Bend, slave! Grant me your strength!
Let those who have tusks listen and hear the truth of Malacath!
Once I got used to the distant screaming, I barely noticed I'm living in a sewer.
The Emperor used to hold great debaucheries directly below the White-Gold Tower.
Hmm? Let me know if you want anything.
The books are unaffected by mold. An enchantment? Or the page composition itself ….
I found the dog in the Memorial District. No idea how it survived up there.
Never accept a Worm Cultist's surrender. They are no longer worthy of mercy.
My mother would be so proud, if she knew I lived in a sewer.
This one grew accustomed to the stench. Imperial diets must have included beef. A lot of beef.
I was raised in a swamp, and even I refuse to swim in these waters.
Mother said I'd never amount to anything. Here I am, crucial to the war effort. Shows what she knows.
Yes, all is for sale.
The creatures here are relentless. Draw no attention unless you must.
This is all according to plan. A terrible, poorly constructed plan. Praise the Tribunal.

I like taverns. Some of my best memories were made in places just like this. I wonder if anyone plans to start a good, old-fashioned brawl?\n\nI suppose that with all the Orcs around, chances are pretty good. I can't wait!
Daggerfall has been apprised of Baron Materre's treachery. He shall pay for the lives lost on that icy shore—including the life of his son.
No one hurts my durzog!
Durzog, to me!
Almost had one as big as my arm! But it just took my bait. Typical.
I wish I hadn't listened to her. We should have come to the city together.
<<1>>, here, boy!
Stretch your legs, <<1>>, we'll be on the hunt soon.
The slaves act on ancient orders. You disturb their work.
<evil laughter 2>
Hmm. That doesn't appear to be very interesting.
I am a servant of Trinimac. I am a servant of the Vosh Rakh.
I serve the Vosh Rakh. I believe in Trinimac.

This probably sounds strange, but I found the blizzard to be mildly exciting, what with all the wind and the crashing ships and everything.\n\nI have a few things for sale, but I'll need to fill my stock when we finally reach Orsinium.
Your death will elevate me. For the Vosh Rakh!
No, no, I don't lend out gold anymore. Too many of my friends took advantage of my generosity and now I'm more destitute than a peasant from the outlying clans.
How did you get out of your cages?
Keep those healers away from the tree!
Save the briarhearts!
I've never wanted to be tied down. No stall or confined selling space for me!
Unless you're a really tall mug of bog-iron ale, get out of my face.
You look like you carry a full pouch of gold. This one finds that very attractive in a customer.
We are merchants, yes. From a far-away land. We bring strange and exotic goods to the people of Orsinium.\n\nOnce we're set up and open, this one will be happy to show you our wares.
I have come to Wrothgar to make my fortune. If you would be so kind as to buy something, I will be slightly richer than I was before you arrived.
Use your nose, <<1>>.
Intruders! Now we can kill the priests!
Don't go clogging up my alembic with any of those fancy High Elf reagents. Flower petals and butterfly dust … bah!
In the market for a new rucksack? You won't find better—not even in Orsinium. Have a look.
Looking to taste some Morkul spirits? A touch too strong for these foreigners, but I reckon you'll love it!
Thirsty? Kick your heels up and knock back a few!
Not much grows up here. The soil's too hard. But I do have a few things that might interest you.
Horses, bears, cats, guar … it's all the same. Show them respect, and they'll do the same.\n\nBut enough lectures. What do you need?
Enchanting is a far grander trade than smithing, don't you think? Please don't tell anyone I said that.
Remember, a fine Orcish jack should be snug across the middle.\n\nIf anyone complains, tell them to stop gorging themselves on raspberry pies.
Ever seen a Morkul smith put hammer to anvil? Well, keep your eyes open. You might learn something.
Smell that smoke? Hear the pump of those bellows? Nothing like a day at the forge to stir our blood, eh?
Been shipping lumber to Orsinium by the wagon-full. If they don't finish that damned city soon, we'll have nothing but weeds to work.
Hungry? Well, I don't serve anything flashy, friend. Just good, wholesome Orcish fare.
The ogres around here kick like mammoths in heat. I'd buy some strong armor if I were you.
These Morkul Orcs are pleasant enough … as Orcs go, I mean. Just don't speak ill of their forge. I'd hate to lose another customer.
I've got plenty of fine goods for sale! No raw pig meat, though. You Orcs do like to eat raw pig meat, right …? Did I mention I love Orcish culture?
Better loosen those purse strings, stranger. Arcane goods don't come cheap out here.
One stroke with a Morkul blade is equal to three from any other weapon. Our arms are peerless. That is a fact.
Beautiful view, eh? Can I help you?
You need goods? I got 'em.
Everything's for sale—except this mug. This mug is mine.
Don't bother with the others. You'll find the best merchandise right here.
You have angered the wrong king!
I will avenge her death!
I'm not religious, but if worshiping Trinimac helps drag our backward arses out of the strongholds? Sign me up.
I would rather burn down this mountain than let my enemies see victory!
My friends tell me I shouldn't drink my own stock. Know what I say to that?
I wonder what those Dwarves used to drink? Probably spring-grease and mole droppings or something.\n\nI'd try that.
Hungry? Of course you are. What'll you have?
If we don't hear anything from the quarry soon, I'm packing up my things and heading for Orsinium, clan be damned.
Clearing that quarry out must have taken a toll on your gear. Can I get you anything?
Looking for soul gems? Well, I'm the only game in town.
I'm going stir-crazy in here. My brother brought me some books. Hrmph. Not a single picture in any of them.
Hmm. That wasn't supposed to happen. Do the statues suggest an order?
You shave coins, I ban you. So don't shave coins.
Just keep your hands where I can see them until we're done.
Nobody followed you down here, right?
Ah, my favorite customer! How can we help each other?
Suspicious behavior? I'm just watching that … box over there.\n\nIt's a … fascinating box. All rectangular and everything.
You know what I hate? Stolen goods. They're grimy and covered in other people's crud.\n\nI hate that!
I did it! I picked a noble's pocket!\n\nWhat a thrill! What a sense of accomplishment! I can't wait to go out and try it again!
I sure would like to rob a noble. Any idea where I would start? No? Forget I asked.
"Trinimac's blessed child Avalian charged the mountain, driving his blade into the heart of the beast."
I've heard reports of strange weather out on the coast. Rogue blizzards or something. If you're headed toward the sea, be careful.
Nobody steals from us!
The enemy is upon us. Protect our quarry!
If Snagara dies, we're done. Protect her!
I told you this would never work!
You can't have the snow rats!
Face my shield, horker!
Protect the old snow rat or we don't get paid!
Thief! This catch is ours!
Just imagine, a guildhall right in the heart of Orsinium! A safe haven for the research, experimentation, and learning of magicka. It's remarkable!
Not many safe havens in the mountains. Better to stretch one's legs than watch one's tail.
That's it! I get better every time!
I hear the food isn't going to last much longer in the city
You still think the city is running out of food, I don't think so.
Pull up a chair. Have a drink! You're welcome as long as you bring no trouble.
Got fresh ingredients from all over Wrothgar—and I do mean fresh. Some of this meat bites back!
Nothing happened. If you must guess, at least try to guess correctly.
The mammoth are sparse here. Have you noticed? Their population dwindles.
The soldiers will send me back to the wild if they spot me. Do me a favor and keep your mouth shut.
Slay the mortals! Leave none alive!
Mmm … those smells coming from <<1>>'s kitchen!
I might try a helping.
I used to think she was a roadside cook … not an artist with an oven.
Look, little beasts! More toys!
Be praised! More blood for the feast!
Blood! Taste the blood, my beasts!
Kill them all. Save the strongest for my scathing-blade!
Ah, to murder innocents by Scamp-fire … such a delight!
Molag Bal will be pleased that we continue his work!
This quarry will make a fine hunt!
Gorag gar!
Yorag gara!
Soon you'll be soot and ash!
Ah! Another skeleton for the tree!
After I kill you, I shall animate your corpse!
Behold my lovely roiling cloud! I shall await you there.
I will scorch you to ash!
Now for the final phase. Watch as I absorb all the power I need!
Blood and meat, that's all you are to me.
I shall cremate you before you die!
Worm! I'll swallow you whole!
You are just a pest to be swatted away!
Got you now, weakling!
Enough! You try my patience. Take this!
That just makes me even angrier!
You shall fry in your own skin!
Pain! Pain! PAIN!
Burn! Burn! Burn!
You'll die—like all the others.
Now you shall taste the lightning!
Think you can take me? You're wrong!
The light will not save you!
You are not worthy to gaze upon her!
I'm going to enjoy this!
I challenge you!
Time to prove what they say of you!
Worm! You're making me angry!
Are you a coward?
You don't have the guts!
I'm too much for you. I see that now!
This will sizzle your spine!
Ha ha ha! Bring me another!
Mortals! So predictable!
The ritual, interrupted, is nearly complete. You will be my final test.
The ritual is complete! Know my true wrath!
Supplies are now reaching the city on a regular basis. Maybe now our basic city functions will get repaired.
Yeah! The king is dead! Long Live King Bazrag!
I welcome Morkul clan to Orsinium! Their work is without compare. Some will say otherwise … but they are wrong.
Are we lost? It feels like we're lost. I'll … you know, I'll just follow you.
Pathetic.
This one does not mind the cold. It keeps the goods fresh, yes?
To Oblivion with this—somebody get me a splint! I'm done just sitting here and—gah!
Be careful out there, friend. Just look what the mountain did to me! Actually don't look. It's, uh … it's far too gruesome!
Harpies here are vicious. If you forget to watch the sky, they'll pick you up and crack you open.
I've followed the researchers for months. They feed me and let me sleep in the equipment tent.\n\nI should probably ask for a job, but I don't want to ruin a good thing.
Dig in. It's all fresh.
All the cups are freshly scrubbed. Just like all the records of Varen Aquilarios.
This one sells no skooma. It is a vicious rumor! Everyone knows to go to <<1>>'s cousin for that.
Shouldn't have stocked that much armor. Busted the wagon on my way in. Care to lighten the load?

It's no inn, but I prefer it to the noise in Orsinium. "The only steel worth wearing is steel you forge yourself, blah blah blah."\n\nSpend a bit extra for an import from Rivenspire. Just as strong, and much nicer to look at.
Do you feel the more gold you come across, the more problems you see? This one does not! Let us deal.
Paupers beware! No haggling!
A lament: The Mane has not been by this sale season. As many shames as moons.
A lament: Never have I once successfully sold an item to King Emeric. Said he, "One crown is enough."
The ancient dwarves traded in a coin made of something far denser than gold. One finds this curious — is gold not enough?
This one does not accept barter of trinkets or enchanted butterflies. Gold, only.
Come, erect your spine of trade, let us share our profits!
Valenwood has a long and rich history, do you know? Is its history rich in gold?
This one does not accept barter of holy objects or work in kind. Gold, only.
This one does not accept barter of ash or scrib jelly. Gold, only.
This one does not accept barter of favors or threats. Gold, only.
This one does not accept barter of moon-sugar or skooma. Gold, only.
Can you take gold with you to Sovngarde? Leave it here, it will be safe. Have faith!
This one does not accept barter of arms or armor. Gold, only.
This one does not accept barter of swords or sand. Gold, only.
A good day. A good day to spend all of your money! Or just much of it.
A fine night, to drink, or dance, or spend a tidy sum on only the very finest of things.
Do you dream of being pursued by hunters, longing for your hide? Dream instead of riches!
Let us deal, yes? But we leave the bats and such things at home.
We find retail more profitable than mercenary work, truthfully. But this one has never profited from such a noteworthy contract as the Guild's.
The Madgod would encourage you to spend on trifles such as an acreage of cheese or shoes made of live cats. He and we are nothing alike. Spend here!
We know, gold is meaningless when one could die tomorrow in another, stranger, dungeon rife with peril. Spend your money here instead!
Let our relationship be clear! You are poor. Look, don't touch.
Though this one hungers for gold, she does worry after the needs of the individual. Take care of yourself.
In all of your time adventuring, what is the size of your hoard? Unburden and unpack! Give me your money!
One suspects, if you are so affluent as to afford these goods, you may have had a somewhat dodgy inheritance.
Always a pleasure to greet you. What can we do for you this visit? These goods may thrill!
Your shipment makes standing here all day worthwhile.
If you need anything, please speak to my wife. She'll be more than happy to assist you!
The cod are running thick this year. They're a little scrawny, but I make it up in volume.
I'm sorry I was late, but a bat … made off … with the baby. How do you tell someone that? Hoo, I could go for some skooma!
I wish I had some autumn-honey tea to sell. These Twilight Cantors are going to sing themselves hoarse.
We try to be … accommodating to our clientele.
Our vault is secure. Despite the rumors.
No complaints about the prices. I won't haggle.
You should avoid <<1>>, the blacksmith. He is a known cheat.
Welcome. Did I already welcome you? Apologies.
My condition is expensive to maintain. It's why I charge a premium to the idiots.
I won't tolerate thieves. Show me your coin, or show me your back.
No, I don't follow the Eight. And it's none of your bloody business why.
This city is a dump. Trash, everywhere you look.
Have you considered a new outfit? Fine clothes can turn your fortunes around.
I don't forget my best customers. Nor do I forgive their debt.
Last night I thought the sky had four moons. A few mugs later, it was back to two.
I can supply you with magical supplies. If you're in the market. And discreet.
You should never forgo undergarments when wearing my leathers. All sales are final.
Hm.
Just say what you need and go. I can't be seen talking to you.
My father's treasure should be nearby.
You know what's best with a good red? The Nords call it "mammoth cheese." It's strong yet unrefined, much like the Nords.
Give these monks a wide berth, walker. Their minds still reel and sway with the Bent Dance.
Can Teifi help you find anything? This one is anxious to keep busy.
Pick your poison! Er, I don't sell actual poison. It's an expression.
I charge extra for each pet. And lice are pets.
It sees you—or me! Us? Let's share the blame!
Nool—golaraj ra'ham!

I'm one of the Gurgeses. The merchant family? Perhaps you've heard of us.\n\nThat said, I have nothing to do with the business and I positively detest my uncle. I'm part of the guild now and proud of it!
What do you think? Can I pull off an uppity, noble accent? What am I saying? Of course I can! I really am an excellent actress!\n\nNow, where did I put my silver tiara?
Come any closer and I will break you.

Step right up and let me show you what I have for sale!\n\nOh, sorry. Old habits die hard. I used to be a merchant, but that was a long time ago. Now I'm part of the guild. We still have a guild, don't we?

Do you like explosions? I just love explosions! All the bright colors and loud noises. It's so exciting!\n\nAnd fire. I positively adore fire! The way it dances, the way it burns. And fiery explosions? Well, those set my toes all atingle!

The Thazahrr Cartel brought me to Abah's Landing, but the odds of me attaining my full potential are astronomically better if I'm part of the guild. After all, the Iron Wheel has eliminated most of the competition for me.
Your souls are Namiira's, but your skins are mine!

Quen is a decent climber, but she's way too tall to get into those small nooks and crannies where they keep the real treasures.\n\nThat's why the guild needs me. I suppose height has its advantages, but I prefer to keep things short and sweet.
These new recruits are all well and good, but I'm glad to see more experienced guild members, such as myself, returning to the fold.\n\nI just hope Zeira can restore our former glory.
Khashool! Dro-sha zargo!
We will kill you. Lorkhaj will consume you,
Bloodshed is an art. Let us instruct you.

Looks like <<1>> did a decent enough job in my absence. Even brought in a few new recruits of his own. That's what I call "initiative." But now that I'm back, he can leave the guild's protection in my hands.

Velsa was a true professional. Never even had a desire to sample her own wares. I, on the other hand, have no restraint whatsoever. Besides, what doesn't kill us outright is sure to make us stronger.\n\nI do believe I read that in a book or something.

Erengor's one of mine. I brought him into the guild, trained him. I'm glad to see he's made a place for himself while I was gone.\n\nUnfortunately, I don't think he's happy to see me back here. I suppose I'll have to deal with that too, in short order.

I thought it best to wait for the Iron Wheel to depart before I returned.\n\nZeira performed admirably through difficult times. Imagine how much better she'll do now that we're all here to counsel her.

Call me "the Captain." Everyone else does. You know, I was a pirate and smuggler before I joined the guild. Indeed, I poured my personal fortune into the organization. Funded some of our biggest heists, back in the day.
Moonlight cannot thwart me!
Dancers in the dark, come forth!
The end is nigh, vermin.
The Ghost Moon's shadows have gathered again!
The shadows are nearly through! You must hurry!
It'd just go easier if he'd 'fess up.
It is slain? Good. Now hurry—your allies need you!
You think you've won? Pathetic.
Making me wait is going to cost him.
Doom is upon you. You will drown in shadow and blood!
The light will protect you! Go!
I should never have borrowed that money!
Unleash your fury!
Bathe in the hail of sorrows!
I will break you!
Submit!
You cannot hide from me!
Ghost cats, arise!
Weak! You are all weak!
Burn!

I saw those Iron Wheel hooligans wandering around outside the city. Lord Orahan of the at-Addin Syndicate says not to worry, but I know an invasion force when I see one.\n\nMight as well eat now, for we'll probably all be dead by tomorrow.
My wife insists on moving about the city and mingling with the riffraff. Personally, I prefer the charming confines of our suite at the Thazahrr estate, but a little fresh air never hurts, I suppose.

Thieves Guild? Now why in the name of the Eight would I want to get involved with those incompetents?\n\nI make much more gold on my own—and I don't have to split the proceeds with guildmasters who do none of the work and take all of the credit.

Here's a tip, free of charge. If someone tells you not to be a Hew, don't take it personally. That's just our friendly way of saying, "don't be a dumb arse."\n\nSig All-Friend's a friend to all, but next time I'll have to charge you, you understand.

Unless you plan to take off those clothes and get up on the stage with that tasty glass of shipwreck wine, we've got nothing to talk about.\n\nDamn landlubbers always swarming around me like fleshflies to a candle!
A fine day for finding, if I must say.
Have you heard the tale of Prince Hew and the seven sad swans? No? It really is quite amusing.\n\nRemind me to tell you about it sometime.
I wonder … perhaps the new commodore would enjoy a few dancers sent to her quarters? As far as gifts go, that's one I wouldn't throw out the porthole, if you know what I mean.
Ah, what have the waters washed in today?
No questions, only gold and wares.
Looking for some rest and relaxation? Then you've come to the right place! Let me tell you about our services ….
The guild would frown upon anyone filching my wares. Just so we're clear.
Purse feeling a bit light?
Forget something? No need to wander all the way back with me here.
Relieve me of my goods? For gold, I mean.
They claim my anvil isn't as solid as it should be. I say they wouldn't know a hammer from a saw blade if it hit them in the head and said hello!
Your valuables will be as snug as a bug in a rug in our vaults. I guarantee it!
Shall I teach you another lesson in futility?
Hey, what do you think you're doing? Get lost before I decide to add your name to my arrest writ.
I am the chosen of Akatosh and you are nothing.
I'm going to go put our mark in the grotto.\n\nAs soon as my bum knee stops acting up. Yeah, as soon as that.
Feel free to use the workshop. Just stay away from the grain baskets. If I catch you stealing any of my crop, I'll feed you to the next dire wolf pack that wanders by.
Oh, Emperor Varen, you've lost weight! That's good, yes? Fit and lean. A true inspiration for the troops!
No questions, only gold and wares.
This one's back is not as industrious as your hands. No more for today.
I'm a terrible beggar! I can't remember my lines. I always wind up saying the wrong thing. It's so embarrassing!\n\nI should just wander off into the wilderness and die. That's what I should do.
I won't be the one in chains today!
Toss these curs into a cage!
All hands! Open fire!
Blow the mongrels down!
I wonder why they've suddenly put us on high alert?
Search everywhere! She's hiding around here somewhere!
Everyone here is a criminal! Every last one of them!
Busy tonight. Wonder what's got everybody on edge?
Eyes open, this one's used to going unnoticed.
Abah's Landing deserves the torch and nothing more.
This place makes me homesick.
Couldn't they have given us something more glorious to do?
Stay alert! No one gets near the Magnifica!
Goodbye, Hew's Barf. I hope I never see you again!
These merchant lords are dressed up rabble, nothing more.
I only wish punishing these ringleaders would deter their ilk.
Ah, fresh life energy for the taking!
I'll drain the energy from your body!
Arise and defend your master!
Calm down. We're here to help.
My first thought when I arrived in Anvil was, "the Fighters Guild can fix this city."\n\nNow? I think, "whose arse do I have to kiss to get a posting in a more civilized location?"
The Fighters Guild doesn't choose sides. On the other hand, we can be bought. Vast amounts of gold can go a long way when it comes to determining where our loyalty lies.

Rumor has it that the Order of the Hour will soon patrol the streets of Anvil with the same impunity they show in Kvatch.\n\nI can't see the Provincial Governor allowing that to happen, but what do I know of politics?
I admit we're a bit obsessed with the written word, but can you blame us? Words convey knowledge, and knowledge provides power.\n\nIn the end, isn't that what magicka is all about?

We really need to get more organized. So many of our books have yet to be sorted and cataloged, and I hate to see perfectly good volumes stacked up like so much cord wood instead of being shelved for easy access.\n\nPerhaps I should hire an intern ….

Alchemy isn't magic. Not exactly. But I suppose it's closer to magic than to, say, what they do over in the Fighters Guild. What do they do over there, I wonder?\n\nAnyway, feel free to use my equipment. If you need to mix up any potions, that is.
Do you need to use one of my enchanting stations? Go ahead. I rent them by the hour. No, no, just pulling your pigtails! But if you want to buy some supplies, I wouldn't turn away your gold.
My carryalls will keep your most valuable possessions safe from cutpurses, pickpockets, robbers, marauders, floods, famines, and rampaging beasts of all shapes and sizes. I guarantee it!
I import the finest stock from across the land—even got some that were born and bred back on the Shatul Ranch.\n\nThat's why this is the finest stable south of Varen's Wall. Nothing even comes close.
You know what the secret is to making a memorable libation? Good water!\n\nI get my water from the bay where the sewer runoff meets the sea. Best water you ever tasted! Just mind the lumpy bits ….
The secret to my most popular dishes? Wine!\n\nOh, not in the stew pot. The wine goes into me! I can't remember a single recipe unless I'm as drunk as a skeever in a wine cask.

Nothing has gone right since they erected that damn wall between the Gold Coast and the highlands. Except for a few farms, this one must depend on the vagaries of merchant ships and pirates to replenish my stores.\n\nMakes me want to pack up and move.

The Provincial Governor permits me to make most of her outfits. In fact, I'm working on a stylish piece that she'll debut at her next ball. It's my best design yet, if I do say so myself, and it makes her look spectacular.

The provincial governor commissioned an outfit for her next ball! I was able to secure a fine bolt of brushed echatere wool from Wrothgar that will compliment my design amazingly well.\n\nJust between us, it puts Elneri's best work to shame.

You know what I tell every new arrival to the Gold Coast? The same thing I'm about to tell you. You need better armor, or at least a good repair.\n\nLucky for you, you've come to the right place for both of those services.

Someday I'm going to join one of the pirate crews. Sail around the world, pillaging and drinking and singing pirate songs ….\n\nOr maybe I'll head north and sign on with one of the armies. Do you think I'd make a good soldier? No, me neither.
Don't you just love the feel of wood in your hands? So hard, so thick, so ready to reveal its true form as you apply sweat and muscle to the task ….\n\nOo, I get excited just thinking about it!

Planks! I hate cutting planks! There's no challenge to it, no opportunity to show off my massive amount of talent. But what do pirates want? More planks for their damn ships!\n\nDon't tell me you need some planks, too. I hate my life.

We don't talk about the arena, though sometimes I'll take in a bout or two. It's terrible to watch, with the blood and the broken bones, but it's also kind of exciting!\n\nI suppose it can't be all bad if the Count and Primate allow it to remain open.

Have you heard about the latest murders? I wish the count would do something about these terrible crimes. It's getting so bad, it's starting to feel like Anvil and not the fair city of Kvatch that I know and love.
This is the bank for you, my friend! Never a scandal or a problem here, not a one! Can the depository in Anvil say the same? I think not!
Some say that Varen's Wall cut us off from the benefits of Imperial culture. If you ask me, Cyrodiil turned away from us long before the wall was erected.
This is the alchemy shop. If you're looking for the tavern, that's the building up the street with the drunks stumbling out of it.

Ever since Anvil's new governor declared the Gold Coast to be a free and independent state, life has gotten progressively worse here in Kvatch. I really wish Count Carolus would just do something about that dreadful woman!

I love poetry! When I'm not taking care of the stables, I'm devouring every volume I can get my hands on.\n\nI particularly enjoy poems about horses and other mounts. Call me single-minded, but I know what I like.
"Herein lie the countless damned, their worth measured only by the weight of the gold that condemned them. Choose your target and kill well."
Follow me if you want to escape!
I know an escape route!
Oh, you're back? Hold on—let me—grr! Who keeps stealing my ink pot?
Anything I can do for you?
May I be of service?
Stick to the stone floor to avoid the lightning arcs!
More remains? Another dead associate, another piece of this sorry puzzle.
Clarity blooms through the fog of the Hist, but to be charged with such a terrible task ….
<A library's worth of paper has traversed this weathered notice board, but a few fresh bounties have been recently afixed.>
Even the Governor's pirates shop here and spend their gold—and they usually never do that!
It's all fresh off the ship. Which ship? Best not to ask.
Think you'll find a better deal elsewhere? You'd be dead wrong.
Welcome to my humble shop out here in the middle of nowhere. It's amazing how many dubious characters pass by this way.\n\nNot that I'm implying anything about you, of course.

I'll sell to you, but only if you're one of Akatosh's faithful. I suppose I'll even sell to you if you worship any of the other Divines.\n\nBut if you're a godless Daedra worshiper, I suggest you take your business to another city.
These villains are cowards, hiding in the shadows!
And those who treat murder as business are the worst of all!
I trust your contracts have been abundant and lucrative?
Astara seems more relaxed now that we're back to the usual murder and mayhem, wouldn't you agree?
Oh the trials heaped upon Akatosh's faithful servants!
Our beloved Grand Sermonizer has been taken from us!

Isn't Mirabelle amazing? She's beautiful, excellent at what she does, and she isn't afraid to say exactly what's on her mind.\n\nNext to murdering insects for the Night Mother, she's my favorite thing in the whole world!
I suppose you were expecting my predecessor, hmm? Know that I, Fortunata ap Dugal, now rule Anvil and brooks no gainsay from the common rabble.
Rats! I eat you now!
Ha! Now you feed the worms and lizards!
That's not helpful.
Can you spare a few pieces of gold?
Can't you see I'm busy?
When accounts lie fallow for decades, there's no harm in skimming! If only the bank in Kvatch agreed ….
I'm not used to being ashore. All this stability makes me queasy.
I don't want to know you. You'll be dead within the year.
Xal-Nur make lizard dead!
Xal-Nur strong!
All fear Xal-Nur!
Trample stupid rats!
Loose wamasu!
Washing not make you safe, slave-scum!
Have you not taken enough?
Organizing fights is the easy part. It's cleaning up after them that's murder.
Consume! Consume!
Join us!
<A library's worth of paper has traversed this weathered notice board. A few fresh bounties have been recently afixed.>
Limenauruus! Arise! Stamp out the fires of life!
Let the cloak of shadows consume you!
This creature has limits. I do not. Take my power!
What you find here, you will wish you'd left buried.
I honestly hope the Black Dragon finds me. That armor would fetch a fine price. I'll have to be sure not to melt her inside it when I kill her. Maybe best to stick to frost spells ….

I'm so proud of you! Silencer. I never expected to know one of them.\n\nYou accomplished so much in so little time. Fortunata, the Black Dragon, Artorius. Tanek says you did it to make the rest of us look bad. That's not true, though, is it?
Silencer! Well look at you! I figured Tanek or Mirabelle would achieve that rank first, but there's no denying you deserve it.\n\nJust don't expect me to bow or anything.

I know I usually make jokes, but I wanted to say thanks. You killed the Black Dragon. You sent Artorius to the Void. And you accomplished all that without a modicum of my grace or social skills.\n\nWell done, Silencer. Well done.
Welcome, Silencer. Feel free to use our Sanctuary whenever you're visiting the Gold Coast.
My victory is preordained!
The hour of reckoning is at hand!
Akatosh, accept this offering!
Feel that? It's the chill of the grave.
Don't you like my pets?
The hostel isn't as busy as it was before the war, but mother and I always find ways to make ends meet.
Eager to prove your worth, Initiate?
Are you prepared for the day's bloody work?
The Void beckons, Silencer.
Was I not clear, Initiate?
You've returned alive. I trust your quarry does not share that luxury.
Your victim awaits, Assassin.
I await your report, Assassin.
How many have you sent to greet the Dread Father today?
There is not much else to be shared about your task. I trust you will make do.
Good boy.
Good boy.
Our working relationship is as follows: You work, I don't plot your demise. \n\nNow, I would suggest you check the ledger.
If you're hoping I have something special lined up just for you, I do, it's called disappointment. Check the ledger.
If becoming a Silencer hasn't gone to your head, there are still plenty of contracts in need of a professional touch.
If you're looking for more details on your job, Initiate, what's posted is all you get.
How's that contract coming along, Assassin?
There will be plenty of time to talk after you've finished your work.
Good news to report?
You've got a little blood, right about … there. I trust it's not yours.
Silencer, a pleasure as always.
Chanters preach against the Dark Brotherhood. What about dire wolves? More likely to kill you when you're traveling beyond the city walls.
No food but what you see. You want a meal, you cook it yourself. There's a pot around here somewhere.
Priests and pirates don't mix. You remember that, mate.
A pirate fortress and a chapel of the Divines sitting side by side. They're like pond-water and fish-oil, these two … without the great smell of course.
You're not fooling old Ghaturn. Nope. Got eyes in the back of your head …. I mean, my head.\n\nYou know what I mean!
You're not one of those damned Red Sails, are you? Only thing I hate worse than a cheat is a cheat that's rubbish at cheating. Have some pride in the craft, right?
I can tell you, it's tough to go straight in a town like this, but my pirating days are over. \n\nDon't give me that look! I'm serious!

I've heard all kinds of stories about that lighthouse. Some say it's haunted. I don't put much stock in ghost stories, but I've seen shadows in the windows at all hours of the night. Dark doings I wager.
This chapel is a disgrace! I haven't had a naked priest squeeze my bottom in decades! And the bosoms? Don't even get me started on the bosoms!\n\nNo wonder Dibella's turned her back on us!
I'm just here to fight in the arena. Soon as I've filled my purse, I'm headed back to Grahtwood. Can't handle these Imperial priests and their scroll-thumping.
You'd best mind your manners here. The Dragon God of Time drapes his wings around the faithful, but his fury has no limits. You do not want to invoke his wrath.

You seen anything suspicious? The Order of the Hour is supposed to keep us safe, but there are evil forces at work in Kvatch. Good thing I've got such a talented mutt. If there's a dark plot, Gristle will sniff it out.
The light of Akatosh shall destroy you!
Dragon God, protect your servant!
He should have been here hours ago!
Damn it, Alexia. Where have you gotten off to?
Only the finest sweetrolls available, perfect for the arena! Portable, sizable, and delicious!
Muck-dwellers! Kill them!
The Hist demands blood!
Your bones will make fine mortar!
Heed me or suffer!
Taste the sap and give in!
You have no power here. No one escapes Mazzatun!
Wither and die!
I thought Fortunata would help restore my family's honor. Didn't realize she cared more for coin than reputation.\n\nThough I have neither, these days. Rotten luck at the arena.

Despite what the town criers said, I didn't intend to poison my neighbor's children. Those cats of hers would not stop yowling! A plate of poisoned kippers was enough to do the trick.\n\nChildren should know not to eat strange food from the ground!
I taught Fortunata how to navigate. You'd think she'd at least grant me an audience.
Fortunata fell off her own ship, once. It's true! And she'd soaked herself to the gills before she fell in, if you get my meaning.
I'm going to try to meet up with Torrid Torolon at the tavern later. I hope he'll let me buy him a drink!
<Watches you cautiously.>
The blood of a thousand thieves can attest: your wealth is safe with me.
No need to carry all that surplus with me around.
The blood of a thousand thieves can attest: your wealth is safe with me.
No need to carry all that surplus with me around.
Smell the desperation? That's your clue that another Pardoner's Brawl is about to start!
Victory! Three cheers for the survivors! They get to live another day!
Be gone!
Hear the whispers of the night!
Die in the dark!
You think I'm surrounded? How cute.
Boo.
Goodbye now.
Mephala! Lend me your power!
I love playing hard to get!
Mmm. Look who comes crawling back.
What's that?
This is going to hurt.
Blood for the Spinner!
Do not resist!
Behold, the price of kinship.
More souls for the Spider!
Aw, was the dark too much for you?
So plump! So fresh!
Just a taste! Just a taste!
Maybe I should shed some weight.
Chop or filet?
Here, give me a kiss!
Not so fast, sweetmeat!
Mmm … supper time!
You were delicious.
Ah ah ah! Can't hide from me!
The end of the world is unavoidable. Chaos is inevitable. The Serpent wills it so.
Thanks for clearing the way.
That's finished here.
I will stop you dead in your tracks!
Hey, ugly face! Get outta my way! I … wait, I'm sorry. Your face is fine. It's just kind of blurry.
This one is wasted as a laborer. Sahalu is management material.
Vosh golgrashim!
Dung-covered Iron Orcs! What did Shurami ever do to them? Shurami only uses her knives to cut prices!\n\nLet me show you my stock.
Ha! I heard that! Your stomach's growling like a hungry welwa! Sit a spell and let me fill that belly.
If these Iron Orc attacks get any more frequent, I'm going to have to start brewing tree-bark ale and gravel brandy. A woman's got to make a living, after all!
I know, I know. Who can eat fresh meals out here in the wastes? But you know what? Even boot-leather tastes good when cooked with the right spices. \n\nI think you'll like what I've got in stock.

You there, have you heard the one about the Orc chief and the pumpkin patch? No? \n\nDon't give me that look! I've got plenty of Orc friends. One of them even told me this joke! Where do you think I got it?
Feel free to use the equipment—just so long as you don't have any of that damn red brittle on you.

Never thought I'd be hauling red brittle out of this mine, but that twitchy High Elf down in the storehouse seems to think it's worth something. Hopefully we'll be back to mining gold and real ore in a few days. \n\nIt's not worth getting the shakes.
It's nothing. I just haven't been sleeping well. I've got to get back to work. Right after I catch my … my breath.
Fix the winch. Keep it working. Don't let the rope break.\n\nYou know the best thing about being an engineer? Me neither. I should have stuck to gambling.
I'd love to lend a hand and take out a few of those ugly Iron Orcs, but these rocks aren't going to mine themselves.
This town is cursed. Selfishness, avarice, vanity. Get out while you can—before you become another victim like this poor woman.

Want to hear the name of the epic story I'm writing? "Trees Rain Stone in an Empty Sea." Evocative, isn't it? \n\nYou don't look very well. Perhaps you should step away from the mine and get some fresh air.
This one is happy that so many have fled Dragonstar. Azzaril has the whole mine to himself. Harder work, but a bigger share, yes?
Does the unworthy swine have something to say? Save it for the Arena, little pig.
As long as no one hits me in the face, I'll be fine. I hate it when people hit me in the face.
Hail, noble adversary! Come and break bread with me, for tomorrow we may die!
You're wearing that gear into the Arena? Well, I'd bring along a restoration staff or two if I were you.

Excuse me, capon jam. I think one of us is confused. This table is reserved for Stone-Fish warriors.\n\nI don't see any Stone-Fish colors and I don't recognize your ugly face, so I wager you're in the wrong place. Get lost.
Don't believe everything you may have heard. My goods certainly did not fall off the back of a caravan wagon.
The Captain frowns upon loose talk, but I heard the Arena uses some powerful magic. Some kind of glamours they turn on and off like lanterns. Be ready for anything in there. I know I am!
Some friendly advice. In the Arena, keep your menders safe. If you take out your opponent's healer while protecting yours, you'll be one step closer to victory.\n\nHealers are useful that way.
You have that killer instinct. I can see it in your eyes. Hold on to that feeling, stranger. There's no room for mercy in the Arena.
My nan always said that a starving bear will eat itself. \n\nI say it's better to eat someone else. Am I right?
Meat without moonsugar is like chewing without teeth. Bah. Sugar-Dance would trade your left arm for some sugar-cane fritters right now!
This one hopes you have traveled far and wide. Knowing your way through a blizzard will help you in the Arena—or so I have heard.
Why do the furless ones wear so much armor? Do they enjoy getting hit? All those pots and pans just slow them down. That must be why they get hit so much.
Look at some of this so-called "competition." The Diamond's Daughters shall have no problem becoming champions of the Arena.
What? Haven't you ever heard of Dorzogg's Dozen?
This one greets you. Welcome to the camp of the Five Claws.\n\nBut this one can't help but wonder, why are you here?
The air's so fresh and clean up here, it makes me want to sing!
We've got all kinds of goods for sale! Only … slightly used.
Hello there! Braving the Craglorn wilds? How exciting!
You want to buy the spoils of war, yes? Speak to Severa—she has what you need.
I'm not cut out for army life. Too many rules, too much marching. And yelling. I hate yelling.
On the run? Pull up a stump. I could use some decent conversation.
I left the army behind me and I have no regrets. No regrets at all!
Grim times make good business. You should examine our wares. Talk to Severa. She'll offer you a spectacular deal.
Bring trouble to our camp and I'll bring pain to you and your descendents.
The field is ours! Run for your lives, you miserable gray-skinned dogs!
Many thanks, wayfarer. May the stars bless your path.
With the aid of these gifts, I believe we will save Craglorn.
Those Anka-Ra are so … sumptuous, don't you think?
Thinking of trying my luck up at Dragonstar Arena. That's the big time, is what they say.
Ask me no questions and I'll tell you no lies. I have no quarrel with you at the moment, so you have nothing to fear from me.\n\nYet.
Let the games begin!
Mercy only applies to the victors! Fight for your miserable lives!
Smell the desperation? That's your clue that another Pardoner's Brawl is about to start!
Victory! Three cheers for the survivors! They get to live another day!
Let the games begin!
Mercy only applies to the victors! Fight for your miserable lives!
Have you lost your appetite? Because I'm famished!
You know the role of prey well: struggle, resignation, and death.
There is no escape.
Don't fight it. You never stood a chance.
Sorry, this affair is invitation only.

I once ripped a daedroth's jaw straight from it's face with my bare hands. Then I pummeled it to death with it.\n\nThe other daedroth fled when they saw that. They didn't want any part of what Sorasi Mavrand had in store for them.
The stones are ours to command!
We have some presents for the Lady!
Think you can tangle with the Silken Ring? Hah!
Interlopers! We invite you to die!
Mephala! I offer these to you!
Pacrooti tries to keep things simple. What he will never understand is why others insist on making them so complicated. Also women. Pacrooti will never understand women.
Your rewards are ready!
Bright moons, a bonus reward!
Greetings, my good friend!
Ah, my friend returns! This one thinks there is nothing better than a good friend, unless it is a good friend bearing moonsugar treats.
Pacrooti thanks you, and hopes to see you soon!
Another go-around, my friend?
A fine selection.
Good choice!
An exquisite selection.
Bright moons! Excellent!
Magnificent!
An unparalleled reward!
Rise, you little fools! Rise and burn!
Interlopers! Trespassers! Your lives are forfeit!
Are you feeling well? No peculiar dreams, odd sensations, or peculiar emotions?\n\nGood, then we could use your aid with another lost relic.
<Eviler Laugh>
Who wrote this logistics report? It's covered in … is that dried honey?
Looking to join up? Well, you appear to be Fighters Guild material! Go see the Hall Steward and she'll fill you in on the particulars.

Well, yes. I did grow up here in Vvardenfell. But I spent many years abroad, exploring the world and helping establish Fighters Guildhalls from High Rock to Elsweyr.\n\nIf you're looking to join up, you've come to the right place.
Ah, how I've missed this land! My duties within the Mages Guild send me far and wide, so I cherish the time I get to spend in Vvardenfell.

How the Dark Elves can behave like they haven't a care in the world is beyond my comprehension. There's a damn volcano about to explode out there, not to mention a giant chunk of rock floating above our heads! How is any of that natural?

Don't you just love Vvardenfell? You must agree that there's nowhere else in the world quite like it. I'm just glad the guildmaster decided to send me here. The experience has been exhilarating, to say the least!
Don't take this the wrong way, but your armor has seen better days.\n\nIf you're in the market for something new and built to last, I'm sure we can come to terms on a fair price.

This one brings satchels and backpacks from the far corners of Tamriel, and each and every one is perfect for your carrying needs. Let's do without the usual haggling and get right down to the exchanging of gold and product, yes?
I could give you a song and dance, but when all is said and done, this is a bank. Either you have need of our services or you don't. Simple as that.
So many strangers of late. I suppose Lord Vivec's light draws the curious much the same as a flame attracts moths.\n\nWould you care to use our services?
If the volcano gets any worse, I'm packing up my anvil and heading for Eastmarch!
How do I remain sane in this land of nightmare creatures? That's easy. I drink! I recommend a particularly strong brew if you're new to the region.
My workshop is your workshop—just don't break anything and make sure you put everything back when you're finished.
I cook with love. Come to think of it, I do everything with love. Say, what are you doing later, hmm?
Making your own clothing, there's nothing quite like it! The feeling of accomplishment. The attention to detail. The quality.\n\nUnless you're all thumbs. Then I suggest you find a good tailor.

You'll have to excuse me. I'm still getting used to the fare they eat here in Vvardenfell. If there's something you want and I don't have it, that's probably because I thought it was nix-ox feed and sold it to a farmer.
You're a ray of sunshine on a gray and dismal day! Come on in and make yourself at home!
Hold on there! I need to make sure you're not a looter or a thief before I grant you the full hospitality of my store.
People come by to look. They always want to look. But do any of them open their gold pouches and offer to make a purchase? Fewer than I'd prefer, I'll tell you that!
I am a free egg-sister from Black Marsh, here to make a business and prosper.\n\nNo one told me that business was going to be so difficult, though.
You look like you know your way around a riding beast! Try one of my fine mounts on for size and see if you don't agree—you won't find better anywhere in Morrowind!
Why don't you get out of those uncomfortable old things and try this on for size. I know it's going to look just fabulous on you!

Time passes slowly beneath the hollow moon that floats above us. Or maybe it's just the depressing holiness of this place that gets me down.\n\nWon't you please make a purchase and brighten my gloomy day?
Worried about the locals? I honestly can't tell you of a safer spot. There's somewhat of an unspoken code down here.
House Hlaalu? Wonderful folk and fair and honest merchants to the last! House Redoran? Brave and noble, not a bad apple in their basket!\n\nNo profit in talking ill of my clientele. No profit at all.
The Redorans are skeevers, every one of them! And I'll fight anyone who tries to tell me different!
How may I be of assistance?

That volcano scares me more than a mountain bear that's guzzled a gallon of bottled buzz!\n\nStill, I'd rather be here than under that floating rock looming over Vivec City. That's just a disaster waiting to happen.
The silt strider suffers from moss blight, but the speckled nix-ox makes a fine substitute.\n\nIf you don't know what I'm talking about, forget I said anything.
I've got the best goods that the Green can provide! Don't collect them myself, of course, but I can guarantee my ingredients are fresh.
There's a lot of rumors circulating lately. Corrupt public officials, immortal vigilantes, wrongful imprisonments! Never been a better time to come to Suran!
So, you ready to make a deal or what?
Greetings. How can this humble servant of the Telvanni assist you?
Hungry? I season all the food personally. And I do mean personally.
Thirsty? I've got just the thing! And don't worry, it's not a Telvanni brew. You won't wake up with an extra nose come the morning.
The trick to being slave? Be bad at everything! Eventually the master will give you a job that isn't too complicated or taxing.
The mine may be shut down, but I'll be damned if I'm going to let this inn go under. How can I earn your business?
A word of advice. If you ever decide to open a mystic shop, do it in a town that isn't exclusively the domain of grubby-handed miners.
When times get tough, I believe in the power of drink. That's why I keep plenty of bottles and casks on hand.
If the mountain starts to rumble, that just means old Lorkhan ate an under roasted piece of boar. Little shake works the kinks out of the lower intestine, or so I heard.

The poor pilgrims! Set upon by terrible monsters that came out of nowhere and now roam the wilderness outside town.\n\nWe're doing our part to help. We're serving daily specials until the crisis has been averted.
The miners haven't been able to work for days, and no work means no pay. And do you know what that means? No customers!\n\nWell, except for you. Welcome, welcome.

Don't worry about the mountain. It does that from time to time. True, the rumbles have been a little more frequent of late, but I'm certain there's nothing to worry about.\n\nStill, might be wise to avoid standing underneath anything heavy for a bit.
Business was better when Mistress Dratha held sway, but enough politics, eh? What can I get you?
Now that's the face of someone come to collect their reward. Or you just ate a sweetroll.\n\nSo which is it? I'm bad with faces.
You don't look the type to wrestle a snow bear into submission. Maybe a snow bear's cub.\n\nWell, I have a cub-sized problem. Just for you.
Today's selections got a little charred and I forgot to add spices. Plus, I grabbed my scale lotion instead of the butter, so you probably don't want to eat here today.

If you're traveling north and west, watch out for Ashlanders. House Redoran says they're savages!\n\nNorth and east? That's House Telvanni territory. They're crazy old wizards, the lot of them, and slavers to boot! Either way you go, watch yourself.
Welcome home, comrade! Once you sign on with the Fighters Guild, you have a safe haven wherever our banner flies.\n\nNow, tell me about your adventures—and don't leave out any of the good parts!
Our stock is modest, but of the highest quality. You may look it over if you wish.

Always glad to see a fellow adept returning to our halls! I trust your search for knowledge goes well? I envy those members of the Mages Guild that aren't bound to a guildhall and charged with the mundane tasks that keep our fellowship on track.
The Order sees much, but not all. Were you successful?
Another contract came in. I'd like you to handle it.
A free-scale? My, my, my. Let me break out the finery! See anything to your liking, egg-kin?
Sadrith Mora is not safe for our kind, free-scale. Buy what you will, but leave Telvanni lands as soon as you can.

Something was going on in Vivec Palace, but those Dark Elves refuse to tell me anything. The priests and Ordinators keep their lips shut tighter than a House Hlaalu bank vault!\n\nAh, don't mind me. I just feel like I missed out on something important.
You are the type who seeks instant gratification, yes?

Red Mountain seems to have gone back to sleep, thank Kyne! I'll even thank that little Elf, Vivec, as long as it means I don't have to wade through a river of lava to get to my forge.\n\nSpeaking of which, is there something I can help you with?
Welcome to my humble shop, sera. Just let me know if you'd like to make a purchase.
Savarak's gone, Mistress Dratha has returned, and business is booming! Fine day for a sale, yes?
No one steals from the Followers of Nycot!
I can't believe they stole our holy relic!
Lies! This theft stinks of the Tribunal! Pretending to be Ashlanders! Bah!
When we catch those thieves, we ought to toss them into Red Mountain.
Has anyone recovered the staff yet?
Why would our Daedric Prince allow this to happen?
I want to know who fell asleep and let those filthy Ashlanders in here!
Red Mountain awakens. Do you think we had anything to do with that?
Eyes to the shadows, brothers and sisters. Thieves lurk nearby.
Did you hear that? Have the Ashlanders returned?
Ashlanders! The Tribunal should have wiped them out ages ago!
I've killed Hearth-wives with more spine. Take the pledge and prove otherwise.
Always speak your mind. Undaunted should die without regrets. Remember that when you see me tomorrow.
Have your experiences with the dark magics of the Daedra warped your perception of time? Do you not want your reward?
Did I scare you off, or did you leave your reward to win my affection?
Truly? This is to be my lot in life?
How dare you! I just bought this doublet.
Do you greet all dignitaries this way?
You're one of those people that collects trinkets but has no home to display them? This one doesn't judge.
I see you don't have a home of your own yet. Feel free to browse, but you really should find a place to live.
It's all about personal space. A home of your own gives you room to breathe.
I can sense by your morphotype that you haven't made living arrangements as of yet. What are you waiting for, an invitation?
Everybody needs a home of their own. Really. Get to work on that, friend.
No home? I suppose we can deal with that. I don't know what you'll do with it, but I'll happily sell it to you anyway.
It must be terrible not to have a place to call your own. If nothing else, you can still buy one of these baubles. Think of it as incentive.
Homeless in Hammerfell? There's no reason for that. Plenty of places available, if you're not too picky about where you want to live.
No house to call your own? Where do you drink your golden pear ale?
No home? Not even a wretched room in a disreputable inn? I feel sorry for you. Still, I'm sure we can do business if you want.
This one has what your home needs. Take a look!
From High Rock to Hammerfell, you won't find a better collection of home accoutrements than mine.
You look like someone in dire need of a special item for your home.
All sorts of things wash up on Oblivion's varied shores. Have a look and see if anything grabs you.\n\nReally, it might grab you.
Idle gold doesn't do anyone any good. Reinvest it, I say! And my furnishings make for wonderful investments, as you can plainly see.
A little reputation is better than no reputation at all. Besides, it means we can make a deal!
After we finish our business, you need to tell me how you actually accomplished that amazing feat that everybody's talking about!
Ah, champion, you're just in time! I found something that will look simply fabulous in your home!
I can only deal with clients possessing either fame or notoriety. Guild rules and all that. I suppose you qualify, though.
Which crate do you choose?
One crate there. Select it, my friend.
Sadly, you have no more crates. But you can always purchase more!
Begone foul one! We are doing business!
Fame spreads like weeds in a garden. But fame is like the good weeds. Not the strangling, kill all the plants weeds. Um, can I show you my wares?
The rich and the famous intimidate me, so you must realize how flustered someone of your status makes me feel.

A reputation can be tough to live up to. That's why you need one of my fabulous conversation pieces for your home. If nothing else, it'll take your mind off the fact that everybody is trying to kill you.
If your fame grows any larger, your head won't fit through the door of your house! I might have something to remedy that ….
The rich and the famous love my furnishings. Since you count yourself as one of their number, I'm certain you'll find something you just have to own among my wares.
Names are like noses. Everybody has one. What you want is a reputation. I love to help turn a house into a home when a good reputation is involved.
You have the air of a very important person. Someone I can really snuggle up to. Let me show you my special stock.
When you reach the pinnacle of fame and fortune, commonplace items just won't do. Have no fear. My furnishings are far from commonplace.
When you begin to make a name for yourself, well, that's when I enter the picture. It's still a small name, but I'm willing to sell if you want to buy.
You preformed that astounding feat at that place over there. That was you, wasn't it? I knew it! I have something I just know you can't live without!
And so the champion returns to gaze upon my humble offerings. I'm sure my one-of-a-kind items deserve a place in your home.
Perish in flames!
Pacrooti is jealous of your good fortune!
Very nice! You're not cheating are you?
Pacrooti will help you open a crate which contains special rewards. Some of these are so spectacular, just thinking of them makes Pacrooti's fur stand on end!
Pacrooti sees that you are ready to play! Excellent!
These gems can be traded for special rewards in the store!
This one is please to inform you that you are his number one player today! You have beaten all others!
No one has ever had a better run of luck then you, my sleek friend! This will be hard to top!
You look ready to impress.
Got something for me?
Maybe this time the client will be satisfied.
Potion and poison, it all looks the same to me. Here's your fee.
Not half bad. Respectable gleam. Nice, strong style. The client will be pleased.
Clean lines, well-tailored. You certainly know how to thread a needle. Your fee.
Remind me, is this for jewelry, or armor, or what? Whichever. The client will like it.
I'll never understand the attraction of elaborate feasts. Too ostentatious. Here's your fee.
The polish really brings out the grain of the wood. I'll get it to the client.
Ow! What are you doing out there?
State your destination. I'll add you to the list.
I can fit you. We even have a spare hammock!
We still have room, if you expect to travel.
Hmm. That didn't do anything good.
The New Life is about what the old year was and what the new year can be.
You're a natural! Although, I suppose my mentoring has honed your talent.
I've almost got this place back in order. Poor Gray-Skies keeps finding glass with his feet though.
I came to Vivec City with dreams of an elegant little shop, right in the heart of the city. Instead I'm stuck in the mud with the rest of the squabble.\n\nWell, what do you need?

If you must be told the basics, then you're simply not ready to purchase from my shop. Look elsewhere for someone to hold your hand. A mistake in alchemy is the difference between life and death.\n\nWill you be needing anything today?
Disputes between houses are trivial when one thinks of the horrors of Molag Bal. Will you join the fight against him?
Tell me, do you really think you have what it takes to distinguish yourself in the Mages Guild?
So, you've come to weave enchantments? I've got everything you need—and I do mean everything.
Have you come seeking a cure for those prodigious troll-hands of yours? Afraid I'm fresh out of shrinking salve. Can I get you something else?
Pacrooti has never seen such a magnificent display of good fortune!
Seryn, the outlander's lies have no place in this debate.
Ooh gems! Congratulations!
Aherm.
Ahhh! Hmmm!
Ha ha!
<humming 2>
Hmm hmmm!
