Word of your deeds grows, and so too does my selection. You would do well to browse my wares.
I've been saving a few items for a worthy customer, and rumor has it that there's no one more worthy than you. Want to take a look?
You must be persnickety if you haven't found a house yet. I guess beggars can be choosers, hmm?
You're taking a risk coming down here, you know. If those surfacers know you're talking to an aprax, they might toss you out too.
Everything about this place is great—except for the food. What I wouldn't give for a mammoth steak right now ….
Mother is a wise and just leader. Just do not make her mad.

Damn these High Elves and their stupid customs! Ugh! And people say we Dark Elves are strict! At least we never boot anyone out of civilized society just because they punched a bailiff. I mean, I wasn't even sober at the time! How fair is that?
You're new, eh? Well if I find anything missing, I'll know who to blame.
Please, feel free to peruse our libraries. This is, of course, only a fraction of our collection. The really dangerous tomes are well out of reach, I assure you.
You should take some time to explore the tower, cerum. The architecture may be imposing, but I promise you, it will feel like home before long.
Halimorion murdered in broad daylight …. This never would have happened if the Queen—! Forgive me. I'll not lecture you on politics.
You must be at full strength to vanquish those shadows!
Rumor has it that you're the captain of a fine vessel. I'll tell you, there's not a sailor on this dock that doesn't envy you. Including me.
Here's a bit of advice I give to all the captains around here. The fewer who know about your ship, the better. Trust me, you don't want to get caught in these Altmer regulations.
Ahoy, captain! This one has heard wondrous tales of your ship. Perhaps one day you'll invite Zandal on board.
Oh, you're the new captain, right? That ship of yours is something else. You should be damn proud.
I've heard many rumors about your ship. Seems to be quite the impressive vessel.
I assure you, my wares are all aboveboard. Why, if not for the location of my shop, I'd be downright respectable.
Count yourselves lucky! Your deaths will be quick.
Your corpses shall be a fine tribute for Vykosa!
Have no worries. I shall use your corpses wisely.
No longer shall you invade Vykosa's keep!
It's time for the hunt to truly begin!
Feel a werebear's strength!
Feel winter's wrath!
Burn beneath the flames!
Lightning's might! Storm's fury!
Another companion lost.
My claws alone are enough to defeat you!
To me, you curs! We mustn't fail Vykosa!
Feast upon that one first, my pack!
My claws shall run red with your blood!
Let us strike against these fools!
In this prison, I'm both judge and executioner!
Release the prisoners! I'm sure they're hungry.
If magic won't do, how about fang and claw?
Lightning's might flows through me!
You're more resilient than Vykosa thought. Well, no matter.
You'll be crushed by magic's power!
You cannot fathom Vykosa's power!
I'll show you true magic!
Let's see … which one, which one?
The time has come to reveal my true might!
Don't become trapped in those roots!
Those thorns will pierce right through you!
Dark moons, it's summoning spriggans! Quickly, defeat them!
You must defeat the remaining spriggans!
What this pack needs is a good hunt!
<Low growling.>
When's the next hunt? Soon? Oh, I hope it's soon.
<Aggresive snarling.>
Dinnertime already? Lucky us!
<Low growling.>
You're nothing against the Moon Hunter Pack!
<Aggresive snarling.>
I'm ready to fire!
Crouch within the fog until the indrik is discovered!
Looks like our wisp needs some encouragement.
There it is! Don't let it get away!
An Argonian's love is like warm mud. Soothing, sinking … and very hard to escape.
My wares are ever changing, like the direction of the wind. What has my guild asked me to sell today? Feel free to look.
This stall needs more colors, I've told my guild a hundred times! Maybe some bright yellow. I mean, who doesn't like yellow?
Don't like the prices? Don't waste my time. Unless you're eager for a fist in your face.
I try to keep my stall neat and tidy, I really do. But how much can one do when working in the middle of a swamp?
Murkmire is a far cry from the last location my guild sent me. The Rift may have its own cold beauty, but I prefer warmer climates.
Thank you for trusting us with your valuables, beeko. We will tend to your treasures like eggs in flood-time.
Looking for a trustworthy banker? Look no further. How can I assist you today?
Not all the blossoms within the swamp have a sweet scent, traveler. Some carry a noxious gas within them. It's best to keep your distance, should you encounter one.
I've heard that Murkmire mages have the ability to change the time of day, the weather, even the seasons. Of course, I've yet to see such feats.
My packs are all created with special fibers, guaranteed to repel both mud and mold alike. Why don't you have a look for yourself?
The deep marsh provides oozeworthy gifts to those with the eyes to find them. Your eyes seem bright as polished shells, beeko.
Ah, feel that warm breeze. Some hate the warm swamp air, but me? Can't get enough of it.
I used to sell weapons to the Morag Tong. In fact, that's why I'm in this Tribunal-forsaken mud heap. Though I'd rather not get into the details.
Do not forget to gargle your drink, beeko. There is no substitute for good manners.
Most of the lumber around here is soggy and full of grubs. The wood that isn't, though? Believe me—you won't find any stronger.
Moving here to Murkmire was the best decision I ever made. If I'd stayed in Orsinium, I never would have found out how much I love grilled toad livers!
How can I meet your needs?
You picked a fine place for enchanting, friend. Massive wamasu, giant insects, poisonous plants, murderous locals … kind of reminds me of home!
Fate's current carries you down a bloody river, beeko. Let me help you prepare.
I used to sell more local cuisine, until the dryskins started to kick up a fuss. They run from strangeness as the mouse runs from the serpent.
I have a small selection of furniture available for you to look at. Want a larger selection? Accomplish more great deeds!
Many ojel ask to see our Hist. At this, I must laugh. We of Lilmoth have traveled from many tribes and hail from many Hists. It is as obvious as the scales on our faces!
They say the Dead-Water tribe use the hides of their fallen to craft leathers. Have you ever heard of such a morbid practice?
The magic of Murkmire is unlike any other in Tamriel. Once, I thought it dreadfully dull. Only now do I see the true beauty in its mysterious ways.
Scissors slide through cloth, the waters part, a silver trout divides a river of blue.
Saxhleel do not fold metal. Our tools speak the wood, stone, and leather tongue. Even so, I have goods that may aid you. Come and see.
I've got to tell you, this humidity is just horrible for my wares. I had to throw out a whole crate of bows due to damp rot. I don't know how the Argonians here avoid it.
Watch out!
Stay low and you'll keep out of the indrik's sight!
I'll strike you down!
I'll burn you to a crisp!
Feel my claws!
My might will crush you!
I'll choke you all out!
You'll fall beneath my feet!
Even lightning obeys me now!
I'll hunt you down within the darkness!
Hold for another moment! I'm going to set a trap!
My trap is ready! Lead your foe to it!
Time to rip out those hearts!
The spirit of the owl lives on.
The spirit of the stag lives on.
The spirit of the bear lives on.
It looks like the spriggan saplings have awakened!
The spriggan's gaining power from all four seasons! Guard yourself!
Hopefully our next prey will put up more of a fight.
And I thought this would be a hunt worth bragging about. How disappointing.
It's always disappointing when the prey barely fights back.
Make sure to put up a fight. I wouldn't want to bore our Lord Hircine.
You're here for the Great Hunt? Well, Lord Hircine's standards have certainly lowered.
This is turning out to be quite the eventful hunt!
Arrows at the ready! Shields up!
We've got company! Weapons at the ready!
New prey to hunt? Excellent!
Just one death is all it takes! Then you can join us forever!
The hunt is upon us, walkers!
Be quick, walkers! Our prey arrives!
Oh, I just love a good hunt!
You leaf-eaters are going to spook off my prey!
Remember Balorgh's orders! We can't let them pass!
How dare you strike against the Moon Hunter Pack?
I'll feast on your flesh!
For the glory of Moon Hunter!
Are you here to hunt me too? When will it ever stop!
Quickly! Stand within my light!
Quickly, you must get within Z'Maja's gate!
The gateway grows in strength. We must seal it off quickly.
Z'Maja's shadow will soon cross to our world! Destroy that gateway!
Strike them down! Leave none alive!
How dare you strike against the Moon Hunter Pack?
How dare you use such petty tricks!
Gather, my servants! Crush all who oppose me!
<Mocking Goblin gibberish.>
<Insulted Goblin gibberish.>
<Mocking Goblin gibberish.>
<Gloating Goblin gibberish.>
Carry out her will and life is your reward.
Keep her treasures safe.
Obey or die!
You disturb her order!
We had to keep it from them, no matter how much they needed it.
You will be cleansed, do not resist.
You cannot fathom Meridia's power.
Her will is eternal and her reach endless. Submit.
You have paid the price they paid.
You could never compare to the purity of her creations.
Her will is law.
All must kneel before the Lady of Infinite Energies.
<Defiant Goblin gibberish.>
I've always wanted to visit Black Marsh … no time like the present, I guess.
Kyne's wisdom is mine! Light rain shall fall upon your expedition.
<Condemning Goblin gibberish.>
<Howling battlecry.>
We're busy-busy! If you could pitch in, it would be very appreciated.
<Angry Goblin gibberish.>
As always, a pleasure to work with you, my friend.
Something else? Or do you need a reminder?
We are like a nest of giant bog ants. Coming and going and coming again. Have you brought something to our hill today?
I need to maintain my concentration!
<Challenging Goblin gibberish>
My sister Famia needs more supplies for Cyrodilic Collections' operations in Murkmire. If you could spare the time, talk to Jee-Lar. He's coordinating the efforts to equip our next expedition.
It's restored its shock conveyors!
What's the point of doing great deeds if no one ever knows you did them? My furniture can help with that.
Always an honor to serve someone of such great renown. Looking to purchase some furniture today? My wares are sure to impress!
Not sure why someone without a house would be looking into furniture, but hey, who am I to judge?
My furniture is practical for any home, whether you live in a mud hut or three story mansion.
No home to speak of? Then why would you—oh, never mind. If you're willing to spend gold, I don't particularly care.
I muck this entire stable by hand every day, and check over my steeds every evening. Taking pride in your work, that's what's important.
The swamps of Murkmire are filled with danger, yes, but not so much with Daedra. At least, not that we have seen so far.
Ah, what a coincidence! I was just speaking to Hitari about the great need the Fighters Guild has for strapping adventurers, just like yourself.
<Frustrated Goblin gibberish>

There is conclusive evidence that Argonian magic is fundamentally different than the practices of mer and man. The Mages Guild wishes to study those differences, and see what can be learned from them.
Exciting place, right? If you need an excuse to get out of this pit, the outfit I work for is looking for bodies. In more ways than one.\n\nInterested in a job?
Bah, leg's aching again. \n\nIf you're looking to keep busy, I've got something for an able body.
They send you into the great serpent's mouth once more. Do you tempt it to bite, or wish to jump eagerly into its belly, I wonder?
If this collection you are building instills a rightful dread in the worshipers of the Eight, then you do the work of Sithis.
We're done here. I'll flag you down if something else comes up.
Behold! The might of the Blackguards!
And now it's time to face one of the Blackguards' finest!
Victory for the challengers!
Oh! Having trouble there? Hmm?
Our challengers return for another fight!
At last, challengers who fight back!
At last, challengers worthy of the Blackguards!
Can the challengers defeat Battlemage Ennodius? Let's find out!
Let's see how the challengers fare against our beasts!
Our challengers triumphed over flame and beast! But how will they fare against the undead?
The challengers have triumphed against our champions. But can they face them all at once?
It's finally time for our challengers to go against me, Drakeeh the Unchained!
When the river runs dry, it's best to look elsewhere for water. Come back later.
You still here? The task will not complete itself, ojel.
More bloodshed! Bash their skulls in!
Strike them down!
Do you want to get yourselves killed? Idiots!
A sitting stone would offer more of a challenge.
Do the challengers expect to win like this?
Is that all these kuudas can muster?
These challengers of yours are so fascinating to watch, Drakeeh.
It seems these challengers are actually able to hold their own. How exciting.
Oh, my. Did that hurt?
The wind carries you back. Now speak true and say how you fared.
Do you like treasure? Come explore the swamp with Cyrodilic Collections!
I declare truth. While the Naga-Kur is the strongest tribe in all Murkmire, we still request aid every now and then.
I am the master here!
Never in a thousand lifetimes did I imagine I would willingly seek out a Veeskhleel's den.
So you have returned to us, Rootmender. How did you fare in your task?
Your aid is most appreciated, Rootmender.
The Root-Whisper Village is young and tender, like the sapling that sways in the wind. Will you help us grow strong?
In Elsweyr, I was a philosopher. In Murkmire, I am a fisher. These professions are not too different though, no? Still I stand for long hours with nothing but my thoughts.
Perhaps I'm being silly, but I … I have this feeling of dread. Like something is about to happen to me.
I once worked with Cyrodilic Collections. Emphasis on once. Between their carping owner and that kuuda dryskin, I ended up quitting before my first day was done.
Our tribe may now be small, but with your aid it shall grow strong.

My favorite month of the year is Saxhleel. It is when tribe members are encouraged to focus on creative pursuits, whether it be pottery, weaving, or woodcarving. By the end of the month, many beautiful things have been created.
The warriors of Mukmire fight with all that is available. The Dead-Water tribe even uses the bones of their fallen.
I'm the lookout, see! Got to make sure none of them scaly guards get in.
Please, Honei! Can you hear me?
Though the guards of Lilmoth are hired by the various merchants in town, I've still found them to be extremely vigilant in their duties.
When I was a young spear-thrower, this square was filled with warriors. Now, the stream runs dry.

I provide a culinary recommendation. Pukta snake. Covered in honey and then roasted in a fire pit. Delicious!\n\nSome outsiders have mentioned a new sweet condiment I simply must try. I believe they called it moon-cougar. Or something like that.
I provide a friendly warning. Everything here belongs to someone else. If you try to steal it, I shall be forced to raise the alarm.\n\nOtherwise, have a good day.
Whatever you seek, this is not the place to find it, outsider.
If you have any questions or concerns, please direct them to the Jekka-Wass. If you can get him to look up from his book, that is.

The fish avoid my hook today. Perhaps they aren't hungry. Or maybe these fish are smarter than their brothers.\n\nI suppose it could have something to do with that big shadow I saw moving beneath the surface. Best not get too close to the edge.

What a wonderful celebration! It isn't often that an outsider gets to participate in an event such as this.\n\nIf Stibbons continues to refuse to come out of his shell, he's going to miss all of the excitement.
In this particular form, my manservant makes an excellent conversation piece, don't you agree?
I did not even know a Hist could slumber! And you are the one who awakened it? No wonder you are called Rootmender.
We will never forget the sacrifice that Jaxsik-Orrn made so that our new village can prosper. Always will she be remembered, and always will she be honored.
The fishing here is very plentiful, due to the village's previous isolation. Hopefully today I will be able to fill many of the tribe's empty bellies.
That was your last mistake!
A Hist has not awoken from such a slumber since … well, I am not sure. I have never heard of such a thing happening.
Hear the screams of the undead!
The agony of these spirits only gives me strength!

All is created, then changed, then ultimately destroyed. That is why we must allow all things to pass. Why grasp onto that which one day will be no more? \n\nWealth, youth, life. Know they will pass, as all things must pass. And let them go.
Don't let them get away!
Far be it for me to question Argonian culture, but … this is just a bunch of frogs croaking, isn't it?
Your belly is too soft! "Her head cracked like an egg, blood and brains staining her foe's mace." How can you change such words?
It's simply a cultural difference. Such imagery must be presented in a particular way.
Yes?
Surprise, you kuuda!
Now's the time to strike!
I was told that this was the tour of the wondrous mysteries of Murkmire. Not a trek through some desolate swamp!
What, did my lady not realize that Murkmire was a swamp? What else could you possibly expect?
Yes! I got it working!
Set the trap and let's go!
What's taking so long?
No, no. We only cover the ball with mud when points are scored too quickly.
Looking for some easy targets? Head over to Bright-Throat Village. Those limp-fins never see it coming.
I've learned quite a few tips between sales. Thieves are actually more willing to give up their secrets than you may think.
I shall clean your goods, like the stream cleans a bloody knife.
You have come for my services, yes? Quickly, pull it out. I haven't got all day.\n\nAh. I refer to the items which you have stolen, of course.
I've had to turn quite a few coin purses away due to bugs. I may deal in dirty gold, but there is a point I must draw the line.

To one day teach the lessons of Sithis, my apprentice must first learn them. Fear is but one aspect. Change is another. Void, darkness, death.\n\nA nisswo must know all if they wish to one day speak the words of nothing.
You've done more than enough here today. Leave us.

I've felt a connection to Sithis ever since my egg-mother died. That … might sound odd, I know, but there was a comfort in its darkness and carelessness.\n\nI once thought my mother's death cruel. Now I understand it to be but a part of the cycle.
I would love to talk, but I'm a tad busy pondering my own mortality.

I love this time of season. The whole village is teaming with visitors of all kinds. Like you …! And my new Nord friend. Though she is not here now. She gets lost very easily, but I will be glad to look after her!
With so much commotion in the village recently, it's a wonder any work has been done at all.
We must hold them off until the ritual is complete!
This is the best spot in the village to see the torchbugs at night. I made certain to claim it in case anyone wanted to come watch with me!
You will never defeat us!
I can't fend this one off!
Help me!
My defense is cut through!
I do not know where ojel get this idea that Saxhleel take no care for their things. Just because all things crumble does not mean they should be left to rot.
Do not allow them to complete the ritual!
Now, taste the fury of the skies!
Press on, we must be victorious!
With all the excitement lately, everyone could afford to spend a quiet moment fishing. \n\nThere's nothing quite so peaceful as casting a line. It is like an anchor for tranquility.

The Bright-Throats are quite welcoming aren't they? I got separated from my group stranded here. Not two minutes into my predicament and an Argonian named Vetra-Jat invites me to stay in her home!\n\nShe's so inviting, I might not leave!
Ha! Now we've got you!
It's time to attack!
Fancy a look at my extremely, profoundly exotic goods?
Do you hear that distant, sonorous howl? Comforting, isn't it?
So many treats this time of year! I favor all but the swamp fish.
Undaunted, aren't you? I don't accept keys.
I bow my head in gratitude.
I flex my claws!
Begone! Begone I say!
My thanks. Know you are always welcome in Bright-Throat Village.
That was a close one. Thank you.
Help! Someone, please help!
Back! Get back, you beasts!
Thanks to you, I live. May your days be sun-blessed.
Because of you, I am saved. You have my gratitude.
I'll hold them off!
By bark and bite, please! Someone help!
Thank you for the aid. I believed my life forfeit.
What manner of fabricant sheds a feather? Who can say.
I once lived in Imperial City, did you know? Where or when, I shan't say.
This season: Wrothgarian tourism! See the sights, meet the people, and meat the wildlife.
Cyrodiil or Battlegrounds, which do you prefer? Actually, don't tell me.
This season: Love! Should we call fired dazzlers and stolen pigs 'love'.
Allow me to imitate a dear friend of mine: <remains silent.>
Smell the sugar on the air? The honey? The… bananas?
We must talk, you and I.
I say we keep the loot and tell the rest of the gang we lost it.
I don't know … the Dead-Water aren't exactly pushovers ….
I had the relic in my hand! I had it!
I got the daril you wanted. You got the gold?
I'm not sure our gang name means what we think it does.
That xanmeer belongs to the Blackguards!
Dead-Water? Their warriors make my scales go dry!
The mud dries on my scales while we sit around and do nothing!
Get out of my way, kuuda.
Don't look now but I think that dryskin likes the slime on your scales.
I almost feel sorry for the tribal Argonians. Almost.
Those merchants! It's like taking sweets from a baby!
I'm so hungry I could eat a tree root!
The creepy moss gathers all rocks.
You! Drink this so I can see what happens!
Easy there! That elixir is potent!
I could get used to living in a marsh. I just wish it wasn't quite so wet.
My contact in Lilmoth tells me the haul will be huge!
So many thieves and cut-throats. My kind of people!
I'm as tight as a bow string after that last raid.
Quiet, you, or I'll turn you into a tree slug.
The Naga consider themselves so strong, but they are like hatchlings before my power!
Sharing is one thing, but this is ridiculous!
The mud rises in a most pleasant manner.
I wanted to be a Blackguard since I was old enough to hold a sword!
So, what part of mud-filled swamp attracted you to the Blackguards?
I hope the next raid turns up some sweet slime cakes. I love sweet slime cakes!
We wouldn't lose so many relics if you let me lead the raid.
The teeba-enoo court is a popular destination for the neighboring tribes. Just don't ask me to explain the game. I wouldn't even know where to begin.
Alten Meerhleel, they call it. A fishing spot wasted, I say.

The gas blossom smells just as lovely as it looks. The longer you take in its poisonous scent, the more you are choked by it. \n\nAnd make no mistake, traveler. Those gasses are more than capable of killing you.
The bounties on my head may be numerous, but still. Is it worth it to live out the rest of my days in this disgusting swamp? Not to mention all the lizards swarming around.
I thought doing work for Jee-Lar would prepare me for adventuring in Murkmire. So far none of the insect-repelling candles have worked, and all that salted meat leaves my mouth drier than a desert!
This phlegmwine has just the right amount of skin forming on the top. And the sweetbile trembles ever so slightly in the stomach. Perfection!
I hear that up by Gideon, they have frogs that sing so high that only those with the most sensitive of fronds can hear them. They must draw very small crowds.
You will find no Bright-Throat feasts here, but there are lingering comforts for travelers.
Did you come out here looking for your past too? I think my great, great egg-kin used to live here. I don't know what I was expecting to find.
Don't mind me. I haven't got any attachments to this place. If you find anything of value. Just keep it.

I'm considering planting mushrooms here. The old wreck provides ample shade and the trickle of rain lasts many days longer under its leaky trunk.\n\nThere would be the risk of it all coming down on my head, but that is just the way of things.
Do nothing that might cause the foolish dryskin to fall. I must return him safely if I am to be paid and I have had to retrieve him from that sagging wreck three times already.
Tread carefully. The ship is reasonably stable, but of a fragile constitution, as I've discovered. It is a long drop.
Sa tchee shu u vakka.
Many pass through the Refuge lately. Trouble must brew.
I do tire of gathering fresh food to preserve and store, only to take my meals from rations on the brink of rot. This season will be a long one.
As the wind carries leaves away, so will my boat carry you. Do you wish to embark?
Hot sun above, cool mud below. And many wares for you to see, should your gold be plentiful.

Argonian magic never ceases to amaze me. It's far less structured than any other arcane energy I've encountered. Almost chaotic, truth be told. \n\nBut also very … beautiful. Like a song that flows through you.
Why are you still here, outsider? Haven't you done enough?
Our roots will span all of Murkmire when Ree-nakal's work is done.
I miss the shade of the Deepmire. I suffocate in this cave.
If you have any trading connections, please, send them my way. The more connections I can make, the busier my port will become.

While Kishi and Mewah-Jez prepare the hatchlings for the Path of the Lily, the rest of us must do our part as well. We must double our efforts to produce new eggs to fill the nesting creches.\n\nIt is our civic duty!
Most of the Naga-Kur despise outsiders, but I am much more accepting of foreign ways. And foreign gold.\n\nLook around, but try not to let anyone else see you.
Shadow take you!
Drag it over here, beeko!
I've cleared the air here!
Over here! I have an antidote!
Black Marsh has so many trinkets lying around, haven't you noticed? And the Argonians here don't seem to care about them one bit.\n\nAh, well. More souvenirs for the rest of us, I suppose.
I'm going to make sure you never do this again!
What do you think you're going to do? The eggs are hatched and the children are mine!
In Dead-Water, we were united. A single spear that thrust into the heart of our enemy. But in Root-Whisper, we are divided. A rain of arrows which will fall uselessly against our enemy's shield.
Ah! So nimble! Well, I'll soon fix that!
You dare much, ojel fool. Allow me to rectify the situation.
I will not fall to you!
We will never forget the sacrifice that Xukas made so that our new village can prosper. Always will he be remembered, and always will he be honored.
So much power!
I will kill you for interfering!
I was considering a chime, so the Hist may give me a sign of a customer's arrival. You think that's a good idea?
Today, Alten Meerhleel is but a small port. But tomorrow? Well, I am very excited about the possibilities.
I hope Root-Whisper thrives like spring mudblossoms because of your wise guidance. May I be of service to you?

The war in Cyrodiil is so far from the swamps of my homeland. Will such a battle help protect my tribe? Help my village prosper?\n\n Still, a large stone creates long ripples. This, I cannot help but ponder on.
Have you come to watch the torchbugs too? You are welcome to join me as long as you like!
My last raft was brisk as a leaf in the breeze. We flitted from place to place with grace and majesty … we crossed paths with a very thorny haj mota.\n\nI will miss it.
Ruheeva! I don't mean to seem dry to you. I can't—I can't erect my spines because of these Nord bee-ears.\n\nI wouldn't have thought to try bee-ears when they have so much honey.
This village seems busy as a beehive! I wonder why?\n\nOh, what am I doing, talking your ear off! You came here for a purchase, right?
Remember the fire stones!
It's activating a failsafe!
Aurorans! To me!
Here you will learn to obey!
There is no choking down this bile!
A cold heart does not numb this pain!
My tears cling to everything, and drown it in my sorrow.
Feel the weight of our loss!
The life of a nomad promises constant adventure and plentiful gold. But once you have reached this one's age? Such things cease to tempt you.
Potions, brews, and tonics, too! Mix it all up and see what happens! Well, why not? You'll never learn anything if you're too scared to try!
These Khajiiti blacksmiths, they have no respect for the craft. Makes me miss Cyrodiil something fierce. At least there, I worked among equals.
Hakoshae is said to be cold and unwelcoming, but this is untrue. The town's carpenters were happy to teach me once I showed them the proper respect.
No one in Rimmen is quite as fashionable as Sharazzur, yes? This is because he creates every piece of clothing he wears.
I just find the mages of Elsweyr to be so … charming. But should you desire to be a truly great enchanter? Nothing compares to High Elf practices.
Please, would you consider a purchase? So many refuse to buy because of fear of excess fur, and so Amajhan's wares begin to over ripen.
There are many guilds and many stalls. This one is nice, sure. But Nirshala thinks she could do better.
I may have some wares to offer, but not much. Most of my stock is meant for those of greater deeds.
Plenty of customers have made their way to Predator Mesa to prove themselves as great warriors. \n\nThe ones that don't buy the good stuff don't come back.
This one's brews are as sweet as Mara's bounteous bosom. Care to have a taste?
Many hungry mouths in Rimmen as of late. Saizeh just wishes she had the power to help feed them all.
Euraxia, Ayrenn, what does it matter? These foreign powers demand to rule us, and Mizarr's people seem content to let them do so.
Say what you will, but the Khajiit really know how to handle a finely made piece of leather. I've never had such appreciative customers before moving to Rimmen.
Fashion is ever evolving, you know. That's why I came all the way to Elsweyr. If you ask nicely enough, I may even offer a few tips.
You wish to fight against the Khajiit, no? Then you must best their natural abilities! My weapons will give you the precision and quickness needed to win.
Abazbi prefers to work with hardwood, rather than the softer varieties. For obvious reasons, of course.
It saddens this one to speak of Khajiiti wrongdoings, but he must admit that the city holds many thieves. That is why our trustworthy bank is all the more needed!
You can be assured that all of my bankers, Khajiit and Imperial, are fine workers and honorable souls. I'd accept nothing less.
I may not have much experience selling furniture, but Lathahim says he believes in me. And if there's one thing I don't want to do, it's let him down.
A good pack is like a good friend. Sturdy, dependable, and always by your side.
Senche-mounts have just as much of a sweet tooth as a Khajiit. Add a little moon-sugar to its meat, and you will have a contented steed.
Adi sells only the sleekest wares, guaranteed.
By Y'ffre, I could really go for a decent jagga brew right about now. My guild may pay well, but what's it worth if I can't even buy my favorite drink?
Ah, yes! What can you do for me? I mean! What can I do for you! Sorry, I keep messing that up.
Look at that beautiful sky! Retiring to Rimmen wasn't easy, but it was well worth it. I even got the opportunity to open up this little shop. Lucky me!
My guild has the finest selection of wares in all of Rimmen. Ask anyone around, and they will confirm it to be so.
Ready to fight some Dragons? I'm right there with you! But first, have a look at my wares. A reliable weapon can make the difference between a swift victory and fiery death.
Khajiiti soldiers are resourceful. They may know when to run from a fight, but make no mistake; the cats under my command are no cowards.
Our guild has the largest collection of documented Khajiiti history in all of Rimmen. Many come to peruse our collection.
Need to buy something? Quickly, then. My book isn't going to read itself.
Lucky am I to not be in Morrowind. The Dark Elves dislike all outsiders, even those of us in the Mages Guild.
The Wood Elves, they brag and boast about their Rite of Theft. Pah! The Khajiit have no need to hide behind such ceremony.
All the Khajiit do is brag. We Bosmer, we know how to truly perform the art of theft. And make no mistake! It is a performance.
For years this one honed her skills, mastering the craft of theft. And for what? Now she is old and slow, with only this shop to show for her efforts.
My face earned me the title of hulkynd back in Summerset. But here? Here I'm just another moneylender in a backwater hideout.
I pay my dues to the Jovial Lambasters, just like everyone else in this refuge. And if you're smart? You'll do the same.
The Khajiit here are in desperate need of supplies for their war effort. And Manasi? Why, he is more than happy to provide!
Those stuffy Elves in Summerset knew just how to rub my fur the wrong way! All sorts of taxes and rules and regulations. Such nonsense!
Ever been to Valenwood, friend? It's like Elsweyr, except better in every conceivable way.\n\nOf course, wherever you go, you'll need supplies. How can I help you?
Always good to meet a fellow adventurer! If you've got the coin, I've got plenty of goods to help you along.
This one has traveled all across her beautiful homeland, selling wares to travelers and natives alike! And never has she regretted such a life.
Not much for conversation, friend. You're here to buy furnishings, I'm here to make a sale. Let's keep it simple.
I used to be a gladiator. Now I'm a furniture salesman. Funny how things turn out, eh?\n\nIf you find something you like, just holler.
Fancy yourself a champion, hmm? Well then, you'll need the very best gear available, won't you?\n\nLucky you, that's all I carry.
Claws! Fangs! Blood! Glory! What Khajiit does not love these things?\n\nYou thirst for victory too, yes? You will need Bizdar's wares!
I knew if I bided my time, I'd have my revenge!
Is he going to turn you into one of those puppets, or just kill you? I can't wait to find out!
You always were a pushover.
If I wasn't preserving my power, we'd be done by now.
Through her, I am infinite.
She'll scour the impure from you. Like she did for us.
No siege weapons, no reason for fear! And so Amajhan's business begins to prosper.
We Khajiit, we understand the need for a sweet brew, yes? To serve you anything else, why, it would be a disservice!
Bright Moons, you return!\n\nDid you succeed in your task? Quietly, now.
Off you go, walker. Swiftly, now! Quick work brings quicker pay, yes?
Nisuzi has coin if you have the time. An honest day's work for an honest day's pay, yes?
Ah, the five-claw returns. Tell me, did you succeed?
Swift paws make for quicker coin, child. You've got a job to do, yes? Get to it!
You love gold, yes? Or perhaps you just seek glory. Old Ri'hirr can supply you with both.
We Khajiit know the true ways of battle, walker! My weapons will give you the precision and quickness needed to win.
You want furniture? Without a house? Well, I suppose the customer's always right.
I have some wares for sale, but not all. You must accomplish far greater things to see my entire collection.
A great hero such as you deserves only the best! And the best is only what I offer you.
You have no home, yet still you wish to see my wares? Very well.
Even our finest soldiers cower before a Dragon's might. We must prepare for the beasts, and quickly.
The blood-mixtures made from the swamp creatures make me want to spit fur.
Once the Devourer has consumed its power, he will harvest Dragons enough for us all.
Don't bleed them dry!
What to brew from you, I wonder?
You're a diversion. Be an entertaining one.
Only cowards fear power. Grundwulf understands this.
Rrah! It burns!
The deer make better prey.
Now, Grundwulf! Only your destiny remains!
Bah! It's not enough! I need more!
The blue will cover the world.
Maarselok has made us whole.
Maarselok offers you life.
Take Maarselok within your heart.
Get out of my way and I'll spare you.
Selene's cleansed the seed! Use it against the blight!
We don't have to be enemies, Selene. I am in need of a priestess.
I'm not sure you understand your role here. Granted, it's more fun this way.
You have no one left to hide behind!
I'll restore it!
Keep your pests off me, spider-witch. They're irritating.
Soon my domain will embrace the whole of the world.
You dare enter my domain? Fools.
Has futility set in? Do you finally accept your place in the world?
Prideful whelps. You will be an example to others.
Insolent trash.
Was that it? They seemed so confident too.
This is the price of sacrilege.
Slaying Dragons is no easy matter! You'll need the finest weapons to defeat them. Luckily, that is exactly what my shop has to offer.
Obey me, living flames.
What a trophy you'll be!
Soon I'll taste your heart's blood!
Deliver me her strength!
Blue. The color of calm, measured inevitability, and despair.
A little help!
Flame is the vengeful weapon of light.
Water knows how to obey, and blood is its cousin.
You will know the sun's fury.
Her power courses through me!
I shine in perfect glory!
<Melodic Goblin chant.>
<Melodic Goblin chant.>
What?
This is Jubani's turf! All trespassers lose an ear!
Greetings. Was your assignment successful?
Oh, dear.
Mizzik … is all right.
I'm done toying with you. Die!
I accept all kinds in the Banished Regrets, I truly do. But that Wood Elf bard keeps tracking mud on my clean floors.
What did you touch?
There is nowhere better to sleep off a night at the Gulp, Ahmanra assures you.
Browse all you want, but sticky fingers get broken in my shop.
I feel her within.
I am eternally hers.
I am pure. As she intended.
Lady of Light, keep us from darkness.
I am her weapon!
You do not belong here!
She demands obedience!
You will be one of us.
<Distraught Goblin gibberish.>
The bridge is red hot! Stay on the platform!
You're having no effect on the torso! Try the arms!
It's going haywire! Put it down quickly!

The Knahaten Flu hit Southern Elsweyr harder than just about anywhere else. Entire cities were burned down in an attempt to contain the disease.\n\nIt'll be centuries before the land is fully recovered.
The Khajiit here may be tough to trade with, but at least they're willing to negotiate. Last year the High Elves of Summerset wouldn't even let me on the island.
Alms, walker? Alms for a sick Khajiit?
The Rimmenites need a steady hand. Discipline. Take that away, and this city would be a shambles.
Hmm. You look vigorous. Assertive, yes? This one loves a walker who can tell her what to do! Just so long as they let Chirba decide how to do it.

I must say, Queen Euraxia has been nothing but a gracious host.\n\nHowever, it's a little difficult to see past her particular … disposition when it comes to leadership. Such as her siege weapons aimed into the city.
Not sure why everyone's so worried about these Dragons. If they can bleed, they can be beaten. Simple.
Ah, a hero! You've fought these Dragons, right? If I could just scrape your armor for salivary residue, or maybe just examine the claw marks …. It would only take a month or two! Promise!
To the dungheap with Euraxia and her dock-tailed collaborators!\n\nWhen the revolution comes, we will remember who stood with the Mane, and who did not. Count on it.

Fear is a moonless night, blinding us to the path ahead.\n\nAnd yet, there are still the stars. They light our skies and guide us forward, though they might not be as bright. And always, always there will be the sunrise. This, we cannot forget.

The Khajiit don't tend to discriminate against different furstocks, but we are practical.\n\nA little Alfiq is less likely to be hired as a laborer than, say, a nice big Pahmar. And you won't find many Senche-raht carpenters—no thumbs, you see?

Queen Ayrenn's heart bleeds for the Khajiit, but those considerations are subordinate to the interests of the Dominion.\n\nThe golden banner cannot turn southward yet. Once the conquest of Cyrodiil is complete, then we will deal with matters here.

Many scholars visit Rimmen, but few speak to Ra'ri. Because of his form, they believe him to have the intelligence of a mere house cat.\n\nI am amused that those who claim to be so knowledgeable can be so ignorant. What else can I be?
Please give me some good news … we can add another tick to our count of Dragons killed, right?\n\nThe more we add to our tally, the better off everyone is.
Thanks for your help. Once you're finished, return here. Your efforts deserve recognition and recompense.
Looking for something that promises to be challenging and satisfying? Jump in on some Dragon hunting. I can get you started.
How am I suppose to study Dragons when you hero types keep killing them? Have you no consideration for scholarship?
We Dagi climb trees better than we walk on the ground. So, if you see Samari falling down on his face … then you know. He is Dagi, right? It's so!

I just wish the Mages Guild could do more. The people of Rimmen are dealing with Dragons, tyrants, armies of the undead … and we're powerless to truly help.\n\nI'll just have to put my faith in this uprising I keep hearing about.
I may not be as sleek as some, or as tall as most, but the love in my heart burns brighter than the desert sun.\n\nIf only Chirba could see that truth.

The other races call Khajiit cowards, call us weak. All nonsense, of course.\n\nWe are cunning. There is a time in battle to strike, to retreat, to strike once more. We do not allow foolish pride to get in the way of winning, that is all.
Dragons once ruled Tamriel, you know. They were cruel masters, thinking little of the mortals that they ruled over.\n\nI wouldn't be surprised if they're planning to rule again.
You should avoid the fringe elements, walker—the hissing malcontents that curse Queen Euraxia's name. Nothing but lazy rabble-rousers, the lot of them!
Queen Ayrenn claims to be our ally, yes? Yet here we are, suffering under Euraxia's tyranny while the High Elves squabble with other races over the Ruby Throne.

Visit Summerset, and you'll get nothing but insults and judging stares. Travel to Grahtwood, and you'll likely end up on someone's dinner plate.\n\nBut here in Elsweyr, we welcome all. Especially those with heavy purses, yes?

Have you been to the Sugar Bowl? I simply can't recommend it enough. The food is delicious and the entertainment doubly so. \n\nI'd recommend speaking to Zadazi if you're up for a night you won't soon forget.

If you're here to lodge a complaint, believe me, I've heard them all.\n\nI signed up to protect the people of Rimmen, not subjugate and oppress them. I honestly don't know how much longer I can do this.
So many come to Urbinna for hope, for guidance. And so this one tries to offer solace, as a good adept should. \n\nBut … how much longer can Urbinna offer guidance, when she too feels so very lost?
Don't pay the locals any heed, newcomer. The Khajiit of Rimmen are only happy when they're sugar-drunk or complaining about Queen Euraxia.

The other races allow pride to blind them when it comes to combat. They enter battles they cannot win, and refuse to retreat when all hope is lost.\n\nBut we Khajiit? We would rather live to see another day than die some heroic death.

Sure, I can scare a few city folk and stomp out the occasional uprising. But if this resistance in Riverhold turns out to be something that catches on? \n\nWell, let's just say I prefer to support the winning side.

Before the chiefs, before the Mane, there are the Clan Mothers.\n\nThey guide their clans in times of uncertainty. They speak the histories, and pass down our stories. Their power is as certain and strong as the Moons which pull the tides.
Many of the Khajiit I've befriended have started calling me sweetmeat. I'm not quite sure what it means, but I've been told it's a compliment.

New to Rimmen, are you? Well, allow me to explain the rules.\n\nThe Jovial Lambasters help this refuge run nice and smooth. And for such services, all we demand is a little respect. Preferably in the form of gold and portable jewelry, of course.
I came to Rimmen to learn thieving from the best. And I'm not ashamed to admit that the best thieves in Tamriel are the Khajiit, no doubt about it.
I just don't understand how everyone can be so calm. There are Dragons in the sky! Giant, terrible creatures that could kill us without a thought!\n\nWhy am I the only one taking this seriously?
Riverhold offers a variety of fresh food from our many farms. You'll often find the herders of Anequina pass through the market. \n\nOf course, we'll never be as large or bustling as Rimmen.

Another beautiful day in Merryvale, is it not?\n\nLanasi often enjoys lazing beneath the sugarcane. The sun shining through the green leaves, the sweet breeze gently blowing …. Truly, this one would not give up her home for anything.
This one's local farm is just nearby. She comes to Riverhold only to trade for supplies and catch up on the local gossip.\n\nAnd perhaps a drink or two at the Banished Regrets.
Why a sleepy town like Riverhold would need an investigator, I'll never know.\n\nAnd yet Mizzik Thunderboots has set himself up in the Banished Regrets, just raring to solve a case. What a fool.
Once Nirahni traveled to Grahtwood, just across the border. It was only a matter of days before some Wood Elves tried to eat her … even after this one began to speak.\n\nSo now she stays in Elsweyr.

Victory is never assured in battle, but this one cannot help but worry that the odds are unfavorably stacked against us. After all, what hope have we against Dragons?\n\nStill, we cannot allow Euraxia's tyranny to continue. We must fight.

We wouldn't have liberated Riverhold the first time without the leadership of Gharesh-ri. He has our loyalty and respect.\n\nI suppose he gets that for being the Speaker of the Mane, too, but you get the idea.

Almost everyone in Merryvale works for one farm or another.\n\nM'zum is miserable, but reliable in his payments. J'dathal is far more lenient, but often runs into financial troubles. And Kideya only hires the best of the best.
This one, that one, which one? \n\nI can barely keep up with these cats and their damn speech patterns. Following a conversation is like walking through a maze. Confusing, and often not worth it.
Most moon-sugar comes from the forest of Tenmar, but you can find plantations all over Elsweyr. Khenarthi's Roost and Reaper's March are prime examples, as well as Merryvale of course.

Hakoshae used to be a lot more closed off to strangers when we were first founded. Though after the fall of the Potentate, it makes sense that the town would be on edge.\n\nLuckily for travelers like you, we've opened up quite a bit since then.
I don't think any less of my sister, of course. \n\nShe's still Magnate Feina-Darak, no matter who our ancestors were. And she's still going to make sure our town prospers and our culture lives on.

I was quite popular in Rimmen, you know. There was always demand for every painting I created. Always patrons wanting more and more.\n\nThat's why I came here, to get away from it all. No more requests, no more noise. Just the quiet countryside.

There's only so much you can learn by dueling old man Vek-Drassi. If I'm ever to become a skilled warrior, I need to get out there!\n\nYou're a traveler, right? You get it. The only way I'm going to get stronger is by leaving this place behind.

It was the Potentate who declared the Second Era had begun.\n\nCan you imagine a man so imposing that he would declare the end of an entire era? Truly, the Akaviri people must have been quite influential to have such an impact.
The soldiers, they told us not to go near the Dragon corpse. But Manasi cannot help but wonder how much a piece of that beast would be worth ….

Did you hear that Razum-dar took down a whole operation of skooma smugglers?\n\nMajadhi just can't believe it. Not only is her Razum-dar handsome and charming, but he is a hero as well! Oh, if only he would notice how much this one has grown.
There's a lot of, what do you call it? Contested land? In Grahtwood and Elsweyr.\n\nBoth sides see borders as suggestions rather than rules. Caused quite a few wars, as I'm sure you can imagine.

You know, I met my husband in the battlegrounds. Damn near cut my head off, he did.\n\nBetween you, me, and the tentpole, he's lucky he's cute. If he'd been just a hair shy of handsome, I would have killed him on the spot.
People say I am superstitious. I prefer to think of it as cautious diligence!
There are no finer mounts than those offered by Master Groom Zarbi'dahuz!
I really want to kill something right about now.
Restrain the traitors!
With all these Dragons around, no one cares about us measly bandits.
I don't care if they keep the law busy. Those Dragons leave me feeling nothing but uneasy.
Here! Zamarak can sooth your pain!

The Sugar Bowl offers a variety of entertainments for the weary traveler. Tell Zadazi, what is your preference? Slow and sweet, or fast and vigorous?\n\nAh, this one is talking about the music of course.
You know the messenger. If you survive, you will know the message.
Tamruz lost everything! His business, his home, his prospects! All because some sugar-mad fanatics chafed at an Imperial's rule.\n\nMark me, walker, this new government will collapse in a week!
Euraxia may be gone, but the fight continues. Until we've nailed the hide of every traitor to the city gates, there will be no peace.
Is Anequina too tumultuous for your liking? We're about to load up a caravan traveling out of Elsweyr, if you're interested in tagging along.
Rejoice! Alkosh has come to save us!
You have nothing to fear now! Alkosh has returned!
Come back when your heart knows the truth.
I'm so happy I stole, I mean, borrowed this from Malacath!
I've said it before, and I'll say it again. Souls are overrated.
Defilers! Why didn't we leave?
The oasis will heal us, yes? The oasis will heal us.
That old fool should fetch a rather good price, don't you think?
I practice all day, yet it feels like I don't improve.\n\nI am learning much about futility, perhaps.
The harder I train, the better the results. Soon, I will fight Dragons.
These caravanners are too thin blooded. We should make for Rimmen!
The Clan Mother was a fool to keep us locked away for so long.
What will become of this one's children? They are still so young.
Let us die. Please, let us die.

You know, Minshak could have left it all behind. He could have had grand adventures, traveling to Moons-know-where, doing Moons-know-what. But he decided to be a good son and take over the family farm.\n\nLook where that got him.
Don't know what M'zum was thinking, hiring the Redhands to guard his farm. They're more likely to end up robbing him blind than protecting his property.

Yeah, I used to live by the Green Pact. But then I had just one taste of moon-sugar and I was pretty much hooked. Been living in Merryvale ever since.\n\nI mean, there's a reason the Khajiit basically worship the stuff.

Cicatrice is a sad sight to see these days. It was once such a happy town, yes? Many came here seeking hope, and found it in the healing waters of the oasis.\n\nNow there is nothing but death and decay. How miserable.
I do wonder why Mother brought us to this place. \n\nCicatrice was once a great town, this is known. But now? Now there is nothing but burnt rubble and violent corpses.
Bizahen thought about joining the Order of the Zhan Khaj when he was a younger Khajiit. But all those rules the adepts must follow? Who has the patience for that?
Hope you brought your purse. You don't want to know how Jubani deals with browsers.
The aqueduct brings us water for drinking, washing, and bathing. Bahzdal often enjoys lounging in the cool waters during hot, summer days.
Don't call us mounts. Nobody mounts a Senche-raht. Riders shut up and follow where we lead, or they land whiskers-first in the mud. If you want a mount, go buy a dumb animal.
Feel my blood boil within you, leech.
Fear no death, for you already serve me eternally.
Grovel before me!
These slaves are as limitless as time itself.
I do so worry for the Khajiit. Do you think the rumors are true?
This one hopes it is just wild tales told by the Baandari Pedlars, hoping to drum up sales of emergency wares.
Let the usurper queen's lackeys come! We will fight with teeth and claws to protect our home!
I'll blacken the sky with your smoldering corpses.
You're lucky, but that won't last.
The Argonians claim to be communing with the Hist, but M'aiq thinks they are just napping.
This one thought he saw a Pahmar-raht yesterday. Turned out it was two Dagi-raht standing on each other's shoulders.
I'll stoop to your level, but it won't save you.
I heard some smugglers were selling tainted skooma, right here in Riverhold!\n\nLet's just hope Thunderboots doesn't leave quite yet. Who knows what other troubles Riverhold has up its sleeve?
Drain the corpse dry!
A cage of bones for your soul!
Let these bones impale your soul!
I will wipe out the entire order!
None can deny Euraxia or her champions!
That was a Dragon! Right here in Riverhold! I thought we were finished, but then you … you took him down. That was magnificent!
I'll bury us both in stone and fire!
Khajiit has gold if you have wares!
Get into my protective aura, now!
I'll slake this thirst on you!
No thief, this one. Your things, safer with Ezabi than in some stuffy vault.
You call those warriors? They could hardly stand up to my stare, let alone our attacks.
Do you train your soldiers to lie down at the slightest hint of resistance?
I'll enjoy crushing your mortal bones.
Darloc Brae has conquered armies. What hope do you have?
I have votive items for all of Alkosh's holy rituals. They are yours for a humble donation to the temple.
Perhaps you wish to take a vow of poverty and cast off all your worldly possessions? This one can ensure they will find a good home.
Giving you that hammer was the smartest thing I ever did. Or maybe the craziest. Or maybe both. Who cares? Smash something!
I'm sick of these cats. The sooner we torch this place, the better.
I say we burn the whole place to the ground.
Dragons have the potential to threaten all of Tamriel, and I'm stationed here to help prevent that.\n\nI'm organizing daily hunts to take down as many of these aerial killers as possible.
Old spirits linger here, walker. But Noctra protects those who stay in the shadows.\n\nCome, browse.
I have trained for this moment. Come, and perish!
Tamriel's finest swordmasters lie dead at my feet. What hope do you have?
Does the sound of thunder frighten you, animals?
Is something following this one? I think … yes! Flee!
Ah, hello! Fancy meeting you here! I went for my daily constitutional and—Honor's your uncle!—here I am!
I just had the most enlightening conversation with a Dark Elf stable-hand. Did you know that in Deshaan they call helmets pots? Pots! Ludicrous!
I'd love to stay and chat, but my services are needed elsewhere. A dashing knight's work is never done!
To anyone hearing these words, know that Abnur Tharn recorded them with zeal and purpose.
The only obstacle to true happiness? Family, no question about it.
And thus ends this session of the wisdom of Abnur Tharn. Call upon me again when you want to continue your education.
You are listening to the wit and wisdom of Abnur Tharn, battlemage and advisor to emperors.
Argonians are an intriguing people. Their supposed connection to plant life needs further investigation. When I have the time.
I think we're done here. I wouldn't want to overstimulate your cognitive processes with an overabundance of my impactful words.
Baan Dar gifts us with a rich reward today! Let us take it!
I won't be beaten by vermin!
Good work today, five-claw. You will come back again tomorrow, yes? Old Ri'hirr will have more tasks for you then.
J'baanluk will continue to fight for Elsweyr, no matter what dangers he faces. But with heroes like you on our side? Well, it makes this one a little more confident that we will prevail.
More fodder for my spells!
Take the enemy down quickly!
Our indriks are beautiful, don't you think? Feel free to take a closer look!\n\nYou might also want to chat with the Impresario. She's back from her travels and ready to make a deal.

It was not the High Elves who saved Rimmen, oh no. It was a Khajiiti rebellion, led by our very own royalty.\n\nNow, let us hope that our new queen keeps Elsweyr's best interests in mind, rather than the interests of Summerset.
Wondering what this place is? I can help!\n\nWhen you complete one of our annual festivals or celebrations, the Impresario arrives to redeem your rewards. Come back soon and you'll see!
A Dragon? Flee first. Then this one figures out how to fix what Dragons break.
Kra, a Dragon! I must … report this!
Many things have raised this one's fur, but none so much as this Dragon!
Baan Dar's exile! A Dragon? This one should never have left home!

Urbinna was there when you were found in the rubble of your caravan and brought back to Star Haven. And thank the Moons we found you, for who else would have protected us from that horrid Dragon attack?\n\nMay Bright Moons light your path, walker.

Honestly, my day to day work hasn't changed much since the uprising. Keep the city folk in line, stop the occasional petty crime, be a bit of muscle when needed.\n\nLong as no one asks me to face a Dragon or some such, I should be just fine.
Narazreshi is no longer allowed to toss the dice, but she would wager she has many winning numbers in the canyon below.
Narazreshi bets Khasda wishes he'd been nicer to the Stitches. He will need sewing up if he shows his face here again.
We're starting a pool for how much longer the Stitches holds together. This one thinks a few months, at most.
The cat there's under my protection. You mess with her, you mess with me.
Time to start taking bids on my services before the gang war breaks out. The highest bidder's going to run this town. Mark my words.
If things are starting to go soft around here, maybe it's time I take a vacation. Dragon hunting sounds like a good bit of fun.
The Dragonhorn! Use it now!
A foe to Queen Euraxia is no friend of mine. Off with you, before I do something I regret!
Between you and me. Jubani's pretty miffed about Tasnasi's takeover. It won't come to nothing. She won't cross someone as popular as Tasnasi is around here.
Heard Tasnasi was the one who gutted Khasda. Guess she wasn't content with just Dasalzo's blood on her hands. The price on her head's gonna be huge.
Euraxia never had the people's best interests at heart—I see that now. I only hope that I can make up for the harm I inflicted.

This one may go to the palace to find ghosts. Rumor has it the last Khajiit royals of Senchal panicked during the Knahaten flu and locked themselves away inside. No one ever saw them alive again. Spooky, yes?
I enjoy reading about any topic. You may find a book about farming moon-sugar or starting a kwama mine a little dry, but you still learn about a people or a culture. My curiosity knows no boundaries.

It behooves a woman of means, such as I, to see and be seen, especially doing charitable actions. Perhaps I should venture to the market for that purpose. Of course, I would take an escort. Dragons and unsavory people abound these days.

I didn't set out to be a servant in a palace, but it's definitely a step up from cleaning for bored rich people in Kvatch and Anvil. Just wish Dragons weren't causing so much stress around here. People get sloppy or yell at me for no reason.

I like living here. I can eat vegetables and not have people shun me for harming a plant. Not that I eat a lot of vegetables, but I could.\n\nAm I pulling your leg? Hmmm … good question. I might have enjoyed too many tasty beverages recently.

I heard the Dragonguard are reforming. Or have already reformed. Imagine fighting those flying beasts of terror! They deserve to be knocked out of the sky. With arrows. And magic.\n\nI wonder if they have a height requirement.
Was there something about my idle display of a very sharp dagger, one I know how to use, that gave you the notion that I welcomed an interruption from someone I do not know?

One of the pleasures of life is eating mindfully and enjoying each bite. Tasting it fully. Noting its consistency and texture.\n\nI would appreciate it if you would allow me to continue in this solo endeavor.

My honored Tree-Minder told me to travel and learn of other cultures. Argonians should be aware of what happens in the world. \n\nNot all my tribe agrees with this, but I'm glad I came to Senchal. The Khajiit and Imperials interest me.

The cat people here are friendly enough, but sly. Never really sure if they're saying what they mean.\n\nStill, everyone's willing to talk about the Dragons. And this Dragonguard that's forming. Or reforming? Now that interests me.
I spend more in Senchal than anywhere else. I'm not a big fan of the general, though. He doesn't appreciate my time-honored profession.
This one saw Vijari wander toward the Wall of Life earlier. He did not look well. Not well at all.
This one had never seen a Twilight Cantor before. She hopes we will not need to see another for a long time.

Ghalsu tries sleeping at home and his mate always prods him for something. He tries sleeping in the temple and the little priests scold him. He tries sleeping in the colorworks and is chased out for snoring.\n\nSo he tries the fountain and finds you.
Vijari's gone and taken all the bad omens with him. Poor boy. Burana prays he is with Khenarthi now.
This one has finally done it. His garden is free of every last louse and locust. Fa'zin hopes the fruits of his labor will be worth the effort.
Khina could not ask for a more cozy home, but Khajiit need to lounge in the sun and feel the breeze as well.
This one has been painting since he was a tiny cub tracking through his mother's paints. He still paints with his footpads from time to time. It is a joyful, liberating kind of creation.
What do you think of the painted stones around this town? So colorful! This one is told they hold deeper meaning to the people of this village, but it is lost on her.
Listen to Azrid, walker. If you carry anything of value, keep it close to the skin, yes? A South Guard pickpocket can steal the small clothes off a steel-armored Orc!
I wish the Dragons would burn those bandits out of the South Guard ruins. Of course, there's not much left to burn up there. Just old stone and ashes.
Ah, free! For now ….
You should try looking somewhere else.
The bell still seems a bit tarnished to me.
Just press here ….
We had him! I was almost free!
Grr! That burns me up! Your turn.
I've found the seed. Purge it here!
It's cruel to toy with her emotions like that.
Yes, my darlings, come out and play.
Selene, you're spoiling the fun!
Submit, serve, life will be more rewarding that way. And longer.
Better a servant than a slave.
There's no escape from my fangs!
Haha! I accept your offering. Now make another!
The corruption has taken hold of Selene!
They're mine now. Of course, so are the rest of you.
Your sacrifice is in vain.
You forgot something.
Can you feel your blood betraying you?
Am I too slippery?
Do not let them use the helots!
Herd them like the cattle they are!
We'll take Skyrim back soon enough. Mother will see to that.
I would never disobey our mothers, but this storm … hasn't it gone on long enough?
Intruders. Bring them down!
More Nord-scum? No? Slay them anyway!
Lurag gret grool.
Leave the trespassers to me, sister.
You did not wipe your feet, did you? Did you?
Having second thoughts? Hmm. Cowardice is so off-putting.
Come now, dears. Do you really intend to make us wait?
Dead, dead, dead. Brul gra hoak.
Finally, some peace and quiet.
Ugh, look at their corpses. What a mess. What a mess!
Killed by a corpse …. Ironic.
Is that all? Hmph. It seems we overestimated them, dears.
All he wants is bone and ash? What a waste of time.
Enough grousing! Dig!
Kill them! Kill them all!
Eyes up, Draugrkin! It's the competition!
You going to make me wait?
Do they know the way out? No! No one does! No one!
Our patron can have his bones and ashes. I come to claim something far greater!
Orkey's blood, I thought you'd give me a challenge! Too bad.
No! Don't die! Wake up, wake up, wake up! Tell me how to get out. Tell me!
Poor fools. What hope did you think you had?
Shagrath consume you!
Regret taking us on, walker?
Gah! Dragon's fire never burned so hot.
Easier said than done.
You'll follow Renald to your death!
I'll bury you with him. Be honored.
Come out, pretties! Come out!
I feel like you aren't giving this a chance, Selene.
Enough fooling about. Burn!
Leave this to me witch!
You dare attack me?
Slaughter these cattle!
My gratitude for releasing me from that … monster.
Can't thank you enough. That was … vile.
You're back. Seem to have all your limbs, too, so that's good. How'd you fare?
You've got a job to do, don't you? Doing it sooner is better.
You love gold, right? Maybe glory? You can earn both. Let me tell you how.
Good work today. Come back tomorrow. I should have more for you. Go and rest up.
Ah! Just the doughty, hard-nosed adventurer I was looking for!\n\nWell, don't leave me in suspense! Were you successful?
So, you'll be on your way soon enough, yes? Go take care of business and I'll happily fill your purse when you return!
There's my favorite adventurer! One of several, I mean. Don't spread that around. Someone in my position can't afford to play favorites.\n\nAnyway, you're looking for work, right?
Looking for even more work? By Mara's ample bosom … quite the busy bee, aren't we?\n\nCome back tomorrow, my friend. By then I'll have contracts aplenty. You have my word!
No, no, no! You die now!
Here, sweet boy. You need more playmates!
Frozen gales, take shape!
Come, fools. Feel winter's bite!
Between brute strength and the secrets of the arcane … you don't stand a chance.
Get out of my garden! Get out!
Grakh vahg nool! You die now!
Gohlla, cool down our guests, won't you?
Leave nothing but ashes, Hiti!
They seek death, Bani. Give it to them.
Call down the lightning, Maefyn!
Lend me your strength, sisters!
Taste your own rot!
Join us in the azure world!
Grr! Kill the hoarvors!
Get the stranglers! They're spitting at her spiders!
Such a menacing kitten.
Nisaazda will feed you to her weakest warriors!
Chizbari smells Dragon's blood. The beasts are slain, yes?
Why do you loiter here, walker? You have work to do.
Some say that Dragons cannot feel fear. We put that to the test. Today.
No more hunts today, walker. More's the pity.\n\nMany of these beasts remain alive. Too many. We resume the fight tomorrow.

Percius Loche is a true artist. Bebbia questioned the merit of using gold threads for the restoration, but now that she's seen this technique at work … ah, she believes it will be well worth the cost.
Finally. Hope you brought me some good news.
Back to the Annals of the Reman Dynasty, part … whatever. Where's another sordid handmaiden's diary when you need one?
Still kicking, Dragonguard? Got another lead, if you're interested.
You done good, which is more than I ever hear from Za'ji, but I've got nothing else for you today. Next time you want to look busy, drag it out longer.
The Skald-King? Ha. That bastard's days are numbered.
Way I hear it, Mother's working with someone on the mainland. A real monster.
Bah. Nords are like horkers. Fat, slow, and stupid.
Who's more beautiful than Skelga? No one.
For the Coven and the Reach!
We'll feed your guts to the harpies!
This is our island! Ours!
No survivors!
The Great Darkness has come to swallow Nirni up!
We hide Khajiit from the false light of the Moons.
Namiira will devour the Lost Cat's suffering.
Put fire in their veins and Khajiit will beg for cool shadows.
We are outcast no longer!
Listen to the truth of the beating heart!
We dance, dance, dance. Dance, dance, dance, down in the Darks!
Let the beat fill their ears and our venom fill their hearts.
Hmm. That didn't seem to do anything. Maybe try a different sequence?
Intruders! After them!
You'll make a fine sacrifice to the New Moon!
For the Red Rooks!
We're here to win!
I can't wait to see how you bleed!
Just die already!
Tusk them up, Iron Orcs!
What weak competition!
Almost there ….
This one tires of hunting swamp beasts. She wishes to fight Dragons once again!
I will crush you!
You will not escape!

I have longed for an opportunity to apply one of these Akaviri techniques. Their cost is prohibitive for most clientele. Bless Bebbia and her deep pockets.\n\nThat was metaphorical. Pockets on that gown would be a tragedy.
Hey, I'll tell you when I've had enough to drink!
Damn this humidity! Mauloch's jawbone, I miss Wrothgar.
Baan Dar's arse, it's quiet. This one needs a good fight!
Calling me fat? Hrmph. I'll make him a head's weight lighter ….
Just one more job, then it's back to the Alik'r. Just one more ….
Laugh if you want, but I swear that catfish was as big as a senche-raht!
Sure, I skim a little off the top. But you'd better keep that to yourself!
If that slave mouths off one more time, I'm fetching my shears and cutting his tongue out.
I don't know what to tell you. If you don't want rats in your pockets, don't keep hunks of cheese in there.
Could have sworn I heard something. Just the damn rats again.
This one would kill for a sweetroll. Seriously—who should I kill?
Got to watch your step in the shallows nowadays. One of those salamanders almost got me!
Wharf rat? Fetching nchow. Nobody calls me a wharf rat. Nobody!
Oblivion take that son of a guar. I'll point a knife at whoever I damn well please!
Just let those slaves try to escape. This one could use the target practice.
Shields of Senchal? Heh. Just let them try to block us.
Where are all the would-be heroes? We need some excitement around here!
Come on! Someone sing us a tune! Too damned quiet around here.
Patience, friend. Delicious baked goods and a sweet brew cannot be rushed! And no Dragons threaten us today, so we have plenty of time to savor the sweetness of life.
This one can hear the old voices, lost in the crumbling stones or whispered in the rustling leaves. Senchal is a haunted place.
You aren't supposed to be here yet. Neither am I.
Ah, a fellow traveler. Why not rest your legs and restore your spirit with a great tale?

The only joy greater than stories is sharing those tales with others.\n\nThis one has gathered many tales while traveling the breadth of Elsweyr. Perhaps you would like to hear a story about Khunzar-ri?
Beg, Tulip! Beg! I'm begging, you can too!
By the divines, will this beast do nothing beyond bobbling and heavy breathing?
This one cannot turn a blind eye just because someone is hungry enough to swipe an apple from our stores. If we don't stop them, hungry refugees will take everything for free.

The Dragonguard who came before us certainly left some nice pieces of armor. Flexible enough to move quickly, sturdy enough to withstand a Dragon's attack.\n\nMogdal keeps saying they're too pompous, but that's just her way.
I may not be able to see, but my sense of taste is stronger than ever. That's why I'm able to make such delicious meals for our Dragonguard!
Za'ji! I thought I smelled a rat.
One lousy ancestor fights alongside Hakon One-Eye, and suddenly you're expected to live up to your family name and start hunting Dragons for a living.

You don't get much warning before a Dragon attack. One minute, you're cooking dinner for your family and the next … screaming. Fires. Death.\n\nI'll never forget the smell. Smoke and burning flesh. It was horrid.
I don't think I've heard your name before. Still, I may have some furnishings to peruse.

No one has been able to research Dragons for centuries, due to a lack of specimens to study. But now we can change all that. \n\nA Modern Study of Dragons, written by the Illustrious Menagarion. Yes, I rather like the sound of that.
You're worth a bottle or two!
Let this one go and Khajiit will forget this ever happened. Just a misunderstanding!
Ah! Quit your mewling, cat!

I don't have a sad back story about Dragons slaughtering my family or a naive wish to become a hero. I'm just a warrior looking for a battle worth my time.\n\nThat's why I joined the Dragonguard, plain and simple.
A New Moon rises, rhook. And you can rise with it.
Truthfully? Khajiit cannot live like this any longer.
Khajiit was going to be free!

Father wanted Pirjmina to stay in Rimmen and work in his forge until this one died of old age. But the Dragonguard put out the call for daring heroes to fight back against these cursed Dragons.\n\nA much better fate, wouldn't you say?
You cannot stop me!
Come and accept death, mortals!
This time you die!
Mey! You have no hope of defeating me!
Wherever the paws of Imeretto's love fall, pink lilies bloom from the sands.\n\nHa! Yes! Evocative imagery, pleasing meter, dulcet tones … Imeretto will claim his lady's heart soon enough!
Filthy beasts! How dare you soil my refuge! Crush them!
Hah! Baan Dar spits on you unworthy curs!
Do not mind Korabi, walker. A great battle rages in this one's tummy. Korabi's desire to eat cheese wars with this one's ability to digest it.
Kra, a Dragon! I must … report this!
S'rendarr protect this poor scout. This one had not expected to be spotting Dragons today!
Can't a cat get some needed sleep around here without being poked and prodded. Geesh.
Ah, do you smell it? The scent of freedom! The open road beckons and this one wants to make a trade.
What am I paying you louts for? Defend me!
Ra'khajin revealed the path. Now we must walk it.
The New Moon rises … as do we.
Khajiit say it's trapped moonlight in the waters. This one says it's gold.
Khajiit heard one of the lunatics tried to eat another's face the other day. Stay clear of them.
This one shall know the New Moons' secrets! He must know!
Blessed New Moon, speak the word, and this one shall drown Elsweyr in blood.
I say we train those drug-addled lunatics like hounds. They already go for the throat.
Don't drink the water. Too much runoff sullying it now.
Anybody tried pickling one of those jellies in the stock? Bet they'd soak it up good.
Who here thinks they can drink me under the table?
Khajiit should be riding the wind at full sail, not clearing cave air of skooma fumes.
Tried a nip of the last batch. It'll take the wind out of your sails.
At least we don't see many Sea Elves this far east.
If that Orc tries to pick a fight with me one more time, I'm going to cut his throat and stuff his body in a barrel.
The Khajiit plan to double cross us, I'm sure of it.
No respectable Dunmer would take orders from an overgrown cat. Good thing we're not respectable.
Guess the skeevers aren't scared of Khajiit. They keep getting into the sugar sacks.
How is it cats covered in fur can come from somewhere so hot? At least it's cool in this cove.
Bet that swill tastes like sea water. Khajiit won't touch it.
Boss wants more volunteers. Get moving.
This one would break your twiggy little bones without even trying.
This one won't hesitate to crack your skull if you can't handle your skooma.
All this salt in the air gives me itchy scales.
This would make a good place to raise eggs, but stills work too.

Ugh. When you came in I thought you were my perpetually tardy assistant, Tobar.\n\nHe always has an excuse. "Siladia, this one's fur is falling out." "Siladia, this one ate some bad chicken." "Oh, Siladia, this one's mother is very ill …." Ludicrous.
Tell this one to pray, and he shall pray. Tell this one to kill, and he shall kill.
I fear no Dragons, for the Dragons are my allies ….
We shall tear the old Pellitine apart, stone by stone.
The old gods will disappear in ash and blood. Hail the New Moon!
We had a little farm once. A nice home for Tebabi. This one grew a little of this, a little of that. But now it lies burned and fallow—destroyed by Dragonfire.
<Roaring, hissing, growling.>
<Inconsolable crying and wailing.>
<Violently ill, moaning, heaving.>
<Giddy drunk, singing slurred gibberish.>
<Ravenously eating something, like a wild dog.>
<Terrorized screaming, panic.>
<Hissing, croaking, lizard noises.>
Skooma Cat! Skooma Cat is speaking to me!
Stay away, stay away, stay away, stay away!
Who's—stop! Noise. Kill you!
Make it stop! Make it stop!
Gonna maroon me? Gonna leave me behind!
Ha! Hee! Hee! Hahaha!
Need the sap. Split the bark and lick it up!
Come here, skeever! This one's hungry!
Say the word, and I shall smite them all!
Hurzarr feels as though a gloom has been lifted from Black Heights. Bless Khenarthi for blowing away the darkened clouds.
It's been too long!
Use the power of the mask, five-claw!
Kaalgrontiid takes wing! Prepare yourself!
Remember your grapple-bow! Use it to avoid his shouts!
Another shrine lit. Only two more to go.
Defend yourself!
Keep the Dragon distracted! The aegis is stronger than I thought!
You better not be following me, you horker!
This fortress will be your grave!
You cannot hide from me forever!
Now here's a Dragonguard with a story! And plenty of furnishings to choose from, I might add.
It's an honor to have an adventurer of your caliber stop by my humble furnishing store. Please, have a look.
Well, I'll admit. It's a tad confusing why anyone without a house would want to see my furnishings. Still, who am I to judge? Have a look.
Even in death, there is no escape!
Persistent fleas! Die beneath my claws!
Definitely not a secret passage.
Zar's kra'jun had different challenges in our day. For example, Zar had the Halls of Colossus, whereas you had a floating island. Hmm. Zar thinks he likes your story better ….
This is going to hurt!
Why are these particular graves so important?
We take care of our friends and neighbors here in Karthald. It's just a pity how few of us are left.
Go fetch, mongrels!
You've got nowhere to run.
You've got me bleeding all right. Let me return the favor!
Let's get these chains off you, eh? Time to play.
I'll take that one!
Let's see what you've got!
Dead already? What a disappointment.
Saw a bat hanging from a tree limb in daylight the other day. I remember my uncle saying that means much blood will feed the soil. Makes me regret putting aside my sword practice for … ugh. Years.
I have your back!
You must find me. I suffer. Please.
Yes … yes, you're getting closer.
Finally … a chance at freedom. You're so close.
One last act of bravery. Come, now. It's almost over.
Heed my call, bones of the damned!
You offer yourself? I accept.
Finally, my suffering is at an end!
Enough. I've had enough of your pranks.
What will it take to be rid of you?
How did your field work progress? The Coterie of Organized Scholars can only offer funds for completed studies.
Western Skyrim offers a delightful panoply of subject matter, as you'll soon discover!\n\nWhich reminds me, you should seek out the scholar organizing this study for additional advice.

If it isn't my favorite adventurer! One of several, I mean, but don't quote me on that. The Coterie of Organized Scholars can't afford to play favorites. Literally. We need all the help we can get at the moment. Are you busy?
