While your eagerness for more work is inspiring, I fear the Coterie of Organized Scholars has no pressing needs. \n\nThings do move rather quickly in the world of middle-tier organized academia, however, so be sure to check back soon!
I'm so disappointed that oaf won! I should have bid more.
Oof!
Defend yourself!
Hit him!
You can get out of that!
Stand still, damn you!
Stop his attack!
Keep up the assault!
Cut their heads off!
Keep your voice down. Who Mother Ciannait allies with is none of your concern.
This island will be your grave!
She's still around here somewhere. A Nord that big can't hide forever.
Cut their tongues out!
Cold, eh? Good. I like it cold.
Drive them back to the sea!
You better not have stolen my blanket. I already warned you once.
You've made a huge mistake.
I don't know what Bani's working on, but you'd best give it a wide berth.
Send their souls to Hircine!
Touch me again, and I'll cut off your hand.
You looking to get buried too? Fine!
What's Kjalnar doing, anyway? He should be shoveling ash like the rest of us.
What do you think you're doing here?
Gray Host? More like Gray Toast! Am I right? Am I …? Ah, never mind.
We'll take your bones too!
Fjarold fell down the crevasse. You believe that? What an idiot.
Rip them to shreds!
Did you see the teeth on that skull? It was a vampire all right.
Knives out, Draugrkin!
What're you looking at? Get back to work.
Finally! Been itching for a good scrap!
We almost done here? Got a bad feeling about this place.
I was on the edge of a breakthrough …. You'll pay for that.
Any who oppose me will die!
I only accept victory or death and you're still breathing. What do you have to report?
If you're hoping for a different task, I have nothing else for you.
If you're seeking excitement, the Swords of Solitude can provide. Wager your life and reap your winnings, or at least die with some honor and be able to look your ancestors in the eye.
The Swords of Solitude are grateful for your assistance. We'll make use of your talents again, to be sure.
Have you come here to die like the rest?
Soon, the snow will be red with blood.
You're nothing but a bump on the road to Solitude.
Ah, new blood.
Yandir hates waiting ….
Find your bravery, little ones, and face me.
Prepare if you wish. Just know that it will not matter.
Ha! Send me more warriors! Yandir's beasts haven't eaten their fill!
Hmph. A feast for gulls. Nothing more.
A predictable outcome.
Even in death, there is no escape!
Yes! Come join me in death!
Let me show you true madness!
Rejoice! You have been chosen!
Lonely? I'll gather some friends!
Careful taking kit from potion storage. I don't see'em washing those bottles.
Might want to wait a moment between drinking those. They react poorly.
Durzogs are getting dinner tonight!
Found some spies!
And I thought this post would be boring. Entertain me!
Enough gawking. Wipe the drool from your chins and get on with the test!
Simpletons! Can't you tell this is futile? I am invincible!
Someone get in here and clean up this mess!
Those new vampires shouldn't be possible. And yet, they exist.
Her blood holds power to shape as we wish.
A meal for the pets!
You cannot interrupt Vaduroth's harvest!
Spike of blood. Build her dolls. Send us home.
Standing around only delays your end!
You smell powerfully delicious!
Shells. Nothing but shells. Filled with empty! Now you're done.
Lady Thorn will reward me for this victory!
You see what happens when you come into my home uninvited!
I will taste your agony!
Have you heard the story of Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts, where Ysgramor wrestles spirits? That's why we call those waters the Sea of Ghosts, you know. One day I'll swim among them myself.
Counseling others requires the patience of a mountain and a great deal of empathy. This holds greater truth when speaking to Svargrim these days.
I grew up on stories of Topal the Pilot. Perhaps one day I'll follow the route he took along the Niben River. Maybe even sooner than I think. Solitude feels … off to me now. Too closed in.
I had a perfect spot for fishing right under the arch. But I caught a fish with a slaughterfish in its belly the other day, so now I can't go back there. Bad luck, you know.

When something becomes precious to you, do you not try to protect it from harm?\n\nIt's no different when it comes to instruments of legend. How can we be trusted if a careless student, or Maestro, ruins a centuries-old lyre while it's in our care?

Perhaps if I just wish it hard enough, everyone in Solitude will magically become a better person. Even the one who accused me of waking him up by sending a bird to smash through his window! How would I even do that?\n\nThe docks calm me down.
You'll find no better mead than in Solitude. The honey we use comes from bees that favor mountain flowers. My meadcake is perfection because of it!
I have not missed the annual burning of King Olaf, nor do I ever intend to. What a festival!
Some say Mara's a gentle soul, but if you ever get her angry by, say, breaking a promise you've made in her name? Well, don't get her angry. Trust me on that.
Patrols might increase in Solitude. We've had some mysterious deaths of late, all taking place in plain sight when nobody happened to be looking. Odd, huh?
People say Solitude's seen more travelers passing through as of late. Wonder what the draw is. Maybe the mead?
I spent most of my life hunting game, but that gets boring after awhile. Now, I hunt down lawbreakers. I'll be back at it again shortly. Try not to get on my list.
Watch out for the beggars. They're in league with the local thieves and keep an eye on people and places for them.
Do you know what my secret mead ingredient is?\n\nNo, really. I forgot to write it down. I'm asking everyone. Someone might know!

Because you chose to talk to me and many do not, let me gift you with information. People often choose not to see beggars, so it's no surprise I've noticed more smuggling happen around Solitude. Perhaps soon I'll even know why.

During my trip to Lilmoth, I had to constantly clear condensation from my instruments, sometimes mid-song! All due to the humidity!\n\nKasara, my favorite horn, was never the same after that trip. Such a waste.

Every Solitude Nord says that if you pry up a paving stone, you'll find a carving of one of the Divines on the other side. A sign of their blessing.\n\nSome even claim that the bones of the original founders also rest beneath our feet.

I hear that the author of my favorite mysteries, Yvonna Graymoth, lives in seclusion here in Solitude! I hope that's true. But then, I know everyone living here, so is someone pretending to be who they're not?\n\nWait. Is it you? I don't know you!

On my way to Solitude, I saw a fight between some Nords and several fetchers clad in fur. Well, I suppose they both had fur, but the latter had more. \n\nWhen one of the archers shot an arrow my way, I chose to leave. Quickly.

Nords are … Nords, all over. The same. Maybe different colored … fur? But otherwise the same. Don't like each other much, I think. But I might have had too much mead.\n\nI've been here too long. I'm starting to sound like them.
I feel like I've been to Solitude before. I'm not sure why. Maybe all Nord towns feel the same?\n\nJust don't ever tell them that. They get so angry when you point out their similarities.
I hope you didn't come from the Eastern kingdoms of the Nords. If you did, you might consider keeping that to yourself. To say the Nords of Solitude disdain Jorunn is an understatement.
I'm not sure I understand the purpose of "The Burning of King Olaf" festival that is held here. These people burn their kings? To what purpose?\n\nI shake my head in confusion.

I asked a Nord about one of the three slashes inked on her right bicep. Apparently, she got it after avenging her brother, who died hunting a bear. She ripped that bear apart. With her bare hands.\n\nVisceral, yes? Tonight, I learn about the next mark.

Did you know that some of the locals keep a bowl of saltwater just inside their doorway to capture any wandering spirits from the Sea of Ghosts?\n\nSuch an odd custom. None have allowed me to examine these bowls, unfortunately.

I'm not sure if you're aware of the Way of the Voice. The Nords don't discuss it much with outsiders. The thu'um, or Voice, is a Nord form of magic. The Way involves some concept of "true need." I'm still trying to understand what that means.
The Halls of the Dead intrigue Rathzin. What rites do the Nords hold in those halls? Why hide from the light of the moons?

The people in here in Solitude give useless advice. \n\nI don't understand how putting honey into a jar, burying it at the site of the last death, and sprinkling the area with my hearthfire ashes is supposed to keep my livestock from being killed.

My life consists of traveling somewhere to find a missing relative. Two years ago, I found my cousin in Cyrodiil. She wanted to fight, she said. Before that, I tracked down my father, who simply wanted away from mother, in Stormhold. Stormhold!
The king's daughter gets into more than her father knows. Good for her, I say! Being among the people is his job, yet he hides away from us.
I saw no ghosts on the Sea of Ghosts. Perhaps the stories are false?

The Mages Guild members here seek knowledge of the Dragon burial mounds.\n\nI went out to visit one recently, as did several others. We each visited a different site. I'm the only one who returned. I'm … not sure what to make of that.

I started breeding and training frostbite spiders. Unfortunately, every time I take one with me to go hunting, some well-meaning neighbor kills it before I can even leave Solitude.\n\nIn short, if you see me with a spider, ask before killing.
Have you ever seen a vampire? I did once. Can't quite remember where, but it'll come to me.\n\nI swear I saw some some werewolves on my way to Solitude, too. Or maybe that was in Glenumbra.

Ziss! This one did not expect to find Nords so unwilling to take coin for information!\n\nIlazun fears that even in the brightest of moons' light, darkness festers and rots what passes for good here among the Solitude city folk.
The guards kicked a man out of town a while back for trying to sell fresh Dragon bones. They assumed he was a fraud.\n\nAfter hearing about Elsweyr, I wonder if he was actually telling the truth.
No matter what befalls Skyrim, we are Nords! We are strong!\n\nShor's bones, if I had my lute, I would sing it loud for all to hear!
I love combustion! Haha!
Someone take this cadaver to storage!
I'll cleave your bones in twain!
Bone and ash, unleash your fury!
Sister Balra is a taskmaster.
The land of the Nords will soon be ours.
We still have much work to do.
Every day brings us closer to our goal.
By blood and ice!
The ice in my veins burns cold!
I miss our frozen shores.
We have nothing to fear from the Skald-King's agents.
Did you hear what happened at the other camp?
Working with those not of the coven … it disgusts me.
Remain vigilant. We are close to our goal.
This land is full of fat, sluggish prey.
Where are the witches when you need one?
May the night hide you, my brethren.
They call that a storm?
I grow tired of this place.
Why am I being punished with such menial tasks?
I deserve better than this.
Why do they keep sending me to places such as this?
The coven serves a purpose, yes?
Awake, my creations!
Look sharp, young blood. The holds are in peril.
The scouts say all's quiet, for now. I'm sure there's something that needs doing, but I've got nothing left for you to do this day.
I expect clear skies on the hour.
My knees tend to ache when a storm's brewing, but they're quiet for now. Have you put those harrowstorms to rest?
We will make them fear the Reach.
Has Vund completed the reagent yet?
Vund has true vision. The Reach will triumph under his leadership.
With fire and stone we will turn this place to rubble!
Those fools underestimated the Reach.
What did Vund do with the big one? I saw them dragging him off.
The alchemical solution should be ready by now.
The garrison was weak before we arrived. They will fall easily.
No longer will we hide.
Vund may be crazy, but his power is incredible.
Solitude will mourn its precious bridge.
The bridge will fall like a wounded animal.
Suffocate on my genius!
Not this cart either. I hope we didn't miss it.
A storm is brewing!
Behold my hunger's swirling depths!
Look out!
Muffins! I have some delicious greens for you!
Did you find some yummy plants, darling?
Hungry from adventuring? Buy a delicious skeever kabob today!
Undaunted? You think I'll be bested by a pack of thick-skulled oafs? I'll show you how far beneath me you are!
The struggle only makes your flesh taste sweeter.
Rip you apart!
<Manic laughing, snarling, and howling.>
Now witness the power of the sun cast in a stone mold!
Only a seven on my Inflagram index. Better dispersal of the formula should correct.
Purge the fire! Let's proceed with the next test phase.
Even Ysgramor would quake in his boots before this mighty glacier!
The frost salts to mirriam ratio is too low. A pinch more? Or substitute ice wraith essence?
Finish the heat exchange! It's time for something different!
The storm has not stripped you of your soul? We'll coax it from you yet.
Is that what you call triumph? Broken branches and snapped twigs?
Did that give you a glimmer of hope? One pike is enough.
The pikes are easily replaced. All your efforts are a waste.
The storm is undone, but the spoils are ours! Add their souls to the harvest, my creature!
Fight me, Halfling!
After we take Kyne's Aegis, we'll take all of Skyrim.
Let's get this over with …
Find the survivors! Kill them like the rest!
No one plunders our seas but us, frug!
I feel exposed out here. Like we're being watched.
Carry the Divines with you and you have nothing to fear.
They say Reachmen are prowling around here. Let them come.
Destroying my bloodknights won't save you. I have other creations!
A bloodknight superior to Essenia's in every way!
Assistants! To my laboratory! Now!
You want your home to look stunning, yes? I can help —either before or after your next Battlegrounds match.
I know people. You, for instance, need a place to sit down. Maybe not now, but soon. I bet you want one of my furnishings, too.
I can't wait to get back into combat. For now, I could do worse things than sell worthy opponents like you some useful goods.
Hmm … you should look at my wares. I'm not saying anything against what you have. Just that you deserve better.
Everyone should take more time to enjoy the wilderness.
We would all be dead if it weren't for you.
I had not thought to meet people who believed stranger things than the Stonechewer Goblins, yet here I am in Solitude among these Nords.\n\nThe things I do to bring quality goods to places.
Looking to settle in here among those close-knit Nords? I have just the thing for you!
Agh. My colleague brought in fish to eat again. How many times do I have to tell her?\n\nSorry. I simply can't—would you care to deposit or withdraw something?
Few would take on the Nords of Solitude, which is another reason why banking with us is wise.
Happened upon a Dwarven thimble in a bag once. Odd, huh? Unattended bag, of course, so fair game.\n\nSpeaking of, you want a bag you won't accidentally drop, right? I have some for sale!
I have a long memory. Don't cross me in our dealings. These mounts deserve better than any nonsense some might try with me.
Been talking about hunting mammoths with friends. They're massive, but if you hit them just so, they keel over. Got a few weapons here to help if you're interested.
I sell the best shiny things in Solitude! You'd look magnificent with some of my sparkling jewelry!
I'm not actually from Solitude. I grew up in several cities. Maybe after I make enough coin, I can fund a trip back to one of them and … I don't know. Sleep for a few weeks?
I can't wait to get home and romp with my dogs! Until then, I'm here to sell all kinds of useful goods. Quality, too!
Help me lighten my load before I head to Eastmarch. No, don't tell me what's happening around here. Ignorance is my bliss.
Many goods for sale. Here!\n\nPardon me, please. I had an unfortunate run-in with a horse. Hard to breathe now.
Some say the locals here are aloof. I think it's just a matter of listening and empathizing.\n\nCome, tell me what you need, and I'll do my best to help you out.
Careful of the Draugrkin. They'd sooner make a corpse of you than talk.
Between carving animals from tusks and selling goods, I've little time for exploration. So it goes. Care to look at what I have today?
People here have strange beliefs. Like dropping an egg on stone means you'll find coin? How … I mean why? Ah, well, feel free to take a look at my wares.
I found the most wonderful treat in a tree I climbed the other day. Honey! The bees had a hive tucked inside.\n\nI'm so glad my guild brought me here to sell goods for them.
Dancing among the flowers fine, singing a song that calls to him …\n\nOh, pardon. Just practicing for my Bards College audition. Let me show you some items for sale.
You look like you could use a change. Let's get you to one of the Alliance territories—if you want, of course!
I saw birds fleeing the trees the other day. That's not normal. You might want to stock up on a few things, just in case.

Welcome to Haafingar hold, the center of Western Skyrim! Well, its political center. Because of the city of Solitude. It's not actually in the center of … wait, hmm, I can't recall the last time I looked at a map.\n\nAnyway, want to trade?
Solitude is an interesting name for this place. These days, I can't seem to find any privacy for myself. Part of that is because I buy and sell goods, but still ….
It's hard to get good metal to work with during the winter. Trade slows down a lot. I wish our noble leaders would fix that.\n\nBut, luckily enough, I have wares to sell if you're interested!
I'm quite sure that when a Dwarf sneezed, they'd use that sound to name something around them. How else do you explain Enchoo … umm … Nahchu …. \n\nI'll get it right some day.
You swallow enough of my drink and you'll forget where you are.
Respect the wood you work with. It once lived, and it can live again if you have the skills. Perhaps you'll see what I mean if you look at my wares.
I've lived in Solitude my entire life. I sense change coming, though. Not sure how I feel about that.
Ah, Solitude. People here complain about boredom while refusing to step outside the city walls.\n\nBut enough of that. Wish to browse my wares?
Someone passed through here with several cats the other day and didn't buy a thing. I spent the next hour sneezing. Ugh.\n\nYou'll make up for their lack of consideration, yes?
You'll want to avoid the fish from Reybyt. It's likely several days old. Trust your nose.
I've seen many a Nord carving horker tusks. I tried my hand at it—surprisingly soothing.
I feel like someone's watching me. I have ever since I got here. It's unsettling.\n\nBut you're probably here to buy clothes, right?
Poke them, slice them, bleed them dry. With Storm's blades they'll ne'er know why!\n\nNo, that doesn't work either. I'd want the person I'm killing to know why.
I use wood from Haafingar when making my weapons. Anything else is inferior and, dare I say, cursed. Too many have fallen from using material from other sources!
I stole every single sign from Morthal a few years ago. It was glorious.\n\nDo tell me you have signs of your own to sell.
Every time I leave, I come back to more cats. Oh, you might not see them now. They're sly ones. Perhaps you've been a bit sly yourself? Need a fence?
Returning to Solitude after all my exploits … it's strange to be selling goods here. It feels more isolated than when I left, but that's just my travels broadening my mind.
Bugs. In my hair! And I thought Murkmire was bad. \n\nWell, if you're not keeping hair in our vault, your goods should stay safe.
Come! This one has goods you need. Especially if you stay in Solitude. Such small minds the Nords of this place have. Feel free to visit this one when you need a break from them.
I gave some bread to a beggar who came here from another hold. I did not know my neighbors could scowl so deeply!
All manner of black souls locked up here. They'll go for a fortune.
Careful with those umbric urns. They're a hundred times more valuable than you are.
Fine, I'll dig and you can fight the draugr. That's what I thought.
I know there were more of us down here. Where do those louts keep wandering off to?
How many more tombs like this you figure we'll find in Blackreach?
I always thump'em on the skull once before I try picking'em up.
We grow more powerful every day.
This place is cold …
Our ancestors prospered within these walls.
Did you hear about the Dragons in Elsweyr?
We will rule again.
The Dragon Cult grows stronger.
I'll kill anyone who stands in our way.
The ritual is almost complete.
I caught a draugr looking at me funny.
For the glory of the Dragon Cult.
This is the perfect place for our revival.
Our time has come once more.
Power swirls within these halls.
We must prepare the site.
You come to do war, little fish? Ha! Is all gristle and bone!
Come, pet! Yandir heals your wounds.
Winter serves Yandir!
Drink the thunder!
No! Beast is not yours to kill!

One of my road companions used to chirp. Yes, like a bird.\n\nAnd, yes, it got irritating after awhile. I'm sure the woman was trying to make me go insane. Her unusual habit certainly didn't help that night we got attacked by vampires, either.
Kill, beasts! Kill till you die!
I swear by Old Knocker's fangs that someone stole my entire day's coins without me seeing. I keep my cup in my hand while begging, yet at some point, they vanished.
Part the waves! Break the stone! Yandir calls!
The last time we had a festival here, I danced all night after selling out of food. Folk seem grim these days. I might not have as many dance partners next feast.
I knew you were no good thieves! Guards!
No! Your presence tears apart the very Firmament!
Back! Back I say!
Stars above, you are an affront to my eyes!
The guards are looking for you.
You need to leave. Now.
I want no part of this.
Not interested.
How did you get … nevermind! Away with you!
Abomination against Y'ffre! Leave my presence!
Keep your distance!
Abomination against Y'ffre! Leave my presence!
Remove yourself from my presence straight away.
You're not here to eat us, are you?
Stay back … you!
Please excuse me. I have nothing to say.
Speak with someone else. Not me.
A beast? I erect the spine of unease.
Away from me. Leave me in peace.
Please excuse me. I have nothing to say.
Speak with someone else. Not me.
The sight of you dries my scales, beast.
Away from me. Leave me in peace.
Sap and stone, what are you?
Don't come any closer.
Just-just stay back!
I don't want you near me.
Stay away from me.
There is nothing for you here, beast. Please, just go.
Stay back, beast. I mean it!
There is nothing for you here, beast. Please, just go.
Go away now.
What manner of creature are you?
Not interested.
Back! Back, you horrid beast!
Go away now.
I'll stuff you full of arrows, you horrid beast!
Just stay out of my way.
Snares of Hircine, what a beast!
No! I won't let you bite me, horrid beast!
Leave me alone.
Bow and blood, what manner of beast are you?
I don't like the looks of you.
An affront to Y'ffre, that's what you are! Begone from here!
Get out of my sight, you foul creature!
Get out of my sight, you foul creature!
Bad idea, my friend. Bad idea.
I know you, and I want nothing to do with you.
I'd rather face all the hags of Hag Fen than deal with a beast like you!
Zenithar take me away from here! You are a beast!
I know you, and I want nothing to do with you.
Off with you, creature!
I'd rather face all the hags of Hag Fen than deal with a beast like you!
Not this again! Is no one what they seem?
Gah! What kind of creature are you?
Agh! I've seen you in my nightmares!
I've seen many horrors in my time, but you top the list.
Oblivion take you! I'll not have such a creature in my presence!
Get away … you.
Stay back, I mean it!
Not interested.
Freakish monster! Shoo! Go away!
Freakish monster! Shoo! Go away!
That thing's so ugly it's criminal!
Keep away! You understand? I'm warning you!
Back, vile creature.
Come any closer and I'll scream.
Not interested.
Keep away! You understand? I'm warning you!
Someone get the Fighter's Guild!
How about you find something else to do?
Dear gods, get away from me!
Leave me alone and I'll leave you alone.
Saint Roris's bones! Keep away, you monster!
Get away! Immediately!
Easy. Easy. Please don't eat me.
To Red Mountain with you, creature!
Do not cause trouble here. I want none of it!
You look even more suspicious than I do.
Away with you.
This one doesn't want any trouble.
Do not cause trouble here. I want none of it!
Get lost!
I've got better things to do.
Go away! Or else!
Watch out! We've got a nasty one here.
This one thinks you are acting very suspicious.
I'll keep to myself, thank you very much.
Stay away from me.
Stay back, beast, or by Orkey I'll let you have it!
Be off, creature! Get!
I have no quarrel with you, beast. Just leave me be!
Stay back, you horker.
If you're looking for something to eat, I've got nothing for you!
Good creature …. Nice creature …. Just leave me alone!
I don't know what you are, and I don't want to find out.
Leave me in peace.
Shor take you and leave me be.
Back, you beast! Get back!
Shor's bones, what are you?
Keep away from me.
Beasts like you have no place here. No place at all!
Don't eat me, please. I'm stringy!
Just look at it! What curse is this?
Stay away from me, beast!
Grah! A beast stalks the streets!
Stay away from me, beast!
Get away from me, you monster!
Leave this place, beast! Else you'll feel my axe!
You don't scare me, beast! Off with you!
I'm not looking for trouble. Leave me alone.
You don't scare me, beast! Off with you!
Keep away, keep away.
Get away from me.
Get back!
Tusking dungheaps! What are you doing, changing like that?
Begone, you foul creature!
Get away from me.
Mess with me, and I'll skin your hide to make a coat!
Leave us in peace, you beast! Or leave in pieces.
Leave me be, creature! Seek prey elsewhere!
I have no quarrel with you, beast!
Clear out, monster, or face Onsi's wrath!
I don't like the look of you.
You stay away … you hear?
Please, leave me in peace.
I won't tell a soul. Please, just go!
I don't like the look of you.
Be gone, monster! I'm warning you!
A beast such as you cannot be here.
By Tava's red feathers, what are you?
Leave me alone-I mean it!
Go elsewhere!
Stay back, monster! Please?
Leave me be!
I'm warning you! Take one more step and I'll … I'll do something!
Kragh vuul! Form ranks and fire!
One blossom for the kiss at the end. Surely he doesn't expect us to kiss one of these sconces!
Groog va kagh! Bring me more fighters!
Every now and again I like to grab one by the legs and use'em as a club. You should try it!
The best gifts come within black sweetroll boxes! Taste the glory of pastry today by joining the First Church of the Holy Sweetroll!
The Pale Lady deserves better. If I can't get the eyes right, what's the point of carving her?

Last year, in Windhelm, I brought my mastiffs to show off at the Mages Guild. So many compliments on my dog Woofharth. He just fathered a promising litter, and now guards it day and night.\n\nSometimes, I wonder what he's growling at.

Are you looking for some solace, friend?\n\nI happen to be a priest of All-Maker, from Solstheim. If you align yourself to the harmony of the land, the land will provide peace and sustenance. Come, pray with me ….

Those witches I keep seeing around laced our firewood with some kind of compound that makes us mindless slaves. They're going to feed us to the vampires!\n\nThe town thinks I'm crazy, but my sister Sondi and I know the truth.
We should own the Nord lands.
We need more prisoners for the experiments.

Do you know someone at the Bards College? Can you put in a good word for me?\n\nI've been working so hard trying to figure out the strings and … music … sounds. But no one I've asked will teach me! So many songs are stuck in my head.

If you're looking for hunting tips, look elsewhere. My grounds are my own.\n\nBut I'll give you a bit of advice. Don't get sloppy. Organize your kit and clean it. I see a lot of hunters and trappers around Skyrim, and most of them are absolute messes.
You will do well in my machine.

You seen Vigrida around? I was hoping she'd give me some hunting tips.\n\nI'm not bad at making traps. Pretty good with a bow, too. When I'm finally done being a soldier, I thought I'd take up hunting.

If you've worked behind a desk, shuffling scrolls, writing endless letters … you know how much it can quash your spirit.\n\nGods, what a depressing business. Glad I could leave that behind. The crisp air and crunching snow restores my spirit.
That ritual reminded me of Red Mountain ash storms.
Meridia did a lot of good for these poor saps.
I expected a Daedric cult to fare better against this sorcery.
A shame the storms only make mindless things and not more of us.
The Icereach Coven's rituals are more effective than I could have imagined.
Vampire or no, the Reach magic unsettles me.

You ever fished under Solitude? I caught all kinds of fish in these lands and beyond. Grouper. Sturgeon. Quillback. Boga. Opah. Char. Skate. Steelhead.\n\nI caught a steelhead so big, it had a whole horker cub in its stomach! That's no lie.

What do you want? Stay where I can see you!\n\nIf you think I'm being paranoid, talk to me after you've found a headless doll under your pillow! Go on about your business, stranger. And don't tell anyone where you found me!

I spent a lot of time in the Bards College back in Solitude. My parents are still there, as far as I know.\n\nI'm not a bad singer myself, but my mother's voice is just divine. I'll never live up to her name, so I decided to follow my own path.
Admiring my knife? The smith I acquired it from was quite skilled in his craft. Specialty blades are somewhat of a hobby of mine.

My parents back in Lilmoth told me not to come to Skyrim. They said it was too cold and dangerous, and that an Argonian wouldn't fit in here.\n\nThey were mostly right. But the horker stew is so delicious! It's worth it.

Blackreach is every adventurers dream. \n\nThe foreman doesn't like me dropping my equipment to study every strange mushroom I find, but this place needs to be documented! Someone has to do it. Why not me?
You smell that? Blood, dirt, sweat, and armor oil. It's glorious isn't it?\n\nAnd what's more, it keeps us gladiators sharp, in case we're needed to fight threats to Skyrim.
Sovngarde awaits you, stranger!
Being underground in this cavern is all I'd hoped it'd be. Away from the light of the sun, from the unpredictable nature of weather, I can set up my shop here and not have to worry at all.
As if mining wasn't dangerous enough work, now we're trying to do it in just about the scariest place ever.
I think we got them all!
I miss the sky. Working this hard and never seeing the sun can't be good for us.

Pit Daemons are doing well, but then they've always been great on defense. I'd like to see the offense pick it up a little.\n\nThey're still the best, though. Dollinith doesn't know what she's talking about.
Keep it up, your hard work will be rewarded.
There's still much work to be done, don't slow down!
You should be careful! The dunerippers will get you!\n\nMy friend tells me that those things are all over the place down here. She can smell them on account of her jackal nose, you see.

I am not unfamiliar with the more treacherous parts of Tamriel. Every place has its teeth, and its sorrows. My egg-sisters and I explored many of these places during our travels. \n\nThis one is no different.
Yandir fears nothing! Nothing!

If you need supplies, you'll have to look elsewhere. I'm not selling right now.\n\nI know I'm losing out on good coin, but after a day of dealing with these people I need some time to myself. This is exhausting.
Ha! You flinch? Pathetic!
I hate the chill that comes with this damned place.
I'm tired of living down here. I feel like I can't breathe.
Heard Ullagarde tried to take a bite out of one of those big mushrooms yesterday.
I'm not one for superstition, but it's almost like this place doesn't want us here.
Like a stormy sea, I will swallow you whole!
Cowards! Weaklings!
We rule the seas here.
Let us give the mountain a taste for Nord blood!

I'm not much of a fighter, but I am an Orc of means. I … I could help, maybe. But, who needs the most help? King Kurog? The Khajiit of Elsweyr, attacked by Dragons?\n\nAnd sometimes people don't want help, even when they need it the most.

Ah, the smell of leather, and the feel of a soft-fashioned hide.\n\nIf I can get my business off the ground, I can quit soldiering. Shouldn't be too hard. My father's hides are the best in Wrothgar. I just need practice.

Solitude is home. I was born there, I grew up there, and I long to return there.\n\nBut it is my duty and honor to offer my service in her defense. And to that end, I will hold Dragon Bridge to my last breath, if need be.

Had a change of faith recently. An Argonian and a Wood Elf helped me on the road. The high priests of Mauloch who serve the Pact say these are my enemies.\n\nNot serving a god that labels them as such.

I used to play here when I was young. I remember all the soldiers standing dutifully at their posts, keeping everyone safe. It's why I joined the city guard.\n\nNow I'm here after all this time, and I couldn't be prouder.
I can't be bothered right now. \n\nVery sorry if you're looking for a mage, but I have important matters to attend to regarding the mine. And, no, I can't tell you about them.
All that you have will belong to me!
If you find someone with recruitment potential take them directly to your pentarch.
When the Exarchs rise, the Gray Host will be unstoppable.

Some traveler came through earlier and said he saw Dragons in Elsweyr! \n\nIf I wasn't a member of the guard, I'd love nothing more than to pack up my axe and go get myself trophies. Those horns would make nice decorations.
It's taking everything I have not to grab one of those Reachmen between my teeth and shake them to pieces.
It'll be harrowstorms as far as the eye can see soon.
Error Detected. Activating emergency defense array.

I've asked for this assignment because I've seen enough action for two lifetimes. I needed something quieter.\n\nI'm not against getting into the fight, of course, it's just that I've done my fair share. It catches up with you.
Morthal's rustic. You might not find another merchant like me around, in fact, so you're welcome to see what goods I have.
My goods are remarkably free of insects … unlike everything else down here. Please buy so that I can leave sooner.
People who find their way down here need a good, pest-free sleeping spot and provisions. You interested?
Elle's been working us hard lately.
This place has a strange smell to it.
If they keep charging what they do for food, I'm going to start living off bugs.
Don't know what anyone expects to find down here.
Such sights within the caverns!
Our raid was an enormous success.
Bones and blood. Skin and teeth.
Surely we could conjure the harrowstorms without those filthy Reachmen.
The Ashen Lord has waited centuries for this war. We can wait a little longer.
I've been practicing this technique for a hundred years. It's flawless.
I can't be near the gray reliquaries. The remains speak to me. A cacophony of our brethren calling out to be freed.
I'm honored to be a part of the Ashen Lord's grand design.
I want to see the looks on their faces when the Gray Host comes charging out of Blackreach.
Have you seen those disgusting, eye-less things around Blackreach? Can't wait to be above ground for good.
Don't kill the live ones. Better they get fed to the harrowstorms.
Wish we could sleep on beds and not piles of hay.
With every ritual we grow nearer to our goal.
The ritual is stronger than ever.
The witches are only using us.
We will need more medallions.
We will need more corpses.
They tossed new meat down into the crypts.
Solitude will fall and the Gray Host will rise!
Our task reaches closer to completion every day.
There won't be a living soul in Western Skyrim by the time we're done.
Relax, the storms have no effect on vampires.
I've been shadowing traveller. No one expects what's coming.
Make sure no one escapes. Keeping the element of surprise is crucial.
I grow tired of these coven witches bossing me around.
Has anyone told you what happens during these storms? Me either.
Sometimes I like to lick the blood off my blades.
Hmph. We're only letting the Reachmen think we're sharing with them.
Thought no one would find them in this wasteland. Thought wrong. Heh.
Quit running and fight me!
Weather's a little brisk, eh?
Grab anything that isn't nailed down! If it is nailed down, tear it up!
That fool interfered with our plans.
We must not let defeat halt our plans.
Fools! We've left ourselves vulnerable.
We should not have to hide here like rats.
We will not be stalled by these events.
This place is so barren, so lifeless.
Call upon the blessed warmth of light for us, and the wrath of flame and stone for the Nord.
The vines whisper of intruders in our midst. Be wary.
Og il dunna travern. Shal shug oh pater noch.
Drown the Nord-swine in the hot blood of the mountain!
I think the clouds are turning. We should prepare for a stormy night.
Divines help us!
Come on, Reach-dogs!
I knew this was a bad spot to camp!
Have a little faith. The Divines won't lead us astray.
It's too quiet. I came out here for adventure, not a leisure hike.
You find no warmth here!
Bragh na! Come, Thunder!
Storm! Bring me my brother!
Like water on rock!
Going somewhere?
More food for the sharks!
It has begun!
This reliquary is nearly filled.
Enjoy your freedom from Oblivion!
The reliquary! No! There will be a price paid for this!
I'm talking to you, milk drinker! Fight me!
Ha! The little snowback is afraid of Rolstag!
Rolschlag … Rolstag will end you, snowback!
I thrash lousy skeevers like you … weaklings ….
You can't win, weakling!
Knights! Drag these fools to the grave!
Help me, damn it! Before it's too late!
Kyne's thunder! Save me from this repulsive creature!
About time somebody rescued me!
Finally! I feared you would let me be eaten!
I am in your debt, stranger.
Headache, dead bodies. Thank you, I think.
I thought they said the harrowed would make this easier!
See? This is digging. You should be capable of this!
More interruptions.
Working with these fools is impossible!
No, not like that! Why can't you do anything right?
Now look what you've done!
Thank the merciful powers! I think I need a drink.
Holding out on your own kind?
Greedy bastard! You better share!
Sharing, yes?
You are too generous.
There's enough for all of us.
Not without me!
Praise Tall Papa! Thank you, stranger.
What happened?
Oh, my head … Where am I?
My savior. Thank you for your help.
You saved me? I'm grateful.
You saved me!
Just a taste for now.
A meal. Thank Molag Bal.
Perfect, I am so very hungry.
By Ysmir, that smells divine.
Just a quick drink.
What luck … fresh blood!
Something's not right with this place.
Troll's blood! This ruin is cursed!
By Ysmir's beard!
What in Mara's name is happening here?
Kill anything you see!
Damned Dwarves!
The fool wants to die.
Leave their bodies as a lesson.
Another fool challenges us!
These whelps are finished.
Kill the flat-head!
So much for those s'wits.
What is wrong with this place?
Where are these things coming from?
Stay clear of the shining lights!
Ysmir's beard! What's happening to this place?
Die by fang and claw!
Calm down. They're dead.
Kill the intruder!
Disgraceful — no challenge at all.
Ah, my dear, come get yourself warm! Perhaps fill your grumbling tummy with some of my spiced mudcrab buns?
Make sure you got the right kind of curry comb. Seen some bad quality ones of late. Keeping your mount's fur clean is important, especially if you're always on the road.
We got the nasty bloodsucker!
Looks like it's our lucky day! Two in a row!
I almost wish we'd made it suffer longer.
Another one! Kill it!
We did it! The fanged freak is dead!
Another vampire! Kill it!
Disgusting … these monsters should be eradicated.
You'll die just like your friend here!
Idiot … that thing should have known it couldn't take us on.
A second vampire! Get it!
Those fangs are truly hideous.
Shall we kill this one too?
This one quite enjoys killing bloodsuckers.
This one will enjoy your death, vampire filth!
This one enjoys killing these filthy vampires.
Did we kill your friend, bloodsucker?
This one died quickly. Perhaps it had not fed in some time.
A second one? You will suffer the same fate.
Disgusting vampire.
This one will die like the first.
We got the savage brute!
Come to avenge your kind, mongrel?
Dumac take you, beast!
A second werewolf to kill? Lovely.
Blood and faith! That beast almost took my arm!
Another mongrel! Get it!
These dogs are even uglier dead than they are alive.
Looks like this one had a friend!
Dead. Just the way I like my werewolves.
Did we kill your friend, mongrel?
We will cleanse these curs from here. It is our duty.
You will suffer the same fate as your kin!
This one loves the smell of freshly spilled beast blood.
Another? How exciting.
What a terrible fate, this one cannot imagine.
Another beast! Let's kill it.
A fitting end for a monster.
Another beast comes to challenge us. How foolish.
I like killing werewolves, their bones make nice sounds.
Another mongrel. Kill it.
Sovngarde take you!
Kill the stranger!
You underestimate us, stranger.
Would you like to die, too?
Good, I wasn't done killing.
This fool wants to challenge us!
Let us kill this intrusion.
Monster or no, you die the same!
I will make your death swift.
Kill this fool!
Behold my power in every shadow!
Feel the lightning's wrath!
Behold, my banquet!
Foolish!
Get your dirty paws off my equipment you animal!
Restraining countermeasure charging.
To Oblivion with you!
Why would you do this to our people?
You seem to be on the right track!
No, not that. Try something else.
A wise, but futile gesture.
Wares like these are hard to find in Skyrim. Especially during an invasion.
Like my Pa always said, "Buy what you can while you can." We'll all be dead sooner or later.
I will work with the others, but I do not trust them.
Medallions, more of them.
We will need more supplies for the medallions.
Old Nord ruins are impressively strong.
We should step up patrols with the visitor present.
We are so very close.
We cannot fall behind schedule!
We must train hard for the upcoming battles.
Faolan's blood shall lead us.
We need to be ready when the time comes.
We'll need more bodies for the next ritual.
Wish we could sleep on beds and not piles of hay.
I don't trust these witches, they are not like us.
We will be rewarded for our service.
The harrowed grow restless.
The ritual improves with every iteration.
The end approaches swiftly. We must hurry.
More crates arrive every day.
You continue to disappoint me, child.
Destroy them, my guardians!
You shall fall before my power!
Is it flesh? Yes. Drink it up.
This won't last forever! Hit him as hard as you can!
The power of my blood brings you life!
I command an army of stone!
Try not to die too quickly.
Don't be shy. It's almost time for dinner.
Let loose your blood!
Delicious!
You cannot run!
Come to me morsel!
What inferior taste!
Caught you in my trap!
I enjoy playing with a meal.
It's good to see you again. Were you successful in the task I appointed you?
I look forward to your safe return. With your efforts, we can improve our relationships with the local clans.
I could use your help, if you have the time. Your talents might be perfect for a job I need done.
I appreciate your help. \n\nI don't have anything else at the moment, but I'm sure I'll need your services again. Seek me out later.
You've returned. What of your task?
We gave you a job. Get to it.
Want to prove yourself to Ard Caddach? Put your skills toward the good of the Reach. There's a reward in it from the Markarth vaults if you're interested.
The Stonehands appreciate your help, outsider. We'll have more work for you soon.
Wither!
Mortals.
Whatever he's doing is getting to me! Shut him up!
Looks like more storm-summoning jackals are out and about. Time to gut them all.
No reports of harrowstorms on the horizon, which is just how I like it. Keep your eyes and ears open. There'll be more work tomorrow.
If you're worried about your payment, don't be. Reachfolk keep our word. Now go keep yours and disrupt a harrowstorm.
I see before me someone with a look that says you've committed great deeds. You deal with those storm summoners?
So, you wish to meet destruction?
Not in there, either. Ugh, Verandis! Why are you so good at hiding things?
Now which is more conductive …? You! Hahaha!
I can produce this counter agent all day!
Got critters after you!
Time for you to bulk up! Drink this!
Better, but sloppy. Again!
Die to feed the darkness!
I'm surprised that's lasted all this time.
I don't think we're going to pry him out easily, but a giant werewolf might pop that jar of his.
Watch out for those shock-things taking root! Maybe you can shake them loose?
JB TABLE TEST 1c
JB TABLE TEST 2c
JB TABLE TEST3c
I don't care if they are our guests. The werewolves need to stop shedding in the lab.
Hear about that explosion yesterday? No, another one.
I've been itching for a fight! Least I hope that's what it was.
Hey! Keep out of the laboratory!
Arkasis is going to change the world. Into what, I don't know.
They say the first step to learning alchemy is to start putting things in your mouth.
You can't stop progress!
I've been meaning to try this poison!
Good job! Let's find another ward crystal.
The blood tastes fresher when they are scared.
Something about Argonian blood tastes off to me.
The wood from Skyrim makes the strongest bows.
The Lady deserves our trust and our blades.
Even I get lost when walking around this castle.
Even hunting rats would be more fun than this.
Our blessing will kill them all. Slowly.
We shall bleed you dry!
Why are these histories so boring? This one hoped to spend the day reading about exciting times, but these are full of nothing but political facts and figures. Makes Biro's head hurt!
Your death shall not be quiet!
Interlopers? In our Lady's home?
Our Lady demands a feast!

Sometimes scholars disappear for hours on end. To look for books and such things, of course.\n\nDo not be concerned if Biro isn't here the next time you look. This one has scholarly pursuits to … pursue.
Oh, you live here, too? This is much nicer than those dumps in the Stitches. Much less excrement in the corners.\n\nExcept that one. Sorry.
Bring on the blood!
Get back! That one's mine!
Time for extreme measures!

No matter where I travel, it's the same every time. Shave-skins flock to me, babbling in squeaky idiot voices. "Ooo, who dressed up this pretty little kitty?"\n\nFeh! Do Khajiit not wear clothes where they come from?
Why do people keep offering me mice? Is it customary to bring a guest a flea-ridden rodent in this part of the world?
Did you know that people outside the Reach actually pay others to hunt for them and dress their meat? \n\nLaziness knows no bounds!
Wine, ale, and mead. Wine, ale, and mead. Doesn't anyone around here know how to press a good cider?
No fighting or spitting, got it?
Look what I found on the Mages Guild shelves! It's a genealogy of the Anequina monarchs. There are hundreds of entries to—\n\nWait, you're not listening to me, are you?
Historical vandalism! The author of this piece cited his sources in the absolutely wrong format!\n\nWhat do they teach at the universities these days, I wonder?
What can I do for you?
Welcome!
Yes! Fight!
Feel my teeth!
Argh!
[irritated grunts while searching for something]
[slow groaning babble that indicates she's bored and wants excitement]
[Goblin babble calling out for allies]
[defiant Goblin gibberish refusing to allow player to pass]
The longer you delay, the more certain Encratis will find the book.
You think you know what you seek, but its power is beyond you!
No one will ever find you down here in the ashes!
Naught but cinders, now!
<<Heavy coughing, hacking.>>
<<Heavy coughing, hacking.>>
Drop those pitiful weapons so I can show you to your cage!
You dare! You will reap what you've sewn here today!
Into the stone pits!
Dead. Your bones will go to use.
There, let's hope this holds.
I should have left you as scraps!
Those are perfect.
Perfect, that's just what we need.
There, those are what we need.
Met Ard Caddach once. The Despot of Markarth, you know. That man's eyes'll cut through you like an apple. You don't want him as an enemy. Trust me.
Take it from a carver of wood: Always say a word to the spirit of the tree before chopping. And always plant a new tree in the fallen tree's place. Else you'll suffer.
The ard always has a kind word for me when he passes through. Known him forever, it seems. Others might fear him, but not me.
I can't believe five years have passed since I first astonished the Blackoath clan with my leatherworking secrets!\n\nI'm eager to see if you can match my skill!
Pilbira loves working with runestones. She loves playing with them even more. Except that one time.\n\nLet us not talk about that.

Few Reachmen are farmers. I have to pay dearly to import my produce from lands where people are content to spend their days with their hands in the dirt.\n\nMy wares are as fresh as any you'll find in Markarth, though.
I've heard that the Black-Moon clan is waylaying travelers in the hills outside of Markarth. Better not venture beyond the walls without some form of armor to turn their arrows.
Some clans love learning new things. Others see new things as a curse. Hard to tell which clan is which until the latter tries to cut your tongue out.
Did you know that the Stranglehollow clan, now deceased, used to toast each other with a drink mixed using the fingerbone of an ancestor?
Not a lot of trade is coming in recently. Having to get creative with what's at hand. Interest you in some weeviled-corn surprise or withered beet with drippings? Get 'em while they last!
Reachfolk are many peoples, each following their own paths. We're more like a quilt crafted by many hands—each with their own design—than a wool blanket of one color.
At last, a customer of refinement!\n\nEducated buyers like you often drive a hard bargain, but at least I'm spared from having to explain why I can't accept elk antlers as payment.
Most of my wares are blooded. Just don't ask whose blood.

So much blood spilled in the Reach. It feeds the trees, but haunts the woods. Bones rest amid roots. There's strong magic to be found in the wood of trees watered by blood, eh?\n\nHave a look at my staves and bows. You'll see.
A Druadach mountain bear saved my life when I was a child. The Reachfolk here call me Bear-Blessed as a result.\n\nNow, what can this bear-blessed merchant get you?
I can't abide people who fill their days with a sour temper. Like burrs, their manners catch on to all in their path. Bad for business, that is.
Reachfolk have a variety of markings, based on their clan. I'm here to see them all. Hoping to get inspired for my work back home.
You know what I love? Seeing happy customers! So let's put a smile on both our faces, eh?
Rest assured that your funds and gear are safe here with us. Our martial and magical protective skills are at your service!
Reachfolk deposits tend to be … odoriferous, but you needn't worry about your valuables being contaminated. I keep a tidy house.
Take my advice. In the Reach, it is best to travel as light and lean as a blade of grass. My pouches can help you in this.
The Reach holds a beauty of its own. The people, the terrain, the music, the flora and fauna. The bracing air. The scent of pines. The sound of water on stone.\n\nAll of it inspires me.
Don't ask a Hagraven about crossbreeding mounts. I did once. She misunderstood my meaning and cursed me to never have children, sadly.

Several Alfiq wanted to come here with me—to escape the Dragons, you see—but I warned them of the likelihood that they'd be treated like housecats.\n\nThey flipped their tails in irritation and went somewhere else.
No offense, but can we conclude our business quickly? I have to get back to my research!
Been doing odd jobs since I got here. Not a bad place, overall. So many clans, so many differences. Makes so many opportunities for a mercenary like me.
The echos of what was and the howls of what is both echo through Markarth. Stay resolute, and you will find the calm waters between them.
Looking to travel to more civilized country, no doubt. I can take you to any Alliance capital, quick as a wink. Reachfolk here can attest to my skills—even steered a few through a blizzard once!

It's not good for Reachfolk to live in stone houses built by long-dead Dwarves. It changes your way of seeing things.\n\nI said as much to Ard Caddach, but he ignored me. Loves his great stone house too much.
The thing I love about losing my memory after having my head banged up? Freedom from whatever regrets I might have piled up in my life. What I hate? The headaches slay me.
Those two High Elf bankers we have here? The one reminds me of a hawk. She's got a predator's instinct, quick to strike. Her brother is more like a fox. Clever, and happy in his den.
The Reachmen love their stone knives and animal skins. You, though? You look for something more rare.\n\nLet us try to find what you desire, all right?
I'd tell you all about Markarth, but I've been a bit stuck. Here. Selling things.\n\nProbably safer, to be honest. What can I say? I'm a talker!
You have never seen such firm and luscious melons as the ones I handle.\n\nIf you are interested in melons such as these, I can check my guild's stock for you!
Fishing. I miss it. Dug up plenty of worms for bait back when we wandered freely.\n\nBeing here? Stale. Smells strange.
I traveled all around Skyrim, and it didn't feel as cold as this place. Something about it … bad Dwarven craftsmanship? Dwarf ghosts?
I admit—before coming to the Reach, I heard much about its clans that made me think they'd kill me on sight. Makes one wonder what else we know about the world around us is false ….
This one came to Markarth to learn of the Reach clans and make a profit. Alas, the profit part of his plan trapped this one here.\n\nPerhaps you have fared better?
So, you've still got both hands. You're faring better than half the thieves in Markarth, believe me.\n\nNow, let's see what you brought me.
Unlike some shadow organizations, the Thieves Guild folk are more supportive overall. They won't do things like send you after your own sister.\n\nThere. I said it. Are you happy now, sis?
Been to Solitude's refuge? My colleague there pulled a prank on me years ago when I was just starting out. If he's complaining about his hair, that was me. Left him a return favor!
These hills make the craggy paths of Wrothgar look like an Imperial rose garden. You'll need what I'm selling to survive. Believe me.
You're more likely to fall afoul of a vampire than a Reach warrior right now. And, better, that Reach warrior might just be an ally instead of an enemy.
You're lucky you came across me here, freehand. I don't pass this way very often.\n\nNow, what's your business today? How can I help you?
The stones here have so many secrets to keep. It overwhelms me sometimes.

Z'en brings us many gifts, my friend, if you're willing to earn them honestly and hold to your bargains. Thus I work to bring some more nature to this graveyard of stone and water.\n\nIt's hard work, but it brings me joy each day.
As of yesterday, the Timberclaw clan made full peace with the Starsingers while moving to a more uncertain footing with the Skyweavers.\n\nI believe a pet chicken caused this change.

My father once served in the Reach for the Mages Guild. I rarely saw him, but when I did, he had such tales!\n\nI came out here to see some of what he saw firsthand, though what with all this harrowstorm business, I'm stuck in Markarth for now.

The Shunned Ones appreciate good tales. When faced with starvation, I watched them from hiding, listening. Learning that their preferred currency is tales told of mistakes and lessons, I spun many a tale, asking only for food in return.
Some here find the range of behaviors exhibited by the Reach clans fascinating.\n\nI would prefer they all had better manners, myself.

Clans are not above asking for help despite the rumors to the contrary. In fact, the reason I'm here is because one starving clan sought my aid. I gladly lent my gold to fulfill their provisioning needs in return for entry into this impressive city!

I know nothing of games of chance—my clan believes they simply summon bad luck to those playing. One of our number played one just the other day, and we haven't seen her since. We think a fell spirit got her.

Some of these Reachfolk are terrible gamblers. I've beaten more than I can count at various games—and fights, for that matter!\n\nThink I even saw Ard Caddach himself give me a nod of respect after that last thrashing. Teeth everywhere.

You believe firmly in the idea that one is responsible for one's own choices, yes? This one is glad to have met a clan that embraces this concept. They brought me here, in fact.\n\nThey might have killed the clan I was traveling with first, though ….

Beware the Shadefeathers if you mean to go beyond Markarth. They kidnap travelers and use them for their bloody rituals. They'll even murder other Reachfolk that they find alone.\n\nEvery hand in the Reach is turned against them.

Before you think about spewing vitriol about those harrow-mad werewolves, make sure you limit your cursing to just that lot. We've some of Hircine's blessed in our clan. They don't take kindly to insults.
One clan refuses to learn to write. They believe that if they write down a word, they lose power over it.\n\nWhat power do they have over birds now? Or cats? Nobody has power over cats.

I learned from my aunt that the Reachfolk weren't one solid group of bad people as some of my friends told me, and she's right.\n\nSome I'd avoid, certainly, but others are warm-hearted people with a joy for life.

Each night, the clan I came here with plies me with cider. I distracted a Daedric-worshiping clan long enough for them to sneak past and get here safely.\n\nI would vastly prefer more knowledge of clan traditions since I don't care for cider.
Look to your own, I say. Fight to keep those you hold in your heart safe. Kill any who do harm to you or yours. What more law does a Reachman need than that?
You've not lived until you've climbed to the top of this place and looked down.\n\nJust don't be a dolt about it and act like you're going to push someone else over. That'll get you killed here.
Sometimes when you work yourself into a sweat, you just need to pause and breathe.\n\nIn those moments, savor your life.
Those rebels! Fools! What are they rebelling against really?\n\nDo they even know?
I lost my sister in the storm. I miss her, but life is meant to be a struggle, so I must endure. \n\nI know it's what she would have wanted.
I smell changes ahead for the Reach. There's more on the wind than just vampires and werewolves and their short-sighted plans.

My best deerskin breeches have gone missing. If you spot someone wearing pants that don't seem to fit them right, let me know. I'll handle it from there.\n\nIt's just not right for Reachmen to steal from Reachmen.
They call me the bird woman around here because I know all the birds in these hills by feather, nest, or call.\n\nIt comes in useful sometimes. Not nearly as often as I'd like.

Yes, I know how to read. What of it? My father served Emperor Moricar in Cyrodiil and insisted that I learn my letters when he returned to Markarth. Blame it on him.\n\nMy blunt tongue, I blame on my mother.

Clans die, you know. I once belonged to a clan that got killed by another. Their witches did something to me. Used me in a ritual with the others they captured. I've not been the same since that day. Everything feels duller.

Clans don't normally remain in one place for long, and everything a wanderer carries must be worth its weight. Our art possesses beauty and purpose.\n\nI've killed five raiders with one carving alone.
The spirit of the Reach thrives because of clan differences. Ard Caddach's wish to bring us together slowly kills that spirit.

Whoever said the Skyweavers actually fly is out of their head. No Reachfolk can fly.\n\nThey took their name from their weatherworking skills. Everyone knows that except for the dunderheaded fool spreading lies.

If my experiences here in Markarth are any indication, so-called civilization can eat rabbit droppings mixed with durzog offal.\n\nToo many people in too close a space with too many ideas and not enough to occupy them.
Well, these roads can feel quite lonely. Don't you agree?

So, being a Nord in the Reach? Not the best thing to be. That's why I'm hiding out here. I'm hoping to figure out a way past the Reachfolk, then through the vampires, and the werewolves, and then ….\n\nThis is making my head hurt.

Laughter. So much laughter. The Reachfolk laugh. The dead laugh. The Daedra laugh.\n\nI wish it would stop. Not even when we got to Markarth. Then I found a way out. To here. Not really freedom. Now the stones laugh at me instead.
Keep an eye out for vampires and werewolves.\n\nI mean the bad ones. Harrowed? Something like that. They're everywhere, it seems.
Tell enough people no enough times and they start to resent you for it. Better to leave them behind before they grind that little one-sided grudge to a sharp point.
Your meat must be tender by now.
Works as designed.
Foul thing! Burn!
I'm keeping an eye on any buckets I see. Every now and again I still get a whiff of whatever I was drenched with back in the Stitches.\n\nMaybe one of Vole's degreasers would help.

Remember Tasnasi? I miss her. Yes, I said it. Even if she can be a stick in the mud, she's my friend. Then she left. They always do.\n\nIf you leave, I'm staying here. I'm used to this place and it smells like me.
Tell me about your latest discovery, my friend! Let me live vicariously through your explorations as an antiquarian. I envy your ability to do real archeology!
Ah, guild-mate! Do you happen to know of a good fence nearby? Biro has some … scholarly research he needs to unload and would like to not be unduly cheated.

Don't look at me like that. I'm nothing like my sisters in the Icereach Coven.\n\nFirst of all, I would never bow down to a vampire. Second, when it's time for me to kill someone, I won't be subtle about it.
I think the armor they gave me is too small.
Ah! Competition!
I can't remember what Encratis said it looked like.
You go no further!
Look up there, between the columns. Do you see that portal?
She's drawing power. Use the portals!
My father the Skald-King always says, "Guests are like rabbit meatballs. Too few and you're never satisfied. Too many and you want to throw up."
Have I thanked the owner of this fine establishment lately? No? Ah, well. Remind me about that later.
Evil vampires, good vampires … it's all so confusing! But you say this Ravenwatch helped you defeat the Gray Host? Very well. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt.\n\nFor now.
Princess Svana has grown to be an impressive woman. She will make a fine jarl. Perhaps even a fine queen. I hope this moment of friendship lasts. I would hate to count her as an enemy.

The Skald-King and I owe you a great debt for what you did in Eastmarch, my friend. Not only did you stop my crazed uncle, you saved my father's life. Believe me, I want to avoid the throne for as many years as I can. It's quite uncomfortable.

Adusa is always on the lookout for good places to rest between missions. This is a good place, I think. Yes, Adusa approves. This will make a fine safehouse for the Ravenwatch. But you never heard that name. To you, Adusa is just a houseguest, yes?
We may be vampires, five-claw, but we are not slaves to our affliction. We can rise above it. Use our gifts for the greater good.\n\nThat is the way of the Ravenwatch.

Ravenwatch Castle stands empty most of the time these days. The Ravenwatch is too few and the threats too many. We cannot afford even a moment's respite. \n\nStill, Adusa is happy for this visit. I wish to hear all about your latest adventures.
This one can hardly believe it. The legends were true. There really is a vast underground realm beneath the surface of Skyrim. It does make a perfect hiding place for nests of evil vampires, though.
This one never expected to save Skyrim and the Reach from an army of vampires and werewolves, but the Ravenwatch goes wherever our mission takes us.\n\nAs do you, five-claw. As do you.

Being Undaunted isn't all that impressive. For the most part, we're a bit soft. Fancy tents, extravagant libations. Few of us know real hardship. I mean, I've had to weave nether-garments with my own hair to keep my jibblies from freezing off!

Don't let the rest of the Undaunted feed you that guar spew about how armor makes the fighter. They traipse about like little lordlings in their bewitched britches.\n\nBah! A real warrior charges in bare as the day they were born!

Dungeon delvers? Why limit ourselves to just dungeons? There are more adventures out there than just what's inside ruins and barrows.\n\nNot that it matters. Few new recruits last very long. Figure you'll be dead inside a week, give or take.

Still running Bolgrul's piddly errands? You want to make a name for yourself, it's the Pledges that will win you glory. Complete two or three hundred of those and your standing will rise so high that I'll finally let you polish my boots.

You've seen it all? A real Undaunted would go back and see it again. But this time blindfolded and with both arms tied behind their back!\n\nThe expression, took a licking? I invented it when I killed a troll with my tongue! What have you done lately?
The Dark Heart is depleted! Slay more of the Gray Host to fill it!
I crave blood, yet it does not sate me.
Why have we been forsaken?
Blood, I miss its coppery taste.
The Void sustains me.
Dark Heart, why do you remain silent?
Must feed ….
Lady Belain? Are you there?
The Void, it calls to me.
That's the wrong way. Find me when you return.
I don't know if I trust Caddach. Excuse me, Ard Caddach. What's his game?
Caddach has a lot of ideas. Not everyone in the Reach is behind him, but I say it's about time. When's the last time we had a leader who admitted he might be ready to learn a new trick or two?
The portals, I opened them for you!
Never thought I'd live this long. They say Reachfolk don't die in bed, but here I am.
I thought my father would be safer here with me. Less trouble for his aching bones. \n\nI should have let him be.
A lot of Reachfolk in Markarth these days. Sure, we have some brawls, now and again.\n\nStill, most of the clans that chose to answer the ard's call are willing to work together. For now.
Reachfolk get restless hiding behind stone walls. At least, I always thought so. But many I've met here seem fine with it. \n\nCould be I was wrong.
A chance to study the Dwarven ruins of Markarth? You bet I volunteered.

Until I came here, I assumed Reachmen were just like Nords, just angrier. But I learned a lot of interesting things in Markarth. Reachfolk are very attuned to nature and the cycle of the seasons. I can understand that.
I know, I know. You are surprised to see a Redguard here in the Reach. But I am a trader, and my business takes me to many different places.
The Redguard was wise enough to know he shouldn't just wander the Reach without an escort. \n\nMost clans are suspicious of outsiders. Some are downright murderous.
Our guide, Nevaen? She's actually rather nice. Everyone says the Reachfolk are all barbarians, but I don't think that's true.
I've seen Ard Caddach himself walking about. Always has half a dozen of his Stonehands at his back. Feh.
Who are you? Wait. I don't care who you are.
This tunnel must be the work of thralls. Few vampires would stoop to perform such labor.
We Nords are a proud race. Proud of our accomplishments. Proud of our heritage.\n\nAnd our mead. We're especially proud of that.
Goodbye, wretch.

Khajiit beverages are among the finest in the land. You will find nothing more satisfying than a glass of plum brandy or a snifter of Dark Moons spiced whiskey.\n\nUnless you are a vampire like Adusa. Then nothing tastes better than fresh blood.

And that was when Adusa said, "May your fur fall out and never grow back, you tailless gutter rat!" And did he laugh? Giggle? Even so much as smirk? No.\n\nSometimes, this one thinks her sharp wit is wasted on the villains she fights.
The Ashen Lord calls you to serve!
Your death will make me stronger!
The darkness, it flows through my blood!
We've already had trouble with one trespasser. Remember, he might not have come alone.
For the Ashen Lord!
Fool! When one falls, another takes their place!
You think to challenge us, outsider?
If we die this day we shall live forever!
I see you survived to fight another day. That is good. How did you fare in your task?
Our enemies surround us, waiting in the dark. Remind them that the Reach still has its defenders.
I don't sleep much. Not anymore. But it's a price I'm willing to pay if it means a child of the Reach dreams of better days to come.\n\nCome back later. I'll have a task for you.
The Reach needs protectors now more than ever. That's why the Wayward Guardians are here. Would you care to aid us?
You brought this upon yourself when you resisted the Gray Host!
I will never fight alongside vampire scum!
Reach savages! Show them no mercy!
If I have to rip apart one more Dwarven sphere ….
How many do you think we lost in Markarth?
The Ashen Lord has a plan, doesn't he?
Where's Lady Belain? Where's the Ashen Lord?
Did we know the Reachfolk had their own werewolves?
Where's Rada al-Saran? Where's Lady Belain?
Our losses were heavier than expected. Much heavier.
Why did we retreat? We could have destroyed Markarth.
If I never see another Dwarven ruin, it will be too soon.
Markarth was supposed to be ours for the taking.
Bah. Let the Reachfolk have this place!
They told us the Reach was vulnerable. So how did we get beaten?
I say we regroup and attack again!
A shame to destroy all this knowledge.
Feel the savage power I wield!
Someone got into my potion stash.
Do you even know who you battle?
That one is mine!
Can't believe we marched all this way for a library.
Why would Goblins work with Minotaurs anyway?
I bring your end!
The crackle … the heat … the light … it speaks.
You shall bear our scars!
A spark here. A spark there. A spark here. A spark there.
Meet my friends!
Use the portal, harrier!
Your spirit will be mine!
I feel … so empty.
Surrounded by emptiness!
The void offers strength!
These wounds mean nothing!
My destruction pleases the Exalted!
The forge never stops!
So you come to battle the champion of Molag Bal?
I shall return!
The servants of Mehrunes Dagon await!
An inferno rises within!
Come now, let us dance!
It has pride after all!
Pick yourself up, now! Let us dance once more!
Pick a bloodfiend for the celebration.
Why do we have to patrol this level? The prisoners aren't going anywhere.
What's tonight's entertainment? Have you heard?
Sure the boss is powerful. But he's also a little touched in the head.
Are we going on another raid? I like raids!
A true vampire shouldn't have to patrol the Deep Tombs. It's degrading.
I wonder if Boss Trenlor will share some of the good stuff tonight.
I know there are more Hillhunters out there. We should run them to the ground.
Turning these Hillhunter cowards into Briarhearts is more than they deserve.
I told the Hagravens these wanderers would make poor soil for their crop.
Keep out of the crypts. The Draugr are restless.
Enough with the sacrifices and the mumbling over ritual fires. I'm ready for a fight.
I don't see why we can't have a little sport before we plant them. Right?
I don't care for being at a Hagraven's beck and call. Where's our chief in all this?
These are dark days. No one argues that.
We should join the others below.
Is it time yet? Is it time?
What have I been summoned for? What is this place?
This place … I know it now. Ah, they should not have brought me here.
Are the werewolves to be next? It might be best to see them off while we have the numbers to overpower them.
I wish there was another way.
What do you think? Could we add some Gray Host to the ritual? They're here, aren't they?
The Spirit Queen is here. Can't you feel her presence in the shadows?
Can you believe it? We're part of an ancient army!
This land … I can't believe we need something in this place.
Stay focused or you'll answer to the Ashen Lord!
For the Ashen Lord!
For blood and glory!
These Reachfolk are no match for my claws.
Ripped the arm right off! You should have been there.
I'll tear out their hearts and swallow them whole!
You say the enemy, I say dinner.
The Dark Heart's becoming a prize fought over by upstarts and outsiders. I do not like it.
I have some ideas about how the Nighthollow can survive this setback. Thrive, even.
Why are we attacking that location again?
I've never been more grateful to be numb to the cold.
I was never partial to my old life anyway.
I do miss the desert sands of home, but the sun was deadly there even before my tranformation.
Remind me to tell you the legend of Leki's Blade sometime.
Can't say I like working with the Nighthollow clan. Give me the creeps.
My old clan would be considered positively wretched compared to the Gray Host. Joining was the best thing I've ever done.
I guess I do feel a little bad for the mortals … but somebody's got to be the food.
Ugh, I can't believe I used to be one of those cowering livestock, reeking of piss and fear.
You require my blessing before harming this creature.
Tear the strength to fight from this mortal!
Your efforts fail without the blessing!
This shell brings your death!
You show too much weakness for the hunt.
I call on the grove to aid me!
Your bones shall fall to dust.
[sharp moo of anger]
He may have insulted your combat prowess.
I think he just mocked your heritage.
The power of the Dark Heart is mine!
Bah! I have more than enough power to deal with you.
The darkness, it flows through me!
Coward! Return and face me!
Do not wilt from this challenge, hunter.
I think the clouds are turning. We should prepare for a stormy night.
Have faith. The gods won't lead us astray.
It's too quiet. Nothing exciting ever happens around here.
Spirits, hear us! Hagravens, protect us!
And then I turned that ugly Nord into a newt!
Drown in the blood of your betters.
I'm going to savor killing you.
Bring Rada to the soul trap!
Watch out, partner!
I'll draw the boundaries of my kingdom with your blood.
A frigid death is more merciful than you deserve.
How dare you turn the souls of those you betrayed against me!
Keep sending souls to the Dark Heart! We're almost there!
We've fed the Dark Heart enough! Lead Rada this way!
Slow and clumsy cattle.
The soft part of your skull makes the perfect target.
[sly Goblin gibberish taunting the player]
[proud Goblin declaring strength]
[Goblin nervously attacking the player like please don't hurt me]
[frustrated Goblin gibberish about how minotaur smell bad]
[sly Goblin gibbering that he's tracking the player down]
[Goblin babble bragging about the huge size of the animal he killed]
[excited Goblin babble telling best friend to attack]
[Goblin gibberish declaring she's the most powerful]
Fight me, you tusking coward!
Time to prove your worth!
Don't tell me you're a coward, runt!
You are no coward! Prove yourself!
You must be afraid to die by my hand!
Here, my lord! The finest swill in all the land!
Here, king, king, king! Got your favorite!
Who wants to eat their weight in apple mush?
Come back here, you coward!
Anyone outside Markarth's walls is fair game! What say you?
We hunt with the spirits tonight. May they guide our arrows to the mark!
A storm's in the air. I can smell it.
You look like you need something. Maybe I can help?
Monsters? Villains? What's the trouble?
The day will be ours!
Sheathe your weapons. The battle is won!
Keep your gods close and you have nothing to fear.
Reachmen aren't so different from Orcs. Gotta fight for everything we have.
Gods have mercy!
Come on, you filthy tuskers!
You must try harder than that!
Use this oil to guide Lyranth's power!
That mess you're making will be useless if you don't hurry.
You will be unmade!
To me, mortal! Let my power course through you!
Feel the pain course through you!
You've heard of the plans, yes? After the ritual? Delightful.
Your little rescue ends here!
The more of these creatures we summon, the safer I feel.
Dance for me!
You're mine!
Keep her off me!
I'll handle these!
Get up! We aren't finished yet!
The peace of destruction.
Inconsequential bugs.
Only the finest heartwood for my staves.
Intruders? Not now!
We shall open the way for a new world!
I'll return with more of that black ooze.
Such simple mortals.
This is just the beginning. After this comes so much more.
Presenting, the Emperor of Effluence, the Patron of Porkers, the Saint of Swine: King Boar!
It's Prince Boar the Third! Or is that the Tenteenth?
King Boar requires assistance, my Prince!
Ugh! Gods! It got in my eye! What? What? The king is dead? Oh, good for them, get me a towel!
Many soups can come from a single broth. Swamp eel broth goes well with vegetables, fish, meat, and maggots. But not horker. Never horker!

My soups are works of art. They aren't meant for the hungry or the curious. Such masterpieces are destined for true connoisseurs. For those who can truly appreciate my skills and talent.\n\nIn other words … this soup isn't for you!
Cake baking bears no resemblance to making soup. All those powders and so much measuring! And I do not understand the flavor. Soups can be sweet, so why can't cakes be savory? I am dry with vexation.
A fellow provisioner and passionate about food, too? We must exchange recipes! My soups and I could use a fresh perspective.\n\nNot too fresh, mind you. I wouldn't want to do anything crazy.

I erect the spine of awe. Your reputation as a provisioner inspires countless lesser cooks. Even a cook such as I finds myself impressed at your accomplishments. I contemplate expanding my repertoire, but why deny the world my delicious soups?
Where do they keep the implements of torture? As long as I'm here, I might as well indulge in some recreational bloodletting.

No, I am not imprisoned within this domicile, despite the predicaments you found me in in the past. I am merely here to … how do you mortals say it? To see how the other half lives?\n\nSo far, I am not impressed.

Wards. I can't abide such magic, especially when employed against me. \n\nLittle mortal, as much as I appreciate your efforts to break the wards on my behalf, the very fact that I required your assistance … it galls me. I'm sure you understand.
I've been thinking about why I became involved with the Order of the Waking Flame. Mother always worried I would scandalize the family in front of the neighbors. I guess I decided to prove her right.
I really thought that joining a secret Daedric cult would get me invited to more interesting parties. Not so much.
