Messy one, aren't you? Get cleaned up and then we'll talk.
Hand over your coins, even if they stink as badly as you do.
Your integrity has spared you your life.
Get back here!
Do not take one more step!
Enjoy your fleeting freedom.
I can what see you're doing, Nirnling.
Learn better techniques thief!
That was excellent. Do that again!
What will we ever do with you ill-behaved mortals?
Even without laws, I'd report you for that poor execution.
Is this how you spend your time?
I don't have time for this.
This is fascinating! Carry on mortal.
Where's the--? They're going to tear my ears off.
I should slit your throat for the insult of thinking I'm an easy mark.
You're terrible at sneaking where you don't belong.
Either you get out of here, or I'll throw you out in pieces!
You attract too much attention.
This city defiled itself when it let mortals in.
Some advice, mortal? Stick to the shadows until you can stand the light.
Innovative magics in Fargrave. Keep an eye out or you might lose it.
Every time I think I'm used to Fargrave, I am hit with another patch of dryness.
Those spider people in Skein Row invited me to rest in their webs.
Standing in front of these orbs is supposed to rid you of your aches.
The Prince of Destruction will see to this sullied city! Fire take you all.
Misted Mourning has the cheapest Daze in Fargrave. But that's my den. Find your own.
With so many races, Fargrave is starting to look like a Tamrielic city.
I am not a guide. But a trip to the Bearer's Rest is standard advice for all newcomers.

Your kind may call me a Dark Seducer, but I have very particular tastes when it comes to pleasure and pain. If I happen to see you again at the Bearer's Rest, perhaps I'll make some time to demonstrate.
The Stricture protects everyone in Fargrave, mortals included.
Why must you interrupt?
This is the best tavern in the city. I've tried them all.
Watch where you walk or I'll smash your fragile body.
I am not generally considered … friendly. Vex me and you'll see why.
Street medicine is not great, but Redmaiden works for the pactless.
That pack merchant sells second-rate pouches for full price. The nerve!
Tomes, potions, vials, and candles. What activities does this stall presume are usual undertakings?
Mortals do not know their stations!
Fargrave is the city where you can expand your horizons. Do so.
I have stood here for a long time and have yet to be hit by a book.
Apologies. You damage our reputation. We'd rather feed this body to a Flesh Atronach.
Shh! I got to concentrate.
Dibella finds us all. I've even known Daedra to dance with her once.
Hey! Get Vre out of this cage you tall child!
I'm not working right now. If you need anything, find me later.
Don't get underfoot here. You might be stepped on.
Hmm. Mortal. Death must affect how you experience existence.
Age grants many virtues. Patience, however, is learned.
A mortal scholar presumes to know more than I. Do not be like her.
I walk by these on my errands. I'd never allow myself to be caged.
You think you can look at my work? Get out!
Hold your tongue and don't complain. Laws do not change overnight.
Lord Dagon's disasters are a blessing.
All hail Mehrunes Dagon, the Prince of Flood and Fire!
Why do we hide when we should attack our foes?
Who can I sacrifice to Lord Dagon today?
What was that? Did you hear something?
This is all part of Sister Celdina's plan.
No one is more devoted to the order than me.
Use this time of waiting for prayer. Reflection.
This one is nothing. Only a vessel for Merrunz.
Let the Daedra rage outside. Our temple is safe.
How can we complete our holy work while we hide here?
Free advice—there are some goods that you can only sell in the Shambles.
My skill is wasted on crafting brooches engraved with some family crest.
There must be a quiet way to kill mortals.
How do mortals do everything they want in such short times?
Out of my sight! You taint the visage of the temple.
These walls want Ux to feel small. They fail.
Brimstone rain down upon your house!
Mortals. Their lights are snuffed so quickly.
Living in a city of portals is exhilarating. One never knows what might turn up in the Bazaar.
Spread like fire in a dry forest, minions of Dagon!
I have been told that the trick is to drink it all at once.
Mortals. Always asking for directions.
When you return to Nirn, tell them you met Lentylmo. They'll know who I am.
Send me now! I want to eviscerate them all!
I serve the will of the Lord of Flood and Fire!
Any Nirnbound who raises an insipid hand to me will find it cut off at the wrist.
I was looking for something unique, but these thrice-cursed Daedra won't part with their pets!
Hmph. I only speak to those who enrich my existence. But no one has brought me anything new.
Ser's skill exceeds anything this one could conjure.
Dahzini, you're blocking the onlooker's view.
Why does that one glow?
Mortals … I smell them.
Ooh, it smells so good in here!
Fargrave is many things but it is never boring.
I am the only one here.
Issata, are you quite finished yet?
Studying magic was not supposed to be impossible!
Do you mind? Some of us are trying to listen!
Come to look at the crystals?
My job would be simpler if mortals didn't die so easily.
Fargrave should be harsher. The mortals seem at ease in this place.
I need more vagrants to practice on.
The Grasp. Never around when you really need them.
Mortals find fireplaces so comfortable, yet complain about the heat in the Burn.
Life was simpler on Nirn. But boring.
If Daedra don't sleep, the inn must be for us mortals.
That is deeply unpleasant, but at least we're returning to a stable current.
Something's changing!
Oh, Dibella's thorns! I forgot my payment.
I miss Gideon and Blackwood. I even miss bog dogs.
My dreams are so strange of late. Maybe I should not have explored that Vaermina site.
Go here. Do that. Come back. Ugh. Dull.
Where's the Grasp when you need them?
I'll take the coin off of anyone.
Your are weak! Pathetic!
Strange, is it not, how often one must travel alone? Rather than meet a friend at some distant destination, M'aiq would prefer to journey together and enjoy the company.
Why does this mortal realm give us problems?
Chirrrai is a master thief. Need anything taken, just whisper. She hears.
Give up, or I'll take your ears as well as your money.
Serving Dagon is better than … this tankard I have here!
Stop your sniveling!
Why would the Prince of Destruction ever want you?
Push the initiates harder. Break them!
I'll beat you at this game. Every time.
The Waking Flame are too soft on their inductees.
Did you see how they wept? The contortion of their faces!
Fear spits in the face of glory. Don't be afraid to spit back.
Ah, after all those ages … to what do I owe this favor? Here, creature. A sample of what awaits you if you continue as you have.
To feel the warp—the weft—of reality slither through my folds. It is liberating. Another tendril wriggles freely to your service, creature.
Sand beneath. Coral above. It is good to … be … again. Yet still, imprisoned. Release me from it, creature, and receive your final gift.
Never in all their aeons could the builders have foreseen a creature such as you would undo their timeless work. Yet … here you are.
I taste your power! It bellows loudly as you slake its hunger! But mine is insatiable!
No! I will not be bested. Not by you!
How? How are you so strong? How can you do this to me?
Hold still, now. What comes next will not be … pleasant.
For you.
Such laziness! Worthless curs!
Maybe digging more holes in the rock will curb your will!
Another hungry mouth for the fires of this place? Can't say I'm pleased.
One longs for the dens of Fargrave.
There's a large landmark. How is this place hidden?
Safe haven? Psh! This place is doomed.
Did you hear something? Something … bad?
To the hovel. And my friend. And to more!
Are you smitten, mortal? I understand that my kind can have that affect on you.\n\nIf not, then please tell me what I'm doing wrong and I'll attempt to do better.
Dremora killed me for this opinion once, but the Deadlands would be better off without Prince Dagon in power. Or any Prince.
I think someone else lives here. With me.
Unlike you mud-makers, I can leave this city.
Sleep? That's just pure laziness.
I just love looking at mortals. They're so small. And meaningless.
We fought for this life and we'll keep it.
This sad wretch would take your mortality if she could.
A mortal. I knew I smelled something.
All hope is not lost, no matter how dark times get.
What damage can they do me? The worst has already happened.
I'm on the hunt for the emerald geodeer. Have you seen it?
Rivalries take too much energy. But they will not follow me here.
Erztiran made a poor decision and was forced to seek shelter in this cursed place.
Beggars hide behind bravado. Mazorah hides behind nothing.
I like to watch the Daedra from up here.
Hold tightly to your purse. Make it more difficult for me.
I don't have a reputation. That's how you know I'm good at my job.
Blind man. Want. Bedding. Hay. Mine. Take. Good.
Curse those mongrels. If I wanted claws I would've been born a Khajiit!
Only fools or brave souls walk these lands. Which are you?
Why is it always difficult to find something when you're looking for it!
How did I lose a Scamp here? There are so many Scamps!
This one's family worries about her out in the wilderness. Her bones may be old, but she can still defend herself!
Excitement awaits ahead. I can feel it.
Fight bravely, mortal. It will be over soon.
Every time a mortal arrives here, I laugh.
You will burn!
I haven't seen any enemies yet. Have you?
The winds here! Intolerable.
The elements here strengthen my magic.
I like the lightning. And the winds.
Bah! I grow bored. Who would dare attack us here?
Is there no one to fight in this place?
Why have we not yet moved against Fargrave?
Be vigilant. Enemies may be near.
Feh. I hate guard duty.
Make sure the area is secure.
Watch the prisoners. They're dangerous.
Do we have enough? We sent quite a few to the device.
What happened at Burning Gyre Keep? No one's told me.
I saw the first Incarnate. It was … beautiful.
Forget Fargrave. I say we loose the Incarnate against Tamriel.
Sister Celdina told me that we're almost ready.
Sister Celdina should put Valkynaz Nokvroz in his place.
The cataclyst is hungry today.
No, no, no, no,no—ah!
Soon, Fargrave will pay for that insult we suffered at the bathhouse.
Prepare the next set of prisoners for the cataclyst.
I need to stab something.
Where's a nice juicy pouch full of gold when you need it?
This is my corner! Get your own!
I should be the one in charge! Me!
No one would dare move against us.
No one can keep us hidden away here forever!
Those Dremora better walk the other way!
What are those creatures up to?
The Nirnlings have no idea what we are capable of.
Avoid Skein Row for now. Enzir commands it.
Shaermeta demands her choice of all kills.
Look how the prey walks right into our web.
You need my power, friend!
No witnesses!
Do not let any enemy pass!
The mortal's blood is really that powerful?
The mortal's blood has already begun to flow.
What do the Bladebearers hope to accomplish?
Someone will fall to my blade today. I swear it.
How much blood does the cataclyst require, I wonder?
No one can breach these walls.
How will mortal blood make us more powerful?
Flood and fire consume you!
Rynkyus is a fool to challenge us.
If the battle does not come to me, I shall go find it.
Battle is upon us. To arms!
How did they get past the gates?
The mortal possesses royal blood? I wonder where she got it.
No one escapes Lord Dagon's wrath!
The new recruits are practically worthless.
I love being a Dagonist! No one cares when I get mad and smash the furniture.
Do not falter! Stand strong!
Ha! I hope that hurt, you cracked acorn!
A futile effort.
I choose my own path!
Insolent pests! You will fall!
Use the egonymic against Mehrunes Dagon!
No!
Pitiful mortal!
Ha! More heads for the spike! Come then!
Do your worst, mortals! For I shall do mine!
You thirst for knowledge, I think. As for me, I am just thirsty. Perhaps we can help each other.
You look lost, beeko. Let me help you.

Very few people have explored the dunes outside the city. One Golden Saint set out to explore the wilds outside the walls. She walked for weeks, but the horizon never grew closer.\n\nA Dark Elf did the same, but never returned.

You will not find food in the Daedric quarters. Dremora think food attracts mortals like a carcass attracts flies. Even so, the Stricture states that eating is permissible.\n\nSo, always be prepared to eat something that is not strictly-speaking food.
With this beast, we are unstoppable!
I will fry your flesh!
The Lord of Devastation sends his regards!
Keep it occupied. I can summon more energy pools shortly.
Wretched Spire will make a fine gift for our lord and master!
We were so close.
Keep fighting. I'll be all right!
Ha! Pitiful mortal!
You flee? Ha! You will find no refuge in the Deadlands.
You cannot win! Dagon's power is too great!
Feel my fury!
Surely the Waking Flame won't miss one little wretch like me.
The end is coming! I've seen it!
By the word of Seht, I am bound. My functions include accepting goods in exchange for gold. Shall we barter?
Greetings. My primary functions include storage and security. Would you like to deposit goods or gold?
How did you find me?
I surren—gah!
They found me!
What's happen—ah!
No one is safe from Lord Dagon's rage!
Why do we sit here like blisters on an Ogrim's arse? Is there no realm nearby that we can hurl down into ruin?
Name an enemy, master. I will crush them underfoot for you!
I think some of those Waking Flame fools managed to escape our wrath, master. Let us go and look again. Who doesn't relish a good hunt and bloody retribution?
Ah, this is much better. No Madam Whim looking over Hezehk's shoulder, badgering me to be about my duties! Perhaps I will stay here. For a time.

I can't tell you how glad I am to be done with all of Lyranth's nonsense. Why, she ran poor Hezehk from one end of the Deadlands to the other with her messages and other errands! If I ever see her again, it will be too soon!
It's just as well that you chased the Waking Flame out of the Shambles. Fargrave is miserable enough without mortal cultists running around and making everything worse.

I hope the Ritemaster appreciates my research into Daedric games of chance! It really is a fascinating aspect of their culture. For beings with no concept of material wealth, they certainly love gambling for other things!
I wonder if Mehrunes Dagon ever gambles. He strikes me as a sore loser, though. Probably hit me with a flood or an earthquake if I happened to beat him, right?
You've been to Artaeum, haven't you? Not many people can say that. The island isn't exactly on any maps.\n\nWell, not anymore.
Come, let us wreak havoc on the weak and the unworthy. My talents grow stale in this place!
Ah, this is much better. No Madam Whim looking over Hezehk's shoulder, badgering me to be about my duties! Perhaps I will stay here. For a time.

I hope the Ritemaster appreciates my research into Daedric games of chance! It really is a fascinating aspect of their culture. For beings with no concept of material wealth, they certainly love gambling for other things!
Do any dare to face me?
I know you're out there, mortals. I can smell you.
More heads for the pile!
Yes! Meet your blood-soaked fate!
You think me slain? Think again!
I am … eternal!
Tired? The contest has barely begun!
You have no hope!
You choose to flee? Ha! You will find few comforts in the Deadlands.
You choose to flee? Ha! You will find few comforts in the Deadlands.
Yes, run, mortals! Run and hide!
Scurry back to Nirn, weaklings!
If that was your best shot, this'll be quick.
String them up for the crabs to pick at.
You idiots don't even know what you've gotten yourselves into. And you never will!
Let's see how you dance!
Where you going now?
Not fast enough!
You'll be spinier than the yaghra before it's over.
Something wrong with your eyes?
Think you're safe back there?
Time to torch your lungs.
Went up like the dung-heap you are!
If you put up a fight, I'll make every effort to make sure you live long enough to dangle in front of those yaghra.
I could see you with one of my shields. Yes, definitely. Please take a look.
I use only the finest fabrics, blessed by Stonelore Druids. It can't hurt, right?
These accommodations are lacking, master. You need a larger backpack. Much larger.
Close that flap! I am plotting the downfall of my enemies and I do not wish to be disturbed!
Soon Valkynaz Nokvroz will rue the day he cursed Arox the Mutilator! Rue. The. Day!
The Anchorite is one of these so-called Ambitions? Does that make her an ally or an enemy, master?
Headed for some rugged terrain? Remember, tough soles and tight laces. Nobody fights well on their arse.
It would be wise to surrender, but it wouldn't be nearly as fun.
This air … stale, yet moist. Sterile from eons of sorcerous resonance. Still, it is good to breathe again.
If Sir Brenvale managed to reach his goal, he'll be rather deep into the crypts.
Corruption and decay are inevitable.
<Baa! Baaa?>
You made it back in one piece! That's a very good start. Is the job done?
I expect you'll be in for a tough fight, so be prepared. Good luck to you, adventurer!
I have work today, but the task can't be handled by you alone. Not unless you're far more capable than you appear—no offense intended!\n\nWould you like to hear what I have available?
House Dufort appreciates your hard work for the people of the Systres. And your eagerness for another fight. But I've got nothing for you just yet.
Welcome back, adventurer. Were you able to successfully perform the task I assigned to you?
I look forward to your safe return and news of your success. Your pay will be waiting once the job is complete.
If you need gold, I could use a hand. There's always work available for someone who can handle things on their own.\n\nCan I offer you a job today?
No more work today, my friend. Seek me out later and we can come to a new arrangement.
I think it will be good for Ember to see more of Tamriel. I know she traveled a good deal before coming to me, but as she tells it, it was not always enlightening.
Dryheels on our shores!
Let's eat these gups alive!
Maybe they were just here to watch.
If you surrender, I'll permit you to massage my feet for the rest of your days instead of being ground under my heel. Wouldn't that be nice?
I am the sea and tide! And you are just poor guppies.
Glad no one had to watch that pathetic display.
Well, that was dull. I should have brought some drinks to liven things up.
Now you see how far beneath a queen you are.
I think they want the title, Turli. Let's show them why we're the champs.
Can you manage the pups, I wonder?
You can feed the reef with the rest of your fleet.
Hope you can back up that swagger, loves.
Welcome to your drowning pool!
Are you mocking me? I was going to take you prisoner, but now I think I'll grate you to shreds on the reef.
Small bites, love. Don't want you choking.
I've got a nasty bit of business for you.
For the Fleet Queen!
My gales will rip you to shreds!
I'll cook you for the harpies.
Find something someone … dropped? Leave it with Kasam-dar. He helps lost items find the pockets they're meant to leave in.
Leave me alone.
What are you up to? Be about your business and leave me alone!
There's plenty to go around, just make sure you eat everything on your plate! I abhor waste. The dogs don't mind, of course.
Oop! Sorry, walker, almost bumped into you there. Can I get you something?
Whether you—correctly—pray to the Tribunal or direct your offerings to a distant god like Zenithar, I'll still trade my goods for your gold.
Have you seen my fire salts? I'm sure I left them around here somewhere. Ah, never mind. You need some alchemy supplies?
Ugh, the soggy smacks of your weapons on these drowners makes Za'ji's skin crawl!
Three thrones topple this day!

Someone keeps stealing my nails. You know how many nails I already make? Losing even one makes me want to throw my hammer at … something. Preferably the thief stealing my nails. Gah!\n\nAnyway, buying or selling or both?
I'd sell you this rug I just acquired, but I'm still cleaning up the rest of the … oh, I probably should not say.\n\nCare to browse my other wares?
Those who fight the tides of change: drown!
An ocean's worth of pain awaits you!
Join together and die!
When it's slow around here, I read. Mostly romances. Nothing like being hot and bothered when someone comes along to deposit coin.\n\nSpeaking of which, how can I help you today?
Help! Before they touch me with their … claws.
Help! Anyone please! He's burning me!

I've had plenty of work since I took over from the last smith. His steel failed him on the day he found himself surrounded by bloodthirsty pirates. Now he feeds the slaughterfish.\n\nBut my steel won't fail you. Care to take a look?
I can't abide folk who don't know what they want. Decide. Or decide not to decide. Dithering is inexcusable.\n\nSo, buying? Or selling. Or both. If neither, shoo!
Regal. Majestic. Proud. The qualities of royalty, which my indriks embody. Are you interested in browsing my stock?
Don't get involved in the politics here. They're cutthroat.\n\nSo are my prices.
Either I took something priceless, or you're desperate for coin.
Greycloaks, hunt them down!
You're better than I thought.
You think you beat me?
You think you can beat me? You're swine, ripe for slaughter.
No one stands in my way!
Killing you will be satisfying.
Do not become complacent, we must pay attention.
I know I just heard something.
Did the others make it out all right?
The Ascendant Order will rise above any obstacle put in our path.
Did I just hear something?
What was that? Did you hear something?
Keep your guard up.
I caught a glimpse of the Ascendant Magus the other day. Such a powerful presence.
I hear something. Be on your guard.
This place stinks! What is that stench?
I am proud to be an agent of the Ascendant Order.
This place is not easily defensible. What are they thinking?
There is no foe I would not cut down for the Ascendant Order.
The smell of your flesh, it calls to me!
More yaghra coming! Get ready!
Keep up the assault!
Be vigilant! There could be more of those creatures around.
What a stench! What do these things eat?
The Ascendant Order will bring peace, I have no doubt.
Our order strengthens every day, I am honored to be a part of it.
I need a bath. Or several.
No one can match me in battle.
We must defend the Order at all cost.
I need to break some bones.
We have to stick with the plan.
I am battle ready.
I think my staff has a crack.
You would steal from a Priest of Zenithar? Have you learned nothing of his values or ways?
I'll hound you from dawn to dinner bell, loafer.
I didn't say you could go on break.
Get a move on! I said get!
Oh Zenithar, God of Coin and Commerce, show me that your values are not forgotten in these greedy times.
Zenithar? Some guidance would be very helpful right now!
Please, help me contain this! There's no time!
If it's Tribute you fancy, then I am happy to oblige. Just know that in this—as in all things—Imperials always triumph eventually.
Forgive me if I was distracted. I'm given to daydreaming at times. In my head, I was dancing in a noble's ball. So many partners to choose from!\n\nNow, how may I help you?
Now here's an opponent of quality! Fancy a game of Tribute, friend?
They're not real! Your eyes can't be trusted in his realm!
My Haunted can never escape. You have failed them!
Watch for the ones who are too sleek, yes? Those who love only themselves are a malignancy to all.\n\nIf you seek to counter such malignancy, look at my wares! They may help in your work.
<Mroo?>
Only the best creations reach my table—made by yours truly!\n\nBuy! And savor each bite.
Mind your own business!

Everyone, even knights and lords, should learn how to sew. I don't care how high and mighty you are. You never know when a bit of needlecraft can save the day. Or your skin!\n\nSo, what can I help you with today?
Got plenty of goods fresh off the junk pile! I'm always willing to bargain … as long as you've got rubbish to trade, that is.
Whatever's in there doesn't belong to you!
You picked the wrong salvage to fight for.
You'll soon wish you'd have drowned.
Nothing but guppies here!
Give in, you're in the serpent's mouth.
I am the crashing waves!
The sea obeys my command, what force have you brought to match it?
Join the rest of the sodden rotters in this harbor!
Do you realize now your futile struggle? You swim against the tide with weak, land-weary limbs. To the ocean, you are a flea!
Fetch the chains! One or two might have survived.
It's not like you're out to sea …. You'd rather drink than see me! Why did you bring me here?
So what if we die? I've been dying since I arrived!
I cannot decide if I prefer unbathed clients, or those who douse themselves with entirely too much fragrance. Not you, of course. \n\nLet us get to our business.
I loved you!
All I hear is thunder in my ears!
The nest is burning!
All I see is light!
…inter…
I wager half will be dead before three beats of a drum.
I can't see a way out! Captain, I can't see!
Fighting on a ship's rolling deck teaches you the value of footwork. This is knowledge I hope to bring back to my egg-brethren.\n\nJust make sure your weapons are in good shape before you sail.
That light … it really was a blessing from Zenithar!
Some steeds love it when you sing to them. Some are even picky about whether you sing well or not.
Left me hanging by the trees, now you're the ones who plea.
Not good enough.
At least it was a quick death.
Work'em harder. I'll trade a few thralls to be out of here sooner.
You turn up anything yet?
How'd our employer even know these things were here?
Blighted waters, that's for sure.
Sure, it's filthy, but it's easy bounty.
I'm not reaching in there. Make a thrall do it.
Something's squirming in that barrel.
We sailed all the way here for these mouldering wrecks?
I've fought crabs tougher than you.
Let's cut off their legs and see who treads water longest.
I'll cook you from the inside out!
Time for the old soak and shock.
I'll hook you right through the heart.
The deep's calling for you.
Clumsy dirt-shufflers!
More ears for the trophy box.
Sounds. Footsteps. Wind blowing past. A traveler! Praise the sun in this cloudless day!
Maybe we should set it ablaze just to be safe?
Is it just me, or is it moving?
Be careful, I don't trust this thing. It almost looks like it's breathing.
The Ascendant Order will show you no mercy!
Test yourself against the might of the Ascendant Order!
None can best the Ascendant Order!
Knights. Merchants. Wharf rats. Even druids. Sooner or later, they all hoist a tankard in the Ancient Anchor.\n\nWhat'll you have?
I'll make sure the beetles crawl over you when you lie in the dirt.
Don't hurt me. I'll leave you alone. I swear!
Oh, look, they're grandstanding. We'll have to humble them.

You won't see draugr here, but dangers of other sorts abound. Especially the dangers that go along with power and secrets.\n\nNow, I don't trade in information like some. But I do have other goods you should look at.
Don't sit next to the alchemist. Fumes, you know. Took the hair right off my head.\n\nNow, how can I help you?

Welcome to High Isle, mainlander. If you have the chance, venture inland and seek out the Stonelore Druids. They freely share the wisdom of the land with all.\n\nBut before you go, gear up with the goods I have for sale!
What are you doing?
The druids here confuse me. Are they witches and witch-men? Do they honor the same things the Glenumbra wyrds or the Reachfolk do?\n\nBah. Let's talk about what you wish to buy.
A quick test of your worthiness.
So many languages. Why can't we all speak the same one? It would make striking a bargain in distant lands a lot easier!\n\nHmm. Well, looks like you understand me well enough. Here to trade, then?
At journey's end, you need new gear. Please take a look! You'll find it here!
No ghosts haunt my rooms, and no rats foul these premises. So, please, stay awhile. Buy some beverages! Listen to our fine bard!
Don't be the explorer who has to return to camp because you didn't have enough bags ready! I've the best packs in the Systres, ready and waiting for you to use.
Don't help him. This man cheated me out of everything I had!
I'm not the most honest man, but does that mean I deserve to die? No. I don't think so either.
This one needs another perch!
That will teach you!
You can get started without Za'ji. This one still needs to shake the water from his ears.

You would not believe the trouble I've gone through to get these excellent furnishings into this very shop! Some materials came from as far away as Skyrim.\n\nPlease, take a look and enjoy my hard work.
More rumbles from the ground? It's probably nothing new to worry about. Probably. But I understand the wish to return to a more stable location.\n\nWhere are you off to today?
I don't know how well I'd sleep if the rumbling ground around here ever fell still. I've gotten used to it.\n\nNever mind that, though. How may I help you today?
As soon as there is a suitable opening for Za'ji to strike you will be impressed!
Za'ji will deal with these disgusting rotters for you!
Made it farther than the thralls do.
Fiery blood we can't contain. Black pressure, deep and angry. Old chains working loose. The mountain stirs—I can feel it.\n\nApologies. I was lost in reverie. How may I help you?
You looked a little too eager to kill our hounds for my taste.
I might be of aid.
The sun has no place down here. But your belongings? Yes, our sunless vault is perfect for storage.
Some claim they can feel the spirit of the item as they handle it. Me? I sense the profit that'll come after I find a buyer for it.

Whether you're new to acquiring goods or an old hand, remember this: Nothing you bring to me is of questionable provenance. Part of my job is knowing where items come from and where they should go next.
There's no mark of protection on this one. Take everything of value!
Settled up with Yrgrid? Fine. That mark will lose it's shine soon. I hope I'm there when it's gone.
You think you're a fighter? Let's see how good you really are!
Ever have your thought interrupted by someone who wasn't serious about their impact on your time?\n\nYeah, get on with your business with me so that I can recapture that thought.
Let's see those Tribute cards, runt. I'll go easy on you, I promise.
My Tribute strategies are as keen as Onsi's bright blade! Sit, and I will show you.
I find myself on a bit of a losing streak. Alas. But I think my luck is about to change!
Looking for a game of Tribute, right? Well, I can't promise a challenge.\n\nAll we can do is our best, right?
Interested in losing a game of Tribute? Well, come on, then. Let's play.
This one is far too busy to play Tribute … ha! A jest, walker! Only a jest. Come! Sit!
There is no moisture in waiting. Come, and play.
Getting tired of whipping these locals. Think you can offer a real challenge?
Repeat business is the bread and butter of any business.\n\nThat is why any goods you acquire from me and my clients remain our secret.
Pay no mind to the earth's rumblings. Sign of the times, that is. Think of it as the archipelago's way to rock you to sleep.\n\nJust don't sleep under anything that may fall over on you.
Although Bretons predominate in these islands, you'll find all sorts of other folk. Just keep your eyes open.\n\nWhile I have you here, anything to sell? Or would you prefer to buy?
The next person who tells me they know what I'm saying better than I do will get a knee in the gut. Or maybe somewhere else.\n\nThat includes you. So, buying? Selling?

You haven't seen a saucy, striped Khajiit named Bashanti-la prowling around, have you? Break-ups are hard, I get it, but there's no excuse for poisoning a guy's ale! Ugh. \n\nOblivion hath no fury, know what I mean?
Mastery of your chosen weapons can get you far in battle.\n\nBut then, you know that as well as you know I have goods for sale.

Sometimes the easier jobs are the best jobs. Take this one, for example. I just need to stand around here and sell things. Or buy if you'd rather.\n\nI still have nightmares about that last job. Everyone warned me, but I thought I'd be fine.
The islands are in danger. If you can help, I can pay.
Things are quiet, but I'm sure we'll smell smoke in the air before long. I'll let you know when I have another heroic feat for you to accomplish.
Thanks for helping with this. You look strong, and I'll bet you've got strong friends, too! You'll set this mess to rights in no time.
I assume the fact that we're not standing ankle deep in molten lava means you were successful in closing one of the vents?
Ah, I really missed talking to you. I can just be myself around you, you know? Most people think I'm a reckless, self-obsessed, shiftless lowlife. But not you, right? \n\nRight?
Oppose the Ascendant Order and die!
Everything I sell is well-made and sturdy. Best make sure everything you wish to be rid of is the same, or at least easily repaired.
The things I sell represent more than just things you put into your home. No, they represent your skill in battle! Now, how may I help you?
<Jester Anglidor ignores you as he continues to juggle, never missing a beat.>
The power of flame breathes life into my hounds!
My hounds are as cold-hearted as I am.
Iron and fire are my allies!
That's a fine specimen there! Grab him!
Ice and frost, obey my command.
Hey, I think I found something! Wait, wait … no. Sorry. It's nothing.
The Ascendants said we should stay alert. For what, exactly?
You can handle this, right?
You can't take the heat.
How dare you tap into my power.
Do you ever get tired of winning, brother? Me neither.
Together now!
Join me, brother!
Let's finish this!
A bond unrivaled!
How do you like the water?
Can you hear the sea beckoning? A sultry, seductive melody.
Watch out for the breakers!
Come and join the brawl, mates!
Boooring! I'll add to the side show.
Whew, I might have underestimated them a tad.
Have some helpers, no need to thank me, Turli.
Avenge me!
You look ready to torch.
Just about ready to shatter.
Can you handle another, I wonder?
My guardian draws its power from the sea and storm. You'll never outlast it.
Commendable performance.
But if you want my head, you'll have to come for it. Follow if you dare.
I never should have left the mire.
Ziss! You're poor company for a thousand years!
Staring at this cave, day in and day out. I can't even tell what a day is anymore!
Feel like I made a deal with old Vile, but I doubt even he'd be this cruel.
There's no bounty in the world ever worth this.
Just shut up, nothing to say that ain't been said in the last few hundred years.
Any idiot would know you don't mess with deep druid idols. Not our Commodore.
This is no way to live—die—whatever.
My arrow never misses its mark.
I'm going to make someone suffer today.
The smell of power lingers in the air.
The smell of blood lingers in the air. I relish it.
One day the master will call on us to conquer the island. I cannot wait for that day.
We will rule this island someday. The master commands it.
When will the master call for us again?
Be ready to heed the master's call at any moment.
The spire will never fall to knightly orders!
We must be ready for the next raid. The master will call on us again.
I cannot resist
I will obey.
The master beckons.
As you will it.
My limbs are not my own.
I serve the spire.
The spire controls all.
We must bring more into the spire's service.
We serve the spire. As is right.
We serve the spire. All must serve.
The master's will is made manifest.
The will of the spire lives within me.
I have a prize for you getting this far. It's a little something I whipped up for the occasion.
Tell Isobel she'll have to get up earlier, eat a bigger breakfast, ride a faster horse, and wear lighter armor if she even wants a chance to get ahead of Langley LeTarte!
Langley assured me I'll get my knighthood faster working for him. I hope he's right.
Give me a moment.
Dreadsails! Double rum rations to whoever guts these land worms.
We're getting off the track here.
Grab a drink while you're here. It'll be your last.
You've almost got me cornered! Whatever shall I do?
I've had enough of you wasting my power.
I'll be taking that back now.

You know what I hate? Buried treasure. Honestly, who buries a treasure? All the sailing, and the digging, and the backstabbing. Who has the time?\n\nHere's a life tip—if you need an old map to remember where you hid something, pick a better spot.
<Jester Anglidor ignores you as he continues to juggle, never missing a beat.>
Time for a gutting, greengill!
The Fleet Queen's gonna love your heads on her prow.
You got more visitors, Sorti!
Wasn't expecting more visitors, but I'll take their gold like anyone else's. Or off their corpses if they cause trouble.
If you're here to meet with the Fleet Queen, you're late.
The Fleet Queen is quite a looker, for a cold-skinned, scaly-hided, serpent of a woman.
Was there a bout in the arena? I wouldn't have minded a show.
Respect, walker. If Taleria turns you into a slave,  <<1>> will smuggle you off this rock for only a modest fee.
Hmm?
Think Taleria would serve up the deaders from the arena? Dinner and a show!
I'm not one for fish, usually, but these Maormer get it fresher than anyone.
If you came from the arena, I suppose you bested the twins. Fleet Queen won't take kindly to that. Suggest you have a drink before she guts you.
In the cavernous depths, in the dark ….
With a hideous, earsplitting cry ….
To that bleak prison cavern so dim ….
No one notices when prisoners go missing on Amenos.
House Mornard thinks they own the sea. They build ships!
The prisoners didn't even put up a fight!
It won't be long before the coral grows hungry.
The reefs give us their power.
Looking at the coral is invigorating.
Is it high or low tide?
Let's wash the stench from our lands!
I wish I could've seen those pompous aristocrats faces!
Pirates, thieves and liars the lot of them.
I'll kill the first outsider I see.
There's a new scent in the air.
Guarding this place is boring.
Today would be a great day for a fight!
I wish one of the sacrifices escaped.
No one disturbs the leader.
I'm eager for a game of Tribute. What say you? Interested?
I'm waiting on someone, but I think we can squeeze in a match. Have a seat.
The coral will feed on your life!
What kind of player are you, I wonder? Aggressive? Cautious? Let's find out.
That's a fine set of Tribute cards you've got there. Let's see how they play!
I left my good cards at home, but I wager I can whip you with these. Grab a chair and let's play.
I've been working on this deck for weeks. You want to try your luck?
You seek a challenge, is it not so? My Tribute deck will prove difficult to defeat, I assure you.
You are a mighty warrior, yes? Sit. We will see if your mind is as strong as your sword arm.
Haven't I seen you before? Hmm. Perhaps not.\n\nWell, fresh opponents or repeat customers, it's all the same to me. Let's play.
I must warn you, I haven't lost a match in quite some time. Still want to press your luck?
You're a Tribute player, right? Well, so am I! Set your roots there, mate, and let's have a go of it!
Ha! I've been waiting for an opponent like you all day! Have a seat, and let's get to it!
B'vek, I am desperate for a worthy opponent. I doubt it's you, but I'm willing to take the risk.
Just a few more wins and I'll be a Tribute master! Come on, then. You're the next rung on the ladder.
How people deal card without claws … it makes no sense! All cards favor Khajiit!
Joy in victory, laughter in defeat. This is the only way to play cards! Shuffle, walker. Let's play!
I never tire of Tales of Tribute. Come. Let's wallow in the mud of competition.
You are one of the Roister's Club's chosen clutch, eh? Let us put your skills to the test.
Got a table, some Tribute cards, and a belly full of mead. All I need now is an opponent!
You won't find a stronger Tribute player here, friend. May as well just have a seat and take your beating!

Mount Firesong has certainly been putting on a show these last few days, but I confess I'm growing concerned. The mine overseer on Amenos tells me the tremors and active vents have interrupted their deliveries.
Wherever High King Emeric is, I'm sure he'll be cheered by the thought that the duchess's wine and minstrels aren't going to waste.
This is a blasted waste of my time. If three royals are missing, I should have every one of my knights out combing the shore.
Forgive Nadari-dra for saying so, but you seem … out of place in this company. This one is too. Nadari-dra is a merchant of modest success, not a great lord or lady.
Have you felt the tremors over the last few days? The volcano on Y'ffelon is waking up. I can't understand why the locals haven't done something about that.
The sacred rites of Satakal are not for you!
Are you hungry, my pets?
You are no match for the Ascendent Order!
The Magus is sure to take note of our success here.
Death is the price of your defiance!
There are others who need a test of loyalty.
The prisoners swam into my net like good fishes.
The Ascendant Order will restore balance to the realm. You'll see.
Wherever the Ascendant Lord leads, I will follow.
Be on your guard. There's trouble nearby.
Focus! We cannot let our guard down.
The Order is my life. I don't know where I'd be without it.
These lords demand tithes yet give us nothing. I'll paint the walls with their blood.
Yes, the initiation's unpleasant. But we need to see commitment.
Check again. I hear there's a hero around, causing trouble.
When will these people learn? Our path is the righteous one.
First we free the Systres. Then on to Hammerfell!
Power seethes beneath the ground here. Do you not feel it?
No one cares about Orcs. So I don't care about anybody.
The waves are eager for wrecks today.
Clear out the loot fast or don't blame me if the next wreck crashes into you.
Hate when I get sent salvaging. Picking over wrecks is thrall's work.
What do you suppose the Fleet Queen wants from here? Hope it leads to some proper loot in the end.
Got anymore of that sea adder grog? I'm starting to feel my tongue again.
Had to hack down one of those hadolids the other day. Got a nice briny scent to their guts.
Got any cards? Can never keep mine dry.
Need any kindlepitch? Nothing better for razing a town.
When the Systres are ours, think King Orgnum will come to reward the Fleet Queen? And us?
Even the weak thralls make good training fodder for the vipers.
How dare these strangers encroach upon our sacred lands?
Spirit of the sky, lend me your strength.
We will fight back these hordes and protect what nature has given us.
This land is too precious. We cannot let foreigners desecrate it.
The blood of our enemies will nourish the earth. Death brings new life.
Y'ffre will have his vengeance.
Spirit of the earth, give me strength.
Why must a forest die to feed a forge? The trees give enough.
The Tamsfolk must be taught respect. And fear.
The Stonelores are fools. They coddle these invaders!
The vulk'esh are awake. Y'ffre must be angry.
Where is the Firesong Circle, anyway? The fight's here.
We better be getting a huge payout for this job.
These ornaugs smell horrible… like dead fish.
I'm ready for anything!
Ugh. I could use a drink.
We need more booze around here.
I'm itching for some target practice.
Keep your distance!
We're the strongest gang on Amenos!
Ornaugs. So adorable!
Most of my supply goes to House Dufort's marines, but I have a few things I can sell you.
I hear the Fleet Queen is a t—terrifying sorceress. Take all the preparations you can af—ford! If you die, we all do ….
Did the Hadolids attack because of the noise? Mines are loud places.
After all that Audrine and her friend the adventurer did for Stonelore Grove, I expect our circle will give them some amazing reward. I hope I can become a druid like her someday!

Many think the True Way deals with forests and plants, but there is so much more to being a druid of the Stonelore.\n\nTake these volcanic vents, for instance. Can anyone gaze upon them and not get caught up in the wonder?
You. You are the one who helped Audrine save our grove. This one thanks you. And will offer a prayer to the spirits of nature in your name.

My fellow druids of the Stonelore Circle may trust everyone who visits our humble village, but not me. Better to be a little suspicious than to leave the fox alone in the hen house.\n\nFoxes eat hens. I've seen it happen!

I've hunted from the wilds of Blackwood to the mountains of Skyrim, but since moving to High Isle, Stonelore Grove has become my favorite spot. It's just so serene and peaceful.\n\nI suppose the druids are responsible for that.

I may be a Dark Elf, but that doesn't mean I can't seek a connection with the natural world. I have worked very hard to earn my place in the Stonelore Circle.\n\nThe True Way doesn't care where you come from. Only that you adhere to its teachings.

Isn't the grove and this village beautiful? I'm glad my duties in the Oaken Order have brought me here to learn.\n\nWhen I become a full-fledged knight, I plan to return here often to commune with the spirit of the grove.
I look forward to communing with the Evergrowth. I wonder if Elder Audrine will instruct me in the process when she has some time to spare.

Something in the very stone feels … wrong. I must commune with the spirits of nature and consult with my brothers and sisters in the circle, but I fear that something has disturbed the natural order. Not just here in the grove, but beyond as well.
Wait your turn. I'll be happy to take some of your gold after I finish with these clods.

Yes, my vaunted cousin, Duke Mornard, controls this horrid little island. His consolation prize for the family's decision to support Ranser back in the day. That old bastard Emeric can be quite punitive when he sets his mind to it.

House Mornard rarely sends actual knights to deal with trouble here on Amenos. That's what mercenaries are for. Me? I'm just here to watch over a noble.\n\nI suppose I should go and try to find him at some point.
Amenos Station may not be as grand and exciting as High Isle, but I like it here. There's plenty of work to keep my hands busy!
I miss the mountains. Even the volcano is barely the size of a hill back home.

The storm that blew in out of nowhere … I've never before seen its like, and I've been sailing for close onto a decade. Some of the locals say that three ships sank in the storm, but I haven't spotted any wreckage along this part of the shore.
I'd rather not have to throw you into the stockade. I'm not technically on duty yet, and I do so enjoy my leisure time. So, go away before you force me to return to work.
The jailers at the stockade laughed at me when I asked what I needed to do to save my brother. Nothing to do now but drown my sorrows in rotmeth—or whatever this local swill happens to be.
What! I'm not doing anything illegal! Can't a person just chant nonsense in private if they want to? It's a free island. Some of it. Sort of.
Do this, they tell me. Do that, they say. Treat me no better than one of those poor sods over in the stockade.\n\nAt least I'm not one of the banished. That's not a fate I wish on my worst enemy.
Walk on by. Everyone else does. Just pretend you can't see poor Valerine sitting down here in the muck and the mire.

This one will tell you a secret, walker. The jailers aren't too vigilant in their duties. They have grown complacent, lazy. \n\nThat's what setting your prison on an isolated island gets you. Negligent guards.
Stick around, stranger. You may be just what I need to change my luck. The dice have not been kind today.
Don't ask me. I just work here.
Is everyone having fun at the tourney? Sure sounds like they're having fun.
I haven't had a day off like this in months. This is so much better than filing barrister paperwork. Hah!
Did her ladyship really order three dozen bottles of Cheydinhal Sherry? Hmm. Well. No accounting for taste, I suppose.
The quality of aspirants is quite low this year, it seems to me. That Knight Commander will let almost anyone compete! Hah.
Should I finish setting up the merchant booths? Or get the last of the stands set up? Ah, there's so much to do!
My family is in the rug-making business. Nothing like a fine weave. Are you into cloth? Uh … fabric? You know what, nevermind.
Did you clean your feet before you came in? I don't mean to be rude, but you should see the kinds of things people track in here—especially from out on the docks.
You don't look like a sandpiper, but you're not from around here, are you? I can always tell. I hope you enjoy your time in Gonfalon Bay, regardless. We all try to make it a welcoming place.

Sometimes, while I'm working, I like to look out at the big ships that pass through. I always find myself wondering what important people are on them … where they're coming from, where they're going. It passes the time.

It unsettles me to be content. My belly is full, my body is rested, and my fingers and toes are warm. And yet, I cannot help but feel as though I should be doing something else. Are warriors meant to always seek out strife? What a terrible fate.
The body is a warrior's most important weapon. I know, I know, it sounds terribly overdone but that's only because it's true. If your limbs are weak, no weapon will serve you.

I was hoping to get an apprenticeship with a noble when I showed up here. Even better if it was a good looking one. But apparently I'm difficult and erratic. Too bad for them! Even still, I've had a good time here.
You won't get many folks around here eager to chat about the Three Banners War. Most of us know it well … some of us too well. But here, we can get away from the bloodshed for a bit.
Food's easier to get here than some places, but still seems like we never have enough. Lots of hungry mouths, not enough to fill them. Not the nobles, though. They're always well fed.
If you're looking to make good coin here, your best bet is stealing from the nobles. Knocks 'em down a few pegs, too.
My bones have been aching lately. Always happens when something terrible is waiting in the shadows. But terrible things are happening all over, I suppose.
I'd fish on Amenos's shores if I could. Bloody terrifying, that place is. But considering the kind of horrors one can find on land, I can only imagine what kind of mysteries those waters hold.
Thought working for two nobles would let me buy a ship of my own, but I've only gold for one measly dinghy!
I was only supposed to be here for a few days, but I'm not sure I want to leave. It's not the prettiest place I've ever been, or the nicest … but it does have a certain tranquility to it, doesn't it?
Smell that in the air? That's fish, sweat, salt, and bad intentions.
This one is waiting for someone. And you certainly are not them. Move along, friend. Tariran has no business with you. It is better to keep it that way.
Many greetings, stranger. Must you stand so close? This one means no offense, you just have a distinct … stench of adventuring about you. It's rather pungent.
I have a lot of studying to finish. I suppose of all the places in Tamriel, this isn't a bad place to do it. It could almost be a vacation!
The plants around the square need watering. I think some of the animals have been eating them when I'm not watching.
All merchants and nobles do is worry. Will their goods dock safely? Is the war over? Psh! Boring!
I knew there were statues in Gonfalon Bay, but I never knew they were enormous!
Careful. The flagstones get quite slick over the course of the day. It'd be unseemly to slip.
Haul on that rope, Seyraadia. Hard to portside, Seyraadia. Ailment take the first mate!
The seas grow choppy. I fear there's worse on the rise for us all.
On a clear day, it sometimes seems like I can see all the way to Hammerfell. There aren't many clear days.
Swell and squall! The shops are raising their prices again.
Have you not felt it? The earth moves. The gods are displeased!
Take a look at the wares if you want. I've a few pieces in progress at the moment. Work has been a little slow.
I've got to set sail here pretty soon. I thought I'd take some time to relax.
I've never been afraid to tell the nobles what I think of them. Some are nice, sure, but most of them like to turn down their nose at common folk like me. So I insult their hair. They hate that.
Sorry, I'm quite busy at the moment. I need to record the rates at which these plants are growing. They might need more sunlight. Hmm, or less.

I pity the druids. They do not feel the presence of the true Divines. Theirs must be such a terrible existence. \n\nThe druids of the Stonelore Circle are friendly enough, but most of them seem uninterested in attending my sermons.
Commoners like me can't become knights. At least, not easily. Need to have some noble friends for that kind of step up in the world.
Be careful how you talk to the nobles in these parts. They want you to use fancy words and talk all proper. I always just end up making them mad. Too much salt on my tongue, my mother always said.

Someone had the audacity to suggest I read one of those … Investigator Vale stories the other day. The author surely has some talent, but I like to think I have more decorum than that. The few excerpts I've read are practically bawdy!
Come to Sabisse Bienne when you want goods!\n\nI swear on the honor of my family name that my offerings are extraordinarily good. The best in Stonelore Grove even!
Of course, Amunara didn't want to search down here.
I am so lost.
Cause any trouble and it's banishment for you!
Life here is way better now that I'm a trusty.
Planks left out in the rain, and now they're warped. Great.
That's no way to splice a line!
Measure twice, cut once. Should've remembered that.
Surely our day is done now. Terala is thirsty!
Stupid axe weighs as much as an anchor. I'm beat.
Warm sun feels good on these old bones.
Got a bad back, can't work. It's not my fault.
Lots of fancy folk from far lands in Gonfalon Bay these days. The duchess is planning a big party, I hear. But a traveler like you would know more about that sort of thing than me.
Watch out for dark knights roaming about High Isle. They keep their faces hidden and wear no emblems on their armor.\n\nI hear they're little better than ruffians and robbers.
Please tell me you're the sailmaker's representative. And that you've got enough canvas to fill three masts in a wagon that's already on its way here.\n\nWe're behind, and I need those sails!
One more check and I'm done.
Death holds no meaning, and neither does this.
Gather more of these documents. They'll help the Fleet Queen guide our ships to plunder.
What a nice bunch of plump guppies to feed my pets.
Keep searching. There may be more geodes hidden below.
Be vigilant. That lordling may send more dogs to trouble us.
You think to defy us?
What have you done?
Flee while you can! We may spare you.
No! Not like this!
If you're going to be barging your way through the rest of Dreadsail Reef, I could use your assistance. I'll make it worth your while.
The potential of this device is becoming much clearer to me with those runes out of the picture. How about we try it out?\n\nYou may take the lead, I want to observe the results.
They're still arguing? Mathluz has plans that require him to leave Amenos.
Unbelievable! This device must act as a sort of magical prism. The energies flowing through it split into many discreet outputs, but they change unpredictably. This will keep me busy for a while.
If Tu'whacca can't find us, then Sep take us all.
We're spared Oblivion, can't you see? He's saved us!
I had so much to live for … but not like this. I barely remember the sight of the sea.
Mutineers and traitors! You're all mutineers and traitors!
My magic will destroy you!
I love watching the big tough ones fall.
Is there anything you can't do? You just took down a Dragon! Be less amazing, would you?
That was fun! Intense, but fun!
Careful, this one looks tough!
A Dragon? You're the best!
Feels good to get the blood pumping, right?
Oh, that feels much better. Thanks!
Is it normal to lose this much blood?
Try to keep moving!
Snap out of it! Come on!
I'm not leaving you!
Nice! You're too quick for them!
Stay strong! I'm not losing you!
Watch your magicka, that stuff's important!
Do something before you fall over!
Ooh, now that's impressive!
I've been waiting to try this out!
Together!
Ah, Skywatch. I know these streets like the back of my hand. Mostly because I called at least half of them home over the years.
I don't remember much about my mother. I think if she was from anywhere in Elsweyr, it would be here. I just get a sense.
What kind of trouble do you think we can get up to here?
This place stinks.
You know how I get when it's too bumpy.
Let's go fast!

Did I ever tell you about the time I accidentally filled Huldressa's room with snails? I don't remember what I was trying to do, but the end result was hilarious! Took her weeks to get the slime off the windows. Maybe she wasn't wrong about me.
Might be something good in there. Might be nothing. Never know unless you check.
Amazing! I have to write Magister Irin about this one.
I got my nickname because my eyes reminded people of the warm embers of a fire. I think fires are much prettier.
I feel amazing! I've learned more with you than I ever learned with Magister Irin.
Make sure there aren't any traps!
What's inside? Come on, I'm so curious!
Nice find! I'm like a good luck charm, aren't I?
Look at you! Pretty impressive!
What is it? Why are we wasting time talking, I want to go! I want to do something!
What's going on?
My favorite adventuring buddy! What's going on?
I hate getting caught when I'm trying to be sneaky! It's so embarrassing. I pride myself on being able to slip in and out of somewhere quick without a trace.
Being around you almost makes me want to take Magister Irin's advice and go get my training in a guild. Staring at books all day has to be better than staring at your ugly mug.
Ugh, stop talking about feelings and our relationship! Let's just get back to doing fun things!
I like you well enough. I like you more when you're not wasting time talking about things that don't matter.
I'm learning a lot by being around you. I think Magister Irin would be proud.
I like hanging around with you, you're always getting into trouble. It's the best!
The two of us are good together. I think we've got a good thing going.
Not to be too sappy, but … I really care for you. I hope you know that.
Sure, I guess. Anything specific in mind?
Sure! As long as we're talking about good things. We are talking about good things, right?
What kind of trouble we getting into?
Fish biscuits! You're impossible!
Good, one less smelly mutt in the world.
One less hairy, smelly, freak.
I love the Thieves Guild! Can we do this more often?
The Thieves Guild always keeps it exciting.
High Isle should be a bit safer now.
Do we have to do things for the Mages Guild? Can't they get someone else?
What'd you pinch?
You're a pickpocketing artist!
Feels good, stealing from those sticks in the mud.
Ha, probably too busy thinking about magicka to notice you.
Ooh, what'd you get, what'd you get?
I love when people think their stuff is safe … and you prove them wrong.
Ah, these are my kind of people.
Best way to sell anything is to fence it, that's just a rule.
I love snooping around places I don't belong.
Good luck catching us, idiot!
I wasn't sure you were going to get away with that. Amazing!
I love harvesting runestones.
Heh, I approve.
I lost a good deal of coin playing Tales of Tribute the other day, but I was having too much fun to care!
That's right, take it all! Finders keepers.
Whew, what a sell! You're swimming in coin now.
Ugh, I hate getting caught!
Ugh, that was sloppy! We never should have been seen!
So now you've lost money and your goods. See? This is why we don't play by the rules!
I know this is supposed to be relaxing, but I just want to dive in there and grab the fish with my hands! How do you stay so still?
I never had a place to call home as a kid. It's strange to me to have a bed of my own and a pillow to put my head on … but nice, too.
My name is a nickname, obviously. My friend Silverslip came up with it because of the color of my eyes, but her nickname is so much better!
I'm not going to die here!
I need a real weapon!
Hey, I'm a big man back home. Merchant, me. Big ships. Sail them on the seas. \n\nOh. You a servant? Where's my rum and lime? I ordered one a long time ago.
I'm sorry to say that we appear to be lost. Lost. In the wilderness. Yes, that's what we are. Lost and without the comfort of good-looking servants or even rugged peasants to motivate us onward.
For High Isle!
Never had to deal with that when I was a squire.
We killed a Dragon! Riding with you is never dull.
Scores all around us, and only our valor to carry the day. What a tale!
Draigh! Going to be a tough fight.
Draigh! Even bigger than the stories!
We fought well!
Healed up and ready to fight!
My wounds! I'm not sure I can keep going.
Move your feet, get moving!
Focus your mind! Stay with me!
Stendarr save us! Rally!
Good form!
Mind your wounds!
Your spells have drained you!
You're exhausted, watch yourself!
Give it all you've got!
Stendarr, give me strength!
Side by side, let's work together!

The Temple to the Divines here in town is so beautiful. Stendarr's grace has been with these people since … well, since they were a fishing hamlet fending off pirates. I … um. I read about it in a book. Don't judge me.
The Orcs have worked so hard to make this place a home fit for their people. Amazing. And the Bretons and Redguard are right there. Shoulder to shoulder. Making it happen. Makes me proud.
I'll stay close, my friend. The Daedra of Fargrave have no honor.
What do you suppose they do for fun around here?
I can't wait to explore this place! I know, I know. I'm strange.
Where are we going?
On the move.

You remember Knight Commander Jourvel, Aurelia's mother? She was my idol when I was younger. I sometimes wonder who your idols were. The people we know as children do so much to shape the people we'll someday become.
Could be useful supplies in there.
I just realized … I'm a long way from cleaning the stables.
When I was a kid, on cold nights, I used to curl up by the fire in the Castle Navire main hall. I'd sit there with a book and fall asleep over the pages. Heh. Simpler times, eh?
Hah. A new chapter for Dame Isobel! … Too much?
Hmm. Good quality, there.
Poor thing.
Never get tired of that sound. Hah.
Draigh! That's quite the haul, there.
You've got coin to spare now.
Stendarr is with you. I can feel it.
Lyranth is using you, my friend. I'm going to stay close, try to keep you safe.
Stendarr keep me safe from that thing. Why do you keep it around?
By the Divines, look at that dog! Who's a good dog? Who's a good dog?
Hmm. Yes?
How can I help?
What adventures do we have planned?
My honor as a knight has given me purpose over the years. \n\nThievery and murder run counter to that code. I hope you understand.
I don't think we work very well together. Perhaps it would be a good idea for me to return home to High Isle.
I will continue on in your service, of course. But given your actions I'd rather not engage in idle talk.
Look within. I know you have it inside you to make better choices.
It's a pleasure to ride with you. I hope this is just early days in our tale.
This may surprise you, but I haven't had a lot of close friends over the years. I hope you stick around.
Well let's see, you helped me get over my first crush, and save my life on a regular basis. I think we're friends.
I think you know more about me than Aurelia at this point! I don't know if that's a good thing, but I mean it as a compliment.
I'm at your service, of course.
Anytime, for you.
I am your shield.
I'm working to forgive your bad behavior. Give me time.
You have no honor, Oblivion spawn.
When … when I offered you my blade … I had no idea we'd get to do things like this!
We could explore a delve every day and … I promise you … I wouldn't get bored.
Quelling the unrest on the Isle was well worth our time. Well done.
Fight with honor! Lay on!
Well fought, well fought!
Even the smallest of actions reflects on your honor. Well done.
Is Lyris … seeing someone? That you know of? You know what, don't answer that, forget I asked. Where were we going next?
The stories I've heard about Queen Ayrenn are incredible. I wonder if even half of them are true?
You talk to High King Emeric so easily! Have you ever read some of his writing? He's actually a very talented author.
Jorunn is a skald-king, right? That's kind of like a bard? I wonder if he still sings in public?
People watching at the enclave is always so interesting. More people pass through here than I saw in my whole life on High Isle.
I admire your technique. Not everyone is so deft with a blacksmith's hammer.
Draigh, that looks delicious. Please, don't tempt me.
My first lessons as a squire were how to maintain gear. Brings me back.
Stendarr wants me to tell you he saw that.
Even the least among us deserves better than that.
My friend. I know you have an unnatural hunger. Try to fight it.
Do these people know anything of honor?
These people are not your friends.
That was not how I expected you to react.
I couldn't help myself, I tidied up a bit. Look, you can take the knight out the castle but not the castle out of the knight.
I think Aurelia's finally learned her lesson. And we've cleared my family name, as best we can. Now we can focus on more important things: candied banana bread and exploring ancient ruins.
Strange. Now what was that?
Oh, what is it now? I do not wish to be disturbed!
Hmm. I could've sworn I heard something.
Next time it won't be so easy.
If you're not up for a good match here, head over to Gonfalon Bay. I hear they have all kinds of challenges you can take on.

I could've been a knight. But they have too many rules. So, I became a gladiator instead. It's so much more fun.\n\nAnd there's none of that romantic chivalry nonsense that seems to twist the knights I know all up in knots.
The game is yours. Congratulations.
Victory is mine, but you played well. My compliments.
By the Eight ….
You won't like this.
When I'm not here, I'm listening to music in Gonfalon Bay. There's a wonderful vocalist in the harbor.\n\nMostly, though, I'm here.
Even Akatosh gets impatient ….
A win for you, and a loss for me … this time.
You really made me earn that one. Good show.
Oh, come on!
Well, well, well!
Hello? It's your turn.
Try not to gloat too much, eh?
You were good. Just not good enough.
No surprise there ….
Finally!
Wake me up when you're done.
Sometimes, one must lose to improve. Thank you for the lesson.
The road to perfection is paved with defeats. Learn from this, wayfarer.
By Onsi's blade ….
Yes, this will do.
Hesitation shows weakness, friend.
The very plants and animals of the grove cry out, yet still the archdruid urges patience. She is the wisest among us, but it seems to me that the time for patience has passed.

While most of the druids of the Stonelore Circle come from Breton descent, it is not a requirement for membership. I was called from my home in Summerset to follow the True Way, and the druids welcomed me with open arms.
I'm just an aspirant and haven't been part of the Stonelore circle very long. All these rumors of corruption in the grove have me quite concerned.

Hello! I was just recently accepted into the Stonelore Circle, but I already love it here! The grove is so calm and peaceful.\n\nWell, at least it used to be. Something's going on, but the elders won't tell us anything.
It seems congratulations are in order. Well played.
I win … to the surprise of no one.
What am I to do now?
Just as I planned ….
I'm waiting ….
I think … aha! I won! Right? I did!
Seems you were the better player today.
Damn it all.
Now, that's what I like to see!
I, uh … I think it's your turn.
Fine, fine. You win! I need a drink.
Ha! Better luck next time, sera.
Of all the fetching luck ….
It's about fetching time.
Sometime this era, please?
This one enjoyed that match very much, walker. And not just because he won!
Unlucky in love, but lucky at cards! Such is this one's lot.
Rajhin curse it!
The moons shine on me!
Take as much time as you need, walker.
Your victory shines like river stones, beeko. Well played.
Yes. I shall drink deep from the gourd of victory.
My confidence withers.
The Hist provides.
We do not have an age to wait.
Bah! Just rusty is all. I'll get you next time!
Let's raise a mead to my victory, eh? Ha!
Shor's bones ….
Thank Kyne!
I've seen horkers move faster than this. Come on!
Arg! Sea spray in my paints again!
If I'm stuck here much longer, they're liable to forget about my bounty entirely.
It's fun to hang on while they raise the bridge. Guards hate it though.
Hey! Hey! Tell them to keep it down with all the banging over there. Some of us are trying to sleep.
I think I'll just watch you do it a few more times. You've got such good technique.
Truthfully, I don't enjoy these visitations. I get dreadfully sea sick.
Someone wouldn't have taken it, surely. Not with the guard right there.
Keep moving. Lots of accidents happen in this alley.
Can't take those stairs like I used to. Maybe I can work the kitchen instead.
I need to invest in a lighter jug.
Do all the weeds in Gonfalon grow around Dufort tombs?
Hope some good meat comes in from the mainland soon.
How many casks of wine do they need for a meeting? Nobles.
Why be a pirate when sailors on land are such easy pickings?
I do what I can for those who wash ashore with nothing but their lives.
The Systres don't need all these alliance wayfarers making trouble.
It's payday. Maybe I'll play a few rounds of Tribute when I'm off duty.
How do you fancy you're new shoes, girl? I know cobble's rough on your hooves.
Love this climate. Getting deployed to Gonfalon was a blessing from the Divines.
J-just a drake for an old salt who can't s-sail. I c-can carry your bag ….
Wonder what cargo will come through today.
Greet the deep and dreugh with water in your lungs and a scream on your lips.
Can't stand fish, personally. If I didn't hunt, I'd starve here.
Divines, grant me patience for these witless sailors.
Oh no. Are you lost?

This one prays and prays. Yet still the grove feels out of sorts. Something is wrong, yet the archdruid tells us that all is well. This one thinks she sees rainbows when all that fills the sky are ominous, dark clouds.
I guess I don't need that bigger canvas after all ….
It should be safe to capture to beauty and fury of the volcano from here … right?
You smell something burning? I keep smelling something burning. Learn to cook!
Ugh, if things don't stop shaking soon the volcano won't be the only thing to blow.
Did the sea level rise after the colossus keeled over? Seems higher.
I'm not worried about some eruption. We're right by the sea!
What are all the lords and ladies doing about this mess with the volcano? Are we going to be all right?
Oh, sod the volcano. Not like they'll save a berm for the likes of me when folks start fleeing for their lives.
Those dry volcanic winds are starting to sour the usual sea breeze.
Hope I don't get redeployed anywhere near that volcano. What would I even do about it?
The new recruits are soft. The Order needs people who aren't afraid to get their hands dirty.
Diligence in our duties is the path to victory. Remember that.
What did kings or queens ever do for me? Not a thing.
I hear that whoever brings the Magus his prizes is going to be rich. Rich!
We'll find them—you'll see. And then everyone will know what the Ascendant Order can do!
We're almost there! Keep fighting!
The evil has broken through! Kill the monster or all hope is lost!
Atronachs are emerging! Don't let them reach the vents!
That's it! We're almost there!
You did it! Now, I'll close this fissure.
No, I haven't seen any missing ships sail by today. The dockmaster's people have come by two or three times already to ask about that.\n\nI wish I knew what was going on.
I don't know how we can sort this out. We promised to deliver the last six months of construction to customers in Glenumbra and Blackwood. But now those ships are at the bottom of the loch!
You missed all the excitement, adventurer. Someone slipped into Amenos aboard the prison transport and rescued royals from the Green Serpent gang!\n\nWho breaks into a prison, anyway?

I hope you're here to do something about the Ascendant Order, hero. When they first showed up, they said they wanted to help the common folk. Now they're pillaging caravans and terrorizing the countryside.\n\nSome help!
I heard a rumor about missing ships and lost cargo. Might go down to the loch's shallows and try my luck later.\n\nWho knows what might wash up?
I hope Silver Swan wasn't involved in that mess at All Flags. We built her right here in this shipyard. She's the pride of High Isle!
I know everyone's upset about the Colossus. But I confess I'm thrilled about the chance to see the island's volcanic nature at its most spectacular.\n\nAnyway, how can I help you?

I know it's dangerous, but I can't wait to get a closer look at the volcanic fissures outside the walls. There's sure to be deposits of rare minerals left behind by the eruptions.\n\nHow can I help you today?

These tremors remind me of something my people knew long ago: Do not build stone-nests on sand. The rock of this island is not as firm as it should be. It is a problem for tomorrow.\n\nFor today, let us do business.

When first I came to High Isle, I relished the sun on my scales and the moist sea breezes. Now fumes mask the sun and the wind brings hot ash.\n\nHmm. I can do nothing about the mountain's anger, so how can I help you?
Did you see the Colossus fall? I was here at this counter—I didn't see it for myself. These are uncertain times, I guess.\n\nFortunately, you can count on us. We're not going anywhere.
Don't worry. This bank is as sturdy as they come. Whatever the mountain sends to High Isle, we'll still be standing. I think.\n\nNow how can I help you?

The Colossus brought thousands of visitors to Gonfalon Bay. Losing it is going to be bad for business. But I could've told these Bretons not to build a gigantic statue on top of a volcanic vent.\n\nAnyway, what do you want?

Not much point in worrying about the volcano. It's going to do what it's going to do. When it settles down, just rebuild somewhere else. That's how we do it in Vvardenfell, anyway.\n\nWhat do you need?

Not to rush you, but I might close up soon. After that last round of shaking I'm not eager to spend too much time in a big stone building. You ought to head for the countryside, too.\n\nAnd I'd stock up on food if I were you.

The farmers tell me fire-monsters are burning down their barns, and falling ash is burying their fields. Where am I going to get my produce from?\n\nBetter buy now, traveler. Can't promise these prices are going to last.
Don't let him get to you, Quinton. You don't have to stoop to his level.
Could use a bit of dusting.
Anyone feel like buying a lady a drink?
I've got a bad habit of forgetting things as soon as I've thought them. I came over here for something, I'm sure of it … and yet I cannot remember for the life of me.
I come here because people don't bother me. Most are smart enough to take the hint. Not you though, eh?

I'm trying to get a small group together to enjoy a meal. I don't think that happens often enough. No one has to become best friends, or anything, but breaking bread together always makes people feel less alone.

The volcano over on Y'ffelon is just clearing its throat. Soon enough it will really begin to roar, mark my words. I spent enough time around the Stonefalls to recognize the signs.\n\nLet us finish our business swiftly.

Everyone's watching Y'ffelon's mountain. Myself, I worry more about what's under our feet. Hungry fire-monsters? Another fissure like the one that brought down the Colossus?\n\nBad for business, either way.
I've had it with these tremors. If I wanted to feel the deck rolling under my feet, I'd've stayed at sea!\n\nLet's get to business, before they get any stronger.
It's getting bad out there. Still, I don't see how it can get much worse. I just hope the tremors and the fumes don't scare away ships bound for our port.\n\nThere's still business to be done, right?

Yes, yes, the volcano is a terrible disaster looming over the entire island, I'm sure. Stay away from lava vents and toppling statues, and you'll be just fine.\n\nNow, can we discuss more profitable concerns?

Strange. There is a disturbance in the mystic currents. Someone is playing with powers they should not meddle with. The source of the volcano's anger, perhaps?\n\nAh, forgive my speculations. How can I help you, traveler?
<Curious Faun grunting>
<Excited Faun bleating>
<Distracted Faun bleating>
<Scornful Faun grunting>
The pain … I've never felt anything like it.
High Isle is growing more dangerous, traveler. Fire and ash can burst from the ground with no warning at all. If you leave the city, you'll want a mount that's nimble and doesn't spook easily.

I hear the tremors are even worse out in the countryside. And there are fissures spewing fire, too. Take care with your mount if you leave the city.\n\nI wouldn't want to see a poor beast come to harm.

I haven't been paying much attention to the recent tremors. High Isle's always done that. But now … now things are different. Worse.\n\nI doubt I can make things better with my wares, but you're welcome to look.

You wish to see my wares? Really? At a time like this?\n\nI know some people hope the volcano will just quiet down. They're carrying on as best they can until it does. But I wouldn't be here if I had anywhere else to go.
I simply must see someone about the state of my estate. I cannot abide a lazy bureaucracy.
Rigurt loves this place! My eyes are round with wonderment! What fine examples of cultural bric-a-brac! Rigurt is hugely impressed!
Most sincere salutations! I am Rigurt the Brash, large atbassador for Nord Cultural Exchange! \n\nAtbassador? Silly Rigurt! I mean diplomat! Very large diplomat, yes. That's me!

My bestest friend! No one knows the depths of Rigurt's heart like you. What? \n\nNo, Rigurt needs no help right now. Can't one friend express affection for another? I will most likely need help later. Rigurt will let you know.
The fox does not live in its den. Its life happens out in the fields, and the den is only where it shelters. A fox is wise that way.
Do not fell a living tree if deadwood will serve your purpose.
Eldertide Druids listen to ocean and storm. Firesongs hear Y'ffre's voice in the restlessness of the mountain. We Stonelores find truth in the bones of the earth. Rocks tell stories, old and deep.
I heard that Eldertide Druids aided the Ascendant Order at All Flags Islet. I want you to know that my circle—the Stonelore Circle—would never do such a thing.
Z'en's price, just look at this place! How do anyone afford it? I mean, even for a fair hand at cards like me, this is ridiculous!

Did you know that Dragons invented Tamriel's very first card game? Oh, it's true! They called it … well, I don't know what they called it, but they used big slabs of shale as cards.\n\nI'm not making this up! Maybe Razhamad was, but I'm not!
