You really showed those Ascendant Order fools what's for! Nice going, chum!\n\nYou know, we'd be better off if everyone decided to settle their differences with a game of Tribute. Less blood that way. Well, a little less, anyway.

You really beat the stuffing out of Varnauld and his cronies! I bet that starchy prig will think twice before challenging the Gonfalon Chapter again! Let's hope he doesn't wait too long, though. I'd love to watch you thump him one more time!
What? Where else should I wait until my ship is ready to sail? It's warm in here, dry, and the drinks are strong—just the way I like 'em!
Good job, it's down!
Crash seeds. Crash! Time to hatch.
That last one threw rocks at me!
Only five kills. I'm disappointed.
You're not a Stonelore. Maybe you can fight.
You won't make it out of this!
Stop those Firesongs!
Newcomers in our grove. Friends? Foe?
You sided with Stonelore? Let me show you what real power looks like!
More bodies to feed the Deeproot.
Look, Laurel. Your last hope dies at my feet.
No one gets in the archdruid's way!
<<Heavy coughing, hacking.>>
Finally, a good fight!
Retrieve the seed and our names will burn in the eternal flames of Y'ffre.
Get ready. Here comes another one.
I wanted to commune with the spirits. The archdruid gets all the fun.
You won't get past us.
I hope I get to see the seed.
It's gathering power!
Our grove. Ours! You cannot claim it.
Trespasser. Out. Out!
You think this is simple? Let's make it interesting!
The sacred seed is mine!
Why do you hesitate? You freed me. Your death will be swift.
The tide of red water will flow over the world!
Your blood will be mine!
Why do you wait? You would keep me thirsty?
A roasted soul will taste delicious.
You will never uproot us.
Siding with that swindler? Then I'll fight you too.
You got what you deserved.
Tricksters add voices. Sing with us!
The Society's approach is very holistic. We'll heal them, mind and body.
Healer Roslenn insists this treatment will work.
He just needs to take deep breaths. He'll get through this.
Ralkluk thinks any day with the flowers is a good day.
Falling out of a tree is more restful than my sleep.
You think I can rest with those Daggerfall fetchers hanging around?
Andre was right, this water calms my nerves.
Make it stop!
Lord Bacaro said I'd heal here, but the screams—they're getting worse!
The Marcotts are true royalty!
We're short. No doubt about it. How did that happen?
Where's that messenger? I can't leave until I hear from the steward.
There's got to be someone in this town who needs killing.
Let the one who stole my steel pay the Blood Price.
You come to this one for a Tribute challenge, yes? Kishka was deep in her cups when she came up with this one, so … hopefully it makes sense?

Marunji hears stories about adventurers thumping each other over the head in Cyrodiil. Is it not better to thump other adventurers with cards? Take this challenge, for instance.\n\nIt is gentler on the claws and leaves more time for eating!
Haha, when I sailed from Sentinel I had no idea the High Isle markets would be so lucrative. Well worth the trip!
Do you think if I compliment his very fine hat the Captain might knock a few months off my service?
I think later I'll head over to the Ancient Anchor and have a nice, big meal. Maybe take a nap. That sounds like a plan.
I know in my heart what the right path is, but it's so hard to take that first step. That's why I'm here. Perhaps the Divines will show me what to do.
How is it possible for one woman to have so much luck! Draigh!
What do you say, Ghaffaman. Want to go double or nothing?
When something as indestructible as the Colossus of Gonfalon Bay breaks apart, it's time to think about sailing away on the next ship to—well, anywhere!
Don't let them get behind you.

I understand that you have obligations to your friends in the Dark Brotherhood. If I might ask a favor? \n\nAllow me to step away when you're engaged in such activities. My honor makes it hard to reconcile our friendship and your actions.

You have quick fingers, and while your skill is admirable, it's also … ugh. I always feel like such a stick in the mud. Aurelia used to joke that I was worse than the guard. \n\nLook, please don't steal things in front of me? Thank you, my friend.

You have quick fingers, and while your skill is admirable, it's also … ugh. I always feel like such a stick in the mud. Aurelia used to joke that I was worse than the guard. \n\nLook, please don't steal things in front of me? Thank you, my friend.

I understand that you have obligations to your friends in the Dark Brotherhood. If I might ask a favor? \n\nAllow me to step away when you're engaged in such activities. My honor makes it hard to reconcile our friendship and your actions.
Doesn't the archdruid seem a bit too feral to lead?
I will crack your hide to drink your soul.
Your storms fizzle beneath the waves.
Darkness swallows your light.
Even in darkness, I find you.
Nature dies by my hand.
The dead can only have one master.
I enjoy playing with my food.
Can you break its protections?
I can't repair that part.
My sight will pierce your fragile soul!
Your soul belongs to the unbreathing!
Take your last breaths!
Get behind this stone pillar!
An unforgiving punishment.
Laurel's not the only one who can move rock.
Even the smallest energy can defeat you.
The pack strikes at your back!
Fall before me!
Feel my power!
Brace for pain!
No one lives to tell of my form.
This form is too good for you.
Do your legs tremble at this glorious contraption?
No one can ever leave this island!
I honor the Firesong and Archdruid Michiel.
The Archdruid is our burning flame.
Our bears will make quick work of our enemies.
The flame of knowledge will swallow those who defy us.
We will crush the enemies of all druids beneath our heel.
How can anyone doubt the power of the Firesong?
Having a sea view is a lot less glamorous than people think. It's wind and water. I could make the same effects in my bathtub. \n\nNow, a volcano? That's something truly magnificent.
Too many damned bugs out here.
I saw an ornaug eat a whole crab the other day. Such a good boy.
Serpent's breath, I'm hungry.
I miss the sway of a ship beneath my feet.
I miss when plundering was simple.
I think I'd like my own ship some day.
There's nothing on land that can best me.
Oh my head … I didn't drink enough last night.
Something is amiss. This land flows with massive amounts of energy.
The Three Banners War has long moved passed the chance of peace.
Anyone who supports the nobles will meet my blade!
Our independence lies with the success of the Order.
Greed blinds nobility, but so will my arrows.
The Order has treated me better than the nobility ever has!
A sword and shield can only do so much. You need a strong mind to wield them properly.
Stand ready! Who knows what's wandering around.
My greatsword itches for another fight.
We will deliver a message that the nobility cannot ignore!
The Draoife are fools if they cannot see what must be done.
One arrow in the right place can win a battle.
What kind of coward armors himself from head to toe?
If the archdruid allowed me, I'd whip those Stonelore into shape.
The Firesong Circle deserves the seeds. More than anyone.
Ugh. I am never drinking with pirates again.
Stay alert. Strange things have been happening lately.
We've been preparing so long. Surely Archdruid Orlaith thought of everything.
I hear the Stonelore and Eldertide have new allies. Mainlanders.
Did you feel that tremor? The mountain grows angry.
How foolish to think this so easy.
<Distracted Faun bleating>
<Scornful Faun grunting>
<Excited Faun bleating>
<Curious Faun grunting>
I heard druids don't eat fish. What kind of life is that?
So long as there's enough coin for ale, I'm happy.
I grow tired of your incessant whining.
Listen, I just know I'll make a terrible ghost soldier. Could we discuss alternatives?
Watch Mount Firesong. The real eruption is yet to come.
Ash enriches the soil of this island. A gift of Mount Firesong.
City-folk are blind. Can't they see we must return to our roots?
It takes a keen eye to find beauty in a shalk. But it is there.
Squawk! Squawk! Fine day for a keelhaul!
I can't take your gold. My reasons are my own. Please, move along.
The tide is rising. But I know how to swim.
No, captain! I can't swim!
If I see him again, he's dead!
I want to see the light again. It's so dark.
Such a fool. Too many souls lost.
I was supposed to meet a friend here, but she's late.
I really should set up another chat with the local druids. I have an idea for their herb gardens.
Hmm I can still see straight. Time for another.
This is my favorite song. Isn't that right Cornflower?
I've out-drunk Sanguine.
Is it too early to visit the tavern?
I read that driftwood burns with a different flame, but I've never tried it.
I do enjoy the view of the bay from the top of these steps. Like to imagine myself pushing the boats along with my hands.
No one respects stable hands. It's backbreaking work. What would these streets look like without us?
I've found that giving some of the peskier rodents cheese or fruit to nibble on keeps them from eating my notes.
Saw some spilled invisibility potion near one of those big spiderwebs. You don't think the spider …? No. That'd be ridiculous. Right?
Sometimes I'll sit in the sunlight and listen to the running water and just drift away into my thoughts. Not the most productive thing to do, but it helps recharge the mind.
I sampled the wine. I think someone watered it down.
Don't go trying to sneak a few fruits off the vines. They're not ready yet.
Live outside the city. Stay away from the nobles. There's more for everyone out here.
Best not stand too close, might mistake your foot for a fish and neither of us want that.
I'm doing it, I'm getting all the steps!
Vastyr is built in harmony with Y'ffre's creations. See?
Only the Fighters Guild would find this decor valuable.
If anybody's just standing around, I could use a hand re-stuffing the practice dummies.
One day I hope to have a statue of myself in Vastyr. I'd have to do something mighty honorable, but I like to think I have it in me.
This one's fur just dried after the last rainstorm!
House Mornard thinks they're doing right by us but our troubles keep coming.
Been waiting on new ink nibs. My manuscript is a mess!
Oh, don't look so sour, dear Marbel.
Hmm. These walls are so drab.
Something big's swimming under the docks. I can feel it.
I don't mind scrubbing the docks. The repetitive motion is kind of soothing. You should try it.
Those cursed pirates are making it difficult to sail out of this damp port.
Hey, it beats playing Tribute.
Mind your coin. You wouldn't be the first visitor to have their purse stolen as they tour our docks.
I've got a good eye for painting. Not the naturalistic, artsy kind you find on the walls of nobles, but the working kind. You want your home to pop against the countryside, I'm your man.
I hope my journey ends far from here. That is the only way I can see it ending safely.
Ah, well. Best to let him mope for a bit.
Every day I discover something new in this city.
The pig's looking a bit leaner than I'm used to ….
I've got sand everywhere.
The salt in the air adds a nice texture to the clay. Makes for a unique touch to archipelago pots.
I've been a crate checker for nearly my whole life. I could probably tell you where a crate is from just by the wood it's made out of.
When my child asks, I'll tell her that pa did good work today.
Sure hope those Sea Elves pick some other port to attack today.
No one will find me here. Then again, I doubt anyone will go looking.
After almost a season on rocky seas, this one could curl up in front of that fire.
When you're the one I've sent out on a job, I don't even feel like I need my lucky spriggan totem with me. \n\nWhich is good, because I seem to have misplaced it somewhere ….
Have we returned with good news?
Good to see you again, friend. Please tell me you're seeking work today. I could use someone as dependable as you.

Clear seas to you, sailor. If you're looking for a story, I'm afraid I've been told to stop telling my favorite one. It's about lowering this craven idiot into shark-infested waters and watching him disappear from the toes up. Shame. It's a good one.

Most assume I left my life as a pirate behind out of fear. I did nearly die, but if I was the kind of cur to abandon a way of life due to cowardice, let me eat sand! It wasn't fear—it was curiosity. A thirst for something other than seawater, ha!

You remember the island we found in Graven Deep? I was thinking about our time there. Sure as sand I'm glad you showed up when you did. I keep imagining dealing with that by myself. Tu'whacca's tail, I could not have handled that lich without you!

When they saved me, I assumed that all druids were like those I met in the Stonelore Circle. But our adventure among the wyrds taught me that Firesong Druids are not nice people. When you wander the Systres, be on your guard, mate.
Clan Mother Tadali has heard that many of the furless cannot tell the difference between an Alfiq and a housecat. She is … disappointed.
Tadali has observed a few things since coming to this place. She has some small improvements in mind. This one will make you a list.

You know Tadali's cub, Za'ji? Is he still drinking too much? Traveling about with that Caska? Such a bad influence! Za'ji was such a good Khajiit once—and then he turned three and it's been nothing but heartache ever since.
The islands of the Systres Archipelago are quite beautiful. Sometimes I stand on the shore of High Isle and can almost forget the sickness and death raging across the mainland. Almost.
The All Flags Navy sailed thousands of years ago? Good one! Next you'll try to convince me that the Abecean Sea is made of clam chowder and the sky rains crackers!

I'm not sure how he did it, but that foppish manservant walked right through me! The sensation was very … disconcerting. I don't know what magic that Stibbons employed, but it was almost enough to convince me that I am a ghost.\n\nAlmost.
Now you look like a person who has seen the world! Do you have good news for me?
You're so enthusiastic! I love it! But unfortunately I don't have any new jobs for you.\n\nSwing by later! Something is bound to pop up soon!
If you're hungry, dinner will be ready soon.
Ready to head out into the beautiful, lush wilds of Galen? Well, do I have a job for you!
The ram's cranky today, almost chewed off my finger.
Cheap glan'nt! Druids and their lack of coin. They've plenty of lint and dirt in their pockets, though.
No, no, that's not right. Tomorrow the world shakes. Not today.
Hmmm … pretty sure this should say marital, not martial. Though my own experiences do confuse the two.
I'm not going to steal that fruit. I'm not going to steal that fruit.\n\nIf I say it enough, maybe people will believe me.
I'm going to wade in the stream later.
Very good. I want you to practice this on your own.
If I don't catch a fish, you don't have to clean a fish.
Root and rot! You can make wine out of torch bugs?
Y'ffre knows only one thing will heal my wounds. Revenge.
If you hadn't bitten four druids today, you wouldn't be up there all alone.
No matter how many times Javolia explains it, I just can't get this spell right.
Outsiders, pah! Encroaching where they're not wanted.
One day you will grow strong. And your roots will strangle outsiders who plant here.
Oh, the carvings here are exquisite!
I can't believe they just let outsiders in here.
Wow. We're really high up.
You almost got it, Marwig. Try again.
So many druids from different circles. How interesting.
Cold water flowing in from upstream. Good.
I'm getting it!
I know. Everything's a little out of balance at the moment.
That rumbling … I wonder if the vent is active again.
Been playing so much Tribute, my fingertips are sore.
Should've just gone to Vastyr myself.
If I didn't keep losing hooks in the wreckage, this place would be perfect.

I've got nothing else for you today, friend. \n\nUnless you've seen a spriggan totem lying around somewhere? I try to practice whittling when it gets slow. It's rather rough. It may just look like a … piece of wood. Never mind.
The Druid King could bind spirits to his will. Imagine that power!
What are we waiting for? We should strike!
I'll kill the first outsider I see.
Guarding this place is boring.
I wish one of the sacrifices escaped.
We'll need more workers.
We need better houses to sleep in.
You don't belong here!
Protect the tower!
Centuries ago you escaped. I'll not allow it this time.
Why do you hesitate?
Fall, Scourge!
Bring me their heads!
Stop where you are!
Our food tastes rotten.
Weak! You're weak!
Did you hear what she said?
My sword bites deep.
Dusty. Too dusty.
Bring them down fast!
I'm parched.
You think yourself brave, invader?
I've trained my whole life for this!
Come then! Show me your strength!
Finally! The chase ends here.
Why resist? It is futile!
Your sad efforts waste my time.
What do you hope to accomplish? Who hired you?
Who dares stand against the Allwither Order?
It is the Allwither Order's time. Our time.
Those fools didn't even put up a fight!
This is the day our reign begins!
Power is ours for the taking.
I hear a song in the fire. Do you?
Do not mourn our losses. They were weak.
The temple is ours. Find the king!
Let us be done with this.
No survivors. No witnesses.
I lost?
Surely there was some way the Firesong Druids could have been reasoned with. They can't all be murderers. \n\nRight?
I say, druids have some strange ideas sometimes. Strange, but inspirational.\n\nI've tried to incorporate that inspiration into these fine wares.
These are tough times. Working helps met to focus.\n\nHeh. As does selling that work. Care to look?
Ahh, feel that? The skin-tightening heat of the forge. \n\nCan I repair something old, or are you here for something new?
If you're looking for dangerous work, I can pay a fitting sum.
All is well for now. Enjoy your respite. I'll let you know if we need your expertise again.
Thank you for your assistance. Now, make sure you enlist some assistance of your own. The creatures you will face will be most formidable.
You're back! Please tell me you were successful.
Sometimes I worry if I have done enough for the city, but Varisse says our work is enough.\n\nSo I erect the spine of welcome, adventurer. How can I help?
With all this chaos, I find my thoughts are wandering to my Egg-Kin and, well, Varisse.\n\nStrange how you can grow so attached to someone you … work with.
Forty eight, forty nine, forty, forty one … Wait, no, that's not right. Where was I?\n\nBy the Egg, that's the third time today. One, two, three …
Most folks think it uncouth to drink on the job, unprofessional even, but not me.\n\nIn fact, it ensures that I serve our customers only the best.
Now, I know we're all trying to pay our respects, but please refrain from pouring one out for him.\n\nThe floor is sticky enough as it is.
Everyone seems so cheery lately. Even myself. The number of times I've caught myself humming?\n\nWell, let's just say it's an embarrassing amount of times.
It's hard work shaping wood into whatever you may imagine, O wayfarer, but it's honest work.\n\nMy bones may ache at day's end, but I'm always proud of what I make.
Rotten bark, gnarled roots, sometimes the best thing for a tree is to cut it down.\n\nThen you can breathe new life into it with a chisel and saw.
We'll mourn those we've lost in due time, but for now, I pour myself into the wood's grain.\n\nThis work, my trade, it gives me purpose beyond just coin.
I used to apprentice this tiny little Wood Elf. He crafted some fine staves for me, but we were always a little short-staffed.
Queen Maraya stayed here before she was married, you know. She and her sister. I don't think those princesses cared for the climate, either.
I can mend most anything you might have that needs fixing.\n\nAnything except the spirit, anyway. For that, I recommend you start with a strong drink.
The Systres aren't so different from where I grew up. The archipelago has all the better parts of home … and even a volcano. \n\nWhen you're home, what of your adventures will you want to remember?
It's the places where you least expect trouble that it's most keen on finding you. Never let your guard down, and make sure you're adequately armored.
It was the cathedral yesterday, and it'll be Castle Mornard tomorrow. Mark my words, before the year's out, I bet the whole of Vastyr is just going to crumble into the sea.
You're better off over-prepared to fight than under. If you can travel the island in numbers, even better.
Can't promise we won't get attacked by Dreadsails, but for all my journeys around the Systres, they've yet to sink us. It's the most you can ask for, sometimes.
People spend buckets of gold to get to the Systres, and then they just keep on spending. But you won't catch me complaining about it from this side of the counter! \n\nHow can I help you?
None of my stock goes to waste out here. Folks on holiday from High Isle might turn their noses up at what I'm offering, but those of us in Vastyr can't afford to be picky.

My former associates accuse me of being too good to hang around with the likes of them anymore. They try to pretend they aren't jealous of my landing this shiny new job. \n\nBut I am, and they are, so what am I supposed to do about that?
Commerce makes buyers of us all.
The druids give me odd looks when they pass through. I suppose they think I should untie my horses and let them all run free!
It's a terrible shame what happened to Count Mornard. But I'm certain his son Stefan will lead Vastyr to greener pastures.

I know I won't have to look far to find a man who'd treat me better than my last husband. But I stand here all day looking at Chath-Kasi, and … well, it's enough to make a woman wonder.\n\nI'm sorry, what can I help you with today?

You weren't in the cathedral when it …? No, I suppose you wouldn't be here if you were. It seems like everyone saw it, and everyone knows someone who was there. Everyone except me. \n\nOh, right. What service can I help with today?
What? Well, I never! This must be the rudest squirrel on Galen!

Long ago, before I became a mother, I was actually on track to become a priestess of Dibella. But, you know … such things aren't as interesting in practice as they sound to young ears. \n\nWhat service can I provide you today?
A well-furnished space is the sign of a well-furnished mind.
Careful where you let those hands wander. Last person trying to sneak a sample without paying lost a few fingers to my cleaver.\n\nWe never did find all of them.
Losing both the Count and the cathedral? That's too much grief for most people. You see anyone out there struggling you send them here for a warm meal, you got that?
I won't even pretend to know what possessed those druids to do what they did, but I'm just happy to have everyone home safe and sound.\n\nEnjoy a warm meal, you've earned it.
I have room for you aboard my ship, but considering all that's happened, I'm sure it won't last long. \n\nWhat's our heading?
Huh. The birds seem less keen on diving at me so long as you're here. \n\nCome, browse my wares! Stay all day, if you'd like.
The Druids say it was Y'ffre who gave all birds the gift of song. Makes me wonder what Daedra gave seagulls the gift of screech.
We get all sorts in here, dear. You either become a regular, or you move on from Galen.\n\nHow can I help you today?
Far fewer Daedra here than other places I've been stationed. Fewer cults, too. I wonder if it's something in the water?

The biggest thing Stefan Mornard has against him is that his grandfather was a traitor. I'd say his actions show he's overcome that already, but outsiders might not look so kindly at him rubbing elbows so close with the druids.
People say the Stonelore Druids are trustworthy enough. I say anyone that accommodating has got to be hiding something.

What little we know of the deep druids comes from waterlogged journals written by dead adventurers. \n\nSo if you go out investigating them, waterproof your paper so we can actually read yours after they've killed you.
There's a trick to remembering your runestones using the joints in your knuckles. I don't remember it, but there's a trick.

If the ground starts shaking violently I would greatly appreciate it if you laid on the floor and let my expensive equipment fall on your soft body. A small discount will of course be offered in return.
I would offer you a discount for all you have done, traveler, but I have to keep a roof over this shop. My polite thank you and wily charm should suffice.
If you hear any scratching noises, do not be alarmed. I had a pair of boots get out of their cage this morning and I have been far too busy to catch them.
Be sure to keep your leather goods properly oiled, especially if you aren't used to all the salty sea air. Nothing sadder than a salt cracked jerkin I'll tell you that.
I once had a customer come in asking for only left boots. Just left sided ones. He purchased three. I wonder what he is up to.
Be wary of the coral crabs around here, I've watched them claw their way into satchels when no one is looking, the wily little creatures.
I heard the Count is dead. Terrible thing. I had just made him a new satchel. I hope it brought him comfort in the end.
Take great care when placing a bag on the beach. That coarse sand is liable to get in every crease and fold. Best to avoid it entirely.
Seashells can be such a colorful trinkets to add to your robes. Why not wear a gift from the sea? It may even bring good luck!
During the attack, all I had to protect myself was a pair of linen sheers. I am grateful for heroes like yourself and the guardsmen, O Wayfarer.
I have been experimenting with using sea water for my fabric dyes. The salt can be a pain to wash out, but it does make the color a fair bit bolder.
Being near a port gives us access to amazing pieces of furniture from all across Tamriel. If you have the coin, we have the goods.
During the attack, a guard fought a Sea Elf and threw them down onto one of my tables and guess what? Not a single scratch. Now that is craftsmanship.
Nothing is more important than a bedroom full of matching furniture and don't you forget it!
We've got everything you need and, if we don't, I can have a ship bring it in within a fortnight.
That Stefan kid, I'm not sure he has it in him. Me and some drinking buddies have a running bet on when he fails. You want in?
So what if some of my stock comes from shipwrecks? They're not planning on using it anytime soon.
The arcane arts are a splendid craft if you're willing to put the time and effort into honing your skills
I'm not saying that I trap debtors in soul gems, but if you're contemplating accruing a debt … don't.
The island finally feels at rest. Strange how even a gentle breeze can feel like a sigh of relief.
Rumors abound of tension between the druid tribes, but I try not to worry too much. What are a bunch of nature lovers going to do beyond bicker?
A portion of the coin you spend here will help those recovering from the attacks. It's the least a merchant could do.
I hope the Firesong can find a better outlet for their chaotic magics. I am certain there is good to be had from a second chance.
Arzalaya admires your equipment, traveler. Perhaps something of use can be found in what I trade.
Arzalaya wonders if Stefan can replace the Count, but you are not paying for my opinion. Unless, you would like to pay for it?
Have you come to trade? This one is very good at finding what you need.
Careful where you leave your gear. The children around here like to make games of traveler's belongings.
Stefan is a strong warrior. Some have their doubts, but if the Count believed in him than so do I.
The children of the market have asked me to teach them how to fight. Little warriors, the lot of them. Maybe a few sword swinging lessons will do them some good.
Only a fool comes between a hunter and their prey.
No escaping, I've got you now.
Quick and quiet, now. I want to see it burn.
Fire-senche, burn my foes!
Burn them all!
Beat your fiery wings!
Burn, fools, burn!
The new Druid King is born in fire!
Let the fire overwhelm you!
Please, someone help! It's getting … a bit … hard to breathe!
You are nothing before my flames!
You cannot stand against an archdruid!
Tougher than I expected.
I've got this one!
Have you ever seen the other side of the stars, my friend? I can show you, if you like.
Would you please dig it up? Help a friend in need?
Kiko good boy? Good boy! Squawk!
It's going for the distortion!
Such immense power!
Get to the light!
Track that orb and stop it!
You shall feel my rage once I'm free!
By Y'ffre, we shall take this energy!
My freedom means your death!
Fire is mine to command!
I've never felt like this before.
Do you come to Llanshara often?
Is that lavender I smell?
She just smiled at me. Maybe I have a chance.
We should take more than this small beach.
How about all of us? No need to choose.
You see the face in the rocks, right?
Bring him. And her. And him.
What type of druids lived here when the Sea Elves showed up? And why create a love relic?\n\nWell, not important. Look for leads on the relic's location.
I don't think they went this way.
Burn this ship to the waterline!
The Firesong Circle will triumph!
Burn in the flames!
Burn or drown—the choice is yours!
Leave no one alive!
For the Firesong Circle!
Send this tub to the bottom!
The sea will be your tomb!
Is this all Vastyr can muster? I will make short work of you!
You would challenge me? Come on, then!
This city's so different from anything we have back at home.
That ship has an air of dread around it. I'd never travel on it even if it were seaworthy. Shame that.
The dead and living next to one another, it's poetic.
Maybe I can find a berth on another ship.
The wagon isn't going anywhere for now. I guess we should set up shop here.
What? The dead aren't the only ones here who need a rest.
Don't want my healing? Fine. Your spirit won't have to go far here.
Necrom is odd. I never thought to come here when I left my egg-kin. I would like to see more trees, perhaps, and more shade.
I make this offering on behalf of my master.
I'm not sure I've got a deep enough purse for this place.
Funny how nobles who win against me in games of chance end up gifting me with their wins. Not willingly or knowingly, of course.
Don't waste your coin on cheap mazte. Get the good stuff!
The Keepers of the Dead don't like splinters. We'll need to sand these again.
Those dead keepers put a chill on me.
I can't wait here all day.
Feh. The flowers are already starting to wilt.
I wish my ancestors were preserved so well. I don't even know where their bones are.
A ghost paid me to kill their murderer once. That was a strange job.
All these people visiting Necrom for purposes other than visiting ancestors. It puzzles me.
There's trouble brewing. I can feel it.
You don't care. No one cares.
O fair Llathasa … hmm. This is hard. What rhymes with Llathasa?
Those who came before me built the foundation on which I stand. Thank you, ancestors, for your efforts and know that I will build the foundation for those who come after me.
I should travel light. Whatever I get, I'll have to carry halfway to Solitude.
Boss, I know it's bad. It's all my fault. I get it.
I'm not saying the Living Gods aren't powerful ….
He was a credit to House Indoril, and now he's dead!
Stormwing hasn't sailed yet? She's behind schedule.
This pint's for you, dear sister.
Mother was never impressed with me when she was alive.
The dangers of pax hurt all but a few. Distilled into brine it kills all your mildew.
Only the finest goods for my ancestors.
They said keep an eye on the docks, so that's what I'm doing.
Aye, that was a fight. But I taught the troll a lesson he won't forget.
The keepers only have eyes for the dead. They rarely watch their purses.
Had enough?
All these candles … maybe I should have become a chandler and set up shop here.
Minurrim has much to learn about using new materials.
Only two more cords and I get to take a meal break.

Dark Elf families puzzle me. One member strives greatly to kill another. Then, after succeeding, venerates their spirit.\n\nPerhaps I'll learn more about why this happens while selling furnishings here in Necrom?
There is no shortage of fools in Necrom who believe a collection of novelty glass bottles makes them an impressive alchemist. I hope you aren't one of them.
I've got all manner of metallic martial materials here!\n\nCome take a look around!

I thought I'd have to fight an army of ghosts in this city. Turns out all I have to fight against is these dead keeper's snooty attitudes. Don't worry, the quality of my wares quickly impressed even the keepers.
This is a city of riches and opulence. You can guess how secure my bank is from that alone.
This is the most secure vault in all Necrom. For valuables, I mean. There are vaults for people too. Er, in the catacombs, not the bank.\n\nPlease don't leave dead people here.
You'll find no end of spirits telling you how to do things—if you let them.\n\nEspecially smiths. Or so I've experienced. When I die, I'm keeping my smithing tips to myself.
I have found that outsiders who are, let's say, put off by some of Necrom's traditions feel a lot better after a drink.
I use only imported timber. None of this local stuff.\n\nCare to take a look around?
I keep meaning to experiment with all those odd mushrooms outside Necrom, but I haven't managed to get away yet. \n\nYou'll just have to choose from traditional recipes.
I dye all the fabrics myself. Hope you like the colors.
Pollen bats are lucky, you know. But they do require a lot of sweeping up after.\n\nNow, what sort of enchanting needs do you have today?
I've learned much about selling goods to Necrom's visitors over the years. Perfected my art.\n\nCome on, give it a try!

I don't believe in black markets in so much as I don't enjoy selling goods in damp caves or cobweb filled catacombs. I much prefer selling my wares under the sun and if that means not selling contraband, so be it!
You have to keep your eyes open around here. There's all sorts of things going on.\n\nSo, can I help you?
Take as long as you want here. The more people who stand in front of this shop the better. It makes it look like I have something amazing to sell.
Hope you have the gold to cover your purchases. Someone tried to swindle me recently and I won't let it happen again.
Falani can see that you have a discerning eye. Well, you won't be disappointed with the goods she offers today!\n\nHow can Falani help you?
Might I interest you in a barglethargrum?\n\nOh, did I get the name wrong?
You won't find a single unpolished surface in here. That's what I'm known for you know. Murkholg's wares are so shiny you can see your ancestors in them.
I've got bits and bobs and a variety of sundries.\n\nWhat'll you have?
Talking to customers like you gives me a second to stop stitching my pieces together. Which is great, because that's my least favorite part of the whole process.
Magisters and their associates buy from me. I might not be a Telvanni, but I have their respect. I think.
They call Necrom the City of the Dead. But my draughts and potions can keep you from becoming a permanent resident.\n\nWhat can I get you?

Some spirits around here take offense to me selling soul gems. I suppose I can see their point.\n\nIf you can't, perhaps more study into the nature of soul gems is worthwhile? Start with Warlock Elinyon's Soul-Trapping I.
The rigging's taut and the sails itching to unfurl. All we need is someone to set our heading.
Big bags, small bags, all sorts of bags! It's a one-stop bag shop!\n\nHow can I help you today?
Take care of your mount and it will take care of you. That's the most important rule of my contracts.
Smell that? That is the scent of profit, my friend. What would you say to making this one's day even better?
Dark Elves are good customers. Not a day goes by without someone in this city getting stabbed. Make sure it's not you, eh?\n\nWhat do you need?

Coming to Necrom might have been the best decision I've made in my life! The Dark Elves here seem more welcoming than most. Though I admit to not having traveled much before coming here.\n\nAh, right. You want to maybe buy something?
Mara turn the shining sun of your perfect face upon this city of mournful wails and quiet reverence.

Ever read a book you shouldn't have? No, don't answer that. Just think about it. Do you really need to know the contents of every book you come across? And are you ready for the consequences if you feel that you do?
All these candles, they must cost a fortune to maintain.
I'd rather be resting than fishing.
A sad moment, but perhaps all too predictable. Lloros Telen has departed this life.\n\nIf he owed you money, I regret to inform you that he is occupied with different matters now.
Those mountains cast an eternal shadow over the harbor.

Lots of folks have little tricks for dice throwing. A certain wrist flick, or maybe a favorite surface, but me? I wait until my tail tells me to throw. I can't much explain it, but a tail has a mind of its own and I like to listen real close to it.
Look at this! My own little spot in the marketplace. Soon I'll have enough pieces made to start selling them!
Work, work, work. There's never time to rest.

Never fails to amaze me. The Dark Elves of Necrom build grand houses for their dead and bring them presents all the time. But if you ask me, the people of this city ought to pay a little more attention to the living.
So many stairs. Why stairs? Is it because of all the construction work digging out the crypts?

You never know what sort of traps have been set by a Magister trying to protect their goods. I once saw a thief freeze solid right before my eyes. That's when I learned to always check the shipping manifest. Better safe than sorry.
They have mushrooms that taste like my mother's cheese here! That's all I've been eating since I got here.
Word to the—well not wise, but a word of wisdom for you—don't eat the mushroom towers.
This place used to be much more impressive. Cleaner, too.
My friend Ragbara here was hoping to take a tour of the catacombs. I'd be happy to guide you too, but I'm afraid they've been closed lately. Perhaps tomorrow?
Dead don't sleep quietly. Which is something that my associates always seem to forget. Don't worry, I'll remind them. Before they get our families in generations of trouble.

My dear sister likens magic to music. That a well executed spell is like an opera. I think that's a foolish thought. Magic is like magic and I simply won't entertain flowery prose that says otherwise.
It's hard living under the eyes of the dead. So many expectations.
It's hard to live here and not feel intimidated by the Magisters. I can feel every time they cast a spell.
One good thing about House Telvanni. They know how to treat spellcasters properly.
You look lost, stranger. Let me guess: You're looking for the inn. Or perhaps the guild district. Take the stairs behind us, and turn left. I'm sure you will find whatever you need below. Good day!
If you're looking to purchase goods, you'll want speak to the traders and crafters below. Everything here has yet to be inventoried.
Sailors like to debate coming back here or getting buried at sea.
I can't believe they are selling this rubbish on the streets of Necrom.
Is there something I can help you with? And mind how you answer. Elvel doesn't pay me enough to put up with clumsy passes, if that's what you have in mind.
If you're looking to cut corners and pinch coin then I'm not the crafter for you. Our ancestors and loved ones deserve only the best funerary rites. And I offer nothing less than the best.
My grandfather once appeared to me here and warned me not to leave Necrom for a while. He said I'd know when to leave.\n\nI still don't know what that was all about.
Both the palace and the necropolis, this is not an easy position to guard.
In my line of work, there are few problems a big axe can't solve. Of course, I could take up woodcutting if mercenary work dries up!
Wandering the stairs keeps my body active as well as my mind.
Necrom is a city of many dark corners. Careful where you walk at night, stranger. Beasts aren't the only creatures hunting in the dead of night.
Newcomers tend to think this city is dreary and macabre, but it isn't. What is better than taking delight in death?
Oh, I'm sorry! Please, don't let me get in the way of your mourning. I'm a scholar with an interest in family trees, not a friend of the deceased. I can wait until you're finished.
Slay them all!
I was sure I was dead!
Thank you!
The sacred regalia and the nature spirit are the keys to our victory.
Be cautious. We can't let anyone stop us from achieving our goals.
My axes have slain many. I can't wait to add a few more to the count!
Archdruid Rahval's sacrifice was necessary. It served as a warning to the weak and feeble minded.
The Stonelore and Eldertide circles are pathetic!
The Ascendant Order understands the importance of unification under a worthy ruler.
The Druid King's tomb was something to behold! It was an honor to see a true part of the Breton legacy!
The outsiders are useful allies, for now.
The Eldertide and Stonelore must realize that a new Druid King is the correct path!
The noble houses must fall!
With the blood sacrifice made, the volcano spirit has been awakened.
They will learn to fear the Firesong!
It is a frog's belly for you, fool!
I will be the Druid King! The prophecy demands it!
Feel the power of my flame!
I thought the Dreadsails would kill us for certain. Then the other Sea Elf appeared out of nowhere and struck down the Dreadsails who took us prisoner.\n\nWhat is going on here?
Drown in the fire of the mountain!
Let the lava engulf you!
I command nature itself!
This room seems cozy enough. I think I'll host a lecture here. \n\nIf my mentor approves it, of course.
That sure was something, wasn't it? We felt a mighty shake and some of the tunnels collapsed. I've been too preoccupied with mixing potions and shifting dirt to even sleep.
The Stonelore are still settling back down. I'm not sure what they're up to. I'm so curious to know what the druids plan next.
Chef Rhazeez over there thinks he's the best chef in Tamriel? My father's burnt seafood stew tasted better.
Violence this close to where I sleep is unacceptable. But I can't leave. Traveling requires more provisions than I can afford.
It's about time all this business was wrapped up. Nobles and druids and their grand plots. That doesn't help the common mer now does it?
Care to join us? Drinks with two is not so different from drinks with three.
Days like these remind me why I drink.
I'm glad those Stonelore are still around, they make the best brews.
Hmm. I'll reserve judgment on you until I know if your skill is a stream or a river.
Druids fighting each other? What happens next, Coldharbour warms?
I hope the druids stay wary of each other. it makes city life so much more entertaining.
This is what I like best about Vastyr. All the talented musicians!
Escalette was recovering nicely before the attack, now I wonder if she even knows she's dancing.
Hang, on, I think I saw something.
Never mind. Let's keep moving.
I'm keeping my sword sharp in case those fobbing Sea Elf pirates attack again.
I've painted every island in the Systres—even Amenos thanks to my aunt, but Galen is the prettiest.
I'm going to have to repaint my view of Vastyr now that the Cathedral's gone.
Back up. Watch this one's coin, yes? Are you sure it's the same coin every trick?
The knights patrol more heavily now. Chirrdibazi's memorizing their routes.
I would dance, but I doubt my kind of dancing would improve this milk-drinking crowd.
It's so dark in here. I know Grandvache is beyond the law but must we be beyond light too?
Lots of commotion topside these days. They're fit to bury us.
I hold back the power of the rifts, do you think you stand a chance?
We will string you up and watch you burn slowly.
I'll record your pitiful passing in my own accounts.
Now to deal with that insolent Keshargo.
You want to see the true power of the Riftmaster?
You should've done your research before challenging me.
You dare enrage a superior combatant? So be it.
You dare challenge me? The Magnastylus?
Cushions or no, these chairs always hurt my backside.
Did you see this guild hall has an underground river flowing through it? \n\nIt's interesting, but … a window or two might have been nice.
No better place to learn about risk and reward than the tables. Foundations of my family were built at similar halls.
Seems like all I want to do these days is stay inside and stare into the fire ….
I'd ask Thurgazog to get some fresh air with me, but then I'd have to spend time with him!
Did you see Marwig? Oh, you probably don't know who he is.\n\nGlimmertarn's just down that road if you're a visitor.
Y'ffelon is quiet … for now. But if one listens closely, one might still hear whispers.
To tell you the truth, Raz is not sure. He hasn't spoken to Cariel, Egranor, or Aroz'lai in some time. Perhaps it's time we had a get-together. We will charge it to the crown, of course.
Sometimes, the forest must burn. Sometimes, the earth must turn. Someday, new life will grow.
Ah, my friend returns! This one thinks there is nothing better than a good friend, unless it is a good friend bearing moonsugar treats.
Sleek and sugary.
A marvelous reward!
No more crates. But you can always purchase more!
Pacrooti will help you to open a crate, which contains a chance for special rewards! The move is yours, my friend.
Pacrooti sees that you are ready to play! Excellent!
Ready to play? Outstanding? Let us see what the cards hold ….
An impressive amount of gems!
Not what you were expecting? How sad for you. But you're not ready to try your hand with me.
Well, you found me! Am I as glorious as you expected?
I used to come to this spot with someone I cared for very much. It was very special to us. \n\nBut these days, it's only special to me.
I came back to spend my day reading here, even after what happened. This place is too special for me to just give it up!
Sometimes, I read books so miserable that they make me want to get up and walk into the sea! I wish I had someone to talk about them with.
Keep an eye on that rabbit. She likes stealing dinners.
Just trying to keep my mind busy. I've been a bit shaky after the attack.
I dreamed of being a mage when I was little. Then my father said I had to get a job.
Some of us have fled to Vastyr for protection, even though that's where the Firesong attacked. Is there anywhere safe anymore?
Sometimes I let my feet sink in the sand and just pretend all my troubles are disappearing with them.
Nothing clears my head of brew-fog better than an accidental plunge into the bay.
I've considered taking a break from Vastyr and getting away for a bit, but I am far too behind on my reading list.
My mother wonders if I'll ever have children. Ha! If I wanted to listen to the pitter patter of little feet I'd get a steward.
I'm a scholar, studying the ways of the druids. The Stonelore here are happy to cooperate. The Eldertide, not so much.
There's nothing quite like losing yourself between a book's pages. Well, the beaches of Galen do come close.
As a scholar, I often find myself ill equipped for times like these, but that won't stop me from offering a hand to those in need.
For all my knowledge and research, I can't help the Stonelore or Eldertide keep the peace with the Firesong Circle.
This is such a special place. I came here to study druid culture, but I might just decide to stay if they'll let me.
I've lived in Vastyr all my life, and I've never seen anything like that collapse. Is it still safe here? I don't want to leave. I can't leave.
I've never been one for poetry, but the sound of crashing waves does remind me of the turning of old pages.
I'm not after gold. Or food. I don't know what I'm asking for. I guess I'll know it when I see it.
I've heard people saying Vastyr's such a gloomy city. I say it's only as gloomy as we let it be!
I suppose I understand why people think Vastyr is such a gloomy city now.
You! You're the talk of the guild hall! Welcome!
Hmph. Nobody wants to spar with me anymore.
Forge kindling, fresh saw dust, boiled mudcrab. Just a few of my favorite smells.
I've never been afraid of the heat of a forge, but the fire's of that mountain? No tempering a heat like that.
If you're looking to keep busy, plenty of people need things crafted.
We should all be sparring and running drills. Nobody has the motivation to … including me.
I'm trying to convince my guild mates that we should help more to fix up the city. Maybe I should ask them to spar and let my sword do the talking.
I don't want you tracking mud through the guild halls. Or blood for that matter. Wipe your feet.
Perhaps I'll read by the beach. The cool water on my feet would do me some good.
I should check on Verick. Lad would forget to it if you didn't put a plate of food in front of his face.
I heard one of our very own fast-fingered types found a strange stone in the rubble of the cathedral. Glows a bit.\n\nI told her to get rid of it. Nothing good comes from strange glowing stones.
You need to keep on top of the vermin down here. They like to hide amid provisions and straw. Especially the straw.\n\nOur crab over there likes vermin-based treats, by the way.

You know, I've been here for months and I still find sand in my clothes. I guess I brought a little bit of High Isle with me.\n\nAh, well. When you get on a noble's bad side, it's best to find a new island to call home.
Always carry a weapon. Even if you don't know how to use it, people might think twice before trying to cross you.
I've got people I look out for here. They may not know or appreciate it, but who else is going to do it?
I'd join the city guard with Stefan Mornard in charge. He seems to actually understand the needs of this city!
The trouble with lost shipments is most of the time you won't even get word that they're lost. You just get nothing.
Those sailors are no good. Always loitering about and drinking too much. They don't know a full day's work.

I find fishing to be incredibly relaxing. I may not smell pretty like the fancy people coming out of Castle Mornard, but I get to stand here day in and day out listening to the water lap on the shore. Much better for my health, I think.
Everybody's got their hands full in town these days. Including me.
Thrilled to hear that the Dreadsail fleet won't be a problem going forward. Now I just need the weather to be on my side, for once ….
Whenever I'm stressed I like to count the steps up to Castle Mornard. I won't say how many there are, that might spoil your sense of wonder.
When you've spent your whole life in one place, getting to know all its faces, it's immensely sad when you lose someone. Like a part of a painting has gone missing.

I can't believe so many people are gone. When word came about the attack, I knew it was going to be bad, but you just never think … you can't imagine how terrible it truly is until you see it with your own eyes.
Critters and beasts I can handle, but insects with stingers? You better be ready to pay well, because they are my mortal enemy.
My wife made me this fishing rod. Used the wood from a door frame in our old house to make it. Might be my most cherished possession.
Mind the fowl wandering about. Terrible, smelly creatures, but the druids are more likely to take their side in an argument than yours.
You should always be sure to take care of your armor. From thin linens to tough iron, a dutiful hand makes all the difference.
The Three Banners war hasn't really touched our shores in Galen. I'm grateful for that.
How could our city have let such a thing happen?
So many people still rattled from being kidnapped by the Firesong! Can't say I blame them. What a terror that would be!
A mace isn't like a sword. You don't need any fancy training or footwork to make it effective. You just swing!
Had some mead once from Eastmarch with juniper berries mixed in. Blegh! Never tasted anything so vile in all my life.
Bet I could get away with sleeping on the street if I were dressed up like one of those druids.
I thank Tall Papa every day that I am able to be here. I love the water … it is so very unlike where I grew up, but my heart always yearned for it. Even before I ever encountered it!
Tall Papa will guide those we lost. Each star in the night sky will lead them … none will be lost.
Lots of work to do, especially with something this big. But I'm looking forward to it! I'd rather do this than be stuck on the docks smelling like fish all day.
I gather fruits along the stream, just to have an excuse to dip my feet in its running waters.
Birds always get quieter when a beast is nearby. Always keep an eye on the forest line and an ear to the sky.
So many mortals die without having contributed anything. Try to avoid that fate.
I'm fresh returned from Fargrave, with a number of items to trade. What's your pleasure?
The smile may seem genuine, but his eyes follow you everywhere and it all starts to look a bit sinister. I'm not sure I can look away.
We have to tend to these waters carefully. A ripple upstream may become a wave downstream.
Of course we took in the Eldertide. They're druids, too, after all.
Rolmalnoril isn't an elder. How does he know all this magic already?
Don't you try to take me back inside. Rather stretch out here on the grass than get tossed into some druid cave again!
This wine tastes strange. I'm feeling a little dizzy. Perhaps I should avail myself of the local cuisine … if I can find anything fit for a discerning palate.
Oh, don't tell me. You're a hero who has come to save us from the destruction some villain or another plans to inflict on us all.\n\nI do mean it when I say don't tell me.
When I set up my own gaming hall, I can assure you everyone will be welcome. Except for those local beggars who refuse to bathe. And druids—I don't trust their magic.

Whenever the world outside this refuge gets to be too hot, if you know what I mean, just come join us down here. And bring whatever you find along the way. I'll find homes for it all—for a cut, of course.

Little enough is known of Vaermina, yet scholars claim they know more than they do. Before you ask, no, I'm not a Vaermina cultist, but I do pay attention to what sleep brings me, as should you.\n\nAnd now, I'll pay attention to what you bring me.

Don't tell me—you saw me because of this lantern. It's remarkable, isn't it? A friend found it in a sea captain's house and claims a ghost gave it to them. Who am I to say no when a friend offers me a ghost-given lantern?\n\nNow, to business.
Whether you're on the hunt or being hunted, I'm sure my guild has something to help you out.\n\nAnd if you're being hunted, please be quick about your selections.
I'll take just about anything and secure it away from the law and the lawless alike. But not for righteous arses. Don't be a righteous arse, and we're good.
I am Stonelore, and I offer goods to druids and outsiders alike. Would you care to see my wares?

Each land I've traveled has its own troubles. For now, I am paying attention to the druids and their endeavors.\n\nPlus, of course, I can help you with yours. Care to lighten your load or buy something?
Fiery moths, fiery frog, fiery rock seeping out of the ground … why is everything on this damn island on fire?\n\nNever mind. Are you looking to buy or sell?

When I was a boy, I split my time between the training grounds at Castle Mornard and the wilds where the Stonelore Druids made their camps. I opened blisters on my hands using training swords by day and learned how to heal them with herbs by night.

I don't quite consider myself a druid, but I don't count myself apart from them, either. I feel I have a foot in both worlds, so to speak. Part of me will always be from noble stock, but the rest will always belong to the Green.
So, you've met Druid Laurel. Isn't she everything I said she was? If only we didn't exist in two entirely different worlds.
I'm not sure what kind of leader I'm turning out to be. I can only hope it's one that my father and Archdruid Rahval would both be proud of.
When I'm not taking some much needed downtime, I'm the first mate of the Perfect Pounce. Finest ship to sail out of Senchal—at least according to her captain.
I knew you were coming. You have a very distinct scent.

Well, aren't you a welcome scent on this glorious day! If you happen to see Za'ji, don't tell him we talked. I'm sure he wants me back on the Pounce, but I want to enjoy my vacation for as long as possible.
I may appear to be at ease, but that is far from the truth. I am always wary, always watching. At any moment, the hunt may begin again.
Hmm … suspicious reports of exsanguinated livestock near Bergama. A new threat emerges. I'll have to look into that. \n\nEventually.
Well met. Do not be alarmed. Your vampiric affliction will not move me to violence. \n\nUnless you give me reason to change my mind ….
I received a letter from my family. They normally disapprove of my calling, but it's remarkable how quickly their tone changes when a bloodfiend begins stalking the foothills near our ancestral home.
Let the Firesong come! We can take them!
I will die with Firesong blood on my blade!
How did these lubbers find us?
Watch and learn, land-dweller. This is how Sea Elves fight!
I don't like this. Where did the Firesong come from?
The druids! They're all around us!
We're ready, Captain. Point us to the fight.
Gut them, Gilded Blades! Feed them to the sharks!
Watch your backs. The druids could be anywhere!
Come on! Clear the deck of this druid filth!
The fire-druids! They're hiding in the fog!
This is our battlefield, land-dweller!
The filthy druids. They turn our own ships against us.
Blood in the water. The sharks feast today!
These islands belong to us!
Didn't you learn your lesson in Vastyr, Sea Elf?
I thought the Gilded Blades could fight!
Save your breath.
They'll be here any moment.
The light is mine!
The Scourge has come!
The insects here drive me mad.
What's going on with the bridge?
I'm ready for you!
Come forth, servants!
What's this?
They could be anywhere.
So, you've come!
Kill them!
The sky! Is this an omen?
The Matriarch told us to hold steady.
The Scourge comes!
Feel the poison's burn.
<<Heavy coughing, hacking.>>
Our blessing will kill them all. Slowly.
<<Heavy coughing, hacking.>>
Our blessing will kill them all. Slowly.
What a mess! Have they no respect for the written word?
The Magnastylus's Study is right through here, come on!
Over here!
This will happen again!
Feel it crawl under your skin!
Become unmoored from now!
A gift from my lord!
Time fragments under the strain!
Stay sharp, Dusksabers. We have a job to do.
Not today!
Down, beast!
Hermaeus Mora? I've heard of him. Maybe we shouldn't touch anything in here.
Any idea what a glyphic actually looks like?
Herm … whatever. I don't think he really exists, do you?
What are we looking for again?
First time on a job outside the peninsula? We get paid extra for travel, you know.
I wonder if cultist blood tastes different ….
It feels a little strange attacking sacred places, even if they are dedicated to Daedra.
I smell trouble coming this way.
I think I chipped a fang on that cultist.
Hermaeus Mora is … very strange.
No one can stand against the Dusksabers!
Such fury. Our captors have feared this day for years. Who they call scourge, we call heroes.
You have done what even Beexilko could not. The tales they will tell.
When you first came upon the mines, there was much fear among us. I am grateful you are on our side.
I don't know why we have so many chests. Really it'd be better to put everything on display.
You slew the Cartoklepts? I knew you were more reliable than those record-loving scribes!
Thief! Vagrant! Key-stealer! To arms! To arms!
I got cornered in a pub once by some little Breton who tried to convince me to worship Sanguine.\n\nYeah, me. The life of the party.
There's nowhere to hide.
Our records will be smeared with your blood.
Knowledge, give me versatility.
Your resolve is weak.
Scamps move better than you.
I am undefeated.
That was irreplaceable!
No! You cannot best us both.
Spiders like their meals precooked.
Your fate is sealed. I'm only helping it along.
Fire cleanses bad text.
What are you waiting for? Keshargo? Come and get him.
Is that the best you have to offer?
This isn't so bad. I'm just glad to be out of the sun.
It's always Daedra nowadays. Why can't we get hired to go up against mortals?
What are we looking for? And what are they worth?
I rather like death hounds. You get what you see.
Those Hidden Kindred cultists make my skin crawl.
Is that Dremora truly on our side?
Who built this place? Before it fell into ruin, I mean.
When we finish here, we should go find a town. Have some fun.
If I never have to deal with cultists again, I'd be overjoyed.
Guard duty dulls the fangs. I'll take a fight anytime!
Fire is a tricky servant. Even I get burned sometimes.
Enough of this. When can we hunt again?
The ciphers grow soft, but even they serve a purpose.
A single strand is meaningless. We must examine the entire web.
To gaze into fate is to know the future as clearly as one remembers the past.
Memory is brittle, so we feverishly keep records.
A good book keeps your mind sharp.
I misplaced the tome I was reading.
Someone must deal with those filthy Dremnaken tearing up our tomes!
The Hushed should be eliminated, not pitied.
Like the pages of a book, mortals are so easily torn.
Smash the next intruder like a torchbug between the pages of a book
Knowledge is like an ocean and I want to drink deeply.
Lord of Knowledge, hear my prayer!
I won't stop until I tear their entrails out through their mouths!
Vanton gave this one power. No one can stop us now.
You think you can save Vanton? What's left to save?
Only fools defend mages.
Nothing will stop us now. Not even Vanton.
At last, I can reach the mortal world.
Your challenge is meaningless, I will crush you.
I will cover the ground with wizard blood.
Resistance? This one will crush you like the rest.
Is this dream too simple for you? Very well, it can change.
This mind is in splinters and you want to save it?
You think you can handle me? I must've broken your mind alongside Vanton's.
<Zilipif whistles in a friendly way>
I should have made a map ….
Use my ghost sight here!
Either you haven't set out yet, or you completed the task I set for you. Which is it?
Try to return in one piece. I've waited a long time for a capable warrior to tackle these tasks. I'd hate to prolong that search.
Hmm. Your skills are a match for the work I have to offer. I could use your assistance, if you have the time and fortitude for it.
I've nothing right now, but I look forward to working with you again. With the Three's wisdom, more work will be available soon. Talk to me later and I might have something for you to do.
Hermaeus Mora will regret stealing from the Lady of Dreams.
I wonder … do the Hushed still dream?
Do not forget. Prince Vaermina sent us here to punish the Eye!
I have long awaited my chance to wound the One Who Knows.
Enough complaining. The Dark Lady is allied with Peryite. Do you question her?
Bah. I doubt I'll find a foe here worthy of my blade.
The Hidden Kindred cannot serve two Princes. I do not trust them.
Mora took something from both Vaermina and Peryite. That's why we have allies … for now.
*Angry Gibberish*
*Angry Gibberish*
To some, pestilence is no different than a waking nightmare.
Must we work so closely with the servants of Peryite? They smell foul.
Hermaeus Mora is no fool. We must work quickly.
Hermaeus Mora will pay for what he's done, I swear it.
Our Lady of Dreams acts through our devoted hands.
Any living thing can carry disease.
What is all that knowledge for, if not for power.
I'll do whatever it takes to please our princes.
Vaermina's Mind Terrors really do earn their name.
Fear? There is nothing I fear more than Vaermina.
They will thank me for the warmth of this sickness.
I'd rather not linger longer than we have to.
Our Peryite allies know nothing of fear… an enviable trait.
All I do, I do for Vaermina.
I'll deal with the floor.
Mortals so rarely appreciate the beginning until they reach the very last chapter.
If only mortals realized that memory was more valuable than jewels and gold.
Why does the Prince of Fate need mortals? He has us!
If I catch an intruder, I will use their flesh as paper!
The threads of fate are sorely tangled.
The Great Eye sees all!
Lord of Patience should be added to Prince Mora's titles.
The next intruder I see is going to become ink for my next scroll.
Mortals should never touch the books. You never know where their hands have been.
Information is the currency of this realm.
Seekers! If Mora insists, I won't kill the next one that drops a tome.
Stack the books neatly. Neatly!
You've returned, my friend. How did your assignment go?
The sooner you get a move on, the sooner you get paid.
Put your skills to use for the Ordinators of the Telvanni Peninsula. You'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.
The Ordinators appreciate your help thus far. I'm sure there will be more work for you soon.
I know all, where did you come from?
I understand more languages than you've ever heard.
Fall before the power of Apocrypha.
Limbs bubble. Undulate. Hands for writing—arms for swimming with fate.
Don't say the Magnastylus doesn't do anything. Without her, I'd still be in a cell in Rimmen.
Any of you run into Reinfyr? Don't.
I hope you like darkness.
Finally. Something other than books to fight.
The air reeks of Dark Seducers.
All hail the Prince of Madness!
The master unleashed madness upon this Asylum. It is glorious!
Dark Seducers will cease to exist.
Destroy anything that resembles a Dark Seducer.
Quiet, I heard something.
Sheogorath grants us strength!
I shall die a thousand deaths in service to Sheogorath!
I long for a challenge, not these pathetic Dark Seducers.
Sheogorath laughs and the world trembles in fear!
The chaos is just a new beginning
Asylum or no, the madness is enlightening.
The chaos in this Asylum is the master's doing.
Sheogorath we serve you my lord.
We will make this Asylum our home.
This insanity is soothing.
Where are the Golden Saints?
The Golden Saints will die by my hand.
I grow tired of this. Where are the Golden Saints?
I need no blade to deal with measly Golden Saints.
What can we destroy today?
These Golden Saints will bow before us.
Devastation comes to The Golden Saints this day!
All this blood drives me into a frenzy.
Don't let the blood hit the shelves.
Valinna won't even let us get close to the rifts.
I much prefer reading away from the sun's blinding rays.
This is the end of your book.
When will a rift to Ashpit open?
I assure you, my count of slaughter far exceeds your own.
Do you think it's here? The thing the pen-wielding maniacs seek.
At last, something besides monotony.
Where did you come from?
Your opinions bore me.
A bug that crawls on two legs.
The next scribe to ask a dumb question will be fed to Lamikhai.
Drain the intruder's essence.
You think your skull-plate is better than mine?
The spiderlings will feast on your flesh.
You won't live to regret this.
Now that I've survived in another realm, the Riftmaster will let me join him.
You're not supposed to be here!
The Magnastylus favors Mephala's creatures. Why doesn't anyone like snakes?
I made a terrible mistake!
That went poorly. And no witnesses? Well, not for long.
I didn't sign up for this.
My blade cannot be dulled by the likes of these monstrosities!
Take care, these creatures are slippery!
This one has never seen such curious creatures!
There is enough magic in this place to fill all my welkynd stones.
Starlight can't possibly penetrate these immense stacks of books.
This place makes me uneasy.
Strange. This book has my name in it!
Where is my servant? I need my staff polished immediately!
From fire, life; from light, magic.
It's mine, all mine! You can't have it! You—gaah! Graah!
Something has changed. I … have changed. What is this?
Another page? Let's keep looking!
Imprison her in the ice!
She's going to try to burn us out. Run!
A wamasu! What a wonderful opportunity for some research.
This place stinks. Don't you people ever clean up?
You hear the prisoners beg?
This is, by far, the worst of our camps.
I've added hundreds of coins to our coffers. What have you done?
You been to Khartag Point? Why don't we send the fetchers there?
Necrom's filthy with grave goods, I say we take them off the keeper's hands.
No one values my restorative magic.
I need a drink.
We don't need the Great Houses.
I don't like having those n'wah here.
Cooks better change up the menu. I'm getting dangerously tired of ash yams.
Ugh, this is so dull! When are we going to do something fun?
Those indecent fur balls were right about skooma.
Don't let the others hear your talk like that.
Now you are going to suffer!
Fear consumes you!
Is that a mortal I smell?
Your overconfidence betrays you!
All will fall before the Prince of Madness!
The Mad God sends his regards.
Come and find your end!
I sense so much fear!
Now you all will suffer in fear!
Let the madness consume you!
Seducers have a stench about them.
Your frailty betrays you, Seducer.
Sand? What is it doing?
This will be easy!
I thought I smelled mortals!
I'll stomp your face!
You can't escape mortal scum!
Die mortal!
Move out of the way!
Sheogorath calls you to serve!
For Sheogorath!
This is going to hurt!
You will not stand in our way!
Enough from you!
You cannot run mortal!
This staff's a lot more powerful than I'm used to.
Alone. Alone. Alone. Where are they? We are lost. Too alone.
Was that Akkhiri's stomach? A meal break might be in order.
This one mustn't trust the food here. Bittergreen is boiled slime, and boiled slime makes Eluzzur's tummy ache.
My ship won't take me back.
I should make a note of that.
My stomach, did I not feed you enough?
Get a hold of yourself. You're embarrassing me.
Beached again! My coin won't last long in a fancy city like Necrom.
I've had more types of mushrooms now than I've had types of mead. I need to go back to Solitude before I turn into a giant mushroom.
Would it really be so hard giving me a coin or two?
That's intriguing. I wonder if it's a clue.
My blade is sharp, is yours?
I feel uneasy about the practices here. Why would you not want to go to the Ashpit? Why linger here and talk to your progeny?
One would think there'd be more work for an archer in these lands.
Enjoying the music, little one?
House Telvanni refuses to explain their magic. How am I expected to learn if the powerful refuse to teach?
Everything must be in order. This one promised her friend Rovone that she would see him home one final time. A warrior's death, and a warrior's funeral.
I wonder if the distance a Dark Elf family has to travel here with dead kin determines whether they're cremated or put into a coffin.
You know, the most surprising part of Necrom has been the food. If I didn't have a wife to hurry back home to I'd consider staying a little longer.
Mournhold, Stormhaven … anywhere's better than here. Soon as I save up a little coin I'm sailing away from this great big tomb of a city. Mark my words.
I thought there'd be more magisters here. \n\nFrom what the other mages are saying, I'm lucky there aren't, but still, I have questions that only they can answer.
A whole city for the living and the dead to coexist? How marvelous!
I met these Dark Elves as their lives drew to a close. I stood by the Keepers of the Dead when they prepared their shrines. It is … fitting … that I honor them as their people would.
Have you been inside Necrom's catacombs yet? I've heard such marvelous things about them. So much history lies just beneath this city.
Do you happen to know who was buried here? No family has come to visit in living memory. Not even the Keepers of the Dead remember whose memorial this is.
Recently, I've felt a renewed fervor for my studies. \n\nI thought I didn't have the energy for it anymore, but blood and tears I'm not going to complain!
The internal structure of corundum makes it a poor candidate for adding to the binding agent.
A foolish contract. I'll never find the Wood Elf in this madhouse.
I know a spell to make books speak their words.
Who thought using priceless books as foundations was a good idea?
The wagon's running late again.
So much to learn, so little time.
Balancing the stacks is dangerous work.
Thawia cannot do the impossible!
Insolent furball. A Dremora for Hermorah? Pah!
Where can I find the texts on healing?
It's harder to hunt for books in these stacks than it is to find rabbits in the snow.
I swear I saw that book change into a scroll!
This book is definitely not meant for me!
No one's figured out what that spine belonged to.
Practice keeps your skills sharp.
Sorting and cataloging makes me thirsty.
A word of warning. The Watchers don't miss a thing.
Should I start from the top or take a book from the bottom?
Waters black as ink, a sky without a sun … I don't belong here.
Ah. I knew there had to be an explanation!
I … have no idea what that word means.

Ah, a newcomer in Cipher's Midden. Do not be afraid.\n\nOnce my people saw me as an outsider. But we cast aside our old skins when we become Ciphers of the Eye. Here we all are outsiders … which means that none of us are.
Do your eyes show you things that cannot be? Put them out! The Woodland Man can teach you what you need to know by graving it in your bones.
I remember when this building was constructed. Before they came up with the name Cipher's Midden.

Interesting. You are no cipher, yet I see that Hermaeus Mora has marked you for a special task.\n\nGo on with your business, mortal. If you do not yet know what Mora wants with you, I am sure it will be revealed in time.
Sometimes your ancestor spirits send you on a task so impossible that you must seek the aid of a Daedric Prince to fulfill it.\n\nAm I talking about me? Perhaps. Perhaps not.
You can't drink ink … not that many of the high-brow scholars around here seem to know that. Someone's got to look after the provisioning, and I guess that's me.
Don't believe the uniform, we're all misfits. The ciphers take in anyone with half a mind and the good sense to be loyal to them. How else would I be here?
Words I cannot fully fathom trace their way across the pages of some books. I understand them only by their context.
Who keeps sticking notes in these books? It's foolhardy and a waste of time. They always disappear before the next reader sets eyes on them.
Pa wanted me to be a scholar. He never approved of my devotion to Hermaeus Mora. Well, I'm a cipher now, pa! It's like being a scholar but without any of the constraints of academia.
Be careful which books you pick up in this place. You may learn something that you'd rather not know. You can't un-read a book, after all.
I tried to count all the books one day. I was about halfway through when another cipher asked me a question. I lost my place and hit him with a tomeshell.
Hermorah's realm is vast and complex. This one could spend a lifetime studying the dirt and still not understand it.
Hermaeus Mora makes my tusks freeze. Still, that's what the Princes should do.
Don't you just enjoy being a part of history? If not, you should.\n\nEven standing within Necrom these days—you don't have to lift a finger to cause an impact.
These streets have been my home for longer than you've been alive. \n\nTake my advice, fledgling. Don't dig around the street corners.

Not much work around here for a professional raider. I can't fathom it. I thought these Telvanni lords were always at each other's throats, but no one's hiring on foreign marauders. And I hate to work on speculation.
Bah. Let the coin decide it!
Why does she always do this to me? I'm not some sort of pushover. Boundaries. I need to set more boundaries.
That thief sold me a fake map.
This will slow you down!
Do not waver!
What is taking so long? Destroy them!
Rid the Asylum of this scum!
Make quick work of them!
Attack! Show no mercy!
Advance!
Step into the focus to use my ghost sight!
My ghost sight can defeat this enemy!
I am a vessel of the Great Eye. Call on me!
Feel the power of fate!
The currents of fate shall revitalize you.
Get closer to me, friend!
Dance you pathetic mortals!
Pathetic mortals, burn!
Confused? You should be!
<Intense cold radiates from the Atronach, chapping your lips and making you shiver.>
<The heat of the Atronach's flame blasts across your skin, this close to the Daedric being.>
Fortunate that I found this one, before one of the others did.
Fascinating. There is a certain … allure to the Underweave. An air of great mystery.

Isn't it nice getting to kick back and throw your feet up? Not having to worry about guards hunting you down or someone recognizing your face? Relaxing without some rival trying to stab you in the back?\n\nHmm. Maybe that's just me.
Best knife I ever owned had a pommel made from an iridescent clamshell. Cut right through leather like a dream. Dropped it in the sea, though. Never saw that damn blade again.
I enjoy seeing what people find out here. I don't love the bad luck that sometimes accompanies goods I buy from cultists, though.\n\nYou aren't a cultist, are you?
The timing of my arrival coincides with yours. Was it fated? If so, who foretold it?\n\nAh, it matters not. But best check out my wares in case I have something you need.
You're alive! And you seem to be of sound mind and body, more or less. Does that mean you were victorious in Bastion Nymic?
The attacks on Bastion Nymic have ceased for now. Enjoy this respite while you can—I'm certain it won't last. The Golden Eye will have need of your help again soon enough.

I'm glad to see you, hero. Hermaeus Mora's foes are nothing if not persistent. Bastion Nymic is once more under siege. It falls upon us to teach these lesser Princes the folly of their efforts.\n\nHermaeus Mora needs you again, hero.
My sister Josseline sent me a strongly worded letter the other day. Something about never wanting to see me again and that I should sleep with one eye open. \n\nNice of her to keep in touch.
All great warriors should travel the world and experience the many trials it has to offer. What good is a sharp blade if you are not prepared to learn every move an opponent may make?

This one enjoys the heft of a good mace. Every swing should feel like the pull of Jone and Jode, with each strike nearly pulling your arms from their sockets. That is the sign of a good weapon for a Pahmar-raht!

The fight against the Dragons rages on in Northern Elsweyr, but this one has never seen its people so brave and ready to defend their land. That is in no small part thanks to you, five-claw. You are an inspiration!
This one admires the sheen of your coat, walker. Elsweyr is beautiful beyond compare, but it leaves me dry and dusty after a long day's work. We really must compare washing techniques.
Peryite may be the Daedric Prince of Plague and Pestilence, but that's not as bad as it sounds.

Skeevers. Fascinating creatures. And beloved of Peryite, don't you know? \n\nWell, yes, he also loves Dragons, but those humongous monsters scare the dung out of me, so I'd rather you didn't mention them again!
Shouldn't have let that dry. Now it'll never scrape off.
I think I stepped in something.
Perhaps he's lost? I gave perfectly clear directions.
I swear I saw a Morag Tong agent come through here. Who for, I wonder?
Don't expect much help from anyone in Ald Isra.
