"Throbbing violet coprinus …." Are there any euphemisms in here that don't involve alchemical reagents? No?
You have to do everything for yourself to get by out here. Don't expect any kindness or helping hands.

It does the soul good to leave those dark halls and towers and see the sun every once in a while.\n\nThe Mouths and magisters of Ald Isra don't believe me when I say that. If you ask me, that just proves my point.
You wouldn't believe the amount of alchemy reagents I get called on to bring here.\n\nOr maybe you would. Suppose you look like the scavenging type, too.
Wine is so very dull to drink alone. But that's the time when one needs it the most.
I saw the most beautiful woman pass through earlier. When I realized she was Morag Tong, my infatuation only grew. I haven't been able to stop thinking about her.
Scrib jelly. Why did I use scrib jelly?\n\nI guess it could be worse. I could have used dragon's bile. Or clam gall. Tava's mercy.
I remember you. Look, if you're still interested in joining the Order of the Sacred Skeever, we're almost ready to start processing memberships. \n\nAlmost.
Buried here, all alone. Everyone has forgotten them. And I could be next!
What did you see? A squirrel? A witch?
I wish I could do more for you. I wish I had.
Very nice. Nothing that won't be missed, of course. Heh heh heh.
Let's see if you can pay attention!
Think you are really safe from my pets?
A stretch of the imagination!
Leave!
She's messing with my mind.
No, this isn't who I am. This isn't what I want to be!
Your interference only delays the inevitable.
This is my dream.
I can't hold her back much longer.
Found him.
I think I heard him mumble something about a river of blood. Are you sure you want to go in there?\n\nAll right, take what you need.
Anything you want me to hold onto in the event that you don't make it out of there?\n\nIf you want to trade coin for wares, I'd be happy to take that weight out of your pack, too.
Ignore me at your own peril, fool!
Freeze to death in the house of gryphons.
Burn beneath the house of the lion!
The wamasu's house strikes you down!
The gryphon is strong, but you may be stronger.
It's awake. The chimera!
You beat the wamasu. Please don't die now.
Sleep, chimera. Lend your power to Twelvane!
The lights join this one's cause.
Your failure gives me strength.
You're weak. In mind and power.
The chimera is awake!
I hope you freeze quickly.
Come here!
A traveler? It's fine, breathe deep and relax. Just a traveler.
It's time to cast you from this island!
Time to put an end to this. It's past your bedtime!
You are no match for us!
Let the fire guide you!
Make quick work of them my pets!
Attack, my pets!
Make sure you free yourself from the grime of the world before heading into Necrom, friend. Some spirits may appreciate your efforts out here, but others do not.\n\nLet's speak of my wares now.
The Dark Elves burn their dead. Did you know that? I should learn more within Necrom.\n\nPerhaps after helping competitors with their Battlegrounds needs.

I hope nothing dire is happening in Necrom. My schedule of late hasn't allowed me to look around the catacombs. Now I can't even if I wanted to.\n\nLet's speak about more pleasant things, though. Do your weapons need repairs?

I've not yet been inside Necrom due to their recent troubles. I'm glad they seem resolved because I find myself curious to learn more of their funerary customs.\n\nBefore you enter that city, though, did you need any armor repairs?
You have the look of a true champion, walker. Here you can find trophies to match your talents!\n\nPlease. This one is honored by your interest in her goods.
This will be your final mistake.

Are you looking to mount up and join the ranks of warriors marching into combat? You have the look about you. Maybe I'll hear a song of your great deeds the next time I go into a tavern. \n\nWhat can I do to send you on your way?
Be mindful of ancestor spirits, adventurer. They may be pompous and dismissive, but I've known a fair few to try and pick your pocket. We take our habits to the grave after all.
We stay to the shadows, but pull the strings of the world.\n\nDo you have business with us?
It is a bit dingy in here. If you need me to light a candle so you can see your purchase better, let me know.
The goods I deal in are as fine a quality as any you'll see here.
Never you fear. I do my best work on my third mug of mazte. Sometimes my fourth. Or fifth. Whichever one I'm up to today.\n\nHow can I help you?
In my travels, I have gathered many mortal goods and wares. Care to take a look? You wouldn't want to be caught unprepared, not when there are so many eyes watching.
Our merchants always charge a fair cost. They've looked at the battlefields. They know the real cost of their goods. Much better than the other groups. Their merchants are greedy layabouts.
Oh, is it time for the next match already? Will you be my opponent? You seem like a worthy competitor. I certainly hope I won't have to maim or kill you!
I spent days fishing it out from underneath a house in Cipher's Midden. I'm not leaving till I find it again.
The tides take you, little one. I need the knowledge those pages hold.
I can't shake the feeling that I've lost my knife. Isn't that just the worst?\n\nOh well, if I don't find it before the call to arms I'm sure I'll find one on the battlefield.
Conjuring isn't natural.
Did they think they would get away?
You would defend a malpracticer?
You definitely won't live long.
Would you rather I fill your lungs with water, or burn you from the inside out?
They're all so weak without magic.
Another fool comes to die!
You won't interfere!
All alone. Poor Vanton.
Do you remember that time he tripped right in front of Twelvane?
You can't save him.
He's useless. Leave him.
All that fancy magic and they can't even save themselves.
I heard Yaseyla wanted to kill Twelvane herself. Wonder what that worm did to deserve that.
What are you doing?
You won't survive here.
I heard Vanton's working with Twelvane now. Good.
Magic's not that hard, I don't understand how you're too stupid to do it.
Don't stoop to their level.
You won't win.
You can't fight your own mind, Vanton. You know it's right.
The other mages see how weak Vanton is.
You're useless.
Ansuul is tired of your interference!

The Khajiit regard Hermaeus Mora as a god of the sea. They call him Hermorah, Spirit of the Tides. Now I find a shipwreck in the middle of Apocrypha. It makes me wonder if they know something about Mora my people don't.

Something is not right. I constructed this place with exquisite care. Gathered the proper tomes and accessories. Yet the energies I hoped to manifest here are … absent.\n\nI do not want to start over.
Do I count both copies of Illuminus Morticatum as one book or two?\n\nNo, I'm not asking you.
Those other devotees of Hermorah stay in their settlements and deal with the tomes they can, but this is Apocrypha! We should have no limitations to what we explore!

Wrecks and debris can either be gifts or tragedies depending on your circumstances. The same restless waters which spell death for the sailor can be salvation to the castaway. The same holds for the will of the gods. Keep this in mind.
Why do I wear a helm while hunting my targets? Because I want to live, wanderer. Head blows are serious even if you survive them.
I'm curious what alchemical properties this great fungus might exhibit. A poison? A balm? A purgative? There is only one way to know!
In my younger years, I could strike those cliff strikers in mid-flight. Sadly, my throwing arm is not what it used to be.
I'm after an Inner Sea scalyfin today. In Bal Foyen I heard you can sometimes find the big ones up the coast a bit, so I'm here to try my luck. None yet, though.

I have had some unsettling dreams of late. The work of Vaermina, as my friends here say, or something I ate?\n\nProbably best not to think about that and simply focus on the task at hand. So, how can I help you today?

Dangerous knowledge always gets passed around, you know. Or so my egg-kin noted. It's never lost. Just … misplaced, perhaps?\n\nBut maybe you know of this tendency already and simply wish to see my offerings?
I'll break your arms you insolent beast!

Folks die no matter what you do. That means people are still performing funeral rites, mourning, and so on.\n\nBut, I'm not paid to keep an eye on that trade. Smithing and repairs, on the other hand, I pay close attention to.
You ever quench your work in the blood of your enemies? I find it satisfying.\n\nNot that I've done that. Recently.

We see Hlaalu, Telvanni, Dres, and so on come through here. No rivalries between the Great Houses erupt here. Or between alliances, for that matter. It's odd when you first arrive.\n\nI've come to like it, frankly, and don't wish to go back home.
I'm all stocked up with food to tempt your palate.\n\nIt's also filling, in case you're wondering.
I don't sell passes to the Catacombs. I sell things for my guild, which doesn't sell passes to the Catacombs.\n\nNow, aside from passes to the Catacombs, what are you looking for?
Necrom sees a lot more merchants these days. Makes for an unpredictable marketplace.\n\nSometimes I have something for a while. Sometimes I run out immediately.
Another one of my sigils. There's a cache buried here.
With all the unease in Necrom, I worry that some spirits may not fare well.\n\nAh, no use borrowing worries. Let's talk merchandise.

I found a perfectly fine soul gem in my boot this morning. How it got there is a mystery. How it got filled is a conundrum.\n\nI washed it well before putting it up for sale, but I understand if you'd rather see my other wares.
Not feeling well, chosen?
Don't let her get away!

I overheard some folks talking about a sickness of some sort. Ooh, I hope it isn't spreading!\n\nSorry, I hate being sick. Worse than having a shield splinter under a blow. Speaking of … I have shields for sale.

I think I saw a Buoyant Armiger spirit the other day. So distinguished and well-spoken. I wonder if her family came to visit. I wonder what they wanted.\n\nAgh. Apologies for my speculation. I get bored. But I'm not now—you're here!
We better be getting paid for this.
I keep hearing something in the walls.
Curse this fetching confinement! When I get out of here ….
No more talk of witches and ghosts! You're jumping at shadows.
Wait, was it actually that turn back there?
Argh!
Stupid nest!
K- kill these things!
The nest! Destroy it!
By the Three! Kill that monster!
What's wrong? Aren't you hungry?
You'll make the right choice, I know it.
The treacle makes my teeth hurt. Still, he'll probably like it.
Sour? Well that makes sense, it's delicious.
This meal is mine!
"Glass-as-steel split asunder, the alit's head did …."\n\nAh. The flow of composition falters in your presence. Speak.
Though blood does not soak the ground beneath you, this is the site of many battles.\n\nI have won them all. But I will fight another.
Get away from me. Please! Stop.
Those ciphers didn't put up much of a fight.
What kind of monstrosity is that?
I … don't feel well ….
That was … much too close. Thank you, traveler.
I think I'm going to be sick ….
I fear the Lord of Secrets. Vaermina is a powerful ally, but ….
Hermaeus Mora will pay for offending Lord Peryite. I swear it!
My whole body aches … Lord Peryite blesses me!
I haven't seen any skeevers around. Don't they have them here?
Our enemies shall be blessed … with a potent poison, that is.
Don't any of these books have a good poison recipe?
<Fast-paced unintelligible gibberish.>
An adventurer! Your timing couldn't be more perfect!
My polyglottal prowess is going to amaze you!
From aegis to cudgel.
The lightning crashes!
Watch as I speak to this creature in its native tongue and invite it to join me in dance!
The hammered blade sparks.
Are all these books poised to curse us?
How did we get trapped in here?
We're just rats caught in a trap.
We will never leave this place!
I hate this place!
It was foolish coming in here unprepared.
<Extremely excited gibberish.>
Get 'em!
Another notch in our belt.
We took down a Dragon! Bet we could make a living doing just that.
They just kept coming. Glad you knew what you were doing.
You're not prepared for a fight with us.
Get ready! That thing's lethal from every angle!
You weren't keeping score, were you? … Me neither.
Much better.
I'm about to dry out.
Don't just stand there!
Ground yourself!
I'm not doing this without you. Get up!
They're all yours!
Watch it! I can't pick you up!
Your spells are all dried up. Watch it!
Keep it together!
Give them everything you've got!
Face my better nature!
I'm with you. Let's do this.
You know, if you need some practice at picking pockets, the Outside Inn is a great place to learn.
No authorities. No castles. No mushroom towers. No crowds. And it's far away from everything. I mean, really—what's not to like about Lilmoth?
I met some mercenaries on the north side of town here once. Sometimes I think I'd have fallen in with them if I wasn't so busy running around with you.
Is it always this crowded?
Eyes up? Weapons ready? We've got this.
Where are you taking me?
Ready.
People talk about finding someone you could share long, companionable silences with. Didn't know what that would be like until … well, just now.
I see something nice. Yours for the taking.
Well, it sure is something. Now what?
Good thinking. Let's thaw out a little before we get moving again.
Getting stronger every day.
You could craft something nice with that.
That jingle of coins. Always a comfort.
Is there any better feeling than finding free stuff?
How'd you get so lucky?
Impressive.
Yes?
Let's hear it.
I'm with you.

I don't like ghosts, ghouls, spirits, what have you. I'm always trying to get them to cross over. Move on.\n\nI'm stubborn, but when I leave this world someday, there's no way I'm coming back to cry and moan about my unfinished business.
I feel like I knew someone like you before I lost my memory. Someone I'm happy to forget.
You ask too many questions. Say less and maybe I'll like you more.
The less we have to say to each other, the better.
Why, are you getting tired of me? If you are, just be straight with it. I've got thick scales.
I'm not used to watching someone else's back. Or having them watch mine.\n\nI don't hate it.
You seem the type to have a lot of friends in a lot of places. Don't know why I'm one of them, but I'm glad I am.
Come on, do I have to say it? You could run straight into Oblivion or worse, and I'd be right there with you.
I guess we could do that.
Fine. Only because it's you asking.
Well? I'm here.
What a waste of time.
Can't stand all that clicking.
Give it a rest!
Just keep knocking them down. That's how we stay in business.
If only the rest of Morrowind lived like these Ashlanders. Still wouldn't see fit to call the place home, but it'd be far more bearable to visit.
If only the rest of Morrowind lived like these Ashlanders. Still wouldn't see fit to call the place home, but it'd be far more bearable to visit.
These trees really can grow in all sorts of places, can't they? All they need is proper maintenance from someone who cares enough to see them thrive.
Well, if it isn't my second-favorite Khajiit.
Don't spend all of that in one place.
Good eye.
There's strength in numbers. Good thinking.
That was embarrassing.
Looking stronger already.
Charged up? Then we're ready to go.
Re-up that enchantment before you're caught without it.
Good on you. You're ready for anything.
Well, aren't you lucky?
Big beast. Big loot.
Gorgeous catch. If it wasn't worth so much, I'd say let's eat it right here.
Patch up that gear, if you know what's good for you.
That gear of yours won't hold out much longer.
Hey, hey. Why are you throwing away perfectly good coin?
Never figured you as one to line their pockets.
Picking at bones is a waste of time.
Guess you think they should work smarter, not harder.
Don't need an excuse to just go fishing instead.
It's just going to get messed up the first scrap we get into.
Always found it funny how curious people get about what happened to the Dwemer. How they just up and disappeared one day.\n\nI hope they find out, so maybe they can do the same.
Mevei and Federo. Who would have thought they'd be the ones lighting the way forward?\n\nAnd when they need someone with my set of skills, I'll be right there with them.
Perhaps a tactical approach.
I could write a dozen papers no one will ever read on that beast.
I thought they were illimitable!
This is intolerable!
Distressing. Most distressing!
And that's done. What's next?
Appreciate the top up!
Ah, losing vitae here!
Increase your mobility!
Attention here, hey!
Reject necrosis! Rise to the occasion!
Superlative!
Heal your trauma!
You're oozing magicka there. Top up!
You seem knackered!
How imposing! Hah!
Ruinous Ebullition!
A peerless duo!
The architecture is exquisite, true. But try finding spellthread on short notice and you'll see why Sentinel and I do not get along.
Erm, let's avoid the Mages Guild tower here if you don't mind. Soothsayer Erralle and I have … history.
Sage advice: avoid that sweet roll mead Sirirenna pushes at the Kaladas Inn. Yech.
Planning to improve your equipment while we're here? Smart.
Eyes open. Books, letters, scrolls, tomes … you know what I'm after.
I'll let you take the reins. Happily.
How do you drive this thing?
Being brilliant and growing up in the middle of nowhere is … well, I don't recommend it. It turned out all right in the end though. I've been to more realms than we had structures in the village!
Hmm. Might be valuable.
This is pleasant. Now we just need to brew up some tea.
Enlightenment! Progress!
Quality material makes for quality goods.
Did that creature offend you somehow?
Ah, spiffing! More coin for your purse.
That could prove useful in our work.
An unanticipated windfall!
Mora has his eyes on you. I can feel it.
This creature serves Apocrypha. Why are you here? Speak, damn you!
What a well-formed aberration! Delightful in its symmetry! And look at the way its little nose twitches. Heh!
What? What? What?
Speak. I'm listening.
I am familiar with that expression. Something's up.

Well as you know, I'm always looking to fund our research. I hear people pay good coin for a little enchanting expertise these days. Writs, you know? With our combined acumen, we could accrue investments ad infinitum!
We are not friends. Please cease your prattle.
Let's keep the chatter to a minimum, if you don't mind.
You've given me cause for concern. Reconsider your actions in the future.
Favorably. Why? Do you have cause to think otherwise?
Cordial. Engaging. Jocular? Intellectually stimulating!
I believe, in the fullness of time, only Martina was as close a collaborator. You're in rare company.
I am uncomfortable expressing the level of appreciation I have for you in my life. I hope you can respect that. You … you're great.
Mm-hmm.
For you cohort? Any time.
Arcanist here.
Distrust. Disquiet. Detestation!
Disgusting creatures.
Ugh. Don't throw up. Don't throw up.
Big stink. Even bigger corpse.
Peerless work. If I publish a paper about this experience, do you want co-credit?
Unsurpassed. Our research into thaumaturgical infusion is coming along nicely.
Do we have time to interrogate some of the locals? Think of the mystic quandaries we could resolve!
Hmm. You never forget this particular smell. Dry desert air and farm animals. Reminds me why I left.

There's an old theory saying these wells marked lines of magical power. Most modern researchers hold this idea in contempt, but I believe there may be some truth to this notion. More research is indicated.
Standing stones exist all across Tamriel, and regional scholars have chosen to affiliate them with regional concepts. For example, some stones in Cyrodiil are mythically aligned with former Emperors.
Like a hound on a scent, we're on the move. History is our prey.
I have enough notes from this extra-planar excursion to write a paper and a half. At least. Exquisite.
And tranquility descends. Let's make off with our ill-gotten gains while we can.
Hmm. Sublime technique there.
Tantalizing! Marvelous! Truly glorious!
Hmm. Think I've read that one before.
Refreshing! Take it in. An opportunity for learning.
Hah! Better to be in our hands than lining the chests of those Psijic cretins.
Hmm. I'm not sure that's to my taste but I bet you'll make it well.
To align runes that powerful takes a resolute hand and a steadfast disposition. Peerless.
Exemplary! Mythical! Phenomenal!
Ahh, yes. I'm intrigued to see how this fits into your combat schema. What will you do now?
Modifying your implements to fit your needs is shrewd, cohort. But how will this fit into your schema? Let's see ….
That smells delicious. I recognize the extreme value it represents, both in potent mysticism and resources. But could I have a nibble?
Spectacular scent profile. I would savor every note. Well done.
I'm no expert in trinket valuation, but I know magic!
There are people here that would see me quite cadaverous! Deceased. Demised!
They seemed a bit suspicious to me.
Was that prudent?
A game? Cohort, we have research to do.
Eww. Be sure to wash your hands.
Ahh, coffee. Tastes like the brine of Apocrypha.
Yech. Smells like the Deadlands.
I find tea-making quite meditative, you know. Calms the mind. Heating the water, placing the bag. \n\nSugar or milk, or not. Helps me to focus.

Perhaps someday I'll perfect my research, and understand fate in the way that Hermaeus Mora does. \n\nIn any case, I've decided my failure is its own kind of epiphany. After all, without my misadventure we never would have met!
Much to learn from that one.
How stimulating. Look at this place.
What a performance. Imagine what it'd be like with music!
I scryed. I read. Now I look. For you.
Oh! You startled me sneaking up like that. But sneaky is good. Look there, sneakily ….
They told me I was crazy. Mad. But look! I found the Prince of Knowledge.
Don't look at me like that. I'll prove it!
Let the new blood take first watch. Anything happens, that's just one less share to worry about.
We're not really going to kill any more of the hostages. Are we?
Divine and wise Prince, so full of divinity and wisdom! I pledge myself to your service!
Are you a monster? No matter. Just keep away from me!
I don't want to hurt you, but I won't be responsible if you don't go away!
Suffer!
I do not trust these mortals. Most of them serve Peryite.
Bah. Is there no foe worth my blade here?
Another den of iniquity purged for the glory of the Kindred!
We've done good work here. But much remains to be done.
You will regret interrupting me, trespasser!
Feel the fury of my arcane powers!
Only the chosen few can understand my secrets.
No, impossible…
I've just learned a new spell. Care to see it?

Next thing that'll happen is that every word in this city of the dead comes to life and hunts every mortal down. That'd be fun.\n\nNo, it wouldn't be fun. If you think it'd be fun, please venture elsewhere.

Look at you! I bet you've done something you're proud of recently. You have that air. If it had anything to do with ending whatever caused the locals to get upset, you have my deepest gratitude.\n\nNow to find a new place to call home.

The priests here are wonderful about ensuring that funeral processions are properly observed. Well, most days.\n\nI once saw a couple of priests force a procession to turn around. And by once, I mean within a handful of hours ago.

The bard funeral processions here are my favorite, I think. Music, singing, dancing, and all kinds of stirring performances capture and share the life of the deceased, both during the procession and at its end.
I saw an Ashlander the other day. Surprising, considering that few make their homes here in the Telvanni Peninsula. We had a nice chat while he looked over my goods.
The other day, I'd run into at least five priests before breakfast. Now I'm lucky if I see one all day.
Sometimes the insects crawling on the produce here will swirl off in a cloud of glittering wings. Or so the farmers who bring in the goods tell me. I've yet to see such a spectacle.
Despite all the strong feelings drifting about and disturbing the peace here in Necrom, I'm sure it will come through just fine. Now, as to the people here, well, that's a different matter.

I wonder sometimes if having a lot of the dead in one place will draw things people find unsavory. Were I them, I'd set up a lot more guardians around here.\n\nPerhaps something like draugr. That might work.
Do I know what's happening in Necrom? Yes. And no.\n\nYou're in a position to find out more outside this refuge. Why do you linger down here? No, don't answer. That's rhetorical.
Where should I venture next? And what history will I observe as it spins out from present to past?\n\nI hope to see you again—possibly in the thick of new events, I'd hope.
Savor that, cohort. Every cup is a new and singular experience.
If you put that on a weapon, just be careful not to nick yourself. I'm speaking from experience, here.
You've got to watch those enchantments of yours more closely.
Need some words of wisdom, eh? Keep your botched potions. You can pour them on visitors who won't get off your front step.
Every dream becomes a nightmare!
Nightmare copies of Shelreni's body. Gather their energy!
Let me end your suffering!
You cannot resist my power!
Ah. Wrong coordinates.
See more of Telvanni Peninsula on my friend Trinni here. She's got a smooth gait and can soothe even the most anxious of passengers with her sonorous calls.
This will make you feel much better, I assure you.

You're just in time to embark on a wondrous trip through the Telvanni Peninsula and see what Necrom has to offer you.\n\nDon't let the idea of a city of the dead put you off. And Bittersweet here would love for you to join her.
You dare try to steal knowledge from me!
These pages reveal your doom.
Most disappointing.
Now my chapter ends.
This place is forbidden, your presence is unwelcome.
The trespasser is stopped. The secret is safe.
Are you sure you know where you are going?
Everything's going dark ….
You look like you know what you want. Good I like that in a customer.
Once more.
I've just learned a new spell. Care to see it?
Who challenges the Dreamcarver Clan?
Vaermina's dreams will break you!
All fall to the power of Valkynaz Dek!
Vaermina! Claim your servant's soul!
Dinner is served!
Don't these guardians know their master disappeared years ago?
Kill … fate's flea!

So many of Tamriel's citizens focus entirely on our masks. Beguiled by the supposed truth they hide. How mundane. Why not focus on our hands? Find the art in a palmed card. The beauty in a lute player's calluses. \n\nThat is where our truth lies.

A solo tour is a rare delight for one such as myself. There is no greater test of one's skills than to take to the stage without a safety net. No dashing juggler. No fanciful furry companion. Only your wit and your grace. I do adore the challenge.

Rinyde has begun teaching entry-level courses at the College of Sapiarchs. Can you imagine? Sweaty palms teaching young Summerset elites. I'm so proud of her. She may have doubted her abilities, but not once did I waver.\n\nShe's special, that one.
A clear horizon, a steady wind, salt spray in the air …. There's nothing that compares to being at sea.
I've got an itch to sail the Padomaic Ocean. Point the bowsprit at the sunrise and keep on until I find something worth seeing.
I've had some time to think about the relic we found at Betnikh. I said some hard things to you that day. But I understand why you made the choice you did.
Regret is the most pointless mortal delusion of them all. The past is written. You can't change it so why fret about it?
My leftmost tentacle is shorter than it used to be. Either I was careless in reconstituting myself or this realm's dimensionality is beginning to fail.\n\nMust be the latter.
Strange to encounter you here, mortal. I imagine Hermaeus Mora anticipated our meeting when he sent me to observe this realm. So, don't mind me. I'm just going to stare.
I command nature itself!
Never a bad time to cast some lines.
Your ashes will be scattered to the farthest corners of the world.
Never trifle with gods!
I'm done toying with you. Die!
Some version of me will fight again.
I create my own order.
My ink is more versatile than you know.
I inhabit records of the Scaled Court.
Train your body for agony.
Ink can cut deep.
I'll write this ending myself.
Let us test your patience.
So, you can put up a fight.
We are cyclical. We cannot be killed long.
Does killing things make you strong?
Oh no, not another Tho'at!
This won't be the last time we face each other.
You're not what I search for.
I am everywhere. I am eternal!
You cannot harm me in any meaningful way.
Your tenacity is delightful.
Activating kinetic barrier.
Additional targets deployed.
Puny weakling! Xeemhok feast on your flesh!
Join us in the azure world!
She's destroying the building!
Why is she making this happen again?
Don't breathe that.
I don't even need the Blade to best you!
I don't even need the Blade to best you!
Why resist? Your deaths are assured.
Consume their souls!
Good, it's you. You can help me. You helped me before when everything was disorganized. You will help again, right?
You're here? But there's nothing I need you for right now. You're not supposed to be here unless I need you. This isn't where you're supposed to be. You have to leave. Now. \n\nPlease.
I wish I could go with you, but that involves going out there. With all the chaos. And the disorder. Books everywhere. No thank you. \n\nI'd rather translate Goblin folk tales.
Back again? I knew you'd succeed! Never doubted it for a second.
Death won't be the end for you. You will serve me for as long as your body remains.
You'll never leave this place. Not alive, anyway.
None of you will survive this.
My light will feast on your flesh!
Reduce the mortals to dust!
Nirn and Coldharbour shall be one!
I will not be contained!
I shine in perfect glory!
Deliver me her strength!
Water knows how to obey, and blood is its cousin.
You will know the sun's fury.
Flame is the vengeful weapon of light.
Her power courses through me!
All must kneel before the Lady of Infinite Energies.
Her will is eternal and her reach endless. Submit.
Aurorans! To me!
My prey never escapes!
The dark of Coldharbour take you!
This spell will break you.
Perish in Coldharbour's flame!
Nool—golaraj ra'ham!
That goat's been eating my sweetrolls!
I'll make good gold from chopping you up.
Argh!
The struggle only makes your flesh taste sweeter.
Let us see what challenge you offer me.
All this effort for naught.
For some reason, I expected Tho'at's presence to feel more viscous.
Step up here when you're ready. I won't use the nymic until you're set.
I read all that you are. I command you to come here!
You see what happens when you come into my home uninvited!
Maligraphies aren't the only trouble here. You could take the second portal. The filers say there's a Verse in it for you.
Delicious!
You cannot run!
Don't be shy. It's almost time for dinner.
Come to me morsel!
No, no, no! You die now!
Leave me to this empty existence!
See these? All mine. Could be yours. Need to give me something that's of equal value. No fakes! Counterfeits are valueless—don't want them. \n\nSo? Do we have an exchange?
They say the north wind cuts right through you. Let's find out.
A flash of pain and the creeping dread of poison in your veins.
Consume the fire or be consumed by it.
The snap of lightning's jaws sinks deep.
The lurcher embraces death every fall and rises anew. It will be no different for you.
You have paid the price they paid.
Feel the weight of our loss!
A cold heart does not numb this pain!
My tears cling to everything, and drown it in my sorrow.
I have mastered Oblivion, now I will master you!
The order's honor is avenged.
Show your back and die!
You got lucky this round. I can't wait 'til next time.
I may be small, but I am merciless!
Before I learned to levitate, I was forced to rely on witless fools to get me where I needed to go. Independent movement is not an ability to take for granted.

Apparently just killing a bunch of Dragon cultists did not permanently remove the curse as I had hoped. I need to do a bit more research. \n\nIn the meantime, I am comfortable here. It's certainly better than a few caves I've had to hide in.
A pleasant abode, a chance meeting, a charming conversation. Just the diversion Mizzik needs to clear his head before his next investigation!

Mizzik has been thinking about his name. One does not hear thunder until it is already upon you, yes?\n\nSo it will be for Mizzik Thunderboots. Scoundrels cannot hide from the sound of thunder! A much better quality than quaking at its approach.

If only every perpetrator was as careless as Rideza the Rogue. But if every investigation were as easy as following jelly footprints, one supposes there would be no need for investigators like Mizzik.

Bretons and Orcs think they live so differently from one another. Your average stronghold chieftain isn't so different from any duke or baron. Pampered milksops surrounded by leagues of women who could do their jobs ten times better.
I think everyone should learn how to fight. Not for some worthy cause or anything as noble as that. But for yourself. For the people you care about. Things that actually matter.

The first time a woman in a tavern chatted me up instead of Darien, it kind of drove him crazy. My face might look like a durzog's backside compared to him, but some ladies just like more meat on the bones, you know?\n\nHe had to learn to respect that.
I'm a researcher, not a fighter!
Over here, you useless thesaurus!

Back and ready to clear more Maligraphies out of the Infinite Archive? Are you in it for the rewards? Or, do you just like hunting copies of Tho'at Replicanum?\n\nEither way, your work allows me to do mine and that's what matters.
You're already taking steps to improve. Next time, the outcome may be different.
Ooh! Confidence. Do you have the skill to back it up?
These maligraphies are tough, but I've seen you defeat greater challengers.
You're a good sport. Fighting well beyond where you could stop to save face against an opponent is worthy indeed. With some more practice, you'll be a great duelist as well!
I'm shocked. To think that I've gone so long since suffering a loss. \n\nWell, I'll just have to use this as motivation to better myself. Next time our paths cross, I will be ready.
We won. Well, you won. I helped.
I need to research Tho'at Replicanum more. Her abilities elude me.
When you continue, take care. I know better than to hope other maligraphies won't stand in your way.
We're part of something bigger. I know it.
I can't wait for the last memory to fall into place.
Keep sharp. Don't lower your guard.
A day of reckoning is coming. You'll see.
You see one ancient ruin, you've seen them all.
The Recollection gave me a purpose.
Those who refuse to remember must be swept aside.
The Recollection knows the path to power.
Just try to keep us from restoring our heritage.
They took our memories.  We're taking them back.
I don't suppose you want to join the winning side?
Do you like my construct? It is quite imposing.
I have competent Wood Elves by my side. You have an Orc with delusions of power.
The Recollection remembers, but you were forgettable.
Over already? But we were just getting started.
Looks like my oath was stronger than yours.
Show them what losing looks like.
We couldn't keep one of them alive?
You don't have to die.
I don't know what you're complaining about, this is lovely!
Let's end this quickly.
Aradros must know something we don't. Otherwise, why are we here?
There's more here.
Anyone else hear that strange voice? Just me?
Trying to make me mad? It's working.
For the pack!
What's that supposed to be? A challenge? I'll take it.
Die in the Lodge of the Axe!
You mock my skills. I will burn the life out of you.
You will taste fire!
You made your choice when you came here. Don't hesitate now.
You lost the Trial of Blood.
The one who bleeds the least wins this fight.
I've had ages to strategize, you only moments. Don't rush.
Controlling the battlefield means little if you're dead.
Defeat me and control the battlefield to win.
Are you too scared to attempt the trial?
Cut off the head and the army crumbles.
The size of our atronach armies determine the victor.
Mercy comes later. Right now we have a mission.
This is where I was supposed to be all along.
I'm not afraid to die. Not if the Recollection needs me to.
Why did we draw the boring watch?
I'll just have to treat this like a cliffhanger.
I'm fading. I can't hold out much longer.
Not again. Bring me back together. Please.
It will take far too long to manifest now.
Don't let the ghost lights get away.
Did the frog do this?
Looks like I'll have to start from the beginning.
Faster. There's treasure on the line.
If anyone asks, I wasn't scared. This is a defensive maneuver.
Maybe I can reform myself soon.
Don't let them get away!
You're lucky all I did was scatter. Well? Help me.
You're too slow. Now we can't play.
If you don't help us, we will haunt you.
Fix what you broke!
We remember and will have our revenge!
Mora's bonds weaken. Our Prince will soon be free!
Make Apocrypha suffer for Mora's audacity!
Memories rush in, but are they real?
Our Prince's scion calls us to battle!
Shardborn! Slay all in your path!
Time to make them all remember!
Remind these curs that we are Shardborn!
You return. Tell me, has the assignment been completed?

The wilds of West Weald have become increasingly more dangerous. I assume by your dress and weaponry, you're no stranger to trouble. Still, it pays to be cautious.\n\nShould you survive and do well, I'm sure we can extend this arrangement.
You have the look of someone who likes to get things done. Care to help out the Imperial Legion and earn some gold along the way?
All of my tasks have been dealt with for the moment. Return later and I am certain to have something else for you to do. Count Calantius and the Imperial Legion appreciate your interest.
Welcome back. West Weald hasn't crumbled yet, so I trust you bear good news?
Remember, the Legion is relying on you. Moreover, I am relying on you. Please, do not become another problem for me to solve.
Joining the Legion was supposed to be a great honor. I never imagined it would be this stressful.\n\nHonestly, West Weald faces threats on all sides and the Legion could use all the help we can get.
Thank you for your service to the Legion. I have many reports to complete at the moment and I'm terribly behind on my paperwork. I'm sure I'll have a need for you again soon.
I'm pleased to see you, hero. The Daedra of Mirrormoor continue to attack West Weald. If you're willing to help out, I can promise you another battle. And another reward.

An Imperial Legion feeds on paperwork, hero. We both know perfectly well that we need fighters like you out in the field, but I'm not authorized to hire any more adventurers today.\n\nTry again tomorrow.

Follow the sounds of fighting—you'll find an incursion soon enough.\n\nDefeat the Mirrormoor champion leading the attack, and you defeat its incursion. But first, you need to kill the Shardborn valkynazes protecting the champion. Good luck!
Onsi be praised! You return on your feet, not on a stretcher. Tell me, adventurer, were you successful?
We're going somewhere quieter, it's too crowded here.
This won't do. Only two arms? No.
Thanks for helping me with the tomeshells. You can have your silly form back now.
What? You didn't kill them all? Ugh, come back here.
Your turn to hunt the tomeshells. I'm on my break.
Follow my lead!
I know a trick. Let me help!
Stay away from those sweetrolls!
Stop running away!
First you take my sweetrolls and now you take my wife?
Finally! I'll be more successful without his dead weight.
Go get the cookpot!
You lead while I look around.
Something feels wrong about this tree.
The corruption's too strong! Please help!
Those roots nearly devoured me. Thank you, traveler.
You'll pay for disturbing us!
You will feel a mother's vengeance!
Did you see that?
You'll be a layer of ash.
Take a peek in that barrel. I'm sure it's harmless.
The fires will turn you to ashes!
I think my mother's calling me!
The sky will wipe away your defiance!
Those fools in Skingrad will bow to the Recollection!
Succumb to my illusions!
My roots will destroy you!
Fall before the Recollection!
My death is just the beginning!
Everything's all fuzzy ….
Where … am I?
The voices … are gone!
We're … free at last!
I thought we'd be under their spell forever! Thank you, friend!
I'd almost forgotten what a clear mind felt like. Thank you.
What is going on over on Valenwood's borders? What does it mean?
Read this. Remember that. I have so many better things to do.
You never saw me, understand?
You protected eons of knowledge from devastation.
Ah, I was just about to join in, but I see my services are unneeded.
Not many books misplaced here. Shouldn't be difficult to clean.
This is the most violence the archive has ever seen. That's a thought worth filing.
Nothing is safe here!
You're ensured to do your part, I merely seek to oversee it.
Don't start without me!
This place looks fantastic. My organization really works.
Be careful and try not to cause any more disarray.
Attend to the fray.
This is just the sort of excitement we needed here.
This wing is particularly flammable. Try not to set anything alight.
Try not to get ink everywhere.
Burn one and two more sprout!
Bah, who needs schooling? Especially when I am plenty smart already!
I hear there are Daedra roaming the wilds.
I need a good wallow in the mud.
Soon, I'll have more than rags to wear. My husband is extremely wealthy. And very late.
Maybe I should try the battlegrounds ….
Is there supposed to be a forest southwest of the city?
Colovians are stuck-up prigs.
Let's toast a hard day's work!
Is the devastated area spreading?
Y'ffre smiles on those who share their bounty, traveler.
Arguments among the clan are the worst.
I hear a spinner has a new tale to tell us!
The greenspeakers are investigating the devastated area.
Maybe I'll go back to the vineyard for a bit. The wine here is watered down with tears.
Can't the Mages Guild do something about the Daedra?
Baan Dar's playing tricks on me again. I can't seem to win a Tribute match here.
I hear the Colovians plan to drive us out.
I may need to range deeper into the new forest for game.
All who come in peace are welcome in Vashabar!
In Vashabar, we respect the Green Pact.
Any gold to spare?
For a few coins, you can buy the satisfaction of knowing you helped someone in need.
Scars are just reminders of things that didn't kill you.
Everyone expects a healer to be compassionate, even if we're not.
The Legion could use more recruits.
I should remember to take some food to the grape stompers.
Always give your opponent a fighting chance.
The world just seems gray when my dearest is gone.
I could go for a glass of wine right now.
Work hard enough and you'll be rewarded.
My ancestors will be so pleased with these gifts.
I suppose you're right.
Who knew a Dunmer would find a place with the Bosmer?
Boils are the mark of a true follower of the Blighted Lord! Come, share in the bounty!
Isn't the smell of gold wonderful?
Lord Sanguine, hear my prayer.
I'd never make a good legionary.
They are serving roasted steaks for dinner. I should really make sure we have enough red wine.
Narsis Dren? A fabulist, of course, but there are bits of truth in his wild tales.
Are the quarriers starting trouble again?
I can't wait for the next vineyard expansion. More vines means more grapes means more wine!
My family had an estate once. The Shadowed Path burned it down.

Ugh, please don't remind me of the town gowns. I know I designed them, but they're incredibly out of season. Why did I ever think draping sheer linen was a good idea? \n\nNo matter. Skingrad's fashion only moves forward, as do I.
Why does no one get out of the way?
Sometimes you only need a friend to hear your sorrows.
This one wonders what the count plans to do about that jungle.
This one can be quite stealthy when she puts her mind to it.
So much fighting for Zayabazi. Reaper's March, Valenwood, the Imperial city. All for a soldier's dinner.
This one heard about a new forest and had to come see!
Where does the count expect these newcomers to sleep?
When the mistress of the house says jump, I ask how high.
A bad day fishing is never truly bad.
The work never ends.
At least all this lifting keeps me fit.
I feel like singing!
Strike first, question later, I always say.
Skingrad is an oasis of peace and calm in a world of strife.
That's slander, friend.
I must have taken a wrong turn.
Skeevers, they're everywhere!
My knees creak like the mast of a ship.
I have so much to do! So many irons in the fire right now! So much to be done!
My swords are too heavy? Perhaps his arms are too weak.
He took my book. It had all my notes.
Better hang on to your coin purse, friend.
There is never enough time to do things right, but always time to do things over again.
My master told me to be worthy of my weapon.
Anyone see my Book of Circles?
Hard work is honorable, but innovation is rewarded, too.
So tired. I must have the fever.
Tall Papa be praised, the fever passed me by.
Like the serpent god Satakal, my hunger knows no bounds.
Crafting is a beautiful thing.
All we do is work and work.
Anything happening at the Stonechip today?
Colovian bows are adequate, but Redguard crafting is superb.
That hint of citrus, perfection!
I wonder where the Legion will send me next?
Dice, cards, wagers … doesn't matter. I can't win a thing.
Have you become acquainted with others of my kind? \n\nWe were filers, but with the current ailments within our archive, I shudder at what purposeless creatures we are now.
Master Malkhest may be an excellent researcher, but he is ill-equipped for the perils of battle. You know what I'm referring to.
This is my favorite room in the entire archive. The Index is useful and there's limited books to file. I can relax here.
Don't try to comprehend the scope of our responsibilities. Last time Master Malkhest tried, he had to lie still with his eyes closed. Infinite is not a misnomer.
This should be refreshing!
Don't fight it. You never stood a chance.
Time to sweep you away.
Come on! My blade's still sharp.
Don't forget about me.
Going through all those portals really messed with my sense of direction.
I don't feel a breeze on my face, that's weird.
Sighted ones!
The Blind warned us about you!
Ah yes, studying your opponent. Not a strategy that guarantees success.
That is a Mind Terror. I'd tell you what they're capable of, but you'll see soon enough.
Well, master. What will we do now?
I hope you learned from that last fight.
You were weak. Ingrates! The lot of you.
Cut them in the name of the Blind!
I should be by the Blind's side.
We won't be stopped!
Why couldn't we stay with the Blind, doesn't she need our assistance?
The path will continue.
Watch where you step. I think I nearly fell off the edge there.
Surrender to the path or die!
Be quiet! We don't want to be discovered.
Bravado and confidence often get confused. But we'll see which one you have.
Ooh, you are feeling confident.
Impress me!
Strike true and cast quickly!
I'm not going to be intimidated by a flag!
This will not end well for you!
You cannot hide from me!
I will break you!
Submit!
Bathe in the hail of sorrows!
Moonlight cannot thwart me!
Stay alert, my friend.
Move along. This doesn't concern you.
Let's find Grivier and Tham.
They captured me and were taking me to Fort Colovia. Thank you.
Doom is upon you. You will drown in shadow and blood!
Cremation ruins meat, but it's fun!
Lifeforms detected.
Engaging threat.
Divide … by … zero.
Grakh vahg nool! You die now!
I taste your power! It bellows loudly as you slake its hunger! But mine is insatiable!
Hold still, now. What comes next will not be … pleasant.
I'm not complaining, I just think Aradros should let some of us stay in the warmest room here.
Ugh, Hurthan keeps looking at me. What does he want?
Leave no one alive.
Stop the intruder!
Did you see what I did to that last Orc? Incredible, right?
Aradros never tells us what the plan is. Is asking for details too insubordinate?
The pit is ours!
Killing you will be easy.
I'm not looking forward to burying all these Orcs.
Who built all this? The Orcs? I didn't think they had the skill.
Aradros doesn't want to be bothered.
We have guests.
I'm used to trees, but these rock structures aren't half bad.
I've never tried it, but I wonder how long it'd take to saw through one of these Orcs.
We've got a fight on our hands.
There's more over here!

I would sell you a map of the Infinite Archive, but it won't fit on your mortal papers. \n\nBesides, the scribes who went in there last haven't returned. You'll just have to be content with everything else I have available.
Is that your protection? It's bad. Very bad. Azimurr doubts it can withstand the claws and fangs of West Weald's beasts. But you came for Azimurr's armor. This is good. Very good.
I love selling swords because they bring in my sharpest customers. People who want mauls are too blunt and staff buyers are so wooden.\n\nI joke! All my patrons are lovely.
Not enough time! Much healing to do today.
Skingrad has so many threats right now. An overly aggressive forest, strange new animals, and Daedra everywhere you look. Don't know about you, but I want my possessions safe in times like these.
Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh. Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh.
There really is a forest where the rolling hills and vineyards used to be. It's amazing! And sort of scary. Where did it come from, I wonder.
All these new faces in the city really should watch their coin purses more closely. Makes my tail twitch seeing so many unsuspecting newcomers. Out of concern, of course.
You spill one bottle of priceless Colovian wine, and you never live it down. My employer has been calling me Awkward Augun for weeks now.
Just as the wind makes a dune walk across the desert, troubles drive my people to strange lands. West Weald isn't what I would choose for children of Yokuda, but here we are.
I suspected the miracle of Dawnwood was too good to be true. To think that a Wood Elf king would unleash something like the Wildburn!
Lately I have heard tales about dark plots and great deeds in this land. I have a feeling you played no small part in these doings, stranger.
Tall Papa warns us not to consort with Daedra lest they lure us away from our walkabouts. So whatever mischief the Recollection was involved in, it's good they were stopped.

I've run with some gutless petal-pickers in the past. You know where they are now? Begging for scraps in Riften. Or dead. Well, maybe one's arranging flowers for a soft Skingrad noble.\n\nPoint is that you gotta live life with your tusks bared.
Ontus is overflowing with new arrivals. I suppose I'm one, too, although I keep a lower profile than these Redguards. My employers generally prefer discretion in my line of work.
I do my work and rush right home. The fever isn't going to catch me!
Have you heard about all the workers who died? They say it's some kind of illness!
I yearn for the day when the Prince of Trickery brings me to his side. I will stroke the fur of Barbas, and enforce my master's pacts on Nirn. That day cannot come soon enough.
I wonder if I should resign from the Legion and stay here in Ontus to help my family. I like being a soldier, but my father needs me.
Maybe if those stinking travelers actually had to clean up their own messes, they would stop tracking filth through my freshly cleaned town!

All my life, I've loved fish. Not fishing—the creatures themselves. Oh, not to eat! They're so agile in the water, easily navigating the currents and waves. If only our lives were as simple as theirs.
Quarrying was all right, but I prefer collecting honey over stacking and chipping rock.
Why do the quarriers and the ranch hands not get along? Just because the bosses are in competition, doesn't mean they have to be, too.
A glass of wine a day keeps the fever away.
Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh. Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh.

Call me Keshu or the Black Fin. I serve as governor of Gideon, but before that, I traveled the world. I was a mercenary, a general. Some say a war hero. That I established the Ebonheart Pact. In truth, that was mostly Jorunn. But I helped. A little.

Prince Irnskar once asked me if I knew his mother. I told the boy the truth. I was in the tent next to Jorunn's on the night he was conceived.\n\nI had forgotten that Nords do not appreciate such stories the way we Saxhleel do.

When I was young, I loosed a wamasu in a hatchery as a prank on our egg-tender. The careless damage it caused ones so young and innocent—I am reminded of it when I think of the Four Ambitions. They deserved better. All of them.

No one believes I'm an assassin with the Dark Brotherhood, but it makes for some rousing conversations in situations like this. Everyone ooo's and ahh's and pretends to be shocked or frightened. It's good for a laugh and they're none the wiser.
Perhaps we ought to do something for the Wood Elves in their time of strife. I'm not sure what though … I'll consult my ancestors at their tomb and see what wisdom they can offer.
With the Legion at our side, I'm positive they'll have this business with the Daedra cleared up shortly. In fact, I think a celebration may soon be in order. I'll alert the ancestors!
Everyone is celebrating, but it feels like a cold wind just passed over me. I can't quite remember what I was doing before this. Strange. I'll have to see what wisdom my ancestors can offer.

As much as I try, I'm not really the sneaky type. Oh, I can be invisible in the forest when I'm hunting a rabbit, but sneaking up on someone marked by the Sacrament? No, I'm more of a rush-in-and-crack-your-skull kind of guy. It gets the job done!
I prefer to stay out of current affairs. My job's easier the less I know about my targets.

Whether or not Skingrad is at war with its neighbors, there will always be work for assassins here. Politicians have opponents, soldiers hold grudges, and Colovians have long memories when it comes to the ways they've been wronged.
Those Recollection bandits aren't long for this world. My employer has already provided my next assignment. Excuse me, my blades need sharpening.

Hildegard's family treated her horribly. I've seen many families act that way. Well, not the drinking the blood of were-beasts part, but you know what I mean.\n\nDespite our flaws, our family looks out for each other. Don't forget that, Silencer.

If you see anyone making eyes at my little sister, let me know. Hilde is much too busy and much too werewolf to get involved in any romantic entanglements right now. Just don't tell her I said that. She hates it when I scare off potential suitors.

You're a werewolf, aren't you? I know that look. A hunter's eye. The confidence of a predator. A smell like wet fur ….\n\nSome of my best friends happen to be werewolves! My little sister, in fact. Really. I've got the scratches to prove it!

So, friend. Werewolves. I've done my best to help Hilde with her condition, but neither of us are experts on the subject. If you get the chance, could you have a talk with Hildegard? You know, werewolf to werewolf? Just to compare notes? Thanks!

We're not supposed to talk about it, but you seem friendly enough. My brother Kor and I, we're part of the Dark Brotherhood. And I'm a werewolf. Keep it to yourself and Kor probably won't try to kill you.\n\nProbably.

Visiting the cathedral always makes me wonder if the Eight Divines are friends. Do they get together? Share a meal or a drink?\n\nI like to believe they do. After all, eternity is a long time to spend with people you're not fond of.

My big brother Kor found me at my worst. I'd wandered alone for so long that I forgot how to talk to people. There was no balance between the wolf and the Nord.\n\nHe was kind to me. He understood my loneliness. I think he was lonely, too.
What do you want, traveler? I'm no longer a soldier in the Legion, which means brawling with civilians isn't a punishable offense anymore.
Everyone's in high spirits at the moment, but I need something to settle my nerves. Better get moving before the wine runs out.

You know that cage where you saw me the first time? That area used to be Elam Drals's bedroom. He liked it because of all the space. Kor claimed he got special permission from Elam to build it, but I suspect it involved a weapon and some threats.

Is there space here for Kor and I to do some sparring? We like to stay prepared for a fight and he's the only person I trust when the wolf comes out.\n\nIt should be somewhere with no valuables. Or furniture. Or people. Actually, we'll go outside.

What's the best and worst thing about being a werewolf? I'll go first.\n\nBest. The power and the freedom. I love to howl all night long! Worst. Waking up with mystery bits between my teeth. I don't know about you, but werewolf me isn't a picky eater.
So we're both werewolves. No big deal. It's not like we're suddenly going to transform and tear everything to shreds.\n\nRight? I'm never quite sure of the policies in these instances.
I'm supposed to be taking inventory. If my superiors catch me slacking off, they'll give me double drills when training picks up again.
Don't waste my time with your war stories, traveler. They're all the same. I'd rather drink skeever milk than listen to another one.
How does one get started as an adventurer, I wonder? I just need someone to trust me with some sacred duty or to present me with a epic quest. I would accept it in a heartbeat!
Do not mind the Colovians, traveler. They care too much for names and titles, and not enough for sweet wine and idle moments basking in the sunshine.
Nothing gets my heart pumping as much as watching legionaries in action. I may just have to pick up a sword and join them, although I usually prefer fighting with my fists.
Does the status quo mean nothing anymore? At this rate, I might as well wear my shoes on my head and walk on my hands. By the egg, I can't take this!

Not all Bretons are magical geniuses. I'm walking proof of that. I tried to tell the Legion, but they didn't buy it. Then they gave me robes, served me three meals a day, and I was saluted in the street.\n\nIt's a complicated situation.

It's hard to know who your real friends are here. I grew up in Skingrad, and I'm still not used to the ambition and Imperial fervor. I take a more direct path, but Imperials are swayed by appearances. Don't forget that, traveler.
Ah, the violent tendencies of mortals with much to lose. I'll bring your spoils to Master Malkhest.
Master Malkhest calls these things nymic fragments, but it's more likely that they're paleonymic fragments. Just informing you.

Attempting to ingratiate myself to the local nobility is proving more difficult than I anticipated. I have tried plying them with wine and flattery to no avail. Perhaps I should sharpen my dueling skills. Bah, what am I thinking?!
This is a dark day for the Wood Elves, but there is still much to celebrate. West Weald continues to stand strong, and a dangerous threat has been eliminated. It may even be worth a toast.
I can't do another night in one of Skingrad's cells! They're so cold. My fragile constitution can't take it. Be a friend, and don't share my whereabouts with the Legion, please?
It's best to avoid the wine, if you ask me. Colovians don't hold to the Green Pact, so you can't be sure how they brew their drinks. The trees have long memories, and the Ooze is always waiting.
Oh good, the maligraphy's gone. I can fetch the fragment and return to arranging my wings of the archive.
There are no books up here. I'm too smart for that. Smart enough to take the fragment to Malkhest as well.
What is it? Do you wish to be blessed with Hircine's Gift? Bah, the Father of Manbeasts only bestows such a blessing on those who are worthy. Lycanthropy is not for the faint of heart.

Truly, Skingrad is a city of immigrants. Everyone is welcome here. Even those who have no skills and no apparent use. But I suppose even the dullest knife can still spread butter. Perhaps that is where your path lies, wayfarer.
What brings you to Skingrad, traveler? I must document your journey for my studies! Did you come for work? To join the Legion? To taste the wine? Please, I can't stand the blank pages in my notes!

Raise a toast, traveler! All of Skingrad celebrates today. The Legion has conquered—or, no, that's not right. They vanquished—what was it again? It is becoming difficult to discern when one victory celebration ends and another begins.
I missed the battle? Ah, well. There's always the next one.

The Imperials are strong soldiers, but they lack imagination. When their ranks break on the battlefield, they can't do a thing without a commander's orders. Say what you will about the Nords, but at least our fighters are independent.
Verses and Visions aren't just gifts. They make your fights more interesting. Don't waste them.

Others may not understand it, but I find immense satisfaction in the service of others. There is a joy in a job well-done, even when the task is as menial as sweeping the floor. And I sleep better at night knowing the floor is clean.
Your gifts from Hermaeus Mora are ready for you here.
Servants glean a lot of information, you know. We're always there—sweeping the floors, serving the food—while the Colovian elites conduct their business.
I see you're proving your worth. Glad to see other entities doing their share around here.
Is it true? There is a new Daedric Prince? How can that be? This one does not believe it!
Daedric invaders and Wood Elf plots. It's enough to drive one wild with curiosity, and this Khajiit is no exception. It's an exciting time, no?
Ah, sweet wine and celebration. There is little else this one would ask for, except a story, perhaps? She thinks she is forgetting an enemy that worked with the Recollection.
Some Verses allow you to transform your mortal visage into terrifying creatures. \n\nI always hope those are offered to you. They look like a smashing good time.
Don't underestimate anything in the archive. Just because you defeated an enemy before doesn't mean you will again. I read somewhere that overconfidence has killed more mortals than daedrats. Truly!
When you choose the Verse, do you think the tentacle will disappear? I don't mean to offend Hermaeus Mora, but it is throwing off the balance of this wing.

I'm not going to say that you need to take the Verses. But even if you were strong enough to easily dispatch the maligraphies, would you want to look a gift from Hermaeus Mora in the eye and turn it down?
By all means, keep trying the door. It won't open until the threads tying you to the Index reform.
A sharp sword is a clean sword. Never forget to clean and maintain your equipment between skirmishes. That was the first thing my masters taught me.
I say, leave the Daedra to the Legion. Between them and Tall Papa, we will be safe. I prefer it when the Legion is out of the city, anyway. Makes my line of work easier.
Bear in mind, traveler, a smile is not always sincere, and a simple glass of wine may conceal many things. Especially when it is such a delectable red hue. Hmm, I'm getting thirsty.
I like a heavy sword. My sister says it slows down my attacks, but I like to think my opponents get up a little slower, too. Plus, strong arms mean strong punches.
All this celebrating means the city's going to be a mess tonight. [Sigh.] I suppose I should get back to my post … but no one has to know if I nip a little wine on the way.

I have learned that Colovians appreciate authenticity. That is why I tell them all my goods are genuine Redguard artifacts, even though I make them here in Skingrad. After all, my purse is genuinely empty.
You have no idea who you're tangling with!
I once honed my ax so fine, I sliced a man's hand off and he didn't even notice. It's true! That's what good blade maintenance will get you.
It's easy to find jobs here. Finding anyone who pays enough, that's the hard part.
Criminals like us aren't so hard to get along with. We've got our own rules and traditions here. Just keep moving, carry a sharp blade, and always sleep with your back to the wall.
I don't understand why this place is important.
Careful. You never know what's buried in these old ruins.

My mind drifts like a leaf on the breeze sometimes. I can't help it, leaves are so pretty when they get blown around! Why would I want to be stuck on a branch? Surely it's better to follow the wind!\n\nThere I go again. What were you saying?
An assassin can find work anywhere, if they're clever. Even smaller settlements like this have their tensions. Just need to find the thread and pull on it until it closes around someone's neck.

Every bone is its own work of art. I'm especially fond of the hands. So many interconnected pieces make up the fingers alone! Just think what would happen if one tiny section was out of place. Well, you'd have a broken hand, for starters.
Our work is more vital now than ever. Dawnwood's growth has covered archaeological sites in the area. We have to document every detail before the ruins are completely buried beneath the Green.
If you're ever lost in the woods and need a place to rest, don't trust the birds. They have terrible taste. And by the Green, it's hard to sleep in a tree.

Look, I know it doesn't look appetizing, but I promise my scamp gut rotmeth will change your life. Or at least your taste buds. It leaves a very strong taste in the mouth. I'm still balancing the flavors.
I never thought I'd miss Skingrad, but there's nothing to drink here except fermented milk and meat juice. I'd take an axe to the face for a bottle of wine to toast a job well done.

I still haven't adjusted to the high amount of meat the Wood Elves consume. Last night, I nearly offered to gather some fruit to share with them before I remembered their aversion to harvesting crops. I'll just have to wait for a windfall.
You can relax here, traveler. The clan doesn't bite. Usually. Just don't bring up the Green Pact. Or the Dawnway. As a matter of fact, you should keep your opinions to yourself.
We claim this fort in the name of the Recollection!
The legionaries never knew what hit 'em!
The next legionary I find gets fed to my welwa.
This place, like all of this land, belongs to us!
We recall, we remember!
Those Daedra creatures are helpful, but they still scare me.
The Legion warriors were unimpressive.
They think us small and weak, but we are strong!
Let me guess—you're just looking today. Everyone's always just looking. Might be nice if someone surprised me by buying now instead of just looking.
Any smith can sell you something sharp. But perfect balance? A grip that won't slip, an edge that won't dull? You need Dangurd.
No! They're everywhere!
No! Stay away from me!
Yes, you can make a bog-standard poison from off-the-shelf components. But a careful ingredient selection will make that concoction sing.
No, stay back!
Someone do something!
You saved me! I'll never forget this.
I thought that was the end of me!
I died from exhaustion. And now I am eternally tired. So, you know, boo. Whatever.
For a moment, I thought we'd have a run on Wood Elf deposits in holding. But it looks like they won't be run out of the city.\n\nWhich is good! I don't want them to get run out.
I can no longer accept coin that behaves strangely or comes from worlds outside our own. My apologies for the inconvenience. Happy to take a normal deposit, though.
I like a sense of safety more than danger. People put gold in the bank when they feel safe and take it out when they're in danger. That makes safety better, in my opinion.
You interrupt my devotional activities, traveler. Worry not, the Prince of Fate told me this would occur.
The master of Apocrypha spoke in my ear during my devotions. You seek a game of Tribute. To prove yourself.
Show them your real power, construct!
Fight us yourself!
We better get our share from this auction.
Stay light on your feet, it's still here.
Remember, no one's allowed down here.
Why aren't we allowed to attend the auction?
Valente talks big, but he better follow through on his promises.
Fear tactics only work on cowards.
Anyone have any extra arrows?
Here it comes!
So far, Valente's a better boss than Bogvir ever was.
Lot of powerful vampires attending the auction.
Careful! You're as clumsy as a blood fiend!
I'm so hungry!
Can you imagine? Eat wine sodden mortals and become more powerful!
The blood was on my side. Our fight continues!
You didn't listen. This battle is about territory. I won.
It's not about killing me, it's about having the largest army.
More flames for my war machine!
Claim territory in my name.
Defend yourself!
I thought slacking off during drills would get me kicked out of the Legion. Turns out, that just bought me more training and one-on-one lessons.
Let's burn away the old growth and allow new opportunities to thrive.
<The diminutive construct stands ready, gears furiously churning within.>
The right enchantment can make all the difference in a tough scrape. And believe me, I've seen a few!
Have you heard? King Nantharion turned out to be a cultist! He fled Vashabar. Exciting times, friend. Now, what do you need?
First, war breaks out to the east. Now we have fighting all over West Weald, and I'm stuck here, minding a shop. How boring!
What? Oh, sorry. I can't shake the feeling that I've forgotten something important. Well, no matter. How can I help you, traveler?
Hey there. I'm always buying, and I don't ask awkward questions. What do you say we do some business?
I know some Wood Elves. They're furious with that would-be king of theirs. Furious! Nantharion wore out his welcome in Vashabar.\n\nNow, what do you need?
I'm glad someone dealt with those Recollection fools. But I still hear rumors about strange Daedric knights running around West Weald. What's that about?
I don't know what that whole Recollection business was about, but I'm glad it's over. Some kind of Daedric cult, I guess. Well, whoever they were—good riddance!
(Goblin GIbberish 02)
Malthil is my last wolf. I won't lose her.
The fire will engulf you!
It's not that one. Right, Tutor?
Watch your back!
Which enemy will you focus on?
Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh. Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh.
Behold the power of Mirrormoor!
Fools! I am your end!
You dare defy Mirrormoor?
Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh! Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh!
Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh! Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh!
Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh! Irnak hizaal, sumi zagh!
Champion of Mirrormoor, we summon you!
Champion, we summon you!
Champion, the path is prepared!
Traveler, are you worried about the devastated region? I heard it's growing larger and will soon encompass Skingrad!
Lack of punctuality, incompetency with their weapons, poor hygiene … these new Legion recruits have much to learn.
My tongue thirsts for the sap of the Hist. There is nothing like it here.
There is a difference between admiring the natural world and letting it run amok. It is a distinction the Wood Elves never properly learned.
Skingrad is a lovely place, but I sometimes feel stifled within these walls. In the wilderness outside the city, I can truly be myself.
Our victory is inevitable!
Flee, you mortal fools!
Foolish mortals! This is but the start.
You cannot withstand the coming of Mirrormoor!
We aren't done yet.
Defeated? Think again!
Together, we spell doom!
We strike as one!
Face the wrath of Mirrormoor!
See your doom in the sky!
Your defiance ends now!
Witness Mirrormoor's might!
Your dominance will not last!
You think you're getting the Echonir without a fight? In my realm?
Finally, a real fight!
Fight like my treasures depend on it!
Scatter!
There's no escape.
Time to increase the pressure!
I thought the Atronach would've shattered by now.
I feel the torment from that thing and I like it!
There's a reason he's called Maxus the Many. What was it?
Looks like you found the limit to your army's size!
I missed the sound of those skittering feet!
Remember where the plants and the cleansing pools are!
Your weakness is a disgrace to my blade.
Drown in the blood of your betters.
I'll draw the boundaries of my kingdom with your blood.
A frigid death is more merciful than you deserve.
Don't forget, those spiders hate the light.
That poison is deadly, you shouldn't let it linger.
This fight has plenty of surprises.
As my old magister used to say—I'd rather be drinking than thinking. At least I think that's what he said. He tended to mumble a lot.
The count's a greedy bastard.

I work in the morning for a vintner, who gives me breakfast. I work for a merchant in the afternoon, who gives me lunch. I work for a tavern-owner in the evening, who provides dinner. Three squares, and three salaries! I do all right.
We build our business on trust. Trust and the thickness of our vault walls, of course.
Feel free to browse. I'll try to stay out of your way. You look like someone who knows what they want.
This is the finest Inn in all Skingrad! This structure has stood for a thousand years. With luck and hard work, it will stand for a thousand more!
I just received some new soul gems. See if there is anything here that tickles your fancy. If your fancy needs to be tickled, of course.
We do not apply the word "used" to our stock. Instead we say "vintage" or "well-traveled" or "gently handled."
Have you seen what the other merchants are offering? The clutter from someone's backyard shed or closet! This one only deals with the most reputable of guilds and brings the savings to you.
You think it is easy, stuck here among these Imperials? Their politics are childish squabbling compared to the finesse of the Telvanni Masters.
Do not waste my time. I know my way around various implements, sharp and blunt, and have no qualms about using them.
A brave traveler like yourself might be interested in my more adventurous vegetables.
I just acquired some new items. They have a few leagues and adventures behind them, but they look as good as new.
I've been working this job for many, many years. I know a bit about what I'm selling, and what I have for you are some of the finest wares I've seen in a while.
I have everything that the discerning homeowner needs. You need rocks? I have rocks! You need plants? I have plants! You need weapons? Well, I recommend you find a good blacksmith.
Come, browse my wares. Run your fingers over the materials. Feel that texture. Drink in those dyes. Have you seen anything so wonderful?
Of all the places this one has been, Skingrad is the most appealing. Imperials are quite friendly when they aren't invading lands that do not belong to them.

In the course of battle, it may be necessary to execute a strategic retreat. If you do so, flee as fast and as far as you can. You can do no further harm to your reputation, and if your pursuer catches you, you'll be beaten as well.

When you go into combat, it is not just you that is in the fight. Your family, your teachers, your allies are all there, even if they are not present in the moment. You fight not only for yourself, but for them as well. Remember that.
Count Calantius does not like us, but he recognizes we serve a vital purpose in society. So long as we don't get too successful, he keeps the guards away.
There are those who work in the sunshine and those who work best in the shadows. Myself, I prefer a little shade in which to conduct my industry.
Good to see you again! I think it's again. I am so bad with faces. Not a good trait for someone who depends on repeat business.\n\nEither way, let me help you.
You need to be careful traveling in this area. There are some nasty customers around. Not you, of course. You're one of the nicer customers.
I really shouldn't leave my tools laying around. Watch your step.
Things are getting back to normal, but I still don't trust the Gold Road. I'm staying in Skingrad.
Did you hear? The king of the Wood Elves is dead. But I understand the real power behind the throne in Dawnwood is a Daedric Prince!
I went out to this Dawnwood and found it filled with Wood Elves! They're chasing away the locals! Count Calantius should do something about this!
There's a whole new forest sprouting up near the Gold Road. And that means opportunities! I'm going to head out there and see what I kind of work I can find.
What brings you to Vashabar? A bargain, I'll bet. Well, you have come to the right place. If this old Wood Elf doesn't have it, you probably don't need it!
Maybe he was in the wrong, but King Nantharion gave us incredible opportunities—a new land and a new forest! Now, what can I get for you?
Pity about Nantharion, but at least he improved the neighborhood. Now if someone could only do something about all these Daedra running about!\n\nStill, I have some goods you might be interested in.
Come, look at what I offer. I specialize in furnishings not only from the Highlands, but Valenwood as well. My people keep me well-supplied.
All the sudden changes to Dawnwood interrupted my regular supplies. Fortunately, I've set aside a good amount of back stock.
I regret the damage Nantharion inflicted on West Weald. However, I can happily report that shipments of new merchandise have resumed.
Life in Skingrad has calmed now, but that can always change. If you want reliability, take a look at my selection of furnishings.
Who are you? What do you want? Oh, perhaps need someone to hold something for you? I can do that. Provided you're the trustworthy type.
Can I hold onto something for you? You can't trust anyone these days, what with Nantharion's people scurrying about. Keep your eyes on your belongings.
You heard that Nantharion's dead? I'm not surprised. Nothing good comes of dealing with Daedric Princes. Attracts too much attention.
Things have calmed down since the Wildburn has stopped spreading. There are still bandits and creatures about, so you're best off keeping your valuables safe.
Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh. Irnak Myrr-mahr, suni zagh.
From our three fonts we remake this world.
Furried friends. Defend!
We are everywhere!
I suppose I'm a terrible disappointment to my ancestors. Well, they're not here but you are. What do you need?
This is fine horse-country, friend. Anyone could do well dealing in mounts around here. Even me!
Do not be too swift with the plane or the knife. What you cut away you can never put back.
You picked an exciting time to visit Skingrad, stranger. Oh, they've got their troubles outside the city. But we've never been safer here.
People worry about the Wood Elves. Turns out they're not our enemies—it was King Nantharion! King no longer, or so I hear. Now, how can I help you?
What can I get you, friend? If you're arming yourself for some cultist-hunting, you're a bit late. People are saying that some hero killed their leader Nantharion.
It's funny. That Recollection army and their Daedric allies are on the run. But no one seems to know why they were here, or how they were defeated.
Do you think Kanashurr deserves his fate? Go ahead. Mock and belittle him. Everyone else does.
Tethi grew up in Reaper's March. She has fought Wood Elves more than once. But those Elves never brought a whole new forest to a fight.
Tethi thought for sure there would be war between Skingrad and Dawnwood. Now she hears that Nantharion was the true villain. A crooked tale indeed!
Travel is never safe … especially in these parts, yes? Still, Rakamati knows the routes to get you to your destination without encountering wild beasts.
