Who are you working for? Why attack us?
Mistress Selene forbids me from speaking.
This one needs no more in life! Moon-sugar, wine, and coin!
Those dirty bookmakers look down on us Bosmer. I've lost every single bet I've made!
I understand the Bosmer better now that I'm amongst them. I respect their savage need for survival.
I wish this rabble would stop blocking my view!
The only real world is Satakal. Satakal is the world.
Colovian scoundrels! We will not stand for this!
Prepare to eat mud!
You've shown your strength. I yield.
As long as my lovelies are happy, I'm happy. They mean the world to me.
Not this way! Go back through the cave, towards Two-Blades!
It must be electrifying to watch a master such as I while I work.
Come, fools. What more can you bring to bear?
Wonder how bad the docks are.
Watch out, they're trying to surround you.
May my fortunes take flight!
Luck be with us both!
That was my favorite cart too…
We gain nothing by carrying the grudges of our past.
I have heard that elsewhere, dogs are raced instead of lizards. \n\nCan you imagine? I scarcely believe it!
We're never going to be ready if you keep taking breaks!
Luck be mine!
Fortune favor us!
It's just going to get undone by the next storm anyway…
Have you learned nothing after all these years?
That storm couldn't have been natural.
I wish I was still on my ship… if it was still afloat anyway.
I wonder if we should start rationing now. Who knows when we can get more?
I hope we don't get a harpy infestation from this.
Why are the creatures acting so strangely today?
<<1>>, my daughter. First over the rail in thirty raids.
If there must be an Emperor, best an Elven one, I guess.
The Altmer are in for a surprise. Not all Bosmer will be as accepting of their stone buildings and formal ways.
This town would be lovely if it didn't rain so much.
Happy? I won't be happy until we craft enough weapons to put a dagger through the eye of every living thing on Nirn.
They will rot in the library forever.
I could read these books forever.
When you walk in the room, everyone "leaves" don't they?
Stop making excuses! Why did you come to Coldharbour?
Yes.
Leja said you'd come. Let's head to the guardhouse!
If you want that ash, you're going to have to fight me for it!
This one is thinking, a boat with many sails, yes. A boat that moves fast.
Woe is <<1>>! Beset by a winged menace!
Let us pray this time of trouble passes.
When will this end?
Maybe if I sang to the fish? Maybe?
Yes!
There will always be good meat and a shady tree for our friends, but it is getting a little crowded around here.
I don't mind the Altmer; it's the Khajiit I don't trust.
"An exotic locale will inspire you." "The fresh air will help you finish your novel."\n\nIdeas are only bad if acted upon.

Whatever you do while here, please do your very best to monitor your use of the school of Destruction.

There would be something of an outcry if a tree were to be injured.

Now, go on—what can I do for you?
There's a bad wind in the Vale. I don't like it. Not one bit.
I've never seen the Wilderking, but surely the magic of these trees is sight enough.
Tell me what it is you do all day. Tell me, in as excruciating detail as you can manage, what you do for the Guild.\n\nAnd if it's worth it, we'll reward you.
New orders. No one gets through the Orchard. No one.
Kill the invaders!
If we can fix these ships, maybe we can get out of here and break the curse.
Molag Bal will reward me when I add you to his army.
Look at you! So brave, so determined! I'm going to enjoy making you cry.
It must be a relief not to have Titanborn following you around like a lost puppy.
This is all my fault. I should've burned that map.

It's hard to imagine how things came to be such a mess in Hectahame.

And, of course, we have you to thank for delivering us from the undead menace.

We'll take care of the leftovers. You've already done so much.
Please don't worry about the wings! We'll be able to clear the bodies out and take care of Hectahame from here.
All who tire of the war raging across the land are welcome to join our order.
Last excitement we had was a month ago, when an ogre wandered onto the grounds. Ate an initiate before we put him down.
I'll make you my undead footstool!
The captain will decide what to do with you.
Graves for the loyal. Buzzards for the rest.
You won. We get it. Let's go our separate ways, all right?

I don't see how anyone could trust the Ring of Daggers. Covenant mineworkers have those mercenaries staring down on them as they work. How could you work like that, knowing that if you grew tired, you'd get a Ring's club on your skull?
Are you prepared to sacrifice one of your own?
This one has full pockets!
When oath-bonds are weak, there is pain, and shame, and darkness.
Yes. Sacrifice those servants in my name. Let's give you something worthy to sacrifice!
They're weakening. Hit them where it counts!
Don't cause trouble.
When the storm comes, they'll get theirs.
So many dead. I don't understand.
So much evil. So much death.
A friendly one, isn't it?
Lizard spit! Disgusting!
What will it be this time? Daedroth? More Dremora? How about this?
Yes. Sacrifice those servants in my name. Let's give you something worthy to sacrifice!
I'm unsure which I despise more, Khajiit or Bosmer.
A noble High Elf raised in such environs. It's a travesty!
It's a little underdeveloped, but I really think Prince Naemon could do something with this island.
Come on, don't make me do this myself.
Stop toying with my brother, and try a real challenge.
Like all worldly things, you will in time wear and be used up.
You and I know how this ends.
They'll never make us their slaves!
For King Xakhwan!
The Three ensure the safety of the appointed leader of the Ebonheart Pact, and we are their blades.\n\nDo not attempt foolishness.
Slice them to ribbons!
Hah, feel that heat! Just a moment and I'll prepare the core.
I demand to know what you're doing!
As part of the Dominion, you will gain security.
Good luck, dearie. I'll wait here. I'm too old to play with snakes.
We'll even make the Trickster God himself laugh!

With the invaders routed, you never know what you'll find in the aftermath! And what's more, you never know when you'll need a bag to put it in!\n\nI'm your Elf. Lenor, the bag Elf! Remember me, and come to me with all your bagging needs!
In Vaermina's realm of Quagmire, we shall all be born again, to live in her presence forever! The best among us shall aid the Omens in their holy work.
Oh, my poor inn. When I returned, I found blood and trash everywhere. Such a trifle to tidy up!
Behold, the bringer of weal and woe.
Good to see you. You look well.
I will take back what is mine.
Kasura will be avenged.
Death is nothing, Outsider. The only thing that matters is Brackenleaf's survival!
Nothing can hurt you, Sai. Unless you want me to hurt you.
Enjoy your visit. You will never leave the Halls of Torment alive!
If you have a thirst, Rakkhiza can quench it! Ask, and it can be yours.
Be wary. The dead may still lurk about.
Take their bones!
Savages. The Jackdaws were nothing but savages.
Choosing the proper equipment is half the battle, you know.
The battlefields of Cyrodiil are littered with the bodies of the unprepared.
Only way to survive out there is to be prepared, trust me.
You return at an opportune moment, warrior. We have an urgent task.
Too much to carry? I have what you need.
Please, I have fresh fruit.
Don't bring a sword to a spell fight!
Rogues' armor! Doesn't shine, doesn't clank!
Healers' garb! Our garments won't stain.
You can't break jaws with a leather glove. You need metal gauntlets!
If those soldiers hadn't touched <<Az:1>>, we wouldn't be in this mess!
The gods frown on you! They frown!
Because I don't think I'd taste very good!

I, Jacmund Cine, have a little something for everyone and anyone! All people are welcome to trade with me,\n\nExcept for werewolves. Anyone I think is a werewolf, I don't deal with. I am very protective of my body.
Watch yourself. Things aren't as peaceful as they used to be.\n\nIf you need some extra supplies for your travels, I might be able to help—but I can't spare too much.
That's got to be the last of them, right? There can't possibly be more cultists.
Mezha-dro would like you to know he is glad you fight the Daedra, and not for them.
Me, not them!
Delicious!
You came a long way to die, stranger!
You're back—good. A vital mission awaits you.
So, you're back. Good. I have an urgent mission for you.
The Dominion requires your best effort, soldier. This is rewarded with the finest equipment and supplies.
For a hero of the Dominion, my wares are a necessity.
Know that only prowess on the battlefield earns one the right to claim my wares.
Don't waste my time if you haven't earned the right to these goods.
Few have earned the right to purchase my goods, soldier.
Heroes of the Pact have earned the finest equipment. I am honored to offer my stock.
I think the Rivenspire soldiers should take us to Shornhelm. I don't want to stay out here.
I don't think I'll be safe anywhere after this.
By my father's head, it hurts so!
I can't feel my toes… Rolbert, my toes!
I have to get away, before more of them come!
It's Molag Bal! If we kill him, we stop the Planemeld!
This does not seem to be how Boethiah would wish us to live. This city is so… safe.
Someday, I'll travel to Vvardenfell and walk the Pilgrim's Path. I know walking on my knees isn't necessary, but I feel I should anyway.
Living under Mother Almalexia's benevolent grace is most inspiring… Though I will never understand why she is offended by mages' levitation spells.
Blasphemy!
What else can we learn?
After this, we will find Uela. The hag must die.
Heed my call, mortal.
It's rare for the Bramblebreach clan to speak so highly of an outsider. You have my respect.
Thank the Eight you were able to defeat that wild mage at the Wilderking's Court.
Is it true you drove the vampires out of the Shademist moors? You're braver than I am. I'd have run the other direction.
I'm not saying I don't believe in Queen Ayrenn, but doesn't it tell you something, that so many people want her dead?
A dear friend fought alongside the Dominion forces at the sanctuary. This one is grateful you were there.
Sergeant Galandir told me what you did at Moonhenge. Amazing!
Sergeant Galandir says they couldn't have stopped the Daedric invasion at Moonhenge without you.
Everyone who was at Hectahame is talking about how you and Indaenir saved the Heart of Valenwood and stopped Naemon! Incredible!
My son … good son ….
They just keep coming! Another group from the south!
The west, again. The west!
Quickly! More coming from the east!
Run!
Yet another senseless kill.

Come to wet your whistle? Then you've come to the right place. I've got something to quench most any thirst.\n\nAnd I don't mind saying, our troubles have made Shornhelm a very thirsty place, if you catch my meaning.
Did you know that the wettest place in Tamriel is a small island in the Iliac bay?\n\nWell, now you know. You are thus armed with useful knowledge!
I … I had the horker dream again. What does it mean?
Times like these, I miss my mother. She was a mage, I think. Maybe she was a warrior?\n\nAnyway, she exploded one morning. Worst Tirdas I ever knew.
I mean, who throws out a sweet roll? Honestly!
If you're hungry, you've come to the right place. I studied the culinary arts at the finest kitchens in Wayrest. My food is positively divine!
People say I sell common goods, but mark my words, there's nothing common about my stock. Step closer and look around. I'm sure you'll find something you can't pass up.
I wonder what the arena's policy on taking trophies is?
I need to get home. I need money to get home… I need a winner to get money…
On second thought, no. That would never work - they'd simply kill me.
The next time I fight an Orc, I want to taste its rage. I want to understand their fury and feel it for myself.
A bit of advice: If you go to watch a fight, bring your own chair upon which to sit.\n\nThis one has had the misfortune to sit in errant viscera, and her fur took some time to clean, yes.
If I'm lucky, I could make it to Rawl'kha… But it's all so hopeless. I've lost everything!
Since coming here, I haven't actually gone ranging for… weeks, it feels like. This must be what cities are like, but with more fighting.
Maybe I should just go live elsewhere.
This town has really gone to the birds, hasn't it.
As you guided Saint Alessia, guide the magistrates along the narrow path of righteousness.
Whatever sorcery bewitches the people of Southpoint, my earnest hope is that my prayers will be answered. May Stendarr's mercy and Julianos' wisdom free the minds of my fellows.
The blood you shed fills rivers.
You should be the one to die.
Oblivion has pies. Ask anyone who's been there.\n\nDeadly pies.

Falinesti is, of course, an ideal. Perhaps it was placed into the world by Y'ffre, then removed after a time by Y'ffre?\n\nWhy would a god do such a thing? To teach us the value of idyllic models, of archetypes. To give us notions for which to yearn.
You don't think Falinesti was taken to Oblivion, do you? A Daedric Prince, uprooting such beauty … it chills me to think of it!
The strangest theory I've heard is that Magnus stole Falinesti away into the stars.\n\nIt's all wrong. The timing, the circumstances? Simply ridiculous!
Children, father has a new piece of meat for you!
Fools! Time is meaningless in the Halls of Torment! Whether it takes a day, or a thousand years, Sai Sahan will be broken!
I rule <<1>>. Respect my power!
You cannot survive <<1>>!
The worst thing about Northpoint's whole ordeal is that now, of course, many of the townsfolk would like to have a stiff drink.  And … well … supplies are limited.
Pluck its eyes for staring brandy. A gift for the Madgod!
I miss the horses. Where did they go?
Horse stalls get dirty, so I clean them up. That's what I do.
Scouty McWhiskers! Straighten that uniform!
The Mother is merficul to her children, but against her enemies, her rage is boundless!
Only one remains!
Nerien'eth! Please stop this! Anconath has done nothing to deserve this!
Tell me what I can do to end this, Nerien'eth! Please!
The knowledge is there. All you must do is take it.
A crisis will come to Tamriel, when the bladed paths open.
You there! Stop!
Off to the stocks with you.
Blacksap, help!
Damn.
Lacking in companionship? Can't seem to make a lady smile? Don't worry! In Pa'alat the ladies smile for a song!
Hear and know! Krin Ren-dro slain by Dominion operatives! The Eagle banner flies over Pa'alat!
Troll fights, troll battles, troll wars! Come bet on the black and white fighting trolls of Hadran's Caravan!
Hate slavers? Unsightly chains? Slavery banned at the new kinder, gentler Hadran's Caravan!
You can't go in without permission!
Stop! Please!
None will stand in my way!
More mages, that's it. We could do with more mages.
I can never leave this place anchored to this vessel. Please—end me.
I am working as hard as I can already!
Oh I hope this one has a beheading!
The Queen speaks fondly of Alik'r, and of her home with the High King, of course.
Do what you promised!
I just received an order for hundreds of jarrin roots, extremely toxic … well, my policy is to not ask for details.\n\nQuestions are not good for business, I've discovered.
Be wary, abandoned shafts such as these are prone to structural collapses.
They mined for gold, or glucinium, or grossular … graphite. One of those minerals, it's not important.
So delicious … I can smell it. The juices frothing in the fetid broth … you can stay for dinner if you like.\n\nOr perhaps you can stay for my next few meals ….
Agriculture … alchemy … anthropology … hmm! Atronachs. Have to come back for that one.
Shikruz has many bags to sell to types like you.
I have heard that the fields of Cyrodiil are lush. What would they want this place for?
This is ridiculous.
It feels like I've been waiting for days.
Who taught that one to fight? The God of Self-Punishment?
I don't remember my life before Coldharbour. It's all fading away. But I'm hungry. I'm … so hungry.
Too many times have vagabonds stolen from me. No more!
The winds are strong of late, and bring us much to consider.
I'm going to die down here. Hungry, alone … I must smell awful.

The past five hundred … five thousand … five hundred thousand years, they've been really hard on me.\n\nYou have no idea. It's like swimming upstream in a waterfall. I don't know who or where I am anymore.
Look, everyone! It's the champ that brought down Ishalga!
I'll bet against anyone you fight in the ring from now on!
Not bad, not bad! Maybe you'll be able to handle the next legless nix hound that you fight!
I'm going to … going to … I'm going to shave your head!
You might as well just lie down and cover your eyes, it would get more done.
My children are dying of hunger!
The rumors about the Empire enslaving civilians are completely untrue!
Kill them!
I got this mammoth cheese!
Middas is the purgatory of days. It's like I'm stuck between stone walls that are closing in.
I can manage. Please, help the others.

So really, time as a concept is more relevant to the whole of Mundus, of course. Nobody is arguing that.\n\nBut people, by and large, think of themselves first. The Now resides above the Mundus in the consciousness of most. Thus its importance!
Spirit of the trees, who taught us both what it is to be a tree and how to sing the tree's own song ….
Don't harvest so close to the Elden Tree. You'll offend it!
Countess Tamrith puts her trust in the gods. As should we all. That's what I say.
I heard that Countess Tamrith spends more time in prayer than talking strategy. Sorry to say it, but that just won't work.
Good. I hated everything about them.
You get the lightning! Now, you get the lightning!

Part of our difficulties in dealing with the Bosmer as allies is their difficulty in understanding the concept of money. It simply does not matter much to them.\n\nEvidently carrying practical things, such as food or arrows, is more important to them.
Not even the rats will eat this one. Am I … a cursed chef?
<Excited crowd cheers.>
<Person gasps in shock.>
This can't be real. It's not like this between Sai and me.
This one has given much thought. If a Wood Elf mate were to insist on cooking Wood Elf foods, it would be all right.\n\nMaybe. If they are very small, though. Very small, indeed.

I have reached the conclusion that these symbols mean nothing. Unless they are devotional engravings to the Bosmer tree-god of drunkenness and song, Y'ffre.\n\nThey might mean something in that case. Aside from that, however, they are meaningless.
The age of this stone is … yes, interesting.

There's something about watching that scholar squirm that I really enjoy. I wonder if anyone would have a problem with me keeping him.\n\nOh, but I bet he'd rummage through my things and make assumptions about me, even after living with me for a year.
One from your past is not in your present. This changes very little—the sacrifice seals the future in its place, just as the stars have sealed your name among them.
I'm not sure I've ever been this far up before. What happens if someone falls?
Let's continue on.
The Dragon may cross waters and mountains, but it cannot live in these jungles—it withers upon the shore.
Contempible creature.
You'll never leave this place alive!
You'll die screaming!
I wonder if my family's moved on. I just hope they're safe.
The way is clear! <<1>> is leading the others to the forge.
Do not lose heart, Vestige. You are close, now.
I hope nothing terrible has happened to them ….
I'll find out what happened here if it's the last thing I do.
Hosts of Oblivion, come forth and feast!
Are you lost or have you decided not to help me?
Stay true to Arkay, and the Light shall hold you in its warm embrace. Unlike these fools. Imagine, siding with Montclair!
We'll make sure that Shornhelm remains calm and well-protected. Montclair won't get the jump on us again.
None must reach the crystal alive!
I don't think those were Hircine's minions. I think I'm out of my depth ….
What are these beasts? Keep away!
Is someone there?
Burn it! Quickly, set it aflame!
My loyalty is not in question. I am a loyal subject of High King Emeric.
I'm a loyal subject of High King Emeric. Countess Tamrith and Baron Dorell are too.
I was sad when Baron Tamrith died. But his daughter, the Countess. I'm glad she's returned to lead her house.
I like Baron Dorell's approach. Straight to the point and no-nonsense. He's the best leader for Shornhelm, if you ask me.
Be wary of creatures that pose as sculpture.
You should probably turn right back around.
We don't have much, but if you are that desperate for an old apple, go ahead, root around.
Together, we can fight our way through!
Come, you fools. If you're so eager for death, Adusa shall grant your wish!
Adusa warned you, but no one ever listens to Adusa.
Dwellers of darkest Oblivion, come forth! The veil is pierced! Pass through the gate, I entreat thee!
If you keep that up, we'll burn alive!
We're going to suffocate at this rate.
Whatever you're doing, it isn't working.
Blast! Keep trying, I think you're on to something!
Keep at it, we're nearly there!
Eagle's triumph!
Oath of Ebonheart!
High Rock and Hammerfell!

There must be only one true Wizard in all of the sorcerous world, Lord Sotha, divine and perfect in all of His unfathomable mystery.\n\nSo many of these mages are entirely insufferable, leaving their tomes and gemmed skulls wherever they like.
Yes!
<evil laughter 3>
Bah! I'm so sick of mushrooms! I'd sunder Darvynil's head in front of his own mother for a slice of my Aunt Hilde's horker pie.
You look very hungry. But you've come to the right place. Where else will you find authentic Nord cooking in all of Rivenspire? Nowhere! Now come, I'll make you something special.
Outsiders bring strife. I wonder what you bring.
Leave us be.
May the light cleanse this vessel and let it rest in peace.
I'm not sure what that thing was, but it nipped at my finger!
That's my aging bait!
That old fish is mine! Best bait on the dock! Now leave it be.
Get out of my sight, you rotten thief!
A strange man led me to this city. Sir Cadwell, he said his name was. I do believe he was wearing a pot on his head.
I spoke to Cadwell the other day. He's quite mad, really, but in the most polite manner.
Both guilds ended up scattered all over Coldharbour. We lost some good people when that happened.
I'd like to have a word with the mages who said the portal to Coldharbour was a fine idea. We ended up scattered all over the place!
Once the city is sealed, the plague will have no way to reach us.
It was only a matter of time before those Maulborn fanatics revealed their true colors.
What is that thing? Do you see it?
The next one of you to drop a cask gets fed to the plague husks!
We're under attack!
You know what stinks? Dead Orcs. We're going to have to haul all the bodies off and burn them. Otherwise, we'll never get their stench out of this part of the forest.
Don't even think about it!
Feeling footsore? Maybe it's time you exchanged your gold for something faster.
You remind me of my minions.
This should be fun.
Try to put up a decent fight?
Ha ha ha! Stop! I need more mead.
Whoa, sabre cat! Let's go back to drinking.
My minions will tear you asunder!
Soon your powers will belong to the Serpent. He will use you to bring about his glorious reign.
Look upon the blade and tremble.
Fall.
The rain hardens!
The tide turns.
The guard advances.
Burn in Yokuda's remaining light.
The calves are crushed under the weight of one-thousand techniques.
Defeat is only a state of mind.
M'aiq's father was Qia'm, from a long line of Qia'ms. But M'aiq does not believe this. His father was a known liar.
M'aiq was soul-trapped, once. A mad Elf tried to bind him to a stone!
M'aiq wonders. Are the skeletons in minotaur graveyards half-Man or half-bull?
M'aiq wants nothing to do with Daedra. He hears they can make trees burn forever. How can they do that?
M'aiq thinks some places defy explanation. They have little to do with magic, and everything to do with the weather.
M'aiq hears of shapeshifters hiding in abandoned tombs and secret forests. Ha! M'aiq prefers to lurk in plain sight.
M'aiq speaks the truth, except for when he doesn't. With you, always the truth.
M'aiq can't tell Spider Cultists apart from the usual riffraff. Perhaps they need matching uniforms?
M'aiq would gorge himself in a Kwama mine, if time allowed.
The witches and witch hunters bicker so much. M'aiq wonders if they fancy each other.
M'aiq cares little for politics. Truly, he thinks everyone is his ally.
M'aiq doesn't care if the tunnels beneath Wayrest are a feat of engineering. The smell is horrific!
When young, M'aiq wished to attend an adventurer's school. But Tamriel has more crypts than schools.
Volenfell is where the famous Dwarven hammer fell, yes? M'aiq wonders if "Where the Hammer Fell" is a better name.
M'aiq thinks the maddest thing about the Vaults of Madness is their location.
M'aiq tried to swim out to sea, but had to turn back. Slaughterfish. Always the slaughterfish.
Have you seen Dragons? No? M'aiq thinks they must be hiding … for now.
When M'aiq enters a new place, he pictures it within himself and meditates for a short time.
My pick! You broke my pick!
Quick! To your feet!
Die! Die! Die! Die! Die!
If you'd kept quiet, they wouldn't have heard us!
Next time, don't boast about your purse in town!
You aren't paying enough to deal with your prattle!
To think, I left the army for this!
Fear not! You're safer than unhatched egg!
This isn't what we discussed!
You thought this was the safest route? Pah!
You said this "looked like a shortcut!" Next time, I choose the shortcuts!
I knew we should have stuck to the main roads!
I won't pay a bonus for sloppy fighting!
Meddler! Interloper!
You'll never hold the Ruby Throne!
This body won't fail me. Can you say the same?
The Celestial Mage has called on me to repel you from this realm! She did not say you needed to survive!
Your flesh will be torn apart!
After this, no more mining and shoveling for Sahalu. This one will get a new job as a chef … or maybe an acrobat. There's a lot of gold in the flippy tumbling business, yes?
Our fire burns anew!
The flame is fed!
Rise from the ashes!
Out! The lot of you! You've no right to enter!
Fools!
I warned you. These weapons will destroy you.
I warned you to turn away.
This will end you.
The Learned One wishes to remain secluded. Turn back.
Crush the intruders.
I'm stuck here until I'm sold out. So buy something, already.\n\nPlease.
You certainly seem like you can take care of yourself. Where did you learn to become so formidable? Sword-singer manuals?
M'aiq takes no comfort from the lack of Imperials in abandoned forts. All too often, less savory things find their way inside.
This will end you.
Let me go, curse you!
Target in sight!
Defensive position!
Take them apart! But leave Alanwe alone!
You'll never leave here alive!
My magic will consume you!
The Blade will end you.
Your deaths here were meaningless. I hope you're pleased with yourself. Your bodies will serve me, now.
You're not going anywhere!
Let's see if you can keep up.
My minions will rise when struck down. Will you?
You will regret challenging me.
Your scorched corpses will feed the spiders.
Your journey through these Crypts ends here.
My brother and I will turn you to ash!
This one cares nothing for snakes or corrupt caravan guards. Shurami is only interested in the art of the deal.\n\nCome, fragrant one. Let us talk.
Want to know my secret for scrumptious gorapple pie? Come closer. This isn't for everyone's ears.\n\nIt's the crust! I use genuine crust from the inside of a kwama's shell!
Sometimes I miss the sights and sounds of Morrowind. But a few stiff drinks take care of that lickity-split!\n\nYou know, you look like you can use a stiff drink yourself, my friend.

You've come to me at the right time, friend. The last wagons to arrive before all this trouble began filled my bins with goods, and much of it is still fresh!\n\nI'm sure I've got something you'll like.
Black hands embrace us.
A beautiful web of grief and betrayal has been woven here. You will not disturb it.
Your blood will stain the sand!
Plenty more minions where they came from.
Burned and blasted. The most exquisite kind of corpse.
What did you hope to accomplish by coming here? We will feast on your carcass, and thus, your carcass will make these grounds fertile.
Don't you walk away from me. Yes, I'm drunk. I'm very drunk. I even threw up over there in the corner.\n\nBut that doesn't make you better than me. Nobody's better than me. I'm a perfect drunk!
She's in my head!
What am I doing?
Are you here to kill me?
Burned and blasted. The most exquisite kind of corpse.
Burned and blasted. The most exquisite kind of corpse.
Why that strange High Elf is so eager to purchase red brittle is beyond me. But I'm sure you have more important business to discuss with me.

This Iron Orc nonsense, it's all just an elaborate trick. It's the Dragonstar Caravan Company. Figure if they scare us, we'll be more willing to put up with their outrageous demands.\n\nWell, Tall Papa never paid gold for dung, and neither will I.
I can't stop shaking. It should pass in a moment, though. Then I can get back to work.
Sometimes I wonder why I left behind all the comforts of Rivenspire. Then I remember. It was the vampires. I never could abide such creatures.
I once spent five days drinking mead with Thane Jeggi at a fishing hole in Eastmarch. We had a fabulous time!\n\nBut never try to match Jeggi mead for mead. The man drinks like a thirsty mammoth!
The dormant fire will awaken, your people will perish—blinded and choked and consumed by flame.
Come. Entertain me as your friends die.
A traveling bard once told me to write what I know. But who would want to read a story about sifting dirt and digging rocks?\n\nThere's nothing so dry as advice that contains no water.

Stupid, clawless, incompetent fools! Someone cracked another slab of red brittle trying to extract the foul metal.\n\nIf this one gets the shakes, someone can expect a gigantic hairball in their evening stew.
Molag Bal's minions can do what they like. They can kill us, they can torture us, they can even drag us into Oblivion.\n\nIn the end, we will always stop them.
Fall before Trinimac's truth!

For a long, long time, the Rat never left the sewers. He likes the air better out here, but not the people … present company excepted, of course.\n\nAll these others, they're just self-centered bastards. They may need help, but the Rat doesn't care.
You don't think there are trolls in the Arena, do you? I hate trolls. And ogres. And ducks. I really hate ducks.\n\nI guess I hate all the things.
Why the sour look, friend? Come. Dance and make merry! Nothing like the threat of a gruesome death to make you feel truly alive!
Don't worry, I'm not with Legion Zero. I'm loyal to the Empire, and right now, that means whoever's here to help the city.
I'm not sure I even care any more. \n\nIf the Temple of the Divines is lost and everything within, what purpose do I have? Serving at the Temple was my entire life!
I am the stars and the sky, and everything that lies beyond. There was no hope for you.
Have you ever tried Voljar's mead? Better than that swill I hear they serve in Sovngarde! Better than anything!\n\nI wish I had some Voljar's mead.
If you're Stone-Fish material, then I'm the king of Shornhelm. Move along and don't look back, sour tart!
Want to see what I have for sale? Of course you do!
The Captain really thinks we can bring Imperial Law to this backwards region? That'll be the day! When pigs fly, I say.
Regulations, this! Rules, that! What nonsense!\n\nI will drink whenever it pleases me. It's medicinal. And besides, what will Lucina do? Flog me? I'm their damn healer and they need to keep me happy.
What a hit! That had to hurt! They hit you so hard I almost fell over! Well, put yourself back together and try that again!

Just look at those skeeving Imperial diamond-backs. So clean and proud in their fancy armor. \n\nOne of these nights, I'm going to give them a proper deep-woods welcome. Cut them ear-to-ear with a deer antler. Just my way of saying hello.
Grab a bowl and find a spot. You won't be able to conquer the Arena on an empty stomach.
More brave souls here to compete in the battles? Let this one sell you something before anything too terrible happens to you.
Another morsel for the Arena? Better hurry, little morsel. When the Five Claws are finished in there, nothing else will remain to fight!
Perhaps you should simply end your lives now and save yourself the embarrassment of a sound beating.
Have you ever been to a swamp. Dreadful places, but this one has heard that such knowledge will aid you inside the Arena.
This one wonders why all these so-called warriors don't just pack up and go home. Now that the Five Claws have arrived, none of them stand a chance in Oblivion of winning.
Are you just going to stand there admiring my armor or are you ready to enter the Arena?
Know your place!
The master will not suffer this intrusion.
Rot!
By choking air and purging fire—your kind will end.
My comrades look worse than they smell, don't they? Don't let these bastards intimidate you. Take the Undaunted pledge!
We will end you!
My comrades are louts. Pompous, undisciplined, just waiting for death to take them. Show me you are not like they are. Take the pledge.
Every cultist and Daedra you kill will ease my misery a little.
It's probably only a matter of time before the Daedra break down these doors too. That would be a shame. I would've preferred to die in the temple.
I wish she would stop pacing. She's making me crazy.
Talk to Kerennia if you want information. I'm just hoping to live through another day.
Ready to bloody Molag Bal's nose again, comrade?
It is good to see you here. Not so good for you, perhaps, but good for us.
Glorious, simply glorious. Those ruins will make excellent subject matter for my next painting.
There's nothing better than ripping victory out of its tomb and clubbing it over the head. Nice work today. Make sure to see me tomorrow, eh?
Make yourself at home, then talk to Kerennia when you're ready to go to work.
Don't go near the Imperial Prison without a lot of swords at your back. The worst Daedra in the City are in there.
More spelunkers? You'll burn the same as the others.
Is the Undaunted obsession with robbing the dead a reflection of some kind of inner darkness? Return to me tomorrow, and we will ponder this further.
Come, greet the new day, and die!
Got something to sell? Well, we put the "profit" in "profiteer!"
For Dagon!
The site is yours! Now hold that position and split your group to clear the other side!
The Daedra are re-taking that site! Stop them!
Fall in a lake and die, you overgrown campfire!
Run along, pup. This is no place for the likes of you.
Come to compete in the games? I hope so. You look like you might actually be able to shake things up around here.
I wish you well in the games … but not too well.\n\nFor you see, we plan to win the champion's crown before this day is done.
A trusted team is the key to victory.
That Aspera lady is one strange acorn. I don't know who she is, but I have the feeling she's important.

That Aspera woman told me I was too short to compete in the games. Well, who does she think she is? She's not a Daedric Prince or anything!\n\nBesides, the Battlemaster said my head was at the perfect height for his sword swing.
My companions are just angry because I drank all of the ale. What can I say? I was thirsty!
I need another ale. By Mauloch's right nostril, I need another barrel of ale!
The Arena isn't a place for novices and puny pony guar. But it's your funeral, I guess.
Something more is at work in this place than a simple contest of champions. Be wary, stranger.
Why I decided to lash my wagon to a scholar, I'll never know.\n\nBut she is incredibly good in a fight—after she's been properly motivated.
I can't find a group worthy to fight beside the mighty Frozen-Fist. Milk-drinkers, the lot of them!\n\nI'd be better off with a mammoth and two pony guar—but this Craglorn place is fresh out.
A newcomer! Marvelous! Come in and tell me your story.
I could be a writer. It doesn't look that hard to me. But spelling? I hate spelling. I'll get someone to handle that for me.
You're not here to take me back to my cohort, are you? I'm not going back. Not a chance.
Slay them! They are not to reach the Valkyn!
Did you get poisoned? Are you slow-witted now? Don't you want your reward?
Hmm. Your armor has seen better days. Why don't you let me set you up with something more durable.
Truth be told, I'm a terrible hunter. I prefer to let others do the hunting so I can concentrate on making masterpieces!
I can talk about Orcs and their accomplishments all day, but I'm sure you're here for my wares. What can I get for you today?
The finest silks in all of Wrothgar can be found here.\n\nNot that that's saying much.
Wretched mortals. Always undoing our good work.
Goes against everything I've been taught, but I've got to admit it—Trinimac helped us turn this junk heap into a real city!
Dagon's flame ignite!
My sister and I hail from Daggerfall. Honestly, it's a little strange here. Doesn't quite feel like home yet.
This city makes me proud. I never expected to return to this part of the world, but now I'm glad I did.
Show them how we treat visitors to the Deadlands!
Let the flames consume you!
You think you'll survive this?
Cut them. Burn them. Bring their bodies to me.
Your day will end in fire—and begin anew.
Embrace change. Embrace the dawn.
I will teach you to respect the Valkyn.
You cannot escape the fire.
Halt and burn.
This will consume you.
You look like you traveled far to visit our fair city. Beautiful, isn't it?\n\nHow can I help you today?
Need a new pack? Of course you do! Step right up and let me show you what I've got.
Don't let the appearance of the stable bother you. All creatures under my roof receive the best possible care.
This one can help you with all your enchanting needs. And if you don't see what you want, feel free to ask.
Clan Shatul runs these stables now—it's a damn good thing, too. These locals can't tell a mare from a gelding!
Some Orcs left the clan when you became chief, but I say let the strongest rule. \n\nLooking for a mount? The strongest chiefs need the strongest steeds!
I came to Orsinium at the king's invitation. I should have known his subjects would be less … urbane.
Can you imagine the nerve of Ushruka! Imagine—a woman chief! I'm glad you stepped in when you did.\n\nNow then, what can I do for you, chief-maker?
Did you need something?
Make ready, troops! Let's send these savages back to Oblivion!
Under Trinimac's guidance, everyone who works hard has an equal opportunity for success—weavers and warriors alike.
I miss the days when I could pick a fight in the morning and end the evening with a good, strong drink.
I'm not here as a Redguard or as a member of the Daggerfall Covenant. I'm part of the Fighters Guild, and we're here to provide a service. We lend steel and shield to anyone who needs our help.
We go where our members go, offering support and whatever aid we can. Wrothgar is no different from Rivenspire in that regard.\n\nWell, I suppose it's a little different ….
Othukul, our Magus, has worked tirelessly to offer the hand of friendship to the Orcs. Based on their response, I'm not sure why he bothers.
Drink me under the table? Me? Nah, never happen! I'm not only the brew master, I'm my own best customer!
May I help you?
Once you eat echatere, everything else tastes like chicken!
Just so we're clear, I don't haggle. I ask a fair price and I won't hear any different.
You dare? I will end you!
Help me!
To me!
Shor's bones, that looks heavy. How much is in there?
When the crates are full, this one will load the wagons.
A delivery befitting a grandmaster.
Come forth minions and engulf these pests!
Yes, over there is fine. I'll have it packed up before long.
Worry not that these goods have been used. This one assures that all are in excellent working condition.\n\nFull refunds for those who are unsatisfied. If you can find us.
I could use a nap. After I square away your shipment, of course.
The fires from her arrows burn long. Escape them and more will come.
You? You cannot seek refuge from the Daedra here.
We're still short on supplies, but this will help us stock up.
Mortals smell better charred.
I will turn you to dust, and you will forget.
How may I serve?
You have business here?
May I be of service?
You bring me business?
How may I serve?
May this one be of service?
I'm going to do it this time. Here goes. All right. On the count of three.\n\nOn second thought, never mind. I need a little more time. Let's make it a count of three-thousand-two-hundred-and-six.
It's your turn. Go on, you'll be fine!\n\nRemember—jump out, not down. That way you don't go splat on the rocks.
Why didn't someone think to grab a few furs instead of the moldy flour? \n\nA fur coat sure would be nice right now.
I haven't worn shoes since I was a knee-high to a mammoth, so I'm not about to start now.
We're a small clan, so our resources are limited. Even so, take a look at my stock. You might find something you can use.
I heard what you did for our village. Thanks.\n\nIf you want to fish, I wouldn't mind the company.
My father was a great chief and a great Orc. It's not his fault that he never died in battle and lived to be so old.
If you want to lighten your load, we can put your extra items to good use. And I've got gold to spend.
The cold doesn't bother me. I like it.
The chief can be real stubborn, but he only wants what's best for the clan.
Not a word from the quarry. Not a single one!
Something I can do for you?
Move it—we have a lot more to go.
Let's show them who really controls Wrothgar.
Want some free advice? Go do something else. Anything else. Be a farmer, or a … I don't know … a muck raker or something. Anything's better than soldiering in these Eight-forsaken sewers.
I do love a good roasting! Look at it burn!
The king eats more food than anyone I've ever met, but I still have a few things left for sale.
If you're looking for Canuldil, he's not here. He should be back soon, I think.
Some say the quarry is cursed. I'm starting to think they're right.
We've got a lot of work ahead of us, but Clan Tumnosh always follows through.
I would have been in the quarry myself, if I hadn't gone for a drink of water.
Business would be better elsewhere, but this one wants to help however he can.
This one's mother taught him always to be patient and good things will happen!
You see those rats? They're going to be gnawing on your bones for days!
Just kill me if you're going to. I've nothing left to live for.
For now, the danger is past, thanks to you. But it will not be long before Molag Bal's minions gather their courage and threaten us once more.
You're a true hero, friend! This medicine's going to do a world of good. Trust me.
You look like you'd make a good arena fighter yourself. Knowing how to fight isn't enough though. You've got to be able persevere.\n\nI've lasted as long as I can. I'm too weak for another bout.
One thing's good at least. I haven't seen that damn Thrallbinder in a while.
Can I go home now?
How did I get here? Did I escape that madman?
Never disappoint General Nedras, warrior. Despair is the certain result.
You are the one who secured the district in the upper city, yes?\n\nPerhaps you can help Shaghila in the sewers now? There is much to do before they can be secured.
We've been through tough times before, but never anything like this. I've been trying to keep Annia's spirits up, but I wonder if I'm just being foolish.
I know many others died aside from Maximinus. I didn't even like him, but to hear of his death is another hard blow.

I have to tell you, I've heard a lot of high praise for this King Emeric of yours; they say he's a real man-of-the-people. \n\nIf that's really the truth, then where in Oblivion is he now? Not here. I can tell you that much.
By the Eight, I can breathe again!
Let's go before they come back!
Divines help me, I'm free!
Don't leave the nest—danger lurks outside!
Get them off of me! The spiders!
The worst part is those legs, all those legs.
How can something so soft be so strong?
What is keeping you here? Run!
Waxhuthi! My scales were bound but are now free again.
I thank you. Your scent is forever welcome in my nest.
Tall Papa be praised, I live again!
Thank you, wayfarer!
The Lady destroyed? If only my hand had killed her!
Beware the Lady. She will return!
Nothing in the sewers can be worse than this!
I must get home to my children!
Sadly, there is no safe place in the City anymore.
I cannot stay here!
Spider silk sticks to the fur!
This one sees spiders everywhere. Perhaps there is no escape.

I can't tell you how much I hate it when someone tells me that my work has all gone to waste, so I hate to be the one to say it to you.\n\nUnfortunately, however, it seems the Daedra are again trying to conduct that summoning ritual in the temple.
The Daedra can taunt me all they want. I'll respond in the arena.
You will suffer for this indignity, mortal.

You're lucky you're not a Daedra. I was just waiting for one of the damn things to come up here. I was all ready to clobber them.\n\nYou see, I know where their weak points are. I can take them out in one punch … I think.
It is frigid out here. I hate to say it, but my mother was right. She told me to wear a shirt, but I was hot … and stupid.
When I was a child, I visited the Elven Gardens in the upper city. It was the most beautiful and wondrous place I had ever seen.\n\nI pray that it has been protected from harm.
Nice to see you again. Glad to see you've survived the City so far.
Break you in half! Damn your eyes!
It rubs this one's fur the wrong way to remain hidden in our base; there is great need of warriors in the city. \n\nBut duty is duty, no matter how distasteful.
You and Tapak make a good team. You go forth into the sewers and find more of those patrol documents, and Tapak will give them to General Nedras.
Yes, we're still here in the sewer. Would that we had a few more soldiers like you ….
You look somewhat confused. If you're looking for the Pact's stronghold, you've found it. It's a bit homely, I know, but it will grow on you … much like a fungus.
That coin-pouch getting heavy?
It costs you nothing to look.

Don't I know you from somewhere? I'm a little fuzzy on it, but there was this one night in Wayrest before we were deployed ….\n\nWell … if that was you, thanks again. That was a night I'll never forget.
I walk the shadows!
Run, mortal!
My shadows will tear your life away!
Dark light take you!
Have some tainted flesh!
Flee or die, fool!
Let's grind some meat!
I won't be denied!
This delightful new strain of hoarvor will fight on the front lines soon.
These fumes will burn your blood!
Don't hurt me!
Help!
If you have any more bad news, please keep it to yourself.
I'm sorry. I'll do a lot of things to advance in the guild, but I'm not getting close to those flesh colossi. \n\nEven if they don't tear me in half, I'll die from the stench of those necrotic sacks!
I am so very grateful to have my book back, but I just noticed … it's got that stench. It's the same one I smelled on you—the sewers. It's turning my stomach.
A curse on all the scum plaguing the city!\n\nYour courage deserves a reward, warrior.
These soldiers cower here while their corrupted brothers and sisters walk the streets. It's insufferable.
I don't care what banner you fight for. In this place, banners are meaningless … even ours.
What are you doing? The prisoners would give their lives to leave this place!
Give up, fool. I will always return!
I will see your flesh burn!
Again? Do you come here to mock me, wretch?
Foolishness masquerading as bravery. I will enjoy killing you.
Burn, wretch, burn!
This time, you will fall, fool!
All pretenders to the Ruby Throne must be destroyed!
You were lucky last time. It will not last.
You return to join my collection?
You will perish in flame—you and all your kind!
You look weary. Come, and rest.
The Lord Warden calls you to serve, prisoner!
Your flesh belongs to me.
Consume them. You must grow larger if you are to serve in the war.
Your bodies will aid us in the destruction of your kind.
My spinning blades bite, fool.
Drink deep, my children!
You are summoned, my subjects!
The dead arise to serve me!
There is no escape from this place!
You look good enough to eat.
Wish I could go hunting once in a while. Why should everyone else have all the fun?
Bored? I've got an idea! Go run around the sewers and make a lot of noise. I can guarantee you one thing—you won't be bored any more.
To me, minions!
I wish I had my broom. This place may be cozy, but I think I could spruce it up.
Where have all the servants gone?
Seek mortal blood, my minions!

When I was a child, I asked my father about the Reachmen taking over Imperial City. He shrugged and said "Bah, let them keep it." \n\nI'm beginning to understand what he meant. Even without the Daedra, this just doesn't seem like my kind of place.
I hope you like your goods cold and soggy.
I'd be happy to look after your goods, friend.
A cold wind blows in the upper city, and the sewers are frigid with death and dark magic.\n\nWhy not stay a while here in the warm? Spend your gold while you yet have time.
It may not be as impressive as it was before, but you are looking at the most respectable bank in all of Imperial City.\n\nIf anything in this city is safe, it is the things you store with Shamaea.
No haggling here. I know a sellers' market when I see one.
Consider well what you carry with you out in the sewers. Why give the Daedra more supplies?
The danger has passed for now. But tomorrow will doubtless bring a renewed attack. I hope you will return to help me again.

I know not if it is fate, destiny, magic, or the hand of the gods, but you have arrived at the perfect moment. \n\nThe Veilweavers have renewed their efforts and I have just finished preparing the spell.
I don't know what I would have done if you hadn't found my dogs for me. Probably just curled up here and died. Now I have something to live for. We'll make it out of this city. I know we will.
These sacs are helpful, but I'll almost certainly need more before my study is complete. Please, check in from time to time. I may have more work for you.
I am sorry to send you out into harm's way once more, but … well … I've got to send you back out into harm's way. Sorry.
My scouts are still getting ready for the second salvo. Come back tomorrow, eh? We'll be ready.
There's my heavy-heeled decoy. Right on time.\n\nDon't look so offended—decoy's an important job!
Though Father and I have had our differences, we're both grateful for your help. Be careful—the City grows more dangerous every day.
I appreciate you freeing me. You go on now; I'm going to rest here for a while longer.
The Elven Gardens have always been protected by magic, but those protections are no match for the dark power of Coldharbour.
If you see any Xivkyn out there, feel free to kill them. As far as I know they have not yet restarted their mission to burn down the district, but it may simply be a matter of time.
Do you smell it? The smoke, the fires? The Xivkyn have returned and the district is again in danger of being completely destroyed. \n\nI hope you will consider coming to our aid once again.
Eager for more work? This is good, but sadly, Aishah has nothing available right now. Perhaps later.
Do you know what Aishah sees when she sees you, walker?\n\nShe sees opportunities.
So … remember that terrible monster you killed for me the other day?
The Calidia family will always be in your debt, friend.
We appreciate your efforts. Your exploits have inspired other soldiers to step up and take more assignments, so I have no new tasks right now. Check back later, all right?
I hope Holia does come looking for me. Serve her right, getting eaten by Scamps or even a clannfear. \n\nThough the poor creatures would probably get indigestion.
I have half a mind to go to the Arboretum and find Gryna myself. I just might do that.
At least we won't go hungry for a while, thanks to you. We still can't go outside, but maybe someday….
Something is wrong with my eyes. Everything seems so blue.
Worm Cultists sure love to hear themselves talk.
I spoke with Mannimarco, once. It was … unsettling.
I used to enjoy a good storm. Now I despise them.
Priests die the same as any other. Where are the Eight now, eh?
None think they'll break. Not at first.
Someone bring me a legionnaire. I want to set it on fire.
One day I'll make it to Coldharbour.
I examined a Skyshard, once. My teeth … I thought they were melting.
Need more corpses to burn!
Sloads? I've not dealt with one for a thousand years.
Fools! Attack the ones with swords, not hooves!
To arms! I sense mortals near.
The Lord of Domination leads the kyn. For now.
Where are my fresh corpses?
Bits of the bureaucrat's flesh still decorate my shield.
The Dark Lord's might encompasses all in this city.
Enough of this. Wake me when the Planemeld happens.
I thought this would be far more exciting than Coldharbour.
Fool. Eyes ahead.
Look at how they squander their souls. Why shouldn't we take them?
General Kryozote refuses to eat mortals. He consumes only Scamps.
City walls are no barrier to the kyn.
I despise these mortals. Their cities are weak, their lives short.
Killing mortals is an art that sometimes calls for patience.
Take your groveling elsewhere. Obey quietly.
They hide in sewers, closets, and basements. We've not found them all.
They cannot elude us for long!
Nothing gets by, on this side or the other.
Thought is weakness. Obedience is the true power.
In our victory, the mortals shall proclaim a third era. The era of the Daedra.
I miss Coldharbour. When do we go back?
Those who fail to do my bidding lose their rights to exist.
Our Dark Master should cut his ties with the kyn. We are all he needs.
I taught Hzu-Hakan how to enchant his fire arrows.
I sense a powerful mortal near. Be cautious.
Where did that little, green one go?
The arena provokes such eloquent screams.
I would rather clothe an ogrim's nethers than serve another Prince.
They'll give them cast-off weapons, and make them kill each other.
That Worm Cultist spoke as though we were equals. The nerve!
I don't want parts. I need whole bodies!
Keep your head down and don't give me away. This post is dangerous enough as it is.
Become one with the fire of Coldharbour!
Capture the strongest, slaughter the rest. Go!
Capture the strongest, slaughter the rest. Go!
Have you heard the screams coming from the arena? And that awful announcer! Reman's boots, sounds like my uncle gargling rock salt.
Fresh meat for the Arena!
Fresh meat for the Arena!
The kyn does not deserve such treatment.
Part of me wants to go into the arena and show those Daedra what happens when you provoke the Legion. Y'know … the dumb part.
You provincial soldiers are welcome, as long as you're here to help us. If you're here as conquerors, we'll fight you too.
You look like a seasoned warrior. That's good. I keep watching these young recruits … they won't last ten minutes in the sewers.\n\nI'm afraid most of our efforts in the sewers have come to naught.
If more and more Daedra keep pouring into the sewers, I wonder how long it will be before they discover this place.
Leave me alone. Go to the Market District and fight in the Imperial Prison, that's where all the really bad Daedra are.
Take my advice—get out of the city. Nothing but misery and death here.
These legionaries are mad. Don't trust them. They'll turn on us, just like the others. You'll see!
I've been watching these corrupt legionaries for hours. Even recognized a few. I always thought Decimus was so handsome. Damn shame.
Nadara means to make for the Temple District when things calm down. Still too dangerous, though. Far too dangerous.
Stay away from the Market District. Between the prison entrance and the Dark Anchor, that district's the wrong place to be in the city.
By the Three, I wish I could …. Sera, I'm terrified of heights!\n\nCourage, Remyon. Courage.
How these creatures can be so cruel I don't understand. But the city will survive. I just know it.
General Pollius sent me over here from the Nobles District. No idea why. There's enough trouble back there to keep us all busy for years.\n\nYep, we're prepared to fight them for that long.
This lot gave as good as they got. Heroes, all of them.
What in Akatosh's name are you doing in here? You have weapons, training—make yourself useful! Go kill some Daedra or something.
Great treasure and little danger, the rumors said. This one no longer believes rumors.
If the Daedra find this place, the least I can do is die fighting.
You can't see the Temple from here, but at times the screams carry across the district.
I thought this'd be an easy post—just hide out and watch. Toughest thing I've ever had to do.

Someone stop that thief before they get away!
Mauloch's arse, I don't care what you did.
What a thumping. The Guard should see!
Trolls take you, criminal!
The guards are coming.
A murder, by Mauloch!
Go away and I won't report this.
I promise not to say a word.
Can I help you with something, troll breath?
I'm going to inform the guards.
Why would I betray you to the guards?
That must have hurt.
Mauloch knows what you did and so do I.
A bounty! Where's the guard?
You toothless runt of a coward!
I need to get away from you.
What guard would listen to me, anyway?
Mauloch's third fang, what are you up to?
I need to report this.
Hrmph. Whatever.
Knock it off, you thug!
I can't believe you would do that!
We've got a criminal here. Fetch the manacles!
Dead? By the First Forge!
Don't touch me!
I didn't see anything.
You're up to something.
Scourge thump it! It's a thief!
Better be careful.
This is pointless. Stop it!
I'll see you in chains!
I saw that! Guard!
You'll pay the blood price!
Not another step!
I don't want any trouble.
Are you supposed to be sneaking?
Put that back!
Mauloch's arse, I don't care what you did.

Not another step!

Are you supposed to be sneaking?
Put that back!
Do not worry about me talking.
What are you thinking?
Someone--fetch the guards!
You cannot break the law without consequences.
That was cold-blooded murder. I saw it.
You stay away … you hear?
Tava's grace! Just-just let me be!
What are you doing, I wonder?
Stealing is against the law. The guard will deal with you.
Don't worry. I don't talk to the guards.
I will not tolerate bloodshed!
Zeht's tears! What have you done?
You have sullied your name with this crime.
I wish I had not seen such horror.
Get away--or I'll call the guard!
Please, leave me in peace.
You have not escaped notice.
You are guilty of stealing. There will be a price to pay.
Leave me alone and I'll leave you alone.
Stop this violence at once!
Guard! There's a foul criminal among us!
Faithless coward, stop where you are or I'll call the guard.
Murderer! You won't get way with this!
By the stars and sand, leave me alone!
Enough. I'm not part of this.
You are behaving very suspiciously my friend.
Cease your lawbreaking, thief!
I don't know what you did, and I don't care.
Guards! There's been an attack!
Vile creature. Call the Guard!
I can't believe you did that. Guard!
Someone stop them! The killer is getting away!
Please, stay away from me.

Netu anselim, thief. Damnation lies this way.
Walk away. Easier for us both.
Cease this violence immediately.
The guards will deal with you.
Summon the guard!
That was a disgusting display.
I need to be elsewhere.
Leave me be and you won't regret it.
Your actions betray you, my friend.
A lawbreaker! Do something.
Blades, I don't care what you did.
An attack! Summon the guard.
Your bounty will be harsh indeed.
Stir the guard before they get away.
Zeht's tears, why doesn't someone do something?
Stendarr's shield, leave me alone.
I just want to live.
I think trouble is your other name.
Guards, I've found an unworthy swine to hoist on your pike.
Make way, make way.
Stop this bloodshed!
Guards, stop that Goblin-spawn!
Not so fast. Guards!
Guard! Someone has been slain!
Stay back, you filthy cur!
I'm not one to interfere. Honest.
By Ruptga's starry breeches—stop skulking!
That is not your property.
Did you just--? Huh. You did.
There is no need for this!
What madness is this? Guard!
Hey! The lawbreaker's getting away!
You will pay for that, butcher!
Leave me alone--I mean it!
All is forgotten.

What madness is this? Guard!
Hey! The lawbreaker's getting away!
You will pay for that, butcher!
Leave me alone--I mean it!
All is forgotten.
What are you playing at?
Do not let that thief get away!
It's best not to think about the rations down here. Not a lot of dogs running around, let's put it that way.
Some days you're up. Some days you're down. Today is an up day.\n\nWhat can I do for you?
The city's seen better days. Let's hope it survives to see them again.
They have a strong appetite, my lovely ones. I hope that … I hope that I will be enough.
I like you! And because I like you, I'm going to make you an offer you won't be able to walk away from.
We really need to stop meeting like this. Hold on, I'm just pulling your leg! I'm happy to see you and I look forward to letting you avail yourself of our special opportunity.
I thought I had what it takes, but I suspect I was never meant to be an arena fighter. I should've listened to my mother. Now it's too late.
You don't know me yet, but I'm about to become your very best friend!\n\nLet me tell you about a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that's so much better than anything the Enforcers offered you.
Once you leave, you're dead to me.\n\nHold on, I'm just pulling your leg! I'm happy you're back and I look forward to letting you once again avail yourself of our special opportunity.
I'm going to have to ask you to reconsider this life of crime you've adopted. Otherwise, I'm going to have to clobber you.
Some folks think Enforcer methods are too brutal. They don't know what it is we face.\n\nOutlaws don't have time for rules. Why should we?
Justice knows neither rest, nor truce. The Enforcers are Tamriel's last line of defense against the armies of lawlessness.
Here's the procedure. You pay the fine, I let you go. Otherwise, I kill you.
You have fallen afoul of thy lords the Three. You will make restitution.
It doesn't matter what you do.
Step right up. I can let you in on something quite profitable.
Famius and I were talking just the other morning, saying we wanted to start a family and such. That idea's just laughable now.

I wish I could convince your general to do more for the citizens. So many of them have been killed or driven from their homes. \n\nLet the Daedra raze the city; we just need to get the people to safety.
Molag Bal, Clivia, Mannimarco, the Council, Legion commanders … it's all the same. We all … we all end up slaves.

Oh yes, the Rat remembers you. He had a very interesting conversation with you, and you were helpful … but the Rat cannot afford to make friends!\n\nNo. No. Don't get too close. If you wish to talk, you'll have to wait until the Rat is ready.
I have to get out … I have to get out of the city. The Warden's eyes are everywhere! He'll find me!
Way to rattle the cages, comrade. Let us handle things for a while. These grunts need the exercise.\n\nFeel free to check in from time to time. We may need you again soon.

Illusions, even botched illusions, have their benefits. For example, I can tell what you're wondering, and the answer is—yes! I am completely naked.\n\nIt's quite liberating! Frees up the mind to think of more important things. Every mage should try.
Vergilius Quarra.
<The creature narrows its eyes. As it notices your belt pouch, it seems to relax.>
I think you have this well in hand, so I'll stand back and give you room to work!
For King Kurog! For Orsinium!
That storm … Mara's heart, I've never seen the like. I wish I had never left Wayrest.
You will not survive this!
These are strange times. Strange times, indeed.
I have more than enough patients to tend to, if you don't mind.
Sometimes I want to just rush out there and hack off a few Winterborn limbs!
Mazgroth warned everyone to stay in the village. Something about wandering dead people.\n\nMe? I'm not afraid of dead people.
So far, so good—but the worst is yet to come!
See, my minions! This is how it's done!
Another thrilling match! I'm sorry it's over.
A telling blow!
You may be an Orc, but that doesn't make you part of our clan. I don't trust anyone who isn't part of our clan, so I don't trust you.\n\nI'm just saying.

Most of my clan is too polite, but I'm not afraid of outsiders so I'll tell you the honest truth.\n\nWe don't want you here, we don't need you here, and we certainly don't trust you. Well, at least I don't trust you. Not one bit.

I've been pondering the question posed by the new city of Orsinium. Are Orcs beholden to Malacath or Trinimac?\n\nMy conclusion? We're not beholden to anybody. We're Orcs! And that's good enough for me and my clan.
I understand you had a hand in calming those dead Nords from the barrow.\n\nYou have my thanks for that.
It looks like … yes, the challenger is trying again!
The lead wagons were full of Orc peasants. They never stood a chance.
That Chief Bazrag. You have to be brave or stupid to go after an army of Reachmen with just a handful of warriors.
There were dozens—no, hundreds! We were attacked by hundreds of Winterborn!
I knew taking on all those peasants was a mistake. Between them and the cargo of food and supplies, we were too tempting a target for Ice-Heart's marauders.
The letter I received never said anything about fighting the Reach.
The poor Orcs! This one hopes that Chief Bazrag can save them, but the Winterborn seemed so determined.

We're very particular when it comes to our clientele here. We have to be, what with the king and his honored guests coming and going at all hours.\n\nI guess you could say this is something of a private club. Very exclusive and all that.
This club's getting busier by the day. I liked it better when we were an exclusive establishment. No offense.
Ah, outsider! You must tell me all about your exciting adventures!
You've traveled all over the world, haven't you? You really must tell Ufgel all about it. She'd love for us to travel someday.
I have more gold than most nations but still I am not content. For that reason, I have decided to use my vast fortune to support the king and the idea of an Orsinium reborn.
Burn in the wrath of Malacath!
Trinimac's truth compels you!
The Vosh Rakh will have our revenge!
Are you so destitute that you need to steal from a poor old woman?
What is Wrothgar coming to? An old woman should be able to walk the roads in peace without being assaulted by religious fanatics.
I spent some time in Skyrim, at the guild hall in Windhelm.\n\nTrust me, this is a thousand times more inconvenient.
Half-ears! Split-faces! To the surface! Attack!
Stupid! Weak! I crush you!
Join the Vosh Rakh or die!
This is an ambush, you fool! Time to die!
You don't care who you hurt, do you?
You are the worst bodyguard I've ever had a displeasure of hiring!
They never would have bothered us if you didn't flaunt your wealth at every opportunity!

Have you visited the new museum? I'm not much into history, but I understand the place is pretty good if you happen to be interested in that sort of thing.\n\nMe? Old stuff kind of gives me the creeps, so I avoid the place like the plague.
Another straggler? Trinimac looks poorly upon those with no sense of urgency. To the left, go!
You picked the wrong Orc, troll-breath!
I demand blood, Elf-lover!
More blood to honor Malacath!
Have you ever used a shovel before?!
I don't see you digging.
Guess that adventurer doesn't care about rebuilding Orsinium.
I will bring Corintthac your head!
Hopefully we meet again on the streets of our glorious city!
My life for yours, my son!
This city has old bones. Solid, like Hist roots. It will serve the Pact well.
I know we had more supplies than this!
This building used to be an old barracks. It's still got that rustic, sparse charm, don't you think?
If you throw up on me, I'm going to knock you off of there! Count on it!
They'll feel that one in the morning.
Now, we kill the mortal.
To me! At once!
The Orcs smell, the Nords are rude, and the Bretons … gods, don't get me started on the Bretons.
I can't repair the fence without wood, but if I leave to get wood, you little furballs will run away, won't you?
Fear the power of the storm!
Not the archives! There's centuries of history in those pages!
Commerce, industry, infrastructure … a wise man with a handful of gold could make his fortune here.
I saw an Orc trying to repair a water wheel the other day, but no matter how hard he punched it, the darn thing refused to turn.
Quiet! Don't let the green-tusks hear you!
You will face justice! All of you!
I don't see why he can't be anywhere on time!
Do you mind?
I just have to make sure I don't land on anyone, I guess.
She'll never forgive me. And why should she? You're a fool Kavzind! A fool!
If the guards find me here, they'll kill me! Let me in!
A melon rind or a scrap of meat? Some old bread? Anything, please! I'm begging you.
Someone's deep in their cups again.
What're you talking about? I'm not drunk! I think you're drunk!
Please, when you're done using the tables, clean up after yourself.
Ugh. Even the filthy echateres are beginning to look tasty.
Damn these fish. I need a spear … or a crossbow. Or a crossbow that shoots spears!
Don't interfere! This is mine and mine alone!
I never knew the Orcs were capable of building such wonders!
Headed outside the city? The rest of Wrothgar isn't quite so inviting, friend. Why not stock up on the essentials?
Leave that broken corpse! Only the best bodies for the flesh colossus.
The Vosh Rakh needs you. Don't make us kill you.
Are the relics even here?
There! That's how it's done!
Isn't this great? You know you love it!
Do you know what kind of swill they drink in Valenwood? It's disgusting!\n\nRest assured, you won't find any fermented boar meat here.
Dagon take you!

I've traced the lineage of an old Nord shield. It's really quite interesting! I'm confident that it belonged to Frohild Frost-Heart, who led a group of warriors against the rogue Dragon priest.\n\nI wonder … was she among the draugr in the barrow?
Daughter? Where are you, girl? Is that you, Orluguk?
Taking a pounding!
Are we supposed to be impressed?
If I'd paid for this, I'd want my money back!
Let's see some more of that!
More! More!
Oh, look—they want to make friends!
Give us more of those!
That was rather admirable!
I smell weakness!
There you are, weakling!
No match at all.
I wish I'd placed a side wager on this!
Don't just stand there and take it!
Yes! This could work!
Don't be afraid, it will all be over soon.
Raaaaaagh!
Yes, yes I see.
[Loud quick shout]
Futility.
[Warning Call]
Shh … hush, now ….
Araaaaaaaaaawwwwnnnnnnn ….
[Loud grunts]
Yes, yes! Delightful!
[A quick shriek of ice on ice]
Where are you aiming? Focus on the door, you fool!
Have at you, simpleton!
No one will consider you a failure if you never abandon your goals.
Trinimac knows that deep down, we're all Orcs at heart.
I'll avoid the Elven Gardens if I can help it. Let that Dremora think it finished the job.
Trinimac knows the heart of every Orc, praise his powerful sword!
How does it all connect to the Dark Anchors? I …. Ah, a customer!
I understand there's a war and all, but they could send us a bard every now and again.
I'm glad they don't make me say "For the Dominion." I'm just here for the coin.
We're stationed where the emperors fling their dung. Smells the same to me.
Kill them! Kill them all!
What would someone who isn't an Orc know of betrayal and broken promises?\n\nMalacath's blessing is not for the likes of you.
Come, beast, and pay tribute!
Malacath knows the anguish in every Orc's heart, praise his relentless fury!
The Imperial City's architecture is quite impressive. Except for all the broken parts.
The Elder Scrolls don't exist. The Moth Priests? Skooma-blind … everyone knows that.
Hmm? Prices aren't negotiable. They sell for what's listed.
We've begun to add books recovered from the city. I hear there are many in the Arboretum.
Some Dremora tied a severed hand to the dog's collar. I think it was its owner's.
No bounty is high enough for the Worm Cult's many crimes.
I know what you're thinking. Yes, this place did come with the original grime.
It is no trouble to run a shop down here. Well, it is many troubles. But this one endures.
We must be making progress. We'll retake the city and end the war soon—I bet.
I never expected the Imperial City would be so … provincial. Mother really talked it up.
No haggling. Prices are final.
The alleys conceal you, but keep watch. An ambush will ruin your day.
Keep throwing more soldiers at the problem. That always works. Hail Jorunn Skald-King.
I'm impressed with what the Orcs have accomplished here. Orsinium is an amazing city.\n\nI just hope it doesn't get sacked again in ten years.

I have no time for disagreements about politics or religion. The trade agreements I'm negotiating will persist, regardless of who is in charge or which god they bow down to.\n\nIn the meantime, I still have much work to do.
You'll find my durzog to be well-trained.
Durzog, on my target!
With all these people coming into the city, we'll be able to sell these fish at twice the price … if we can catch them, anyway.
If she's out drinking again, I'll feed her to the durzogs!
Come here, <<1>>!
Don't wander too far, dog. I'll need ya!
You cannot know the master's schemes. They are everlasting.
<evil laughter 3>
As an expert, I assure you that that isn't what you think it is.
This is my home. I serve Trinimac. Trinimac is all I need.
Praise Trinimac. Please don't hurt me any more.

When I started this trip to Orsinium, I expected to make a new start in a new city. But believe me, this wasn't what I had in mind!\n\nStill, I have stock and I'm open for business, so I guess I can't really complain.
How did you get past the others? Die!
I'd love to talk, but I've got to wipe down the counters.\n\nRight after I finish this beer.
Don't let them escape!
The menders, they're counteracting my elixir. Stop them!
Kill the intruders!
Ah, the fresh air does wonders for my frame of mind! I feel so good, I might just give you a discount today!
Know what I want to do? Drink this down in peace.\n\nKnow what I don't want to do? Answer some damn fool questions!
This one is certain that she can fulfill your every need and desire.\n\nWhat? I am talking about my trade goods. What did you think I meant?

This one doesn't care what you may have heard. We do not deal in illicit goods.\n\nHowever, if you return after we've finished setting up our shop, I may have something that would be of interest to you. Nothing illicit, of course.
Gold. I admit it. I have an unnatural need to collect as much as I can.\n\nThat's why I can't offer you a discount, but I promise that we can strike a good deal.
Nothing in this patch.
As soon as I spread the word, the false priests die!
A good Morkul tonic should always go down gritty. It's good for the digestion.
Hare and doe skins make for fine boots, sure. But if you're looking for a new bag, you can't beat echatere leather.
Only thing we Morkul grunts like better than steel is a stiff drink. Lucky you, I've got plenty to spare!
Tired of the slop they serve in the longhouse? I've got plenty of fresh ingredients right here. Have a look.
These nobles and their high boots and riding crops and lacquered saddles, bah! A true rider needs nothing but a stout heart and strong knees.\n\nThink you've got what it takes?
Lazghal has been kind enough to let me continue my studies. "Anything to keep you away from the forge," she says. It's funny, right?
Morkul garments are made to last. Think you can do better? Let's see it.
Malacath help those smiths in Orsinium. Nothing but a bunch of soft-soled, nub-tusked, Elf-lovers. Just my opinion, of course.
All right, friend, it's time to tighten those tusks and get to work! What do you need?
Hardwood's tough to come by out here on the coast, but I've got plenty of other goods. What do you need?
If you're looking for the forge, it's just across the bridge. But you can't fold iron on an empty stomach. What can I get you?
In the market for some new armor? Every piece is fit for a chief.
It's been a slow season, what with all the filth from the Reach. So how about it? Want to make a deal?
If you plan on getting in a scrape out here, you'd better stock up on gems. These old crags never play nice.
Cleave your foe with a Morkul weapon and he will not rise again. That is a guarantee.
All manner of goods if you have a mind to buy. What can I get you?
Like what you see? Not me, numbskull, the merchandise! Mauloch's jawbone ….
Selling this junk is hard work. That's why I never do it sober.
Great gear at rock-bottom prices! Don't believe me? Just have a look.
You've angered mother!
I will spit on your corpse!
You want some advice? Buy some provisions, get a little shut-eye, then get on the road. This stronghold is a dried-up relic. Orsinium's the future.\n\nTrust me.
Die in a fire!
You know what makes me thirsty? Everything! Let's have a drink.
Rooting around in that quarry must have made you thirsty. Here, have a drink!
Better loosen that belt. Only thing more dense than graystone is one of my suppers.
Hope you're not looking to buy stone. The quarry's gone dry. If you need supplies though, I'm your Orc.
Ah, it's the Dwarf-junk slayer! Good riddance, eh? What can I get you?
"Elf mischief," they say. Pah! I make more gold in a day than they make in a week. Quarry workers are such wimps!
Never thought I'd miss hauling stone. But I'll tell ya, it beats the snot out of being stuck in a bed all day.
Are you all right? Keep trying—we're close, we must be.
You want to buy something? This better not be a trick.
Let's do this quick. I plan on retiring tomorrow.
Stolen goods? Not so loud. The law has ears everywhere.
The Guard sure doesn't know what we're up to. What are we up to? No? No reason.
"Rhogar held her shield above her head, knowing that Trinimac watched over her."
I never thought an Orcish city would have so many books! Perhaps our people really have turned a corner.
We may not act the part, but Orcs are natural mages. I've barely passed my first tests and I've already learned so much!
It doesn't even hurt. Amazing, huh?
I hope someone deals with this shortage of food soon.
The city won't let us work without feeding us, stop worrying about that.
Fancy a fresh meal? Why not make your own? I've got everything you could need.
Remember, each bas-relief told a different part of the full story.
I miss Eastmarch, but the hunting here is so much better.
I'd like a chance to sample <<1>>'s latest dish!
I hope there's extra.
We believed in her cooking before anyone else. Well, I did. I don't know about you.
Finish the anchor! All others in this land were destroyed.
Soon I'll taste your heart's blood!
Yar gor garag!
Yara ar yorag!
Fire will consume you!
We will make this quick.
You can die. We Daedra cannot!
I'll turn you to soot and cinders!
Your death means nothing to me.
You make it almost too easy!
Look at the pathetic mortal!
Foolish creature! You only delay the inevitable.
This one is the true champion here!
Now you will suffer!
Grovel, and I'll kill you quickly!
You dare not touch the flames.
Now you will feel pain!
Die, Nirnspawn!
