Don't get me wrong. I'd rather the Queen never opened our borders. But some of these foreigners aren't totally worthless. The cat, for example, brews a decent ale, and I found a lizard who works wonders with a mop.\n\nNow, about our business ….

I know a few of my guild-mates have dreams of maybe one day getting invited to join the Psijic Order. I am of the same mind as Vanus Galerion, however. The Mages Guild is superior in every way to that ancient, intractable order.

It has come to our attention that strange sea creatures have been encountered in the wilds of Summerset, even in locations far from easy access to the sea. I find that hard to believe, but we investigate all such reports as a matter of course.

There's something fishy going on in the monastery, and I'm not talking about Adept Glaniano's regular Fredas-night shimmerpike simmer.\n\nBut I digress. Packs. I have them, you want them. Let's make a deal, shall we?

The Divine Prosecution actually had the audacity to examine my sales records! I don't know what they were hoping to find, but I'm sure it has something to do with my new clientele. Well, the Queen says I can sell to whoever I choose! For example ….

The Proxy Queen makes as many proclamations as the Distant Queen, and it causes Marakar's fur to itch! Weren't there enough rules and regulations? No? She had to add a dozen more!\n\nDid you hear the latest? All newcomers must purchase a new pack, yes?

Sleek and fragrant! This one drools at the sight of you, my dearest five-claw! Marakar knows a place where we can zuub-zuub until our tails fall off. Very secluded.\n\nBut business before pleasure, you understand. This pack matches your eyes .…

Sea monsters! Can you believe such tales? Next they'll claim the Sload are invading the island!\n\nI suppose it falls to the Mages Guild to investigate such reports, but frankly, I'm getting too old to run around and cast spells in the wild.

The Proxy Queen sent the strangest request to the magister. She wants us to look into reports of attacks by sea monsters in Rellenthil. You'd think we were back in Black Marsh and not here in civilization.\n\nWas there something you needed?

Psijics running hither and yon, Daedric cultists infiltrating High Elf society, stories of terrible sea monsters … it seems that there's a new threat every other day.\n\nMakes you wonder what kind of a game the gods are playing with poor Tamriel.
I'm still getting used to these Elven cities. Too many spires and towers for my taste, but at least the streets are clean.\n\nSpeaking of clean, I just washed the glasses. Want a drink?

Friend High Elf, welcome! Let me draw pleasure by filling your stomach with the finest food in Summerset!\n\nAn Argonian stopped by and asked if I had a six-ooze parfait. I thought she was joking! The arrivers need to learn to appreciate real food.

Another bit of driftwood tossed up from the sea …. I suppose you heard that I am the greatest chef in all of Alinor? That the Proxy Queen herself loves my peacock confit?\n\nNo? Well, if you were a High Elf, you'd be impressed by my credentials.
They're scattering like minnows! Keep on the offensive!

Well look what the sea washed ashore! Another one of our interesting visitors! Your gold and valuables will be treated with the same care as any High Elf's, you have my word.\n\nYou do use gold as a currency where you come from, don't you?
Greetings thrice over, friend High Elf! May your gold equal the number of stars in the sky above and the number of drops in the sea below!\n\nHow may I be of service?

This is so frustrating! I was sure these reagents would combine to create something useful, but all it seems to turn into is yellow goo.\n\nMaybe a little distance will help me solve the problem. How can I help you?

All the strange faces have badly frightened my countrymen. They see invaders around every bend. Horrible creatures from the ocean depths. Marauding bands of Sea Elves. What's next? They'll probably claim we're being invaded by Daedra! Or Sload, even!

Metal. I love the way it smells, the way it sounds when you pound it with a hammer, the way it feels after it's been shaped and polished.\n\nSorry. I can get kind of emotional about my job. It's a passion, you know?

Before you can use the equipment, I have to ask a few questions. Have you ever used a saw? Do you know the difference between a chisel and a hammer? Are you seeing anyone? If not, what are you doing later?\n\nHey, I don't write the questions!

I saw an absolutely amazing rendition of the Bard of Black Marsh performed by the House of Reveries. It's not as grand as your High Elf operas, but I enjoyed it.\n\nChanging the subject, did you see who entered the palace today. Um, just curious.

Tell me, traveler, have you ever met a Psijic? Those mysterious arcane monks from the displaced island of Artaeum?\n\nOh, no reason. Just trying to make conversation. If the Divine Prosecution asks, though, I never mentioned the topic.

We're as much a part of this alliance as the high-and-mighty Elves and the mangy cats, but how do they treat us? Like unwanted relatives that overstayed our welcome!\n\nSorry. My anger gets the better of me until I have my third cup of bloodfroth.
That's right, I'm a Wood Elf. You got a problem with that?\n\nLook, you're either hungry and want to buy some supplies or you're not. Makes no never mind to me.

Friend High Elf, welcome, welcome. How may this one serve you?\n\nNervous? No. Why would you ask such a thing? Does Nuzon look nervous to you? This one has nothing to hide from the Divine Prosecution. Nothing at all. Did I ask how I may serve you?

This one thinks coming here was a terrible mistake. Despite the queen's promises, the island isn't accepting and open-hearted. Not completely, anyway. Some High Elves are rude, mean. Some are violent.\n\nAnd then there's the Divine Prosecution ….
He left me, abandoned me! But now I serve another!
Feel Spellbreaker's might!
I've lost my voice, but my fire remains!
Let the fire consume you!
Feel winter's cold embrace!
Prince of Pestilence! Make them pay!
My shield! How dare you fools make me drop it!
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
<Sniffling, runny nose.>
Can't you see I'm working?
Oh, how the sickness spreads!
She will wipe the world clean!
You'll never stop Scalecaller! Never!
No! You can't disrupt our research!
Don't fight it! Let it spread!
Be careful of those storm winds! They'll freeze you!
Those freezing attacks could make for good protection!
Perhaps we can use those ice pillars to our advantage!
Be sure to hide behind something before you're hit by an ice shard!
Keep those two apart! They're making each other stronger, somehow.
Oh no, the ogre seems to be summoning skeevers!
Strike any petrified teammate to free them!
Help your friend escape their stone prison!
You can't allow that stone orb to roam free! Eliminate it!
Combat sequence operational.
Stay back!
The Divine Prosecution provides protection for all, even newcomers.\n\nBut even we need help, what with all the incidents springing up around the island. Care to take on a contract?
The Divine Prosecution always appreciates those willing to risk life and limb for the citizens of Summerset.
I thought the contract was self-explanatory. Do you require more information or did you just want to chat before you completed your assigned task?
You should feel honored. You'll all be among the first to feel this blessed illness!
That was fast. I'm impressed! And you know what would impress me even more? If you tell me that you've successfully completed the contract.
I've prepared an antidote for you!
Quick, grab some beetle juice for me!
My blessing will leave you weak!
Do you feel it oozing? Such loving sickness!
Nasty, nasty spells! Let's put a stop to that.
Quick, get me some imp innards!
I require stranglers' sap for my antidote! Quick!
Are you fools going to watch me suffer? Come out!
Wonder if I can train a skeleton to fetch its own femur?
Don't go hoarding all the best parts.
I should learn to command draugr ….
The dead aren't meant to be honored. They are meant to be used.
All this digging. I'd rather kill my own fresh corpses.
Let our enemies come. They will serve us until they crumble to dust.
Good vantages in this ruin. But invaders will have the high ground ….
Ugh, hope that's not Tunnel Cough ….
Watch out for the geyser! I can hear it rumbling!
One strike from that giantess and you're done for!
You get to die! Exciting!
Such supple skin!
You're ours now!
See how I wield death!
Making corpses is my favorite part!
Your corpse will be my prize.
Should I let the spasms kill you?
Fang Lair belongs to the dead!
Summerset remains threatened and the Divine Prosecution needs assistance. Will you once again offer yours?
My respect is only for those who have truly proven themselves devoted to the Divine Prosecution's mission. But I must admit, you're showing promise.
The safety of Summerset remains our highest priority. Make haste and complete the assignment we gave you.
My time is short, so let's keep this brief. Have you completed the task I placed before you?
Will you stop with those nasty antidotes?
Yar gor garag!
It won't be long now. Power unseen for ages.
Fear nothing, the master can mend even death!
Don't let them interrupt the ritual!
You're perfect for my latest experiment.
Yara ar yorag!
Keep behind me and watch them fall in droves!
You broke my chains, I'll break theirs.
Insubstantial and insignificant.
Let's light things up a bit, shall we?
Weak, weak guards! You need to be stronger!

Your timing is impeccable, newcomer. Word of more abyssal geysers have reached my ear. I need you to once again put the knowledge that Cainar and Miriya brought to us to good use—destroy those geysers!
Thanks to you and other brave newcomers, the threat of the abyssal geysers have been kept at bay. Keep up the good work.

We can't leave even a single abyssal geyser active. To do so could spell disaster for all of Summerset.\n\nFind allies among the newcomers and deal with this threat. I promise a reward … provided you succeed.

The Proxy Queen keeps me as busy as a Sapiarch's apprentice! If I need to deal with one more disaster today, I may order the Divine Prosecution to round up vagrants for me to beat upon!\n\nNow out with it. Were you able to disrupt the abyssal geysers?
What is that approaching? Some strange sea beast? Prepare to be boarded, mates!
No! This one is not for eating!
The Oracle can't hide forever.
Did you foresee this, Oracle?
If I knew Master Rolis would be this picky about his clientele, I would've sought another apprenticeship. Do come back later, please.
Well met. What can this humble apprentice mediator do for you?
Truthfully, at this point, you should just ignore most of what Master Rolis says. He's rather an odd duck.
Lotus wouldn't be out this far, we should go back.
Why won't they listen?
I'll strike you down, one by one!
You dare stand against my mistress?
Yours shall be the first of many deaths!
Are you all so eager for death?
How could I lose … to ones such as you?
You fought well, but not well enough.
I shall prove myself worthy of Z'Maja!
I die in … disgrace.
Z'Maja will not … be pleased.
I'll quickly strike you down!
My victory was the only outcome.
You'd do better to join us! Z'Maja is unstoppable.
Cloudrest has already fallen. And so too shall you.
Your shadows are mine!
You shall be lost in my shadows!
Cloudrest has already fallen, you fools …. And so have the Welkynars.
How can I be of service to one as distinguished as yourself?
We newcomers have to stick together! Not sure how else we're going to make it here.\n\nBut here I am, yammering on. Did you come in for something?
Some of the stories I hear, why it's enough to break my heart. Who would think that Summerset citizens could be so cruel? We must help one another in these troubling times.\n\nNow, how may help you?
My chef Holi is just upstairs if you're in need of a hot meal. Such a sweet girl. \n\nOtherwise, I'd be happy to help whatever you need.
If you're heading into Ebon Stadmont, you may as well purchase something. Who knows how long you'll be in there.
Light as a griffon feather, and strong as Trinimac's shield! You won't find better armor in all of Summerset!
You're in the market for leathers, yeah? Here's a tip—don't bother with this frilly High Elf junk. You want sturdy, reliable armor? Buy Orc.
There's no greater joy than having purpose, and my purpose is to help you find just what you're looking for. Come, have a look.
As per my contract, I'm obliged to tell you about the wonderful items I have for sale.
What an honor, that a kerr-oo-vale enter my shop! How can I help you?
These strange High Elf words—my tongue cannot grasp them. Like catching an eel with your bare hands. It's much easier to sell my goods to a fellow newcomer.

Hasn't been easy recruiting new members in Summerset. Most of these Elves seem to think it's beneath them to do the good, honest work of the Fighters Guild.\n\nBut you look like a decent sort. You should consider joining up.
Hasn't been easy recruiting new members in Summerset. Most of these Elves seem to think it's beneath them to do the good, honest work of the Fighters Guild.\n\nBut you and I, we know better.
Don't know why a scrawny thing like you is even at my shop, but you can't turn away good gold I suppose.
I don't want to go back to the library. They can't—they can't make me!
Vykosa said we'll be safe. She'll keep us safe.
Hunters? In the keep? Just my luck!
Get away from my pack! They're all I have!
How do you taste, I wonder? I bet you're all delicious.
You dare strike against the Moon Hunter Pack? Idiots!
The Silver Dawn was foolish. Weak. Just like you.
The Silver Dawn thought to lure her. Trap her. But Vykosa was prepared.
I'm sure my guards will appreciate some fresh meat!
My victory shall make your corpses taste all the more delicious.
Your deaths shall be but a note in my archives!
Such fighting spirit, wasted. What a pity.
Our prey has finally arrived!
Why did you hunt it? Why didn't you turn back?
All I need to do is rip out your heart. Should be easy enough!
I know you're stronger than this. You have to keep trying!
This grove is now your grave.
And so the hunt has finally ended.
Well? What are you waiting for? Be off and get that pledge done right!
I hope you're here to tell me of your tremendous victory! And not the kind that involves the local tavern wench. \n\nWell, maybe you could tell me about that later.
Insignificant worms!
Mortal fools, how dare you defy me?
I grow tired of this game.
You only delay the inevitable. The island will sink beneath the waves.
You only delay the inevitable, mortals.
I dwell in the darkness and one day I shall return.

Why, it's been nothing but excitement with all these visitors in Lillandril. But sometimes, one does fear you may all be overstaying your welcome.
It's been nothing but crime sprees and beggars, ever since these nebarra have begun squatting in Lillandril.
The Sapiarchs sure seem to have been in a tizzy, ever since the Mage's Guild arrived in town. I've never seen them quite so flustered.
I am not alone in this fight! My shadows shall aid me.
You'll all burn beneath my flames!
You dare attack my mistress? Heathens!
To fight Z'Maja is foolishness. You'll never win.
You're nothing against Silaeda's flames!
Strike them down, Belanaril!
My gryphon shall freeze you where you stand!
So this is the Kinlady's mighty resistance? Pathetic.
You dare try to resist? Don't make me laugh!
There's no use fighting back when we've already won!
How could I … be defeated?
The Guild tells me to hold my tongue against these High Elf insults. But there are only so many storms a tree can weather before it breaks.
The Mages Guild cares about new ideas, new discoveries. Ever is our eye on the future. The Sapiarchs, however, seem content to only wallow in the past.
Soon as Daring put on that mask, all the High Elves started treating him different. Respectful like. I could use me that kind of respect.
Paredan, read us something! Paredan?
I have many things on my mind. Making new friends isn't one of them. Please leave me alone.
The sea promises a safe journey today. Care to travel somewhere?
Do you see how Cloudrest has fallen? This will be Summerset's fate, if we don't stop that accursed Sea Sload once and for all!
Sunhold has already fallen. There's no hope left for you all!
Forget the nobles and deal with those intruders!
Quickly! Kill the prisoners!
Summerset will fall! My death means nothing!
There'll be time enough to fix this once you're all dead.
Not too sure about that Mirulon guy yet.
The Sapiarch will loosen his grip on us. Or we will make him.
Keep your weapons within reach. Enemies lurk nearby.
When your muscles go rigid and your flesh burns, remember: this is your fault.
This is the calm before the storm.
By sea and spell, by wind and magic!
This would make a fine place to begin a new brood.
It's like they want to be caught in our web.
To feed us is an honor. Why do the mortals flee?
A mortal heart beats nearby. Keep wary.
These damn Yaghra are ruining all my research!
We need to find a way to purge the ruin of these beasts!
Weak wine. Bland food. No wonder these Elves are so mirthless.
I swear these nebarra have soured every bottle by their mere presence.\n\nIf the proprietor hires any to stomp the grapes, I'll wash my hands of this place forever.
I prefer my mead to any wine, but the grape stomping does look fun.
Can you believe someone of my status has been tucked away into such a homely nook? My normal rooms have been reserved for some artist.\n\nWell, where is she? I haven't seen her?
Did you—did you know—that this establishment throws out people for—for disturbing the harmony? Have you ev—have you—what's that even—absurd, right?
Newcomers continue to enter the city in droves. How are we to keep track of them all?
My family has bred horses for generations. You won't find their match anywhere in Summserset.
Ever been to Wasten Coraldale? Well, don't. Nothing of interest out there unless you fancy yourself an angler.

I have never understood the idea of a public house, but I think I finally see the appeal. It is like leaving all decorum at the door and letting some beer-soaked beast take the reins. It must be very liberating.
If the Queen likes you so much, maybe she can clean up after you!
That bailiff has been counting every board and nail in my crates. I don't know what she's looking for, but she won't find it.
Trouble with the law? Head to the door right around this corner. I know some folks who can help you.
Summerset used to be balanced. The right amount of people, the right amount of space. And, of course, the right amount of prey to hunt.\n\nWhat was the Queen thinking, opening the border?
Anginil's been complaining about his fish supply lately. I wonder if anything's the matter at Wasten Coraldale?
I guarantee you, my weapons will never falter in the right hands.
And the low growl of his voice built in an … echo? No—crescendo of lust and … and … loneliness! A crescendo of lust and loneliness unfurled.\n\nOh! This book is going to make me rich!
I cannot believe one of these newcomers tried to pickpocket me! And when I tried to lecture him on the nature of moral compunction, he ran off. The nerve.
Quite a few of my High Elf customers have complimented my beard. Well, at least I think they were compliments. A bit hard to tell, sometimes.
I get new shipments all the time. Take a look, if you like.
See something you like? Feel free to take a good, long look.
My wares speak for themselves. If you're interested, good. If not, farewell.
Whatever you need, I have it! Probably.
Buzzing, cousin, shoving? Ah, sorry friend! Huzzin is just trying to come up with his next catchphrase. How can he help you?
All are allowed within our temple, should they choose to follow our moral path. But I do fear such enlightenment may be out of reach for many newcomers.
We must solicit the Proxy Queen for more funding. The number of visitors to the monastery may have increased, but donations have not.
"Though there may be work without glory, there is always glory to be found in hard work."
I like this spot. The gentle babbling of a nearby waterfall, the shade of this beautiful tree. If you ever need a quiet moment, feel free to join me.
Welcome to one of Alinor's finest shops! Not that the High Elves would ever admit such a thing, given my round ears and all.
I shall not remain on the streets for long, be sure of that!
It has been said that you are a mighty warrior. We shall see what you are truly made of if ever I spot you in the Battlegrounds.
The Battlereeve claims you have potential as a warrior. I don't yet quite see it.
Though one must be wary of the perverse influence of outsider music … I must admit the tune is catchy.
I heard that Ebon Stadmont is haunted. Or was that the Direnni Acropolis? No, no, it was definitely a forest. Or maybe a town?
No need to look drab in your outings. Let's bring some vibrancy to your ensemble!
I know these newcomers expect Elven buildings to spring from the ground like magic, but the grandeur of Alinor is shaped by generations of expert masons.
The Captain's seemed … wistful since we got back from the front. War has left its mark, I think.
This would be a wonderful place to try flying, don't you think? One day I'm going to jump and spread my wings for all the city to see.
There is nothing in this city Khajiit finds so fascinating as this fountain. How does the water get from the river to here?
Take a moment to center yourself if you plan to enter the Royal Palace. It is no place for frivolity or haste.

You've proven yourself on the Battlegrounds, and now it's time to remind others of your great deeds.
Can I help you with something? Some new furniture perhaps?
Everyone needs something to keep them kicking in the field, and I have the wares to help you do just that.
You want to hear the crowds cheering? For your name to be sung? For victory after victory to be gained by your hand? \n\nMy shop can help you accomplish it all.
The creatures known as indriks present a rich subject for study. I may have to visit the Royal Menagerie in Sil-Var-Woad, so that I might observe one up close.
With the Mages Guild I'm given the opportunity to travel the world and study the mysteries of creation firsthand. If I'd joined the College of Sapiarch, I'd likely never leave the grounds.

I've been assured this place is a well kept secret, but I can't help but get nervous. For all we know, the Divine Prosecution could do a sweep any minute.
Let's get down to business, shall we?
Been more than a few newcomers trying to move in on my territory. Not anyone you'll ever meet, mind you. Unless you got a thing for corpses.
What was the Queen thinking, opening the border? Now we have to inspect every inch of cargo to ensure nothing illicit is being brought into the city.\n\nNo one ever thinks of the customs inspection.

Did I get an invoice in Shimmerene for that banner cloth? Oh, wait—the banner cloth wasn't for the Royal Palace, was it?

Never know when one of those geysers will spring up. Better make sure you're prepared.
Death in these wilds can be a sure thing for some. You would be wise to purchase precautionary supplies, should the worst come to pass.
Someone needs to drive the Maormer from Sunhold. If you're willing for such a task, my goods can help you prepare.
Interested in a purchase? Despite my isolated location, my wares are all of the highest quality.
Strange news on the road from Russafeld. Might give the town a wide berth for awhile. In the meantime, are you interested in a purchase?
Take a look at the goods I have. Brought them all the way from Hammerfell!
Pretty strange happenings in ruins of the Keep of Eleven Forces. People go in, different people come out. What could possibly be going on in there?
Have you seen the Crystal Tower? You won't find its like anywhere else in Tamriel.
Most don't like to eat indriks. Say it feels unpure. Me though? I just see them as deer with a little bit of extra magic, is all.
I used to guide travelers all over these coasts, from Corgrad to Alinor. But then those vile creatures started swarming ashore. It's better to stay in a place with walls.
Just the other day I saw a member of the Mages Guild take a trimming from one of my plants. The monster! The aesthetic value was tarnished, and for what? Alchemical experiments?
Thankfully, neither the Sapiarchs nor members of the Mages Guild seem interested in drinking here. It's one of the few places where I can find peace and quiet.
This one knows of a menagerie on the other side of the island where the Elves have found a method to tame indriks. Think of it! To see these magical beings, to study them.
It's common knowledge that the Sapiarchs are going out of their way to hinder our practices in Lillandril. Just how petty can they be?
I thought being stationed to Summerset would present new challenges, but the only thing I grapple with is whether to put my trousers on before noon.
I was hoping to get a cheap room for the night. But the ephems have the entire city booked up! Typical.
In honor of the Queen's decree, I'm toasting every year of Ayrenn's reign! Hip hip!

Whatever parchment the High Elves use for their books holds an edge better than steel. I'm on my sixth paper cut this hour!
There's rumors of strange things crawling over this island. Make sure you're ready for every eventuality.
If you wish to see the plethora of items I make available for purchase, then by all means.
As soon as I heard Summerset was opening its borders, I knew I had to seize the opportunity. And, if my sales are anything to go by, I was right to do so.
Every bed in town has a body in it. Some have several. I've been sleeping beneath a hedge for the time being.
A few people disappear into the Monastery, and everyone assumes the worst. My opinion? Ignorance is bliss. The less you worry, the better off you'll be.
I didn't think there would be reason for the Fighters Guild to come to Summerset, but it seems everywhere has danger these days.
As calm as the port is, the open ocean was a nightmare. I thought we'd sink every few minutes during the crossing! But now that I'm here, I have to say that the view is very much worth it.

My superiors in the Divine Prosecution were very insistent that all proper procedures be adhered to and signed, in triplicate. Of course, such thoroughness will result in processing delays for newcomers.
There's got to be a dice game somewhere in this city. Even the shining island of Summerset has a shady side.
I have been on the same page for over an hour. Every time I try to make progress, some errant shout from the dock breaks my concentration. \n\nMust I become a recluse to read in peace?!
The tavern offered me a room if I could bring them a basket of fish, but I haven't even gotten a single bite today. Just my luck.
Lots of folks passing through the city these days. Lots of luggage ripe for plunder, if your fingers are quick enough.
Kinlady Avinisse knows what's best for Shimmerene. That's why all newcomers are checked twice before being allowed to wander the city freely.
I'm a little annoyed that the guard won't tell me how long my husband will be inside the Monastery. But we waited months to get here. I can wait a little longer!
The mer of this land trace a lineage to the divine. Though we are clad in mortal flesh, we can hope one day to join our ancestors amongst the stars.
Sadly, not all of my beasts weathered the passing well. My poor camels haven't eaten well for days.
A dockhand is only good as their strength. With growing age comes unemployment. But where else will Farniri go?
The authorities of Summerset aren't keen to call upon our guild for aid. We'll just have to show them we can be depended upon.\n\nYou look like a warrior of worth. Why not join the cause?

I know I'm the only merchant in Rellenthil. So why are you my first customer today? It just doesn't make any sense!

Hey, do you think I could get into the House of Reveries? I was always told I had a nice voice. Though hiding this face behind a mask would be a real shame.
As stage manager, I'm in charge of every set and prop on stage. Sometimes it's thankless work, truth be told. After all, the audience tends to focus on the performers.
You won't believe how often my wife and I are teased about our matching names. I admit it may be a tad tacky, but Adagio was just so happy when she suggested it. How could I say no?
I just love spending my holidays in Rellenthil. I'll watch a performance, have a nice meal, and end my trip with a day in the bathhouse.

You'll find many of our troupe members throughout Summerset. After all, we cannot expect every patron of the arts to make a trip to Rellenthil.\n\nOf course, the Manor of Masques shall always be home to us.
The name's Mead. A little silly, I know, but I thought it fitting. Might not be quite as fancy as the other performers, but then again, neither am I!
Be careful, newcomer. The undead beasts behind those walls will make a meal of you without the goods I provide.
I've got to admit, I'm a little thrown off by the aesthetic, mate. No un-paintings, less than a thousand angles, hardly any transliminal spheroids …. I don't know. I'd give it a soft "adequate."

If I had to pick a favorite cursed item it would definitely be the silver-tongued quill. Oh but the fan of the false-face is also very good! And the crystallized indrik heart is always so pretty. Curses. I don't think I can pick a favorite after all.
I cannot rest! I must defeat you!

I shall relish the taste of your flesh!

Welcome to the Lilmoth Countinghouse. How can I help you today?

I erect the spine of cheerful commerce. Please, tell me what you need.
Looking to purchase? Have no fear. I sell only that which the dryskins consider quality goods. Whatever that should mean.
I'm in the business of heroes. Not training them or nothing, but rather rewarding them. The more deeds you accomplish, the more furniture will become available to you.
Always you travelers move this way and that, like so many fish in a river. Remember to take the time to wallow, beeko, or one day you'll find that the mud has dried. Stay moist!
Crocodile hide makes for both sturdy and attractive armor. It's not a look that many can pull off, however. Takes a certain amount of confidence.
Once, I was egg-sister. But now that I have joined the Mages Guild, I am lukiul—Imperialized. I feel I shall never again belong in Murkmire.
This purple is no good, no. It must be bruising, pulsing. Like the bloated face of a drowned dryskin.
Sithis is the changer, and there is no greater change than the killing stroke. Use these goods and you will earn the Serpent's favor.
I've been hoping to cut a deal with the Dead-Water tribe for a while, but they refuse to trade with outsiders. I suppose I'll just have to stick with Lilmoth folk for now.
No, no!
Stay crouched and focus on tracking!
I'll tear you to shreds!
It's time for my dark hunt to begin!
I'm creating a trap for your foe! Hang in there!
Now, now! Lure your adversary to my trap!
Let's finish this hunt!
I can never be truly defeated.
My defeat is not my end.
Even in death, I can still fight.
The spriggan saplings are gathering power!
You must protect yourself from the spriggan's elemental might!
You're now as silent as the owl's wings.
Another successful hunt. As always.
It seems you were nothing against a bear's might!
In the Huntsman's name, I shall strike you down.
You should run while you have the chance. I always love a good chase.
I'll hunt every last one of you down!
Hunters! To your positions!
Move, you dungheaps! We've got prey to hunt!
Lord Hircine continues to give us such exciting prey!
The Hunting Grounds are glorious! Don't you want to remain?
Raise your weapons! Our prey has arrived!
Never has this one seen such spotless prey!
Fresh prey? Why, it's my lucky day!
By Hircine, stop moving around so much!
Hurry up, you curs! Our enemies are upon us!
I'll bury you in an icy grave!
Your flesh will become my strength!
What fools to fight against the Moon Hunter Pack!
We're trapped within this eternal hunt! Let us leave! Please!
My spear of light shall show you the way!
Z'Maja opened a gate into her dark realm! We must destroy it.
We must destroy the gateway's source of power!
If that gateway isn't destroyed, Z'Maja's shade shall cross over!
Let's show these runts what the Moon Hunter Pack is made of!
The Moon Hunter Pack will crush you all!
You think you can trap me?
I've had enough of this. See how you fare against my undead servants!
<Confrontational Goblin gibberish.>
<mocking Goblin gibberish.>
<Celebrant Goblin gibberish.>
<Reverent Goblin gibberish.>
Her light is always guiding.
I live to serve.
Defilers!
Defilers!
We stood by as our empire crumbled, but it remains here. That's all that matters.
You were blinded by greed, but her light will make you see clearly.
When you are remade, you will wonder why you resisted.
You may live to serve, or die a pointless death.
The guiding light burns everyone who reaches too closely.
You should have begged for mercy.
Your will was never a match for hers.
Supplicants, you will serve for all time.
<Threatening Goblin gibberish.>
Murkmire, eh? I could use a change of scenery.
Heed Kyne's wisdom! A terrible storm brews within the skies of Murkmire!
<Maniacal Goblin laughter.>
<Great exertion.>
This venture grows bigger and bigger! It's a tough beast to wrangle. Could you lend Jee-Lar a hand today?
<Bellowed Goblin gibberish.>
If there were two—perhaps three—more of you, this expedition might not be necessary at all!
The sooner you finish that task the better, my friend.
Have you finished that errand I gave you? It would be most welcome-welcome news.
This stage of the ritual is crucial!
<Defiant Goblin gibberish>

Jee-Lar has been tirelessly working on procuring resources for our expeditions into Murkmire. I really don't know what Cyrodilic Collections would do without him!\n\nIf you would, you might offer him some assistance.
Try using the skeevatons to sabotage it!
My furniture is sure to impress anyone who visits your house! After all, someone of your reputation deserves a chance to brag.
Many call themselves heroes, but so few prove it. It's an honor to meet someone who has. Feel free to have a look at my wares.
All my wares are blissfully free of mud and maggots. Not something I can say for every vendor peddling in Lilmoth ….
Guars are excellent for traversing in swampland. Many travelers are deterred by the fangs, but I assure you; all of my steeds are as even tempered as they come.
Either the Argonians of Murkmire are very good at keeping Daedra away, or very lucky. Either way, we cannot let our guard down.
<Tantrum Goblin gibberish>

I've spoken to many mages in Murkmire about their practices, and most have been happy to share. But the way they speak is so … metaphorical. Abstract. Overall, near impossible for an outsider to understand.
Hey, swamp-bait. There's some work that needs doing that I can't get around to. Interested?
Suppose I'll have to get used to seeing you around. Unless this work finally gets you, too.\n\nGot a job if you're willing.
You've developed a taste for this. But has Sithis developed a taste for you?
If you continue to seek its favor, Sithis may numb your agony with its cold gaze before it sinks its fangs into you.
Nothing else needs doing right now. Take a break or something.
You may have survived so far, but the worst is yet to come!
Finally! It is time for the final fight!
And so ends this bloody contest!
That's how the Blackguards fight!
And so the challengers come crawling back!
Perhaps the challengers have some fight left after all!
We are the unshackled! We are the unchained!
When fruit falls from a tree, the wise hunter seeks sustenance in other places. Be a wise hunter and return later.
Swift action yields swift results. Get to it.
Come on, put up a fight!
I want to see blood!
Weaklings! Do you want the challengers to win?
This fight drags like a limp leg.
A foul wind has blown for our challengers, it seems.
A mire gnat bites harder than these challengers.
I always do love watching a little bloodshed.
What a clever strike, challenger!
You'll have to move much quicker than that, dears!
You look like the wamasu that caught the dragonfly. Was your hunt successful?
Are you an adventurer? Have I got an adventure for you!
I offer a test of spirit and skill that will push you to your limits and perhaps lead to your swift and painful death.\n\nThere is no greater honor for a warrior of the Naga-Kur!
Your corpse will serve me well!
This might be working! This might be working ….
Ah, Rootmender. I am glad to see you have returned.
Completion of this task will greatly help the Root-Whisper Village. Thank you.
You planted the seed which grew into this village. Will you also help it grow?
The Argonians have a funny way of thinking. To them, things like regret or grudges are useless. Perhaps that is why they were able to make peace with the Dark Elves and form the Ebonheart Pact.
You ever feel like you're being followed? I just … can't shake the feeling, ever since I arrived in Lilmoth.

If you ever meet a priest of Sithis, try to talk as little as possible. Anything you say will just encourage them to keep spouting their nonsense.\n\nXuth, we don't call them nothing-speakers for nothing.
May we one day be as strong and proud as the Hist which guides us.
I've carved quite a few seed dolls for bonding rituals. Frogs tend to be the most popular.
Do not strike until you see the sweat glittering off their scales!
You better be up to no good, you hear? Otherwise you best be walking away!
Honei, are you out there?

Lilmoth is known as the Festering Jewel of Black Marsh. Not surprising, given the humidity. And the bugs, of course. And the occasional festering corpse ….\n\nBut other than that, it's been a great place to visit!
When I was young, hatchlings emerged from their shells with a spear in one hand and a sword in the other. Now? Well, see for yourself.\n\nNot one of them will survive the Path.

I boast, but every word is true. I am the tribe's best hunter with a bow, though I do not need it to hunt most game. Slugs, for example. I simply sneak up on them and scoop them into a basket.\n\nThey are exceedingly slow, after all.
I open wide and munch upon this delicious bowl of worm and marsh moss stew.\n\nI would offer you some, but I understand it does terrible things to an uninitiated outsider's internal organs.
Do not get too close, outsider. I would rather not catch any of your strange afflictions.

I assist the Jekka-Wass in studying the calendar. \n\nIt is fortunate for him that I offered my services. He is far more concerned with his books than the basic maintenance needed for such a monument.
I give you a petulant gaze and ask you to leave me. This is my quiet place.
Well, here's something you don't see everyday. A new village rising out of the swamp like a baby bird emerging from its egg.\n\nI hope Stibbons takes the hint and does likewise.
I always said that Stibbons was a tough egg to crack. Now that's literally true.
So many stones within this village. It makes me feel … restless. How did our ancestors once live within such confinement?
The Root-Whisper Village is still in need of a tree-minder. Until then, I trust that Xukas will look after the needs of the Hist.
I have heard many speak of the village's defensive strength, due to the stone which surrounds us. This will be useful, as our warriors are only now learning to fight alongside one another.
Look at this bleeding heart!

I feel it in my bones, Rootmender. I am a part of this village now. A part of this Hist.\n\nTruthfully, I am a little frightened. Such a change I have never expected, and never known. Still, I must embrace it. So is the will of change.
The spirits cry out! Do you hear them?
The void shall become my power!
We must be empty, like the void. And from that emptiness, we shall create, like Sithis created all that is.
It's time to meet your end!
How am I supposed to dance to this? There ain't no tempo. Heck, there's not even a melody!
I grind my teeth in vexation. "His bones cracked beneath the might of his enemy's heavy club." These words cannot be rewritten!
Good to see you!
All right, that should do it!
What's taking you so long?
Hurry it along already!
If you ever come snout-to-snout with a Shadowscale, you're only chance at survival is to run. And even then? It is not a very good chance.
During the day, I sell items for my guild. But during the night—well, I actually work nights as well. I need the gold.\n\nBut one day, I shall become a thief!
Your hands have moved swiftly, like the storming winds, carrying away what you wish. Now my hands will clean that which you have taken.

I may be used to handling dirty items, but it seems every inch of Murkmire is covered in mud. If only I could return to Elsweyr ….\n\nOf course, I would be executed immediately if I did. So it is a life of swamps for me.
The Argonians may not care much about the past, but that doesn't mean they're forgetful about their debts. Trust me, I know that better than most.
In Murkmire, the priests of Sithis are known as nisswo, the nothing-talkers. This is because they speak the words of the void. \n\nOr so Nisswo Kahei tells me, at least.
More are on their way!
The ritual is in danger!
Keep your money - I'd rather enjoy your experiences.
Ever feel like something is following you? Something hollow, perhaps?
Been caked in mud yet? Perhaps the plunge? Either favor the complexion, I hear.
This season: Adventure! Through the dankest holes, deepest ruins, and darkest woods, all.
This season: Fabricants and animunculi! You've not known life until you've seen a clockwork gala.
This season: Collecting unusual stones. Ideally from the heart of Cyrodiil.
There's an old Orcish saying about birthdays … Never celebrate your son's.
Not much of a one for competition, personally. I do enjoy a friendly wager, though.
There's this cocktail, quite popular - the "dubious throne." Reminds me of a chamberpot.
I've a hobby this time of year. Trading in commodities, if you take my meaning.
It's a birthday! Though for whom, I'm not sure. Or what, perhaps.
Fancy a brief chat?
We're ready to move against those weakling Bright-Throats.
And the shop owner never locks his door!
You dryskins! You're all so soft and squishy!
Tough? Those Dead-Water kuudas are scaleless tail-lifters!
The cargo train only has two guards! It's easy pickings!
We're the Blackguards. Mayhem is our middle name!
Bright-Throats? How can they be prey when they barely understand the meaning of the word?
Famia and her ilk … they task us!
We've fallen behind on the slave trade. Time to double our efforts.
The merchant caravan? Not a problem!
Is that pouch of gold for me? I'm touched.
They actually came to the marsh! For a vacation!
Daril! Who stashed the daril?
Why must every coffer I open contain slug slime? I hate slug slime!
Give me your share or I'll hold back my support the next time you need it.
Just drink it. I made it myself.
I may not have scales, but I'm as much a Blackguard as you are!
Another ship full of tourists has arrived. Their gold is as good as ours!
It was another one of Famia's crew. They're everywhere lately!
Don't mind me. I'll just sit here until you decide on our next target.
That last shipment we absconded with was oozeworthy!
The miregaunts are particularly active today.
The outsiders, they have no idea what's about to happen.
Can someone explain the plan to me again?
Put down that haunch of guar and get back to work!
Someone let the cooking fire burn out again.
Don't look now, but I think that dryskin is staring at your tail.
If the guards get in our way, kill them all.
Ahkur is the harbormaster for Alten Meerhleel. You can find him in the dock house, down the way.
So many visitors, so many boats. At this rate all of these fish will be frightened away from my favorite fishing spot.
In some ways, the lantern mantis is more akin to a beast than a plant. Walk too closely by it, and it will be quick to strike you.
If one more of these fetchling lizards calls me their beeko …. I am not, nor ever will be, a friend to these s'wits.
Prey is scarce these days. Too many careless feet stomping the muck.
Waxhuthi! Norgsa oj!
Do you seek passage? Come, let the waters take you where you wish to be.
Many steps I have taken, and many more I will take. But for now, I stand and wait for you. Are you in need of my wares?
It's my hope that we can learn more about this monument, and share that knowledge with the rest of the Mage's Guild. Luckily, Jekka-Wass Vozei has been nothing but helpful.
Because of you, Mewah-Jez has been relegated to assisting Kishi. You may have walked the Path, but I am not impressed.
These are not our egg-brothers and sisters. Not yet.
All the Hollow are good for is mulch. They rot too quickly for dead-walkers.
The tribes of Murkmire do not understand. If we do not work with the ojels, we will one day be consumed by them. Best to make allies, not enemies.
I remember when I walked the Path of the Lily. If Kishi is half the Naga his father is, these novices will have no problem acquiring the sacred flower.
I accept your gold, outsider, but bear in mind that I only carry the finest wares of the Naga-Kur. You will not find any strange, foreign vendibles here.
You cannot stop us, greels.
Look! Another ignites!
To me! Over here!
Fall back, I have a potion for you!

I've been all over Tamriel, you know. \n\nOrsinium was nice, but a bit too … barbaric. Morrowind was lovely, if not for every other Dark Elf calling me a fetcher. And Summerset? Beautiful, but far too politically charged for my tastes.
I deserve it, but not half as much as you!
Look at him, Haxara! You're nothing to him. He's going to kill you and not even care why!

I once thought the Bright-Throats weak. They cowered behind flower words, and refused to defend our home from the outsiders who would ruin it.\n\nBut without the help of their tribesmen, this village would have never awakened. I cannot deny this.
A volunteer? What shall I make of you, then?
That hurt, but your pain will be so much more intense.
Death won't stop me, ojel scum.
The Root-Whisper Village is still in need of a tree-minder. Until then, I trust that Jaxsik-Orrn will look after the needs of the Hist.
The Remnant is mine! Mine!
I will not let you take this from me!
We Bright-Throats trade with many tribes. If you have a need, I'm sure we can fulfill it.
Both wares and travelers travel through Alten Meerhleel, like fish in the stream. And when they need new wares? I am here with an open net.
The chimes shiver with joy from your passing Rootmender. When you visit, every step is music.

I long to test myself in battle. Perhaps the war in Cyrodiil will help me accomplish this.\n\nBut is such a goal worth dying on foreign soils, away from the roots of the Hist? I am not sure on this, and so I sit and think.
It's strange, but sometimes I can … feel the Hist. How can that be so? I haven't been in Murkmire since I was a hatchling!\n\nOh, ignore me. You didn't come to my shop for chit chat, after all!
Use your brains as well as your brawn!
It's gathering power!
Warriors of Light! Join me!
Can't you see it's futile?
The spices of Elsweyr sell for twice as much within the lands of man and mer. But always there is the danger of bandits, of beasts, of death. That is why Nakiri now plies his trade in Rimmen.
A bit of this, a bit of that! Strong enough to kill a cat! Poisons bubble, poisons brew. And what can I do for you?
I come from a long line of respectable blacksmiths, dating way back to the middle First Era. So you can trust that I sell the finest steel in all of Rimmen.
Riverhold is a fragrant town. It was there that I first learned to whittle wood.
Sharazzur has received many fine proposals from many fine Khajiit. But this one's true love will always be the clothing he creates.
I fell in love with Elsweyr the moment I arrived. It has a certain … rustic charm. Not to mention an urgent need for competent enchanters.
Today, Nirshala faithfully works for her guild. But tomorrow? Well, tomorrow is a different matter altogether.
My wares will celebrate your greatest accomplishments. Once you've accomplished them, of course.
Rumor has it that a Mehrunes cult settled in Darkpool Mine. I bet they're up to all kinds of trouble. I wouldn't sell to them if they paid me all the gold in Elsweyr!
If ever you are hungry, you come to Saizeh, yes? Her meals are best for filling empty bellies.
Mizarr feels as much a part of the Dominion as he does the Empire. After all, both care nothing for Rimmen, much less this one's humble inn.
I've learned so much since coming to Rimmen. My leather wares are now more supple and durable than ever! Care to check for yourself?
My peers back in Summerset were just so narrow minded. When it comes to fashion, we High Elves can learn so much from the other races. Especially the Khajiit!
You have not wielded weapons like those of Khajiiti make. Swift movements, precise strokes! All can be yours, provided you have the gold to pay.
The wood that Abazbi crafts is both strong and supple. Of course, she would work with nothing less.
Sad to say, but your valuables will not last long against the many cunning thieves roaming Rimmen's streets. So why not deposit them here?
The Rimmen Bank is an honorable institution. You'll find no place in Elsweyr that comes close to our gleaming reputation.
Yes, we have, a lot of … furnishings. To, you know, furnish your home. If you want it furnished!
Warm days, cool drinks, and plenty of packs to select from. What more could a Saxhleel ask for?
There are many varieties of senche-cat steeds. Senche-lions are common in Anequina, but you'll find more senche-leopards down in Pellitine.
When someone has a need, Adi has the answer. See for yourself.
You know, when I was recruited by this guild I had no idea how much I would miss Grahtwood. Especially the trees. Why doesn't Elsweyr have more trees?
Hello, I have many fine swears—wares! I mean wares! We have many fine wares for you to swear. To peruse! Ha.
Many greetings, traveler. Why don't you take a break at my shop? I'd be just as happy to hear a tale as to collect some of your gold.
Ask any question of me, and I shall humbly answer. For it is my only wish to serve you faithfully, just as I serve my guild.
The Dragon attacks have been rough. I've lost more soldiers this past season than I have in years. But we're learning, and we're still fighting.
I have visited many storytellers, writing down their words and documenting their stories. This way, I hope to preserve such stories for future generations.
Yes? Oh, right, you're a customer. Let's make this quick, then.
It is my hope that the guild will one day send me to Murkmire. I have often heard that the magic performed by the Saxhleel natives is quite beautiful.
Never have you seen finer thieves than the ones within this refuge. Unless you look to my rival, Bolefin. He is a distinct exception.
I don't even know why I stay in this city. Between Migarra's bragging and all the sugary meats …. Well, least I got customers.
To be young again! To have all the wisdom of her age, with the limber hands of a younger Khajiit. Dahzini would be the greatest thief Rimmen has ever known.

Being a hulkynd doesn't allow you many options in Summerset. I had to do some rather unsavory things to survive. But now I live a quiet life, counting change for petty thieves.\n\nFunny, but that's a step up.
You think the Jovial Lambasters would be interested in letting me join? I mean, I have a lot of experience. Admittedly, most of that experience is in sales ….
Alik'r is warm and full of riches, this is true. But the Redguards do not easily trust Khajiiti merchants. Even one as charming as me.
These Elsweyr Khajiit aren't so bad, once you get to know them. Smell a lot better than I thought they would, too.\n\nBut enough about that. What can I get you?
The Prowl's full of dangerous creatures if you're looking for big game. Me? I get my thrills on the open road.\n\nBut look at me, prattling on. How can I help you?
These city merchants look at Halani as if she is dirt, just because she does not have a fancy stall or fancy papers. But she also does not pay their fancy taxes. Ha!
All prices are fixed, and all sales are final. You want to haggle, go find a fruit salesman.
Be careful out there, or you'll wind up like me. Crippled, ornery, and an expert on rugs.\n\nSpeaking of furnishings, what do you need?
You won't find better equipment anywhere in Elsweyr. Trust me, I've scouted my so-called competition.
You are in the market for a new sword, yes? Or maybe a sturdy axe? With Bizdar's weapons in hand, your victory is assured!
Now you're in my trap, Tharayya!
Ex-wife, enjoy your ex-life! Hah! Haha! Hahaha!
Like I'd let you kill me.
Where did you learn to fight, Shad Astula Academy?
There is no light beyond hers.
All we need is her. You'll see.
Once more, the city of Rimmen is free to enjoy Amajhan's tasty wares without fear of death or fur! All thanks to you and Queen Khamira, of course.
This one trusts that a refined Khajiit such as yourself has the taste for sweet brews. Please, feel free to have a look.
Thank the Moons, you are back. Old Ri'hirr worries in his old age.\n\nSo, how went the hunt?
Don't lounge about too long, walker. Your prey awaits.
Fighting wars and Dragons is all fine and good, but Elsweyr faces other threats, too. You will lend a claw, yes? Old Ri'hirr will make it worth your while.
This one has the finest weapons in Rimmen. Swift movements, precise strokes! All can be yours, provided you have the gold to pay.
I sense a hero's heart beating within your chest. And I have just the thing to commemorate such bravery. Come, have a look.
So many now speak of you, the wind itself seems to carry your name. Come, have a look at the wares I offer.
Zahari always thought of Dragons as nothing more than monsters in a moon-singer's story. Now they have suddenly come to life, leaving death and destruction in their wake. We must prepare.
Nisaazda will show us how to tame the Dragon's blood. Have faith.
This blood-brew is potent. Trolls taste vile, but you will never feel more alive.
Have a taste of this!
Save one for Nisaazda's studies!
Dro'zakar will taste your blood before the Dragon's. He is always hungry.
The Devourer will claim the Dragon's power and drive them from our lands.
I'll not be defeated by this!
Yes, die now. You were starting to bore me.
No more distractions. Our moment draws near.
Yes! Greater battles will quench my thirst. They must!
Claim it all for Maarselok.
Maarselok reshapes the world.
We'll all be one soon.
The seeds of paradise are here.
Stay out of this! Carindon must pay!
That seed will weaken the mass!
This petulant defiance is growing dull.
It's too late to devise an escape from my trap.
Shagrath drink your souls dry!
Its heart's the key!
I've had just about enough of this.
Alas, the fun is over.
Leave and I may spare you.
You're boring me, mortals.
You think yourselves Dragon slayers. You'll soon learn that not all Dragons are created equal.
This was deserved.
A brief distraction. What more could I expect?
The faithful will celebrate your failure for thousands of years to come.
It's not everyday I meet a Dragon slayer! I can't help but be a tad jealous of your great victory. I just hope my wares suit your needs.
The flames can feast on you.
Your life ends now!
I'll tear you apart, limb by limb!
By her will, we stand united!
Purple. The color of regality, and savage gashes in the night sky.
He's winning!
You will burn in her radiance!
The cold will leech your insolence until you are frozen in eternal supplication.
Her light will strip you of all your failings.
Lightning is the whip she will use to break you!
Bask in the full spectrum of pain.
<Cursing Goblin gibberish.>
<Cursing Goblin gibberish.>
Stupid.
Trespassing? Big mistake!
You have returned to Zahari unharmed. Good. But is your assignment complete?
Ah …!
Mizzik needs to stop doing that.
That's it. Now you die.
Mizzik is the model patron, as always. Keeps his room clean, pays for everything in advance. And it doesn't hurt that he's awfully handsome, yes?
That was not the off switch.
This one has several hangover cures certain to get the taste of the Gulp's swill out of your mouth, no matter which direction it's flowing!
I don't sell the drinks. Don't ask.
I am hers, body and soul.
We obey, Lady of Light.
We are filled with her light. We need nothing else.
The sun sets, but her light is forever.
Be blinded by her glory!
Defiance means death!
Purification comes!
Conform to her will!
<Angry Goblin gibberish.>
You'll never survive that heat! Get back to the platform!
It's impervious to your attacks! Look for a weak point to focus on!
It can't take much more! Keep the pressure on!

The only ones left in Southern Elsweyr are opportunists; those who decided to profit off the chaos and suffering of the Knahaten Flu.\n\nI'd rather live in the streets of Rimmen than bow to the crooks that now rule Senchal.
The Khajiit might be mild mannered when it comes to most social interactions, but have you ever tried to barter with one? That's when their claws truly come out.
Bindabi is too weak to work, and too poor to buy food. Please, walker … spare a coin or two?

I didn't always live here, you know? Before the anchors started falling in Cyrodiil, I was a man of means. Respected! Envied! Now? Now, I'm just a mark for these bloody Rimmenites.\n\nTake my advice and get out of here while you can.
Chirba has lovers all over Rimmen. Some strong and confident—some weak and compliant. You strike this one as the former, yes?
Soon as I kill my first Dragon, I'm going to have a blacksmith make me a fine set of Dragonscale armor. And maybe a Dragonbone sword while I'm at it.
The Dragons are endlessly fascinating, wouldn't you agree? How do they fly, given their prodigious size? How do they breathe fire? So many questions!

There are those who speak words of smoke, wilting your whiskers. They wish for nothing more than to choke you with their despair.\n\nDo not let them. Look to the skies above and breathe in that gentle air. Know that their desperation is not your own.

Certain furstocks don't tend to venture out of Elsweyr much. Alfiqs are constantly talked down to, given their small size. Senche-rahts are mistaken for beasts, and may be attacked.\n\nIt is a sadness that the rest of Tamriel is so ignorant.

These Dragons were better off locked away. If the Akaviri could best them, then what chance do they have against the might of the Aldmeri Dominion?\n\nEmeric and the Skald-King quake at our approach. These beasts will learn to do the same.
Ra'ri cannot tell you how many times an outsider has cooed and crooned and even attempted to cuddle him. This one, a fully grown Alfiq!\n\nTheir ignorance continues to astound.

Did you finish the job? Some here seem to have wagers on whether you have or not.\n\nI'm not saying I'm among them, of course. I'm also not saying anything about having to dance if you're still on the hunt.
Thank you for helping. After you come back to me for your reward, I'm sure many would love to hear of your exploits.
We have more reports of Dragons in the area. If you have the skills and time, we could use some more Dragon hunters.

Despite popular belief, many have theorized that Dragons still survived in Tamriel.\n\nNow we have conclusive proof that they simply hid themselves away. Or, in the case of the Halls of Colossus, that they had been forcibly trapped.

Samari drinks too much. No, no, no … shhh. Do not argue. It is true.\n\nPeople say a person Samari's size should not drink an entire keg of … whatever this is. They are probably right, you know? But what can this one do? Get a job? Pfft. No thanks!

I'll never win the love of Chirba with sweet words alone. I need to prove myself.\n\nPerhaps if I stole a great treasure for her? That's how Rajhin always wooed his lovers, yes? Hmm. What would impress someone as beautiful as Chirba ….
There is nothing quite as satisfying as your paw connecting squarely with your enemy's jaw. And when you hear the bone crack? Ah, such a lovely sound.

If there are Dragons about, you can be sure that Dragon Priests will follow. \n\nThe Dragons fill these special masks with their power, and then give them to loyal followers. It makes the Dragon Priests damn near impossible to defeat.
What's not to like about Elsweyr? Beautiful people, breathtaking landscapes. Only the occasional Dragon flying over head.\n\nJust about perfect, if you ask Ranji.

Rimmen has a colorful air about it, wouldn't you say? Though I suppose that has more to do with the Khajiit who live here than with anything else.\n\nIt makes Grahtwood seem downright dull in comparison, I'll tell you that.

Azurah made the Khajiit fast and clever, the best climbers and the best deceivers.\n\nSo we do not merely run into battle with spells and swords, no? We plan our attacks and allow wisdom to guide us. And, if we are lucky, our allies listen.
When the Moons speak, it is the Clan Mothers who have been taught to listen. This is why their words are so valued by the clan.
I'm never alone for long in this city. Whenever I visit a tavern or take a stroll, it seems that there's always a friendly Khajiit who wishes to converse with me.

I'm sure you'd love to join our ranks. After all, who wouldn't want to be part of the most powerful group in Rimmen?\n\nYeah, well, sorry: the Jovial Lambasters are a closed organization. You don't contact us, we'll contact you.

There's one advantage I have over the Khajiit, and that's their own underestimation of Argonians. They think me as slow and dull-witted as the lizards that skulk their sands.\n\nLet them think it. It's always good to catch your victim unaware.
Dragons haven't been seen in Tamriel for hundreds, if not thousands of years! Why, oh why did they decide to return in my lifetime?

Originally our town was called Rawla-Kei, meaning "River-Land" in Ta'agra.\n\nBut after centuries of trading with and being outright invaded by Cyrodiil, the name Riverhold was adopted. And so it has been for quite some time.
The Moons tend to shine a little brighter on Merryvale, yes?\n\nEveryone looks after each other in this town. And when you are as small as Lanasi, friendly neighbors make all the difference.
Riverhold isn't just known for our farms, you know. We also export a good deal of fish, due to the local river. Thus the name, yes?\n\nThough we can't hold a candle to Southern Elsweyr, of course.
An Imperial once tried to stroke this one while she slept in the sun. Thought Nirahni was someone's pet!\n\nLet us just say that he left Riverhold with less flesh than when he entered.
I wasn't sure about Khamira at first. She's so young! But she knows what she's doing.\n\nMust be all the years of tutelage under Lord Gharesh-ri.

Moon-sugar is valuable, yes. But the skooma one can make from it? There are many who have become very wealthy selling such a drug.\n\nUnfortunately, this means that Merryvale is often targeted by bandits and thieves.
People keep asking if I'd like some mead. You know what? I would. And don't add none of that moon-sugar syrup to it neither!

What a shame that man and mer often hesitate to try moon-sugar. Just one taste is all that's needed to see what a delightful treat it can be.\n\nThe lizards, well, this one thinks that they don't have the palate for such things.

Luckily, Hakoshae has managed to stay neutral to most of the region's conflicts. \n\nYou won't find anyone willing to join a war in this town. It's bad enough that we have to deal with these Dragon attacks.

I'm so glad that Hakoshae still accepts my sister as their magnate.\n\nShe truly does her best to help our town, you know. No matter what needs to be done, she's the first to help. And that's how a leader should be.

Merryvale has already done so much to heal my soul. Perhaps it is the sweet air or the friendly eyes of the farmers who live here. Perhaps it's just the serenity of small town living.\n\nYes, I do believe I'll stay here awhile longer.

I do want to leave Hakoshae, but … I can't help but worry. My Akaviri blood, thin as it might be, has been a part of me for as long as I can remember.\n\nWhat if I lose that identity, out in the big world?

Did you know that it was Potentate Versidue-Shaie who sanctioned the Guilds Act? If not for him, we wouldn't have the Mages Guild, the Fighters Guild, and so many others.\n\nThe Akaviri gave so much to Tamriel, with so little given in return.
So many pretty soldiers have come to this one's shop today. Ah, Manasi is a truly lucky Khajiit to be surrounded by such sweetmeats.
Majadhi wonders what kind of Khajiit Razum-dar might be interested in?\n\nPerhaps pretty young ladies with glossy, black fur and sparkling, green eyes? Oh, if only that were true.

The Khajiit say that Azura was the one who gave them shape. Turned a bunch of Wood Elves into the cats and called it a gift, you know?\n\nI can't imagine what I would do if someone suddenly covered me in fur.
Another day, another swing at glory, eh? Keep your shoulders tight and your knees loose and you'll do fine.

Did you toss a pinch of moon-sugar over your shoulder when you came in here? Ziss'vo! Now I've got to flip all the furniture and dip my tail in lamp oil. Again!\n\nAnd before you say anything, this is not superstition! It's totally normal behavior!
You must truly have an eye for the best to seek out my mounts, rhook.
Can't believe the prefect disobeyed a direct order ….
Like rats in the sewer, just as the queen anticipated.
Perhaps we should pay Two Moons another visit. Easy pickings!
I best get my equal due in the next raid. Sharpclaw gives us nothing but scraps!
Zamarak's aura can restore your will!
So many travelers have not known the warm company of a Khajiit before traveling to Rimmen. They are so often surprised by our … vigor, one could say.
Wake from your sleep. Preserve our legacy. Destroy the outsider.
Azurah willing, we'll be on the road on schedule today. Interested in tagging along? We can always use an extra caravan guard.
The Dragon King of Cats has come to lead us!
Blessed are we! The First Cat has returned to his people!
Natrada shall pray for you. All of you.
It's hammering time!
I'll be sure to yell something inappropriate at your funeral.
We hurt her. Defiled her. Why did we defile her?
The lizard said she would make a cure. Please, we need a cure!
Maybe I should become a Ziz Kurah adept instead of Vrin-Thak. I don't think all this pounding on things with other things is working out for me.\n\nI don't think I am quite that violent of a person.
An adept of Ziz Kurah must remain mindful of the body's flow. But then probably so must other adepts. I only know my own practice and training.
I never want to see that tomb again. Not even to hide from the sun.
Don't kill everyone. Herd some to the ossuary.
Moons, heal this one's children. They are still so young.
Why is she doing this? Why won't she let us rest?

Minshak doubts that Raz remembers his old friend. After all, did he ever write? Did he ever visit? Not once, not once. Now, this one is sure that Raz has more important things to do than grab a drink with his childhood friend.\n\nThe bastard.

Before we were married, I was terrified to tell my wife about my past with the Redhands. But as soon as the truth came out, she was more than accepting. \n\nHonestly, I think it excited her a bit. Not that she'll ever admit it.

Moon-sugar for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. What a life!\n\nThe Khajiit around here say I'll eventually get used to it, but what's that supposed to mean? I'm plenty used to it already! And plenty happy.

Sezdi's children ask her, "Why did we come here? What is there to find?"\n\nShe tells them, "Look at the ashes, the crumbling stone. Know once that this was a place of healing, of peace. And know how easily it was destroyed."

I am sure that Iokkas and his apprentice have been met with much distrust. After all, many Khajiit still blame the Argonians for the Knahaten Flu.\n\nNot I, of course. As long as Iokkas treats me as a friend, I will return the favor.
Bizahen once studied with the Moon-Singers of Rawl'kha, but telling stories didn't suit him.\n\nThis one is much too literal for such work as that.
All are free to bathe in the cool waters of the lower pools.\n\nIf you wish drinking water, it is best to go upstream where the water is clear. You're also free to gather water for your shop or home.
A Dagi made fun of Tsazura once. Joked about this one's lack of opposable thumbs. So Tsazura bit his hands off.\n\nWhat's funnier than a Senche-raht with no thumbs? A Dagi with no hands. Right?
Shrink from the flames like the vermin you are!
Make a future for yourselves. End these blasphemers.
You look as insignificant from down here as you did up there.
Slaves! Your god grants you a chance to redeem your past failings.
My rage only makes the flames burn hotter!
Just die, you maggots.
Necromancers focus on raising the dead. M'aiq wonders why not raise crops instead?
In Tamriel we grow moon-sugar. On the moon do they grow Tamriel sugar?
This is tiresome. Get out of my roost.
Bring me more! More!
These bones cannot be broken!
Death conquers all, fools!
Zumog Phoom! I hate him! He made me fight my own friends after they fell in battle. And then he raised them again!\n\nPromise me you'll kill the bastard the first chance you get.
There's nowhere to run from my wrath!
Friend, you seek to sell honest goods?
Mulaamnir prepares to attack! Let my magic protect you!

This one keeps your sleekest possessions safe and sound. Your dull-clawed items, too, if you want.
This is absolutely pathetic.
You must be used to defeat by now.
Soon, you will be nothing but a stain beneath my feet.
Be proud that you died at the hands of Darloc Brae.
Follow the clergy's direction in all rituals, lest you displease Alkosh.
In need of gold for offerings? Why not lessen your burdens and uplift your spirit?
They just don't summon gibbering idiots like they used to.
There's nothing here! We're just wasting our time.
Even Dragons bow to Queen Euraxia.
The more Dragons we kill before they spread, the better off everyone is.\n\nCome see me each day to join in on a Dragon hunt. I assure you that a hefty reward is involved, too.
You slump under the weight of all your goods and coin, yes? Barter with J'darji. He will lighten your load.
I have slain scores Tamriel's greatest warriors. This will be no different.
I can read your every move. You've already lost!
I love a good storm.
This one is sure a terror bird approaches. This one has named it Bawksquawker. Now this one flees!
Sir Cadwell of Codswallop, at your service!
Honor? Honor? Have you seen my faithful steed? Answers to the name of Honor. And Tumbleweed. Frankly, if food is involved, he'll answer to just about anything.
Farewell for now, my friend. And in case I don't see you, good afternoon, good evening, and good night!
These are the words of Abnur Tharn, battlemage extraordinaire and advisor to emperors.
I earned many titles and accolades in my long years of service. I suppose I collect them, much the same way a Khajiit gathers fleas.

Those were the words of Abnur Tharn, battlemage and advisor to emperors. If the meaning of them eluded you, feel free to return this tome to the nearest Mages Guild Hall. Someone there will undoubtedly appreciate it.
You have come into the possession of this arcane tome of wisdom, as written by Abnur Tharn. Consider yourself extremely fortunate.
The Elves of Tamriel represent different branches from a common root. I have yet to determine the veracity of the root, however.
So says Abnur Tharn, overlord of Nibenay, Chancellor of the Elder Council, and battlemage extraordinaire.
Rajhin's shadow haunts you, dull claws. Let us dance to your death!
I'm still strong enough to crush you worms!
Quite a hunt today, eh? The Hungry Cat, Hircine, smiles on us both. Come back tomorrow and we will honor him again!
You dare to interrupt a master at work?
Destroy any who disturb me!
I love talking to customers, but you're probably here to speak to the Impresario. She's right over there!
Welcome to the Impresario's home away from home! She's not here right now, but she'll be back soon.
Ziss! As if a back-breaking workload weren't enough, this Dragon shows up?
Ziss'vo! Little is worse than unexpected Dragons.
Baandari wisdom says to flee from Dragons. Who am I to ignore such wisdom?
Dragons? Jone and Jode! Not what I wanted to see on my travels!

Numaia demands the best from all of us. So, as dung-rakers go, I'm second to none!

Maybe your watery blood will cool my tongue!
All sales are final! Mojaluz doesn't care if you threw up the potion you drank or if your skin turns green. No refunds!
This one buys goods from all over Pellitine, such as jagged ores, ground minerals, and even those fancy green rock things! Maybe forge a sparkling hammer?
Stay away from the wood out in the Scorch. Smells like death and doesn't hold up at all. Tenmar Forest, on the other hand, has some quality lumber.
You want a good product that will keep you alive when fending off undead or other vile creatures? Then you're in the right place.
Listen, just see what we have. This one really can't pronounce any of the things we are selling. Sanuzh wants only to pay off a debt.
You ever realize how big this inn is? The other day I found another level I didn't even know existed. But, oh, you probably want to buy something, yes?
I wanted to be a bard. Alas, I don't sing and I don't like to write songs or poems, so now I make armor! Take a look.
You want to make friends in Senchal? Buy some drinks and hand them out! There's no finer gift than a freshly made brew. Especially my brews!
I just hope you have a more refined palate than most of my customers. If I hear one more request for moon-sugar, I'll … I'll …. Well, I'll lose it, that's what!
What brings you to Senchal? Wait, never mind. It's probably better that I do not know. Instead, please do take a peek at my wares.
Zurso uses different types of hides. Traveling to Purring Rock? You want wamasu hides. For the Scorch, guar hides because they're light and breathable.
It would be a pleasure to make sure your equipment is in good shape. \n\nTry my repair kits.

The other evening, a drunken fool of a Khajiit screamed when he saw me and ran away yelling that Dragons were attacking. Believe me, if I could shoot flames out of my mouth, I'd not be selling wares in Senchal.
Many of my wares are castoffs from the Thirteenth Legion; my severance pay for years of service, you could call it. Heh. Most soldiers get a medal.
A good bow and a keen eye can take you far in life. Knowing a good alchemist and poisoning your arrows can help out as well.
This one may have a few things for you now, though you are yet young in your fame and feats.
You have been making a name for yourself, friend. Shuva has some very nice things you may wish to see.
A pleasure to see you, my friend. This one can offer rare and wondrous things to one with a reputation as fine as yours.

You wouldn't believe the things people give us to keep locked up. I could tell you stories to make you feel more comfortable if you are hesitant, except it would cost me my nice position. So, know that we don't judge.
I don't care to know where or how our clients get their gold or precious items. All I care about is making sure they remain locked up until the client needs them.
I've made some friends among the Khajiit. I know they look like cats, but they are smart, funny, and almost as sneaky as I am! I think they like me because of my little horns.

People don't want to ride horses anymore. Camels, bears, even guar. But not the lovely horses.\n\nPersonally, this one thinks guar are hard to train and provide a bumpy ride. And their noses? Not soft. Pity.
This one stands ready to assist you, should you have any questions.\n\nJust forgive Maguzak if he scrambles beneath the counter in terror. Dragons make this one's pants sag!
Rimmen was nice, but I have to say, I like the rough and tumble atmosphere here in Senchal a bit better. Could do with fewer Dragons, though.

Greetings, cerum. Please note that this is a coin-only shop. Pay in full or toddle on.\n\nDon't usually have to remind people of such things, but accumulating debt is practically the national pastime here in Pellitine.
Take a look. Lots of goods. You get the idea.\n\nSorry, just working off a hangover here. That moon-sugar rum kicks like a mule, let me tell you.
Only the finest goods from Elsweyr and lands beyond!\n\nHave a look, sera. You'll find something spectacular. Of that I have no doubt!
Take the crocodile's advice and keep your eyes pointed skyward, friend. Too many Dragons hereabout.\n\nSpeaking of Dragons, you need fresh supplies to face them, I think.

What can Kargik do for you today? Are you an aspiring mage in need of a sturdy staff to fend off smugglers? An experienced adept in need of a protective glyph to fight Dragons? Kargik has magical wares!
Have you seen the smaller talking Khajiit? Alfiq, they're called. I nearly fainted when what I thought was a regular house cat asked me how my day was.
You bring Abizag something good, yes? Come, come, let's have a look.
You are up to no good, I take it? Well, no good is very good for the likes of us.\n\nLet's see what you've got.
One of these days I'll take my business top-side again. Just waiting for things to die down a little. And before you ask, no, I didn't eat anyone's mule!\n\nNow, what can I do for you?
Red diamond, red diamond … dah dah dah dah …. Ugh! Sorry, just can't get that song out of my head!\n\nYou need something, right? How can I help?

People told Murimdak he was crazy to open a bank in a refuge for outlaws. But do you know what's really crazy? Leaving your workplace to relieve yourself. Down here? Ha! The world is Murimdak's chamber pot!
We're about to set sail, friend. You're welcome to come along if the price is right.
What shall I reap from you?
Debaasi had more to sell, but with the recent Dragon attacks, this one's stock is low. Still, how can Debaasi help you?

Feldarr takes to heart a philosophy from the lizard people of Black Marsh. Don't grow attached to anything. It all changes. Also, some Imperial will burn it all down. Groundless, is this one. Especially around Imperials.
I've lived in Senchal all my life, and I'm disgusted to see the state it's in. I'd move north, but the Khajiit there have a long history of tribalism. Better to stay here. Maybe help rebuild.

This one hates Senchal. Well, not really. This one lost much coin gambling.\n\nIf someone invites you to Black Kiergo, take Shavnargo's advice and run. In the opposite direction. Maybe even to those Dragons. Now leave.
Hmmm, this one has not seen your face in Senchal before. Or maybe this one has and you are just not that memorable.
The wreckage 'round me I hold dear, I cannot flee away from here. My Senchal does not stand with pride, but crumbles like a flouted bride.

Purari likes it here in Senchal. The inn serves good food, and many interesting people stop by.\n\nThey say when the royal family was here, it was very elegant. Elegant may be pretty, but Purari prefers a Senchal that is rough around the edges.

I'm pleased the General remained here and formed the Shields of Senchal. A few claim this shows his disloyalty to the empire, but I disagree. He shows honor by defending this ruined city.\n\nAnd I get to spend my days in this wonderful library.
