The Khajiit adore sharply pointed roofs, judging by their architectural choices here. One of my partners said he thinks it reminds them of their claws. Another said she believes it allows heat to rise. But don't Khajiit like heat?
Sometimes I just sweep the dust under a bench or table. No one notices because this place is so big and dusty all the time anyway. Soldiers and their dirty boots. The bane of my existence.

You know, if we all flee Senchal, in a few years it'll have more limbs and leaves than the Elden tree. Jungles and forests always reclaim the land.\n\nThat'd be fun to see. All the kitty-cat statues covered in vines. Greenmanes, I'll call them!

After the Dragon sunk my last job, I'm earning gold here in Senchal doing odd jobs, but my bow craves use.\n\nAs it stands, I've used sharp words to fend off folk who want to be more than friends. Ugh. I'm not a romantic person at all.

I'm sure you have some pressing information or exciting news to impart that impacts all those within this ruined city. I am equally sure that dozens of others around here would be delighted to talk to you. \n\nI, however, am not interested.

Though the Knahaten flu happened twenty years ago, I find it odd that they haven't done more to restore the city. But, not having lived here, I don't know what challenges they've faced.\n\nPerhaps the Shields of Senchal will help? Time will tell.

A Khajiit told me that he thinks Argonians are related to the Dragons that darken the skies here. Because we both have scales, he said. He was drunk. \n\nThe Hist offers nothing about Dragons, but we would know if a link exists.

I'm curious about this Dragonguard. They say Sai Sahan himself leads them. Even as far away as Orsinium, we've heard of that great warrior.\n\nI'd like to get eyes on him. Not like that! I can respect a renowned fighter for his prowess, can't I?
Senchal isn't too bad. At least, not since the flu ended. And the fires.\n\nI just wish someone would do something about those damn Dragons, though.
He has nothing!\n\nDo not startle Ghalsu like that! He gets no sleep among bandits and thieves in Senchal. All he wants is some peace ….
Our people are masters of colorworking. Speak of a hue, real or imagined, and we will work you a paint, ink, or dye befitting your vision.
You should visit the temple to Khenarthi while you're here. It's just south of town.\n\nBe mindful of the little priests and priestesses within. It is bad luck to step on clergy.
This one hears that Dragons cough flames hot enough to melt steel! Good thing we dwell so close to the laughing waters of the Topal Bay, yes?\n\nAzrid should probably learn how to swim ….

Have you heard about this New Moon cult? As if we don't have it bad enough …. Now we have to worry about skooma-addled vagrants screaming about the apocalypse the whole night through.\n\nOnly place to find any peace and quiet is out here on the road.
Kill him! Before he takes me again!
Nothing useful yet? Hmm.
You almost had it! Maybe?
Try again! Za'ji knows you can do it!
I'd rather die! I'd rather—ah!
Did I mention I'm a sore loser?
His rot's inside you! Here!
Did you think you saved her? Hah.
Did that hurt? It looked like it hurt.
What a splendid display of excretion.
This was inevitable. What's a spider-god compared to me? Really?
I am reborn in azure!
You'll sweat or you'll bleed!
I take this power as my own! I am the Devourer!
You've ensnared her, you fools!
What will sprout from you, I wonder?
I'll be taking this.
Keep your blood in your veins. I prefer to drink from your throats!
Do you hear the Doom Drum growing louder in your ears?
Did you not wish to spill my blood?
Defend me, Devourer!
Take a bite of my prey, blood-kin!
You hear something? Bah. Probably the rats.
Those Nord skeevers have no idea what's coming!
We'll have your hearts in a basket!
Draw your weapons. Make them bleed!
I kill it for you, mother.
I can smell your terror. Mmm … delicious!
You're rotten! You're all rotten!
Longing for the Bear-Woman's help? Alas, alas ….
Having second thoughts? I certainly would.
Stay down.
Dead? Good. Now, where's my cauldron ….
More corpses …. We always need more.
They were so vigorous! What a waste.
Like plucking weeds from a garden ….
Those Pyre Watch guards went down easy enough, eh?
Shor's bones, these statues creep me out.
Treasure's ours, you hear? Ours!
Bury these fools!
The longer you make me wait, the sharper my swords get.
No one leaves. No one ever, ever leaves!
Whatever preparations you're making, it will not be enough. You are overmatched.
What lies beyond the door? Ha! Guess you'll never know.
Dead. Dead like me! Do you like it? Do you like it?
Don't worry, heroes. I'll find a use for your corpses soon enough.
I won't be kept prisoner any longer!
Dance to my flames, interloper!
Pests! Worms of this wyrm! I'll mash you under my boots!
Stay closer and I could.
Whet your appetite, Devourer!
This'll be done before I work up a thirst.
Your precious Green will make a better azure.
I am … the Dark Aeon!
A feast for the chosen!
Ugh, what happened? My mouth tastes like a compost heap ….
Give that Dragon a sock in the jaw on my behalf, yeah?
So, how went the hunt? Wish I could've joined you, but between my back and my knees, I can barely make it to the tavern some days.\n\nOh, and no knee jokes, yeah?
Don't hang about too long. Your target's certainly not going to.
Fighting Dragons is all fine and good, but they're not the only nasty problems out there. Want to hear more?
You did good, yeah? Come back tomorrow and we can talk about other things that need killing.
Ha! I knew you'd come back! You were successful, yes?
Divines protect you on your quest, my friend! Guybert will try not to fret while you're away!
Valiant deeds at exorbitant prices. I offer my clients nothing less! You get what you pay for in the hero business, am I right?\n\nSo, care to assist me?
You want more work, don't you? Alas, I have none to offer. But do come back tomorrow. Guybert's folio of perilous yet profitable tasks never stays empty for long!
You survive the storm only to die here? How tragic.
I'll feed your frozen corpses to the sea!
Mother want you dead. Have to please mother!
Gohlla! Chill them to the bone!
Set them ablaze, Hiti!
Bani, their flesh is yours.
Maefyn! Unleash your thunderbolts!
Gohlla, Hiti, Bani, Maefyn, your power flows through me!
I'll purge you from this valley!
Alive or dead, you will become one with Maarselok!
I need to concentrate. Don't let these creatures get near me!
The spiders aren't going to make it to Maarselok if you don't protect them! Go for the stranglers!
Cats aren't the only ones who toy with their prey.
You've already lost your friend, next your life!
Chizbari hears rumors that several Dragons fell to the Dragonguard. A true tale, yes?
Chizbari has many virtues, but patience is not among them. Kill your Dragons, then we talk.
If you come to hunt Dragons, let us speak. If not, be off. Chizbari has no stomach for small talk.
You wish to kill more Dragons? Chizbari approves.\n\nTomorrow, walker. For now, sharpen your weapons and dream of battles to come.

Bebbia is thinking of hosting some sort of grand unveiling once the tapestry is completed. \n\nSenchal's finer society is sadly in shambles, but she thinks this work should be appreciated by all the city's people. Not just the wealthy.
Hmm? Sorry, was actually reading something interesting for once.
And bring me some rum while you're out. I get bleary after a while and a tipple helps clear the fog.
Hey, hey, I need you to do something for me. For the guild, I mean.
Shove off now, I got reading to catch up on. Was just getting to the good bits.
Never speak ill of the Coven. They're always listening.
We'll take Solitude first. The rest of Skyrim will fall soon enough.
Don't you worry. The Coven has a plan for all of us.
That giant's going to break loose eventually. Just you wait.
Survivors? Cut them down!
You'll never leave this island!
Flay them alive! Feed what's left to the sea!
More sheep to the slaughter!
Not quite there. Ugh. I know we can do this.
Don't let them get away!
Halt!
This one knew you could do it.
Did you see the Devourer's fight with the Dragon? To think our blood could give us such power!
A thimble is the sign of an amateur, but my fingers are going to be quite raw by the end of this project whether I prick them or not.
I'm so delighted to run my own business! And I didn't even need to spend years apprenticing to someone because I taught myself everything. The customers love what I make!

The terrible flu took many lives. After, some left Senchal, to our sorrow. The Shields of Senchal claim they can bring the city back, but to me, Senchal belongs to the past. And now Dragons come. This one wonders if we drift through nightmare lands.
You don't look like a fancy mudcrab.
Welcome, friend! Please join us.
Come join us! The more who hear the stories, the greater becomes the joy.\n\nThis one was just about to tell another tale of Khunzar-ri ….
Tulip! Shake! Shake. Come now. Shake! You're already bobbing up and down so you're halfway there.
No beast can resist my masterful tutelage for long. I stake the reputation of all of Sil-Var-Woad's handlers on it—I will not rest until this stubborn creature does something cute on command!

If you have coin, this one can serve you. If you have no coin, try one of the stalls the city do-gooders have set up. And before you accuse Pirlasa of being cold-hearted, we donate leftovers to them. So there!

You've certainly turned this Dragonguard into something spectacular. From a ragtag crew of smugglers to a Dragon hunting order of great notoriety.\n\nThat's why Mogdal and myself joined up. We wanted to be part of something great.
What the Dragonguard need are warm, hearty meals! And that's what I aim to provide.
You got some nerve coming here, Za'ji!
I don't know why my family forced me to join this dreadful Dragonguard. It's not like there's any Dragons up in Morrowind.

I don't know what I would do if I didn't have the Dragonguard. The thought of killing the beast that slaughtered my family …. it keeps me going. \n\nA life fueled by vengeance may not be a happy one, but at least it's a life.

There's no end of Dragon material to research. Right now, I'm researching the alchemical properties of Dragons blood. I haven't discovered anything conclusive yet, but I'm very excited about the possibilities.
Khajiit just wants their skooma!
It's gone! Dragons burned everything. Khajiit has nothing to give!
Blah blah blah. Heard it all before.

The first time we killed a Dragon together, Bahalzim proposed to me right on the spot.\n\nI turned him down, of course. No time for romance when there's battles to be fought. Besides, no man has ever satisfied me like a well-earned kill.
There is no more need to fear the Dragons. Our path will see you saved.
This one will take any help he can get.
Khajiit won't live like this anymore!

Pirjmina did well on the anvil, and Father was always impressed. It was a simple life.\n\nBut this one does not want simple. She wants daring adventures, heroic feats! And that's exactly what the Dragonguard offers, no?
I will incinerate you all!
You should have stayed in that pit!
Why fight, brother? You cannot hope to win!

Do you hear it, walker? Khenarthi plucks her majestic lyre and inspiration follows!\n\nThis one shall compose a play! he shall call it … Dragons Burn a Wagon. A piquant satire of predatory commerce in the wake of calamity! How droll!
Greasy interlopers! Filth! Slime! Kill them all!
This one will tell their cousins and their cousins' cousins of your generosity!
If you ever see this one reach for another wedge of cheese, chop his hand off. The pain and anguish would be far less severe than what roils in Korabi's belly.
Ziss'vo! Little is worse than unexpected Dragons.
Ah, no, this one prefers not to tangle with surprise Dragons!
If this one wanted to talk to strangers, this one probably wouldn't drink. Go away.
Debaasi warned this one to beware of Dragons. They are everywhere! And they are bad for business, yes? Speaking of … shall we trade?
Come here, you muskarses! We've got intruders!
Fools! Unbelievers! We shall show them the New Moon's strength soon enough.
To doubt is a sin! The New Moon's power is absolute!
This one has sailed with the Tigershark for years. He knows what he's doing.
She knows sugar-tooths are mad, but she has never seen anything like this.
Wield my strength, New Moon. Make me a vessel for your wrath!
A new era approaches, born in flame and death!

The Shields of Senchal do more than defend the city from Dragons. I facilitate imports, for example.\n\nDon't scoff! It's no easy task. Just the other day I had to …. I won't burden you with the particulars, but it involved smugglers and a goat.
Yes! Yes! This one hears your commands, Ra'khajin!
We must prepare our flesh for the fires to come! Join me, brothers and sisters!
Elsweyr's rebirth is upon us! Repent and serve!
This one will serve. This one must serve!

My wife and I made a little place here, but we grow old and tired. This one does not know if his beloved Tebabi will recover.\n\nAt this point, she may be better off in Khenarthi's embrace than here with me.
Ask my aid, and I will destroy your enemies!
Now this is more like it!
The mask is ready. Call down Nahfahlaar's fire!
You can't beat him in the air. Force him down or wait until he lands!
Use the grapple-bow when his shouts grow too large to outrun!
Good job! Only one shrine left to light.
What are these things?
Just a little longer! I'm nearly finished with the aegis!
You again? Get out of here before I call the guards.
Do not think you can elude me!
Show yourself, nikiriin! Face your death!
My store has plenty of options for a hero such as yourself!
No one in our Dragonguard looms quite as large as you. It only makes sense that I offer you a comparably large furniture selection to choose from.
You think you know fear? Let me educate you!
Lowly scavengers! I will consume you!
I'm not touching that.
Khunzar-ri, Khunzar-ri! Sing it loud, sing it clear! Khunzar-ri, this is he!
You think you know pain? Ha!
Examine the headstones and see what you can make out.
There was a red mist … a haze, really. Then the storm struck. It was horrifying!
This should liven things up a bit.
Dance for me, eh?
You want a real fight, eh? Here it comes!
You hungry, boy? Eh? 'Course you are. Go get them!
Time to dismember the monsters!
Finally. I've been itching for a scrap!
Killed in a grave. Convenient.
I hear the Riften Ratway has a lot of skeever races. Seems dull to me. Now, horker races, those'll get the heart pounding!
Come on then.
Restless dead, come forth!
So you've chosen death. Very well.
You survived the field work. Excellent! Tell me, were your findings at all conclusive?
If you haven't already seen to it, check in with the scholar running this study. They're most eager to see it get underway.
The Coterie of Organized Scholars is conducting a new study and we're prepared to pay for your assistance! Is rigorous fieldwork to your liking? Any problem with heights? How about widths?

These changing formats are confounding! Should I use the Stormhaven style of citation? Something more Cyrodilic, perhaps? I must insist upon using the Colovian comma, of course.\n\nSorry, friend. I'm a bit busy right now. Check back later, won't you?
This is so thrilling! I can't wait to see the next offer.
Argh!
Get your guard up!
Hit him again!
Break free, my friend!
Die already!
Interrupt the attack!
Press your advantage!
Gut those intruders!
The Glenmoril Coven? Nothing but tree-worshipers. The Icereach are true witches!
Knives out, Reachmen!
Eyes sharp. Some of those Nords could still be skulking around.
Rip them apart!
I don't care if you're cold. Quit your bellyaching.
For the Reach!
Summoning a storm like this? That's true power.
You're done for!
The Reach belongs to us. Never forget it.
To battle, Reachmen!
Mother Ciannait would never join forces with an outsider. You must be mistaken.
Are you ready to die?
Another day, another robbery.
Bring them down!
How many of these things do we have to fill?
Snuff them out, lads!
Bah! To Oblivion with these ashes! Let's grab a few of those statues instead!
Prepare to die!
Keep an eye out for intruders, eh?
You're in for it now!
We'd better be well-paid for this.
No survivors!
Yeah, I saw a vampire once. Burned him alive, I did!
You show up unannounced, and then make me wait. Insufferable.
You cannot alter fate!
The Swords of Solitude need another victory. Have you brought me one?
Neither of us will collect a single drake if you don't complete your task. Get on with it.
Our militia is recruiting for a dangerous mission, but I'm up to my ears in milk-drinkers. You've got some guts, haven't you?
Try not to celebrate too enthusiastically. We'll likely need you in fighting shape again soon.
Blood really does run colder in the north.
We have all the time in the world.
I'll tear you apart and leave your pieces for the Giants.
You're already dead. The only question is whether you'll come back.
Come on. Draw your weapons!
Hesitating will not save you.
I hunger. Why postpone the feast?
Barely a challenge ….
So weak.
What a pointless diversion.
You think you know fear? Let me educate you!
You think you have friends? We all die alone!
Gaze into the abyss!
One, two, three, four, spread it 'round a little more!
No more hiding, spirits! Come out and play!
Would it kill them to label what could kill us?
I don't know. Arkasis doesn't seem that crazy.
Found some fungus feed!
Spare a few for the laboratory!
I smell the blood of my packmates on you. I'll wash it out with your own.
Do you expect me to watch you stand there agape like Rieklings watching ice thaw? Commence!
Small-minded fools! Why do you always come when I am on the verge of a breakthrough?
Let that be a lesson to all of you! I am not to be disturbed!
The Lady wishes to explore more avenues of power.
The fiends smell a bit ripe after a while.
Hearty stock for Vaduroth!
You were not invited!
Place is now. Ready? A simple drip.
Where are you hiding, Gwendis? Come out and fight!
I hope you fight well, blood is so much tastier when terrified.
You do nothing. No soul. No teeth. Void. Just void!
You came all this way for nothing but failure!
You wrecked my beautiful castle on your way to me. You deserve more than such a simple death.
You will die!

I haven't heard from my cousin in a few months. Last time we spoke, he said something about looking for Blackreach. He's a hardy warrior, of course, but sometimes I wonder why he goes looking for trouble.

You might not know by looking at me, but I once sparred with the entire Dragon Bridge garrison and won. Afterward, I drank them all under the table. \n\nNever assume you know the path others have journeyed.

I recommend everyone travel Tamriel for a few years. Otherwise, you become close-minded and isolated. I learned more in a month as a sailor than I have in a year in Solitude, and trust me, I've tried my best here.
You know, I've never been that far outside Solitude. Sounds like the rest of the world is falling apart. Why would I want to go out in that?
One's voice is a sacred instrument. \n\nIt's one of the hardest to train, and also one of the most beautiful to hear when used by a skilled vocalist.

Insulting the woman who might have lent him coin, right after asking for it … my master is an arse of the lowest order.\n\nI had to come here after he blamed me for that whole incident. He deserves to have more than mead thrown in his face!
My sister traveled to Windhelm once. She hated every moment of her time there. That trip … changed her.
You can thank High King Erling for the sturdy outer walls of Solitude. Each stone is blessed, so it's not just the wall that protects us. The Divines do as well.
You'll find the presence of the Divines everywhere in Solitude. Every touch of wind. Every ring of metal on metal. Replenish yourself in their grace here, my friend!
There's a chest tucked away in the Lonely Troll rumored to contain the bones of the first settler of Solitude. My first question: Why would someone store bones this way? So, probably not true.
I'd avoid Morthal. They're solitary, rude, and think they know best. Try to tell them how to do something better, and they'll push back so hard your neck will ache from the whiplash.

Though we worship the Divines here in Solitude, pay heed to the old ways. Some still adhere to them and will find you wanting if you don't respect them—even unknowingly.\n\nGo listen to a bard sing "The Song of Gods." That'll help you.

Did you just see that Argonian? The one with all the cats following him? People insist he's just my imagination, but he's not! Given that some folk here believe snakes are manifestations of Orkey, how can they question something like this?
Skeevers everywhere these days. Chittering in fear. Need more cats to kill them. So much chittering. Why do skeevers chitter anyway?

I could use a warm bath, a wonderful foot massage, and the death of a certain small-minded, big-mouthed fetcher who undoubtedly enjoys both warm baths and foot massages each day.\n\nWill I get these things? Maybe when all is said and done.

People at the college still talk about how we should handle our exquisite legendary instruments.\n\nThaezara makes a compelling case for availability, but I agree with Viatrix. We need to protect the instruments from careless drunks like Hrofgen!

Our precious instruments! It's hard to say if the late Maestro Nel Farsong did more harm than good by hiding them from us.\n\nWithout a doubt, their loss further divided the College. But … their recovery could draw us closer together than before.

The mystery author Yvonna Graymoth knows a lot about vampires. I do, too, but that's because my family dealt with them a few generations ago.\n\nMy weapons—the ones you can see anyway—are not only for show. Vampires can be nasty.

I came here from Morthal. Interestingly enough, both the Nords here and the ones in Morthal feel about the same way toward each other.\n\nIt wouldn't take much to have them at each other's throats. I wonder if they realize that.

I watched a Nord writing the other day. She dipped her quill in some metallic liquid before using ink. I asked why, and she said it was to make sure the words she wrote never came true.\n\nNords are odd. But their mead is excellent.
Solitude should have some more Argonian-friendly places. Staying moist is difficult most days.\n\nI erect the spine of yearning for my home.

The only reason I'm here in Solitude is penance. I was a bit … quick to use fire against someone who turned out to be a fellow student. Now? I must find all the recipes for healing burns in Tamriel and bring them home, no matter how long it takes.

Yesterday I saw a woman pluck four feathers from her chicken. I asked why, and though she was reluctant to tell me, she said it would ensure that strangers would not kill it.\n\nIs this some new form of magic? I see no cause and effect.

One lovely Nord here has the Silver Moth of Dibella tattooed on his back. The wings spread out, rippling as his shoulders move …\n\nI hope to show him some of my less visible marks soon. Such art should be shared freely.

Having traveled through many Nord holds, including those within Jorunn's grasp, I can say with some authority that Solitude contains the most knowledge-free bunch of folk I've ever met.\n\nThough those in Morthal, with their rustic charms, come close.

After spending time here in Solitude learning more about Nord stone art, I hope to find Blackreach someday. The Dwemer called it Fal'Zhardum Din.\n\nSaying that name took less practice than many other Dwemer place names. Give it a try.

This one woke from a dream of darkness and ice. Perhaps night horror is a better way to describe it.\n\nRathzin's blood still runs cold thinking of it. But then, this one's blood runs cold every day in Solitude.
Living outside the city as I do, I see folk from other holds and other lands pass through on their way to Solitude. They're a curious bunch. Some of them travel only by night.

Since coming here, I keep dreaming about someone staring into my window, watching me sleep.\n\nOof. Now I'm shivering again. But if I ever do see someone doing that? I'll blind that miscreant before he can even blink.
I don't know what it's like over in Jorunn's lands, but here? You'll find no alliance-seeking milk-drinkers among us.
The tales the sailors tell of the trip to Solitude over water are truly harrowing. To my mind, those crewing these ships are better tale-tellers than some of the bardic students I've met here.
Some ruffians from the Thieves Guild stole from one of the Mages Guild coffers. The rogues grow bolder each day! Damnable skeevers.

During last year's Burning of King Olaf festival, I overheard two Bards College students arguing about someone named Svaknir. The two nearly came to blows before I interceded.\n\nI don't think they appreciated being dumped off the docks.
Feel free to give me any of your unwanted mead, friend!

This one knows that many people are lost throughout Skyrim, yet Ilazun must focus on his own search for his sister.\n\nWhispers of a place called Blackreach have reached Ilazun's ears, so he goes there next—if he can find it.
My eye twitches in irritation.\n\nNo, no. Don't even try to ask me why. I've had enough talking to anyone after last night. Respect my wish for quiet.
We may be a divided nation, but in our hearts we are all Nords. I have faith that one day Skyrim will be whole once more.
Let's see how you react with fire.
I look forward to your dissection.
I'll feed you to the pit!
Beneath your feet, there is only death!
Saturate the husks!
There's trouble on the horizon, young blood. Brace yourself for a hard day of fighting.
Now that the harrowstorms are clear, maybe we'll get to enjoy a nice, brisk blizzard.
I envy your vigor. The last time I swung my axe in battle, there was a Longhouse Emperor on the Ruby Throne.
All's quiet in Solitude. What about the rest of the holds?
You should never shake this. Oops.
This formula may shock you. Hehehe.
Blood and ichor, heed my power!
Be careful!
Where could she have wandered off to?
We'll have some sweetrolls when we get home.
Skeever kabobs for sale! They'll fill you up!
Declaring victory before we've even begun? Oh, you will regret underestimating me!
You're going to make me work for my kill? Good!
Tear! Limb from limb!
<Mad howling and snarling.>
Blaze like a forge!
Still in the red spectrum? I want a brilliant white heat!
Expel flame formula!
Now let's try temperature tolerance at the other extreme.
Maintains a healthy frost rime. I should try for more ice accumulation.
Commence defrosting!
Yes! Rage against the storm! Let your vigor seep away and join our great harvest!
Were you expecting something more for your efforts than splinters and pain? You cannot quell the storm!
You are weevils among cord wood. Irritating. Nothing more.
You'll soon wish the storm had swept away your soul.
You shall not claim the gray reliquary. Oblivion will take you first!
The Frozen Coast is ours!
I've heard some unsettling rumors, as if there are any other kind out here.
A little gloom is nothing to fear, but I'll pray for a bit of sunshine all the same.
I'd welcome some trouble right about now. I'm bored to tears.
Hahaha. Who needs bloodknights when I have so many other experiments on hand?
The revivification is complete! Come, you must be hungry!
No secondhand goods here! The latest furniture to make your home fresh!
Today is a glorious day to do the thing we love best in the world—buy furniture! Let me show you my wares.
Though I'm stuck vending goods, you aren't. Go hit your opponents hard for me when you're done buying my wares.
I have it on good authority that my gear has kept many a person from an early trip to Sovngarde. Take a look!
We spend so much of our lives surrounded by walls when the whole world is laid out before us …
I'm grateful to the divines for your arrival.
Should I leave Solitude? That is a question I should answer soon, perhaps.\n\nIn the meantime, feel free to browse. I'd love to feel useful.
Something's bothering the Nords here. That, or they just all had a bad batch of mead. It's hard to tell.\n\nAs long as they keep buying from me, I've no complaints!
I hope you're enjoying your time in Solitude! We have so much to offer, including banking services, which I can help you with right now.
I had this exquisite slaughterfish meal the other day. Delightfully prepared. So light. Delicately spiced. Imagine such a perfect dish. Just like our banking—pure perfection!
I once found a ball of red yarn poked through by hundreds of Khajiiti whiskers inside a flimsy bag. Bad work, that bag was. Mine are only the best quality! Take a peek.
I killed a man for mistreating his horse in front of me. And I remember every mount that comes through here. I'll remember you too.
Sometimes you just need to walk around barefoot and feel the earth and stone beneath you. Ah!\n\nEven better? Doing so with a skull-cracking weapon at your side.
My last magic ring project caused one of our bankers to hate the smell of fish. I sell only my successful projects, though. Promise! Take a look.
I saw a line of skeevers leaving a ship in an orderly fashion the other day. When I told one of the locals, she gasped and ran off. Now I'm worried about her.
You never know what I'll put up for sale each day. That's one of the fun things about being a merchant. Though, I love my time with my dogs even more.
Need some goods? I have some for sale. For free, I'll note that sometimes things you think are bad end up saving your life.
Ready to buy? I promise you I'm not sick. It's horses. A bunch of impatient folk left town on them and ran through here first.
I've noticed a change in the flow of mercantile goods of late. But that doesn't impact my wares—distinctive goods for discerning people!
None of the souls in this horrid pit received a proper burial. Neither will we if we aren't careful.
I'm carving a mammoth to send home to my family. The native merchants give me odd looks now and again, but I'm used to it.\n\nSpeaking of merchants, care to see my wares?
Sometimes it's safer to wander the wilds than live in towns. That's why I'm buying and selling goods out here.
Since being assigned here to sell for my guild, I've noticed that the Nords revere the Divines, but also have strange superstitions. Perhaps they've been isolated too long?
The talent at the Bards College is astounding. After you're done looking at my wares, be sure to visit them.
If you're anything like me, you want a nice safe spot to mull over some hard decisions. If your favorite spot is in the Alliance territories, we can get you closer to it.
An entire pack of wolves died from something with claws last week. Strange times.\n\nBest stock up on goods now, yeah?
Strange things travel the roads of Western Skyrim these days, friend. I suggest you find shelter before too long.\n\nIn the meantime, can I interest you in my humble wares?
My potions are fresh, and guaranteed to make you smile. Literally, but only for a moment.\n\nI might be joking, I might not. Why not find out?
Some Bards College students try to sneak into the Blue Palace every now and again. Last week, one of them hinted that they'd buy lockpicks if I had them.\n\nHere's a hint: I don't have lockpicks.
Solitude. A glorious place to work with metals. But contrary to my expectations, none will teach me how to pronounce Dwarven names.
My sales have been up of late. I think people are afraid of something.
The wood near Solitude has a special quality to it. Each day I work with it is a gift. Care to see the results?
The high king's daughter seems spirited to me. She bought something from here the other day. Knows quality, she does.
Welcome to the most unwelcoming city in this part of Skyrim!\n\nI'm only slightly exaggerating. Take your mind off the state of affairs here by browsing my enchantments?
Let's fix the problems here in Solitude before helping other holds. When have they ever helped us?\n\nOh, but you're probably here to support your local merchants and buy!
Been hearing about all kinds of bad omens. Watch your back out there. Something's stirring.
I'm not normally one to put feelings over reason, but it feels like someone's dancing on my grave. Again.
Thank goodness you're here. Would you mind sticking around for a bit? I think something bad's about to happen.\n\nPlus, it never hurts to see what outfits I'm selling.
Fear enveloped her for the first time in her life. "No!" she said to Lord … Lord … Killsalot? Ah, horker's arse, I can't remember the next part.\n\nUm, buy my blades. Lord Killsalot would approve.
Lightning struck a tree outside town recently. Poor Ilfete took a splinter of trunk to the leg. Bad sign, that.\n\nI made a staff out of the rest. Care to see?
The Bards College had a sign telling its students not to drum outside unless given permission. Emphasis on had. It's in my collection now.\n\nNow, let's see what you have.
Skeevers. Once, more skittered around here, but these cats … vicious hunters! You'd think the skeevers would learn, but something's got them riled up these days.
The Lonely Troll. I still remember stealing my first mead there. They called me Little Frog. Ah, memories.\n\nSome of my goods might prompt good memories of your own!
If you want to store goods within our safe —\n\nThat's it. I'm shaving my head. Why do people even grow hair here? The insects seem to seek it out! The biting is incessant! It's not just me, is it?
The bards at the college gained this one's respect. They come here sometimes to buy goods. They listen and entertain, too!
My cat, Master, scares easy these days. Perhaps I should take that trip to Senchal sooner rather than later. Cats know things we don't.
Idiot. The dead are the treasure here.
I'm keeping that one. It's got good teeth.
This might be a better haul than the one in Bangkorai.
Who's afraid of some ghosts?
You seen one barrow, you seen'em all.
Hoo, don't take a whiff out of one of those jars.
Hurag grool! Yandir chums the sea with your blood!
Goorg va nagh! No time for rest, beast. Come!
Foam and frost, to me!
Behold Yandir! Son of storms!
Beast dead? Gakh voonagh! Cowards!
I may have been born in Solitude, but I'm a man of the world. This city could never hold me! No place can.
Rip! Claw! No stopping! No mercy!
I once worked a forge and crafted wondrous metal baubles. You'd not think it of someone who now begs for their coin, but hard times can come to anyone. Remember that.\n\nI didn't, and now here I am.
Graven oaths, heed Yandir's word!
I hear that some warriors learn to dance to help them with their battle training. Perhaps I should seek them out and leave this stall to my sister.
You better leave before my guards find you!
Flame-throwers, stand ready! Loose!
Hmph. There must be a sequence of some kind. Check Maelmoth's riddle again.
More warriors to the beach! No survivors!
If they give you any lip, pull their heads off.

Seek not pies or cakes or lesser pastries! No, only the splendor of the sweetroll is worthy of your reverence.\n\nYou don't want nasty tummy aches, do you? Because too many of those lesser baked goods lead to them! The sweetroll does not!

I make statues of the Pale Lady, you see. My little girl Marielta went missing some years back.\n\nLegend holds that the Pale Lady steals daughters because she lost her own. Maybe if I can make a statue beautiful enough, she'll bring Marielta back.
Traveling around Skyrim on foot is more dangerous than ever. An apprentice was attacked on their way to Falkreath last season!\n\nTo this day, the apprentice can't describe what tried to kill them.

The people around Morthal won't listen to me. They just give me cold stares and curt responses.\n\nDon't they realize their worries of witches, vampires, and other dark forces are clearly the work of the Adversary?

Yes, yes. That must be it. The firewood rack in town is poisoned! Or … or cursed.\n\nListen to me! The Trailstompers left for Solitude recently and took some firewood with them. Sondi overheard someone in town saying they never made it!
The day's end can't come soon enough.
Skyrim will soon be ours!
I think it goes like that … wait, no. Huh. Did that sound like My Love in Falkreath to you?\n\nA little coin in the hat would really help me out!
Ugh, the mud in Morthal is some of the worst. It resists detaching itself from my boots. \n\nLike a filthy, clingy child.
You cannot stop the Gray Host.

You ever been hunting? You look like you've got some skills. A few more seasons and I'll be out of the soldiering business. Thinking of taking up hunting then. Probably safer, I'll bet.\n\nThough I suppose it depends on what you're hunting.

Some people make hunting their business. I'm here for the quiet. The isolation. The thrill of a chase.\n\nI take only the meat I need for the day and give the rest to those who need it more than I do.
Start herding the harrowed. They'll make for good foodstock.
Storm didn't hurt the wildlife none. Not sure how I'd feel about vampire bears.
Never underestimate primitive magic.
Will all our plans go this smoothly, I wonder?
Keep an eye on the witches.
The witches leave us little to do but clean up.

You need to know about a fish? I know about a lot of fish. I won't recite them all just now. But, believe me, I seen 'em all.\n\nBit worried about the ruckus around here of late ruining my fishing spots. You better not be adding to my problem, yeah?
People warned me about signing on for this venture. I should've paid more heed, but how could I turn down the promises offered? \n\nI didn't think about how they wouldn't be any use to me dead.

Keep an eye out in the caverns. The other miners mentioned dark shadows and voices near the ruins. Best of luck on your journey!\n\nSweet Frelytte the Fair, hair the color of hay. Like spun gold and honey! Bright sun at midday.

The miners always talk about how dangerous Blackreach is. They forget the true value of it.\n\nThis place is freedom. Hidden from the watchful eyes of society, we can be whoever we want, and live as we please.

A trader told me Dragons fly freely in Elsweyr. If I recall correctly, Skyrim lore is filled with Dragons, but I haven't seen any here yet.\n\nStill, I'll take my chances if it means I get to experience a wonderful and unique meal.

I don't think any of the miners understand what a rare and wonderful place this is. They bore through the rock and swing their shovels around like brutes. \n\nThey have no regard for the treasures Blackreach has to offer. It drives me mad!
I heard rumors of witches doing some terrible things over in Icereach.\n\nYou in that fight? I prefer the arena, but if some witch heads need cracking, I'd oblige.
More? Kill them!

You don't strike me as a laborer—you're more like one of those adventuring types, right? If more of your ilk explored the area, found treasures, and looked for supplies, I'd certainly be doing quite nicely, I think. Hm!
All kinds of strange creatures down here, don't even know what half of them are.
How did we survive that?
The deeper we mine into this place, the more darkness we're gonna dig up.

The Pit Daemons' color scheme is just fabulous, isn't it? This shade of green is perfect for inspiring terror in our opponents. And scaring off any giants!\n\nMuch better than the pumpkin and eggplant colors of the other teams. Hear that, Dollinith?
We have the honor of being the first to break ground down here, that's not nothing.
Good work, keep going.

My friends tell me what's happening around here. You can see them, right? Everyone says they're not real, but I know different! \n\nSometimes they tell me such nonsense. One of them said I should be on the lookout for vampires. Ha! How silly!
This place reminds me of my own adventuring days. My root-brother, Tuleezna, met his end in a cavern exactly like this one.\n\nThings lurk in the shadows here. Keep your teeth sharp.
Ha! Yandir stands ready, little fish!

I don't venture out of Dusktown much. Only if I need to meet a shipment, really. I've no reason to explore.\n\nEveryone here knows how dangerous things are outside town. It's not just cave creatures, either. Something is stalking us. Watch your back.
Ha! Yes! Retreat! You are no match for Yandir!
It's too dark to even see what you're doing down here.
This place is full of nightmares. We never should have come down here.
Broke my pickaxe on one of those damn crystals yesterday.
If I work any harder, my arms will come clean off.
Nuragh? Very well. You will not survive.
Like a flimsy raft in the chop! Broken!
Some raiders they turned out to be.
Dance until fire and ash rain down upon Solitude!

People here in Mor Khazgur need help. But ships are being crushed into the ice shelf to the east. Maybe I can hire a crew to find those ships and help them out.\n\nOh, I don't know. I've got to dig in, like my mother says, and decide.

Sure, a lot of people make leather armor, but I've got a great source for material and an eye for fine stitching.\n\nHoping I can get my hands on some Dragon materials soon. Though I might need to go hunt a few Dragons myself first. We'll see.

Rations are in short supply here. Some nights we eat nothing but watered broth and a hunk of bread for dinner. After a long day of work, it's a bit disheartening.\n\nStill, this is my duty. I'm not here for luxury.
The worship of Mauloch in Orsinium felt so rigid. Couldn't adhere to their guidelines.\n\nBut now? In Mor Khazgur, I'll help out however I can. Guess a new beginning requires new skills.
Solitude is ignoring us. It's like they just stopped caring all of a sudden. \n\nThe captain doesn't want us spreading that around, but everyone knows it's true.
It's a trying time for the Orcs of Mor Khazgur. The crisis in the mine is putting everyone on edge, and our leadership needs my services.\n\nOff with you now. I must return to my work.
This ruin will be your grave!
I find blood tastes best after a long chase. It's the fear.
Don't let the pentarchs catch you feeding on the prisoners.
Whoever's stealing our food should show themselves and quit skulking in the dark like cowards.\n\nIf those skeevers want my dinner so badly, they can try to take it from my very plate.
Bah, we're werewolves, not watch-hounds.
I heard the harrowstorms don't affect werewolves, but I don't care to find out.
Warning: Context Invalid.

I sure hope the next supply shipment has a couple kegs of mead in it. \n\nThe others would rather get some foodstuffs, but I can live on the broth. What I need is something to take the edge off a long day, you know?
Traveling through the holds around here yields goods to trade, and also some insight. The Nords around here? Very superstitious.
I thought my time in Senchal was troublesome, so I chose to follow a mercantile opportunity in Blackreach. You'll not find a braver merchant for quite a distance, given everything happening here.
Spend too much time in the gloom and spores? I can set you up with a warm, spore-free sleeping experience, and good potions to help soothe any damp aches you might have.
Don't let them catch you pocketing ore. No law but the Bitterblade's down here.
I tried pocketing one of those crystals the other day.
Brought back a gem the size of a baby last night. Or was it day? I don't even know anymore.
Can't take a step down here without running into something that wants to eat you.
I feel like something is watching us.
A unified Reach will be unstoppable!
The sisters' will shall be done!
Be patient. The Ashen Lord has been preparing this plan for thousands of years.
When the west falls, the east will soon follow.
Don't anger the bloodknights. I saw one pull a harrowfiend apart bare-handed.
The rebirth ritual goes far beyond simply raising the dead.
Bah, harrowfiends. Death hounds are smarter and more obedient.
I love not having to hide our true nature any longer.
The undermining is expanding rapidly now. Soon we'll be able to strike all across the western holds.
Have you seen an Exarch? They have power we can only dream of.
Did you see that fiend eat those skeevers?
I don't trust all of these strange faces.
The harrowed feel nothing, do not be gentle with them.
Darkness falls on this place. The Reach will rise!
Do you think the harrowed feel pain?
The harrowstorms fill the sky like blood.
The barrow, it stinks of dead Nords.
Greymoor grows more crowded by the day.
Wait, what's that? Eh, just feeling jumpy.
We need to complete these rituals without anyone the wiser.
The coven make better allies that I thought.
If anyone comes poking around the witch pikes. Kill'em.
My fangs are aching in anticipation.
We won't need to remain hidden much longer.
I heard there are easterners tracking the coven. Be on the lookout.
Don't tell, but I ate one of the Reachmen. They're gamey.
I grew up on stories on monsters in the night. Now I am one.
Glad to be off the boat for a while. Too cramped.
All right. You grab the legs. I'll grab the arms. On three.
Don't kill the cute ones. They make good pets.
Smash these curs through the ice!
I dislike it here. These ruins have no life, no blood.
We should be safe here, right?
This will not halt what we have set in motion.
We must pay the price for such incompetence.
I'm so thirsty. I wish we didn't have to hide.
We must regroup. Take precautions.
The heart of this mountain is close to nature's ear. Let it hear our words!
The land will flourish once the mountain's wrath burns away the Nords.
Caern co bran baugh goen!
I'll kill a few more beasts for offerings!
The skies are full of dark clouds lately. I don't like it.
Reachmen? Here?
Not another step closer witch!
What are they chanting?
A little more prayer and a little less complaining would do you some good.
What's all this scratching in the dirt? Reachmen?
Blow, chill winds! Blow!
Sky's rage, strike!
Thunder! Take shape!
I will shatter those bones!
You won't get away that easy!
This island belongs to us!
They answer the call!
More souls! More!
This reliquary is filled!
The harvest! Wasted! Now your kind has died for nothing!
Are you too chicken to challenge Rolstag? Hm?
You coward! Come fight a true Nord!
No one's as strong as Rolstag … especially not you!
Nobody beats Rolstag … always win.
I never lose! You won't survive the likes of me!
To arms, my champions! Bring them down!
Gods, please, save me! Kill that awful thing!
Please, help! That pale hunched thing is going to feed me to its pet!
By Ysmir's beard, I thought I was dead for sure!
Thank you, friend! May Dibella smile upon you.
Oh, my head … thank you for saving me.
Oh, I missed the fun—but thank you!
Ugh! These harrowed test my patience.
With your hands—no, don't bite it!
Kill the intruder.
Useless! Do it right!
Again, watch and imitate! Like this!
Attack!
I'm still alive! Thank you, kind stranger!
I do hope you intend to share.
You think we're stupid? We want some too!
You couldn't wait?
You could not wait?
I'm here!
You couldn't wait?
My thanks to you, traveler.
Thank the gods you came by!
You have my gratitude, stranger.
I'm not dead? I thought for sure ….
I almost died … it's not safe here.
I'm alive! Thank the gods!
At last, a private meal.
Perfect. A feast just for me.
I think I will drink this one dry.
Time to feed.
Someone left me dinner.
I've been so hungry ….
The creatures in here aren't normal.
I don't understand!
Where are these things coming from?
How do we get out of here?
Things are dropping out of middair!
I'll cut through anything this place can throw at me!
More? Does your kind never learn?
By the Stars, we survived!
Do these fools never learn?
That was exciting, my love.
More? Do we look scared?
We're alive! Vivec must still smile on us.
What's happening?
Stay away from the portals!
Kill anything that comes out of a portal!
Gods! What is this?
How many of you are there?
Once again, we survived.
What, more troll dung?
Fools thought it would be easy to kill us.
The outside world can fade away when you're in here. Just let it go and savor the warmth and cheer we have inside.
Bit of lavender goes a long way when you're storing your saddle blankets. Might want to put in some mint, too, to help with various mites. Don't want your mount rearing up on you at a bad time.
Shor's bones, that was close! The thing almost bit me!
To Sovngarde with you, bloodsucker!
That thing's taken its last victim!
Come try and avenge your kin, monster!
One less vampire to prey on the innocent.
Two in a row? What luck!
How do you like that, you pale freak?
A second one! Kill it!
I don't think I'll ever get tired of killing these things.
Your death will be painful!
Blood crazed fool. It should be thanking us for ending its miserable existence.
Are you just as eager to die as your kin?
How pathetic!
Another one!
It is dead, yes? Perhaps someone should check.
We will not let you get away!
We killed it.
Brave of you to challenge us.
Excellent work. The fiend never stood a chance.
Spineless vampire!
That's one less werewolf that draws breath! Well done!
Two werewolves in a row? My lucky day!
Another mongrel slain by our hands.
Another beast! Kill it!
What a craven beast. It was too easy to kill.
There's another one! Kill it!
The werewolf is dead!
Filthy animal, we'll kill you too!
How many werewolves does that make? Twelve? Thirteen?
Let's make this one suffer.
I would think such a mongrel would put up more of a fight.
Another one! Slay it!
Zadiran-do welcomes you to your death, beast.
A second? Do not let it escape!
This one has no qualms about killing rabid animals.
This one looks stronger than the last.
Should we dispose of the body now?
Another werewolf begs for death.
Killing werewolves is almost as fun as killing vampires.
Let's make this one suffer.
Oh, so you want a fight, do you?
Are you lost, friend?
You have bad timing, friend!
Someone else comes to challenge us!
Kill this fool!
We will show you no mercy!
Prepare to meet your death, stranger!
Kill the stranger!
Do you know who you're dealing with?
Let us teach you the might of the Death Hunters.
I am eternal!
You will learn to fear the thunder!
Feed, my pets. Feed!
You will not live to regret that.
Brutes! Nincompoops! Dung-rolling hounds!
This can subdue the most uncooperative test subjects.
Enough, father!
That did something.
That wasn't helpful.
Run from your folly if you wish, but your fate is already sealed.
The harrowstorms bring such silence before they strike.
Soon we will know the taste of triumph.
We grow ever closer to our goal.
The harrowfiends serve us well.
Skyrim deserves what's coming to them.
I love the smell of dead Nords.
I require another focus to improve my spells.
The tailor sewed this much too tight.
We shall need wine to celebrate our victory.
A shadow draws near.
This place will know the fury of the Reach.
Did you see that fiend devour those skeevers?
The harrowed are a means to an end.
There is such power in the harrowstorms.
I feel the ritual's power deep within me each time.
Urgala provides only the best supplies.
Soon, all our efforts will be rewarded.
Who prepares this evening's meal?
See how the tower protects me!
It falls. No meaning. Step across! Delight.
I brought something for just this occasion!
Break free and crush these bugs!
Don't move around so much. You never know what lies in the dark.
Embrace the pain!
Such delicious power.
Let me feast on your terror!
Ugh! The taste of rodents!
Don't look so worn out. I'm just getting started!
I hoped to see you again soon and here you are! I assume you completed your task successfully?
I haven't done much exploring in the Reach myself, outside of meeting with my contacts. I wish I could offer you some guidance, but aside from what I've already told you, I know little else.
Some of the Reach clans are looking for help and I'm acting as a liaison for them. I can pay you for your time if you're willing to listen.
I'm sorry, I don't have any tasks I need done at the moment. I'll speak with my contacts in the Reach and have more work for you soon.
The ard demands success. How did you fare?
The Ard's Stonehands don't accept failure. Go on, get out there.
The Ard's Stonehands seek brave, skilled warriors. Does that describe you, or should we keep looking? There's a reward in it from the Markarth vaults for those worthy.
One threat down, but another will come. Be ready to answer the call.
Wane!
Enemies.
Ah! It's like a hammer on my skull! Keep him from doing that!
Those damn storms! They're unnatural! Care to help us put a stop to them, outsider?
I hope your slaughter of those lunatics that summon the harrowstorms convinces the rest to go home. Still, I doubt it. Come back tomorrow.
If the ard hadn't forbidden it, I'd join you in splitting the skulls of these witches myself. Paint the soil with their blood for me while you're disrupting the harrowstorm ritual, will you?
Markarth's skies are quiet. Been busy, have you?
Come! Test your mettle!
Empty flasks. Good to know they're here, but not what we need at present.
Lightning test!
Good … if you want a spear in your belly! Do it again!
Yuck. Be careful touching that.
You feel that shaking? Cave in? Yes there's coffee in this potion. Why?
I'm just here to stand watch and get paid. I'm not helping with your study.
I'm off testing duty tonight!
You picked the wrong place to explore!
Sure the pay's not great, but free health potions.
I did poison tasting yesterday. Can't feel my tongue, but I'm getting good at it.
Hey! You're not volunteers!
I found trespassers! It was me!
That was definitely a rumble! Let's go check the castle.
Who picks up after the death hounds?
No one gets past me with their limbs intact.
Have you ever used a bloodfiend to practice your aim?
When does the supposed conquering begin?
The Lady's time grows nearer!
Lady Thorn demands perfection from all her clan.
Our research is going too slowly.
Ha! More training practice!
Ah, this one intended to tidy up, but the day just slipped away. Moon-sugar, what can one do?
Finally, some action!
I prefer my meals on skewers!
Our home is breached! Kill them!
This one is shocked—shocked!—to have come into some gold recently. Scholarship pays, it seems.\n\nDinner is on Biro-dar!
What kind of inn is this? I've been sitting here for hours and nobody's brought me a drink. This is why I refuse to be a paying customer.\n\nAre you the proprietor? Bring me some wine!
Slash and tear! Stab and rip!
Our Lady wants no visitors!
Where's my wolf tonic? Here!
Ohh. No talking now. Massive headache. \n\nOnly two known cures for headache. Not talking. And wine. I need both. Now.
Someone vomited by the cooking fire. Very inconsiderate. \n\nYou should probably clean that up. I'd prefer not to step in it when I go to get a snack.
I once saw a Breton woman wearing a skirt so long it brushed the ground. I am certain she was unable to run very fast when the troll happened upon her.\n\nI, of course, was long gone.
A merchant whistled at me today. He will not make that mistake a second time.
I'd rather be cracking heads.
I received a letter from Verita Numida herself today. She actually read my essay!\n\nShe disagrees with every one of my findings, of course.
I need to ask a few questions of a historical figure. Unfortunately, she's been dead for quite a long time.\n\nAny chance you happen to know a friendly necromancer who charges reasonable rates?
Fighting's thirsty work, eh?
I suppose I could use another break.
Too slow!
Getting mad!
Blood!
[proud Goblin babble, like bragging]
[satisfied Goblin babble from eating a good meal]
[confused Goblin gibbering as though caught unawares by an enemy]
[enraged Goblin attack threats]
Deciding whether to turn back?
How brightly you'll burn!
Never lost a fight. Wasn't about to do so today.
Fuel for the flames.
<<Sniffling, runny nose.>>
<<Sniffling, runny nose.>>
A bit scrawnier than my usual servants but you'll do.
Come! Take what you seek, if you can.
Ha! Victorious once more!
Such a waste of precious time.
Great work with that amplifier!
Not me, you clumsy oaf!
You've a knack for this, outsider.
Good, those will do.
Yes, those will do.
Dwarfcraft and Reach tools don't compare with the hammers and tongs of Orsinium, but we work with what we're given, right?\n\nWhat can I help you with?
The mix of clans here in Markarth make for interesting … debate, let's say. Just last night I stepped in on an argument over whether a doll is simply a trinket or a receptacle for witch-work.

Hides, leather, wool … those are the proper materials for a Reachman's garments. If you have a mind to stitch together something suitable, I've got the materials you'll need. And a few extras, besides.
Some people hate the smell of tannins, but me? I can't get enough!\n\nSo, let's both take a big whiff and get to work!
You can learn much of the Reachfolk's customs by plying them with drinks! Just know it is impolite to refuse to drink from a skull.\n\nBut enough of that. You are here for enchanting, yes?
The ard has the darkest scowl I've ever seen. And I've seen Hagravens scowl! I'm certain his vexing glare soured my fruit that day.
Huh. Strange that vampires and werewolves and witches are working together. But then I look around here and realize that people make strange alliances when pushed.
Some of Ard Caddach's warriors act more like assassins, to my mind. They prefer to work from the shadows.\n\nMe, I prefer a fight out in the open.
Care to sample my wares, freehand? If you've a thirst, I've got a good strong drink to quench it!
Have you seen my cleaver? Ach, my eyes are no good anymore. Next thing you know I'll be adding bitterseed to my meat pudding. Whoo, wouldn't that be a kick in the gut!
Think of my inn's threshold as a boundary of sorts. My guests leave their quarrels and their feuds outside, eh?
Looking for something specific? If it's shriveled roots and deer-knuckle dice you're after, you'll have to speak with one of the locals.
Don't hunt in Wildspear territory. The clan'll harry and hound you into your grave if they catch you.
The ard smiles sometimes, but I don't trust it. How can I? His smile hides too much. Anger. Hatred. Fear. Death.
As a purveyor of furnishings, I've got to hand it to these Reachmen. Combining Dwarven furniture with bones and skins is no easy feat!\n\nForgive the rambling. What can I get you?

I'll take your measure, if you're looking for something to fit like a new skin, but leave any pointy bits on the counter first. The only things getting poked here are seams, or I'll use your eyes for pin cushions.
Ard Caddach is a generous host when he wants to be. Just mind that glint in his eye—means he's playing several games at once.
Ard Caddach's cruel, sure. But at least you know where he stands. Emeric and his cronies back in High Rock? Who knows what they're up to?
Adventuring brings with it great danger and greater burdens. Lighten your load, knowing it's safe here with us!
Don't mind the frightful surroundings. Reachfolk are unpredictable, to be sure. But your valuables are quite safe here.
Your bags are overburdened, beeko. If you do not want a sabre cat to feed you to her hungry litter, you will take a long look at my wares.

I thought, based on what everyone outside the Reach says, that the Reachfolk didn't know how to make anything requiring skill. But some of their handicrafts—woodwork, bone-carving, leatherworking—are quite artistic in their own way.
The ard demands only the best steeds for those who fight for him. I'm honored that he trusts me.\n\nAnd I know the consequences for failing him.
My dancing earned me a spot in Skyweaver clan. Apparently one of my dances resembles theirs to an alarming degree.\n\nI say alarming because it involves quite a bit of fire.
Ard Caddach is only the most recent leader of Markarth. I'm watching how someone like him manages all these different clans.
Yeah, you won't find me out there fighting whatever's got these clans stirred up. Not unless I have to. I prefer smaller jobs.
I erect the spine of welcome, and hope you find my wares pleasing.\n\nI fear you will need them before long.
Vampires descending upon the countryside seems as good a reason as any not to spend too much time in the Reach. Not that it's better anywhere else, am I right?
People are arseholes. Plain and simple. Don't care what clan you come from. Or what you call yourself. Aye, I include myself in that.\n\nNever have liked people too much.
I'm so grateful for this job. Not knowing where I came from doesn't impact my ability to find good homes for great items!
After all this blows over, I might roam beyond the Reach just to see more of the world out there. Just need to survive this dust up first.
I am not sure Ard Caddach dances. That seems like a very dry existence to me.\n\nYou know better. Let us put a smile on that face.
So, I heard one of the local chiefs told Ard Caddach something so funny he nearly wet his … you know, his loincloth or whatever.\n\nYou didn't hear it from me, though!
When all you do each day is stand around and sell goods, you don't want to sound boring.\n\nOr maybe you do. As for me? I don't want to sound boring.
I'd sell you my collection of worms that dried up in the sun, but that's all I have left of my life outside Markarth.
You touch some stones around here, and they're cold. You touch others, and they're hot. This place isn't just dead stone worked by Dwarves. Anyone who tells you differently is a fool.
The hills of the Reach have more components and reagents than I could ever have dreamed of! Pity it took this long to get at them.
Dwarves never tried to dash across wet stone. Had they done so, they would know the embarrassment of slipping down stony inclines and ending at Ard Caddach's feet.\n\nHe wore fine boots, indeed.
Look, I'd never tell someone to stop thieving. Just got to be careful.\n\nBretons'll clap you in irons. Dark Elves'll toss you in a volcano. But Reachmen? Reachmen do far worse.
Pay no mind to any chills you might experience while buying from me. Though … you wouldn't happen to see any ghosts right now, would you? No, don't answer. I'd rather not know.
I've worked in every single refuge there is. Might stick around here despite the goings-on in the Reach. This place is solid. Feel it in my bones.
Most people see Reachfolk as a bloodthirsty pack of animals. Truth is, some of them are bloodthirsty, but mostly they're just suspicious. As an Orc, I get suspicious.
Find it odd to see a Nord out in the Reach so openly? Sometimes I find it odd, too, but it leads to all manner of excitement, let me tell you!
I'm promised to clanfolk in three different clans right now. Yes, in marriage of a sort. Don't have plans to ever fulfill on those promises. Didn't want to make them in the first place.
I've always avoided Dwarven places. I feel so odd around them. Not myself. The spirits in these stone houses are blind to us.

If you see any caterpillars around here, please handle them.\n\nAnd by handle, I mean kill them with as much savagery as you can. Those things kill my plant friends. Don't talk to me about butterflies, either. I don't care.

This morning, a woman ran through the streets of Markarth screaming something about an evil doll chasing her. I didn't see it myself, so I can't verify the truth of it.\n\nI feel like every day, reality stabs me in the gut with nonsense yet again.

Ard Caddach once had a protege of sorts who tried to take his place. The tactics included whispers, setting people against each other, and lies.\n\nWhen the ard figured this out, well, let's just say it ended badly for his advisor.

I'm here on behalf of the Shunned Ones. They seek entry, though Ard Caddach is reluctant. What would entice such a man to allow them in while remaining true to the request of my benefactors to be wholly honest? A quandary. My quandary!

I'm positive I won't cover myself in glory by spending time here. More likely I'll be covered in gore. But then again, I asked for this post. Therefore, I must make the best of it until I'm called back.

Perhaps, if I can find the right pigments and other supplies, I shall paint Markarth in its vertical glory!\n\nYears have passed since I last lifted a brush. Let's hope I don't accidentally summon another Daedra with my art. Not here, too, surely.
The witches in the Reach aren't all the same, you know. We're all people, and people are unique. Maybe you'd best get to know each of them before you go around killing them, hmm?

Passed by some trouble on the way out here. Red swirling storms in Western Skyrim. Made every hair I've got stand on end the first time I saw one.\n\nMessing with vampires and werewolves is tricky in the best of times. Now? No, thank you!
I hear that Ard Caddach frowns on the use of skooma.\n\nThat brings this one much pain. Not that J'ghamar has skooma, mind you.
I hear that people outside the Reach fear our witches. I pity them deeply. Seems to me that being fearful and close-minded is no way to live.

Ard Caddach doesn't waste time with petty politics. Had a pretender claiming to stand for the Shadowbloom clan come seeking to weasel into his ear and elevate himself about our chieftain. The ard lopped his head off in one stroke. Won my vote.

At the end of the day, I need to remember that it's a failure of the teacher to teach, not the learner to learn, if the latter tries hard. Some of my students do want to learn, and I try to find the path toward understanding on an individual basis.
I'm not sure what to make about these harrowstorms and all the magic around them. I hear that they're both beautiful and deadly.\n\nMuch like my ex-betrothed.
The stone here feels different to me.\n\nDid the Dwarves who built this place differ so much from others or is this something Ard Caddach brought about?
You want to avoid Ard Caddach on one of his bad days.\n\nMost of his days are bad days.
Wonder what lives in the waters here? Might find a spot to drop a line one day. Some of the witches think it's a bad idea. They say I might catch a little Dwarven machine shaped like a fish.
I hear that people who work with their hands are sometimes looked down upon outside the Reach. Maybe that's why their weapons are so flimsy.
I'm much happier here than I'd be anywhere else in the Reach right now.\n\nWhich might not be saying much.

I know much troubles the Reach these days. Ard Caddach has an answer. The rebels have an answer.\n\nI think they wish to solve the same problem. And, in the meantime, there are Karthwasten's troubles.

I hear thinblood armies lash you if you have a speck of dirt on your shiny armor.\n\nBah. Dirt is a part of life. The real discipline comes from wading through mud knowing that it'll be on you until you next find water.
I met Ard Caddach once.\n\nIt was enough to keep me far, far away from Markarth since. The man is angrier than the bear that sat on the hornet's nest.
Owlets are the most darling creatures in the Reach.\n\nI will knife-fight you if you disagree.

There's not much call for reading or writing out here, but I don't mind. I didn't care too much for Markarth and its stone walls anyway.\n\nOh, and Ard Caddach's habit of killing people he didn't like. I didn't care for that, either.
I fight to still the screams. It's the screams, you know, that stay with you. \n\nBut any time I smell blood, I hear them again.
Inspiration comes from everything. Even the quiet shadows of this keep.\n\nI just wish I could get a decent night's sleep here.
I hope our clan is the first back out in the wilds after this vampire nonsense is done.
The Icereach Coven are not ice statues brought to life.\n\nIf I find the person running around and spouting off heedless nonsense, I'm going to change them into a headless bit of bloody nonsense.

So, yesterday, I got dragged in to speak with Ard Caddach about provisions.\n\nWhat about me cries out that I'm a master at provisioning things? Then, when I returned to my ever-so-delightful sleeping spot to nap, I found my favorite blanket gone. Aha!
Well, who is this now? Have you come for a tale?
Some of the folk around here claim Ard Caddach changes into a bear, but I'm pretty sure they just mean his temper. Pretty sure.
Only thing that takes the edge off my nightmares is this terrible cider I steal from the inn.\n\nTastes like Daedra piss … if Daedra were to piss.
I'm told that I look like a chipmunk.\n\nMaybe I was a chipmunk and I never knew it? Or maybe I'm a chipmunk trapped in a Bosmer body?

Smile, they said. Don't be contrary, they said. Ha! I smile when I please, s'wit. And any attempt to change my no to a yes is you being contrary, fetcher, because I already said no.\n\nThat's what I told them. Stand by your principles, stranger.
Cursed Bal take what's left.
Superior to the Coven's witchcraft in every way.
Burnt to cinders!

Nazdar's practicing has paid off. He hasn't improved, but he broke all his strings. At least there will be some peace and quiet until he gets new ones.\n\nDon't worry. Humble Zaham is doing his best to smuggle all the strings out of the Stitches.

I heard rumors that Khasda's ghost was haunting the Stitches, his wails echoing through the canyons late at night. Nope. Just Nazdar, singing sad songs. Easy to confuse the two. I sent him to bed and told him to sing more quietly in the future.
My work as a historian involves reading dusty books and searching through old scrolls. But you! You unearth antiquities that real people used in the ancient past. That's not history—that's adventure!
Guild-mate! Good to see you! Have you heard of any heists … er, historic expeditions … er, that need a clever thief … er, scholar—gah! \n\nSubterfuge is hard, yes?
You saw it with your own eyes. My sisters in the Icereach Coven took a dark turn. I'm a witch without a coven now. But this place has a roof and four walls, so I'm content.\n\nFor now.
How much do you bet I find it first?
Hold this line!
I have full faith in our master to pull this off.
Your search ends here!
Above you. Try to make a connection with that portal.
Move! Use a portal now!
I assure you, while I am happy for a place to stay, I am used to much grander accommodations when I travel. I am the royal scion of Skyrim, after all.

I crave adventure! When my father was my age, he was slaying monsters, bedding wenches, and winning wars. And at the same time, he wrote ballads and sonnets considered the best of his generation. And here I am. Here.\n\nWhat a tragic disappointment.

After the events in and around Markarth … well, that was my first visit to the Reach, you know. I'll say this for Ard Caddach. I don't know if he deserves the title of Despot of Markarth, but he can certainly be overbearing.\n\nWhat? I'm just saying.

No matter our intentions, most of the people of Western Skyrim look upon us with distrust and suspicion. You'd think the Skald-King just tried to destroy Solitude and not their own mad ruler! Ah well. We still want to help them.\n\nIf they'll let us.

Thanks to you, I see our allies in the Ebonheart Pack in a totally new light. Where once I saw enemies, now I see friends and colleagues. We are stronger together, but it took you to teach me that. I wanted you to know.
This one is Adusa-daro of House Ravenwatch. From Rivenspire.\n\nAssume I am here on a diplomatic mission. Such assumptions make everything that comes later much easier to accept, yes?

We allow some myths to perpetuate. It maintains our vampiric allure and keeps our enemies off guard. Meanwhile, we must know the truth in order to combat our evil kindred. But no, the only thing garlic will repel is my sensitive nose.
Count Verandis chose well when he decided to bring you into the Ravenwatch's confidence, my friend. Know that Adusa-daro will always do the same.
So now you have met Adusa's little brother. What do you think of Fennorian, five-claw?\n\nYou can be honest. Your secrets are Adusa's secrets, yes?

Gwendis suggested we hire a bard to sing your song, five-claw. The hero of Western Skyrim and the Reach. The slayer of Rada al-Saran. Unless you are too modest to accept such praise?\n\nJust know Adusa appreciates your efforts. We all do.

I wasn't always an Undaunted. Started out as a warrior in the Reach. Served as one of Ard Caddach's royal Stonehands, I did. But you make one little mistake and they exile you for life. Stupid reekers, the lot of them!
Pants are for Nords and other lesser forms of fungi. I only wear them to be polite. But after midday and about eight mugs of beer, I make no promises.
I know. I'll recommend you as an Undaunted Trailblazer. That way, when you scurry away from a battle like a startled skeever, you can just call it scouting.

Look at you. Undaunted. No longer a spineless, mud crawling, dung eating wriggler. You're still a bottom-feeding maggot, but at least you've tasted a little blood. To commemorate the occasion, the next round's on me.\n\nRemind me.
This one's on me, Undaunted. Cheers!\n\nYou've made quite a reputation for yourself. Nowhere near as impressive as mine, but worthy of congratulations just the same.
We've exhausted the trap's power! Send more souls to the Dark Heart and I will summon another!
I will wait here until you return.
I don't like Caddach, I don't like Markarth. I don't even like the ale they serve at the inn.
I've been hoping for a chance to see the ard, but so far no luck. If he'll have me, I'd like to join his Stonehands. I can fight.
Use the portals to get out of there!
My daughter Eoline insisted we go when we heard that Caddach was gathering the Reachfolk here in Markarth. \n\nStill not sure if it was a wise decision.
My father lies dead in the street! I'll never forgive myself.
What brings you to Markarth? Come to see Ard Caddach yourself? I think he's a true son of the Reach, though some disagree with me.
Did you know that there are places in this city where you can pay to sleep in a bed? And take a bath in hot water?\n\nThat can't be good for you.

Did you know this city was actually built by the Dwarves? Well, parts of it, anyway. A lot of so-called scholarship about the Dwarves is nothing but pure speculation. I try to stick to the facts of what I've personally seen or studied.
Thella is very excited about delving into the ruined levels beneath the city. I don't share her enthusiasm. It's cold, dank, and the mechanical creatures give me nightmares.
I've yet to meet Ard Caddach personally. I hope to soon, but I'd be satisfied if his counselors merely relayed my business proposition to him. \n\nAfter all, rulers require gold, too.
Tahzim talks about his homeland a lot. Sandy, hot, no mountains, no trees. I can't even picture it, to be honest. \n\nWho would want to live in such a place?
I'm not sure how long we'll be in Markarth. I do miss Hammerfell, though.
Begging? No, it's not begging. I just need a little help. Something to tide me over until I find honest work. You'll see.
There's too much stone in Markarth. Give me a good tent of hide and heather for my bed. That's all a true child of the Reach needs!
We must be getting close to the Dark Heart, my friend. Soon we shall have the answers that have thus far eluded us.
Have you met the Nord Cultural Ambassador, Rigurt the Brash? Why my father continues to employ that buffoon is beyond me.\n\nDespite his bumbling, though, he somehow gets the job done. Eventually.
The work of millennia will not be stopped by the likes of you!

When Adusa gets really hungry, she seeks out villains upon which to feed. Even then, this one rarely drains them dry.\n\nUnless there is no other choice or option available, the Ravenwatch refrains from executing those we bring to justice.

The leader of the evil vampire clan pulled out a dagger and brandished it at Adusa. "How courageous of you," I said. "Ill advised, but courageous."\n\nAnd then this one showed him the error of his ways.
March, my legion, and win your salvation!
Lady Belain said that no one is to interfere. Remain vigilant.
Must I handle this myself?
Sink your fangs into mortal flesh!
The prophecy shall be fulfilled!
The Heart hungers! It must be fed!
The Wayward Guardians grow stronger with each passing day. We have you to thank for that.\n\nWhat of your latest journey?
Our lands have never been safe. Not truly. But that doesn't mean we can't give the people hope.\n\nGo, and may the ancestors watch over you!

The witches say our ancestors look down on us from the sky above. One day we will greet them and share stories of the battles we fought. Let's give them a good tale, shall we?\n\nBut later, when a task presents itself, yes?
Arana spoke highly of you. Where others flee, you run headlong toward the dangers that threaten the Reach. The Wayward Guardians could use that sort of bravery, if you would aid us.
Your pet was not fit to fight alongside the Gray Host. Join us or die, too!
She was worth a thousand of your kind! Die, scum!
The salamanders would make for useful familiars.
Bring this to an end!
This power belongs to the True-Sworn.
This shall go quickly.
Face your death bravely!
Imagine how powerful we'll be after this.
Pyroturge Encratis's success benefits us all!
Encratis's will be done!
Burn the books. Burn them all. As he said.
No guests!
He promised power. And I got it. What cost? What cost.
Burn it down!
Sharp work, harrier! I'll open another portal.
All shall join the void!
Don't send me back!
Minions come forth!
I summon the infinite!
I draw strength from beyond!
This death is only temporary!
You cannot escape!
Another wishes to test their mettle!
I failed you my Prince ….
Someone wishes to meet you!
I become one with the flame!
Your indecision demeans us both.
Shall we begin, then?
Inevitable, really. I have never lost.
Imprisoning our own clan members seems … wrong.
Boss Trenlor says I can terrorize the villagers next time!
I used to get to lounge around all day in Boss Trenlor's court. Not anymore.
If that prisoner says another word, I'm draining them dry!
And then Boss Trenlor said, "Time to die, mortal!" It was hilarious!
I suppose guarding the prisoners is better than being a prisoner.
After he tossed Freyleth down here, I thought I was going to be next!
I say it's time to hunt our enemies instead of the other way around.
I hear the Hagravens have something special planned for the Hillhunter chief.
Would it be asking too much for the prisoners to meet their fate with some courage?
Watch what you say around the Hagravens, or you'll wind up with a tree in your chest too.
Ach! That last one was a screamer. No pride at all.
I hear Ard Caddach's calling the clans to Markarth. Does that include the Thornroots?
This won't end well. Mark my words.
I'm coming to like it here in these old ruins. Stay here and reinforce the defenses, I say.
What will it be like, I wonder? To be raised up by the Spirit Queen?
It seems as though I have waited all my life for this day.
I do not belong here anymore … let me rest …
They seek to rouse the Heart, do they? I should like to see that …
Nathari had better be right about this. I thought we'd all hear Namira's voice by now.
I know. We can't stop now. We have to see this through to the end.
This is taking too long. The waiting isn't easy.
How I longed for this day. Soon all that we have given up will be repaid twofold.
These Reach fools have no idea what's in store for them.
Stay focused. We have a job to do.
Work hard and we'll make an exarch out of you yet.
Gray Host over all!
I'll test my claws against their steel any day!
I can smell their fear in the air.
The Reachfolk thought they had me surrounded. Stupid mortals.
By claw and fang, as the Ashen Lord commands, we obey!
I do enjoy a good amount of clawing and slashing.
The Heart must be fed. I have no wish to crawl again.
Whose support can I count on?
I hate it when the food fights back!
