Some see an old pirate with too many scars and a staff better for walking than fighting. No one expects me to know a damned thing about magic. Or anything scholarly, for that matter.\n\nI happen to know a lot of pirates who like to read. Just saying.
Tadali is small in stature, yes. But an Alfiq should be judged by the size of her spirit, not her claws. Though Tadali's claws are sharp, too. Would you care to see?
Some say there is foolishness in too much wisdom. This one can assure you, there is not.

Seas and storm, those Sload are terrible creatures! Vile as any Oblivion monstrosity and evil as the ocean is wide! It won't be an easy battle, but we're going to win it. There really isn't any other option.
Hey you! What do you know about this Three Banners War I heard bandied about lately? Why in Nirn would anyone on Tamriel be fighting when we have those vile Sloads to contend with? It makes no sense!
Pacrooti welcomes you! Are you interested in treasures and riches? This one can help!
Excellent!
It appears you have no crates, my friend. You can purchase one to continue.
Bright moons, my friend! Pacrooti is here if you are ready.
There's so much work to be done. It never ends. When I was a child, I used to wonder what kept my father so busy. Then I grew up and he started assigning me tasks. I wish it had remained a mystery.

I trained that much harder to be a knight to impress Druid Laurel. Heh, I was a young boy who wanted to appear strong in front of his crush. I soon learned she was plenty strong herself, and quite hard to impress. But I never stopped trying.
My size can be intimidating. I know that. But I'm really just a big poof ball. \n\nA big, dangerous, unapologetic, poof ball—armed with sharp claws and sharper teeth.
I hear that many types of Khajiit can be confusing to the furless among us. Too bad. We don't owe anyone an explanation.
My first vampire was … messy. Untidy. The encounter left me with permanent scars upon my soul, and a determination that every one thereafter would be cleaner, better.
Do you think perhaps the writer of the Investigator Vale novels might consider a series based on a hunter of the damned? Some of my adventures have been … dramatic. Hmm. Just a passing thought.
Move! Run! Don't stand there!
I hope none of you feel this.
Let me help.

No sense pinching coins when it comes to a good pair of boots. Nothing worse than swashbuckling with sand and seaweed getting into loose-fitting footwear. Besides, my mother always told me that wet feet are stinky feet, and no one wants that.

Whatever you do, don't stare directly into Howler's eyes. It's impolite. You have to shake his hand first and bow. If you don't believe me, go ahead and see how fast he tries to claw your eyes out. He takes proper etiquette quite seriously.

No task is too small for J'baanluk and this one is too tall not to support his community. For example, this one once spent an entire evening getting a pet guar out of a tree. No idea how it got up there, but the child's smile made the labor worth it.

J'baanluk relaxes now, but when he returns to Elsweyr he will heft his weapon and fight like a Pahmar possessed. With mace and shield, tooth and claw. Anything less would be an insult to Jone and Jode.

You wouldn't believe how often we draw the attention of the local authorities. They get one sniff of Daedric worship and they go for their torches and pitchforks! Until they meet us. Then all they want to do is run our blessed diseases out of town.

Have I told you how I found Peryite? It's quite amusing! You see … no, that's actually embarrassing. Maybe … no, that sounds even worse.\n\nLet's just go with how I stepped into something squishy and it turned out to be a plague-ridden corpse.
You can't win, not when the chimera's power joins this one's.
Your mind is as graceful as a kitten tangled in yarn.
Your mistakes waste all our time.
Give 'em a fight.
Finally. Some quiet.
Better luck next time. Oh wait.
(battle roar)
I'm with you.

Hard to find my place in this world. The Thieves Guild is run by incompetents. Fighters Guild, too social. I'm too dumb to join the Mages Guild. Too smart to join the Undaunted. Too sane to join the Dark Brotherhood. I guess I'm stuck with you.
Picking up a lot from you, lately. It's paying off.
Impressive.
I don't like seeing things go to waste. I'd rather you sell something than destroy it. \n\nI hear guilds are good for that sort of thing, but I wouldn't know.
Back at it again.
I get a little stir-crazy if I go too long without feeling the wind at my back.\n\nMight take off on my own for a bit, if nobody's around.
A divergence point, hah!
Hostilities ended. Now to relax.
(unleashed power shout)
(clearing his throat, annoyed)

I know many of my arcanomystically inclined colleagues eschew the simple pleasures of preparing a meal. But I find it very soothing. It also proved a steady source of income over the years, when realm traveling genius was not paying very well.
Ah, newfound understanding! And with it: power.
Mora has his eyes on you. I can feel it.
I am a scholar. I drink tea.  Please, whatever you do, avoid making or drinking coffee around me. The smell is quite discommodious to me. Consume hot and bitter bean water on your own time.
I'm here, and I'm feeling feisty!

Beyond runes and the cookpot my crafting skills are somewhat limited, but I have a great deal of admiration for those who can hone a sword or stitch a shirt. \n\nPerfection is a lofty peak, but it's worth the climb.
A word of advice—Not all Telvanni are as trustworthy as I am. Archmagister Otheri has skeletons in his closet that would make Divayth Fyr blush!

There's nothing I love more than sitting by the fire after a long day of performances. Kicking your feet up. Sipping a glass of sylph gin. Trading tales. Pure bliss. If you ever care to join, just bring a bottle of wine and a good story.

The beauty of a traveling troupe is being able to inspire the common folk all across Tamriel. Performing for the well-to-do's is wonderful and all, but no adoring noble crowd comes close to adding a sparkle to eyes of an overworked servant.
There must be a tavern or a taproom close by. I could do with a tankard of watered rum and a bawdy song.

I doubt I'd ever be content to fully settle on dry land. But I would like to travel across the continent some day. There are only so many things you can see from the deck of a ship and along the shore.
I learned long ago to set no goals and abandon all expectations. There's a lot to recommend it.
Daedra don't know what to make of music. We had no idea such a thing could exist until you mortals came along.
No version of me gives up.
Little reflection, you cannot kill me.
You think you hit hard?
You're a strong reflection. But I am not alone.
Let the fear burn you.
I want to see you run.
Let us try something else.
I reflect you. I cower.
This version dies. The others live.
Your blood will turn to ink. We will be the same, reflection.
I underestimated you before. Never again.
I am the blood of knowledge. You bleed ignorance.
Think you can win this time?
Tho'at, what are you doing?
Get ready, Tho'at's planning something.
I advise against touching that.
If I'm going to use this nymic, I'd like not to be alone when I do it.
I speak the sound of your essence. Follow it here!
Both paths lead forward. Which will you choose? Maligraphies or a chance at another Verse?
I once had a lover who thought she was a real doll. \n\nHow little she knew.
Laugh if you want, but wait until this happens to you.
Ah-Choo! You must excuse Mizzik. Is there a dog in here, by chance? Mizzik is quite allergic.
Mizzik must be careful not to cast aside a fact if it does not fit neatly into his developing theory.\n\nIndeed, it is the facts that do not fit that require careful attention, yes?

If you're the type to mouth off to nobles, I'd actually recommend finding work as a bodyguard. As long as you don't go overboard, the job gives you free rein to tell them when they're being idiots. Sometimes, they even listen.

I had a pet mudcrab growing up. Saved him from some gulls trying to crack his shell open. Eventually, he got too big and started going after our neighbor's chickens, so Aunt Murog turned him into crabcakes. \n\nNever wanted another pet after that.
This defies explanation!
Don't forget who holds your nymic.
Would you mind fighting slower? I can barely record your movements for posterity.
I'm so hungry.
You're a goat. You're meant to be eaten.

I regret never meeting Queen Nurnhilde before she passed. Jorunn—King Jorunn—has said I remind him of her. \n\nI would have liked to see if he lifted her with such vigor as he does with me each time we meet.

What do I miss most about Eastmarch? I am not shy to say it. Rabbit meatballs! Many among the Black Fin Legion have tried and failed to replicate the dish. Some blame the rabbits. I say the climate. The constant frost somehow enhances their flavor.
My work lets me travel across the width and breadth of Tamriel. Wouldn't have it any other way. My feet get itchy if I stay in one place for too long.

Where I come from, most people believe that souls travel to Sovngarde when they die. I have no interest in that. The Void sounds much better. Quiet nothingness for eternity. \n\nAh, I feel relaxed just thinking about it.
You wouldn't know a place nearby where a person could do some howling, would you? Maybe with a nice echo and soft grass to sit in. Just curious.

I'll try to describe the feeling I get before I transform. Have you ever eaten so much honeyed oats that you feel a weight in your stomach but also queasy from the sweetness? \n\nMix that with ants marching on your skin. Yes, that sounds about right.
Dodge! Now!
Join me, my ally!
Conquest! In my name!
I will make an army from you.
The Green is always tweaking, testing, growing to adapt to the world around it. This must be your philosophy as well.
<The construct stares into your very soul. You believe this simple machine would sacrifice everything to please you.>
(Goblin GIbberish 09)
Should have picked the other one.
A whisper, a fleeting whisper, can you hear it? It says my prices are unbeatable.

My connection to the Morag Tong. That's a powerful secret I've shared with you. Betray that trust and you'll find my blade in your back. Or in your neck. Or maybe your gut.\n\nI'll stick it somewhere, you can count on that.
Some of my associates in the Morag Tong say I have an unnatural attachment to my axes. I say I have just the right amount of attachment. \n\nHave you seen my twin blades? They're beautiful!
Meddle somewhere else!
I will not be defeated!
Little mortals, little lives!
(Goblin GIbberish 09)

One summer, my mom made me work at a vineyard. Said it would be formative. Turns out, making wine is very demanding. At the end of the day, I couldn't tell what was a bruise and what was just grape stains.
Ready for whatever you've got.
I'm learning a lot from you.
Let's make this quick.
Just when I hit my stride.
I thought they'd be tougher.
Want to see something really fun?
Easy there.
Never hurts to learn something new.
I thank you for this respite, tamiit. I often forget, in this strange era, to devote time to meditation and prayer.
By your side, tamiit.
Strength of the exiled Boethra. It finds me, even now.
You are a knave and a jeek!
They left us no choice.
Soz fif'rai trajii, sa'purahd.
Dusk and dawn, ignite within me!
You tire of walking? Very well.
The purpose of tamiiti made manifest. We make each other stronger.

I'm fortunate. While I find the sun's gaze uncomfortable, exposure doesn't burn me like some with my condition. What do I feel? Hmm, how to describe?\n\nSunlight feels like someone rolling pine cones all over my skin without end.

Ever since Count Verandis brought me into House Ravenwatch, I've felt a sense of belonging. I never experienced the lust for power or desire to cause suffering that some vampires display. A loving family like this is precisely what I need.

Adventuring isn't just about physical strength. A little bit of ancient Elven will get you far. Shameful how few adventurers study the fundamentals these days.\n\nAh, well. I suppose not everyone shares my academic curiosity and gift for language.

Narsis Dren always has time for an adoring admirer. Although at this precise moment I am busy contemplating my next exciting expedition. Much research to be done. Musty, tedious, soul-rending research. \n\nWhere are my assistants when I need them?

I used to read Maormer stories that made them out to be swashbuckling adventurers. Even dreamed about sailing the seas like them. Never meet your idols. I've seen the harm they can cause first hand. No thank you.
Go on, do something interesting. People like you always do. Go on. I'll wait.
Aww, who's a good mortal? You are! You are! \n\nThere you go. It's really quite affirming, isn't it?

Not only am I at my most peaceful in a garden, but I once fell asleep in a rose bush while hiding from guards. Must have slept through two rotations without getting caught. Best sleep I'd had in ages.

I was raised by nomads before I heard Lorkhaj's call to serve Azurah. I was a fidgeter, and cursed with unrepentant wanderlust. Talbira always said that my choice to follow a hadaliit's path of temperance and patience must mean my calling was true.
Hadaliit of the Hidden Moon were subject to constant training. I hear tales of an … Infinite Archive? Where warriors may endlessly hone their skills.\n\nPerhaps we could test our mettle there?
I cannot be stopped!
Taste our suffering!
Iron Atronachs hate the cold. Freeze them!
Help me. Please!
This one must confess. It is exhausting to be as dashing and handsome as Za'ji is all the time. That is why Za'ji naps whenever he can.
Za'ji's stay here has given him some ideas for redecorating the Perfect Pounce. He deserves a more comfortable cabin, yes?

The druids say that talking to plants encourages healthy growth. That's why I believe the secret to Dufort wine lies in the tourneys held on our grounds. All the cheering and fanfare makes for a delicious grape.

I admit it. I have a small crush on High King Emeric. How could I not? A voice as robust and warm as the wood of a bourbon barrel. I could listen to him prattle on about any subject for days and days. And I have!

I often get questions about the name Muffins. It's what she smells like if you really bury your nose in her fur and take a deep whiff.\n\nAdmittedly, there may be something wrong me. Or with every muffin I've ever had. But the name stuck.

My favorite thing about Muffins, let's see …. It's so hard to choose! \n\nBut if I had to, I'd say her pointy little ears. They're so soft! Lucky for me that she doesn't mind when I pet them, and she loves it when I scratch behind them.
You're on the right track, but we need more. Much more!
The fire's dwindling. Keep at it! Almost there.
Of course.
That's it …
If I catch you kissing on duty again, I'll send you both to Cyrodiil!
A weight has been lifted and peace will be mine. Thank you.
We're farmers and fisherfolk. Why would anyone attack us?
Damn the plague!
You are mortal, but one day you will be like me. On that day you will know torment!
I have to find it!
Is anyone out there?
Break it before it breaks us!
The Ansei spirits won't allow necromancy.
I want their flesh!
You cause any trouble here, you're going to regret it!
You're not leaving here alive.
Take one alive so we can have some fun later.
You'll never amount to anything, you thickblooded idiot!
As your hunt ends, mine begins!
Good, I needed new boots.
Orcs can't talk. Don't be silly.
For ten, place your hand upon its fur! Feel the muscle of a true killing machine!
I know we made a lot of coin from this, but I'd rather rob merchant caravans than chapels.
If you enjoyed your flogging today, please remember to thank your ogrim tormentor.
When?
Wretched things, mortals. May a storm wash you into Coldharbour.
You must bow to me or die. Minions, destroy them!
You think this is over, wretch? Tell yourself another lie.
Varen's gambit nearly handed the empire to Mannimarco—and Nirn to me.
I admire your tenacity, mortals.
I've made you an offer, mortal.
You've always been jealous of my light. I won't let you take it!
Down with Lavinia!
Do not allow your children to wander into the ways of ignorance.
All knowledge is mine. Gathered in time long past and come to me in time yet to arrive.
Care to spend some of that gold you've earned, dearie?\n\nAnd before you ask, I'm all out of boar knuckles. You wouldn't believe the demand on those things.
No, I don't mind, keep chopping.
That was for Esmaeel!
There's no hope! We'll be its next meal!
You will not mar the glory of the Learned One with your presence.
The end approaches.
Gaze upon our light and perish.
No one bests Uzzai!
No one will hear from you again.
I hope you're not sticking around for the consolation prizes. No matter what you've heard—there aren't any!
Look around. Sanctum Ophidia will be your grave!
Even the air here burns your puny lungs. Enjoy!
There will be no trace of you when I'm finished!
More supplies? It seems this shift will never end.
"The lazy Khajiit's tail is soon stepped upon." This one will not lose her tail!
We nearly have enough supplies to start loading the cart.
"A delivery is only as good as its packaging," as they say.
Nobody would notice if I just left. Would they? No, I should stay.
This is going to work. This has to work.
I must return to my love. Will she remember me?
Does my lover still wait for me?
Lyranth deserved everything we did to her. The injustice is imprisoning me.
I'm going to die!
Help me!
You have such curious eyes. I'll eat them!
To me, my subjects!
I demand restoration!
Defend your master!
A feast of hearts would not sate me.
The job's done, huh? This work turns us into monsters, doesn't it? Weighs down my soul.\n\nLet's hope the coins are enough for us to live with what we've done.
There's so much death. So much. I'll sleep better knowing at least one of the death dealers has been eliminated.\n\nThank you, kindly.

Oh, friend, I was afraid I was never going to see you again. I heard the most vicious rumors concerning you and the Enforcers. But let's put that behind us and get you signed up again so that you can take advantage of all the opportunities we offer.
I know it's nothing personal, but feel responsible for this life you're leading. Did I somehow fail to prepare you for the life of an Enforcer? I just hope you'll change your mind.
Valga Crassus.
Perhaps if we had some mead … they are Nords, after all!
You've done well so far! Now, however….
You've beaten the odds so far! Now it changes.
The challenger wins! That was one for the record books.
This combatant can't take much more of that!
Invaders! They attack! Rise! Rise from the tunnels!
Our sacrament … disrupted!
That does it! This is all but over.
If words lack meaning, then they were not meant for you to hear.
I heard we were opening a third tunnel, soon—where was that exactly? No? Forget I asked.
Every now and then, there is a time when one reflects upon one's life and deeds.\nThis is a relevant philosophical question. It's decided: I need more money.
The best feeling is a happy purchase! Have that feeling now!
Hauling your fine work helps maintain my physique.
You need something to disappear?
Really? Ugh!
Tonight, you.
Tonight, you.
Trouble me, it's what I live for.
I think you could use a week at the temple. Mention me and they'll give you a discount.
Trouble me, it's what I live for.
I think you could use a week at the temple. Mention me and they'll give you a discount.
Many thanks, and may you come safely to your journey's end.
Nothing shall be wasted.
Ugh, I'll die of hunger! Come here my darlings!
In times like these, Pacrooti finds it heartening to remember there are always times like these.
Greetings, my friend! Are you ready for excitement and outstanding rewards?
Until next time.
Shall we try again?
Very practical.
This looks valuable.
A suitable reward.
Very sleek!
<Laugh that says "I'm a real jerk.">
Opulence. I have it. You can, too. For the right price.
Very nice!
None of us is getting any younger, you know.
You ready? You look ready.
Mmmmmmm.
Hmmmm!
Hmm hmm hmm, ha!
In times like these, Pacrooti finds it heartening to remember there are always times like these.
Mmmmmmm.
Where is that sound coming from?
Die you milk drinkers!
I can feel pain, you know!
Mortals cannot know the depths of this pain, but we can drown them in the shallows.
Share a secret, with the night. Unclasp your doubt, and give it flight,
Everything will be over soon. Everything.
Strongbox protocols engaged.
Resident detected in proximity. Greetings.
Combat protocols on standby.
May your thoughts remain well-oiled.
Hooooo.
This one welcomes you, and wishes you good luck! Pacrooti thinks we place too high a value on the luck of the early bird. Isn't the early worm even luckier?
In times like these, Pacrooti finds it heartening to remember there are always times like these.
This part always excites Pacrooti!
My compliments!
Hooooo.
First rate!
Let's get started!
This one wonders what your next crate holds.
Rise, my yaghra! Destroy them all!
Summerset is mine, mortal bugs!
The darkness is near.
K'Tora would be impressed if your victory actually meant something.
Oh how you amuse me, my dear, dear mortal!
As the darkness swallows light, so shall Nocturnal consume you.
These spoils are much better than the last raid.
Stand back! This spell tends to make everything explode.
Make them grovel. That's my philosophy.
The Dominion Navy! Like plucking fish from a pond!
Get close before you strike.
Those who we consume shall nourish greatness.
These mortals shall feed our brood for weeks to come.
I sense movement. What guests have arrived?
(Goblin GIbberish 10)
Hey, do you want to learn how to say hello in my native language? All right, mate. All you'll need is a conch shell, six friends, a harp with forty strings, and a newborn calf. I'll wait.
You may have survived so far, but there is more to come!
You may have held your own, but now comes our champion!
A stunning victory for our challengers!
Let's see how long these challengers last!
What are you doing, Blackguards? Get it together!
I'm bored. When can we go and rob something?
I forget. Are we hitting the Lilmoth Counting House or the Lusty Argonian Footman this time?
The necromancer of the fen … why would anyone want to raise the dead?
Your scales appear to have the color of cowardice, clawless one.
The next Blackguard to complain about anything gets a spear in the arse!
You're as fragile as a day-old egg!
I'll lead the raid. I'm clearly the strongest among us.
Another raid? Can't we just sit this one out?
Unworthy.
The blood! The guts! The cheese! It's glorious!
This is what I get for killing every chicken I see, isn't it? Best flee!
The owner of a ridiculous idea is absolutely certain of its merit.

Are you here about a reward? For one of our excellent festivals or celebrations? I'm just the assistant, unfortunately, and I don't have access to our stock. You'll have to come back when the Impresario returns.\n\nSorry!
Come close, walker, and Zar will tell you the lost tale of Khunzar-ri and the Skooma Cat. No, on second thought, Zar will save that for another day.
You've stopped the storm, but you'll never reclaim what it's taken from you!

There might have been a misinterpretation of this one's intentions today. At the market. With the baker.\n\nWho knew they expected actual payment for their wretched moon-sugar cakes? They should thank Biro for taking them off their hands, yes?

There might have been a misinterpretation of this one's intentions today. At the savings and loan. With the banker.\n\nThat was definitely not Biro's hand. In the vault drawer. With his fingers around a fistful of gold. Not in the least.
When you're thirsty, never sample flasks from a tinkerer's bag. Vole either keeps his grease in old whiskey bottles or makes the worst mixed drinks in the world.\n\nBoth could be true with that one.
I may not know how to turn lead to gold, but I can turn any booze yellow just by drinking it. Hee hee.
Your hand. Keep it where I can see it. I know my fur looks soft and inviting, but if you attempt to pet me, you will lose it.\n\nMy claws are very sharp, just so you know.
A loudmouthed dolt disturbed my daily constitutional, so I cursed him.\n\nNothing deadly, mind you. Just a few boils on the tongue. Probably won't make a sound for another day or so.
I need a place to perform rituals and such. Nothing too elaborate. And I'll put everything back the way I found it when I'm finished.\n\nYou'll hardly notice the odor or the screams.

I came across a gold chalice covered in Chimeri inscriptions once. Unfortunately, it was in a cave full of poisonous mushrooms. With walls that dripped with molten lava. And guarded by a horde of Goblins.\n\nSo, no, I wasn't able to translate it.

Most scholars turn to the Mages Guild when they want to conduct significant research, but I've found the Fighters Guild to be a surprising treasure trove of information.\n\nAnd Outlaws Refuges. But leave your gold pouch at home if you decide to visit.
Adusa likes it here. This place is fragrant!\n\nMuch better than most of the tombs and barrows this one has sheltered in. I especially like the distinct lack of untamed spiders.

Folk are always going on about how great the Dwarves were. The buildings, the machines, the seemingly endless supply of mechanical spiders. Well, if they were so great, how come they're all gone? Give a Reachfolk two sticks and we live forever!

Now, Hroltar is not one to boast about his own accomplishments, but I once fended off a dozen Nord warriors wielding axes while pleasuring two dozen Nord shield maidens.\n\nIt was a dare, so it wasn't like I could refuse.
Nobody can drink like Thane Jeggi. His aptitude for consumption is legendary!\n\nI wish he wouldn't refer to me as a skeever, though. It's insulting.
This one is expecting an important letter. It should arrive tonight by carrier bat.\n\nThis one made a joke, yes?
Adusa likes this place. It has … personality!
Let's go find a problem to solve. And maybe get paid for it.
I am not afraid of you!
Courage brings victory.

When I was small, I made soup in mud puddles with the wings of flies. I have since grown as a cook. While mud has its place and flies do add a lovely texture, my palate of ingredients has increased.\n\nFlies do add the perfect amount of crunch though.
I found some wonderfully ripe and sun-blessed roots, along with a few oozeworthy maggots. Also some fermented pond scum. Yum!\n\nWhat? Pick up your spoon and eat your soup. It's perfectly delicious!
Ah, mortals! What curious creatures! Your little antics amuse me so!

Things I learned as a cultist: It's hard to get passers-by to look at religious literature.\n\nIf you wrap your literature around a brick and throw it through a window, though, someone's bound to read it.

If not for the compassion of a certain homeowner, I'd be on the street right now. My family disowned me when I joined the cult, and I had to give everything I owned to the order.\n\nWhen you quit, they do not provide any sort of refund, by the way.
Your death draws nearer every day, the end of your very existence. And yet, you carry on with no unusual urgency. Fascinating.
I have just now learned how the foodstuff you call cheese is created. Truly, to relish such an abomination, you mortals must be made of sterner stuff than I had imagined.
I try to think of the ghosts of my past as unfinished business I just haven't gotten to yet.
All right, but next time you're helping me with something.
No one to cook or clean for? A life free from danger? Even for a short while? Why, I never imagined such a thing!
Be ever so careful when you depart the premises. If my time with Lady Laurent has taught me anything, it's that danger lurks just outside every door.

I came across one of my to-do lists at the bottom of my pack and now I'm feeling homesick.\n\nPrepare fish stew. Sneak a few vegetables into fish stew. Proofread m'lady's new thesis. Organize m'lady's unmentionables …. Ah, such memories!
If you ask me, it's easier to break into rich folks' houses than poor folks. Palaces always have decorative walls and trellises to clamber up. Trying to quietly scale a mud hut? Impossible!
If you've got too many lockpicks, I think they make pretty good toothpicks. And hair pins. And fingernail cleaners—when I've got nails.\n\nMaybe I should write a book.
[wail of Goblin anger at being interrupted by attacking player]
Some say that the Mages Guild is just a fancy book club. A club with some very dangerous books, if you ask me.
I miss roasting pupal scribs over a fire. So sweet and airy, with a hint of crunch.
Be careful when you embellish your tales. You might be required to prove your claims. Then invention becomes the matron of necessity.
Be ever so careful when you depart the premises. If my time with Lady Laurent has taught me anything, it's that danger lurks just outside every door.

I came across one of my to-do lists at the bottom of my pack and now I'm feeling homesick.\n\nPrepare fish stew. Sneak a few vegetables into fish stew. Proofread m'lady's new thesis. Organize m'lady's unmentionables …. Ah, such memories!
People call us Daedra! Can you imagine? Daedra … feh. Like the Blackfeather Court has anything in common with that rabble! Do those ugly, toddler-sized Banekin have knights and ladies? I think not!
Be ever so careful when you depart the premises. If my time with Lady Laurent has taught me anything, it's that danger lurks just outside every door.

I came across one of my to-do lists at the bottom of my pack and now I'm feeling homesick.\n\nPrepare fish stew. Sneak a few vegetables into fish stew. Proofread m'lady's new thesis. Organize m'lady's unmentionables …. Ah, such memories!

Practically growing up in the Battlespire has made adjusting to Tamriel … interesting.\n\nI vaguely remember the sun, but I'd long forgotten the scalding kiss of Magnus on my skin. I didn't know I could turn that color.
If you've got too many lockpicks, I think they make pretty good toothpicks. And hair pins. And fingernail cleaners—when I've got nails.\n\nMaybe I should write a book.
I pity your lack of a beak, featherless. No weapon can match its glossy elegance! I can try to teach you to fight with that soft face of yours, but be prepared to lose an eye!
I don't have many places I'm welcome to visit right now, so I'm glad I have somewhere I can let my guard down. At least for a moment.\n\nAnd, truth be told, I like it here.
M'aiq is called the Liar, yet not a word this one utters is untrue.\n\nAlas, seeds of truth can bear strange fruits in overly fertile minds.
A fraction of my power.
I discovered a mortal kitchen during my recent explorations. The aroma of the baking—what did they call them? Ah, yes, pies—was bewitching. No Mazken ever devised something so seductive.
Don't tell Madam Whim, but I found a way to shave eons from my debt. By the time I finish, she will owe me. And oh, she'll hop and run at Hezehk's command! That is the dream!
All the Daedra I've ever met were bored with their immortality. Ha! Can you imagine? Being bored with a place as fathomless as Oblivion?
Guard your fearsome name with care—the day may come when it is all that is left to you.\n\nI speak from experience, mortal.
Oh, what is it now? Some urgent message to send me running across the planes? An errand that can't possibly wait until Hezehk has a spare moment? \n\nOh, sorry. Force of habit. Don't mind me.

What can I tell you about the Psijic Order without betraying my oath? Hmm. We're the oldest monastic group of Tamriel. And we're devoted to the study and practice of Mysticism. The Old Ways. And we live on Artaeum.\n\nHmm. Maybe I've said too much.
I can think of eighteen ways to kill a man with nothing but a rock. Improvisation. Creativity. That's what makes us warriors.

Hey there, good-looking! I love the ambiance in here, but I could really use a drink. Something sweet and fruity. Some sweet wine or honey juice maybe.\n\nWhat? While I was in Elsweyr, the cats really turned me around on my choice of tasty beverage.
Can you hear the drumming in the deep? It's the crescendo coming.

Just got out of jail. Again. Normally, I escape right away, but there was a gorgeous Wood Elf three cells down. We were really hitting it off!\n\nTurns out, she likes to set things on fire. Including her previous three lovers. So, that one's on me.
Don't mess with a street kid!
Ha! That will teach you to mess with Ember the sorcerer!
I hope I helped!
Let's go fast!
Sometimes I try to picture who your Magister Irin was. Sage old lady? A guar from the swamps? Ooh, or maybe a mysterious masked stranger who you never knew the identity of!
Every day I feel like I understand more about magic than I did before.
Adventuring with you really keeps a girl on her toes. You're getting stronger all the time!
I'm not a member of the Thieves Guild, but Iove what they do. I think maybe someday, I'd like to join up, but for now I'm just content to admire from afar.
Look out, everyone! Tamriel's best duo is back!
Not so yappy now, huh?
Bye, bye werewolf scum!
I didn't have a home growing up, but I think if I did, I'd want it to be something like this.
A knight never yields!
There are none left to stand against us.
On the move.
Your guidance has made me a better knight. Thank you.
Like every good story, your tale just grows in the telling.
I was hoping I'd see you today.
Another Daedra banished from this realm.
Ha! We are mighty!

Stendarr preserve me, you have to hear this. I was talking to my father the other day and he said … what do clams do on their birthday? And that man looked me right in the face and said: they shellebrate. I almost died.
Rigurt knows only one person who can drink more mead than me. Jorunn the Skald-King! \n\nHe has a stomach the size of mammoth! And Thane Jeggi. But Jorunn says he has hollow legs.

One time, Argonian ambassador tried to feed Rigurt something called six-ooze parfait. It wasn't bad to start, but then the oozes started to move! Crawled up spoon. Slithered out of bowl.\n\nVery hard to eat food that refuses to cooperate.
No creature truly thrives when removed from the place where it belongs. This applies to people as well.
A great wide world waits outside that door, that is true. But in my travels I have found no place as beautiful as the hills and woods of High Isle.

Do yourself a favor—never bet on horse races. Or guar, or nixhounds, or giant spiders. Really any sport where the participants can run faster than you. Torchbugs are all right, though.\n\nWhy? If you have to ask, you probably shouldn't know.

According to old Razhamad, it takes nine shuffles to make sure a deck's fully sorted and ready for play. Seems like kind of a lot to me. I figure three or four should do it.\n\nLess time shuffling leaves more time for complaining about bad draws!

Some see an old pirate with too many scars and a staff better for walking than fighting. No one expects me to know a damned thing about magic. Or anything scholarly, for that matter. I happen to know a lot of pirates who like to read. Just saying.

I joined the Mages Guild for a new adventure and found more than I ever imagined. It all started when I washed ashore in the Systres and the druids nursed me back to health. Ruptga forgive me, but from that point on, magic fascinated me!
This one feels … magnanimous. You may stroke her fur, if you wish.

You always seem to be in such a hurry, walker. Why does Khenarthi blow you from place to place like a leaf in the wind? Slow down and enjoy the simple pleasures. If you are unsure how, just follow Tadali's lead.
2E 582? Have you been getting into the ship's stores of rum and ale again, mate? I suggest you have a lie down before we reach Thras and the battle really gets underway.
Stop me if you've heard this one before. Why do Sloads always lose an argument?\n\nBecause they don't have a leg to stand on!
Greetings, my friend! Are you ready? Who knows what awaits you! Let's find out together.
This looks valuable.
Most crates have four rewards. Sometimes a crate will contain five! Can you imagine?
Whenever you wish to begin, Pacrooti is here. We will see what rewards await you!

Some might find it strange, but I always throw open my windows when a storm approaches. I love the smell of impending rain and the heaviness in the clouds. I don't mind if things get wet. I do try to move my books, though.

Nature still calms me, even to this day. When court life becomes too overwhelming, I find myself seeking fresh air. Even if it's just the balcony where I can feel the breeze on my face, the presence of the natural world relaxes something inside me.
Za'ji says I'm a cat of few words. Yup.

I grew up in Southern Elsweyr. Spent years making a living in fighting pits before Captain Za'ji convinced me to join his crew. I love the Pounce, but sometimes I miss the excitement of the pits. \n\nSometimes.
As a vampire hunter, I must keep my own council about my travels. My comings and goings, therefore, may be sporadic. Secretive. This is a necessity of my calling.

The vampires of Castle Ravenwatch are perplexing. A unique collection of personalities and a commitment to resisting their blood thirst. I am of two minds. Perhaps they could be powerful allies. Or perhaps my blade should resolve their angst.
Something big is happening.
This staff really makes you feel in charge.
I'll take care of this one.

Sewing. Learn it. Very useful skill. Best way to add secret knife pockets to all your clothes.\n\nBet you can't guess how many knives I'm carrying. Honestly, I've lost count. That's how many I have hidden on me.
People say I have a bad habit of sneaking up on them. It's not my fault that I'm perfectly silent and they're easily frightened. Sometimes, it's just one complaint after another.
A skilled swordfighter once told J'baanluk that no battle is ever assured, but you can stack the odds in your favor with skill and courage.\n\nAnd a quick prayer to Jone and Jode never hurts.
Magic fills the deserts of Elsweyr. The sands glow with the light of Jone and Jode, their constant dance radiating from every grain.\n\nThe very sight takes this one's breath away!
We are the Order of the Sacred Skeever! We wander from town to town, spreading the good word of Peryite and as many maladies as we can!
I need a word for a group of skeevers. A scurry? A loathe? Maybe a skitter or a craven?\n\nSo many possibilities to choose from! Writing is hard, my friend. Hard and complicated.
Twelvane's rule cannot be stopped.
This one will dispatch one of your friends with every failure.
Addled minds! You can't oppose me.
You wanna die? Fine.
Should have been more prepared.
Ready.
Picking up a lot from you, lately. It's paying off.
You earned it.

I know I'm not the most sociable person to have around. Believe it or not, I'm worse if I haven't eaten in a while. \n\nFrom experience, keeping yourself fed is just another way of staying prepared for anything.
Let's take a trip off the main roads.
I got it in my head once to get into antiquity hunting. Thought I could get rich. Turns out I do not have the patience to dig around in the dirt all day. \n\nCame as a surprise to me, too.
They want a fight, do they?
Ah. Time for tea, then.
How do you drive this thing?
Ah, newfound understanding! And with it: power.
I'm taking notes on your progress, just so you're aware. Galvanizing!

While we're together I'd ask that you avoid Artaeum and Eyevea. Not only are they bastions of pompous, narrow-minded, fetid-mouthed halfwits but erm … it's possible I may not be on the best of terms with a few of their Archmagi.
I'm here. What's next?

I'm aware that I can appear … fussy. Avoiding mushrooms and coffee and harpies and bugs. You have to understand, when it comes to unpleasant scents and sensations, my mind refuses to filter. \n\nObstinate lump of meat. But quite handy sometimes, too.
Oh. If a Temple bureaucrat ever pesters you about tithes I, er, forgot about in life, tell them to take it up with my mouth.

Interested in joining our little traveling troupe? I suppose it would be hard to let go of the fame and adoration that goes along with adventuring, but …. \n\nShould curiosity ever win you over, I could arrange a guest appearance or two.

Folio is a master of puppetry and a scholar of the classics. His rendition of the Song of Pelinal is life changing. I sobbed uncontrollably when he broke the crusader puppet into eighths. Devastating. \n\nI'm not sure I ever recovered.
I've met a few kings and queens in my travels. To my surprise, most of them have exceeded my expectations.
Don't spend too much time admiring your own wake. A wise captain keeps her eyes on the waters ahead, not behind.
I found myself wondering what the mortals around here did with their time. Then I remembered that I don't actually care.
Ah! A new day, filled with promise and opportunity …. \n\nSaid no one in full possession of their reason, ever.
My story doesn't end here. We both know it.
You are finite.
Let this dent your brittle facade.
Never assume what I am about to do.
What shall I do? Make a Dragon!
The ripples say it's time to act!
Repetition is good, but change is better.
This is who's been sent to kill me?
I am the unending search. You cannot change that.
I wonder if I'll find you in these pages, reflection.
Mortals die, words do not.
You think you beat me before?
I have power you have yet to see.
What does she need more space for?
Watch your step.
You cannot resist my call. I command you, Tho'at Replicanum!
If you want a respite from the maligraphies while still getting a reward, I recommend you take the second path.
This curse has left me to spend eternity as a repulsively adorable plaything. Can you imagine a worse fate?
Listen to the words of wisdom from the mouth of an adorable doll. \n\nKindness to those who deserve it. Punishment to all the rest.
Do you have a new mystery for Mizzik? No? Perhaps … the mysterious case of how Mizzik came to be in such charming company?\n\nBut of course, not every mystery is one that needs to be solved.
Explanations of crimes are often deceivingly simple. It is the motivations that become devious and complicated. Only by unraveling the two do we finally comprehend the whole tapestry, yes?
Growing up among Bretons, I don't give too much stock to the ways of stronghold Orcs. But I think they're right about one thing—most disputes are best settled with a good old-fashioned brawl.

Ever see the traveling performers from the House of Reveries? You'd never catch me in a troupe like that, but it got me thinking what my name would be if I ever enlisted as a Hopeful.\n\nSomething like Punch. Cleaver. Knife? Yeah, Knife! Oh, wait.
I'll never ask for field work again.
Tho'at, I'm your enemy.
I wonder how Tho'at realized she could manifest like this. It's still beyond me.
Those are my sweetrolls!
Stand still, you delicious hunk of mutton.

Leading is so much talking. Meeting after meeting after endless meeting.\n\nAfter seeing so much war, I've never made the mistake of longing for battle during times of peace. But during meetings … I must especially resist the temptation.

I have often said that one cannot change the course of a river in a single day. \n\nIt is a privilege, of course, to live in times where we worry about a river's course and not the possibility of it running dry.
We know.\n\nSee how I did that? Sends a chill down your spine, doesn't it?

My targets often flee when we arrive to deliver Sacrament. Sometimes they try to hide in the woods which gives me a chuckle. I'm a born hunter! That's the worst place to go.\n\nIf they hide in the sewer, though, that gets tricky. Uhh, the smell!

Aside from the occasional howl, I'm told I can be quite stealthy. It comes in handy while stalking prey in the forests for dinner. So staying hidden while hunting a contract comes naturally.\n\nUntil Kor crashes by with a raised sword, that is.

I think my wolf side likes Kor quite a bit. She always brings him tokens of affection after each kill. Sure, it's a bit embarrassing when I come back to myself with a finger bone between my teeth. But it's also sweet.
Rise, my atronach!
Capture their lands for me!
Blood is taken. Blood is claimed!
The Green calls, warrior. Let us speak quickly.
(Goblin GIbberish 10)
It's tempting, the thought of whisking you away into the stygian depths. Perhaps another time.
Looking around this place, I'm reminded of all the things I'm not very good at. Cooking, cleaning, kwama mining.\n\nBut killing something? I'm very good at that.

Obviously, I prefer Morrowind's cities to what passes for civilization in the rest of Tamriel. If I had to choose, Eastmarch isn't completely intolerable. Oh, it's as cold as Oblivion and there are too many Nords, but I do love the rabbit meatballs.
I will kill you all!
Defying me was your last mistake!
(Goblin GIbberish 10)
Always ready to jump in.
I'm learning a lot from you.
Please be a challenge, please be a challenge.
Hmm. Keep your weapons ready.
No one is going to believe this.
I hope this works!
Who's a good mount?
You just keep growing.
Blessings from my Moon Mother.
Strength of the exiled Boethra. It finds me, even now.
Khenarthi, make this swift.
Rest now.
Sa'pu val'rahd. In the end, we are stronger.
Miir maaszi, radhiit.
Traj radhin vabazeri. Strength becomes you.

While vampirism isn't my most important feature, people always ask about it first. What about my treatise on witch familiars, or my skill as a glass-smith? No, everyone asks about drinking blood.\n\nOh, I just realized! It's because they're scared!

I greatly struggled with my condition at first. Still do, if I'm honest. But some of the benefits are amazing.\n\nTraveling while in the form of mist? Incredible. Dexterity and strength improved, too. A shame that becoming undead was the cost.

As an adventurer, I consider it my sacred duty to liberate ancient treasures and bring them into to the light of day. Moreover, there's no safer place for those treasures than in my personal collection.\n\nFor preservation purposes, of course.

Of all the audacity! A so-called scholar? Ha! Refers to my interpretation of ancient carvings found in a Goblin cave as both juvenile and outlandish? I'll have you know Narsis Dren is nothing if not an expert on the outlandish. An expert, I say!

Magic might not be my strong suit, but alchemy? It's like second nature. Flowers just show you who they are, you know? Every bloom, ever petal, it's screaming. This is me! Take it or leave it! I respect that.
I'm sure you must be asking yourself, who let Barbas in here? Good question! I'm not going to tell you. Mysteries are good for the soul.
If I could talk, I would ask for a big plate of scrambled eggs and bacon. And some sausages! Definitely sausages!\n\nIf I could talk.

The first time I learned how to breathe fire was when I was trying to blow the candles out on my birthday cake. It would've been funny if it weren't for the fact I also burned off my friend's eyebrows.
Though I prefer to watch rather than play, I am very interested in this Tales of Tribute. If you start a game, please let me know. I would like to assess the odds before placing my bets.

I would rather not share my first era origin with others we meet in our travels.\n\nAzurah sent me back for a reason, tamiit. Best not to doubt her or put ourselves at risk by prompting a lot of questions.
I am undefeated!
Writhe in everlasting pain!
There's no time to do what must be done.
Just think. Somewhere there are villains to dispatch, beautiful maidens to rescue, and misplaced treasures to find!\n\nBut they will wait for Za'ji to have lunch first, yes?
Do not worry about Za'ji, walker—First Mate Caska frets over him enough for everyone.

High Isle would not be the jewel of the Systres Archipelago without the many druids that call the island home. I'd go so far as to say the beauty of our forests, flowering fields, and pristine beaches relies on the balance they help to maintain.

When my time isn't completely absorbed by my duties as duchess of High Isle, I try to visit the sunflower fields outside Gonfalon Bay. A remarkable flower, don't you think? A little burst of sunlight that you can hold in your hands.

Muffins sheds. A lot. But don't worry. I'll pick up every scrap of fur she drops.\n\nI've got a collection, actually. Someday I'm going to spin all that woolly fur into yarn and knit it into cloak. Or maybe blanket. I haven't decided yet.

I had the most handsome Nord smitten with me. Strong, a good fighter, hair like fire, son of the Skald-King. One day, he said to me, "Elsbytte, enough! It's either me or the mammoth!"\n\nAs if there was ever any choice! Anyway, I wish him well.
I just want my family back.
Why would the king send a foreigner after the Ansei Wards?
You've only destroyed my whelps. These minions will not be so easily defeated!
I will dominate this world and all others in time. The strong should always command the weak.
I forged you in the soulfire of Coldharbour to be my tool. Prove your worth.
Where has the giantess gone? Back to milk some mammoths?
Nothing you can do will end this.
May your enemies be broken and bloody.
I, Akatosh, will smite thee!
Shine your golden light and shatter the shackles of the subjugated. We pray in your name. Glory be thine, forever.
Be gone.
The rest of Nirn will die screaming. Just like you.
Am I distracting you? Bothering you? Throwing you off your game? Yes, let's stick with that as an excuse.
With Kyne's luck, your package will be on the next ship out.
This one wonders if her sister could use what you made.
Each of us has a role. You create. I deliver.
"You can't predict miracles, so plan for disaster." The old maxim holds true.
Don't stray too far into the wild. Dangerous creatures out there. Some on two legs.
There are more people out there, I'm sure of it. I'll have these supplies ready for their return.
Do you fancy yourself a benefactor of Daedra, mortal? Why not free me?
Reaking weakness.
The world's a better place without those wretches.\n\nHere's your bounty. Good work.
The poor soul contacted me to let me know that everything was fine. It's a shame such things are so commonplace. I'm in your debt, stranger.
Viccia Vibius.
Most of the Nords I know are much more agreeable than these fellows.
Fine work, friend. Fine work.
Murderer.
Murderer.
Have you considered investing in a cart?
I can't offer any blessings of Dibella, but I know a few oaths she's partial to.
Have you considered investing in a cart?
I can't offer any blessings of Dibella, but I know a few oaths she's partial to.
Exceptional craftsmanship. Hara will want to see this.
May the fires burn up your enemies, and the waters rise to quench your thirst.
Pacrooti is still waiting. This one has endless patience.
This could be helpful.
Well chosen!
A solid pick.
Pacrooti congratulates you!
If I have to wait around anyway, the least you could do is bring me a pillow.
Mmmmhmmmm!
Ooooo!
Ooooh!
Pacrooti is still waiting. This one has endless patience.
Mmmmhmmmm!
I hear these mortals secrets and I'm left wanting.
Memory artifact registered. Cognitive maintenance required.
Dreaming …. Soiled tablecloth. Washboard.
By Seht's will, I am bound to defend.
Greetings. Please report any and all crimes to the clockwork constabulary.
Ahhh.
Hello, my friend! You seem to think that Pacrooti is a good egg, even though you know he is slightly cracked. Pacrooti appreciates that.
Pacrooti is still waiting. This one has endless patience.
The suspense is killing this one!
Top-notch!
Ahhh.
Ha ha!
Pacrooti wishes you luck!
Pacrooti enjoys playing with you very much!
My power flows through the abyssal pearl.
My geysers will consume you all!
You saved the tower, but Nocturnal abides.
The Abyssal Cabal will have its revenge!
You were lucky this time, but luck is my domain.
Defeated? Oh how little you understand, mortal flea!
Meet at the ship and we'll divide the plunder.
All this dry land is unsettling. When do we sail?
(Goblin GIbberish 11)
Have you met that Sotha Sil yet? Now there's an Elf I can relate to. Soft-spoken, reclusive, melancholy …. Actually, now that I think about it, we don't have much in common at all.
A fight? Good!
That's the last of them!
[stage whispering, gossipy Goblin gibberish]
I'm always nervous about taking my horse to Altmer lands. I'd hate for him to meet Elven mounts and pick up bad habits.
I can see why mom has been so reluctant to settle in at home. There's too much to this world to spend our time on it in one place.
M'aiq does not mind waiting. When one has lived long enough, one learns that few things are as urgent as they first appear.
Once, to show the Duke how worthy I was, I lifted a whole melon off the ground. A melon, featherless! I bet you have never seen a wingless squire lift an entire melon before!

Why do the Daedra seem so interested in the affairs of mortals? You'd think they'd have more than enough to do in the vast and infinite realms of Oblivion than torment us. Cosmologically speaking, though, that could be the reason for their existence.
The small, flying things that haunt the mortal realm? Birds, I think they are called. Yes.\n\nDispose of them. I do not like them.
The trouble with the mortal realm is that it's full of mortals. I would almost like the place if it weren't so crowded with so many of your kind. No offense.
The food in Oblivion is strange, but I think I got used to it during my travels. Everything back in the mortal realm just tastes so … cautious by comparison.
You're ready to mix things up, aren't you? Ha! Gather your gear and we'll cook up something good.

People say a wink and a smile can disarm someone as well as any sword. Just know your audience, all right? Winking and smiling at someone you stole from can leave you with a black eye and a loose tooth.\n\nTrust me. I know.
Watch me go!
Ha! That will teach you to mess with Ember the sorcerer!
Nicely done.
Let's go fast!
This sorcerer is sorcering better than ever before! Sorcering, that's a word, right?
Adventuring with you really keeps a girl on her toes. You're getting stronger all the time!
Ember the Sorcerer, reporting for duty!
Sometimes I try to picture myself sitting in a guild hall poring over a dusty old book. It makes all my hair stand on end. Pure torture.
To battle!
Stendarr was with us in that fight.
On the move.
I've learned so much riding with you, my friend.
Like every good story, your tale just grows in the telling.
I'm at your service.

Blessed be the name of Stendarr, the God of Mercy. He strengthens and unifies his Resolutes through his wisdom and blessings. He calls us by day to train with sword and shield to strengthen our might; and by night to strengthen our souls ….
Thanes! Rigurt supposes Skyrim needs them to function, but they are big pain in Rigurt's horker. Still, better than the various lords and counts that other nations must contend with, I suppose.
Discovering magic was like discovering a whole new ocean. Something new to explore. When I was young, I set off to sea for similar reasons.\n\nThis isn't so different, just in reverse.
You will outgrow your foolishness, walker. You are still so very young.

When the All Flags Navy has done its job and those vile Sloads no longer threaten Tamriel, I may just stay on High Isle. Find a piece of land. Build a little house. Start a family.\n\nI'd miss the sea, but you can't go on fighting forever, am I right?
Bright Moons! You have returned! Pacrooti hopes that you are well, safe, and happy today.
Rajhin's Shadow!
Any crate could contain many wonderful rewards. You can preview what a crate could contain, if you'd like.

I'd rather peel the hide off a rabid bear than sit in a room and listen to people squabble over trifles such as titles and favor. I'm a person of action at my very core. Order is important, but talking in circles has never gotten anyone anywhere.
Pellitine. That's the Khajiiti name for Southern Elsweyr. Look, I know the place has problems, but it's my home. I grew up there.

I am allowing myself some measure of satisfaction today. Daesul Brohad, my hunter's blade, burned out the heart of a vampire lord who thought himself invincible. Proving him wrong was … quite satisfying.

It's hard work keeping a ship seaworthy. When I was young I used to scrape barnacles and sea scum off the side of hulls to earn some coin. You learn quick that for every skilled sailor, there's a dinghy full of lazy sods taking up space on a ship.

J'baanluk may be large, but that does not mean he is strong and dangerous. Well, he is, but it does not mean he is nasty and ruthless. Though he can be. When the circumstances demand it. But usually, J'baanluk is, how do you say? A pussy cat?

I have interests other than my work as a founding member of the Order of the Sacred Skeever, you know. I enjoy cooking with moldy meats and vegetables. And I'm quite proficient with the lute. The strings make my blisters and sores bleed, though.
Counter this!
Over so soon?
Ready.
Always room for improvement.
You earned it.
Not sick of me yet?

Some drunk Nord once ask me why I bothered fishing from dry land when my kind was so good at swimming. He insisted I'd catch way more that way.\n\nI called him an idiot, but it still haunts me. What if he's right?
By Mora's many eyes!
Heh. We have an accord.
How do you drive this thing?
An opportunity for erudition! Hah!
I'm taking notes on your progress, just so you're aware. Galvanizing!
I'm here. What's next?

Tea can be a stimulant, of course. But I find the buzz you experience with a nice Aetherial or Spiceberry quite pleasant. \n\nWhereas coffee is like a million gnats dancing within your mind. No thank you.
Did I ever tell you about the time I met Almalexia in Firewatch? It was a summit on the principles of ghostfencing. I think she fancied me, if you know what I mean!

Nothing makes me more ravenous than honey pudding. Just imagine the crunch as you break through that perfectly caramelized top layer. Its silky interior broken only by its bite-size pieces of perfectly toasted honeycomb. Like a dream!
I always find the stars to be brighter the farther I am out to sea. I've spent many a dark watch talking with the Warrior or the Lady—they're friends to all sailors.
Nothing you do matters in the end. All existence will eventually collapse into nothingness. The sooner you accept that, the happier you'll be.
You are an ending already read.
No, I will not say "Mama."

Mizzik has quite the stomach for sea travel, actually. It is the stomach for violence that he does not possess.\n\nOne wonders what might result from combining the two, but—ah, no. Mizzik prefers not to think about that after all.
I'm keeping an eye on the entrances and exits. It's a nice place. You never know who might try to break in and steal something.
The filers wanted me to pass along their well wishes on this fight.

Many ask me what it was like to speak with Almalexia at the formation of the Ebonheart Pact.\n\nRemember, by that point, my shellbacks had saved her people from the Akaviri invasion. I doubt anyone has asked her the same question about me.

I once fought a fellow for three whole days. We began with swords. Those broke on the first night, so we picked up short blades. When they shattered on the second night, we used our fists.\n\nI won, of course. Still, I respect his effort.

My brother Kor was an orphan, did you know that? We're not supposed to talk about our pasts, but knowing that explains a lot about him. He's so eager to help those he's close to. Behind that loud voice, he's a big softy.
(Goblin GIbberish 11)

Alliances. Same sort of foolishness we see with the Great Houses. Imaginary borders and other accoutrements meant to put the masses in neat little piles. Does make it easier for us to do our job, but all the various labels still rankle me.
(Goblin GIbberish 11)
What's the move?
I've still got room to grow.
This shouldn't take long.
Done. But don't let your guard down.
No one is going to believe this.
I hope this works!
Ready when you are!
You just keep growing.
Khenarthi's wind at my back. Let us go.
What is this strength? The might of Alkosh, perhaps?
Let this be a lesson.
Rest and know peace.
Sa'pu val'rahd. In the end, we are stronger.
Let us move.
Traj radhin vabazeri. Strength becomes you.

My siblings in House Ravenwatch lovingly accuse me of being soft. They say we live in a rough world, full of threats and cruelty. I know this well.\n\nI only seek to provide a counterbalance to the darkness by displaying politeness whenever possible.

A true adventurer keeps their wits about them, even when a situation goes awry. I have never panicked when a torch flickered, lost my nerve before a wild beast, or run screaming face-first into a wall at the least sign of danger. Not once! Recently.
<The dog looks at you and pants. He seems bemused.>

I'm a bit of a sucker for grand romantic gestures. I once dated a woman who didn't know what kind of wine I liked so she bought one of everything, just to be safe. Said we'd get to know each other while we worked our way through them.
Is this place typical for a dwelling in this time? I will keep my judgements to myself. I come from a different era, after all. But I am curious.

In Za'ji's business, it is sink or swim. You would think as big as she is, Caska would sink the moment her paws touched water, but she is like a fish in the ocean. Or a whale. Definitely a large fish.\n\nBut do not mention Za'ji said this.

Do you ever find yourself accumulating bits and bobs while on your travels? I started collecting sea shells. Even when I find myself deep inland, there never fails to be a merchant selling the odd rare shell. Think of me if you ever find one.

Muffins got into the flour again. I'm not sure what she's thinking! She doesn't seem to eat any of it. Just rolls around and get it all over her—and everything else!\n\nI never get too angry with her, though. She's just so adorable!
They can't lock us up like this!
You do not yet know fear? I shall make you afraid!
Kill my minions and you only remove the weaklings from my service.
The sacrifices you make are all done in my name. You are and will always be my servant.
Lyris Titanborn. She was the best slave at the Black Forge. Whatever happened to her?
The Daedra. The anchors. You destroy them in vain.
Your strength is mine. Come. Serve me.
You won't kill me again. I'm invulnerable!
I forced the Thief into hiding. I riled the Warrior to frenzy. I shattered the Mage into so many pieces she cannot remember which one is real. What chance have you against me?
You stumbled into here by accident, didn't you? I see no other possible explanation for your disastrous performance.
I hear the roads aren't safe. Good thing your package travels by sea.
Do not ask what all these shipments are for. This one only makes the deliveries.
The roads are harder, farther from the capital. I will need to deliver these soon.
I'm not allowed to leave until the cargo is shipped. I need a better contract.
Couldn't pay me enough to ship this freight. Bandits out there … behind every rock.
I don't trust this place. Our only real chance against the Daedra is to be well-supplied.
When mortals seek power, they find only Oblivion.
You're the great hero, eh? The family offered a reward for a live rescue.\n\nBut you know that already I suppose. Here you go.
Well, at least my friend is safe, huh? Good to know. Such a flighty creature that one. I wonder where the little birdie will finally land.
Regulus Opsius.
Careful! I think this group might be hostile.
I don't really ask where these go. I just make sure they're on time.
Thief.
Thief.
I surrender to nothing, except a notarized certificate of deposit.
Happiness is never out of reach if you put your heart into finding it, or your hips.
I surrender to nothing, except a notarized certificate of deposit.
Happiness is never out of reach if you put your heart into finding it, or your hips.
"Today's idleness is tomorrow's worry."
"A gift given freely is twice given."
Pacrooti is waiting!
A suitable reward.
Definitely up to snuff!
Well deserved.
Well done.
If it isn't the artisan. I'm given to understand that fine work takes time.
Hmm hmmmmm.
Ahhhh!
Haaa!
Pacrooti is waiting!
Hmm hmmmmm.
So many mortals shy away from the concealing night. Fools, all.
Dreaming …. Pottery wheel. Laughter.
Dreaming …. Flower garden. Bird songs.
Calculating patrol subroutines.
I hope you are well, entity name not found.
hoo!
Welcome back, good friend! It is always a pleasure to talk nonsense with someone, and to have his nonsense respected.
Pacrooti is waiting!
Please don't make this one wait!
A lovely sweetmeat!
Hoo!
Hooo hoo hoo!
Great things await!
Each time is so exciting!
The sea abides, and so do the Sload of Ul'vor-Kus!
You cannot defy Nocturnal's will.
You have earned my hatred, mortal!
You plugged one leak, but three more shall take its place.
You can't stop the darkness, mortal, so why even try?
Victory? For a time, perhaps. But time belongs to the Daedric Princes.
I find that a quick slash across the throat quiets the noisy ones.
Stop worrying. The scouts will signal if they see an Altmer ship.
(Goblin GIbberish 12)
You know, where I'm from, warriors wield swords made of pure math. Kind of puts those crude metal weapons into perspective, eh?
[Goblin gibberish declaring she's the most powerful]
Lord Silvelle taught me that a good horse is smarter than his rider, but under no circumstances should the horse be allowed to know this.

I sometimes wonder what it must be like for Daedra. Going through their lives with no real sense of time passing them by. Where loss and death are annoying trivialities. No wonder they feel powerful, and hollow.

Have you heard of the Devourer of Dune? A savage beast that terrorized Rimmen one awful day.\n\nOh, the lolling tongue! The drooling maw! The hot, fetid breath! It was almost too much disgust for this one to bear!

Being a squire is hard work. We polish our knights' talons, organize their piles of shinies ….\n\nWhen I finally earn my knighthood, I'll treat my ward with nothing but respect. Until they step out of line. Then I'll really let them have it!
It's been an adjustment sleeping here. Tamriel, I mean. The hours I've kept had nothing to do with the rise and fall of celestial bodies. I never quite feel in alignment with this world.

I observed a nearby village today. Not a moment went by without some mortal toiling to gather food, struggling to prepare food, or busying themselves with the task of consuming food.\n\nIs eating really that important to your kind?
Oh, what is it now? Some urgent message to send me running across the planes? An errand that can't possibly wait until Hezehk has a spare moment? \n\nOh, sorry. Force of habit. Don't mind me.
I had a little clannfear follow me around for a bit while I was out exploring the Deadlands. It was perfectly pleasant to me. Only tried to eat me once, as I recall. I named them Altaba.
Talent's fine, but the secret to victory is hard work. You put in the time, and we'll make you a legend.

Know any good jokes? I just learned one about an Orc and a stork, and whoo! Let me tell you, the forge wife of the Morkul clan did not care for it one bit.\n\nActually, you know what? I'm gonna keep it to myself. Trust me, I'm doing us both a favor.
You want to die?
I love watching the big tough ones fall.
We're dangerous, huh?
Let's ride!
This sorcerer is sorcering better than ever before! Sorcering, that's a word, right?
Watch out, everyone. This adventurer isn't slowing down anytime soon!
Ember the Sorcerer, reporting for duty!
I think I need to take it easy on experimenting with spells for a bit. I almost fried off my own tail last night. I'm not vain, but I'd rather keep my tail, I think.
Side by side!
We're still standing. Be proud of that.
Here we go.
I've learned so much riding with you, my friend.
You're always striving to learn something new. One of my favorite things about riding with you.
I'm at your service.

When was the last time you were on a boat? Growing up on High Isle you have to learn to sail, it's like running or swimming for Tamsfolk. Just something you pick up. I'd be happy to take you out someday!

Rigurt dutifully keeps a journal. Very important that all diplomatic meetings have accurate records. Like this one. \n\nToday! Rigurt met with friend. Discussed Rigurt's journal. Agreed journaling is good idea. Another diplomatic success for Rigurt!

I have nightmares about waking up aboard a ship. I'm old and gray, my body aches something fierce, and the sea roils and crashes around us. Worst of all? My magic is gone. I'm who I used to be … just older.\n\nAlways leaves me feeling hollow. Empty.
This one hears whispers on the wind. You have done interesting things, walker. Interesting, indeed.
Ah, you sit with Pacrooti once again. Your face brings a smile to his face.
Definitely up to snuff!

Sometimes it feels as if I don't belong anywhere. Like I'm not a knight, nor a druid. Yet other days I feel I am unequivocally both. My own perception should not waver. And I can't keep letting others influence my own opinion of myself.
Ever see what a house cat does when it catches a mouse? Now imagine that, only our enemy is the mouse and I'm the house cat. Get the picture?
Hmm. Is this one cursed with Noxiphilic Sanguivoria? Is it a pure-blood? A Volkihar? A descendant of one of the Morrowind vampiric lines? So many fiends, so little time.

Someone actually wanted me to put Howler up as stakes in a game of Tribute. I accepted, of course, and Howler let me know his displeasure. But I won the match and he's still here. \n\nHe simply has no faith in me. No faith at all.

When this one is away, he misses the prickly flora of Northern Elsweyr. Not everyone admires their beauty, but J'baanluk sees a certain honor in a plant that wears its own armor. I see the strength of all Khajiit in them.

Here's another recitation from my work in progress, Tenets of Holy Diseases. "Bile, pus, boils, and tumors!"\n\nThat's it. I'm still getting the hang of compiling the teaching of the Lord of Pestilence into something the faithful will want to read.
Let's knock some heads.
That's it?
Let's ride.
Always room for improvement.
Look at you.
Not sick of me yet?
I wish I'd learned to play a musical instrument at some point. I like music.\n\nEven like dancing, too. When nobody's watching.
Mora's many tentacles!
And: Tranquility.
We can't take a portal?
An opportunity for erudition! Hah!
Your accomplishments just compound, one upon the other.
Arcanist here.

Being an arcanist can be quite … disconcerting. Tentacles and eldritch runes, the waters of the abyssal sea rushing around in your head every once in a while.\n\nBut it's worth it, a bargain well struck. For power and self-sufficiency.
What is this card game everyone's playing? Trifle? Tribune? A Buoyant Armiger tried to engage me in a game. I teleported him to the top of Tel Naga without his clothes!

There are a fair number of powerful mages in the House of Reveries. Some may associate scholars of magic with vanity and hubris, but the ones I call family? They are the kindest people I know. They squarely seek to showcase magic's innate beauty.
One thing I learned during my life at sea? You can sail into the wind if you're willing to spend the day tacking. But sometimes it makes more sense to wait for the breeze to change.
Mortals seem to care a lot about when and how they die. Is that how you rank yourself against your rivals?
Just wait. Those who did this to me will never see what is coming.

Everywhere he goes, Mizzik always asks questions. Some find it very annoying, but aside from solving mysteries, it is how Mizzik shows his interest!\n\nHe gets called nosy. But this one supposes there are worse things they might call Mizzik.
You ever been through Abah's Landing? I've never been to a more shifty place. If we stayed in the harbor any longer, I was sure someone was going to come and steal the planks off our ship.
It looks tougher than it is. Probably.
It lightens my heart to live among those in Blackwood who speak Jel, my native tongue. But I cannot abide words like ojel and lukiul being wielded like weapons.

Kvatch is fine as far as cities are concerned. I can't stand all the people, though. Too much banging and clanging. Who likes it that loud? Give me a quiet cave or an empty forest any day.\n\nAnd yes, I see the irony.

I heard from a shopkeep in Kvatch that Western Skyrim is having a horrible time with werewolf attacks. He claimed it was some kind of uprising. I wonder if my old clan is involved.\n\nNo, I don't plan to join them, if that's what you're thinking.
(Goblin GIbberish 12)
I just received a writ, so if I disappear for a while don't get too nervous. I have a job to do, just like you.\n\nAnd don't worry. Still doesn't have your name on it. As far as you know.
(Goblin GIbberish 12)
You know, my ears were burning.
I've still got room to grow.
Let me at em!
Bet there's more nearby.
And the crowd goes wild!
Did it work? I closed my eyes.
You lead and I'll follow!
How do you do it?
My moonclaw draws me to you.
What is this strength? The might of Alkosh, perhaps?
I am with you, tamiit!
Var, var, var.
We are victorious, by the strength of Alkosh.
On the move.
Alkosh smiles upon you.

House Ravenwatch remains unique among our kind, but vampires have a reputation for savagery for good reason. Now that I experience the crushing hunger, I understand. Slipping into evil isn't as unthinkable as before.\n\nI must never forget that.

Ah, levers. I devoted three entire chapters to their use in tombs and ancient ruins. Remember, if you see a lever, give it a pull. Same goes for buttons. Push them all! In my experience something always happens when you pull a lever or push a button.
Snuggly fur, big eyes, a cute tail—I'm adorable!

How are you supposed to learn things about wine? Are there classes for that sort of thing? I just swish it around in my mouth while I wait for others to share their thoughts. Then I just agree with them.
I have always enjoyed meeting those from lands different from my own. A result of my upbringing, I suppose.\n\nIt is quite different to meet those from a different time, but no less enjoyable.
Have you seen the Perfect Pounce, walker? An impressive vessel! Sleek as a greased Alfiq and twice as swift! Speaking of greased Alfiq, tell my mother I set sail. For somewhere very far away.

I'll let you in on a little secret. If you ever find yourself spending long days in the sun, perhaps while on a lengthy voyage across the Abecean, nothing cools you down quicker than a chilled wine.\n\nHow do I chill it? I have mages for that.

I once left Muffins with a friend to go tend to the wake of my Uncle Olnof. Turned out he wasn't dead, just in a very deep sleep. I came home to find my friend about to sell Muffins to a Khajiit caravan! Now I keep her with me no matter where I go.
Hlaalu does what it always does. Nothing!
When you are destroyed, the flies will pick your bones clean.
Your White-Gold Tower will serve as an anchor point for my dark machines!
How many have you killed to defeat me? Each death is like a prayer—to me!
Where has little Abnur Tharn run off to? Where does he hide?
I will ensure no tales are told of your valor.
The time remaining when you can still refuse me is dwindling.
I will hunt mortals until none are left.
That was your healer's fault. No question about it.
"Honest labor is its own reward."
Good work! Thank you for your contribution.
"A good day's work is sweet as sugar, but laziness is like the Trama Root."
I could really use a bowl of stew, but it's not seemly to eat while on the job.
"Honest work for honest pay." Heh. Just the pay, any way I can get it.
Send back anyone you see and I'll get them some supplies. We need to concentrate our forces.
No birthskin escapes my bite.
Innocents delivered to safety. That's what this job is all about.\n\nFantastic. Here's your reward.
You did what? Well, that's impressive, isn't it? Good thing you came to me, stranger. I recognize accomplishment.
Cornelia Vedia.
I'll take care of anything that gets past you!
Good work! Thank you for your contribution.
Watching you.
Watching you.
I draw the line at piggybacks. Never again.
You look tense. A little devotional massage would do you wonders.
I draw the line at piggybacks. Never again.
You look tense. A little devotional massage would do you wonders.
These have been difficult to come by of late.
When all this ends, I will enjoy a cool bath and a goblet of spiced wine.
A solid pick.
Most excellent!
A lovely prize.
Pacrooti is truly impressed!
Hmmmmm.
<gasp>
Hmmm hmmm!
Hmmmmm.
Confessions in the night. Is there anything more enticing?
Dreaming …. Fish pond. Skipping stone.
Dreaming …. Familiar embrace. Moonlight.
Structural integrity diagnostics in progress.
May your discoveries lead the way to innovation.
hooo!
Our friendship pleases Pacrooti. He believes that a  good friendship is like peeing his pants in public. Everyone can see it, but only Pacrooti can feel the warmth inside.
<yawn>
Wonderful!
hoo!
Hoooo, haaaa!
Here you go!
Pacrooti loves the excitement of the cards!
The Sea Sload shall reclaim our ancestral home!
Go forth, my yaghra!
Feel the anger of the darkness enraged!
You can't hold back the sea with a sword, worm.
My power grows, so savor your victory while you can.
Savor this moment. It shall not last.
Falling overboard would be better than this.
If we burn all their cities, where would we raid?
(Goblin GIbberish 13)
Be honest—do you ever wish we hadn't broken the Staff of Towers? Just imagine a world of non-linear time! Wait, is your nose bleeding? All right, stop imagining a world of non-linear time.
[haughty Goblin taunting the player before an attack]
I reckon I can handle anything that comes at me on the road with good manners, common sense, and a full wineskin.
How did you ever get through these long periods of quiet without me?

Beware of people in hoods. M'aiq has never met a trustworthy person wearing a hood. \n\nWell, except on a rainy day. Or a particularly cold day. Then hoods are a basic necessity. Even M'aiq dons one then.

What? I'm not a thief! A true knight never steals. He simply takes things that don't belong to him to give them a more noble purpose.\n\nOn an unrelated note, a mouse just scurried away with one of your items. I tried to stop him, honest!

I find cities to be rather overwhelming. All the sights, sounds … smells.\n\nA battlemage requires years of ascetic training. Study, isolation, practice, and little else. I do want to experience everything I've missed, but preferably not all at once.
This place could use more captives to torment. You can judge one's importance by the quality and quantity of the prisoners they keep.
I've been thinking—I should pay more attention to my own idle fancies. Who will put Hezehk first, if not Hezehk?
Litaalar was always one step ahead of me during our training. I may not be a stronger mage than her, but I'm certainly more well-traveled! She wouldn't know the Deadlands from a pond in Summerset!
Take it from an old tusker, there's nothing wrong with fighting dirty. You want to win? Do what you got to do.

Mmph! Sorry, my fingers are killing me. Trying to learn how to play the lute, you see? I'm told it's essentially a swoon-machine. \n\nI don't really need the help, but you can never have too many arrows in your quiver, right?
Don't underestimate us!
I love watching the big tough ones fall.
Oh yeah, that felt good.
Let's ride!
Watch out, everyone. This adventurer isn't slowing down anytime soon!
